reviews.comment: I went to High School with Roland William "Ashley" Samuelson. He is a brilliant man who is a great teacher, but he is not a her. Take this class if you want to learn a lot but call him Roland or William Samuelson.
Ashley was really nice and a great professor. She is very smart and knows exactly what she is talking about. Not too much homework and replies to piazza posts very quickly
She's really good! Take her if you can

CS400 is structured a little strange with the class switching between data structures and seemingly random topics, but Ashley does a great job of explaining the material. Highly recommend taking the class with her.

GOAT. By far one of the best professors I've had at UW.
I've honestly been quite disappointed with the overall teaching quality here in previous semesters, but Ashley completely changed that for me. She is the reason I see real hope in this school.
An absolute must-take.
A really great professor. Her slides and notes are very detailed and she explains concepts clearly. She is also very responsive to emails and piazza questions after class and always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ashley is a very good professor, slides are very organized and lectures are pretty good for cs400 and are recorded. Learned a lot in this course because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely phenomenal professor. I wasn't even in her section but I'd still tune into her lectures because she teaches so well. She's the only reason I passed the class. The notes she provides are absolutely amazing and she has been an absolutely MASSIVE help. Would 100% recommend 7/5 stars.
She has an unparalleled teaching style and is super responsive to emails + piazza posts. Clearly loves teaching, and is extremely knowledgeable, which is an extremely rare combination.

Dallas likes to give a lot of visual examples of the content and draws them on the board very clearly. If that helps you to understand the content more then he is great. I personally didn't get a whole lot from lecture, and learned most of the content through homework and practice exams. Notes are done on a chalkboard.

My review might be a bit biased because I had some previous calc exposure but he was a great lecturer and taught his classes in a clear succinct way. Can't really complain about anything and was pretty energetic. Would definitely recommend taking.

Dr. Albritton was a very charismatic professor, and he clearly cared a lot about his students.  Typically his lectures were good, however at times the structure was a little confusing.  A few times he began a proof, then  stopped to define something we needed, then did an example, then finished the proof.  He's great at answering questions, though.

I had Dallas for his first ever semester at UW-Madison, so he definitely could improve but he was not the greatest teacher in my opinion. I had taken calculus before and I felt the way Dallas taught was very ineffective. He just writes on the board and does not explain. The tests are easy though because you get all the past tests for review.

Albritton is be the best math professor you could get. Very caring about his students, intelligent, flexible, etc. He is everything that a good professor should be and I highly encourage anybody to take math 221 with professor Albritton!

Overall great professor, I was able to understand most topics in the class. I was able to understand why I would get problems wrong and work on solutions to fix them. I highly recommend going to his office hours, that was where I learned the most. For a first semester at UW-Madison, I think he did a great job!

If you've never taken a calc class before, don't take it with Dallas. He doesn't really teach he just writes problems on a chalkboard, and does them with little explanation/not nearly enough time to try on your own. The organization of the course does not make sense. Students who have already taken a calc class before were just as confused.

This class is an easy science class, and I would recommend taking this class and this professor. You won't really be able to talk to her too much, but she is a great professor, and you can tell that she actually knows what she is talking about. The grades are also super forgiving, with an A being an 89 or higher.

Stravroula was a very kind and easy-going professor. She cares about her students and sets everyone up for success with clear communication and resources. Her lectures included relevant and engaging material and overall the course was not difficult.
I do not have much to say about the course itself, it was very easy but one thing is that the professor will NEVER respond to your emails.

Super easy for nutri-sci. Cancelled class frequently but it never affected us staying on track. Textbook is straightforward and super helpful. Enjoyed how she allowed us to ask specific questions during lecture via an online polling system
Beautiful professor ngl

Always gave so much information in her lectures and was very clear about all assignments and when they were due. All exams were online and final was optional only to help your grade if needed. Gives so much extra credit opportunities and is very flexible if needed. Very kind professor and fun class to take!

Good easy-A class for GPA. She is super sweet, seems very knowledgeable, but is kind of a boring lecturer and reads off slides. By the end of the semester, most people stop coming to lecture. Need to do very little to no studying for exams.
Super easy class. Attendance wasn't required, although there were often participation questions. Easy A, never any in-person element.

Super easy class, everything is online and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. You can tell when attendance is based off canvas. She is nice but knows that everyone is taking the class for the easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class so easy I question if I actually took it. Professor is really sweet and lectures are simple to follow. Participation is occasionally taken but I haven't attended class for the past two months and ended with a 96.

Easy A, everything is online. She seems to genuinely have a deep understanding of the topic, but just reads off the slides. Only some lectures have attendance assignments, so keep an eye on which ones you need to go to.

Prof. Antonopoulos is a great instructor- the outline of the course matched what we learned, and all of the lectures were straight forward and easy to apply to homework/quizzes/exams. There are participation point you need to be in class to receive, but she tailors her lectures to students' interests. Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever but the lectures are so dry. I attended lecture for the first half of the class but I didn't feel like I was gaining much so I stopped going despite the graded participation and my grade is still an A+. Many lectures are either spitballing info or her just rambling. Very knowledgable but doesn't really convey info well.

This class is extremely easy. She reads off of the slides and does not seem to have a great hold on the class. There is random participation, so I went to most lectures. She has so many extra pointless things to make things "better," but it would be better if she would just talk from her knowledge and not the textbook.

She is very knowledgable. But she rarely gets to show her expertise because so much information is packed into the lecture slides. This class is very easy but boring. Lectures were mostly just dumping information on you rather than teaching you.

Stavroula is nice & the content itself can be interesting, but lectures are so boring because she reads off the slides (which come straight off the textbook). Easy class but there're other easy A options w/ less busy work. Weekly quizzes are open note, but the 15 min timer was way too harsh to finish anything in time & questions were unpredictable.

Guaranteed A. No one showed up to class the lectures were not very helpful. Weekly quizzes that you get 15 minutes on, and I don't know how anyone could complete them in time. Overall, some useful information. She's a nice professor who I am sure means well, but just kind of all over the place. Crazy syllabus, I'll say that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stavroula doesn't really do anything. This entire course is basically an online textbook. Your professor is McGraw Hill Connect, not Stavroula Antonopoulos. The lectures are dry, and just repeat whatever is in the textbook. Within a few weeks of the semester, nobody shows up to the lectures anymore. The class is an easy A but painfully boring.

Good professor and very knowledgable, easy class but lots of busy work each week (chapter quizzes and long assignments), everything is online and open notes, participation is often required as she does attendance questions during lecture.

Easiest class you'll ever take, but also a genuinely very good professor. If you are interested in nutrisci and need/want to learn, you definitely will. But if you want to fulfill a science gen ed by putting in as little effort as possible, this is your best bet.

Stavroula was a great professor and I loved her class! All exams were open note, online, and you could take them at any time over the course of a week. Participation is graded for maybe 2/3 of lectures, but she drops the worst 7 and is super understanding of extenuating circumstances. Engaging lectures and easy grader as well!

When many people in the class were complaining that we didn't have enough time on the weekly quizzes, she told us that as long as some people are getting good scores that it was "fair". We get the same amount of time for the final exam as the other exam but there are 25 more questions than normal. She was not willing to change her mind on anything.
Excellent class and professor! I would say it will be difficult not to get an A. Due to many extra points, most people have grades above 100%.

Most people (myself included) take this class as a GPA-booster, Stavroula did a great job for having 400+ enrolled in her class. Expectations laid out very clearly in the syllabus, pretty light workload, some useful insights into nutrition, interesting guest speakers in lectures. Solid freshman year class to knock out some science credits.

Professor Antonopoulos is great. She deeply cares for her students and is always more than willing to help. Her course is super chill and genuinely interesting if you're into nutrition. Exams and quizzes are online.
This class is an easy A but Professor Antonopoulos presents the content in a very dry manner and the assignments are really poorly worded and redundant.

Professor Stavroula is an amazing teacher!! Good lecture, reasonable class mode very professional,thoughful minds. I would recommend this class to everyone. You can learn useful nutritional acknowledge as well. You won't want to miss it.

This class is an easy way to get your biological science credit. All of the quizzes and tests are online, at home, and open note. Attendance is mandatory in the lectures for class credit. She is a good lecturer but there is so many people in the class it's hard to actually gain anything from the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: NS132 was a very easy class to take freshman year. Graded by weekly quizzes and discussions, and a few exams. Not too much work outside of lecture. Professor is very easy going.

Great Professor and Great class class is structured in a very nice and organized way same 2 assignments every week a low stakes quiz and a fair discussion post. Lecture always chill and she does care about her students. 3 Final options Overall couldn't be any better

Prof. Antonopoulos is the best instructor I have ever had. She made everything super clear and all the work was super easy. I felt that I really learned something about Nutrition. I am not a science major and I just took this class to fulfill a bio science credit and it was the perfect choice. As long as you turn in work, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you need to fulfill a science credit, I 100% recommend Nutri Sci with Professor Antonopoulos. Everything was posted and online (quizzes, discussions, exams, lecture notes) so it was extremely accessible. Additionally, she gives you 3 options for the final. She is super nice and cares about her students! Super easy and interesting class!

Really easy class. Structured really well and there were no surprises. 

As long as you tried, you did well. The class is textbook heavy and all she does is go over the textbook.

She's nice and the class is easy.

I really enjoyed this professor. She was very sweet and her class was taught well. The grading criteria was also very clear. The tests and homework assignments were all online so it wasn't hard to do well in this class. I definitely recommend taking this class with this professor especially if you need bio credits.

reviews.comment: All assignments and tests were organized from the start of class. Lectures were not mandatory and content was always posted on canvas, which was very helpful. Class was interesting and easy to stay on top of, great professor!

reviews.comment: Professor was a little clunky with in-person lectures, but the videos are great and concise. Responds to emails extremely fast and very willing to help. Exams are straightforward and easy. Project can be a little unclear but she is willing to clarify instructions and review your work.

Had her for Mktg 310 and for mktg 305. Class only meets once a week which is nice, and lectures are posted online. Some people didn't love her teaching style, but I personally liked it. Her directions can be unclear on the big group projects so just ask a lot of questions. Exams in 305 were fair, more harsh in 310 but manageable for sure.

I took this as a hybrid class, we never did any lecture content during our in person class. We had to read the lecture (not watch) on our own and either had project workdays or did small activities during the in person time. Stang is very nice and accessible outside of class, just didn't like the structure of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As others have said, this class is extremely memorization-based and all learning is done on your own. Very little is covered during in-person lectures and she does not manage time great, often leaving only 15 minutes or less for group project work. However, the class is well-structured, with clear expectations for lecture and group project pacing.

She is very caring and nice, but I didn't love the class. All the material was online and the one class a week was a discussion, not a lecture. I also felt like most of the material was just a matter of memorizing a ton of vocab, a lot of which was too niche and hardly generally applicable to marketing and consumer behavior. It's manageable though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is fine, but I wouldn't take again with her. All lecture material is done on your own and the class period is spent either doing exercises or working on a group project. Nice that she gives class time to do group project work.

Subject should be interesting but you have to teach yourself everything off her boring slide decks that she expects you to have memorized for the exams (nothing tested on is covered during class). Very vague with instructions for the group project and she wouldn't answer the simplest questions because she "can't pregrade." Overall bad professor.

Instructor Stang was very passionate about consumer behavior. My favorite part about her lectures was her personal experiences that she could relate to the objectives being discussed. As long as you show up and keep up, this class is very manageable. The semester-long group project was often arduous, but it gets better.

reviews.comment: Very boring, basically just memorizing definitions. Usual online busy work discussion and activities. Project is a large percentage of your grade and expectations are unclear

I have had Professor Stang for 2 classes now, Market Research and Consumer Behavior. She is really passionate about marketing and teaching. She cares about her students, but it is up to you to make the effort to connect with her. Choose your group for the project wisely and check in throughout the semester to get a good grade.
The lectures are incredibly boring and the grading criteria incomprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Stangs lectures are incredibly boring. She does a poor job of making the subject remotely interesting, which is difficult considering she teaches marketing. Her class format essentially teaches you to memorize terms and definitions which, while easy, makes the topics even more dull. I have taken two classes with Stang and regretted  both.

Professor Stang cares about the subject matter and her students, but unfortunately is extremely dull in lectures.  Definitely utilize her offer of constant availability, especially with questions on the project.  Make sure to pick a good group for the project, as a bad one will make it stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is a good professor and clearly has a passion for Market Research, but struggles to connect with her students. Her lecture format is fairly boring and hard to pay attention to, but it is not due to a lack of effort. The group project was fairly easy and was graded even easier.
Does not focus too much on the book, and the project is not too hard. Liked it to boost my GPA.

"Blah" is the best way to describe professor Stang and her class.  Despite her enthusiasm for the subject her lectures are painfully boring. There is a semester-long group project that requires a lot of work.  On the upside, Professor Stang is extremely available for help/advice, as she allows you to text her with questions. No final exam.

Great professor, easy to get along with. 50% group project (broken into more manageable parts), two 20% midterms. Lecture/exams are straight out of the textbook, which can make class a bit boring and redundant. The project is interesting -  she's a straightforward and easier grader. Overall,  liked this class: not super stressful and very enjoyable

Professor Powers is a pretty good teacher. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is very accommodating if you have any issues. Lectures are sometimes a little hard to sit through, though I am not a humanities major. It is a easy class to get rid of your ethnic studies requirement.

Actually one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. She is incredibly kind and caring. I am not the biggest fan of history but she made it surprisingly engaging. My TA was also amazing. He helped me with my other classes at the time. Overall would highly highly recommend.
She is a queen. Love her. I hate history, but enjoyed this class a lot.

If you're a STEM major looking for a lib studies class, look no further. Prof Powers genuinely cares about her students and class. She removed one of the main assignments because she didn't want to overload us. You should read the sources each week, if you do the class will be easy. Just a few writing assignments and two papers. Take this class!

While the readings every week sometimes felt lengthy, theres minimal work to pass this class. No exams just a few essays. Powers is the most compassionate and caring prof I've ever had. Gave extensions with no need for reasoning and while attendance was mandatory if you emailed her and explained why you were missing she'd give you the points.

She is a very kind and caring professor. She didn't mind shifting due dates or giving extensions to students. The lectures and readings were very interesting. There wasn't a ton of work for this class. As long as you paid attention and kept up with readings, the quizzes and papers were simple. This class was quite enjoyable.

Prof Powers was amazing and very kind. Her lectures were engaging and interesting. Her ta's were also great and important to get to know. They are very helpful outside class and will prepare you before assignments are due. Overall a great course.

Such a fantastic professor, interesting readings and a great class structure. Very caring and understanding, always looked forward to this class. Learned a lot and would take it again in a heartbeat. Cannot recommend enough!

I had zero interest in the subject matter, so I didn't enjoy the class, but that doesn't take away from the fact that professor powers is fantastic. She is very passionate about history and cares deeply about her students. The essays and quizzes were not difficult. Only take this class if you are somewhat interested in the subject matter though.

Prof. Powers might be the nicest teacher I've ever had. The way she talks to students makes you feel like she cares. Extremely flexible with deadlines and extra credit. Lectures are interesting but required. Graded primarily on attendance, participation, and 4 quizzes given throughout the semester. Would 110% recommend any of her courses.
Amazing professor! Super knowledgable in her field and very inspiring in lectures. She will definitely push you as a historian but gives amazing feedback and will help you grow.
Such an engaging class! He loves what he does and you can tell!! He's an amazing professor and such an interesting course to take!! Definitely recommend!!

Shashko is a very engaging professor who presents material clearly and makes lectures interesting and relevant. The course has three essays plus weekly discussions and readings, all manageable. If you put in effort, you can do well. Attendance isn't required, but notes are graded and not posted. Loved this class.
Such a nice professor and lectures were super interesting!
Lectures are very interesting and entertaining. He is well-spoken and passionate about the subjects he teaches. You will need to take detailed notes on the lectures.

Super interesting lectures. Professor is hilarious and clearly passionate about the class.

Great professor, you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students' understanding. Overall, a pretty easy grader as long as you do your work and follow the rubrics

Amazing professor! He makes every class so fun and interesting that you actually want to attend the lectures (plus you get to listen to some really good music). Attendance isn't taken but you need 20 lecture notes to pass the class-- so go to at least 20 of the lectures (and take notes!) or else you're kinda cooked. No exams, only easy essays.

This man is invited to my wedding. By far the best teacher I have ever had, not just professor. Great office hours and the content is fun and engaging. Lots of students stay after to ask questions and the class is very approachable, mostly because of his enthusiasm about the material. Would 100% take again.
Shashko is incredibly well spoken and is very passionate about his students and class material. Expectations are clearly outlined, and it fairly easy to get an A.

very knowledgeable and is passionate in what he does. class is based on 3 papers, 11 discussion posts and lecture notes. TA's are usually considerate and easy graders. attendance isn't mandatory (for discussion it is) but recommended as he verbally explains the content and doesn't record them. highly recommend if you need an ethnic studies credit!
This class was so much fun! You will learn so much & Shashko is a great professor .

reviews.comment: Shashko is a great professor who is obviously very passionate about music. His lectures are pretty engaging and well-thought-out. The class was very enjoyable and his TAs are pretty laid back as well. The exams are papers but they are not very difficult.

Lectures are not mandatory but he makes them so interesting that makes you want to go. You do need to be at discussions but they are quick. You will write 3 papers that are pretty easy. Such a good class.

By far the best professor I've had at UW. I was actually excited to go to every lecture. The content is fun and interesting, and he is just overall a great lecturer. Make sure to take lots of notes, they will help you with the essays.
I really enjoyed his lectures and the content was interesting. He made me want to continue studying Hip Hop.

This professor is incredibly passionate about the material and even better at conveying the knowledge he has. He will change your perspective on music and history with his in depth lecturing. The grading is very fair and it is not hard to get an A if you interact with the material.

Three papers only. (MAX: 3 pages double spaced-basically nothing) Lectures are out of this world. Hands down the best teacher ever. Take the class!!! (Discussion are easy too, just make sure to do them on time.)

Excellent lecturer and very interesting subject matter.  Expectations are clear and not overwhelming, so the students can relax a bit and absorb everything he's lecturing about.  Even for the 4 week summer course (at 4 times the usual speed), his recommended schedule was easy to follow and helped quite a bit.

Amazing lecturer; very passionate about hip-hop, and you learn so much about the genre and history, along with listening to some great songs during lecture. The papers are very easy to get a good grade on, but they are a large chunk of your grade. Two of the three books are very interesting reads, and the other only requires one chapter.

reviews.comment: Shashko's lectures are amazing. Worth going to all

Hands down the coolest and most entertaining lectures I have been to on campus. Shashko never left me feeling bored or wanting to leave his class as he is an amazing storyteller. With that being said, you will have to read quite a but to succeed on the three papers for this class, but were not entirely difficult. Highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Such a cool professor and so interesting and compelling. He tells a really great story about history and music and the songs are so great!! Best ethnic studies credit.

Professor Shashko is one of the only college professors you will ever have that truly inspires you and makes you excited to attend lecture. Coursework is simple and straightforward. The most knowledgeable people I have ever met regarding music with ability to teach music in a way you had never known before. Great Professor, best at UW Madison

You must take this class! I was genuinely EXCITED to attend lectures. Shashko is amazing and truly cares. Fun class, it was a breath of fresh air. If you're into hip-hop, rap, or R&B, you'll love it. Lecture notes submitted for attendance. Also, stay off your phone- he notices. Take detailed notes during class, they'll really help with the papers.

Super engaging lectures, attendance is checked by submitting notes at the end of lecture but I rarely wanted to skip class. The entire course was super informative and I highly recommend to take. Essay rubric is unclear until explained in discussion, but the essays are super easy to write if you just look over the book and attend lecture.

The essays for this class are a little unclear, but TAs are super helpful in explaining during discussion. You need to turn in notes based on the lectures, but these are pretty easy to take since the topic is so interesting and complex. Amazing combo of lecturing and listening to music.

Shashko is extremely passionate about his lecture material, making the class incredibly engaging and genuinely interesting. Took to fulfill an ethnic studies req and I'm so glad I did. Only a few papers and weekly discussion posts which were graded fair. He plays the music for us in class which can be a nice break from content.
He's the goat. That's it. Literally couldn't say one bad thing about him. You HAVE to take him.

The lecture was a little boring, but the professor did a good job. But some of the grades are being graded by TA, and that's critical. My TA did not write feedback or reply to the email, so the score did not meet my expectations.

Shashko is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met. He is passionate, aware, and clear. The 3 papers you write are short, like 1500 words. Discussion was fun and engaging. He is also very inspirational and so knowledgeable in his work. Highly recommend.

Take this class—you won't regret it! Professor Shashko is simply outstanding. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but you must submit notes for 20 lectures by semester's end. Attend weekly discussions, complete the discussion posts, and write three papers. The workload is manageable and rewarding for anyone who takes it. You will do great!

Shashko is awesome. College professors never try to make college actually fun for the kids like teachers used to do in high school, but this guy does. He brought us all candy on halloween, and that was the only time I've seen a professor go out of their way to do something special all semester. Made my day!
Goat lecturer, super nice guy as well. Papers are annoying but very manageable. Do the papers at a good level and show up, and you will most likely get an A.
the campus is lucky to have him. he's a great storyteller- get in one of his classes if you can.

if you have the opportunity to take a class with this man DO IT. genuinely the kindest professor, with organized note outlines that you fill in during lecture, so u actually listen and appreciate the content you're learning. extremely well spoken and knowledgeable, and i feel like i actually took something away from this class. thank you shashko!!

This man recieved a STANDING OVATION in the final lecture of the semester. What other professors do you know of that have received the same? Incredible storyteller, very knowledgeable. I would always arrive to lecture early where we'd talk one-on-one about life and he'd share his wisdom. Extraordinary teacher, and human being.
Professor Shashko makes the course material engaging. The readings are manageable, and with diligence, an A is achievable. Unstuck ai was a lifesaver for study prep.

Shashko was a dream. I found myself excited to attend lecture and learn from such a passionate and well-spoken lecturer. There are a few papers, one of which is on a relatively short, easy-to-read book. If you block out time to get the writing completed, the class is easy and quite enjoyable with Shashko.

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UW Madison. He teaches unique and interesting courses, has many applicable stories to tell, and has a fantastic taste in music.

I think it was an interesting course. I learned about a ton of great music that I wouldn't have known about otherwise. If you engage in discussions and try on the essays, getting an A isn't too hard. I honestly think this class is a bit overrated. There were some pretty dull weeks and discussions were usually no fun, but I do not regret taking it.

reviews.comment: Great professor

Incredible lecturer. Discussion sections: just show up and talk a couple times per session to get points. No exams, just essays and discussion questions. Essays are more about planning and organizing than writing. Very clear about what needs to be included to do well on essays. Grades do take a while however. Lectures are not recorded. High A rate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Shasko is one of the most inspiring and entertaining professors I have ever had. The way he teaches history is like a story, and a good one at that. He genuinely is passionate in what he is talking about and is overall just one of the best teachers I've ever had. We talk about music, listen to music, and he teaches you about it afterwards.
Shashko is perhaps the most entertaining, most inspirational, and overall best lecturers of all time.
Very passionate about the subject, we essentially just listened to music and he talked about why it is important. If you get the chance, take this course.
He is an amazing lecturer and he is effective at making us care about the content too. The TA's are all great as well. Best ethnic studies class
Definitely the best and easiest class for ethnic study requirement.

Dr. Shashko was amazing last semester! I LOVED his lectures. Great class for an ethnic studies/U.S. history credit. Only really graded by 3 papers, but just generally keep up with the class content/books (skimming is fine) and you'll be just okay! He even gave me a point back on a paper. Super approachable, passionate, funny, and inspirational.
Alexander is one of the best profs I have ever had at this school. Never found myself being bored in lecture. He is an incredible speaker and can make things relevant as well as add fun stories.

Genuinely interesting material and teaches with passion. Good communicator, great way to get your ethnic studies credit with little hassle. Readings not to bad, just give yourself time to work on essays and you'll get an A in the class, hard to sell that bad.

One of the best professors I've had at Madison. He's extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the topics in class. He's also an overall great guy. The class was easy and the lectures were engaging. 75% of your grade is made up of 3 papers, but they're pretty interesting and I got 100% on all three.

Professor Shashko is a great professor who actually cares about his students and what he is teaching. You can definitely get an A in this class. There are 3 papers, all based on books you read throughout the class. There are weekly discussion questions based on the readings assigned. Go to class and enjoy, it's a good getaway from other classes.

reviews.comment: Professor Shashko's class was life changing. He is so passionate about what he teaches, which made this class something I looked forward to every day. Afro-Am 154 is an incredibly interesting class as well, and I would recommend it to every person at UW.

Professor Shashko was amazing. I took AfroAmer272 with him, and have never been so interested in a lecture-based course before. The way he delivers material is so engaging and he explains things clearly. He is so helpful if you have questions and is also super fun to discuss other material with. Great way to get ethnic studies breadth.

Prof. Shashko is a phenomenal lecturer. His passion for this class and for hip hop as a whole is so apparent and very inspirational. This class does have quite a few writing assignments (3 papers, 10 disc. posts) but overall, I would take this class over and over again - if you have the chance (even if you aren't a huge fan of hip hop), take it!!

Shashko is a really cool and nice guy! He is so passionate about what he's teaching and wants you to be too! 3 pretty large essays, but you can do them on your own time and they're not too bad if you go to class and pay attention. Good grader too. Attendance is def mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I was an auditor, so I can't speak to anything regarding his assignments or grading, but this is the best class I've ever taken at this university.  










If you can fit this into your schedule, you won't regret it.  Fabulous class - very engaging material, and he is a great lecturer!!
Excellent lecturer and very knowledgable. I love how he integrated stuff from his class on Black musical history. Three essays and attendance count for your entire grade.

Alexander is easily the best lecturer I have ever had, he is so knowledgeable on the subject and makes this class very interesting. There are 3 big essays and weekly 300 word writing assignments which are all very doable. Take this class if you have the opportunity, you won't regret it.

Afro Amer 154 does not have a lot of room for error when it comes to the # of assignments, BUT he was so nice to make the quizzes only 5 points instead of 10 like originally planned. One of the BEST lecture classes i've taken and he TRULY CARES about us as students. Just take all the notes you can during lecture, make quizlets for quizzes!!

Professor Shashko sticks out amongst all the professors I've had at UW. He is an incredible lecturer and insanely respected. I enjoyed attending his lectures, as he is so knowledgable and obviously cares about what he does. I would recommend this class to anyone.
Goat
awesome class, seriously a must take. two exams worth low portion of the grade, 10 questions each. Go to lecture, listen, enjoy, and easy easy A

If I had to take a class a second time, this would be the class. I enjoyed this class and learned a significant amount of information. Professor Shashko was terrific, and his material had a great structure. There are two comprehension quizzes in discussion and three essays throughout the semester. My TA was also excellent.

He wants his students to do well and is very passionate about his studies. You can tell that he has been teaching for ten years. I struggled with the comprehensive quizzes, but there are only two and other people seemed to think they were fair. Just pay attention to who wrote and did what in the Chang book. He makes the class material interesting.
Wonderful lecturer. Shashko is very knowledgeable about African American History. Class has 3 essays but not a difficult grader.

Absolutely amazing teacher, incredible class. Everyone should take his class. Truly life changing lectures (not mandatory but you HAVE to go because they are so great and we listen to the best music in them). We had 3 essays in total, which were honestly fun to write bc you become so passionate about the music bc of Shashko. So. Valuable.

Literally my favorite class I've ever taken. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Lecture consisted of learning about new artists, events, etc that impacted hip-hop in that era. Got to watch a few music videos every lecture. Discussion was also great, the TAs were super engaging. Workload isn't alot, they grade pretty easy.

By far my favorite class that I've taken at UW. Lectures are super interesting and engaging, you basically just watch music videos and learn about pop culture. Absolutely loved it, Shashko is really cool. Three essays, three novel type textbooks, two comprehension quizzes. Really not a bad workload.
Great professor, Great lectures

reviews.comment: He is easily one of the best professors. He is an amazing speaker and creates lectures that are genuinely engaging EVERY class. Really smart guy, you can tell he knows what he's talking about. Overall great class that I would take again.

Loved the class and Prof. Material and lectures were interesting, fun and engaging so I still went to lecture. Prof is super available outside of class and loves getting to know his students. Alexander Shashko is one of the best professors at UW hands down. His lectures were never really required to attend but I kept going because he kept the material so engaging. AfroAmer154 has been one of my favorite classes at UW-Madison. Professor Shashko is an engaging lecturer and class is very easy to follow. Lecture attendance not mandatory, but discussion was. Shahsko is with zero question the best prof at UW. This class quite literally changed the way I think about the world, yet managed to do it in a way that is incredibly entertaining. He is amazing, and clearly loves his subject.

Literally the best professor here at UW Madison!!! I wish he taught more upper level courses just so I could have him be my professor again. Lectures were HIGHLY engaging and I normally walked out of class learning something new. It was a power lecture but never felt like one. Do yourself a favor and take a class taught by him and cherish it!!!!

Shashko is my favorite professor so far at UW Madison. His lectures are incredibly captivating and I genuinely look forward to class. His lectures feel like ted talks and are always so moving. Shashko is very understanding, aware, approachable, and overall an amazing professor. I would 100% recommend his classes!
One of the most well spoken individuals I have met throughout my life. His lectures are captivating, and he always leaves you excited for the next lecture. Highly recommend any class that he teaches.

The absolute goat. Amazing lectures and always excited to come to class. On top of that the class is very easy on grading and if you put a little bit of time into it you should receive an A. Would definitely take him as a professor again.
Great Professor, the only class I have truly loved and looked forward to attending.

reviews.comment: As all the other reviews say his lectures are some of the best. I didn't want to skip his lectures because they were so interesting. Papers are difficult if you don't go to class and that is what most of your grade is based on. 10/10 would recommend!

reviews.comment: Prof Shashko is super passionate about the material. He makes it engaging and relevant to today's world. Assignments (6 papers) parallel the lecture material. Textbooks are a nice supplement but are not entirely necessary.

Shashko is as amazing as the other reviews say he is. He is easily one of the best lecturers at UW. He knows what he is talking about, his lectures are engaging, and he can answer quite literally any question thrown at him. Attendance was graded and there were a few papers, but he is one of the most understanding professors I think I will ever have
I took this class because I heard it was an easy A, so I didn't expected to be this engaged by the content. Amazing lecturer, really interesting course, highly recommend.

Amazing lecturer who is interesting to listen to and clearly cares about subject. Lectures spent listening to and talking about music. 3 books are "required" for class but you only really need to read one of them. Only 3 longer papers and 3 very short papers for whole semester, graded VERY easily (90-95% class average). Fun class, easy A!

Literally the best lecturer I have ever had! You will sit there for 50 minutes and be so engaged that you will wonder how the time flew by so quickly. Lecture attendance is optional, but I highly encourage that you go. Your grade is based off of 3 essays, but those rely most on the reading. He is such an amazing professor definitely take his class!

Great professor. If you into music you will love this class. Im not the biggest music listen so the beginning of the class was a little dry. 3 big papers and 3 small papers graded very fairly. Definitely take this class with him for for ethnic studies. Also ta is great.

This is the class I recommend for everyone. Interesting, not too hard, you write 3 papers throughout the semster. You can tell he really likes what he teaches (same with the TA's). They are very understanding and I wish I could take this class again.
He is cool.

Best lectures at UW-Madison. Shashko is, hands down, the best professor I have ever had. Please take this class if you have a chance. It is an easy A and will feel easier since the material is so interesting. You will not regret it.

reviews.comment: Honestly, he is one of the most concise, well-versed lecturers at UW. His voice is so impactful, and you can tell how knowledgeable he is. He also seems like a great person. Your entire grade hinges on 3 papers, and that's all done by your TA (a real toss-up). Would avoid until in-person lectures resume.

This class was amazing. There is not a better teacher at this school. Professor Shashko's lectures are engaging and there is no one in the world who knows more about this topic than him. The class is graded based on only like 3 essays that you write throughout the semester. If you can get in, TAKE THIS CLASS.

I picked this class with professor ratings for a course that filled the humanities requirement. I was excited, originally. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely wonderful person. Kind, knowledgeable, interesting. Great in discussions outside of class. Lectures are gripping from start to finish. Everything I wanted in a class and a professor. Only thing is grades are entirely based on 3 exams but if you show up and take notes, you shouldn't have a problem. You'll love his classes. Take them.

This is absolutely the class to take if you need to fulfill humanities requirements. He gives fantastic insight into how the music industry works and the messages being spread. The class is fairly easy but you do have to cram/brain dump for the exams when the time comes. Lots of the questions are random bands/authors brought up in lectures.

Prof. Shashko is incredible. He is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. The lectures are valuable and entertaining. Afroamer 154 was the most enjoyable class I have taken and that was mainly because of him. If you go to class you will get an A pretty easily. Exams are essays in class with the questions emailed out before the exam.

Shashko is an amazing lecturer! He is extremely knowledgeable and makes the course extremely fun with many videos during lecture. There are 4 books to read and 2 midterms and a final essay. Very interesting material and I'm glad I got off the waitlist for this course!

Easily the best lecturer I've ever had. He's clearly incredibly knowledgeable and utilizes this in every lecture. He addresses politically divisive subjects with a wealth of knowledge and prowess and explains each subject in a way that's interesting and easy to understand.

Best lecturer in terms of style that I've ever had. But, he is very misleading on some of his political lectures. Also, the Tricia Rose book he has you read is quite possibly one of the most horrible books ever written.

Shashko has without a doubt been the most interesting and well-spoken professor I've had at UW. Would definitely recommend this class for an ethnic studies requirement, or if you're just looking to fill some credits with interesting material. While the exams were somewhat tough, the things I learned about music definitely make up for it!

Prof. Shashko is very knowledgeable in the field of music history and it certainly shows through his lectures. His slides are a little brief but he makes lectures interesting enough that it is easy to follow along. The class is basically based on 4 things: 2 exams, 1 paper, and discussion attendance. It's a hit or miss class but it's pretty easy.
This was probably the most useful class I have taken at UW, and Shashko is a great professor.
I loved this class and Alexander. So far, he gives the best lectures at UW. Don't really need to read the book, just go to lectures. Engaging and interesting lectures, would strongly recommend.

The overall content of the class was interesting, however you are only graded on two midterms and a final paper. He does not provide a study guide and is not available outside of class.

For an ethnic studies class, this is a must take; especially if you want to know more about the history of Hip-Hop.
do not recommend if you want an easy grade

This was the best professor I have ever had! He gives the most inspirational and exciting lectures in class! He combines music and history in the best ways possible, and honestly is a music genius. reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the university. Very knowledgeable and really knows how to teach a class. Really great guy, even if you have the slightest interest in hip hop you will look forward to every lecture. I am upset it has come to an end, I would definitely take it again if I could.
Really passionate about Hip-Hop and it shows in his lectures. The assigned reading is pretty extensive, but you really just need to get the main idea for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Shashko is easily one of the best professors I've had at UW Madison. He is very knowledgeable about hip hop and his passion for the subject is very evident. His lectures are full of information but are extremely engaging and interesting. Prepare to put in work to study for the exams which are essay questions you receive before hand. 10/10 recommend

The best lecturer at UW. Really made every lecture interesting and keeps the class engaged until the last second of lecture. Since he only uses one slide every class, he forces you to listen and pay attention to what he's saying- and it's worth it. Awesome class with an awesome professor.

Shasko is a lecture heavy professor, but his lectures are great. He gives you a lot of information, but all this can be used for his exams, which are essays. He gives you the possible prompts so he allows you to prepare for it, which was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Shashko is very knowledgeable and interested in the subject. He keeps things interesting and in general, is a pretty relaxed class. Two in class writing exams and one paper. Graded pretty easy as long as you show what you learned in class. I would recommend.

He's an awesome lecturer and it's an interesting topic. However I would NOT suggest this class. It has nothing to do with the professor and everything to do with your TA. There's only a few grades so don't chance it; once you discover what your TA is like it's too late. Do yourself a favor and take an easier ethnic studies class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures were engaging, eye opening, and he made them really fun. He really knew his stuff and not only that, just the way he talks is soothing too. A lot to read but it's not that bad. Essay exam topics are also pretty interesting too. Put in some effort and you will get a good grade. He takes attendance!

Shashko was an incredible professor. Not only did he absolutely understand what hip-hop culture and history, you could tell he was truly passionate about it and it made you care about the class too. There was a lot of reading, but it was all relevant, interesting, and helped you understand the class better.

Shashko is an amazing professor, take a class or more with him at all costs.  Show up, listen to hip hop, and talk about race and society in discussion, pretty great.  He does expect you to do the readings, and there are a lot of them, but they are interesting, but if you don't do them, you aren't in bad shape either.
Best lectures of any class I've taken in college. I recommend Shashko to everyone.
An amazing teacher.  The best professor I've ever had at uw madison.  Take him if you get a chance.

Great class! It's not an "easy-A" as you end up putting a lot of work in the exams, but it's easily one of the most interesting class I've ever taken and I value the information I learned from it. Exams are easy as it's 80% essay, 20% fill in the blank. There's a ton of reading but I gave up on it halfway through the semester and so far it's fine.
Shashko was an amazing professor. He was very knowledgeable about hip hop and his lectures went by very fast and his notes were of good quality. 10/10 would recommended taking Afro Am 154!
Alexander was an outstanding professor.  Every class was interesting and well put together.  I have nothing bad to say about him.

Took this class as an humanities credit, and I liked him so much I'm taking 154 for ethnic studies.  You watch music videos/concerts in class so you can literally see what he's talking about.  Lecture is mandatory, but is flexible if you have a good reason (I hurt my back, and he excused me for a week).  First power lecture I didn't fall asleep in

This has been the most enjoyable class I have taken. You learn a lot, but it is not stressful at all, as the lectures are incredibly clear and informative. Super engaging, and it will stick with me for the rest of my life. I was actually upset the couple times I had to miss a lecture!
Great class, clear speaker, really cares about the topic and is willing to open up and speak. Favorite class so far. Just take decent notes and the essays will be no problem

Very clear lecturer. Great grasp of the material. Did use a documentary as instruction for several classes which is a bit odd but luckily it was a great documentary. Exam grading criteria is not always clear considering the broad spectrum of topics discussed. Really informative class, should be required considering how important this information is

Made what I had thought would be boring material incredibly interesting. We listen to songs in class. It's insane how much I learned about music from Shashko. Tests are 10 short answer questions(20%) + 1 essay(80%). Potential songs for the essay, as well as the exact essay grading criteria are given a week before tests.

Shashko is great! Lecture can get boring, but I learned so much throughout the semester and his class made me think about race in a completely different way. I didn't really keep up with the readings, just waited until the exam prompts and read the book, thinking about the prompt. I'd recommend that to save time. Overall, great teacher.

Shashko is by far one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He knows his stuff and is super engaging. The class is extremely interesting and I looked forward to class every day. You get to listen to great music everyday and hear the stories behind it. If there's one class I'd recommend for a student at UW to take, it would be this one by far!

THE most amazing professor. Really easy class, no hw just 2 midterms and a final BUT even if it was super difficult still would be so worth it. I hate getting up before 11 but I wake up at 8 just for this class, lecture is amazing & even if this wasn't for credit I would still go and take it. Honestly cannot recommend it or him enough. Life changer

Shashko's lectures are extremely engaging and he beautifully links together music from the past and how it has influenced present day music. The material you will take away from this class is truly invaluable; makes you WANT to attend lecture! Truly a once in a lifetime experience. Wish I could take it again.
the class is so amazing and inspiring and i could not even begin to talk about how knowledgeable Shashko is on the topic.  LOVE LOVE LOVE WOULD TAKE THE CLASS AGAIN.

Great professor, very interesting lectures and an overall great lecturer. He is very highly respected in his field, and votes for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. A lot of reading every week, but you can get by without doing it, just read the information that pertains to the midterm prompts (in-class essays).

Shasko is brilliant at teaching history: he causes you to examine the past as an evolution and not as brief, isolated moments. Lectures are well organized and engaging. Midterms are not easy, but he helps you to be well prepared. One long(ish) paper, but on a topic of your choice (and he is very willing to help you). Definitely recommend!!

I chose this class solely because of the reviews I saw on RMP. The class is decent, as is Shashko, but not as great as I was expecting from the reviews.  One of the things I got from this class is how much Shashko hates Ronald Reagan. He spent 2 classes shredding him. It was bizarre. (and I am no republican). Shashko is a hardcore liberal

He's an awesome professor and I actually looked forward to all of his lectures. He keeps things interesting and plays songs every day to help teach the material. The content of the class was super interesting and as long as you attend lecture it's easy to get a good grade.

Lectures are mandatory but so good that I looked forward to them every day. Great, relevant course content that made the class seem like more than just a required ethnic studies. Two exams (comprehensive in-class essays that require prep) and one research paper. Definitely inspired me to take some Afro-American classes in the future.

Best professor I've had at UW.  I took the class just because I needed to, and ended up enjoying it way more than I thought I would.  His lectures are almost story-like, and they give you a great perspective on the material covered.  I will forever recommend this class to everyone who has the chance to to take it.

I signed up for this class as an "easy" ethnic studies because of his prior ratings from past students. Unless you're taking just 12 credits4 classes, that's not the case and consumes much more time than needed. Tests are very comprehensive and only test you on your memorization capabilities because he hands out the prompts ahead of time.

272 is one of the best courses I've taken. It challenges your perspective on race relations and professor Shashko's lectures are extremely interesting. You learn a lot but the lecturers seem informal and almost story like. The essay based midterms were tough but the material was very interesting.
Very strict about attendance, interesting lectures, and very fun to have a class with.
Incredible professor. Lectures are mandatory, but I looked forward to them every week. Material is interesting and course workload is very manageable.

I picked this professor based partly on these ratings, and I was not disappointed. He did a great job making lecture interesting, and I didn't think it would be a class I would like. As it turned out, I looked forward to it. He clearly know what he's talking about in lecture. I have even told my friends they should take this class. It's that good.

Professor Shashko was by far the best professor I've ever had at UW. He's a great lecturer and truly enthusiastic about the material he's teaching. I only used the books for exam prep (which he gives you two of the possible exam questions two weeks in advance). Take this class if you get the chance!

Professor Shashko is one of the most eloquent, knowledgable professors I've had at UW. He is a genius in the field of Black Music and makes learning the material worthwhile. Though exams cover a lot of material (lecture, discussion, books) and studying takes a somewhat serious time commitment, it's 100% worth it for how awesome the class is!

Shashko is awesome! He knows so much about the music he covers and you gain a whole new appreciation for it, plus you get to listen to music in class. Lecture is mandatory and we had to choose a seat for the whole semester but this is a fun class to do to so its not a big deal. Only thing I didn't like was that it's entirely graded by your TA.

While Shashko was one of the best professors I've ever had, the grade is determined by the TA and my TA (Everett) graded the class like it was a 300 level class history class.  Participation was 20% of the grade but he would make you feel stupid if you said something he didn't agree with. Wish I would've taken the class a different semester

Shashko was easily the best teacher I've ever had. He is extremely knowledgable and passionate in this topic. I came into the class not knowing much about what it was all about, but left sad that it was over. The material is so interesting and his lectures kept fascinated every time. Excellent class and an even more excellent professor.

Alex was easiestly the best professor I've had here at the UW. His exams were blue books but were really fairly graded. This course was the one I was looking forward to the least and enjoyed the most. Attendance is mandatory but you wont want to skip them cause their so interesting when alex teaches.
Amazing professor, and even better class. Absolutely love the material and how it was delivered. One of the reasons for one of my best semesters at UW-Madison, Music makes life better.

Great professor and great lectures but the exams  are not the best way to test the material since they are graded by TAs, who were horrible.  Easy enough to get an A/AB, way better than any other ethnic study class.
Incredible professor, incredible class. Don't let yourself graduate without taking this course, period.

BOSS professor. wonderful class that really makes you think about pop culture with interesting material. mandatory attendance, but I wanted to go anyway. Really should keep up with readings for discussion and final exam. the TAs this semester were really bad. Just pray for a nice TA.

Possibly my favorite course at UW. Incredible lecturer with great subject material. Spent class listening to music and talking about its significance. 3 blue book exams and paper. Moderate reading load and easy grading, discussion somewhat useless. Takes attendance in lecture, but you wouldn't want to miss it anyways.

3 in-class blue book essays and one essay out of class. Interesting and easy. Be sure to ask your TA what they look for in an essay (content, structure, etc.) since they will be grading it. Keep up on the readings so you don't have to cram. Out of class essay is very easy. Lecture is interesting

Alexander did a phenomenal job teaching this course. I learned a lot, especially about older black artists and history. Attendance is "mandatory" for lecture, and you sign yourself in, but I don't think it counts for the final grade. His beard was great this semester.

very excellent professor, he really knows and cares about what he is teaching.  I looked forward to going to his lectures, I wish they were every day. The material is interesting, relatable, and not very difficult. This class is a must take.

Shashko is an incredible professor for an equally incredible class. There is never a dull moment during lectures. The lectures are mandatory but you wouldn't want to miss the content anyways. I never read (except for the novel Our America) and pulled off an A. One paper, one midterm, and a final. Take this class or forever regret it.

Shasko is AWESOME! Highly recommended class for ethnic studies or just for interest. Engaging and clear lectures. His passion for the topic shows and the lectures are extremely enjoyable to attend. Must prepare for exams, but otherwise paying attention in class is all that's necessary. Take the class and ENJOY it! I'll miss it next semester!

The best class I have taken in my 4 and a half year pedagogical quest.  You listen to great and meaningful music every day.  I actually miss having class over the weekends.  The text books are engaging and the lectures are full of funny anecdotes and witty one-liners.  Don't waste your time on any other ethnic studies, wait for this one.

Afro-American 156 is the best class ever. You get to listen to amazing music during every class. Shashko is very intelligent and very clear with his lectures. I appreciated him playing the music loud in lectures so that people could FEEL the message of the song, and not chat with a neighbor. If you can get in this class (good luck), take it.

I loved this class and Professor Shashko! Every day was interesting and exciting. His use of videos in addition to the music really helped keep people's attention. The essay exams weren't too bad, but make sure to prepare! I would take it again for fun!

Great class!  Listen to music all class.  Don't buy the books except the one for the paper.  The exams are based on the most important topics and songs in class, so if you take decent notes, you will get an easy A

he is an amazing lecturer.  he explains everything with great clarity, and really engages everyone.  you probably don't have to read all of the books (there are a lot) but they'll definitely help you write good essays on the exams.  the only downside is that he will often show documentaries that will take away from his amazing lectures.

Took this as an ethic studies credit. Great class, interesting material, and an easy A. Merely showing up to class everyday and half paying attention is more than enough to do well. If you have even a fleeting interest in music, this class will rock your world! Awesome professor that really cares about his students.

Easy A or AB without doing the readings! (if you luck out with a great TA, such as David Green). Make sure you talk with your TA in order to understand how they are grading you and what they are looking for, or else you will not be happy with exam grades.

I LOVED this class! I would recommend it to anyone! Attendance is mandatory but who would want to miss his amazing lectures? I wish there was a continuation of the class because I loved it! Take it if you need the ethnic studies because it is worth it. The music is good and the history behind it is so interesting. Shashko is awesome!

I LOVED this class! I would recommend it to anyone! Attendance is mandatory but who would want to miss his amazing lectures? I wish there was a continuation of the class because I loved it! Take it if you need the ethnic studies because it is worth it. The music is good and the history behind it is so interesting. Shasko is awesome!
Awesome

This class is not an automatic A anymore. Attendance is mandatory. 25% of grade is a paper, 20% discussion, 25% midterm, and 30% final. Midterm and final are one essay and a short ID section from readings and lecture. The material is very intersting and I think you should be able to get an A if you put in a decent amount of effort.

One of the best ethnic studies classes!  Super interesting, watch videos, listen to music, and he is a great lecturer.  Don't need to read the book because he already covers everything in lecture.  However, if your TA doesn't agree with your opinion in exams and the essay, you might not get an A.

By far my favorite class at UW.  The lectures are actually fun to go to, because for the most part you are watching and listening to music.  Shashko obviously loves what he does, and hearing some of his stories will make your semester.  You will definitely listen to music differently after you take this class.  Amazing class; just sad it's over!
This was probably the most fun I've had in a class to date. He really knows his stuff and the class is not all that difficult.

This was the easiest class I've taken here, and also one of the most interesting and fun.  You never really use the books for anything except the one for the paper, and it's a wonderful read.  I'd recommend this class to anyone, although it is difficult to get into your first or second year.  Very low workload too

Really good teacher, lectures were really interesting mostly because we got to listen to music for 1/3 of the class.  Exams were easy, and there were a ton of extra credit opportunities.  You don't have to read the book as much as he says you should.

Pretty good lecturer. He doesn't use powerpoints, so you need to take good notes. Passionate about what he does. A few opportunites for extra credit throughout the semester. 2 exams and 1 paper are your grade. 2/3 of each exam is writing an essay about one song. He gives you a list of 10 songs a week in advance and 3 of them are on the exam.
This was an 8 am power lecture, but it was worth waking up for.  Tests are extremely easy. Lectures and readings overlap, but they're both enjoyable. Basically, music.

wonderful class. it's his first year so it's not completely well-organized, but he's extremely passionate and a great lecturer - really interesting and clear. no powerpoint though, so you definitely have to come and pay attention, and take good notes.

Shasko is a dynamic and interesting lecturer! The class is mainly about the civil rights movement and he is passionate about it. Doesn't have powerpoint, so you basically listen and jot down the important stuff! Plenty of reading for three credits but class is generally pretty easy. This is my favorite class taken here at UW!
Very clear and organized, knows what he's talking about, and passionate about the subject.

Just came on here to say how MBA is on piazza. She tells you to look at your notes or answrs your question with another question. I would not be asking a question on piazza if I had not already looked at my notes. RMP won't let me say other stuff but the other reviews shed light on how she is.

Professor Anzovino fails to emphasize important concepts during her lectures and rushes through her slides. You will find a better learning experience on YouTube or through other professors. She is an example of having the knowledge, but not knowing how to teach. I strongly suggest another Ochem professor that understands how to engage students.

Mary Beth is great at teaching organic chemistry. She explains things in a manor that is easy to understand and doesn't just go though lecture material as fast as possible. Her Piazza responses might not be super friendly but neither are any of the other lecturers responses. Don't let other people fool you, she is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not a good lecturer.

Had to select 343, but I had her for 345, which is O chem 2. Coming from being in Lampkin, and watching mainly BJE lecture videos, she has a lot of trouble teaching content. She goes extremely fast as well, and doesn't explain content to understand concept.
My 12 year old sister would have been able to teach this class better
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For the lab course you don't really see the professors only the TAs but trying to get help from the lab directors was basically impossible and when you used piazza her responses were rude and unhelpful. It seems as if she doesn't like teaching.
Mary Beth is really mean and condescending on Piazza. Never actually answers your question and instead answers it with another question.

Very inconsiderate when it comes to personal problems and is not willing to accommodate even if something extremely important and possibly life altering pops up. Would highly recommend not taking her, she does not seem to care what happens in your personal life and only cares about following rules they came up with to a T.

rude and condescending during lecture and over piazza. i only understood things after watching other lecture videos, as despite the fact that they were supposedly teaching from the same material, i noticed that she would skim over or completely not mention large important concepts. dont bother going to lecture if you have her.

In the beginning of the semester the class was full but slowly dwindled down to 40-50 kids. She talks through her lecture slides and rambles. She knows what she's talking about but fails to explain it in a way that helps you understand it. Try to get any other professor for your own sake.

She is amazing don't let the other reviews fool you. I've loved her for Ochem 1 &2. Lectures were helpful and her office hours are so so helpful. Anyone who struggles with her likely isn't a problem with the professor but rather the student,
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely the worst out of the 4 possible lectures in my semester. Her lectures were all over the place and I never knew what I was supposed to be learning/studying. Was super passive aggressive and short in her Piazza and email responses. The only thing that got me through this class was being able to watch other lectures' videos.

Her lectures were not as insightful as other professors, and she often rarely looked up at her students and would not go in-depth into topics. Additionally, she was very passive aggressive over piazza and did show much respect to her students, especially over email. It was pretty obvious she was not that passionate about seeing us succeed.

Is a nice person, but outstandingly unhelpful O-Chem professor. Class size started with around 300 kids, then dwindled to about 50 within the first week, and many of those 50 wished they switched when they could have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why people rate her so badly, but I thought she was great! She can definitely seem passive-aggressive and come off as rude through Piazza, but besides that, she was great at explaining things, answered questions well, and was very clear. She had a good sense of humor, and I was always interested in her lectures!

I didn't have her as my professor directly however she answered many different questions on piazza due to being in the quad. She is incredibly condescending, does not give feedback, and clearly does not care about the success of any of her students. Avoid if you can!
Terrible lecturer. Even less helpful on Piazza.
Not welcoming nor helpful when asked questions. Does not seem to respect students either. I would highly request trying to switch professors if you get her.

The course is fast paced, so don't be surprised when you miss key information and forget reaction mechanisms.  That being said, Dr. Anzovino lectures fast but will take questions.  She tends to be a stickler in Piazza; it can be difficult getting answers from her online.  However, she is a lot more friendly during her in-person office hours.

This professor was very rude and unhelpful. She never answered questions on Piazza. She either answered questions with a question, or she straight up told you that you were wrong with no helpful direction. She goes silent during lectures when she writes mechanisms and does not explain anything; she just copies her notes. Don't recommend

I didn't even have her as a professor. She just sucks at answering piazza questions. She answers your questions with basically the same question you just asked so you get nowhere. This happened TOO many times that I'm now forced to leave her a horrible rating bcuz y be a teacher if you DONT TEACH. THANK GOD i don't actually have her as a teacher

Imagine a professor who reads directly from the prepared slides each day and hardly answers students' questions thoroughly. This is MBA. Her style is incredibly one-dimensional and actively curbs every student's curiosity.

One of the most uncaring, inaccessible professors I have had at UW-Madison. You would think that if you went into teaching you would have some semblance of empathy, but she doesn't. Be prepared to be treated like just another number instead of an actual student.

She is the worst professor I have ever had. Was extremely rude and condescending on piazza offering no help towards the students. Often times she will even answer questions with a question! I recommend doing anything in your power to not take her class.

She was quite rude and inflexible throughout the entire semester with piazza posts and assignments. Do not recommend to anyone for 345, and do not even try to attempt to reach out to her in 344 with questions because they will not be helpful.

My main problem with her is that she is rude and super unaccommodating to students' needs.  I have 3 final exams within 24 hours and she refused to let me reschedule my 344 final, despite me telling them that I literally have the ENTIRETY of finals week open outside of that 24 hour period.  Also is rly unhelpful when answering students' questions.

Often lectures were repetitive, unclear, and monotonous. Other students and I would go to other lecturers during their office hours to get proper instruction. Lacks flexibility and care for students. Due to this, I especially do not recommend her to neurodivergent students. If you can, I would switch lecturers.

Amazing!!! I would drop every other class I've had and take a full schedule of nothing but classes with Finn heavily. He cares deeply and has a deep knowledge of what he's talking about. This was also part of a Queer Activism and Art in the 20th century FIG, which I also highly recommend.

Extremely caring about every student in class, Finn changed major parts of the syllabus to account for something that students wanted to spend more time and depth on and offered assistance the whole way.

Finn is a really awesome Professor. You can tell he is really passionate about what he is teaching, and he only cares that we learned. There was quite a bit of reading and many papers, but they tended to be open-ended and about graded very kindly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Finn is a caring and great teacher, however, this class is poorly structured. There are 7 writing assignments that end up being 5-10 pages each. So much work and are graded with a single letter grade and no feedback. Lectures are basically unstructured with no slides, you have to write everything down that's said or there's no way to get it.

Finn is the most caring and impactful professor i've ever had. There are plenty of papers, but the feedback is helpful and they are very fair in their grading. I recommend doing the readings as consistently as you can, because all of the test material is specifics from the readings. Overall amazing class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This class absolutely changed my life, Finn is a phenomenal professor. Because this class was a seminar, it was long, but so worth it. Reading responses were due each week, and we had to present what we wrote, so participation and reading was essential. If you put something into this class, you will get a lot back.

Finn is phenomenal. Although the lectures sometimes seemed to be unstructured at times, all the points Finn made came around and connected in the end. Finn is one of my few professors that I can say that I like and respect. I really hope to take another class with them one day. Papers and readings are long, but helpful and worth it.

Finn's Borderlands & Embodiment class is life-changing. She always values your views and assigns very readable books. Speaking up at discussion is essential. Despite heavy reading and writing workload, class never felt like a burden. One of the best classes you can take at the UW.

Finn is absolutely the best professor I've ever had. I've taken 2 classes with her now, both life-changing. I would definitely recommend her to anyone looking for new ways of thinking and to gain some self-insight. She's amazing.

Such an engaging lecturer. I had no prior knowledge or experience in the subject matter, but Finn's enthusiasm and passion was imparted to us all during lecture.Finn is definitely knowledgeable and can be considered an expert on the subject. Take a class with Finn at least once in your time here you won't regret it. Easy A!!!

all exams were take home essays, graded by TA though. amazing professor who truly cares about students and is so deeply interested in the material. my favorite class of the semester, would love to take another class with Finn!

History of Sexuality: This is a PhD-level class, and _a lot_ of work, but absolutely worth it. Prof. Enke did not speak much; the class ran the discussion. One benefit-students from all departments take this, so perspective were varied. Undergrad or grad--take a class with Enke before you graduate.

Finn Enke is spectacular. She facilitates excellent discussions, chooses awesome reading and produces innovative, original scholarship. She's well respected by students, staff and professors.
