reviews.comment: CS544 is the worst course I have taken during my college.

Honestly, I strongly advise you to think twice about taking this course if you're planning to pursue internships, research opportunities, or simply want to have a life. So many things I CANNOT SAY HERE.

CS544 HAS BEEN MY WORST NIGHTMARE OF A COURSE. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!! 5 EXAMS(because the IPQs weight 10% each), and projects take so much time for only 3% each. Projects are disorganized with overwhelming changes. Teaching team does not care about their students.
He invites the paid TA to remove comment here

Tyler cares a lot about students and has made a course that prepares people for industry. While I'm not the biggest fan of his grade weighting/breakdown for Fall 2025, his reasoning for many decisions with the course make sense and he takes feedback into account. Gets through dense material in lecture well. Course is still quite easy IMO.

For 544, the course design is rough: two 30-minute quizzes at 10% each, no past quizzes, and a graph-drawing section that's 5% of the total grade. The project is also far too long (~15-20hrs) for just 3%. It's so hard you'll likely lean on AI to finish and end up learning nothing. Do not take this class unless they fix the structure.

In lectures, Tyler talks as if he is a professional auctioneer and it is impossible to keep up with everything he is saying. The course covers so many topics that reviewing for the 5 different exams takes a very long time. There are in person grades worth 10% each and they reuse questions for both lectures so the second lecture has a big advantage.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures move far too quickly, with excessive time wasted on demos instead of clear explanations. Projects are overly difficult compared to what's taught and lack proper guidance. The in-person quizzes are unfair since both lectures get the same version, giving later students an advantage and creating unequal testing conditions.
Seems like he's so determined to stick to all these changes despite students' advice

5 Exams 
WOAT-Worst Of All TIME
Worst Class Ever

I would strongly recommend that you consider the workload of other courses since we don't even have one heavy course. Decide to take this course because of good comments, but add more exams. He seems to fix projects at the beginning of the semester, so lots of bug and update. He should test his course during the summer, including bugs and workload

Since Fall 2025, two in-person quizzes are added and each of them is account for 10% of the final grade. What is worse is that there are writing sections that require you to draw out some diagrams shown in the lecture. The questions are really confusing, but Tyler just don't tell you what they mean. Projects only count for 24% of the grade LMAO :(

Since 2025 Fall, I can say this is the POOEREST CS course that I have taken in my life. 5 exams, many projects with infinite revisions of autograder. Chaos lectures, automatical 1.5x speed. Creating new questions on exam without prior experience and examples. Don't want students successed. A good person, but a unsuccessful teacher

I felt that the class tried to cover too much material, and at times it felt a bit unorganized. It would have been more effective if the content was structured more clearly, rather than touching on many disconnected topics. That said, Tyler was a very good professor and did a great job teaching the material.

The class might be useful. The good things are mentioned by other comments. To me, it tries to cover too many things and Tyler did not make sense of much of them during the class. As someone without much system background, it is easy to get confused. I would still recommend it because of the skill you learned. But his lecture can be confusing.

Great intro course for undergrads. The course has a nice balance between theoretical and practical knowledge. Can't thank more for Tyler preparing hundreds of flashcards for reviewing. He also provides constant and sufficient help for your personal projects outside the course. Tyler is an absolute rare-find.

One of the most organized and communicative professors Ive had. Very knowledgeable about Big Data fundamentals and industry practices. Very supportive of students using content for their own projects. Lectures are not extremely engaging but are clear and organized. Lectures recorded but attendance tracked with tophat. Grades curved. Really caring

Tyler is extremely knowledgeable on the topics he teaches and is always willing to take more time to explain things outside of lecture. His way of helping on projects is unique in that he tries to guide students to debugging themselves instead of just telling them which has helped me learn the material better. Well organized lectures with examples.

Super-smart himself, not good at teaching.

His lecture is pretty good but not helpful for any homework. He always give extra reading such as python documentation and tend to be like "be up to you."

Tyler is probably the best professor I have had. He teaches concepts well and is extremely knowledgeable. He is always willing and eager to answer questions whether it be about the class or beyond. He is also caring for his students and makes it clear that he wants us to succeed.

Best instructor ever. Supportive and caring to students' mental health. His course was supportive and the most organized compared to other CS courses. The course website has a lot of materials for study and he will upload recordings of every lecture to the website. In terms of the project being hard, he would do a demo in the lecture and upload it.

Their lectures were extremely fast-paced, but they repeated everything 3 times, so repetition eventually helps you remember it. The exam she wrote was very straightforward and fairly easy. Probably the best out of the 3 lecturers I had this semester. Finished lecture early pretty often, so that was nice. Slides are clear and easy to follow
Exams are tricky; one incorrect word makes it wrong. Extra credit is impossible. Do not take this course.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE if you don't need it. I will never take another evolution course again because of her. She's not accessible outside of class, she relies on students to help each other out (tutor/tutees) using this system as a cop out to help students who are struggling. She is condescending and belittling. Exams are unnecessarily tricky.

She is all over the place when she lectures and has about 90 slides per lecture. It was unclear on what we were tested on and some questions were mainly to trick us. You really dont need the book at all, I rented it but opened it twice. Overall learned some fun facts but was HELLA confused most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She wouldn't take responsibility for problems that were her fault, and she blamed it on technology. She is extremely ableist, joking on multiple occasions that "without autism, we wouldn't have any math geniuses". She is condescending and belittling to students, and when a student offers a correction or different opinion, she dismisses it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've ever had. Prof Lee does not make directions/lecture material clear, cannot work technology (which is great for online class), repeats slides several times throughout lecture. Did 100% quizzes only to get below average on exams as exam questions were tricky and multiple choices could've been correct. DO NOT TAKE CLASS W HER!

I hate to be this person but this was honestly the worst class I have taken in my 3 years at UW. Prof. Lee was grossly disorganized and lectures were hard to follow. 20 minutes before our first exam Prof. Lee emailed us saying she was unable to upload the exam and it will be rescheduled to later in the week. Can't do that during midterms.

She is one of the worst professors I have had. She talks in circles, asks questions and doesn't answer them, allows talkative kids take over the class, is not accommodating to anyone (even with the death of a parent), she is rude, and I would never take this a class with her again. Oh and she doesn't know how to work technology well so online sucks

Very lecture heavy. Wouldn't recommend going but can be helpful sometimes. Often goes overtime because she gets distracted by student questions. Very, very unprofessional: 1. Pushed a test back two days when the exam was supposed to start in 30 min. 2. Wouldn't allow extra time on assignments for my friend when her family member suddenly passed.

Dr. Lee's powerpoints are unnecessarily repetitive and confusing. She will frequently have two slides right next to each other say the same exact thing. Her tests have a lot of questions that ask 'which of these is the most correct', confusing wording, and a few questions that required memorization of specific details or info not in slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lee was one of my all time favorite professors! If you only go to lecture and really pay attention, you will pass. I didn't do any of the readings after the first 2 weeks of class, and I still did just fine. The tests are all about concepts and patterns, so make sure to go to discussion if anything because the handouts are really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The only time you'll need the textbook is for 2 HW assignments. It's definitely possible to get an A without doing the "required" textbook/literature reading. Exam questions test the ability to understand concepts, rather than straight up memorization. She gets on tangents easily, but everything you need to know is emphasized on the lecture slides.

Lee is a pretty good professor, who knows the material well. She lectures incredibly fast, so you have to take notes about what she's saying, not what's on her slides. She's funny at times, and likes to ask the lecture questions in person, not via clicker.  She says her test won't try to trick you and it doesn't.

Carol is down to business, but a good professor. She is clearly very smart, and her curtness can be funny.  Tests are slightly challenging, but fair. The evolution was not what I expected, it was not very interesting, but she is straightforward and teaches the material well.

Of the three professors for the course, she was definitely my favorite. All the information we needed to know was presented clearly, which is something I can't say for the other lecturers. You will definitely LEARN during her lectures. Her test questions are badly worded though, so watch out for that

Dr. Lee goes through her lecture slides very quickly, but she is crystal clear on what she expects her students to know. She emphasizes key points and essentially everything you need to know is on her slides. Her lecture slides and sample questions are a nice way to study. However, the exam did have a few tricky questions.
Shes is an annoying person. Her lectures are disorganized and hard to follow. Her exam had so many trick questions.
I like her and I understand her lectures, I'm more used to her style of lecturing and explaining things. But her test is really a sad story to me, though she's so hot.
Confusing lectures. she skips around a lot and goes on unrelated side tangents. very tricky exam questions.

Highly recommended. Professor Lee's lectures are very engaging. Her academic interests are varied (evolution, ecology, anthropology, genetics) and this often adds richness to the subject material. Definitely look into her research area (rapid evolution).  If you know how to take good lecture notes and how to study well, then you will do just fine.
Pretty cool lectures and wicked smart.

She is very smart and tries her best to explain the concepts but isn't the best at it.  The test questions are very tricky so you will need to COMPLETELY understand the class material in order to do well on the tests.

She is energetic and wants students to succeed, but her class is not curved at all, making it difficult to get an A. She goes on many side rants, which although interesting, do not coincide with the tested material. Her hw is not very helpful. Most of the test questions come from the slides. The e.c. is minimal. Bio & genetics background helpful.

Carol is a very energetic person but she is not a very good professor. She doesnt make her expectations clear and does an awful job explaining things. She obviously tries very hard but just doesnt understand that learning is more about studying. She is also a horrible test writer as her questions dont have clear answers. I would not take her again.

Dr. Lee makes lectures extremely interesting and worth attending, even though attendance isn't technically required. She posts her powerpoints online before class (extremely helpful) and really WANTS her students to succeed, which she emphasizes. She reviewed key concepts over and over until they were difficult to forget. Overall, great professor.

Carol is a very clear, interesting lecturer - I did not have a strong genetics background for this class and did well (but be sure to review basic bio). She reads from her slides (which are crammed with words). Exams logical and require learning concepts and applying them to exam questions. Extra credit opportunities & optional discussion.

Lectures/textbook unnecessary.  Power points contain all information needed for exams.  ***Exams are well-written for a logical mind, but merely memorizing the material will NOT suffice***.  Extra credit opportunities are tutoring other students,  leading discussions, and extra questions on 2nd and 3rd exams.

I liked Dr Lee a lot! I come from a bio/genetics background so perhaps things were a bit clearer to me than other commenters have noted. She is very interested in her field and she tries to get us to think like scientists which I like. Exams are rather tricky if you don't REALLY understand the concepts. A basic understanding isn't enough.

Class doesn't require chem or genetics background, but it should. Very genetics-based. Boring lecturer, more than half the class stopped coming. Terrible test writer, the questions are overly complicated, and she emphasizes different things in lecture than what she tests on. Take with a different prof if possible.

She is a great teacher who is very passionate on what she teaches. She made everything very easy to understand, and I felt as though I understood everything right after lecture without even studying it. However, her exams are kind of difficult. There are a lot of "which of the following is NOT" which means you have to know 4 that are.
The biology department at whole seems kind of out of touch, but she explains things clearly and eloquently and just seems more put together overall.
One of my favorite lecturers at UW. She made class interesting and enjoyable.

I have to disagree- I think she is one of the best test writers I've ever had! If you attend lecture that's all you need to do to ace the exams- the questions are about understanding the material not memorizing useless terms from the lecture slides. She occasionally goes off on tangents but otherwise a very good lecturer.

Dr. Lee is an amazing Lecturer. She has a ton of experience in evolution and will keep you interested in what she's talking about. She doesnt require much reading or memorization. Going to lecture is necessary, but it is enjoyable. However, her exam was extremely difficult, a lot of tricky wording and similar choices. Good lecturer, bad exam writer

Clare is the first professor I've had where she leaves a comment on every single assignment. She actually listens to her students and understands how we think and feel. Shes very understanding and a phenomenal role model. I highly reccomend taking her.

I LOVE PROFESSOR HADEN! Despite this class being entirely asynchronous online, she always had extremely productive and kind things to say in her assignment reviews and always kept me motivated to work hard (and she always graded things freakishly fast, like sometimes within hours. Very useful.) Would recommend her to ANYONE.

Professor Haden is the best. Completely virtual/no lecture class but she is always extremely active on Canvas and online to grade everything extremely quick. Nothing more to say: we need more professors like her.

Clare is THE BEST!!! Wanted an easy course for two credits, but ended up learning so many tools that have helped me become a better, more confident speaker. She really cares about her students and always leaves personalized, inspiring feedback. A great course to take even if you're not into theatre. Assignments vary every week and are super fun!!

As long as you show up and do your best on the work, this is an easy, fun class. Clare is bright, funny, and passionate. She cares about her students and is very flexible about all skill levels and interests in theatre. Readings are fairly short, writing assignments are short and informal, and due dates are easily met. Great extra class to take.

Professor Haden is one of the kindest people I have ever come in contact with, she gives great feedback on every assignment and is always there if you need her. The class was super simple and engaging thanks to her!

Clare is the sweetest woman! She truly wants her students to succeed and she will do all she can to help you succeed in her class. I have no interest in theatre but the content in this course is applicable to other ares of life. Easy A and felt like less than 2 credits worth of work.
Such a great class! definitely take it with her if you can. I learned so much

We had to do two monologues for 240. We also did many physical and vocal activities. Clare does a great job at making everyone feel comfortable and included while at the same time pushing them to grow and experiment and try new things. She is also really good a balancing a class between theater and non-theater majors. She is very caring/helpful

Clare made me feel very comfortable in this class despite my limited background in theatre and public speaking. She was constantly challenging us to grow and learn more and gave excellent individual feedback. We also did a lot of movement, yoga, and meditation in addition to vocal work. I'm still using things she taught me 1.5 years later!

Clare is an absolutely amazing teacher. Her teaching method is beyond fantastic, and what she teaches is applicable to outside the realm of theatre. She really puts a lot of effort into her craft, personalizing the major assignments towards both pushing boundaries and helping us shine in our roles. This class was easily the best class I've taken.
She is so great! I learned a lot!
Clare is so great. Even I am not major in theater, her lectures inspired me to take more theater classes. I had so much fun and learned a lot. She is helpful. She is amazing!
She is amazing. If she is an option as a professor, always pick her. She is very helpful, engaging, and caring. Loved every second of the class.

If anyone is looking for any fun course and don't know what course to take, take this. You won't regret I promise. Instead, you will thank me. Amazing professor! You'll crave for every class to come and you won't want to miss any class because it's so much fun and learning experience.  Work in the class: Have fun in the class! I am not kidding!

Clare is an amazing teacher; by far one of my favorites during my college career. Her enthusiasm is awesome. Taking her class is fun and also connects to how you can use your breath, voice, body, and mind altogether!
Clare is so fun! She truly wants to help all students succeed. She is very enthusiastic about theatre and teaching, which is great!

Clare makes everyone feel comfortable and welcome. This class was an early morning class, but it was a great start to my day. Clare is very friendly and helpful. Anyone can benefit from her voice training classes, not just an actor or theatre and drama major. Highly recommend.

Clare is so awesome! She's talented, and always enthusiastic about theater, especially teaching. She's great about helping students individually and is honestly one of the nicest people I've ever met. The class is fairly easy, and a lot of it is physical participation (stretching, etc.). Papers and performances are helpful and easy.

Clare is one of the most amazing teachers to ever come through this department.  She actually makes learning enjoyable and you want to come to class everyday.  She really encourages students to focus in on what is going on in the class and believe me, you will DEFINITELY benefit.

When I say DO NOT take this class I mean it. You are graded by four essays in which no rubric is provided at all. He grades them like he has to prove how much smarter he is than you. He will correct things one version and ignore them in the next it makes no sense. He is on a genuine power trip the whole lecture. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In my four years at UW-Madison, I've never had a professor as terrible as professor Close. He provided no positive feedback on papers and created a really uncomfortable class environment. Participation is mandatory (he marks down how many times you participate) but if you don't agree with him he will give you lesser marks. Stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was my second time with Profe Close and I really like his teaching style! Each class you read one piece and then a group presents and there's a class discussion during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The movies we watched in class were horrid, and we had to write a paper for each film. He does pop quizzes in class, so be prepared for that. He also has a clipboard that marks how often you speak in class. This class is a LOT of work. Try to take another class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you're not willing to work hard. Exams are heavily essay based and mc often are unnecessarily specific. He ranks people on participation which at times can be stressful. However, most people in the class struggle w/ exams, and it will be accounted for in the final grade. You'll learn a lot and he's a nice guy overall. :)

Professor Close might be the most pretentious professor I have encountered in college thus far. He provides no positive feedback, and his comments on writing seem as though he is just trying to show how smart he is. You learn about interesting content but then are assessed on narratological knowledge instead of class content. Stay Away !!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Close was a really great professor! He tailored the class often to our interests and fostered really interesting discussions. He also gave amazing and super detailed feedback on all of our assignments and went out of his way to provide extra resources/advice to strengthen our writing and our own personal interests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Glen is a very kind and caring professor. However, his class is structured in a way that is not designed to succeed. For participation (20% of your grade), you must speak in class while he tallies your responses on a clipboard. Exams were very long and all short answer and hand-written. The class is a lot of reading and work, but Glen is very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you need to take this class with him for Spanish credit, choose an independent study instead. Easily the worst class/professor I have experienced in the Spanish department. Forced participation, reduced grade if camera is off, heavy points off for minor grammar errors, and much more about his teaching style will make you want to drop.

Prof. Close was a great choice! Took Spanish film with him and enjoyed the content alot, but the reading assignments were too long for a T/TH schedule. Takes about 2-3 hours per lecture of prep reading. Attendance/participation is mandatory. He keeps a record how often you speak in class. Picky with grading content on essays (8 total in course).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor who actually cares if you learn the language or not. Class goes by fast and topics aren't boring. definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I have excelled in all of my previous Spanish courses receiving nothing lower than an A, but this class was an exception. I felt that he never provided clear grading rubrics or instructions for what he actually wanted. He called me culturally insensitive for giving my honest opinion about the awfully boring movies that he made us watch. STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: As senior (who has never gotten below an A in a Spanish class), I can confidently say that Glen's class was the worst I've taken had in all 4 years. Grades are based on weekly essays and pop quizzes. Lectures lack relevancy. He tallies your participation each day on a clipboard. Gotta give the guy some grace but MAN, his class was rough.

This is one of the better professors I've had. He cares about the subject matter, and fosters interesting discussion. Make sure you speak up because participation is a must, but he is easy to approach and non-intimidating. The class was very interesting about film in Latin America; we watched movies, wrote mini papers, and never had an exam!

Great professor. Truly cares about his subject and it shows. Makes class interesting with music and video clips. Study main points talked about in class for exams, easy essays, must talk in class to get an A (but he is not judgmental and if you say something stupid he will turn it around for you).

high expectations, but still grades fair. will help if you ASK and answer emails promptly. dificult material: reread before class! relies too heavily on pwr pt, but posts it online after class. you MUST speak up in class to get a good grade. exam questions kinda come outa left field, so go in a talk to him before if you are unsure of things.
No Comments

A genuinely nice guy. He answers questions very thoroughly and appreciates participation, even if you get an answer totally wrong, he's nice about it. The class is really boring, though, the material and his way of teaching. Papers are easy A's but exams are a little tougher.

I don't think he was the worst professor ever, but I definately was not interested in the material. He chose to play music from various hispanic cultures at the beginning of class, which I thought was fun and educational. I guess it's a good class for a requirement, but he wasn't my favorite prof.
Very dense, but clear, lectures. Be careful of time on the exams. Easy papers. He can be dry at times, nevertheless I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.
BORING lectures, not even necessary to attend.  Discussion is important... tests are HARD!  Study up!  Papers are easy A's.

His lectures are boring as hell and he presents the most random crap. He is not interesting to listen to and the midterm was hard as hell, but the other stuff isn't so bad. I could hardly stay awake during lectures, though. Discussion is what got me through this class.
Challanging course, but he made sure that everyone's questions were answered. Not too hard to get good grades on papers if you go and talk to him - super approachable and willing to offer advice.
Your habit of constantly jingling the keys in your pocket is incredibly distracting. Please empty your pockets before you start lecturing.
Stop making the final exam a surprise format. If the midterms were multiple choice, the final shouldn't suddenly be five long-form essays.
Your habit of sighing loudly when a student gets an answer wrong completely destroys their confidence and stops others from participating.
Please stop holding mandatory events outside of the scheduled class time. We have jobs, families, and other classes to attend.
You need to be more responsive on Canvas messages. If you prefer email, tell us, but don't just ignore the messages sent through the portal.
Stop making us buy physical copies of novels that are in the public domain. We can read them for free online.
Your exams focus entirely on rote memorization of definitions rather than our ability to actually apply the concepts to real scenarios.
Please stop using red font on your slides. It is incredibly jarring and very difficult for colorblind students to read.
You need to actually explain the theory before jumping into the complex math. We need the foundational "why" before the "how."
Stop making assignments that require us to use our personal social media accounts. We have a right to privacy.
Please stop making sarcastic comments
You need to provide a clear breakdown of how the final grade is calculated. Is it total points? Weighted categories? The syllabus is unclear.
Stop making us write essays on topics we haven't covered in lecture yet. We cannot analyze material we haven't been taught.
You need to be more concise in your lecture delivery. You take twenty minutes to explain a concept that could be summarized in five.
Please stop talking over the video clips you show in class. We can't hear the documentary if you are narrating over it the entire time.
You need to actually test your Canvas quizzes before assigning them. Half the questions had the wrong correct answer marked in the system.
Stop making us pay for a textbook that you wrote, especially when you only assign two chapters out of the entire 500-page book.
Your habit of drastically changing the syllabus schedule right before finals week creates massive, unnecessary stress for everyone.
Please stop reading off your notes with your head down. Make eye contact with the class to actually engage us in the material.
Your policy of dropping a full letter grade for one unexcused absence is entirely too rigid for a class of adult learners.
Please stop using highly offensive historical terms without providing the proper academic context and trigger warnings first.
You need to be more aware of the classroom temperature. If the AC is broken, prop a door open or move us to a different room.
Stop making us do group work in a massive lecture hall. We can't hear our group members over the noise of 200 other people talking.
Your exams are entirely based on the lecture, yet you refuse to record them or post the slides. This heavily penalizes visual learners.
Please stop ignoring emails that ask for homework extensions due to illness. A simple "yes" or "no" allows us to plan our recovery.
You need to provide clearer instructions for the peer review process. Giving a fellow student a grade requires a very specific rubric.
Stop making assignments due on university holidays. If campus is closed, the Canvas dropbox should not be due that night.
Your habit of ending class 15 minutes early every day means you are shortchanging us on the education we paid for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please stop pacing back and forth so rapidly. It is visually exhausting and makes the entire front row dizzy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You need to actually return our graded exams. We can't learn from our mistakes if we are never allowed to see what we got wrong.
Stop making us print out the syllabus. It is a 15-page document that we can easily reference online whenever we need it.
Your lectures completely lack visual aids. Incorporate some diagrams or charts to help the visual learners in the room.
Please stop using a grading scale where an 89.9 is a B+. If a student is that close, round it up.
Stop making us memorize exact dates for a philosophy class. We need to know the concepts, not the year the philosopher was born.
Your grading on group projects is incredibly unfair to the students who end up doing 90% of the actual work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please stop talking down to students who ask clarifying questions. If they are asking, it means your initial explanation wasn't clear enough.
You need to provide a clear explanation of what will be on the final. "Everything in the book" is not a valid study guide.
Please stop using multiple-choice questions where the difference between option A and B is a single comma.
You need to actually read the syllabus you gave us. You keep contradicting your own written policies during lecture.
Stop making us use lockdown browsers that flag us for cheating just because a roommate walked past the door in the background.
Your policy of strictly enforcing a 100-word limit on discussion posts completely stifles any actual intellectual debate or deep analysis.
Please stop holding class the day before Thanksgiving. Nobody is going to show up, and you are just penalizing the students who went home early.
You need to provide more comprehensive feedback on our coding assignments. Telling us "it didn't compile" doesn't help us fix the syntax error.
Stop making the midterm exam worth 50% of our grade. If we have a bad test day, our entire semester is completely ruined.
Please stop refusing to answer questions about the homework during class. If the whole class is confused, it warrants a five-minute discussion.
You need to be more clear about the parameters of the final presentation. Are we supposed to dress formally? Use slides? We need details.
Stop making us buy a custom binder for the lab manual. A standard three-ring binder is a fraction of the cost and works exactly the same.
Your exams heavily feature trick questions. Test our knowledge of the material, not our ability to navigate linguistic traps.
Please stop showing up to class ten minutes late. It shows a complete lack of respect for our time and our tuition dollars.
Stop making us do icebreakers that require physical contact. It is highly uncomfortable and completely inappropriate for a college classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Your grading curve is a complete mystery. You need to publish the formula you use so we can actually track our progress.
Please stop making sarcastic comments about the students' generation. We are trying to learn, not be insulted for our age.
You need to actually supervise the group projects. Don't just assign them and disappear until presentation day.
Your habit of going on twenty-minute tangents about your personal life completely ruins the pacing of the lecture.
You need to be more approachable. Your resting face is very stern, and it makes students terrified to ask for help when they are struggling.
Stop making the final exam cumulative if the class is completely modular. What we learned in August has nothing to do with what we are learning in December.
Your exams test our reading speed more than our actual knowledge. Give us enough time to actually read and process the complex word problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please stop giving us assignments that are clearly just busywork. We want assignments that actually reinforce the complex concepts of the lecture.
You need to actually answer the questions on the discussion board. Letting students answer each other often results in the spread of misinformation.
Your habit of sighing heavily when a student asks you to repeat something creates an incredibly toxic and intimidating classroom environment.
Please stop scheduling office hours during the exact time our lab block is scheduled. We literally cannot attend your office hours.
You need to provide a clear rubric for the essay. We need to know exactly how much weight is given to grammar versus actual content.
Stop making attendance mandatory if your lectures add zero value to the assigned readings. We shouldn't be penalized for your poor teaching.
Your lectures completely ignore the textbook. Why did you make us spend $150 on a book if you are just going to teach from your own notes?
Please stop putting questions on the exam that rely on us having watched a completely optional documentary.
You need to be more clear about what constitutes plagiarism in a coding class. Working together to debug a script shouldn't result in a zero.
Stop making the final project due during finals week. We have exams to study for; make the project due the week before reading days.
Please stop using multiple-choice questions that have "All of the above" and "None of the above" as options for every single question.
Your policy of not accepting any late work, even with a doctor's note, is cruel and lacks basic human empathy.
Please stop holding class outside on days when it is 90 degrees. It is impossible to focus when we are sweating and getting sunburned.
You need to actually explain the mathematical steps. Skipping from step one to step four because it's "simple algebra" leaves half the class lost.
Stop assigning group work where the groups are larger than four people. Anything bigger just guarantees three people do absolutely nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please stop reading your emails on the projector before class starts. We can all see your private messages and student grade inquiries.
You need to provide a clear and organized syllabus. A completely unstructured Word document makes it impossible to track deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stop making the participation grade based entirely on talking. Allow written reflections to count for introverted students.
Your grading speed is unacceptable. Handing back the midterm exams two days before the final gives us zero time to correct our studying habits.
Please stop assigning readings that are 50 pages long but only have one paragraph of relevant information. Just assign the relevant pages.
You need to actually moderate the classroom debates. Letting students yell at each other over controversial topics is not a productive learning environment.
Your lectures focus way too much on the history of the field rather than the actual modern applications we need to know for our careers.
Please stop giving out massive amounts of extra credit to students who can attend optional events. It penalizes those who work full time.
Stop making us memorize dates for a literature class. The themes and character arcs are what matter, not the exact year the book was published.
Please stop ignoring the students sitting in the back row. You only make eye contact with the first three rows of the lecture hall.
Stop giving out assignments that require us to use expensive campus facilities that aren't open on the weekends.
Your Canvas gradebook is completely unweighted. We have no idea what our actual grade is because a 10-point quiz looks equal to a 100-point exam.
Please stop making jokes about how hard your tests are. It just makes the students incredibly anxious and ruins their confidence.
You need to actually show up to your own office hours. I have waited outside your door three times this semester and you never arrived.
Stop making group projects mandatory if the class is completely asynchronous. We can't coordinate with people we literally never see.
Your lectures are completely disorganized. You jump from topic to topic without any clear transitions, making your notes impossible to follow.
Please stop holding office hours in the middle of the day when everyone has other classes. Offer early morning or late afternoon slots.
You need to provide a clear explanation for why points were deducted. Just giving a 8/10 with no comment doesn't help us improve.
Stop making us do busywork just to prove we did the reading. Reading quizzes are fine, but writing a weekly summary is completely tedious.
Your policy of not allowing any bathroom breaks during a two-hour exam is unreasonable and heavily penalizes students with medical conditions.
Please stop using incredibly dense academic jargon in your introductory lectures. We need you to define the terms before you use them constantly.
You need to be more responsive to emails sent over the weekend if you have an assignment due on Monday morning.
Stop requiring us to memorize the periodic table. We will always have access to a reference sheet in a real lab setting.
