He assigned a HUGE amount of reading, but I think it's because he really just wanted to cram as much info into people as he could in half a semester.  I'm sure a lot of people took this as a requirement, but he wanted people to share his passion.

Bill is the man.  He knows an incredible amount of information and is extremely accessible.  He loves beer and once met with my group at the rath and bought us all beer.  He also took the class out for beer after the public symposium.  Textbook was not necessary for the class, I didn't buy it and got by just fine.

Professor Gartner is to date the best professor I've had at this institution.  He is very passionate about subject matter, and he definitely does have a disdain for anything Western which I can relate to.  This course is VERY reading intensive.  It's a bit overwhelming, but I would definitely like to take another course with this professor.

The class is extremely reading intensive, but if you're interesting in Environmental Studies, it should be a relatively interesting class for you. If you have no interest in Env. Studies, it may be torture. Prof. Gartner is very passionate about what he teaches and that helps make the class a bit more interesting. Beware of his puns.

This class is easy and informative. Bill doesn't believe that exams are a good indicator of ability so there are only 2 exams. The exams are easy and the 4 written assignments are also very easy. Basically, if you come to class you are guaranteed at least a B.

Very easy. I expected a science class, and got a liberal arts class instead. Gartner is thought provoking, but contradicts himself often and makes blatantly untrue statements. Has a deep disdain for anything western and loves the noble savage. Take this to fulfill the environmental issues requirement for civil engineering.

This class is super easy. There were four really easy writing assignments and two midterms that consisted of multiple choice, true/false, short answer - all of which are pretty easy to handle if you at least look at the posted notes.  The class is kinda boring but good if you want to fulfill a social science credit.

This is an online class, so I never really interacted with this professor outside of comments on my assignments. This class was very straightforward, and you can tell that Professor Hernke knows what he is doing. Awesome job!

106 is online so I never had a physical lecture with him but his feedback was always good and allowed for resubmission to fix mistakes even if it was past the deadline. He actually wants people to pass this class and cares for his students.

prof hernke wants the best for his students. if something isn't working out just talk to him and you'll be fine. i had one professor the first half of this class and hernke the second half. i would recommend just taking the class when he teaches the full semester as diff teaching styles get confusing. HIS exams weren't bad. overall doable class
Super easy course

Michael was very sweet and caring, and the participation activities were clear and helpful for learning. The preparation work was easy, and his slides for before class offered useful guidance. While the course often requires teaching yourself, Michael consistently made himself available and provided supportive help.

Professor Hernke is very kind and I could tell that he cared a lot for his students and their learning. The content was difficult, but he explained it well and had old videos posted explaining it too in case you miss lecture.

The chillest professor I had, plus his unique style of lecturing, was interesting and engaging. Make sure to study well for this class since you'll need to get every point that's not the final to have a good chance of getting an A in this class. Be sure to practice the Excel skills that you learn in class before going into the exam.
Great guy, He wants to watch everyone succeed and insanely accommodating when it comes to exams and assignments.

Such a sweet and wholesome guy, you can tell he really cares about his students and just wants to watch everyone succeed. So insanely accommodating!!! His voice fluctuations don't make him the greatest lecturer, but he makes up for it in everything else.
Michael is so chill and he understands it's not worth it making everything hard for students for no reason. The class is very easy. You don't need to go to class, just watch his videos on Canvas.

Michael is a great professor- he is well-versed in statistics and business, but he cares deeply about his students and knows success is about more than what grade you receive. Lectures flipped between "normal lectures", and participation activities with a small group which I really appreciated- it helped me apply and master the content we learned
this class is very easy and is pass/fail. he is very nice and grades easily. i spent around or a little less than an hour on this class per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nice person!

He is a nice professor willing to spend any time necessary with any problems you may have. That being said, this class is quite difficult if you aren't that good with numbers, so I highly recommend getting to know him and asking lots of questions. Once again, a really great dude.

Hernke is an awesome professor and very kind and helpful. That being said this class itself is very challenging. Watch every lecture very closely and practice a lot outside of class. This is ACCT level difficulty because the exams are not easy. Set aside time to really work in this class and do not fall behind.

GB307 is now entirely taught online and split between two semesters. Professor Hernke is wonderful. You are almost guaranteed 100% on all of the homework assignments. All that therefore remain are two very fair exams with no surprises. Dr. Hernke's lectures are clear, concise, brilliant, and lacking in nothing necessary. This course was run well.

Prof. Hernke is great. This class is very easy if you take the time to watch the videos and do the practice activities. I had no experience with Excel prior to this class and I feel pretty comfortable with it's basic functions now. If you're struggling, Prof. Herke has office hours where he can help you out.

Easy class that can be done all online. Unnecessary to go in-person unless you need extra help, which is nice. I definitely think that this half of the course was more applicable to real-life situations. Test wasn't "easy," per se, but if you do the activities and homework assignment on your own (which it seems that most don't), you'll be fine.

I worked really hard and thought I would end up with a fine grade and ending getting a horrible grade for the amount of work I put into the class. Totally not fair. Would never take a class with him again.

The class all semester was totally manageable and quite alright. But at the end of the semester his grading policy was wack where a 70-72% was considered a D. I've never heard of such a thing. He was really nice and helpful in class but the grading scale was terrible

Professor Hernke was one of the kindest professor I've met. He was always ready to help. I took his GB307 in the summer, the intensive four-week course. The topics are really interesting and useful. Workload was manageable and exams were fair. It was not hard to get an A in this class.

This class is online asynchronous and has 4 sections. Get 80% on each section of quizzes (take-able as many times as you want) and you pass. Plain and simple. Watch the excel videos because they do a better job explaining the skills than the reading does. You don't get a grade for this 1 credit class, just pass or fail.
He is very caring and extremely understanding. He wants you to succeed!
I had so many issues with excel in this class and Hernke was very accommodating. He just wants to see his students succeed and I am forever thankful for this professor.
Michael's online videos were the least helpful thing. They often had nothing to do with the actual assignment.

Hernke teaches the 2nd half of the class in the spring semester. His material is easier than the content covered during Hoban's half. I thought his lectures were pretty good in explaining the concepts. His final exam was fair and easy. Make sure you do all the participation activities by yourself, and you'll be fine. Don't copy others on them.

I don't have to much to say about Michael. I mean he is fine but I found his lectures a bit boring and dull. Maybe in person they are better, but the recorded ones are not the best... I think if I had him in person or in a live class I would have a different opinion but I did not.

Michael is a sweet guy and genuinely wants you to do well in his class. His lectures were a little hard to follow but he made up for it with being super helpful during computer lab time and outside of class. He is always willing to help and wants you to understand the content. Exam and assignments were very fair.

Michael is an amazing professor. He teaches the last third of Analytics 2. He is incredibly caring and reasonable. He even knew my name without having to ever tell him. His participation activities, quizzes, and final exam were VERY fair. From him, you really get to see how analytics applies to the real world. 10/10 recommend

Hernke taught the last part of 307. His power point slides were sort of confusing, but he taught the material well if you pay attention and follow along with what he is doing. He is more than willing to help out students and answer questions.

Amazing professor. The class is tough but he's probably one of the most patient, helpful, understanding professors I've ever seen. I struggled a lot during this class because of personal things and he noticed enough to reach out personally and ask me if I needed an extension for my exam - I was able to pass the class thanks to his understanding.
Michael's awesome.  Calm demeanor, the best stories, and INCREDIBLY helpful---even over email.  Never will not reply with an incredibly helpful response--and offer to continue the conversation.

Hernke is a solid professor. This is a tough class and he goes through material pretty quickly, but is very patient and helpful during practice days. He is very passionate about what he is teaching, and uses stories to make sure we understand the importance of what we are learning.

Michael was a very nice prof who seems to like teaching and cares about his students. You can tell he is VERY smart and is operating at a level above most of his students. I wish he would have dumbed it down and SLOWED down. We often finished early without actually understanding material. His tests were difficult but are doable. Go to lectures.

HIGHLY recommend taking Michael's class. You can tell  that he is passionate about his studies and his students. Even though his lectures are boring, you get a little break in the middle and you can skip presentation days (5 classes worth) which is really nice. Homework is helpful and there's an extra credit opportunity to boost your grade.

Michael is probably one of my favorite business professors - you can tell he really enjoys his work (teaching included) and he tries his best to be there for students. His lectures tend to be slightly tedious but that's only because it's tough material. He goes out of his way to help students so don't be afraid of asking him for help!

Lectures can get long but he builds a short break in the middle which is pretty cool. I have a hard time trying to figure out what to write down from the slides but they are on moodle. He is always available for office hours and makes extra time around the exams.

Business Analytics II: Michael is one of the nicest and most helpful professors I've had in the business school. Although his lectures (statistics) can be long, he really goes out of his way to help students during office hours and ensures that students know their material. He makes homework flexible and manageable according to students' needs.

Michael is amazing. Business Analytics 2 is a SUPER difficult class - for me, the content was extremely challenging and very frustrating. The 4 homework assignments are a LOT of work (start a week early!!!) but that's how I learned the material (rather than lecture, which was confusing). Michael is amazing and always very helpful on those homeworks

Professor Hooker made this chemistry class as interesting as chemistry can be. He made the hardest lessons feel manageable. The british accent makes his class feel way more interesting and calm---trust me. I would take him for every single STEM class if I can. Ask him random questions besides chemistry; he is awesome and a really great professor!!
Paul is amazing. Appreciate your time with him.
HES PERFECT

Overall decent professor. Chem 103 is a weed out course and you can tell. As a lecturer, though, he was engaging and moved at a steady pace that I wouldn't call too fast or too slow. Decent amount of assignments per week and exams were difficult, but overall I'd recommend.

Professor Hooker was the best STEM professor I've ever had (both 103 and 104). I struggled initially learning how to study and keep up with heavy and hard coursework. I got a C on the first 103 midterm, started going to office hours and ended up getting an AB in the class. He was very motivational while being realistic and gave great feedback!
Best chemistry professor ever!! If u have a chance to take his class do not miss it
GOAT. Nuff said.

Dr. Hooker was an amazing professor who made Chem 103 a super enjoyable and manageable course. If you do the readings, pre-lecture activities, and show up to lecture, you should get an A. His lectures struck the perfect balance between entertaining and informative, and the notes he took on the slides were SO helpful to my understanding of content.
Good professor, lots of work though

Professor Hooker genuinely cares about his students and is very approachable outside of class. His lectures are clear and thorough. Chemistry isn't easy, so readings take time, but expectations are always clear. Exams are fair. The midterms test your ability to apply concepts, while the final is easier. Highly recommend going to office hours.

Chem 103 is a difficult class and it is a lot of work, but Hooker is a fantastic professor. He is passionate, knowledgeable, and great at explaining the concepts. He is also a charismatic guy and is engaging during lecture. I'd definitely recommend.

Paul was the best! His lectures were engaging and clear, and he did not mind getting a little behind to make sure he was going over the material thoroughly. The exams are very difficult, but Paul prepares you better than anyone could. I recommend doing all the practice problems possible. Your notecard will not save you on exams.
Amazing professor for such a hard class. He makes lectures interesting and is very clearly passionate about the subject.
He is passionate about chemistry and has engaging lectures. Hard to get to his office hours, recommend talking after class. Made chemistry more bearable for me.
Professor Hooker is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. He explains concepts in a clear and easy to understand manner and exemplifies everything a great professor should be.

Professor Hooker is an incredibly engaging and funny lecturer. Lectures were very well organized and he is a very clear instructor, although he sometimes got behind. Quiz and exam problems were great to build on knowledge instead of just being repetitions of problems in class. He was an even better instructor outside of class during office hours.
All topics are explained very well, and he is a very fair grader. He is also the only reason that I liked Chemistry.

Don't know what more you could want out of a professor. It is a tough class, but he does about as good of a job as anyone could. Sometimes he gets a little behind, but anything he doesn't get to is taken out of the exam. Overall a great professor who clearly wants his students to succeed.

Paul Hooker is the best chemistry teacher in the UW-Madison chem department. Chem 103 is a rigorous course, but Paul prepares you well. Lectures reflect quizzes and exams. Also, he is very entertaining during his lectures. He teaches in a way where you want to learn more. He has a soothing voice and a british accent which accentuates the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Such a great professor and hilarious. Would take his class over again!

Paul hooker is amazing, and his lectures are really fun and enjoyable to attend. The exams are tough, but it's expected. He does get off topic at points about the Premier League and tea. But other than that, he is hands down amazing, and I wish I had him for 104.
Incredible Professor! His lectures were very informative and interesting. Learned lots from him.
Cool British guy.

Best professor I have ever had. His teaching is clear and he is good at answering questions. The tests matched the class content very well and Professor Hooker provides lots of resources for studying and practicing.

Such a great professor! I had him for Chem103, and chose to have him again for 104 because of how great his teaching style is. Chemistry is a tough subject, but somehow Hooker makes it fun, and you will genuinely look forward to lecture. Expectations are clear, and exams are definitely tough but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took my glorious king Paul Hooker for both 103 and 104 and got an A in both. He has good, engaging lectures and even though he sometimes takes it slow and gets the class slightly behind, he does it to explain the difficult topics and always catches up before the next exam. I highly recommend taking chem with professor Hooker!

Hooker is the BEST Chem 104 prof PERIOD. His lectures are very engaging, he is very active on piazza, and gives VERY fair exams that actually test concepts learned and not trying to trick you. Also Hooker explains the material in a very simple way in lecture that makes the chemistry seem simple. Highly recommend asking TAs & using piazza for help.

Great prof, funny guy. Really understands how students learn; takes it slow, explains every step, doesn't try to over complicate anything. Super calm and collected lecturing style, feels like you're listening to a podcast. You can tell he's been doing this for a long time.
Hooker was a pretty cool professor. Engaging lectures, very understanding of illness and whatnot, and exams were not too bad.
Good at teaching, good looking, and british.  Do you need anything else?
wow i love paul hooker. one of the best profs ive ever had, and i wish i could have him as my professor for the rest of my life.

chem is a hard class so you'll still have to work a lot outside of class to do well in this class, but prof hooker is a great teacher and is very in depth, which makes the hard material easier to understand. take with this prof if you can, class averages are significantly higher!

Had him for Chemistry 103 fall sem of 2024 and loved him as a professor. Lectures were mandatory but entertaining, coming from someone who doesn't love chemistry. Lectures and discussion are important, and you will still have to do a lot of practice problems on your own. He also came dressed as a pack of Skittles for Halloween.

I had Professor Hooker my first semester of freshman year for Chemistry 103 and he was amazing. Lectures are mandatory (TopHat questions are part of your grade), but are enjoyable and incredibly useful for exams. Some of the exams were hard, but if you take the time outside of class and discussion to work on practice problems, you'll be fine.

Fantastic professor, engaging and very obviously knows his stuff. I took chem 103 and 104 with him, got an A in 103 and AB in 104. I hate chemistry but his lectures were the only thing that made it bearable. Amazing professor

I love him so much that at the end of toay's class (his last lecture for me) I cried. 
The BEST, BEST professor ever.
great professor
He was nice, just super inaccessible outside of class and it sometimes felt like he really just didn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Hooker is good-natured and likeable- his lectures were definitely engaging and enjoyable. He provides detailed explanations and examples, which definitely makes a difficult subject easier. However, due to that, our section was almost always behind the other sections, which caused quite a few problems. Apart from that, awesome instructor.

Paul Hooker my goat!! He is an amazing lecturer, very funny and engaging. Chem 103 is a very assignment heavy class, but it begins to feel routinely after a week or two. He is excellent at presenting the course content. Do not miss lecture- attendance isn't taken but you will fall behind. If you are struggling, ask him or a TA for help!
Chemistry is a really tough class but Prof. Hooker makes it so worth it. He's hilarious and made me want to show up to class.

Professor Hooker was amazing. Chem 103 is a difficult class and I am not a person who likes chemistry, but he made it a lot more enjoyable and manageable. His lectures are entertaining and you can tell he cares. If you have to take 103 I highly recommend Hooker!

Paul is AMAZING! I loved every one of his lectures and he made the content easy to understand and exciting to learn about. You can tell he genuinely loves to teach (rare from a prof) and cares deeply for his students. This was the best class I took this semester; he motivated me to work hard in his class.

Extremely helpful and knowledable. He explains things in a way that make sense to people with no chem background. Cares about your performance in his class, and never makes you feel dumb for asking questions. He olds extra office hours during exam week which is great. Highly recommend both 103 and 104 with him if possible.
Amazing teacher with amazing and interesting lectures. What he puts on the exams are always covered in lectures. Very nice one on one and has lots of office hour times. Amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chem 103 is a really tough class, but if you have to take it I would definitely try to get Professor Hooker. He explains difficult chem content SO well, and he's also hilarious and makes the class engaging. I'm not sad to be done with chemistry but I'll definitely miss professor Hooker.

Genuinely the best professor I've ever had. You would expect chem lectures to be very boring and uninteresting but professor Hooker makes them so much better. This class isn't easy nonetheless, but it's a lot better overall if he's your professor. He makes sure every class that he takes lectures slow so all students can grasp material very well.

Dr. Hooker was extremely funny, which made long chemistry lectures less monotonous. He explained concepts extremely well during class and was extremely kind when answering questions at the end of class. Would definitely take another class with him again.
He was a very good lecturer and explained concepts well. I have nothing bad to say about the man.

He was a fun lecturer to watch and extremely helpful in office hours. He was more than willing to answer any questions and did so very clearly. He is definitely the reason I passed chem 103 and 104. I would highly recommend taking chemistry with him

Good lecturer and funny guy, but moved at such a slow pace. Our class was an entire lecture behind the other sections and it didn't help when it came time for lab. Pre-Class assignments were ahead as well and didn't go with lecture very often. Just an average professor.

It's Chem 103 so it's going to be hard, but professor Hooker makes it so much better. I had him for the longer lecture period and he keeps everyone engaged the whole time. He's super funny and nice, if you're taking 103 try to get him.

I really enjoyed all of Dr. Hookers lectures. He truly made chemistry not only very logical but also very fun! I feel like the difficulty of his class was very fair in comparison to other chem 104 classes. He is one of those professors that is able to create such an amazing environment in his lectures.
Just another review saying Dr. Hooker is awesome and chem 108 might as well be chem 08 because he makes it that easy.
Although chemistry is the bane of my existence, Dr. Hooker made lectures enjoyable. He is funny and very knowledgeable. He respects his students and TAs. Great professor all around.
Paul is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. He actually makes learning fun and engaging and the concepts very easy to understand.
Chem 103 is a lot of work, but Professor Hooker is an awesome lecturer who is clearly a master of his craft-- both in chemistry and in teaching. I would definitely recommend taking him.
hard class, but he is amazing.  id marry him if i could :)  i turned in a lab late once and he didnt care, so lovely

Professor Hooker is an amazing professor. His lectures keep everyone engaged, even when the topics can be a little boring. The class is somewhat difficult to do well in, but it's graded on a curve, so it entirely depends on how well the rest of the class does (top 25% get an A). He's a great person and will absolutely give help during office hours.
The GOAT.

Paul made a daunting class and topics very accessible with his lecture style. He crammed in a lot of information and the lectures were definitely fast paced, but there was enough anecdotal commentary and humor added in to make the information feel digestible, even though there was a lot of it. There was an abundance of resources for the content!

Super fun lecturer who made chemistry not only an interesting class but fairly easy. Staying on top of assignments is key. There are so many resources he and the chemistry department offer for this class which make it easy to succeed. Would definitely take his class again.

Had him as a roundtable leader in the Bradley Learning Community. He is funny and super smart. 

Would have loved to have him as a chem prof, he seems really smart and entertaining.

Professor Hooker was amazing. Gave amazing lectures. As long as you put in your work, you will do fine. The quizzes were not bad. The exams were difficult, but this is to be expected as it is a weed-out class. However, the amount of dedication Professor Hooker puts into this class definitely gives you the foundation to succeed.
Best Professor ever. Lectures are well structured and I always learn and laugh a lot. Prepare to get horrible grades on your exams, but there is a curve.

Dr. Hooker was amazing. He was very funny in lecture, and he got through a lot of content in 50 minutes and made the content seem easy. When I had to reach him outside of class to discuss a personal matter, he was accessible and very understanding of my situation. Although I did not like the class content, I highly recommend him as a professor.

I cannot wrap my head around chemistry, so I dropped it. But with Dr. Hooker, I was able to understand it a little but more. Dr. Hooker is great at explaining the content and is engaged with his students during lectures. Many jokes incorporated as well.

Great professor, unlike some professors, he doesn't assume that anything he teaches is easy, so he breaks it down in a way. He's very humble and understands that the students aren't yet chemistry wizards. That being said, the class is extremely difficult but with the curve and receiving the help you can get through it. Very funny and kind as well.

Dr Hooker is such a good professor. The material can be challenging as it is a chemistry course, naturally it is difficult. However, Dr Hooker makes his lectures so fun and engaging and cares greatly about the wellbeing of his students and is extremely approachable. If you struggle with chem, I totally recommend Hooker.

A great professor that often creates funny stories and examples to keep the class engaged. There is a lot of homework and pre-lecture assignments, but there are only 5 fairly easy quizzes. The tests are moderately hard but if you studied like in Chem 1, you should be fine. In the end, 25% of the class is guaranteed A so there will be a good curve.
Hooker always kept lectures interesting. He is excellent at explaining tough topics in a simple way to understand. He showed he really cared about his students.

I understood every concept very clearly because of his wonderful teaching. I would say show up to lecture because I would be able to notice my understanding of the concepts in class would be much worse after missing even just one lecture

I took him for chem 103 and am currently taking his class for chem 104. He is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. He takes the time for each student, staying long after lectures answering students' questions. He also is very entertaining and knows how to hold your attention. His lectures are easy to follow and are very interesting.
Dr. Hooker keeps the lectures fun although they are sometimes boring. Grading is clearly laid out. There is tons of outside resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paul Hooker is a great prof and the reason why I haven't dropped. APchem was the most difficult class I took in high school, due it being online. I hated chemistry, but Paul Hooker's lectures, his humor made me love chem. It's still challenging, and still my worst subject, but my goodness it would have been so much worse with a different professor.
Chem 103 is a lot of work, but Dr. Hooker has very fun and interesting lectures.
N/a

Professor Hooker is very funny and you can tell he actually cares about his students. That being said I would say his chem sections could have the lowest grades because his tests are so hard. Also some TAs are definitely a lot more knowledgeable than others. Overall I was happy to have him and the curve is huge. Just pray everyone does as bad as u

Absolutely loved Dr.Hooker. He is so knowledgeable and wants you to do well. Chem 103 is challenging and honestly depends on how good your TA is. Show up for lecture and take notes on the slides he gives out. Overall super amazing, just be prepared to be humbled

Professor Hooker was AWESOME to say the least. He is very engaging and interactive with his lectures, even though it is 300+ students he is able to teach well and have a fun lecture. The material is hard, but Professor Hooker makes it much easier with his easy to follow slides and helpful notes. I would recommend him to everyone for Chem 103!

Paul Hooker is a fantastic lecturer. He delivers the content well and is entertaining and quite funny. He is good at responding to emails and is flexible when it comes to his students' needs. His exams are difficult but the class is curved so it's not too bad. Overall if you have the opportunity to have him as a lecturer I would definitely take it.

Dr. Hooker is an amazing professor for CHEM 103. He makes chemistry interesting and he cares that students understand the material. However, the class is hard and the exams are very hard, but the curve helps. If you put in the work and commit time, you will do just fine.

I love coming to chem class because I am engaged the whole time. He adds a few jokes in each lecture which helps them be more interesting. The tests were super hard, especially coming from someone who only took general chemistry in high school. I had to put in a lot of extra work to be up to the level that was expected of me.

Absolutely loved Dr. Hooker. He keeps his lectures interesting and engaging given it is a general chemistry class. Gen Chemistry is rough but having Dr. Hooker as a professor helps. Definitely try to get him as your professor.
I love this man, I am just bad at chemistry.

CHEM 103 sucks, but good ol' Paul Hooker makes it bearable. If you must endure this class, you HAVE to have Professor Hooker. Lots of homework, quizzes, and hard tests, but unfortunately that is the course itself and not his doing. Everyone loves this silly British man, and he will 100% help you better grasp the material.
He is absolutely hilarious and keeps you engaged and the conversation light while he teaches.
He spoke clearly and was a very interactive professor. Overall a nice experience

Paul has been my favorite professor in my first year at UW-Madison. He made lectures interesting and explained concepts very well. He is very understanding and compassionate. I recommend him to anyone that is taking General Chem. There is nobody better than this man!!!
i love this british man so much.

Dr. Hooker is a proficient and well-respected chemistry professor at UW - Madison. He makes seemingly difficult concepts easier to understand, and is clear, concise, and straightforward. I was one of his students for both CHEM 103 (B grade) and CHEM 104 (A grade) - his lectures are engaging and well worth the time, so don't skip them!

Took both chem 103/104 with Paul hooker, amazing lecturer. He really explains the material well, whereas some of my friends in other lectures with other professors didn't have the same experience. I got As in both. love the British accent. course was hard, he made it fun.

Dr. Hooker has great lectures and tries to add humor and make them all enjoyable. He's a really nice guy and he's crazy smart too. This class is quite demanding, as is any chem course, so be prepared to spend most of your time on it. I'm terrible at chem and likely would have failed without him as a professor. Definitely choose him if you can!
Very funny guy who seems very passionate about teaching students basic chemistry. had very good conversations with him about renewable energy and felt like he cared about my success in the class.

I had Professor Hooker for Chem 104, and I would highly recommend him for any chemistry class. He tells at least a few dad jokes in every lecture, and he points out what material will be on exams during his lectures. He does a good job going through each type of problem that you'll be expected to do in quizzes/exams in class as well.

Dr. Hooker was the best science teacher I have ever had! He was so kind in his explanations and lectures were VERY engaging and I felt super prepared for the exams based on his teaching and advice as to how to do well. He made the content a challenge to overcome, all while making it interesting to be there. I wish I could take him again!
the best professor i've had in my first two semesters at uw. he explains every concept in great detail and even finds a way to bring humor into his lectures everyday. he loves tea.
Absolute W professor. He taught with more passion than Hao Shen's passionate TA.

Paul was an amazing professor. He had very clear lectures, and added humor in wherever he could. He would also be available after class to ask questions to, and his explanations topics very clear. He is the best professor I have ever had.

Prof Hutton is very knowledgeable and passionate about religion, his work, and teaching. Sometimes his lectures seemed unorganized but very informational. He effectively interacts with students and let everyone share/discuss their ideas. It's clear he cares about his students and is flexib. I'd say he's a very easy grader. He sometimes cold calls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lashed out after we didn't watch the movie we were assigned (there was no way to watch it other than "figure it out"). Lenient grader, 2 exams (in-class essays), 4 2-page papers, mock trial, artistic performance final. Extremely knowledgable. Do not take class if you don't like the Bible/Torah. LOTS of reading. He is a little bit scary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's very accommodating and gives detailed feedback. Class isn't too challenging and he grades easily, but you really do have to do the readings. I would reccommend him if you have a background/interest in the subject, if not then no. You can tell he's very enthusiastic about what he researches and he can get upset if people aren't interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely rude and unprofessional. He refused to give me academic support when I asked. Had to report him to his department. Hope he can't teach for much longer

Genuinely just rude and overly uptight. He threw a tantrum twice that not enough people were raising their hands to discuss the hours of assigned readings per night so he sent everyone home 15 min into class. Massive waste of everyone's time. Did a pop quiz in place of an attendance sheet randomly because his feelings were hurt again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was my fav class all semester. I highly recommend Prof Hutton he is very enthusiastic about Egypt and his lectures are interesting! There is a lot of reading its important to do them to do well in the class. I knew absolutely nothing about Egypt before this class and got 100 on the first exam. If you study and go to lecture, you will do well!
Professor Hutton was enthusiastic, engaging and created some of the most thought provoking discussions I've had in lecture. He is kind, accessible and challenges students in the best way.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Hutton was one of the best professors I've had. He really cared about students and their needs and was flexible. His main goal was learning. For a four credit class, the workload was very doable. A background in religious studies would be helpful, but not necessary for understanding content. Definitely recommend taking a course under him!

Grade is almost entirely dependent on writing. If you don't like to write, don't take this class. I find the word count requirements to be excessive for the complexity of the questions asked, but anyone who is super into the topic/writing might find it easier. Professor accepts late work and doesn't seem to take any points of as far as I can tell.
This was by far my favorite class this semester, this is the only professor where after the class ended I sought out what he'd be teaching next.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jeremy is your classic Egypt history buff/lover. Very enthusiastic about the subject material which is nice. Seems more like my older nerdy cousin than an actual professor, which I could be good or bad depending on your outlook. Class itself was very easy, sometimes lectures were disorganized, but we worked through it fine. All in all, not too bad.

Professor Hutton is an amazing teacher! Really easy class and also super interesting topics. You can tell he is passionate with his teachings and has a great sense of humor. I absolutely LOVED his class. We did not receive a final exam, and there were only two midterms with three small essays. No hw, just readings. Come to class and he covers it.

If you don't have a background in the old testament, good luck. I do, but others will have a tough time because the professor presents it in a way like you already do. Class is kind of dry. Tests are short answers and there are a couple papers. Just read the Bible passages, take good notes, and go to discussion and you'll be alright.
Hutton is a fantastic professor. He is very engaging and excited about the material. Makes class fun. There are a lot of readings, but he does an excellent job explaining everything.

Wonderful professor. Previous knowledge of the biblical text is helpful, but not necessary. TAs are picky in grading, but if you study for the exams how Hutton tells you, you can get an AB or higher no problem. On top of that, the class is very interesting if you are into sacred texts at all.

I'd highly discourage anyone who is not familiar with the biblical text to avoid this class. Professor treats the course more as a graduate level biblical lit course and is incomprehensible as well as the textbook(collins). In addition, TA's for the course grade very harshly in terms of the essay questions and make it extremely difficult to earn As

Great professor. Very knowledgable about biblical literature. Lectures can get boring but he throws in a funny joke or two every once in a while. No need to read the book if you attend lectures and take notes. Overall great guy great class
He is a fantastic teacher and such a nice person.  He is SO passionate about the subject it makes it interesting to listen to.  I highly recommend him.

He is such an intelligent man, and he truly wants you to do well in his class (i.e., giving you all the essay questions in advanced) and is so helpful if you just go to him after class. Yes, it can be pretty dry, but so is the material and he does a good job at describing everything you need to know. Just go to lecture, and reading isn't necessary!

ok class. questions are given ahead of time but a lot of reading is involved to do well on the course. TA's are very specific on what constitutes an A exam so be prepare to be write very thorough responses
Really smart guy, knows a ton about biblical literature! Lectures are kind of hard to follow but exams are pretty easy and the questions were given to us ahead of time.

Hall is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate. However, this class is designed primarily for ROTC members, and as a non-member, it can feel a bit isolating and daunting. While it was overall insightful and interesting, I wouldn't recommend it for that key reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, definitely take this class!

Hall is a very good professor. He knows a lot and cares about students just as much. His lectures are interesting and the humor he injects every once in a while makes students feel at ease. This shouldn't be understated considering his mightily intimidating resume. I recommend taking his honors section--learn as much as you can from him!

Professor Hall's lectures are cool, the content is very interesting, and I leaned a ton from this class. Definitely sign up for his honors discussion, its worth it. However, he is an extremely tough grader; I put a lot of time and effort into my term paper and he said my work was gross in his feedback, I didn't like that very much.

If you don't enjoy history take this class. He cares about what he teaches and used to do it for some of the most important military figures in the country. If you take this class you won't regret it. Always ask questions and you may learn something new. He is willing to talk theoretical questions about the topic while engaging in good conversation

Amazing professor! Super knowledgable about the topics being taught! I had him for history 354 and he was extremely fun to take a class with! very understanding of student's needs and works to connect with them on the topics! Would recommend!

A very good speaker. John gives crisp lectures that are engaging and interjected with humor so that I never dozed off near the end. Assigned reading are interesting and well-balanced. John has a more than adequate knowledge of the subject matter and a surprisingly balanced viewpoint considering his military background. Great class for a non-major.

Prof. Hall is an amazing professor. His lectures are very interesting and he is very nice and always willing to talk with you outside of class. There is a lot of reading, around 30 pages per night, but the books are pretty good and relevant to the class. Even though I am not a history major, this was my favorite class this semester.

Professor Hall is an amazing teacher. His class is one of the hardest I have taken as a history major, but is easily one of the best college courses I have ever taken. You have to read about 60 pages a day, but if you will come out of that course knowing a lot more than when you went in. If you are a lover of history this course is a must.

John Hall is an amazing professor and extremely knowledgeable about the topic. As a history major, this was one of my favorite courses, and even though my breadth is European, Hall rocked out hard. A great guy, too, very approachable and helpful despite how severe he looks. Wish I could have taken 427, but I am graduating. You must attend lecture

Professor Hall is fantastic. He is so knowledgeable and makes the subject really interesting and his lectures are always engaging. Do not take for an easy Humanities credit however. Reading is required and there is A LOT OF READING. Quizzes in discussion over reading. All exams are take home essays - graded by the TA. Maggie Flamingo is a good TA!!

He really knows his stuff - very eloquent, great professor, great guy.  Class is difficult, or was for me, but worth it.  A lot of reading, writing.  He does expect the best, but is one of the most interesting professors I've had.  I got a B in the course, and worked fairly hard.

John Hall is a tremendous asset to the University.  His syllabus outlines a course based on lecture, reading, and discussion components. Students who neglect any will be disappointed with their grade.  Hands-down the best course I've ever taken at UW.  Bring your writing skills!

The man is brilliant:  eloquent, insightful, rigorous, grim and funny.  Expect to work very hard.  It will be worth your while.  It is possible to do okay in the course without attending every class, but you will miss out.  His lectures are pretty much works of art.

Dr. Hall is an amazing lecturer, but it's nearly impossible to take organized notes because he has no real outline. Readings and writing requirements will kick your butt. This class is difficult, because Dr. Hall expects excellence, but it will push you to be the best student you've ever been.
This class will kick your butt, but worth it.  Required to read about 60 pages per day.  Essays are difficult at best.  You get out of this class what you put in.  Don't take as a blow off.

awesome professor. really knows his stuff. do all of the readings or lecture will kick your ass, go to ALL lectures! lecture passes by fast because he gets your interest from the start. pretty funny as well

Milt was a great professor and worked hard to try to engage everyone in class. He is clearly passionate about the material. No tests and quizzes were online, I thought they weren't too hard. TA did all of the grading until the final project to which I think was graded a bit hard. But overall, very interesting class although some lectures got long.

Milt clearly cares about his students and is very passionate about marketing!

However, 460 includes a lot of easier in-class work and revisits many frameworks (eg; SWOT) from earlier classes, which limits course depth. For a capstone, more focus on current industry innovations and tech applications would make the course more engaging.
Milt Hwang is one of the kindest and most genuine professors I've had. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches and is always helpful, supportive, and accommodating to his students.

He's very nice and clearly passionate about digital marketing. He's very understanding if you need to miss class and very accessible. He was kind of a tough grader; just make sure you're asking him questions about assignments if you're confused. I'd say his courses are easy to get a B or even AB in, but harder to get an A in.

Professor Hwang was okay. Compared to other professors, I felt he graded harder, but if you ask for feedback and try to pay attention to the lectures, you will be okay. There were no exams, but quizzes that were harder than you would think. His lectures felt long at times and could get off track, but he is passionate about marketing.

Gen Bus 311 is online and and asynchronous. While Milt does have a 30 minute recording posted every week that connects the topic to a  case study, I feel like he should be more involved in the course. Almost all learning happens over the Cengage textbook, and as a result, the content did not stick with me as well as it should have.

GenBus311 is a good class for non-business majors to get their foot in the door with business. The class is set up so you can go at your own pace besides the weekly discussions. There is only a midterm and a final, which are both open notes. Overall would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Milt offers a great current and future-focused perspective on Digital Marketing. He's clearly passionate about the topics and genuinely cares about his students. Each lecture includes current events, hands-on activities, and engaging discussions. The workload is light, so the class is really what you make of it.

Milt is a nice guy but his lectures can get kind of long winded. He's a fine professor, seems to know what he's talking about and not too much work for this class, but he's not as easy to get an A with as the other professors for this class.

Tony is very passionate about the topic. Encourages students to ask questions. Grade for the class is only tests, but you are given lots of extra credit opportunities. Teaches the class in a way that you learn how to connect common themes. Lots of reading, but is manageable if you continue to read throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Had Tony back in 2017 for ecology. Great class, great man. Always wore the same belt buckle since the day he was married. Quizzes were relatively challenging, but not impossible. Interesting subject matter.

Professor Ives has been one of the best professors I've had at UW-Madison and he genuinely cares about ecology. His lectures are interesting and opens lectures with organism of the day, which is fun and engaging

Tony is a really passionate and understanding professor. He wants to give his students the best experiences possible, and there are plenty of opportunities of extra credit. I felt like test questions were often imbalanced in terms of question difficulty, and though he makes a point to write good questions, there's always room for improvement. 7/10

I think overall, Ives is a good professor. He's knowledgeable and cares about students. However, the lectures are not very concept-dense, and rely more on examples. The course is almost entirely graded on exams, which is really stupid, and the exams questions are seemingly intentionally vague, near the point of unnecessary trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tony is really passionate about the subject which makes him great to listen to. Each quiz is out of 20 points (except the final is out of 60), so even a couple wrong will bring your grade down. DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT!! It's enough to bring your grade up over 10 percentage points
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tony Ives is as good as professors get, his lectures are super interesting and he outlines things you need to know for tests super specifically so if you don't get an A in this class it's your fault. He cares way more about you learning than about making the class hard so I learned a ton and got good grades. He offers lots of EC and is a real gem.

Tony is a knowledgeable professor with a passionate interest in all topics in the ecology field. His lectures are interesting, and they are posted online as well. The exams are kinda hard, but nothing too ridiculous. Also a lot of extra credit opportunities, so take advantage of that. Overall, solid professor.

I liked this professor a lot!! He is very passionate and it's very possible to do well in this class. Lectures are posted online and there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit. I wish he taught more undergraduate classes. Material was straightforward and interesting. This class influenced me to declare environmental studies as my major :)

Professor Ives does a good job of keeping lectures interesting. I especially loved the organism of the day. He has all his lectures online. Grades are based on the tests which are 20 ? and you go over answers right after the test and a 60 ? final. Plus  there is more than a whole test worth of extra credit points so take advantage and do it early.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a very good professor. His lectures are interesting and always super engaging. I didn't mind the organisms of the day. I learned a lot from this class. Quizzes were really tough, not going to lie. There was options for EC.

He is an excellent professor and very knowledgable and passionate about ecology. He posts all lectures online so you don't have to go, but in class discussions are helpful. My biggest complaint is that the quizzes are set up to stump you and it's very difficult to get an A on them, so DO THE EXTRA CREDIT to bump up your grade.

Probably one of the best professors at UW. Enthusiastic about the subject and really wants people to learn. Grade is made up of 6 tests, 20 questions each except for the last one which is 60 questions, all multiple choice. There's ample extra credit too. He even uploads all the lectures so you only have to show up for tests.

Online lectures but spends the first 20 minutes talking about organism of the day and there's only one test question about one organism. Haven't learned anything in this class. The exams are poorly worded and intended to trip you up. Ridiculous testing because it is meant to trick you. Studying doesn't help. I love ecology and this class kills that
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy class, good prof. Sometimes lectures would be very dry, but they get more interesting as the semester went on

I wouldn't recommend this class to Bio (or similar) majors because it is way too easy and repetitive of other core courses. I learned about basic cell structure for the SIXTH time in college. Everything is dumbed down until he gets to the ecology part. BUT, lecture recordings are posted ONLINE and there is no homework. 6 exams, tricky.

Professor Ives is a great teacher. He makes class very interesting and enjoyable. There isn't a textbook so you have to go to lectures but they are really interesting so you'll want to go. There are 5 small tests throughout the course that are tricky multiple choice but he provides a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Fun easy bio course

Tony is one of the most interesting professors I've had at Wisco. There isn't a textbook, so going to lecture is a must, but they're so interesting you'll want to go. Quizzes are given throughout the semester and they're tricky multiple choice questions, but he compensates for it with tons of extra credit. If you need a bio credit, take this class!

Love this guy. He cares a lot about his students. Very genuine and down to earth.  But be careful, when he says that this class tends to drive engineering majors nuts, he mean it. He doesn't purposely try to do that though. The class in such a way that if you cant establish a crispy biological rationale at all times, it's going to be rough.

Anthony Ives is the best professor I've had in 3 years at UW. He is the coolest. His life experiences are amazing, and he really cares about making sure his students are learning. Listening in class and reading the books are the best ways to prepare for the tests, but the class and the books are so interesting that it shouldn't be a problem.

Tony Ragnar Ives is the bomb.com. He's literally the cutest thing ever. His lectures are generally interesting however he does jump around a lot making it difficult to stay involved in the topics. Overall a great introductory course, don't let the readings and lectures slip away though, very important for the tests!!!!!

Prof. Ives is awesome. He is incredibly intellegent,and genuinely cares about his class. He makes every lecture interesting, and will answer any question at any time. Smaller lectures, little homework, easy grading. There is no textbook, so just make sure you go to lecture. This is a great class to take for a bio credit, or just for fun.

Tony is the man. I might actually switch my major to ecology just so I can hang out with him. He is so cool and the class was unbelievably easy with lots of opportunities for extra credit if need be. I can't imagine anyone not enjoying this class. And there's no homework so that's a plus.

Prof Ives is one of my favorite professors. Funny guy and keeps lectures interesting and tests are fair. Optional discussion which I never attended. However, need to attend lecture to get notes because no text book relating lecture material. Lots of extra credit which makes easy to get an A. Take for bio science credit
This professor makes this class great.  I have learned so much in this class, while enjoying it.  If you need a fun and easy biology credit try to take this class.  You won't regret it.
I loved this class! Interesting, fun material and  not too serious. Great intro class that got me more interested in Ecology.

Lectures are interesting and full of hilarious fun facts about animal copulation. He is the nicest man you will ever meet, and his grading is extremely fair. This was the most pleasant class I have had at UW yet.

Really nice, intelligent guy that cares for his students! It's not that the material he presented was hard (or that the way he taught it was bad!), but I felt that it was very hard to prepare for his tests due to lack of textbook and him not really emphasizing particular points in class. Lots of extra credit opportunities though!

Tony is a really nice guy who clearly cares deeply about how his students perform. Not exactly the easiest professor but he is most definitely VERY fair with his grading. He provides enough EC to boost your letter grade up by multiple letters and even applies a curve to further it. I learned a lot, as you take tests instead of just 3 exams. TAKE!

This class was very interesting, and didn't require any previous knowledge of botany. The professor really cares about the material and the students doing well. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities and the tests are all multiple choice. Attend class and you will do really well. Good way to fulfill science req.

A great guy, obvious that he really cares about his students. Sometimes gets a little confusing in class but he does try very hard to keep things clear and simple. Definitely be prepared for the exams! They can be tricky.

Excellent professor and a great class.  Lots of fun and interesting.  Not very much work, tons of extra credit, and generally pretty easy.  Not great tests though-little point in studying, they're pretty random and not overly related to the materials.

Tony is a great professor! He's really interested in what he teached and loves answering questions and helping students. This class can be challenging, but its really interesting and Tony provides lots of support for his students.

One of the BEST professors I have ever had.  EXTREMELY knowledgeable and a huge nerd, which is a very good thing.  Knows what he is talking about and is very approachable and helpful outside of class.  Definitely recommend taking any class with him!!
Very knowledgeable and interesting, he really puts in the effort to help students understand the material. He's also very approachable and friendly!

Very very very interesting class. Seems easy, but it's not. There is a lot of potential extra credit as long as you put in the work. There is a nice curve as well, but exams are multiple choice and can have trick questions. Do not take studying for granted because there are not a lot of points and you can find your grade slipping easily.

Great professor. Makes the course material very interesting. He can answer almost any question you can think of, and if he doesn't know he'll usually get you the answer within a week or two. Exams are a little hard, but he has a very generous curve to make up for it
Organism of the day rocks!  Must got to lecture to do well exams but he makes lectures fun.  Course content is very easy, especially if you've have any past bio experience.

Who doesn't love a redheaded british-canadian with a great accent, birkenstocks, and wool socks? Especially one who lets students submit test questions and then gives you extra credit if he uses them. EVERYONE SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS, THIS MAN IS AMAZING!!!

Don't miss any lectures because there is no textbook and you might not hear the information again. Tries to make things interesting by telling stories and showing pictures of his travels. He insists on hand-writing notes on the overhead projector, which could be hard to follow sometimes.
This guy is great.  The best part of the day is organism of the day.  He has great stories, the reading is good, and the tests are easy.  You can not ask for more from your prof.

I'm in the middle of taking his class, and I think he's among the best professors in terms of organization, clarity, and helpfulness.  He doesn't leave the class hanging high and dry and on their own.  He simplifies complex ideas gives great study advice, both in general and for his exams.

Really funny and interesting guy. He has good, straightforward lectures and always gives sample questions in class and then talks through them.  He uses an overhead, not powerpoint, and has bad handwriting. The tests questions are harder than expected.
No Comments
he's a really good lecturer and makes the content really interesting. the class itself is really easy, all the content is from lecture and there's no outside readings.

PLANTSCI350=HORT350. Irwin is a wonderful professor in my opinion. The content in this class was very interesting and I still think of some of the topics daily. The lectures are definitely long but by midway through the semester he started letting us go 15-30 minutes early everyday. You do have to study hard for exams, but are they are doable.

Irwin was fantastic; he is the best of the 381 professors. His evolution unit was captivating and he made me excited to go to lecture, and his exam content of evolution was not too difficult. He did spend multiple lectures talking about Darwin and his life which is not very relevant to the course or exam but he still made it interesting

Super nice guy! Definitely is passionate about what he teaches the only downside in my class was the exams were all short answer and pretty hard. We also couldn't see our overall grade the whole semester.

I really enjoyed this class, even though it something that I don't need for my major. Irwin is my favorite teacher I have had so far, as he reminds me of a fun grandpa. He is really sweet, and really enjoys what he is talking about. I would highly recommend taking this class just for fun.

Horticulture 350 was my favorite class taken at UW Madison so far. All of the lectures were very interesting and made me think critically about the world around me. Also this class is not just limited to horticulture but the lectures encompass many other academic fields philosophy, chemistry, etc. I would definitely recommend taking this class!!

Professor Goldman was always engaging and clearly passionate about the class lectures and content. The labs were very fun, and the exams were graded very fairly. Some of his personal research gets tied into slideshows, which was very interesting to learn about!

Dr. Goldman has a pleasant and friendly attitude every day. He cares deeply about the subject matter, and incorporates previous research he has performed into relevant lectures. Wonderful professor to develop a professional relationship with.

A very caring professor who was always available outside of class. Always made his lectures interesting and demonstrated dedication. The projects were very engaging and creative, my only complaint would be the fill-in-the-blank midterm.

The grading scale is very harsh compared to other classes, and you have to do VERY well on the midterm to get an A. So much so that many people cheated because it was online. The average on the midterm was around a 30%, and there is no curve in the class. But if you do well on that then you don't have to worry.
Great professor that really cares about vegetables. makes lectures interesting and labs are fun.
Loved Professor Irwin! He's so sweet and truly cares about his students. Classes got to be a little long, but the material is not super difficult, and the projects are actually pretty fun! :)
Cool dude, very passionate about the stuff he is teaching. Very straightforward with his grading.
Lab and class was fun and very informative. I would have liked it better if the exams weren't so nitpicky and easier to study for.

Super fun guy, loves interacting with the class and keeping things chill. I took a first-year interest group that was led by him and we went further in-depth with topics presented in the main class. There wasn't anything on the exams that we hadn't learned about, and he often ended class early. Easy class for anyone who likes plants/horticulture

Irwin was overall a pretty good professor, but he definitely spent too much time on Charles Darwin trivia facts and not enough time on some of the harder material. It's evident how passionate he is about the material and it wasn't too difficult.

This man is a wonderful professor and an even better person. I enjoyed the classes that I took with him. This class is heavy on solid completion for reflections/discussions. However, the midterm exam, the only test the entire semester, was extremely tough. I really recommend this class. If you can, establish a relationship. You won't regret it.
Very very easy and laid back class except for one thing. The mid term was very very hard. The average grade was like a 50% and it is not curved. great class besides that though.

This class in particular was incredibly easy yet incredibly interesting bc of Goldman's choice of lecturers and discussions with students. He didn't lecture at all, but instead just got to know us all. He was sweet and easy to talk to, and an easy grader. He was just as curious as we were.
Prof Goldman is so understanding of technical difficulties, and responds quickly to your concerns! Additionally, the course material is presented very well.
Big fan of this man. He made it easy to learn horticulture online this semester, and the class was really fun.

Professor Goldman is the best! He clearly cares about all of his students and is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. I am a freshman and took this class as an elective and wasn't really looking forward to it, but it soon became my favorite class because of Irwin. Every student deserves to have such a great teacher.

Hands down the best professor at UW-Madison. I cannot speak highly enough about Irwin. He is so kind, caring, and teaches some very interesting material. Take any class with Irwin- you won't regret a second of it.

Good professor. Passionate, engaging, gifted lecturer, and clear presenter of ideas. Too much time spent on Darwin trivia (which was not tested on exam). Some annoying typos and lack of clarity on lecture slides, especially on the calculation problems. Do not bother reading the textbook. Very interesting and caring prof; would take again.

Started off really well with explaining concepts clearly and posted all of his lecture slides, but he wasted a whole lecture talking about Darwin trivia and ended up falling a lecture behind, so he unfortunately went way too fast in the later lectures and ended up skimming over some of the harder things to learn.

Irwin is the best professor I have had so far! He really is passionate about everything he does and cares deeply about his students. There are many opportunities if you get to know him. One negative is the generality on the exams.

Not the best teacher. Lectures are not relevant to test questions. Does a poor job of making important points clear. Spends an inordinate amount of time on unrelated and trivial subjects (Darwin's detailed history,) while neglecting to focus on important concepts that are tested in this class. Also takes FOREVER to reply to emails. Adequate at best
He obviously cares about the success of his students. If you have a chance to take a class with Goldman, do it.
Irwin is the best professor I have had at the UW. Take his class and really listen to him, he knows what he is talking about.

Clear, engaging, and fun. Obviously knows his material, posts excellent resources for studying, gives very good problem sets. Knows everything there is too know about Charles Darwin, and can sometimes go overboard with that, but it's fun. Would take another class of his.
this man is my favorite 50 year old professor. his niece is the cutest little thing and of course very pretty and smart. he is my favorite teacher and he loves me.

Irwin is a great teacher and will talk with you about anything that you want to talk about.  He is very approachable and incredibly intelligent.  Although, the tests were a lot harder than expected, there were still no big surprises when it came to the final if you are prepared.
I really enjoyed having him as a professor and would recommend him to anyone! He is a very genuine and friendly guy that was always really enthusiastic about what he was talking about.

Professor Goldman is an awesome guy. Very friendly, very enthusiastic, good at getting everyone excited about evolutionary concepts. He's also easy to relate to, approachable, and very willing to help. He's also a real scholar of Darwin. He provides interesting examples from his work in horticulture. If you get the chance, take his class!

World Veggie Crops is the best!  The "lab" is basically a taste test and the topics are very interesting.  Irwin is such an amazing guy.  Very knowledgable and friendly.  His exams are significantly harder than Jim's though... you've been warned!

Taking CS 300 in Spring is a great way to tank your GPA. Hobbes loves a 17.8 percent A rate and making you hand-write code in 2026. Very "forward-thinking." Lectures are a puzzle where the prize is being more confused than before. If you enjoy 1,500+ Zybook points and a syllabus designed to make you fail, this is the perfect nightmare for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid CS 300 in Spring. Hobbes uses a syllabus that resulted in a 17.8 percent A rate in 2025. Lectures are unclear and the 1,500+ Zybook points create an unreasonable workload. In 2026, she still requires hand-written code, which is outdated and unhelpful. The course structure is designed to confuse rather than teach. Save your GPA and wait.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Hobbes is great, no doubt.

CS300 could be more interesting though.
She's awesome! I really enjoyed the lectures (that are live streamed by the way), and she did a fantastic job of explaining complex topics.
Pretty good professor for a really weirdly and randomly structured class!

Great professor in a bad course. If you've taken AP CS A, the class is mostly review with annoying restrictions, super long programming assignments, and tedious required pre-lecture readings that go over the same things that are in lecture, making the lectures feel optional despite graded participation. If you have to take this class, pick Hobbes.

Loved her class so much. She is a great professor: funny, engaging and kind. However, the projects and exams make this class quite work heavy and difficult. So I would highly suggest taking the lectures and readings seriously from the start.
Good professor, better than CS400. Group Projects are time consuming but not that bad, tests are pretty easy. Lectures are recorded but TopHat participation in class is mandatory.

Hobbes is a good lecturer and very knowledgeable and caring, but the lectures got to be quite slow, and most of the time was spent writing testers. Codio was also a horrible textbook rife with errors. The grading was very flexible, but the projects were often unnecessarily time-consuming.

Super kind and awesome professor. Decent lectures, attendance required. Course has a flexibility policy so your grade won't tank from just one F. Most negative things one could say about the class would be about the class or its format, not the professor themself. However, the mid-year project was poorly planned, presumably by multiple instructors.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hobbes is a good prof, but her lectures are pretty slow for students who know what they are doing. If you enjoy sitting and listening in a relaxed environment, then she can be really helpful and you will not struggle. The textbook (Codio) that they switched to this semester had lots of mistakes and was clearly generated mostly by ChatGPT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hobbes is fantastic! They are great especially for freshmen getting used to college, you'll always have a laugh in lecture. Hobbes never misses a question and her TA team is SO SO SO helpful, office hours are a LIFE SAVER! The course is only really difficult during recursion, exams are fairly ez if you understand concepts at their core, hw light

Good teacher. The overall course is pretty easy. The projects take a lot of time but if you put in the time they aren't that bad. Tests are kind of difficult especially having to write code on paper. My only complaint specific to her teaching style is that the lecture slides are very light on information which makes it hard to skim later on.

The lectures are boring and entirely unnecessary, but that's to be expected. She gives off a passive-aggressive attitude sometimes, but I think that's just because she's tired after helping out a thousand students, so it makes sense. She's fun, the class is super easy as long as you actually do the homework.
Great professor, lectures are clear and easy to understand. Projects take up a lot of time but are very rewarding in the end.
Good professor, lectures were easy to understand although could be boring at times

Awesome professor. Class is a lot of work but that's to be expected with any proffesor. Only complaint is MAYBE lectures are a little slow but if that's the only complaint than you're a great instructor. 10/10 professor.
hobbes legoat
Hobbes is so funny and caring and her lectures are so fun.
She is a very knowledgeable professor, and it shows in how she teaches.
Fair grading, excellent lecturer
Excellent professor!

Professor is exceptional, especially for computer science. Great to see diverse representation in teaching faculty. Coursework is the same regardless of professor for CS300, lectures are livestreamed and recorded and available to anyone taking cs300. Projects are somewhat time consuming, but nothing insane. Tests are relatively easy. I love Hobbes!

Professor Hobbes was my best professor for my first semester as a freshman. Her lectures are engaging and easy to follow, and she livestreams them if you can't physically attend. A decent amount of homework but overall everything is easy to work with if you're into CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer and has good pace when lecturing (probably slow for some people). For me, I feel the content of the course is a little bit hard for new java learners. Otherwise this would be an easy course.

She's a good lecturer but you could learn most of the material from zybooks alone (typical for CS classes). The most exciting part of class was seeing what awesome crazy shoes she chose to wear that day.

Her lectures are extremely slow. She just talks so slowly. But they aren't bad, I usually got more out of the ZyBooks though. At the end of the semester, she was very vague and unclear about the grading policies after making the tests in person for the first time and chose to not curve even tho the average was like 70. many students were upset.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very engaging lecturer. Easily one of the most likeable professors I've had. Tests were very fair. If you study well, they shouldn't be a problem. Some projects were a breeze, others were extremely hard, and it was pretty unpredictable from week to week. One of my only complaints with her lectures is they are a bit too slow.

Hobbes was a good lecturer. Unfortunately, when I reached out with concerns about my ADHD, they were very rude and condescending. The nail in the coffin for me was when my grade in canvas said I had a B (which I wanted), but the final grade got reported as a BC. They were unhelpful and rude. They seemed cool otherwise, but was really argumentative.

Hobbes is a great professor, however not at fault of her own there isn't too much of a point in going to lectures. ZyBooks and just doing the coding projects are significantly better ways to learn the material. Content is definitely meant to be learned at your own pace, not in lecture

Hobbes had perhaps the most well-structured course I have ever taken. Lectures were organized and easy to understand, weekly projects were crystal clear. And her lecturing style is thoroughly engaging without being overly enthusiastic, somehow. Knows the material in and out. Her and the TAs were very quick to respond to student questions on Piazza.

Hobbes Legault is a great lecturer and very good at running the class. CS300 projects can take a long time, but they are well organized and it is clear what you are creating/supposed to be doing. Enjoy CS300 while you can because CS400 is the complete opposite. Overall great professor and solid class.

Actual goat. I always felt the class was going smoothly, but I realize it 10 times more now. In comparison to the sequel (cs400), cs300 was waaaay better organized and taught. The course was pretty rigorous in my opinion, but with Hobbes it seemed a lot more chill. If you have the opportunity of taking cs300, do so, and enjoy it while it lasts.
Angel

I can honestly say that I didn't attend a single lecture, but she still does a good job of them. You learn 99% of the information via Zybooks, but I skipped around through the lecture videos before the exams. She's funny and engaging, and definitely the best CS300 prof. The class was a solid intro, and not hard if you try on the projects.

The lectures can be attended virtually and are recorded, and the attendance questions are only due before the next lecture, meaning one could get by just fine never actually attending a lecture. Lectures were very clear making it easy to take good notes. Beware of a heavy homework load: the homework assignments were sometimes tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hobbes is quite clear, and I would go as far as to say that with her, you probably have the best understanding of the CS300 course
Amazing lectures. Professor was entertaining and informative. Every lecture was a blast. Although attendance isn't mandatory, there are participation questions due after every lecture.
