Pevehouse is the man but this class shouldn't be taken as an elective. It's kinda tough. I think a lot of people take 103 cause hes awesome but there's other awesome teachers who teach easy classes...

Take this class if you like history. Pretty interesting and easy to fallow. Pevehouse is an awesome guy.Tests are pretty straightforward with multiple choice and short answer questions. A must take class!
Pevehouse is a great professor. His lectures are long so he tries to make them interesting. If you have no interest in politics this class is hard regardless, but Pevehouse does a great job

Prof. Pevehouse is awesome. Even though the power lecture took forever, he provided plenty of entertainment and was very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about international relations. He's extremely passionate and it clearly shows. Tests are difficult but very fair. He's the man!

Pevehouse is simply one of the best professors at Madison. His lectures are very interesting and the way he explains things gives you a new outlook on world events. I highly recommend his course. Its a fairly easy 4 credit class. The only homework is reading and the exams are very straightforward.

Pevehouse is a great professor.  If you have to take PS103, take it with him.  He is extremely helpful--he says exactly how the exam will be laid out and which readings/textbook chapters you should focus on.  Plus, he is a very interesting lecturer and uses a lot of real-world examples to explain otherwise boring theories.
Great teacher, though I had a terrible TA.  He really knows a lot about the field, gives Professor Suri a run for his money.  I took the summer course, was pretty easy.
Pevehouse = best professor. Ever.  Your UW Madison experience is not complete until you have had him. Awesome professor and even better guy.
The best professor. His jokes are the greatest and keep the class interesting. I learned a lot from him and enjoyed the class a lot.
Simply the best professor at UW

Pevehouse is a baller. I took his American Foreign Policy class, so taking his lobbying seminar was a no-brainer. It was literally just 20 students plus Pevehouse sitting around, shooting the**** and talking about politics. Great guy, awesome teacher, lets you do your own thing.

Pevehouse is fantastic, and I never say that. Best professor I have had.  Lectures are incredibly informative, entertaining, and COMPLETELY NECESSARY to succeed in the class.  Go to the 2 pre-exam discussions - it's all on the exam. Exams are MC and short answer. This is one of those must-take professors. UW Madison should be proud to have him.

Pevehouse is awesome! His lectures are hilarious and he can really relate to students. I thought his lectures were really interesting too and I loved the class. He makes the material even more interesting. Exams are very  fair. I would DEFINITELY recommend this class, even if you're not a poli sci major.

I like Poli Sci, so grain of salt and all that, but I thought his classes were really interesting and fun to go to. Discussion sections are optional, so if you're trying to fit it into your schedule keep that in mind.
Knowledgable professor. Very funny man and makes class interesting. I looked forward to attending every lecture.

Awesome teacher and all-around fantastic human being! Make sure to attend lecture and take good notes. I really wouldn't recommend taking 103 unless you really love IR and PoliSci. For non-majors/indifferent people it can sometimes seem really dull and technical (which isn't Pevehouse's fault since it's true of any subject).

Such an amazing professor. I had to work harder for the exams for this class than any of my other classes (even though it's 100 level) but at the end of the semester it was the only class I still wanted to go to. Pevehouse is funny, engaging, and intelligent. I feel like I've learned so many relevant things in his class, so worth it!
Pevehouse is a great guy and is incredibly brilliant. This guy really knows his stuff. However, I found International Relations to be extremely boring, and the tests were rather difficult.
Awesome. Best professor I've had, hands down. He knows so much, is incredibly helpful, and is funny. He is the reason I chose to be a Poli Sci major.
Extremely interesting class as he relates everything to modern events. Clear classes that are actually entertaining. One of the few classes I looked forward to going too.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes lecture really interesting and FUN! I would take all of his classes. His tests are somewhat challenging but if you do most of the readings and go to most of the lectures you will be fine. Seriously he is the best.

A truly amazing professor.  He is interesting, knowledgeable, fair, and absolutely hilarious.  I learned so much and actually had a strong desire to go to class!  You would be lucky to have him as a professor.

Easily my favorite professor. The amount of knowledge this man has in his head is phenomenal. He is down to earth and clearly passionate about the subject. Rearrange your schedule for this guy! Simply legendary.
My favorite professor ever. He lectures well, is funny, and is extremely helpful.

Terrific. A funny, interesting, smart guy. The material is fairly general considering it's an intro course, but he's hysterical, and thus it's far more fun to learn. Do the readings. You are tested on exactly what they say, though he lectures are based around them as well. If you put a decent amount of effort into the course, you'll do just fine.
He's phenomenal.  You will love him!  Absolutely hilarious.  He's god.

This class has absolutely nothing to do with my major and I did not want to take it, but looking back now I would take it all over again. He is such a hilarious and genuinely nice professor. he makes power lectures interesting. absolutely loved the class and didn't mind going. def take this class with pevehouse, otherwise you're missing out!
One of the best profs. I have ever had!  Funny but super passionate about his field.  Going to lecture was less of a task and more of a fun time!
AMAZING PROFESSOR!!  By far the best and funniest professor I have had!  Take a class with him if you can.

Pevehouse is one of the best profs I've had. He really knows his stuff and presents interesting and funny lectures. Discussion sections are optional which makes for an easy, fun class. Definitely take a class with him!
HES A GREAT. BEST MAN EVER. I Wish i could be him

Pevehouse is AMAZING. Best professor I've had on campus-Seriously. I've never wanted to attend lecture so much in my life. Really entertaining, but also very clear and knowledgeable. Take a class with him if you can.

I started looking for classes to take just because Pevehouse was the professor.  I had him right before he left and was lucky enough to have him again once he came back.  Very funny, he makes lectures easy to understand and gives good reviews for exams.  Extremely helpful in office hours and he is very personable!

The course was Problems in American Foreign Policy in 2004. It was fantastic. I just heard in the Poli Sci alumni magazine that he is coming back to the UW. He has a rare blend of humor and scholarship that is a pleasure to be in his courses.
Too bad he's leaving Pevehouse was great. Should be president some day.
Ummmm, not all that remarkable of a professor.  Perhaps this was just an off-semester.  Lectures very dry, boring, simplistic.  No energy.
Halarious guy and all around great lecturer. Lecture gets a little boring a couple of weeks before final- but all in all a great class. If you attend lecture you will do well
Great prof.  The book is very close to his lectures, seeing as he wrote the book.  Keeps things interesting and despite looking like a nerdy computer science TA, he is a very lively young prof.
Love him! Really fun, and makes it interesting and relevant. The overhead notes he uses aren't very helpful, so you have to pay attention and take good notes. Awesome prof!

MY FAVORITE TEACHER EVER!!! He is absolutely hilarious AND passionate about his subject. He seems to know everything about IR and presents it in an interesting way. He prepares you well for the exams by giving out a list of terms to learn beforehand. Least painful power lecture ever because you laugh through half of it!
I love him!!

He is a great professor.  Class is very interesting.  GO TO CLASS.  If you go to class and take good notes the tests aren't that bad.  He gave us a pretty good idea of what to expect for each test.  Great Class.

Awesome professor.  Laid back and fun, yet highly intelligent.  He's super friendly and is a good source for all kinds of advice on grad school, research, jobs, etc. I wish I was an IS major after taking his class.

GREAT PROFESSOR EVER! my favorite on campus, i took him freshmen year and still haven't had a better professor! go to class because that is where a lot of questions come from and read the book! he is very fair and his class rocks
Hilarious, but still gets everything across.

Prof Pevehouse is by far my fave prof on campus.  I actually wanted to go to lectures because they were so interesting.  Reading the text and articles wasn't necessary.  He makes it very clear what is will be on the tests, so they are easy to study for.  He also has a nerdy hot thing going on, which was a plus.  He also reads these reviews, fyi.

One of the best classes I have ever been in. The professor is the man. Go to lectures, take really good notes and there is no way you should get less than a B. Nothing surprising, just go to lectures and make sure you know all potential ID's that he gives you.
Awesome professor who makes lectures really fun.  Just make sure you go to lectures since most of the test material comes from them.

Pevehouse is awesome. He always tries to throw in some jokes and humor during class to make everyone laugh. I highly recommend going to lecture because that's where a lot of material from the test comes from. Also, go to section since the T.A. pretty much grades everything you do and they should know who you are. Pevehouse is awesome!

Very Funny Teacher.  Being a non-poli sci major he made this class easier with his jokes and unique teaching style.  Easily one of the top professors on campus.  If you do the readings and go to lecture and discussion, you should do fine.  Your grade really is up to which TA you get though cause they grade everything.  Amazing Teacher!

Great prof.  Interesting to listen to, quite young, and rather funny.  Explains material very clearly.  Gives out study guides before exams to tell you which topics are potential ID's.  The class is very easy for anyone who knows much about the world, whether history, geography, poli sci, current events, etc.  Interesting intro course.
fun prof, fairly easy class

For non-poli sci majors this class isn't that easy. If you can't devote a decent amount of time studying for the exams and doing the readings, don't expect to get an A. Really depends on your TA though since they grade most of your essays.
He makes the class interesting, informational, and injects some humor into those power lectures. You can't go wrong.
This man rocks my socks off.
great in lectures, very helful out of class as well

I read about 20 pages total in this class and still got an A. The key is actually paying attention in lectures. And then sifting through before midterms and studying key concepts. He gives out a pretty good review sheet which helps figure out whats on the exams.No surprises there. Plus he's hilarious and the topic is interesting.My fav class so far

Pevehouse. What a wonderful professor. Although I got not-such-a-wonderful grade in his class, it was one of my favorites. He is always trying to keep things interesting and likes to take a break from Poli Sci and tell jokes every once in a while. One great thing about his class is that you have the opportunity to fix your papers/exams. Just ask!!
No Comments
Funny and interesting but the tests were diffcult if you didn't go to class. Do not take for an easy A. ps the TAs for this course dont speak english.

One of the best professors I've had.  Hilarious, down-to-earth, and really knows his stuff.  He was completely objective and unbiased.  My TA was horrific, but Pevehouse made up for him.  I would definitely take one of his classes again!
Take a class with this man.  You will not regret it.

Wow, he's a great professor.  He really wants everyone to know and understand the material.  Tests are not bad if you go to lecture,and he's pretty interesting during lecture.  I would definetly take him again.

Wow. what a good professor; interesting, fun and tells cheesy-but-good jokes. WARNING: it is hard to get A's on the tests, although B's are definately doable. Also, huge lecture-very sweaty and uncomfortable...dress in layers.
awesome professor, exams very fair, funny guy
best teacher i have ever had! handsome, kind, witty, and just plain intelligent. a great all-around guy. his wife is a lucky woman!  He is so clear, and really wants to help students.
He was always open for discussion and help during and after hours. He allowed me to take an independent study which was my fondest class memory in college.
Everyone has fun in a class taught by Pevehouse.

I love this man! He is definetly one of the best, most entertaining, and interesting profs i have ever had.  He is an awesome lecturer.  He speaks slow enough and very clearly.  Throws in jokes and stories to keep attention. Repeats definitions so you can write them down. Tests were completely fair and easy.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
He is so knowledgable and extremely witty!!  I love the pictures of Beavis and Butthead that he includes in the lectures
He is awesome and really funny! I love the way I don't fall asleep during the lecture because it is somewhat entertaining.

An excellent lecturer and he keeps the hour and 15 minute lecture lively and entertaining. He makes the material relatable to the students and makes learning it fun. He's not afraid to throw in the occasional swear word to emphasize a point. As a freshman he has helped make the college transition easy.
he's knowledgeable, explains everything thoroughly, but doesn't treat you like a moron, and he's self-deprecating and open to swearing, which you've gotta love.
I have had Professor Pevehouse twice and will have him again. He is one of the best professors on campus. Very fair and very informative, you are missing out if you haven't studied with him!

Great lecturer, funny professor.  I've had him twice.  You get a review sheet w/essay questions & short answer vocab 1 wk before.  Don't waste time doing readings cuz he just repeats it in lecture. All test info comes from lecture.

This course is not easy. It is not an elementary course. Average Test scores were failing or one point above failing. Homework points are taken off, and no reason is ever given. In the last few weeks, half of my row dropped the course. This class took the joy out of being in the sun. Save yourself pls don't let my pain be for nothing.

For 100, the exam reviews are unhelpful; it's 4 vague questions for a 30 question exam. The homework has no rubric, and feedback is not really offered. The 101 portion has its pros, with interesting topics demonstrated with small experiments by the TAs, but most of it is busy work and rushed lectures. This is not an easy physical science credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HEED THE WARNINGS AND DO NOT TAKE AOS100/101 for an "easy" science credit if this is not your major. The homework is graded incredibly harshly with no feedback and it is very unclear what we are being graded on. The tests are much harder than the lecture material even if you use the book. This difficulty does not feel fair for a 100 level class.

Do not expect this course to be an easy science credit. There are no lecture slides to review, and lectures do not encourage comfortable participation. Tests are entirely multiple choice, leaving no room to express conceptual understandings. Grades are VERY unforgiving. If you have the opportunity, take this course with a different professor.

If you are taking this class for a science credit and aren't a science major, please rethink, it's an extremely difficult class and while Prof. Martin is knowledgable, exams are extremely hard to study for and the average is a C. exams are the biggest part of your grade, but homework is graded harshly and there is no rubric to follow.

If you're not interested in Physical Science, or your major/minor has nothing to do with PS, or you just want to earn credits for PS. Please think carefully. 

1)No lecture slides or review sheet/problem sets on canvas 
2)Exams are tricky, harder than lecture 
3)No feedback on assignment

I dropped it after the 2nd exam. It is way beyond "100/101".

If you are looking to take AOS 101 or AOS 100 for a general physical science credit, DO NOT. The class is difficult, with few resources to succeed. Even if you study the questions on exams are so specific and sometimes don't even cover the material. What's worse is that Professor Martin wrote the textbook for class, but won't make it free.

The grading is incredibly frustrating. Exams are the most weighted part of your grade, and no matter how hard you study for these exams, its impossible to get a good grade. The exam grade averages are usually around 66%. The questions on the exams are tricky and niche and even after studying for hours and days, there is no way to properly prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his class 5 years ago but just saw a post about him so I'm coming back to leave this review in hopes someone reads it and takes one of his classes. I still remember this class being one of the best classes I've taken, so many years later, not to mention I probably only remember a couple other of my professors in all of my classes.

Professor Martin teaches an incredible class. He is so deeply invested in the material that it's like watching someone explain their favorite movie every day. His eyes light up with each concept. This is probably the hardest GenEd you will take at UW Madison but Professor Martin makes it extremely easy to know what to study.

Good lectures, exams of expected difficulty for a science course. Very good professor who is engaging and really cares. Homework assignments were difficult but made you think in interesting ways and you had plenty of time to consult others and complete them. Really good for physical science requirement!

Prof. Martin is a great prof he gives very informative and entertaining lectures. Though, these entertaining lectures can leave you with a false sense of security for the exams make sure you spend time doing the homework and reading the textbook will be invaluable for you.

I have really enjoyed this course and Prof. Martin is amazing. However, a huge mistake was made when grading class work. The entire classes grades were incorrectly weighted, therefore the grades were incorrectly listed on canvas for the entire semester up until the week before finals. Several classmates reported entire letter grade changes. Not ok.
A great lecturer, a kind person, and a super fun class. It can be a bit tough but he is super helpful in office hours. Got me super engaged as a student, community member, and weather enthusiast!

Professor Martin is an engaging and passionate instructor. The lectures are informative, and the textbook is a great study resource. Homework can be challenging, but with consistent effort and using tools like unstuck study for prep, you can succeed in this course.

Jon was a knowledgeable and passionate professor. His way of teaching kept me engaged and he always answered any questions with the best of his ability. While lectures are important, the textbook was BY FAR the best study material for the tests. The homework assignments every other week were a little challenging so make sure to ask questions.

Prof. Martin is such an engaging, passionate, entertaining lecturer. His slides made all the content digestible. He genuinely cares for his students, always took time to answer every question, and deliberately scanned the room to make sure he didn't miss any hands. He's probably the best professor I've ever had and deserves all the praise.

Wonderful guy and prof, but a deceptively hard class, especially for non-STEM majors. Lectures are rather fast-paced, though sometimes reiterated verbatim in the textbook. Homework is spaced out and only a few questions apiece. He's accessible outside of class if you have questions. Bonus points for the charming Boston accent.

Prof. Martin is a great professor, really passionate and just a really good guy. Lectures are kind of fast paced, and the course is really physics heavy which was hard for me, it was kinda boring but he made it as interesting as weather can be. His textbook was extremely useful though, very concise, very good for studying and the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tests are worth 75% of grade and the tests were fairly difficult. homework and lab (for 101 section) is only 25%, which is much easier than the 3 tests and one final. definitely do not recommend, especially if science or test taking is hard for you.

Martin holds entertaining lectures 3x a week for his course. However, with the entertainment comes a huge lack of teaching ability. You can attend class everyday and study the textbook and still get terrible grades on exams. Exams are worth 75% of the grade and he is very comfortable letting the average exam score be a C on each test.  My Grade: AB

Attend lectures, read the easy and short textbook, and put time and thought into the homework and you will no doubt get an A. Prof Martin is an excellent teacher and at the very last lecture everything comes together in an amazing way. You will never be able to think about the weather the same again.

Lecture is engaging and interesting. Heard the class was super easy but that is not the case. Not insanely difficult but not a super easy A. Homework is difficult and exams are challenging, studying is pretty necessary. Other than that I absolutely love the class simply because of how passionate he is. Humor is genuinely funny but not excessive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class wasn't easy, but it wasn't insanely difficult either. As long as you attend the lectures, you should be ok. Homework is much harder than the tests. Professor Martin is great, and going to office hours is super helpful!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Homework is a lot harder than the actual exams but his passion for teaching this course is remarkable. Also his jokes are actually good.

Ugh, what a terrible class. Please do not take this class. Contrary to other reviews which I followed and deeply regret. This class was terrible. It was very test heavy and the homework was impossible to get a good grade on and it frankly had nothing to do with the class itself. I would definetly not recommend taking this class.

Professor Martin was super awesome and clearly cares about what he does. I never used the book even though it was "required" and still did very well based off the lecture videos. I took this during an online semester so I am sure that the experience could have been better but I still enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing.

One of the best professors of my freshman year. Very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. I needed a science credit to fulfill my gen eds, as I am a business major, and I could not have asked for a better class or professor. Take him if you can!

This class was definitely one of the more difficult I have had to take. I am not a science major, and I thought this class was going to be an easy physical science credit - I was sorely mistaken! Prof. Martin's lectures were often difficult to understand in the context that he moves quickly though material. Make sure to read up in the textbook!

Professor Martin is a really great lecturer and seems like a really nice guy. I took his class almost entirely because of what I'd heard about him and I was not disappointed. The class isn't too hard if you take a little bit of time to study and actually try on the homework assignments. Definitely recommend him.

I LOVE HIM. I went into this class not ver excited about science, but he really made it fun and exciting for me. I actually looked forward to going to his class. He is funny, caring, and very knowledgeable. The class is graded on 4 exams and 6 homework assignments. I would 100% take another class of his.

Martin's class is a delight! It isn't an "easy A", but as long as you pay attention in class and read the textbook, you'll be fine. His lectures are engaging and he's hilarious. He actually cares about his students. He's really busy so office hours are packed but AOS100 was one of my favorite classes and professors I've taken yet. 10/10 recommend.

The least I can do for Dr. Martin is leave him a great review on RMP. I took the class because I wanted an easy A and he was a highly rated prof. I can't attest to the A being 'easy', but if you pay attention in lecture it isn't too hard. He is hilarious and well-spoken, has lectures down to a science (pun intended). Makes me wish I majored in AOS.

Martin is a funny guy, but the class is not that easy. If you're looking for an easy physical science credit, there are better classes. Taking this class just to have a good professor is not worth it. Exams are only 30 questions so it is easy to get a bad grade. Spends a good chunk of class on daily weather, moves quickly through concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I'm not much of a science person, but Prof. Martin does a great job of making you listen anyway! He's a really fun and straightforward guy that genuinely want you to learn the fundamentals in a way that make the bigger-scale stuff a breeze. The homework is pretty tough, but the tests are so straightforward and fair. Lots of laughs in this class!

If you are looking for an easy class as a freshmen, this is not it. Prof Martin is an awesome guy but his lectures are pointless to go to. He talks about todays weather for half of the class and it's not even on the exams. The homework is a bit hard but nothing terrible to handle. His exams are pretty difficult and requires a lot of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's very well respected and very passionate about the weather! Makes us intrigued about the subject as well. He's very accessible outside class, so you will always have the chance to discuss things with him. If anything, the homework are a bit tough but it's only on biweekly basis. Overall recommended! :)

Went into Prof. Martin's class not sure of what I wanted to study in college and left it inspired. Martin implores his students to have the same passion about weather, climate studies, and natural sciences as he has, and creates fun and interactive atmosphere in the process. Prof Martin is down to earth, honest with students and ready to help 5/5!

One of the best professors I've had at UW! Very clearly passionate about the weather and breaks it down really well, so that it's easier to understand. Class gets a bit more difficult towards the end, but the final isn't cumulative which helps. Take the lab section with the class! Helps a lot with understanding material and can pad your grade.
The class is difficult at times, but Martin does a great job at explaining difficult concepts. Take the lab with it. I never knew someone could be so passionate about the weather!

Martin is great, super knowledgable+enthusiastic about the subject. However, this is NOT a class for non-science majors and will be super difficult if you struggle with science. Tests just don't line up with lecture material&require way too much critical analysis for a 100-level class. If you're looking for an easy science credit, this isn't it
Super easy to listen to and explains everything well.

Professor Martin is incredible! I never dreaded going to his class. He is an amazing lecturer and makes the material easy to understand by applying it to real life situations. He is really passionate and energetic and cares about all of his students. The textbook really helps make the material more understandable as well.

Martin is overrated. The difficulty ramps up exponentially towards the end of the semester. Martin, while jovial in class, is terrible during office hours. He frequently tells students he "doesn't feel like" explaining a concept again. He relies on bad heuristic arguments to explain concepts in class and in his textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall great class and very interesting. Lectures were amazing and he laid out the material in a very relatable and easy to understand matter. The only complaints I have is that the homework is super hard , but it really boosts your grade if you do well.  Additionally,  I studied the material a lot for the exams and still got  b's and c's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Martin was my favorite out of all my professors this semester, and probably out of all the professors I've had at Madison so far. He is hilarious, a great teacher, and very willing to help. Study for the tests and you will do fine. Take from Martin, you won't regret it!!!

Jon Martin is one of the best professors at UW-Madison. He is very passionate about the weather and is an outstanding lecturer. The book coincides directly with lecture and is a useful supplement. Exams are straightforward. Although useful, no prior knowledge of physical science is needed. Pay attention in class, take notes, and you will do well.

Jonathan Martin is a GEM. This man LOVES the weather and he makes lecture super interesting. The textbook is an easy read and it's extremely helpful. Overall, his class is very straight forward and he's really approachable. I highly recommend him for non-science majors!

Professor Martin is one of my favorite professors so far. He made the lecture so interesting and understandable. Homework was hard comparing to exams, but worth thinking. If you take with the lab section, you need to work on more practice homework weekly. Overall, great course!! You won't regret.

AMAZING LECTURER!! I had zero knowledge on weather and climate, and to be honest, I wasn't that interested in it initially. But he was such an awesome professor that I actually looked forward to going to his lectures every week. He's very passionate and has your best interest at heart! Take his class, YOU WON'T REGRET IT!

Take AOS100 with Professor Martin in the spring!  Hands down my all-time favorite professor because he is passionate about the class and his students.  I was looking for an easy science credit, but I got so much more from Professor Martin.

Best professor ever. Take his weather class in the spring. He is so enthusiastic and genuinely cares that you learn the material. Always drops in a couple good jokes and occasionally a bit of profound wisdom. Is not an automatic A, but if you focus on the important stuff you should do well.

Professor Martin was such a delight to see every MWF. He loves the weather so much that I started to love the weather. He adjusts test grades after the fact, so even though tests were harder than I expected I still ended up with good grades. Do what he asks of you, go to his review sessions and this is a great physical science class to take!

Professor Martin was great! I took the course because I needed physical science credits, but Professor Martin actually got me interested in the topic. He is very passionate about weather and is enthusiastic each lecture. He also really cares about his students and is incredibly approachable. I highly recommend!
He is very passionate about what he is talking about and lectures are engaging/interesting to attend.

Dr. Martin is an amazing lecturer. He is the most passionate prof I have had so far and he is funny as well. He makes the content interesting and is genuinely interested in making sure his students are learning in a useful way. If you have a good basic physics background, this class should be pretty easy for you and lectures mimic the textbook.

He is such a great professor, I wish I could take more classes by him! I'm not a huge fan of the subject and still am not, but he presented it in a clear and approachable away. He also offered help multiple times and I really felt like I could go to him with questions.

Dr. Martin does his best to make you understand. The material isn't always the easiest to get, but he gives a lot of examples and loves answering questions. He's very funny and tries making class enjoyable, and it's obvious how much he loves what he's lecturing about!

Best professor I've had! He makes weather interesting. The class was a bit more difficult than I was expecting but if you go to lecture and listen/take decent notes you shouldn't have any problems. He is a fun guy to be around and is always willing to take time out of class to answer any questions and doesn't try and trick you on the exams.

I took this class as a Junior in the business school and loved it! Professor Martin makes the material interesting and easy to comprehend. If you are looking for a science class to fulfill requirements I highly recommend taking weather and climate with him. As long as you prepare for the exams and complete the homework you can expect a good grade.

He is very knowledgeable, and makes his lecture very attractive. Using a lot of simple examples and he is very charming I would say! Take this instead of physical 107 if you want easier and more interesting work!

I'm a chem major who took this class because I think weather's cool. It was great. Exams are easy...everything comes straight from the notes. The book isn't necessary. Professor Martin is a great lecturer...keeps class interesting and entertaining. You can tell he loves teaching, which is awesome. He's super excited to share his love of weather.

Best professor I've ever had.  I'm a finance major who needed a science, and a friend told me to take this class.  Make sure you take it in the spring with Martin.  A few times I went in to ask questions about the homework and we ended up talking for 45 minutes.  Great guy and will make you want to go listen to him three days a week.

Has some interesting stories he relates to material and and is very enthusiastic about the weather which makes for interesting lectures.  He is helpful when emailing about homework, won't give you the answer but looks to point you in the right direction.  Works jokes into lecture well.  Great professor.
If youre a non-science major DO NOT take this course, way harder than expected!

Professor Martin is a cool guy and super pumped about weather. Class required I put in more effort than I had expected to but not difficult material at all. Textbook is exactly his lecture notes. Exams are fair but more difficult than I had presumed, so I'd advise not cramming the night before like I would. All around good guy and pretty easy class

Extremely enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and fun professor. Really excited about weather, wants you to be excited too. Teaches class like the general science credit it is, not like an intro to the weather major class. Fairly easy course if you go to lecture and read his book. I'm not a science major and did fine in the class.

Prof Martin was funny, clear, and knowledgeable in his lectures.  It is clear that he is passionate about his work in climate studies.  If you invest a fair amount of time in your homework assignments, this is a fairly easy course.

Good enthusiastic prof.  Not too hard of a class and the book is same as lecture so you only need one or the another. The 101 section is a good amount of additional work but helps the overall understanding of material.

He is super enthusiastic and it isn't hard going to lecture. The lecture and the book are almost word for word the same because he wrote the book. It was harder than everyone said it would be, but still one of my easier classes. Homework every other week and 3 exams with a final. Homework is pretty hard and the exams have tricky questions.

Was told by an adviser this would be an easy science class. False if you hate science. Lecture is the same as book. Don't bother going to class, just read the book and take notes. Offers little help when it comes to homework and the exams, while multiple choice, can be very tricky if you do not have a good grasp of the book's every detail.

BORING class. I dreaded going to every class.  People say this is an "easy science" ... but if you do NOT like science, it's really not that simple.  I hate science, and he always says that a lot of material is "intuitive," but that is a problem when you don't think like a "science person." Don't buy the textbook, it's literally the same as lecture

The best TEACHER I've had so far. His lectures are very informative, and right when you start to lose interest, he throws in a witty joke or two. Lectures exactly follow the book that he wrote from his class notes, so you don't absolutely have to go to class, but they definitely clear some concepts up. Easy AB or A if you actually do the homework.

Prof. Martin is fantastic. Easily one of the best I've had at the UW. He is a WONDERFUL teacher. He really understands what it means to TEACH students and how important that is. He's great at explaining the concepts and always puts it in terms that everyone can understand. His exams & homework are fair. If you study, you'll have no problems.

The man knows how to insert jokes in at the right time of lecture! Lectures are good, not mandatory, but go to them, so you know what will be tested and what will not. Class is a little bit harder than I thought it would be, homework is graded, so make you sure you do it. Tests are also a little harder than expected.
He is AWESOME!

Martin is the man! I had 0 interest in this class when I first signed up, but he makes this class worthwhile and fun. Enthusiastic and funny lecturer.  Clearly explains all concepts and is always willing to help outside of class. Tests aren't easy, but if you study and have a good grasp on the concepts, it isn't difficult to do well.

The guy's very enthusiastic and clearly knows what he's talking about. That said, the exams are hard. Definitely not an easy A type class. Everything he lectures on is in the book almost word for word so attendance is not super important. Kind of a lot of homework. Definitely don't take the lab - RIDICULOUS amount of work for only one credit.

I did not have a good experience with this class. The homework was a surprising amount of work, but you have a fair amount of time to do it in. The exams were HARD and you really have to know the material and how to apply it to real life problems. The only way I would recommend this class to someone is if they are truly interested in W&C.

Martin is one of the best professors I've had. I'm not a "science person" and I received an A in the class, but I did study for the tests and took my time on the homework. He's very friendly and makes class interesting. If you attend lecture, do the homework, read the book, and study up a bit, this should be an easy physical science credit.

He is a great teacher who enjoys teaching but i would say that his class is HARD unlike other comments mentioned here. I aimed for an A and I got BC on my first test. I managed to take it up to AB but it's almost impossible to get A in this class. Tests are thought required and there is not much practice exams that we can try out.

Great professor, extremely enthusiastic, makes it fun to attend lecture. Self-written textbook mirrors lectures. Four exams and 7 homeworks. An absolute expert who clearly enjoys teaching. Very friendly at office hours, holds own review sessions. Easy and fun science credit.
One of the best professors at Madison. Take this class with Martin

His lectures are right from his book, which are just his notes he's come up with through his career. The class is so interesting, Martin does a great job! And actually uses funny jokes. 4 Exams, 7 Homeworks, and you get to drop the lowest one. I dont think its as easy as everyone says, but either way its a great class for a physical science credit
Great Prof. Knows material very well, and anything not in lecture will not appear on test. Very clear examples, and holds his own exam review, not TA's.

Prof wrote the text you use, so lectures are very similar to book. Exams are rather difficult, so i recommend studying the book/notes WELL before exams. Don't recommend taking the 101 discussion. Overall, lectures are very entertaining and worth getting up for.
Great teacher, wasn't really too excited about weather until I took the class.  Class was actually enjoyable to go to. Martin is a great guy, with a great Boston accent.

Great professor, very entertaining in class. His Boston accent makes class even better. He wrote the textbook for the class, and his lectures come from the book. Don't take any other weather and climate class.

Martin is an awesome professor! Never went to class after first midterm because eveyrthing he says in lecture is in his "own note" textbook. 3 midterms, 7 hw and final (like midterm). Homeworks are challenging and toughly graded but easy science credit
4 exams, homework due every other Friday. He's a great guy, super helpful, really interesting lecturer. I think his old school slides were fine.

Great prof. Very passionate and honestly cares about the students. Biggest gripe is that he uses crude, hand drawn overhead transparencies for all the diagrams and notes. The guy is a scientist with a PhD--it's not as if he is unable to use PowerPoint... Homeworks are fairly toughly graded. First test is very easy, other three a lot tougher.
by far the greatest professor i have ever had in my life. relatively easy science credit.... attendance wasn't mandatory but go anyway, he's a great speaker.

He's awesome. You can definitely tell he loves the weather. He doesn't mind giving the whole class an A. The homework and the exams can be a little difficult sometimes, but if you study and read the book you should be fine. I would recommend this class.
Don't expect to get a good grade on your homework. Tests are not that bad, but people in the class are doing really well, so it's hard to get an A, but easy C,BC, and B.

Prof. Martin is the best teacher ever in UW-Madison. Although I am not good at physical science, Martin's class will bring you a lot of fun. He talks about current weather for 15 mins every class and has a really good ton of the rest materials. BTW, 3cr is much more easier than 4cr with discussion.
great prof.
Prof. Martin made what would have been a very boring class interesting, but all of his lecture material is in his book so you don't actually have to go to class.

One of the most incredible professors out there, this class puts together everything you learned in calculus, physics, and dynamics. It also was the hardest I ever worked for any class in my college career. This class requires 15 hours/week outside of class, more at times. Did I mention he's the lead singer in a band?

Great professor and I would highly recommend him to anyone. He loves answering questions, genuinely cares about the kids, and obviously enjoys what he does. His examples in class are great. Homework is graded a bit harsh, but rest of the class is fair.
Absolutely great professor.  I learned a lot and it's not a tough course and he makes it fun.  Let's just say if all professors were like him the UW would be gold standard of the world.

Quite honestly the best professor I've ever had.  Is completely in love with weather, and it shows.  Very engaging, clear and fun to listen to.  You don't have to go to class, but he's so great that I did anyway.  You rule, Prof. Martin!

Lec's are 15 min of weather report, 35 min sudoku. He is probably the nicest professor and he is very engaging. HW started out simple, but then 3 were incredibly hard and I couldn't even find the answers online. I nailed the EC and pulled off an A, but I didn't do so hot on the midterms. Curved ALOT. Easy to skip. Highlight in the text as he talks.

professor martin is a legend. he is the man. you dont have to go to lecture, but people still went because he's sweet. full of energy, clear, good examples, engaging and funny. lecture is right out of the book, which he wrote. tests are straightforward. take the class! you'll learn a lot, but youll also spend 3 hours/week with the coolest man alive

Prof Martin is a great professor with tons of energy and so much enthusiasm for his subject.   The material itself gets a bit heavy, but if you get lost in lecture, his textbook is literally a script of the lecture, so I usually felt confused in lecture, but once I caught up in the reading, understood the material fine and did well on tests.  If yo

He's a great professor! Keeps the class engaged, and very funny! Textbook is not necessary if you attend all lectures. Don't do the lab if not necessary. A lot more work than the 1 credit it's worth. Oh, he also spends about 15 minutes every lecture to talk about current weather. Really interesting! Take it!

Not entirely necessary to attend lecture, but that's just because it copies the textbook which he wrote. Martin's great at teaching a potentially difficult subject with great clarity, both in writing and in lecture, and he's genuinely excited about doing so. Highly recommended.

Top of the line at UW! Martin is a compelling lecturer AND guy outside of class. My area of study is far from weather and climate, but I loved this course. The text (which he wrote) is easy to read and follows his lectures precisely.  Still, lecture is interesting and revelant.  Great prof with a great Boston accent :)

I took his 101 course as a freshamn 8 years ago, and even though I majored in something completely different,  he and his class always stood out in my mind as one of the most enjoyable.  Incredibly nice and did a great job making the subject interesting.  I love you professor Martin!

You need to get this prof for this class.  Textbook is very condensed which means the 4-5 page reading assignments are filled with a lot of info.  Very passionate about this subject and it shows.  I usually read the section of the textbook 3 or 4 times before the tests and did pretty well.  Each section is only about 20-25 pages long.

Martin is totally cool. He wrote the book... using his lecture notes, so it's all right there. He loves what he teaches, and he makes class fun. Don't be mistaken though, studying and reading the notes HELPS A LOT. He even let me reschedule a midterm to go see an NCAA tournament game. Too bad I never got to see his band perform though...

greatest man ever. so cool, very interesting and funny. highly recomend this class and this prof. final was 37questions, finished in 25 minutes. easiest class of my life and yet i learned a lot and was interested

Professor Martin is one of the best, if not the greatest, professor at the UW. He's very knowledgeable and makes everything easy to understand, although some of the more difficult topics just can't be dumbed down for everybody. He's very friendly and approachable outside or after class. The optional discussion section is pretty good, too.

Dr. Martin is not only interesting, but he condenses and simplifies the material so it's accessible for everyone, he has sincere enthusiasm for what he teaches, he is absolutely available and willing to help his students, and his Boston accent is awesome. The honors option is fun.
Excellent teacher, very clear when describing concepts and always willing to help students both in and outside of class, also students learn a lot of applicable concepts in the class

Perhaps my favorite prof ever!  I wish I could take him again.  He is hilarious, smart, and very nice.  Plus the exams are pretty simple.  Take this class!  One piece of advice: don't take the optional discussion if you don't have to, it actually brought my grade down to an AB.
Take this class!  Doc Martin is the best prof. i've had at the UW.  If you read the book (20 pages) or go to lecture you will get an A.  Good guy, good class.

Jon Mahten is a GREAT prof. Every word of his lectures is in his coursebook. Read it well and you'll never need to go to class. Puts science into simple, mainstream terms, lots of examples, even offers EC. Does NOT rush you into anything. I imagine this course would drive science-oriented people insane. However, blow it off and you're screwed.
Very easy class. Martin is a great teacher, and everything is really easy to understand. Textbook is really small but just read each section 3-4 times before the test and you should do fine.

Prof. Martin is hysterical. He has a really thick Boston accent and he actually makes the topic tolerable. Do all the homework and study for the exams and you'll do fine. He's really great about office hours and going to him for help. If you need the physical science credit take this class, but only if you can get Martin!
Martin is hilarious and loves what he does.  Very helpful if you need it. Textbook is 70 pages and work load is very minimal.  He is a great professor.  Good 4 credit science class.
hes so enthusiatic its funny
Maaaaaaaahtin is a pretty good professor. He seems very helpful and makes things clear. His class is pretty easy. I'll get an A and skipped about half of it.

Seriously has to be one of the best professors on campus. Makes class interesting and fun. He has an awesome Boston accent. I definately recommend taking this class with him. With a little investigating (searching on the internet) you can find the answers to the homework from an old department website.

I loved his class! I wasn't very interested in this class, but Martin is so fun to listen to that he changed my mind! He always tells stories from experience and makes the class laugh. He also wrote the textbook, so it's very accessible and easy to read. Highly recommend this class.
teaches weather in very applicable way

Very good class and very good professor.  I was almost tempted to change my major after taking Weather and Climate with Professor Martin.  I would highly recommend taking this class with Professor Martin.

She's an absolute chiller. She makes an effort to learn peoples names and build rapport with students. She walks through examples at a really good pace and gives plenty of opportunity to think about the material during lecture. She's generally just a really nice and positive person. Just don't pack up early during lecture; she hates it.

Dr. J is by far one of the best professors to have for Math 221 and Math 222. Her lecture notes were organized, easy to read, and easy to annotate. She also gave "you try questions" during the lecture, which I found to be helpful. She is relatable and listens to students. She would even go back and cover material again if there was confusion.
Awesome! She is a very lenient grader
office hours are extremely helpful. great professor and is always happy to help
Best math professor, had great lectures, really cared about her students and how they did in the class. She makes this difficult class a lot more bearable and easier to understand
For a notoriously difficult class, Janoski is the best you can ask for. This is a difficult class, but she makes it far easier. Would recommend
Great teacher, will miss her for calc 3
Best Math professor ever, her lectures literally saved my math 222 grade.
Very funny, but also good lectures, good explanations
Dr. J is great, made me actually want to show up for lecture. Clearly cares about her students.

Dr. J is a great lecturer. She always brought good energy to lecture, explained things well, posted all the slides after class and answered questions. For Math 222 in general, it was harder to prepare for the exams this semester because the curriculum was recently adjusted so Midterm 2 and the final were a little different from previous years.
Has online lectures that can be downloaded and used for annotations. Great teacher in lecture and office hours. Amazing at answering questions.

Dr. J was a good professor and explained lectures in a way that made sense to me. However, the practice in lecture was 10x easier than what was on the exam, which is frustrating. I also highly advise against taking this class if you have more than a semester between taking Calc I and don't take with physics 207, as they have exams back to back.

Lectures contain lots of practice, which is helpful. She will stop and make sure questions are answered before going onto the next slide. You can tell she loves what she's doing which makes the content all the more engaging.
Good professor and easy to understand lectures. Beware that the three exams are worth 87 percent of your grade. But if you go to lectures and watch yt videos you should be okay
Incredibly friendly and cares about the students
Excellent lectures. Plenty of clear explanations and examples. All the slides from the lecture are posted in canvas.
She keeps calc lectures somewhat fun and engaged.

Dr. J was a great professor. She very relatable and she made the lectures engaging. Dr. J made a great effort to get to know the names of all the students in the class. I thought she did a great job at explaining concepts, except for a few occasions where some important topics were kind of glazed over.

Dr. J is one of the best Math teachers/professors I have had. She does a great job during lecture's explaining concepts and making sure you understand the topics. The class itself is hard in nature, but she does a great job explaining each topic.

Dr. J is great.  She made the lectures entertaining and interactive.  She is also always willing to answer questions.  The only problem is your grade is basically 3 test, but there is nothing she can do about that.

Took this class in Fall 2024, it was my first class as a freshman. Dr. J made it very easy to do good in this class because of the great lectures. I would recommend that you go to every lecture because it is very easy to fall behind in Math 222. However, I never skipped a class, attended discussion, and took notes and I ended the class with a 99%.

Dr. J was super sweet, and you could tell that she values making personal connections with her students! One frustrating aspect of the class is that we had three exams, each worth 29%...  if you have one bad exam, it is pretty difficult to work yourself back up (this is standard for all calc professors:( )

Dr. J is a very good professor (and mathematician, I don't know). Her lectures are lively and fun, she likes to describe herself in the third person, and she likes to make little jokes.
Math is boring and difficult for most people, but Dr. J really tries to make the points understandable and accessible to more people!

Dr. J is amazing. She is super friendly and will try to learn everyone's names in lectures. Her slides are organized and she teaches very clearly. Expectations are laid are well. There was even a slight curve at the end of the class which was nice. Do lots of practice problems and you will succeed! Highly recommend her!!!
She cares about her students, but the entire grade is basically based off of 2 midterms and 1 final exam.  Exams were hard, and concepts are only covered once in lecture with no review.

Dr. J is the first person to ever make me not dread going to a math class. She is an incredible professor who cares a lot about her students, even getting to know most students' names. She makes lecture a safe place to ask questions, interesting, and dare I say fun. I would straight up defend her with my life, she's changed my whole mindset on math

Sets up concepts well so class has a good flow and really seems to care about students! Gives great resources for exams so it's not hard to succeed, but discussions can be pretty unhelpful depending on your TA. Grade is mostly based on 2 midterms and the final, so might not be a good fit if you struggle with test taking.

Dr. J is my favorite professor I've had so far! She's very funny and obviously cares about the material. Her teaching was very clear in lectures and she was very helpful during in class exercises. Take her class!!!!

I was not very talented in Math in high school but Dr. J lectures make me become interested in this major and I have become smarter than before. I can also feel her constant kindness and patience. Highly recommend her!

She's the best lecturer I've ever had. She made an effort to get to know her students and made sure to help. She was very organized and explained concepts thoroughly and often makes jokes during lecture.

The best math lecturer! Her lecture notes were nicely organized. She was very clear about the content we needed to know for exams. She explained concepts very thoroughly and made them easy to understand. She was also a very sweet person. She made an effort to get to know her students. I would recommend her to everyone!

THE GOAT. She is the best lecturer I have ever had. She is an amazing person herself. Her lecture notes are amazingly set up. Her way of explaining things is wonderful. I do not have enough room on here to explain how amazing she was. She actually got to know her students by namel. All the other math professors need to learn how to teach from her.

Took poli sci 400 on dictator with Prof. Weeks. Started out with 1 or 2 assignments a week, but halfway through, all assignments disappeared. Spent days reviewing for exams and gave you questions directly from them. If you listen in class and do some of the readings, you will be fine.
Theres a lot of readings every class and you have to participate a lot. She expects a lot tho

Readings every class. Assignments almost every week. But don't let that scare you. Professor Weeks is great at what she does. The grading criteria for some things could be more clear, but her and her TA provide a decent amount of feedback on assignments. If you go to class, pay attention, and participate, you'll do well in this class.

Professor Weeks is wonderful. She's extremely encouraging, kind, knowledgeable about the content, and facilitates excellent class discussions. She cares about every student and works to integrate student feedback & make her course as accessible and straightforward as possible. Very responsive via email and helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unclear grading criteria for short assignments; readings were not always useful; student feedback was accepted, but tried to justify the reasoning for certain things that came across as defensive; did encourage participation from everyone; relied on your personal reflection for participation grade; get ready to write a LOT for your final

There were long readings due twice a week, essential that you read them to be prepared for the lecture, which was centered entirely on the readings. Professor Weeks was clearly knowledgeable about them and foreign policy in general. Simulation grading was a bit unclear, but overall a good addition to an otherwise reading/writing only class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor and her TA, Andrew Fairley, were consistently lackluster in their grading and course quality. Both were repeatedly unprepared, yet they graded us with an unreasonable level of perfection. It is sad to see this, as they were both nice people. The professors credentials do not reflect her level of quality in the course.

Professor weeks is not knowledgeable in her field. There were times where she didn't understand the concepts of a particular reading. Given her credentials, you'd imagine she be the  best at what does but that is not the case. Everything is graded very unfairly and the expectations do not meet her performance.  Midterms were not well throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader for projects but tests were generally easy. If you understand key terms and regularly attend lectures you'll do fine in the class, but getting an A will take extra grind. Great teacher, but 170 was eh. Maybe more a fault of class and circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor. One thing I appreciate is how she clearly outlines what will be tested in the midterm and the final exams. She also provides numerous resources on Canvas for study purposes. The grading is fair. Overall, this class is heavy on lectures and memorization, but if you put in effort, it shouldn't be a big deal
She bores me and doesn't really explain anything. Also, grades are mostly based on the midterm and final. But, she is really good at pointing at and reading directly of the slides.

Professor Weeks is great! She is really understanding of her students needs. The readings in the class get pretty long and detailed, but she is good about outlining the main ideas in lectures and only putting what she talks about in lectures on the exams. Discussion sections are difficult though if you don't do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is knowledgeable about her field of study and pleasant to talk to, but her grading style is a bit frustrating. You either write too much or not enough, and it gets irritating after a while. Got A's on my written projects, but then received an A- in the course because I didn't speak up enough in class (according to her). Super disrespectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Weeks for required research methods. She's a good professor and it's a good class especially if you don't want to get deep into stats but want more of an overview of all the different methods.
I really enjoyed this class. Professor Weeks is super kind and the material was pretty interesting but not too hard.

If you are interested in learning about how to run surveys and experiments in the social sciences you could take this class... or you could read the book in about a quarter of the time. This is not the course for you if you are an ambitious PS major.

Professor Weeks is amazing! Although it was an online course, and I did not get to meet her in person, you can tell she really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. The class was not too bad and is really concept based, so if you're nervous about math/research, I wouldn't be. Really gentle course!
Professor Weeks is the real deal. Most classes are not fun but I loved this one. The simulation was an awesome activity. Tip: do the readings, they help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Weeks exemplifies the depressing situation of a grade A scholar with B to C levels of teaching techniques. Over the course she tactfully inserted Q&A and group discussion sessions to fill the time thats supposed to be used for actually teaching the course material. Also, the instruction style is a bit dry and bland. Please dont bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super easy class, and she gives opportunities for extra credit. I think the exam average was a B or an AB  come to class/discussion and youll probably get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fine but forgettable. Very easy material. Occasional short papers but little else; supposed to do readings but fairly easy to b.s. Make sure to know concepts from readings and class for tests though - tests are fairly challenging. Uses Tophat so be sure to show up
Good prof
not an easy class but lectures are clear and professor is nice. posts slides online which is helpful.

Weeks isn't a bad Prof, the nature of the class made it difficult to teach. She often took substantial time out of class to explain the assignments to the students. The class requirements and what it does for the Political Science major need to be changed, I felt as though it was trying to be both "on the surface" and "in-depth." Which is too much

Weeks is nice, but this class was harder than I expected for being a 200 level course. A lot of concepts were left vague and you really had to work to get a decent grade. Since it's now required for the poli sci major, there's no way around this class unless you want to take a full on statistics course.

She is very fun and laid-back, but also a knowledgeable professional in the field of acting who will help you grow. Be prepared for a decent amount of self-reflection writing and script analysis work as homework though.
Super fun and engaging class! Teacher is so kind and genuinely cares about her students. Super easy grader and easy to get an A on the papers.

Jess makes the class so fun and engaging, and is very understanding of our lives outside the classroom. You are graded on a bunch of different things so you have opportunities to keep your grade high. You are required to attend two University plays and you also do two performances, a monologue and a scene with a partner. Cannot recommend more!

Jess was, without a doubt, the best professor I had this semester! She is truly the kindest, most compassionate individual, and has been nothing but supportive. She created such a safe and comfortable environment, regardless of whether you had prior acting experience or not, and she is very passionate about theatre. Would 100% recommend!

Jessica is amazing! She makes everyone feel so welcome and comfortable. This was my first acting class ever, and I took it just because I had some extra credits and it sounded fun, and it really was! This class was everything I wanted. It got me out of my shell and taught me to be more in touch with myself and my emotions. Highly recommend.

He almost never finished the slides in class and would either post a video finishing them or finish them at the beginning of the next class. Likes to draw diagrams instead of putting them on the slides.

I could tell he liked what he was teaching and felt that his exam was pretty fair. It was a lot of content in a small amount of time, and the lecture slides were not the most helpful, but overall manageable if you take good notes.
He was chill. More importantly he made a fair third exam. Bro is the goat

Jere definitely covered the most content of the three 151 professors, but he was also highly engaging, passionate, and genuine. The exam he wrote was still manageable. He models his lectures off the textbook and has super helpful lecture notes on his slides. I would've loved to have all three units taught by him!
Have to pay attention in lecture. He covers the most difficult content so people hate him for it, but he is very accessible outside of class and helpful.

Dr. Yahn covers arguably, the most difficult and largest quantity of content. However, he is quite helpful in office hours (the week of the exam he held 16ish hours of review). I felt the final reflected what was taught and expected of us to know. Jer is a good lecturer that clearly cares about phys + students. Don't let the low reviews scare you!

Few notes after reading the reviews left here that genuinely do not represent reality:

- Teaching style has obviously changed since 2019. Old reviews no long apply. Lectures incredibly designed + OPEN THE SPEAKER NOTES THATS WHERE THE NOTES ARE! Jeez.

- Very kind and funny man. Respects the learning process, teaching, and cares about students.

He's a really funny professor who really tries to help students understand the content. The only problem that I've experienced is that he tends to get off topic and make mistakes about small details in content. However, as long as you study (Animal Phys is a difficult subject in general), ask questions, and go to office hours, you should be ok.
The wording of his exams are horrible and his lectures are super boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: insanely difficult and so much material is covered. The final exam, although not cumulative, certainly felt like it with the amount of material that was needed to be learned.

I have to say I do not take up my time to EVER to rate a professor and usually do not care that much about how a professor is, so this when you know it's bad. His portion of the class is extremely content heavy.  The problem is that he for one teaches this material at the very end of the semester along with his slides been horrible to review.

I understand it is so content heavy, but we need lecture slides that make sense and students can use to study. The slides are literally pictures of animals or diagrams that we don't even need to know. Too much information taught in the span of 5 weeks and lots of students are struggling.
Awful organization. Don't waste ur time on all of the slides notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jer was my favorite prof this semester. I had him for animal phys, which is a content-heavy section, but that's just how the subject is. You're going to get out what you put into it. He's chill, just happens to teach a difficult course. TIP: His slides don't have many words on them, but he has lecture notes you can easily download from Canvas.

I liked Dr. Yahn overall. His exam was harder than Blair's, but I think that's because Yahn has so much more content to cover and it's more complicated. There were times when I was confused about what was actually going to be on his exam, because there was a lot of optional information presented. You can tell he genuinely loves what he teaches.

This professor is by far one of the worst in the bio department. Jeremiah Yahn is a very arrogant person overall, and his tests are NOT representative of the immense amount of material covered in lecture. His tests tend to extrapolate, and some of the questions are just designed to be missed by all students. Switch lecture ASAP if you get him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jer teaches all the biology lectures he does because he genuinely loves what he teaches. He gives optional more materials to learn about but keeps it clear that its not going to be on exams, and the stuff he teaches are actually very interesting and fun.

He was fine... I mean overall he was funny and easier to listen to than professor Blair (who did the first 2 sections).  However, slideshows were messy and hard to understand what we needed to know.  I probably should have read the text, but I didn't and still got an A.  Note than his exam will be MUCH harder than Blair's (aka the last exam).

I really liked Dr. Yahn's lectures, I felt as though he taught for students understanding rather than just exam preparation. He started out each lecture with a narrative that was quite applicable and interesting. I would definitely recommend going to office hours as the key to understanding the course material was to go over what was in lecture.
Rude and inconsiderate, no grace on late assignments/extenuating circumstances
