Dr. Zelewski is overall a great professor, however your TA is more helpful as discussion is where you will do most of your practice problems and be able to ask more questions. Hopefully you get a good TA! In lecture TopHat is used frequently. The slides are posted the night before lecture so I recommend taking notes before lecture, it really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Linda uses tophat ALOT so make sure you go to class. She also gives a quite bit of homework but if you practice the homework questions a couple of times before the exam, you will do well. There is a slight curve at the end of the semester so do not stress out much. She is super helpful and accessible outside classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You better hope you have a great TA, because the prof is utterly useless as an instructor. Exams have very little to do with the material presented in class. Be ready to memorize formulas for an exam, or derive them, because the formula sheet for the exam is pitiful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I liked Linda as a professor but my main problem was with my TA. He wasn't very good at explaining anything so that is where I mostly struggled. Linda is pretty good at teaching, the course is just difficult. Be prepared for lots of homework and studying. Attendance is MANDATORY to understand course material and answer TopHat questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One key advice is ASK QUESTIONS. She enjoys it best when students do this so I highly advise it. The class overall is a workload but every effort will be worth it. Dr. Zelewski is extremely in the sense that she teaches A and tests A. The curriculum is tough so grading is tough but it's not the professor's fault. Attendance is adivised for TOPHAT.
Professors who teach freshman level courses are the true heroes.
Awesome professor in general

Linda is an average-at-best professor. She has an annoying voice, loses track of time in class, spends way too long on things in lecture, always lose our "review day" because things get pushed back. Her lectures, then, didn't line up with the discussions. She also takes a very long time to get grades back and has a confusing grading structure

Linda basically reads off of her powerpoint for lectures and does not explain things otherwise. It is mandatory to go class because of the tophat, however, to do well in her class you need to use your TA and ask questions. Also, be prepared to study independently for her exams.

Not a bad professor by any means, but not really great either. Exams were fair (from what I've heard, easier than other chem 104 professors), and she provides plenty of materials to prepare for them. If you do all the material you can besides what is required and budget your time effectively then the class isn't too bad.

Zelewski was the better of the 2 general chemistry professors that I had. She was very good at explaining the tough concepts in chemistry 104 and made things simple for us to understand. Her exams were easier than the rest of the professors for chem 104, they were very straightforward and never any tricks.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: She seems to be a nice person. Chemistry is hard in general, but when the pre class doesn't line up with what we do in class, it can sometimes be confusing. Majority of the time we were let out early, which was probably the reason why we were a week behind than what was anticipated. Also recommend getting a tutor or enrolling in the CLC.

I actively dreaded every single lecture with Linda. She spends too long on tophat, then doesn't explain the answer well even if a significant number of people got it wrong. She ever finishes her slides but somehow lets us out early, blames us when the test average is low, and once refused to answer a question in class. She's not hard she's just bad
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Obviously Chem is difficult, so the class was definitely challenging. But Linda is more generous on the exams I have heard. Very heavy on tophat questions during lecture, so pre-class is important.
Decent at explaining concepts. Never finishes all the slides. Spends 5 minutes at the beginning of the class talking about nothing that is relevant to chemistry. Annoying voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Zelewski was amazing. I had her for a summer course and enjoyed going to lecture. She made it worth it for me to show up because her demos were helpful. The exams werent too bad and the final was fairly easy
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: moves very fast in lecture, yet makes the material clear. Uses tophat a lot in lecture which can be annoying cause she spend 5 min on a tophat question yet 30 seconds on a slide filled with info. Super approachable and pretty fair tests
Never finishes lectures on time. Incapable of explaining complex material without getting confused. Literally explained how to make a notecard 0/10 do not recommend

Good professor who explains the concepts very well. Lectures are basically a set of top had question to test your understanding which is great. Go to lecture, do the top hat questions seriously and you wont need to study much more to get an A

Zelewski's lectures can be helpful if you print the slides ahead of time or take notes on your computer; she flies through her lecture slides very quickly so make sure, if you write your notes, you can write fast. She also does a lot of TopHat questions which are difficult but she gives quite a bit of time for her students to complete them.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zeleweski's lectures are very straightforward as she heavily relies on top hat questions more than she explains concepts. She moves very fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I had her for 104 only and I think she really keeps her lectures entertaining by heavily relying on top had questions. I think this really help understand the material she's teaching. The exams are fair, even thought she seems to like putting one very tricky question per exam. If you work enough you can definitely get A

I had Linda for 103 and 104 and I thought Linda was a great professor. She wants her students to succeed and she makes that very possible as long as you can keep up with the work. Her in-class questions are helpful and make this course feel less like a large lecture because it is more interactive. I would take another course with Linda.

The way that Linda structured this course makes it easy to succeed if you do the assigned work. Although I often skip readings for classes I found that if I did the pre-class reading/homework and post class homework I did not need to do much to prepare for exams because the in-class questions are really helpful for better understanding the material
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Zelewski rarely makes it through all of her slides, she skips over information during lecture, and you end up teaching yourself chemistry most of the time. Many times, she assigns quizzes in which you learn the content after the quiz has been taken.

Is super robotic in lecture, and seems to teach just go through the motions of teaching. Tests are pretty difficult and if you don't fully understand the material, they are very challenging. Grades pretty harshly but gives a lot of materials to study for. Grade is largely dependent on TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Had her for chem 104. Lectures were boring and not very helpful when it came to understanding information, she basically read off her slides and clicked through them without explaining stuff very well. Didn't give practice exams or problems before her exams. Exams were pretty much multiple choice and much harder than the material we did in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is super nice, but her test a very difficult. Multiple choice is worth more than the short answer and you are not given many opportunities to get partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Linda moves fast in class and her top hat questions are graded for accuracy not just participation so going to lecture is necessary. She does not give a lot of practice material so seek it out on the chemistry website and do practice problems. She won't test on stuff from hw, only lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: 103/104!! Professor Zelewski is an intelligent professor who is  up-to-date about Chemistry. You must pay attention during lectures because she moves fast and briefly covers topics. Her class is basically based off of your three exams and the final exam. This is not an easy class and you must work for your grade. Heavy lectures and heavy homework.

Linda was far from an ideal teacher. She basically teaches with tophat questions which are graded for accuracy which means you literally cannot skip a single class. Her voice is also kinda annoying and she doesn't give enough materials to review for the exams. On the first exam we got one short practice test, and we got nothing for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had her for 103 and 104 and both were relatively straight forward. At the root of it, chemistry is hard regardless of the professor but she made an effort to make it not as hard. The curve is based off of the whole lecture and is usually super generous, like 73+ has been an A. Do the work, go to class, get help if needed, and you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Linda is a great chemistry professor! Her lectures have a good mixture of content and examples, and the tests are not too hard. I definitely recommend her as your teacher!

Linda isn't as bad as everyone says she is. Her exams are fair. In my opinion, Linda's Chem 104 course is much easier than Chem 103. I found the Chemistry Learning Center worksheets really help when studying for exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor does not clearly explain material and spends more time on clicker questions than actually teaching. Very tough grader, and often has hardly discussed material on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Linda is a great person, however I would not want her as my teacher. She reads really fast from the slides and expects you to know it right away. Although on the surface it may seem like she is explaining things in reality she is not.

She really knows what she's talking about and her lectures are pretty straight-forward. Don't skip lecture, there are tophat attendance questions. Class is pretty hard and a lot of work, but that's not necessarily because of Linda, that's just the gen chems. I really liked her teaching, would recommend as a prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall good lecturer, fairly easy class if you show up and do all assigned work.

Shes straight forward, a good lecturer, understands what she's doing, and grades fairly. I don't expect anything else from a college professor. As long as you do the HW, go to lecture, and study well you'll be fine. I don't understand why her rating is low.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Zelewski is really good at what she's doing. The class is not difficult if you knows something. Her grading criteria is the easiest among all 104 professors.

Dr. Zelewski has been one of my favorite professors by far. Everything she teaches in Lecture and the worksheets in discussion are reflective of the tests she hands out. The only vice I have is that her demonstrations in class don't always work, however this really isn't important towards chemistry knowledge. Would highly reccomend!
Loved her class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor, solid choice. Be prepared to be structured, organized, and prepared to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class works essentially as a flipped class where you learn content on your own before lecture and do examples in lecture. Linda also does tophat in lecture which means you pretty much have to go as part of your grade is based off of answering the questions. Beware of exam 2. Overall okay teacher with annoying voice.
This class might be easy if you like chemistry. Linda expects you to know a lot about chemistry before taking this class, so if you don't, you're going to have to put extra time into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Zelewski frequently has typos and other errors in her lecture presentations. Many of her demonstrations went wrong, almost as if she had never done them Before and spent no time preparing. She lost one of my lab reports and is forcing me to either redo the lab during finals week for credit, or take a zero on the lab.
Great professor, but a lot of material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her tests absolutely had nothing to do with her material.

Her lectures can be a bit disorganized. Sometimes she goes way too fast. Both my TA and tutor have said multiple times, "I'm not sure why she taught the material like that." Most of the lecture is spent reviewing prelecture stuff and doing TopHat questions. Most learning must be done on your own time. She is willing to help during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think her rating should be much higher. Her lectures a little robotic, but they are clear, concise, and well-organized. The class is a lot of work, but that's not necessarily by her choosing. She is friendly and available to answer questions. Her exams are fair and reward those who review the homework and discussion worksheets. Would recommend.

Class is taught well and going lectures are interactive, which I think helps with the learning of the material. There is a grade for attendance, which is taken through answering questions during class (not for correctness, just participation).

Dr. Zelewski lectures quickly but if you write down everything she writes on the chalkboard, you'll be fine. If you sit in front or near the center aisle towards the front, she will always be willing to help you. Midterm 1 is not too difficult, Midterm 2 is quite difficult, MidTerm 3 is all concept based. Make sure to do plenty of practice problems

Pros: very easy to understand, explains content well, available at office hours. Cons: one of the most boring people you will ever meet, puts content on exams that was not discussed in lecture, often does not finish lecture slides
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a very easy to understand professor. She does a good job of explaining concepts and seems to really care that students understand. I used to hate chemistry, and she makes it very fun! Definitely not the worst professor I've ever had.

Most of your grade comes from the tests, which are relatively straightforward, but not easy. She doesn't really go out of her way to trick you, and the tests are pretty much only on stuff you cover in lecture. She has lots of time for discussion during lectures, and if you sit near the front it is very easy to ask her questions during this time.

I took Chem 103 with her in the summer. It's probably pretty different from the academic year. In general, she is a very well organized professor and speaks very clearly. I recommend taking a course taught by her. She cares about her students unlike many other professors.

I funneled most of my time last semester into this course to finish all of the pre/post lab requirements and homework.  She does a good job of talking about the majority of the test content during lectures, and reading the textbook is helpful to reinforce the topics.

Prof Zelewski isn't the worst lecturer. She definitely knows her stuff and does a good job of getting the information out in lecture. The lecture problems are also very helpful in that they get concepts out there and can help teach them. Her tests are very difficult but partial credit is offered. Her lectures are a bit disorganized at times too.
Love her
She's clear, concise, and fair. It's what should be expected out of a professor. She didn't make me adore chemistry or anything but she did her job and taught me the material well.
Everything in class is quite clear to understand. What you need to do is to focus and put your own effort into it.

Fairly straightforward of a lecturer.  Not extraordinary and does problems on the board too fast to both write down and understand.  Tests are nothing like the problems learned earlier and are exceedingly difficult. Avoid if possible

She's alright. Not great, but not terrible either. She's one of those really smart professors, who understands the material so well, she sometimes makes it seem harder/more in depth than it actually is. Sometimes she lectures fast. But the most annoying part of the class were the tests. They were very hard and didn't reflect the lecture/homework.
Linda was very all over the place with notes during the lecture. Her tests were very challenging and didn't reflect the homework at all.

In lecture, I guess she's ok.  In that she covers the material and explains all equations, not well or to the level that would be ideal for a class that plays such a foundational role for the future success of so many people.  Her tests are also much harder than any practice material she gives you, and are graded very harshly.
Covers ALOT of material during lecture periods.

Linda's lectures are straight forward for the most part and not very confusing. They're power lecture though which can make them a little boring. As long as you can stay focused for that whole time you'll grasp the material and be fine. She is very helpful when asked a question and will re-explain confusing concepts if asked.

Not only a horrible teacher but a mean person as well. I once went to her office hours and she made me cry as she yelled at me saying I was not putting enough work into the class (even though I scored above the curve on the most recent test). You will put SO much effort into her class and get little outcome. She does not care about her students.

Great professor, lectures are really clear. Focus in lecture and you're good to go. Homework is expected but very efficient plus there's a problem solving session before the deadline to submit the online homeworks. Really great but requires a lot of money for textbook, iclicker and OWL homework.

Brutal at explaining things. Most lectures consist of her writing endless equations and calculations on the board.  She will answer questions during lecture, but it always seems as if she panics and most times her answers don't really apply to the question asked. Tests are fair enough, but multiple choice will get you. Not the best, but doable.

You're really gonna need to put in the work if you wanna get a good grade in her class. She's unclear in her explanations and makes mistakes sometimes which make learning the material difficult. Do the work and it's possibly to get an A though.

Zelewski is a horrible professor. She goes way too fast in lecture and does not stop to answer questions. When you do get the chance to ask questions outside of class she treats you like you are stupid. Tests are way harder than homework or lecture. You have no chance. If she is the only professor, take the class a different semester.
I don't like chemistry and I usually don't do well. But Linda is very clear and gives really fair tests. She explains concepts really well and gives many examples. I would take her for any class!
you will not do well with Linda. She has no desire to help students learn and is the toughest prof I have ever had. I went in thinking I would major in chem and left contemplating my own existence
Linda definitely knows what she's doing, but she talks at lightning speed and has a voice that will drive you nuts.

Professor Zelewski is really good for Analytical! She works fast, but she tells you exactly what you need to know for the exams. The book is fantastic for her class, so lecture attendance isnt totally necessary to get an A. Make sure you can do every weekly hw. The class is hard, but Zelewski makes it manageable!

Overall, Linda is a good professor. Her lectures are ridiculously fast paced, but if you can keep up, she gives you everything you'll need. Her office hours are incredibly helpful if you're not understanding the materiallabscalculations. This was my most demanding class; exams are intense, labs are long, and grading is tough.

I'm very confused by these reviews because I absolutely loved Zelewski. She's very enthusiastic and easy to listen to during lecture. The tests were very fair compared to other Chem profs I've had.  Do the readings, show up to lecture, and attend her weekly problem solving sessions if needed and you should be able to walk away with an A.
Dr. Zelewski was an okay teacher and seemed very nice but her tests were challenging.  She expected a lot of reading from the textbook and most of the material was just covered in class anyway.
you've got no chance man

Just help yourself out and don't take this class with her.  The multiple choice part of the exams worded very weird and are hard.  I ended up attending another professors lectures to understand the material.  If you have a good chemistry background however, you should be fine for Chem 103 with her.
Overall a very challenging class. You definitely have to put in a lot of work. Your TA could make or break your semester.

Linda rushed through her lectures, and towards the end of the semesters, the lectures turned into her just doing example problems on the board with no explanations. The second test is IMPOSSIBLE. Study hard. Worst chem 103 teacher out of the rest of them- try for someone else.
Sucked. Tests are the major part of the grade, but they are nothing like the lectures or the book. Overall a very difficult .professor and hardest tests I have ever taken

Labs are excruciating. Emailed her for help and she told me to meet with my TA and that she would be unavailable outside of her office hours. Exams were very difficult. Homework was lengthy, would take me around 6 to 7 hours to complete. Some demos in class were cool but her lectures were overall confusing. DO NOT TAKE CHEM 103 WITH HER!

Going to lecture is important, especially because she always included demos or examples on tests. Exams could be tough, including the final, and were very conceptual based. However, she set a pretty generous curve at the end of the class.
She tends to speed through some topics. A lot of work for the class, but it isn't too hard if you study. Attendance is technically non-mandatory, but there are clicker questions during lecture.

Go to lecture, discussion and actually read the textbook before lecture. Zelewski is actually a great professor, her tests just require you to conceptually understand the material which is difficult to do for a topic like chemistry. If you're willing to put forth some effort and go to review sessions this class is doable and can be interesting.

Great teacher when you approach her 1-on-1. Lectures were sometimes confusing and covered a lot of material that didn't go together. Midterm exams were fair, aside from one of them. Final was multiple choice and a little tricky, but class grades are curved at the end of the semester.

She was awful, and the class was awful.  The averages on most of the midterms were barely passing. They are extremely difficult, even if you go through all of her objectives.  Get a different professor for sure.

Take a different professor if you haven't taken APIB Chem. She's fine with having 9% of the class get an A. She doesn't explain in depth. Do all of the mastering chemistry. She helps a lot outside of class. She's boring to listen to. Need to go to class to know what she'll put on exam. Read the book.
Lectures are long and cover only the basics. She expects you to do a lot of the learning on your own by reading the textbook. Lots of Mastering Chemistry homework. Tests aren't too bad.

you can tell she's obviously passionate about chemistry which is nice. some of the material she covers she doesn't exactly explain in depth and just kind of assumes you know how to do it already. first time teaching chem 103 since 2009 and you could tell she was a little rusty. tests aren't too bad, except the second one on thermochemistry.

She flies in lecture and her tests are an abomination. She will mention very insignificant things in lecture that will be put on the test; for instance, on the periodic trends test she put all of the exceptions to the trends which she barely touched upon in lecture. Listen to every word she says in lecture if you want an A.

This was the first time Zelewski has taught 103 since '09, and it kind of showed. Overall she was a good professor, but wasn't always completely clear and assumed we knew some of the material. If you ask for help she is more than willing. Tests are similar to the practice and aren't bad if you get the concept and study. Helps to have a good TA also
The worst professor I had all semester. Her lectures are terrible.

She is a good professor and knows what she is talking about.  The readings will help you understand the lectures the better.  The tests are fair and the objectives are clear-cut.  There are daily questions that count for your grade so attend as many lectures as you can.

She is a very smart lady. However, she thinks in her head a lot and doesn't explain things very well. It was difficult to know what to study for the test. I found this class very difficult. On top of that, I had a horrible TA. The only thing that saved me was the CLC.

First off, she's listed in the staff as a lecturer, not even a professor. READ THE BOOK. Her tests are pretty tough. Class average was 65% on 2nd midterm. Study her quizzes, because there are similar questions on the exam. Honestly hardest class. It's a weed out class.

Teaches straight out of the book and doesn't cover everything in class she expects you to learn. You basically have to teach yourself everything in this class. You should go to lectures, but they don't help at all.
Attempts to teach out of textbook.
She talks way too fast in lecture and all she does is spit out numbers. I went to every lecture and I only passed one test out of 3. I would highly recommend getting a new professor.

I would not recommend Zelewski. She does not do a great job explaining the harder material and concepts in lecture, and the discussions are mainly spent on going over labs. The test objectives and old exam she releases are not good indicators of what the tests actually are.

Zelewski's lectures don't represent the material's complexity very well and does not go in depth enough to the point of what we need to know.  The T.A.'s are more helpful for the most part, but most of discussion is spent going over labs and not course material.  Zelewski's objectives for exams are awful and are horrible representations of the test
I overall enjoyed Professor Zelewski. the class is tough but that's what's to be expected for a chemistry course. She let us out early a lot

This course was not as hard as I thought it would be. I think it's seen as kind of a weed out class for freshman entering the natural sciences but it's still mandatory for many non science majors as a science breadth. If you have any interest in natural sciences she is a very good chem professor.
Would not recommend.  Has very annoying voice. Spends a lot of time going over the basics and then skims over anything more complicated.
Very nice to talk to

I absolutely love Zelewski! I thought you all should know that too! Yes she can go fast in lecture, but honestly she's the most clear professor and most organized woman ever. She tells you what you need to know for exams and that is all! I hardly ever read for her class, just followed along in lecture. I miss her as a prof.

Linda does seem to know Chemistry but has a hard time communicating to the class. She also doesn't seem to respond well to student questions in lecture or at all really. I've learned a lot more from the TAs - they're a lot easier to communicate with and seem to have a better understanding of common struggle points.
She seems like she knows what she is talking about.  Gets lost in her lectures which are hard to follow.  Test are really hard, Labs are long and some what hard.

She becomes a little scatterbrained in her lectures, but if you pay attention you'll be fine. Do all of the homework, and use the practice questions to study for exams. She holds problem solving sessions before exams: go to them! If you have a question in lecture, be sure to sit near the front and you'll be able to ask it right in class.

She know's what she's talking about in terms of Chemistry. However, no one else in the class does. She talks extremely fast, and does not go over what I would say is roughly 90% of the material for tests. I specifically came to RMProfessor to try and help other students avoid taking this course with Linda.

Lynda was the most helpful professor I've ever had, that being said, homework was hard, labs were long, I failed the first exam. Really focus on the learning goals, after working super hard I ended with a B. The final was hell on earth.

Take how easy it normally is to make stupid mistakes in a college class and multiply that by a million for A Chem. She talks fast but is very helpful. There are no new concepts from gen chem but everything is more in depth. Tests are similar to homework, the homework is a pain though. Labs are busy and worth little.

Chem 104 is a hard class regardless of the professor.  Linda speaks fast and has a voice that is kind of hard to listen to after a while.  Every lecture is spent trying to keep up with her example problems at lightning speed.  Homework is lengthy and the exams she gives are harder than the practice exams provided.
Linda was good, the curve sucked, and if you do bad on one test it can really kill your grade. I had an awesome TA so that's the only reason I did moderately well. Also, her final was hell.

In my opinion, Linda was one of the best professors I've had at Madison so far. Very clear lectures that cover all the material on the exams. The midterms were tough, but very doable. She seemed a little crazy, but sometimes made funny jokes and did very cool demos.
She is a good though....clear and helpful....  The average of final is 60 percent, but before that less than 10 percent is over A ( no curve for the final grade). pray for others.

Linda is one of my favorite professors at UW Madison. She provides countless opportunities to get help if you do not understand the material and she truly cares about the success of her students. If you understand the exercises provided in discussion you will do fine on the exams. Definitely recommend taking chem 104 with  Linda!

Linda is a pretty good lecturer, however she at times speaks too fast. Attending class is mandatory because she has clicker points which count towards your final grade. The homework is fair and helps your grade, however her exams are absolutely awful. Her final exam was the worst exam I have ever taken. DO NOT trust the previous exams she posts.

Very poor lecturer, she may know the material but as others have said spends all lecture on easy material and then crams in the hard stuff right at the end if even at all. Labs do not parallel class and are graded harshly. No curve was given in our class even though exam averages were very low. Do not take this class, you will regret it.

Very difficult teacher, you have to work hard if you want to get a good grade. There is little to no curve. You will get the grade you get. So if you are not strong in chemistry and depend on the curve, take someone else. Provides many materials for test and just do practice problems.

Dr. Zelewski is a great professor and she provides you with many tools and resources to do well on the exams. She can speak quickly during lecture at times but as long as you pay attention and take notes you will do well in the class. great professor!

She is awesome. Haven't gotten the chance to know her personally but as a professor she is great! Not only does she make Chemistry easier to understand she makes it more interesting. Her exams are fair. Choose her!

Very satisfied. She moves quite fast in lecture but there are TONS of opportunities to get help if you do not understand something. I've been able to do great on every exam so far simply by taking good notes and attending review sessions.

Linda is very helpful and wants everyone to succeed in her classes. She does not currently do research, so she is able to dedicate more time to students. She acts more as a teacher rather than just a professor. The exams are rather difficult, but she provides many options to get help if one is struggling.

I took her as a freshman during my first semester of college, as it was the only 104 class left open. She constantly feeds you information, and provides you with several examples. The MasteringChem homework was often a pain. Exams are usually tough. I did have an awesome TA, however.

Dr. Zelewski did an excellent job at teaching a tough course. She does write and talk very fast, but there is a lot of material to go over and she is clear and logical. If you are taking 104 it is probably because you need to know the material for other classes, instructors that give you an easy ride aren't doing you any favors in the long run.

She is TRASH!!!! Goes through the material extremely fast. Loves to talk hours about easy stuff then takes the last 10mins to talk about the things that are going to be on the exam. The exams play no games. Homework due a day before the exam even on the final exam. She has no heart.

Worst professor I have had so far. Terrible lectures during which she reads off a sheet of paper and STILL messes up example problems. Anything I learned I taught to myself. She also deliberately made one exam significantly trickier than the rest in the middle of the semester because the average was getting too high.

Exam averages: 57,81,54%. Incredibly hard teacher for an intro Chem course. Rushed thru examples on board, faced only the board, and explained concepts in labs after we turned them in. You can tell she is super smart, but horrible at teaching concepts. TAs didn't understand questions being asked. Dissatisfied and regret taking this course.
THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. she talks to the chalkboard,fails to explain things clearly, and the only reason I went to lecture was for clicker points TAKE ANY OTHER 104 PROFESSOR YOU CAN

NOT a good professor. She talks too fast in lecture & the examples that she uses aren't very helpful. 2/3 of the midterms were less than a 60% average. She seems to spend more time on the easier material & zooms through the more difficult things. If you can, get a different professor.

If you pay attention and do the assignments, this class is definitely tolerable.  I have never felt like she moved too fast.  The final grade is curved, so if you do above average on the midterms you can easily pull off an AB or better.

She rushed through everything, especially examples. Ridiculous amount of work for a general chemistry class. 2/3 exams the average was below 60%. Often, homework and labs are due BEFORE we even learn the material in lecture which is highly unfair for people with labs earlier in the week. Seek a different professor.

If you have a hard time copying notes and listening, I would not recommend. As others have said she speaks very quickly and rushes through examples and lecture. Two of our exams class averages have been under 60%, and one was 80%. She supposedly make the exam harder so our class average would fall. If you take her do a lot of practice problems
She's moves really fast and covers a lot of material in lecture but if you take notes and study you should get a good grade.

Linda is one of the most passionate, experienced, helpful, and motivated professors I have met at UW. In 2 lectures a week she concisely gets her point across and never rambles. There is a lot of work I this class: labs, weekly homework (long and challenging), 3 exams. Don't procrastinate and review the material every now and then ACHEM is details!
I learned a lot about chemistry, but more importantly, life.

As a lecturer she did a fairly decent job. She spoke fast but it was clear and there is a lot of content in this class. As long as you know your stuff the tests are simple and straightforward. Very, few trick questions. The stupid part of this class is out of her control: lab. It is long, boring, tedius, (negative adjective here).
Clear talking and writing. Show example questions that help a lot. Willing to help. Homework is not extremely easy and can be very helpful. What's on the exam is pretty clear.
She likes to talk...fast. Almost impossible to keep up with her on notes. She dragged out easy examples and skimmed over the hard ones. Definitely switch if you get her.
AVOID IF POSSIBLE. If you choose to take this class with her, make GOOD friends with the TA and hope yours is useful.

Doctor Zelewski is not an effective professor. Chem 104 is notorious for it's difficulty, and she made this class probably a hundred times more difficult with her sad attempts at teaching us the material. Every lecture was a rush, every exam was way beyond the level she taught. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!

Linda Zelewski is a horrible professor. She knows the material but is not effective at communicating it and teaching it at all. Her lectures are confusing and she rushes through the material so it is hard to keep up. Her exams are not fair and she allegedly made the third midterm harder because she thought the second exam average(~73%)was too high.

She moves way too fast through material and makes mistakes in her calculations during almost all her examples. You can tell she really doesn't care whether or not students are able to follow along during lecture. Plus she got lazier through the semester by using powerpoint so she didn't have to write as much on the board. I would not recommend her.

She goes way too fast in lecture to make sense of anything. She covers a vast amount of material in such a short amount of time that she doesn't always fully explain it she just states it.  The tests are very very difficult! she no longer lets you use a notecard which makes them very difficult to finish in the time allotted. I do not recommend her
I liked Organic better

Linda is great! She is a no-nonsense lecturer. Her lectures are to-the-point and she does many examples in class. HW is difficult, but basically just a reapplication of an example problem. The worst part of the class is the labs. Honestly, this is the best Chem course you'll ever take. You'll learn a lot of Chem from Linda in just one semester!

Linda herself is very nice and helpful, however the class it the worst. The curriculum includes basically the WHOLE textbook in 2 lectures a week, so she often is forced to rush through lectures and it is very difficult to keep up/retain all the information.  Homework and Exams are very difficult.

Professor Zelewski is very nice and will explain anything you need her to. Homeworks, labs, pre lab quizzes, and tests are very hard and require A LOT of time. you cannot go a day without doing something  related to this class or you will fall behind.
Lots of work and time required.  I loved chemistry before this class.

She has the most annoying accent ever, and she's not that great of a teacher. If you aren't already well versed in chem this will not be an easy class. I took three years in high school and I still couldn't get an A.
Good overall professor.  If you read the book and understand the concepts you will do fine.

If you understand the concepts, not just memorize the problems, you'll do well.  Read the book. Zelewski is 100% average, a chem robot, pretty much tells you what you need.  She lacks any personality but it won't really matter.  Nothing unexpected on exams.  For a TA, if you have Abruna, get on his good side early, and put in face time.

awesome prof. ready to help you when needed. you will struggle on her tests . shes not trying to fail you she just is challenging you. she will help you with anything and she will help you until you understand it

You will not do well unless you have a good TA. Angel Abruna is a horrible TA. If you get him, switch asap. He has a heavy accent that is incomprehensible at times and does a terrible job of explaining material.

I took regular chem in high school but there was a good amount of new material to learn. She covers a lot of material in a lecture and has a Sarah Palin-esque accent. Nothing is curved until the final so if everyone does bad on a quiz/lab/exam, then everyone gets a bad grade. Success = Make good exam notecards and have a helpful TA.
extremely boring and the midterms and final have random trick questions on them. I would suggest getting someone else.

She doesn't curve anything but curves the whole class pretty generously at the end.  Exams aren't too bad, pretty basic and straight-forward.  The problems in the book she recommends are applicable to what is on the midterms.  The final was tough, though; a lot of conceptually-based questions.

she's an ok professor. personally didn't do that great of a job explaining contents, so if you want to do well just read the book. overall her quizzes, and tests were very fair. her final is a bit tricky though and harder than the midterms.
Her final is hard and she doesn't curve

She goes way to fast in lectures. Exams are difficult, and have extremely random questions. Can use a notecard on exams, so that is helpful! Read the sections she's lecturing on before class and you'll be fine.

Pretty good prof. Explains the material well, isn't arrogant, in-class experiments are neat. Do the recommended homework and the class isn't so bad. She keeps the class very well informed on where to be in the textbook and when. Labs are tedious and don't contribute much to a knowledge of chemistry, but that's not really her fault.

super boring, annoying voice, lectures are pointless, cannot teach: all she does is do examples but she does not explain clearly, makes a lot of mistakes during lecture, i recommend another prof if possible

I would highly recommend this professor. All material that is on exams is gone over in class. She does move fairly quickly in lectures, but as long as you read the textbook section before the lecture, you will be fine. She is very clear in explaining all the concepts in class. She also allows the use of notecards on finals which is sooo awesome.

Most interesting and clear chemistry professor that I've ever had. Notecards on tests are very helpful. Study, and get early to exams to pick a good seat, and you can do well! (Still requires work to get a good grade though)
Great professor.  Flies through lectures so you need your book. A lot.  But you get to use a notecard on exams. so it evens out
Great Prof.
No Comments

Amazing professor!! Very easy class, if you need the Quant A credit, take this class with him. All you have to do is go to the lecture, follow along with him, and do the out-of-class short assignment, and you will get an A. He gives 200 extra points in the beginning, middle, and end. Attendance is mandatory. TAKE THE CLASS WITH HIM!!

this class was frustratingly easy. genuinely annoyed that i had to go to lecture bc i could teach it to myself w a few google searches. take for an A but be prepared to listen to him monologue about nothing for 1.5 hrs. trust its more annoying than u think.
bro his lectures are so confusing, i never knew what was going on. crashed out so many times, would fail the class if i didn't have friends in lecture with me. BRING YOUR FRIENDS
nah, crashed out every lecture

Great teacher for LIS 102 as it's an intro course.  The course was designed to help students succeed in the grade column, so they can focus on learning.  In class, you follow along step by step, essentially copying what he does, and you turn in the work at the end of class. For homework, you essentially complete a very similar assignment.

VERY easy class (which he made clear on the first day), basically as long as you show up and follow along with him/ do the homework you will receive above a 100%. Lectures were boring, but he's a very kind guy. Unfortunately, it seemed like not all of the class respected him and some went out of their way to interrupt lecture.

Really easy, too easy in fact that the lectures are the most boring thing of all time. Remember, you pay to take this class, I learned nothing and felt like it was a waste of money. He also sometimes would be late and also go off on tangents about random things during class. All the assignments were the exact same, too. It just got annoying.

Professor Nyhoff is great but his lectures can be boring but there are no tests or quizzes, you are purely graded on the lecture demos and homework. He gives out grace points to ensure that you can miss a class, and it not affect your grade. He is kind but he also can move a bit fast and can get caught up on outside stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
(LIS 646 NOT 440)
Most pathetic course ever. Unbelievably easy content (ex 7 p. instructions on signing up for a website). Most points are for attending his middle school level, outdated lectures. Creepy vibes which he's defensive about. Only take if you want to learn nothing & get an easy A.

Jeff is a great guy. Class was super easy. Just show up in lecture and follow along, and you can't not get an A.  A = 90%. 30min-1hour homework after every lecture, and that's it. Most of the points you get from showing up, the Top-hat, and the lecture-demo assignment. Talks a lot before class starts, treats you like a 6th grader, but he's chill.

Professor Nyhoff is just an amazing guy all the way around. Super caring and understanding of what it's like to be a college student. He offers a large amount of grace points making it rather easy to earn over 100% in the class. Material is fairly simple, hardest thing you have to do is just show up to lecture as attendance is graded.

Jeff Nyhoff's LIS440 was the easiest class I have ever taken. I finished with a 108% doing 0 extra credit. Jeff is nice, but my goodness. The best way I could describe his class is the movie Groundhog Day. You do the same assignments four or five times with a singular switch in variable names. Also, he takes attendance at the beginning and end...
Easy class, get ready to work during lectures and bring computer charge, can be boring but the most EASIEST CLASS EVER

Superrr easy class but the most boring class you will ever sit through. Almost fell asleep in every single one of his lectures. Also sent him multiple emails throughout the semester and he never responded to one.
easy class, easy credit
w class, take it
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: chill and passionate guy, easy class, just do your work while attending lectures!

Very straight forward and easy class, chill professor who is passionate about what he teaches, Most easiest A ever, just come in and do your work, and the assignments given for homework weekly which aren't too crazy. btw no quizzes! take it you wont regret it .
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jeff is a great dude.

LIS 461 was the easiest class I have ever taken and Jeff was a huge part of that with a phenomenal course design. If you are a data science major or certificate just take this class no matter what. Show up to class and just do the work, so easy. can be boring but that's the price you pay for an easy A. all other criticism here is unjustified.
take it, great guy, chill and easy class
easiest class and chillest professor

Class is boring, the easiest A I've had. All you have to do is show up to class and follow along, outside of class work is light. He talks a lot and can be rude if you ask him 1 on 1 questions. Take this if you need free science creds, don't expect it to be super engaging though.
cool guy, easy class

Good and easy class for quan b credit. Although, be ready to use and charge that computer to 100%. Lecture heavy as you have to be there everyday to do the assignments posted and to receive credit. Outside work is posted after lecture tuesdays, kinda long. NO Quizzes, easy pass, he may talk a lot but is overall a really chill professor + great guy.

He such chill guy, I honestly don't understand the hate lol. All you have to do is come to class and do your work by following what he instructs. Outside of class Tuesdays you will get work, but it always will relate to the topic you have done in class. He is also super understandable and yes he may be a yapper but overall the class is super easy.
Class is painfully boring and full of busy work. You will get an A if you show up and do the work, but it is mind numbing.

Prof. Nyhoff seems like a great guy. Unfortunately, his class makes me want to kms. Lectures are useless, he rambles a lot and acts like we're children. There is so much pointless busywork outside of class, and the canvas page is completely disorganized so it's hard to figure out what's going on
He's a bad lecturer but the class is super easy because you just need a 90% to get an A and get a bunch of grace points so that's a positive.

would constantly show up late to MANDATORY in-person 8 am, & didn't allow any makeups/exceptions for attendance (entire grade). When I suggested that he could post assignments before class so that we could start class on time (and not waste 20 minutes every class setting up), he blatantly disregarded me and basically called me rude. easy AF tho

He is not very organized at all. I took LIS 461 with him and if you have already taken any other python intro class this class will be very easy for you. I will say he is hard to reach sometimes by email and was constantly late to our lecture. He was a very nice guy though.

Very nice guy, horrible professor. Constantly cancelled lectures the day of. Fortunately, lectures were often worthless & provided no information. Always went far too in-depth with specific-case examples and consistently missed the forest for the trees. Poor question answerer. Held required "code-along" lectures, which are as bad as expected.

Sent on last day of class:

"Remember that it's ALWAYS hard to be new, ANYWHERE you go. This is normal, so hang in there."

"Remember that, the first time you try something challenging, it can feel like "falling down the steps" the first time around... This is normal, so hang in there."

I don't know what to expect more from an intro course prof.

By far the worst teacher I have ever had. Constantly cancels lectures and when he does hold class he is the worst lecturer. He doesn't know what is going on in the class and often teaches us the wrong topics. Never teaches us the material we need to know for the lab assignments. Also, never responds to emails.

Disappointed this semester with Prof Nyhoff. Very inconsistent teacher, does not respond to emails, and lectures cover bare minimum of topics we have to know in depth. I had to self study topics which were covered in the other Professors lectures but not in ours. Take a different professor if you get the chance, definitely not worth it otherwise.

Dr. Balster is a strict professor but extremely passionate and very friendly. He may seem tough but he ultimately just wants you to learn the material. 

Honestly, what you put in is what you take out, so you might need to give a little extra effort but it'll pay off

Heads up, there is a good amount of reading so be aware of that :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No matter how much you study, it is never enough. Willing to sell my soul to pass. His quizzes and exams are quite literally impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take his classes. Classes are way too hard for them, being intro classes for many majors. Class time is spent talking about nothing that will help you on exams, and when students come up unhappy with their grades, they are told that thinking wrong is incorrect. Makes it hard to skip class by having many in class quizes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: dont suggest. exams are not well prepared for in class. asked help multiple times and kept saying its "logically" based thinking. what does that even mean..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Balster puts a lot of effort into the material he teaches and the videos he makes. He is very passionate about soil sciences and makes the class very enjoyable. He encourages his students to think deeply about the environment and truly cares about what he teaches. I would recommend this class to everyone!

AVOID Super passionate professor ends up never teaching you anything in lectures that are relevant to his already challenging exams. Exams are very difficult. Not mandatory attendence but he makes it hard to skip with assignments.Very challenging, havent learned anything, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS

He is a good teacher but makes the class unnecessarily difficult for an introductory environmental science class. Furthermore, the class is quite boring and does not go deeply into environmental topics aside from soils. Lastly, the exams are difficult to study for since there is no communication on what we need to learn. Avoid if possible.

Has VERY strong opinions, half of the things that he says in lecture are false and backed at all by any science His lectures are required on Wednesday and Friday additionally his lectures were consistently a couple lectures behind what we were supposed to be talking about Overall his tests are just based upon the optional text readings not lecture.

Dr.Balster is incredibly passionate about what he does and loves teaching. He can come off as a bit old school at times, but he really does care for his students and wants them to succeed. The lecture is mandatory as there is not much content learning outside of class, so make sure to go. Exams were entirely lecture material and quite difficult.
Exams are very difficult and he does not prepare you for them.

Dr. Balster was an extremely passionate professor. He changed the way that I think about the environment and soil, and his lectures were always extremely engaging and flew by. Rasing your hand, asking questions after class or email, and putting an effort out to form a connection will help your learning + Balster is a cool guy to get to know.

This class is designed specifically for environmental science students so I'd recommend skipping out on it if you're not interested in the field or just taking it for a breadth requirement. There's a lot of readings and the exams always borrow questions from the practice quizzes. The class is very interesting and the teacher is very passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures feel like one long tangent, and is difficult to depict what is important. There is no way to practice the content besides one optional weekly quiz since this class had no discussions. However, he is very passionate about soil and willing to answer any questions. He also gives lots of extra credit on exams and projects.

Nick Balster is one of those teachers who is so in his own ass about being a good teacher, that he inadvertently becomes a bad one. While he's clearly passionate about teaching and has great lectures, he seems to care more about his 10 page custom made syllabus than his student's wellbeing. If you turn in any assignment late, be prepared to get a 0

Nick Balster is just about as unhelpful as I've had regarding a professor for a course that is not very difficult. If I were to rate the class itself, the difficulty would be lower, however, between never responding to emails, limited availability outside of lectures, and never providing answers to questions, he is just difficult to work with.

Professor Balster is an amazing professor but it was a very difficult class as a non-major. Attendance is not taken, but you get quizzes weekly/opportunities for extra credit so you almost have to show up. Beware that exams are a good portion of the grade and call for much more critical thinking than the quizzes. Good luck if you take this course.

if you're reading this stop now and choose a different class.  i hope I can save at least one soul who is about to go down the path of this class.  the class is unnecessarily tough with quizzes every week. many students dont finish the exams.  i dont have enough characters to describe how much I hated this class.

Dr. Balster truly cares about each and every student and only wants them to succeed. You're encouraged to come to him if you're struggling and enjoys getting to know his students. Quizzes and exams are a little bit more on the difficult side but he is willing to talk over why he graded it the way he did and your answers and work with you.

If I had to give one tip to anyone taking this capstone, it would be to get started on the project ASAP and conduct as much research as you can pertaining to your project. Be prepared to receive a lot of harsh and discouraging comments on your writing portions. He cares about you, but he cares more about the project and will be sure to let you know

Dr. Balster is a very egotistical man. During lectures, he is very passionate about his work and material, however he very clearly only cares about the syllabus and not about his students. He is a very harsh grader and the class is heavily based on the exam grade. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS if you care about your mental health.

Dr. Balster is the most passionate professor I have ever had. He is always open to questions and will take the time to teach any student willing to learn. His classes can be challenging but he is a great guy with a fun personality.

One-of-a-kind professor with an infectious passion for his field of study. His lectures are jam-packed and very engaging. The work in this class felt intentional and fair. Dr. Balster cares deeply for his students' well-being and learning, shown in his teaching style, assessments, extra credit, and opportunities to meet/work outside of class.

The class does take effort but Balster and his TA were there to always help. I recommend taking this course is you want to learn and have fun doing it. Balster is at the top of the list as one of the best professors i've had. So glad I had to take the course. Great class & professor - exams a bit tough but doiable if you put in the work.

Professor has an absolutely massive ego and refused to take feedback from students. Class was extremely difficult for no reason and despite many students averaging C's on weekly quizzes, grades were not curved at all. Readings were long and boring. Overall horrible class and horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've had a lot of bad teachers and professors but Balster takes the cake. This man refuses to have a soul. He puts on a show of charisma and smiles in class to make you feel like he cares. He doesn't. He is wildly inflexible and wants to see you fail. He does not care about the circumstances of you missing a class, he won't help you.

Having done 4 years at UW, Dr. Balster is one of the best professors I have taken. His teaching style is unique but it makes the information stick. He is energetic and passionate about what he teaches. If you can argue your answer with a reasonable explanation, he will give points back on exams. Going to class is important, slides only do so much
Horrible so far. I wish I had taken a different class for general science requirement. The material is interesting but Dr. Balster is not a good teacher.

AVOID BASLTER AT ALL COSTS!! He is so confusing, and acts like he cares, but then is a jerk over email, and canvas. He contradicts himself all the time, and makes lectures drag on forever. Most of the stuff that you learn that has anything to do with the class is done outside of class, and makes you watch hour long videos every week. DON'T DO IT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Balster is a good dude, and he cares a lot about his students and def loves what he teaches. If you get something in wrong on a quiz and can actually back up why you chose an answer, he will most likely give you points back. But, quizzes are hard, there is a lot of work and you learn things that don't seem relevant/important at all.

If you are looking for a class with a lot of work, yet no relevant information, take this class. I cannot express the amount of hate that I have towards this class and teacher. I am not majoring in environmental science, but if I was, Dr. Balster would seriously make me change my major. Avoid this class and any others that he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He acts like a progressive teacher, but his teaching is outdated, confusing, and does not take the student into account at all. If you love being a bootlicker and regurgitating info you'll do great. Weekly quizzes are basically weekly exams, 150 points, and only 50 mins to complete. And somehow I feel like I am learning nothing. Useless class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Balster is horrible. He refuses to record his lectures, they is no organization to the class and the slides are confusing and mostly have pictures so if you miss class you will be totally lost. The quizzes are way too hard and often have trick questions. Avoid him at all costs.
Best professor I've had so far at UW-Madison. His lectures are the only ones I don't watch at 1.5 speed because he is so interesting and fun to listen to. I love this guy and his class.

At the beginning, I liked Professor Balster but by the end I was so ready to be done with the class. He talks about how accessible he is out of class, but I only had issues with him. Group quizzes EVERY class, plus you do the same hour long quiz on your own before each class. Plus, most of the class was spent on learning about the scientific method

Professor Balster is NOT it. Im a science major and I took this my freshman year and it was harder than most of the 400 level classes I take now. Math heavy for no reason and theres a group exam after you take the exam by yourself which was a waste of time. I dont recommend getting sick as he has no empathy for his students when they miss class.

I wouldn't recommend taking this as your capstone. Nick basically gave us a topic and told us to do something with almost no direction. The whole course was extremely frustrating. Take a different environmental studies capstone if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If you don't care about soils when you start the class, you will for sure care about them by the end. Dr. Balster really cares about your learning more than anything. If you don't understand something he is very helpful in office hours to make sure you know what is going on in the class.

Professor Balster is one of, if not, the BEST PROFESSOR EVER. He really wants you to learn the material, he does not care about your grade as long as you put the effort into class. He is super passionate about the subject and he really cares about your learning, I am serious he is awesome. By instructor in my 20 as a learner.
Very passionate about soils and what he does. Thought the class was very interesting. Tougher class, especially if a non-science major, but I thought doable

I'm a non-science major with no science background and found this as my hardest class(is supposed to be a gen-ed). Tests are tough, you have to study a lot. I did well on all the class work/quizzes yet struggled with exams and still failed the course. Would definitely not recommend to anyone as a non-science major.

If you are not a science major of any sort do not take his class, you need a science background. The class was mandatory and his power points were very confusing. There is a graded quiz every week, and his test are unbelievable tough.

Professor is either not knowledgeable or stumbles over topics he tries to exaggerate on, but thankfully are not necessary for the exams.  For example, he showed an example of phosphorus deficiency in corn and it was actually nitrogen.  Needs to focus less on his learning theory and more on soil sciences.  Heavy in math.  Graded Quizzes every class.

Prof. Balster wants his students to do well and fall a bit in love with soil while at it. He learns every student's name - this degree of personal connection is a core characteristic of Balster. He wants his class to be a community and successful.  Lectures could be organized better with more of a clear direction. no exam study guides. Overall AB.

The class is not cake in that you will definitely have to study. it is taught by more than one proff (didn't get much from the chemistry guy). Dr. Balster was best along with Mattie. he cares about learning & likes soil a bit too much. sometimes difficult to meet with. exams are challenging. he does favor those that attend lecture

Fantastic teacher. Awful class, mostly because he teaches with 3 other instructors who are not that great. But if you can take a class with Dr. Balster, definitely do it! He cares about his students and their learning. He sometimes gets off on tangents, but they are usually worth it.
Hard class, harsh grading. Probably mandatory if you are taking it. However, you can tell that he genuinely wants his students to learn and suceed. He is also EXTREMELY enthusiastic which helps.

I did an independent study project with Professor Balster. He was extremely helpful throughout the process of my project and he spent a ton of his time explaining each step of the process. He truly loves soils and is willing to help you out if you put in some effort. He turned a tough project into one of the best experiences I've had at UW-Madison.
I really did not like the professor. He was not very clear and just wants you to repeat what he says. Also his powerpoints are absurd and make no sense.
Nick was one of the professors for my Env.Studies capstone course. He was helpful and you can tell he really cares about his students and enjoys teaching. I would definitely recommend him!

Professor Balster knows what he's talking about, but the class is still hard. You have to work at it. Mallika is the best TA she was able to clarify things when Prof. Balster got confusing, wish we had discussion sections. It might seem easy at the beginning but it gets harder.

Best professor I have ever had.  It requires a little work, but if you put any effort forward you will do well in the class.  I entered the class with no interest in soils and because of this class I am now a Soil Science major.

Dr. Balster REALLY cares about the fact that his students are learning and will go above and beyond to help you. He doesn't just want you to regurgitate on a test, but to LEARN. However, the exams are deceptively hard.
Not as easy as he makes it sound.  Studying for the Exams is not easy...He says you will do fine if you try hard...not true.  A lot of math concepts.

Best class ever! He is truly passionate about soils, and he even makes you care about it as well! At times he can drag on, but he wants you to learn, HE CARES. If you go to class, pay attention, do the work, you'll be fine. I really enjoyed this class, even though I had NO interest in it at the beginning. Now I'm all concerned about the soil now!

Best class i have ever taken - first professor i have had that actually cares about teaching and cares about students and the material - truely loves soils - i did not going in - should be a bit higher than a 200 level course
I often felt like I was learning what he wanted us to spit out rather than gaining any true insight into the subject matter.
Excellent proff, excellent class

BEST LECTURER EVER.  Not just because he keeps it interesting, but also because he is SOO passionate about what he teaches.  He loves teaching and cares about his students and it shows! He just won a teaching award from CALS and deserves so much more! If you have any interest in soils (or even if you don't) take this man's class!!!!

Great prof.... good helper.. you just have to make the effort.. may just be about dirt but its fun.. interesting to me.. if you make an effort he will notice ...not just the numbers. Long at sometimes.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Absolute gem in the CS department- lectures are so clear and straight forward. Ive never heard him say 'um' or 'like' and he never even stutters. I recommend this class if you are looking to put in a genuine effort, it will pay off as its a good investment and you can really learn something. If you do the work honestly its smooth sailing!

Cole's lectures are very good at getting the content across and being a valuable resource for projects and exams. He is also a very nice guy -- willing to meet with you and answer any questions in a way that is not condescending at all like some others in the dept. One of the easier CS electives -- recommend

His lectures are detailed. He also gives us a chance to do a project by either one person or in a group, and you can get full scores if you fulfill all requirements. The midterm is very easy and final is fine. Just need to practice past paper and analyze each question, you can get an A

Cole Nelson is definitely interested in what he teaches. If you're willing to learn the course material, it shouldn't be too hard. Projects are a bit of work, but not super hard. Cole Nelson definitely wants his students to learn, and I think he does a very good job of this.

I'm not sure he wants his students to succeed. The A rate for CS571 has been declining each semester, reaching about 21.5% in the Spring 2025 semester. The final exam is unnecessarily difficult, and the homework load is overwhelming. He allocated 10 points of the exam to projects during the summer, but removed the easy questions from the exam.

Very chill guy, everything you need for the test is on the lectures. Me and my friend both thought he reminded us of a youtuber, we could never put our finger on it, I think its cause he has a calming voice.
Not the greatest professor of all time, but he's a great person with lectures that are incredibly digestible. I would recommend Cole and this course to anyone on the edge.
Very clear speaker and lectures are very informative. The projects were very fun.

The presentation, speaking, and flow in his lectures are almost as clean as a fully edited video. Rarely does he stutter or get off track while teaching. The information in lectures (slides and demos) are presented straightforward and concise, making it easy to learn topics.
Love this guy, he really made the course content interesting and assigned some legitimately fun projects. 10/10 recommend he is the GOAT
Take this guy if you can.
Absolute GOAT
doesnt teach anything in the class, only quiz and inclass exercise. if you desire a tough life, take his course.
RUN RUN RUN
Take his class if you desire a tough life
Very clear with what we needed to know.  Homeworks took some time but were very similar to exam questions.
No Comments

The class itself may appear easy, but be careful, it is very exam-focused. Despite his lectures being interesting and him clearly being passionate about the topic, the tests are 80% of your grade, and the lectures are very general, while the tests are very specific.
Dr. Nolen gives great lectures, is fun to talk to and gives great answers to questions.

Dr. Nolen makes lectures engaging with his teaching style and humor. Exams are almost 80% of your grade, but they are straightforward once you understand the way in which questions are asked. Make a quizlet of everything covered in lecture/readings and you will be solid.

Loved Dr. Nolen and this class. Learned a lot of things more in depth than I had knowledge of. Class is graded based on 4 tests which are multiple choice. Tests are very easy and straightforward if you complete out of class readings. Typically 2-3 readings per week. Attendance is not mandatory but some exam questions are based on stuff said in lec.
One test per unit (4 total) that make up a majority of your final grade. Lecture topics sometimes go way more in depth, or not enough in depth as to what questions will be asked on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learned a lot by taking this course and Prof. Nolen is passionate about sociology. However, the tests are weighted very heavily and there are daily readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class should be an "easy one", however the grades are weighted incredibly test heavy and it is quite hard to get -1 or -2 on a 40 mcq test. The TA for my section also graded incredibly harshly. Overall, Professor Nolen was nice and pretty funny, the class is just ran a bit unfairly in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would recommend Jason to anyone interested in taking a sociology/ethnic studies class. His lectures never felt boring, and he was really able to express his passion for the subject. Your grade is very test heavy, but the class isn't too hard as long as you occasionally show up for lecture and do all the readings. Overall, good guy and good prof.
Dude gives great, clear lectures. The class is both interesting and fairly easy as your Ethnic Studies credit. Would recommend
Great professor, exams are very laid back, just make sure to do your readings and you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, cares lots about what he's teaching and it shows!

He's definitely a nice person, but I found his teaching skills a bit weak. The slides are kind of all over the place, and the exam sometimes asks about stuff that's only in the readings, not the lectures. Also, the discussions feel pretty unnecessary and not very helpful.

I would recommend Soc 134 with Nolen to everyone! Attendance isn't mandatory, but do yourself a favor and go to the lectures; he's funny and it makes the material much easier to remember. There were a lot of readings, but most were interesting. It's only graded on section participation and 4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. If you go to office hours and get a chance to chat with him, you will meet one of the funniest, kindest, and smartest professors at Madison. Dr. Nolen is also a great lecturer.
The course itself is boring some topics are interesting but there's only tests so if you do bad on a single test your grade will be tanked pretty severely the course isn't worth taking

Dr. Nolen explained the content very well in his lectures, and he used lots of examples that made the material more engaging. I enjoyed this class a lot because of his lectures. I would definitely recommend taking this class with Dr. Nolen!

I would recommend you take this class with him! He is very knowledgeable, and backs things with evidence. Exams are easy if you study for them, I found the study guide helpful. Do you not have to go to lecture (he posts the slides), but I found it beneficial, and found the topics interesting. Exams were 20 multiple choice, and 1 written response.
Professor Nolen is really sweet. He really cares about students as well as animals. Super easy to communicate with and generally knowledgeable enough about the topic.

Lectures are just reading off of a slideshow; it is very easy to get notes directly from the slides. Half of the class is outside readings that are pretty boring. There are 4 tests that determine your whole grade, and doing poorly on one can basically tank your grade for the semester. Overall I thought the class was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, and the professor makes it very clear what he wants you to focus on for exams. Interesting and engaging lectures, great professor.

Jason is a very kind and understanding person. He really does care about what he's teaching and makes sure to not teach with a bias. There's a good amount of reading each week and your grade mostly depends on the 4 exams. No final exam. Highly recommend Jason as a professor, attending lecture, and talking to him after lecture for any elaboration.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor for a pretty simple course. The lectures were a little boring at times but they were brief and included interesting topics and videos. The outside reading material was usually pretty easy but he occasionally jump scares you with a 40 page chapter of book, but you don't really need to read it. Exams are incredibly easy if you read.

Jason is a great guy and very fair with material on exams. Not hard to get an A in this class if you study, especially with how helpful discussion sections are. However, Jason is a pretty boring lecturer and doesn't seem passionate about the topic matter, like you would expect of a professor in a 400 level class to be. Still, would recommend.

Professor Nolen was very accessible and open during and after lecture. I really appreciated how he approached difficult topics. You could tell that he actually wanted his students to learn and succeed. I would take another sociology class at UW Madison just because Professor Nolen was the professor.

I LOVE Jason. He genuinely one of the nicest professors around.
