This class was super interesting and honestly not difficult so I would 100% recommend. 4 exams throughout sem was nice, discussion was super fun too (Avery was awesome). Jason is def a prof that you can talk to, so don't hesitate to ask him Qs or just talk about life.

Jason was a very kind professor. I found the class pretty easy as the lectures were pretty straightforward. Some of the assigned readings were a little lengthy but nothing too bad. Your grade is mostly composed of 4 noncumulative with no real final so that was great.
Easy to understand readings and lectures with no final just 4 non-cumulative tests throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Soc 441 with Nolen was pretty easy for a high-level class in my opinion. There are four exams throughout the semester but they're not bad. A lot of the content is memorization. Nolen creates the class to not be too difficult so I had a good time. I would recommend Nolen for this course, he made it an easy A and interesting material.
Loved this class, loved this professor—great lecturer with well-written slides that are always available.

Jason was a great teacher and his lectures were very interesting. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but his exams heavily focused on lecture material which was sometimes not included on the posted slides. The assigned readings for the course were sometimes lengthy, but overall the workload for the course was manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nolen was a great professor!! Not only is the class interesting but it was also pretty easy. It takes maybe an exam or two to get used to the questions that he asks but the exams are generally easy.  Shoutout to the TA David too. Him and Jason were like Shaq and Kobe

Very passionate about the class and incredibly helpful during office hours. No quizzes or tests, just three exams. Content easy if you pay attention in class and do readings. Says things in lecture that are not in slides, discussion section only useful for peer review. Flexible with due dates if you're respectful and communicate ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nolen usually explainex concepts very clearly and even when a topic was confusing, he would often be available after lecture to briefly explain in an understandable way. I also like that exams emphasized understanding of the concepts rather than specific names or statistics.

The lectures for this class are clear, but it can sometimes be difficult to predict what exactly is going to show up on the exam. You can tell he cares a lot about the subject. He also makes all of his slides and materials available online.

Professor Nolen is a very clear instructor. He gives review "cheat sheets" before the exams that are extremely helpful. There are only 4 exams and no papers. This class is a good transition into college for freshmen. The lectures were straight-forward and attending them really locked in my understanding. 10/10 would take Professor Nolen again.
Jason was a great lecturer. Some people thought he was really monotonous, but overall you can tell he really cares about the material. If you go to lecture, the tests are SUPER easy.

Discussions are mandatory and generally helpful, depending on how the collective feels that week. Lectures are optional but very much recommended since some material is added to the shared slideshow that can show up in exams.

Took both sociology 134 and 441 with Dr. Nolen. The material is all interesting, the tests are straightforward and not very hard, and Dr. Nolen seems like a great guy. The only thing is his lectures are very dry and he sounds like he's bored while teaching-- it's hard not to zone out after a while.

Jason is really nice - he has kind of a monotone voice. Lectures are not mandatory and he posts the slides but I'd still recommend going. Grades are 72% test scores so make sure to do the readings and study. The material isn't hard and is mostly common sense if you know anything about soc. Overall good, interesting, easy class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very heavy on test scores since they are the only thing graded from the lecture portion of the class. The discussions are very helpful and the TA's are wonderful. There is no homework for this class but you do have to complete the assigned readings to understand the class concepts. Attendance is not mandatory but is strongly suggested
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jason is such a caring and understanding person. Additionally, the class material was very interesting and important to our everyday lives. I really enjoyed this course and I learned a lot. The exams were no bad and it was very helpful to go to the review sessions! Overall, great class with a great professor and TAs.

Take sociology with Professor Nolen! He's a great guy and his lectures are good. If you go to lectures and discussions you will pass with an A. Three papers and three exams. Exams were 50% from the readings and 50% from the lectures. He posts the slides and lecture attendance is not mandatory. Great ethnic studies class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures were interesting, and tests were very straightforward. If you pay attention in class and have an idea of the main points of the readings, it is very doable. Very nice demeanor with students.

Prof Nolen was an engaging lecturer. The class was easy and not difficult to follow. 3 essays, 3 tests, no final. The tests are easy, multiple-choice, pretty much flashcard questions. The essays are graded pretty leniently, depending on which TA you have. I'd recommend it to fill an ethnic studies credit or to learn more about sociology.

Definitely recommend taking this class with Prof. Nolen. His lectures were usually pretty interesting and the grading system was very fair. Grade is based on three exams and three papers. Class material is all very applicable and relevant to today's society.

This class is easy, but you learn a lot and discussion sections are great. Tests are directly connected to lectures and reading material so there's no surprises. Nolen and the TAs are laid back and approachable, and are usually available outside of class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Lectures can be very long and boring. 3 tests and 3 essays. You will do well on essays if you have an easy TA. Exams can be difficult but if you go to lectures and study you will do fine. He posts lecture slides but go to class bc he says important things in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Despite not being very passionate about the content of the class, I was always excited to go to Professor Nolen's lectures. He made them very engaging and easy to follow as well as connected topics to pop culture in order to make them easier to understand. He was always very funny and willing to give assistance when it was needed.

Prof. Nolen is the absolute BEST. He is so funny and always puts in so much effort to make lectures engaging. This class is very eye-opening and I have learned so much. Whether you take this class for credit or not, I would recommend it to anyone! He is Amazing.

Prof. Nolen is absolutely amazing, and so is this class. Nolen does a great job explaining the course and concepts. Lectures are very rewarding and interesting, but sometimes can be a bit drug on. All lecture slides are posted online, which is really nice if you are sick. I have learned so much, and if you take SOC 134, take it with Nolen!!

I took SOC 134 over summer as my first class at UW-Madison. The class was very interesting and Professor Nolen was a fantastic professor. I would highly recommend him. Grade based on two papers (but there three opportunities; you could drop one), reading quizzes, attendance, and participation (he gave accommodations for shyer students).
Jason is very approachable. He is a very solid lecturer who tries to make them interesting and funny. If you have not taken soc 134, a lot of these concepts will be very insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: loved this class very easy and insightful.

Jason was great and very professional. He covered many current topics in America today and posts all his slides online. His tests can be a bit harder than they seem because he pulls questions off the readings.

Jason is an amazing teacher! I never wanted to miss his class because it was so interesting and I always learned something new. He really cares about sociology and his students. If you read the articles and go to class, you will do well on the test. Go into office hours for your papers and enjoy his amazing teaching. 100% my favorite class so far!

Jason is THEE best. He's so casual with his lectures and a cool person in general. He likes to make jokes in class and is always open for questions. Reading are the one downfall, but that's the only homework outside class and they can be interesting. His exams were fair. Overall such a nice guy and id love to take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Nolen is professional and gives great lectures. The purpose of a sociology class is to raise awareness on controversial issues and encourage conversation about them, and he does just that. Definitely recommend taking this course with him. 3 exams, 3 papers, do the readings and go to lecture and you will become a better person of society
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is professional but still approachable. His exams are very fair and are not too challenging. The material is interesting and important. I feel like a better member of society and a more informed person on the implications of race in this country. Highly would recommend to anyone, especially anyone interested in politics or social justice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Nolen is an interactive teacher, engaging his students in the lectures through his cat pictures and clear knowledge/interest in the subject.
Jason is great, funny guy and his class is fun. Learn a lot during the class but also easy, which was great. Would recommend this class or Jason to anyone.

I absolutely LOVED this class. It should be required for everyone. Jason is one of the most caring people you'll ever meet, and loves to talks to students outside of class. If you go to lecture and read the readings you'll pass with flying colors. His tests are very fair, and what the students think of him/the class is very important to him.

Jason is great! He presents tough issues in a balanced and interesting way; if you're looking for Ethnic studies, take this class! It was very enlightening on the past and current condition of race in America. Don't fall behind on the readings, and pay attention to the news for potential paper topics. No cumulative final. He loves his cats.

Jason made Sociology 134 really interesting.  He was very engaged with students during lecture, so I wanted to come to lecture, even though he posted the powerpoints online.  Also, he will wait for students to finish taking notes on each slide.  Exams were easy and non- cumulative.  This class made me feel like a more informed member of society.

Jason Nolen was by far my favorite professor last semester. He makes his lectures incredibly interesting through riveting material as well as lots of cat pictures to spice up the information and statistics. Although you could probably get away with not going to lecture, I highly recommend it. LOVED THIS CLASS.

Class lectures are not mandatory because all lectures are posted online; however, the lectures are never boring and he expands on needed information for tests. As long as you read the tests are not hard! Nolen always has his students interested and laughing and is always willing to help. The worst part of the class was the papers-hard grading TA's.

Jason is one of the best professors I've had! He is so personable and funny! He does a great job making sense of his material and putting it on a level students can understand. The class is only three exams and three papers. Allow time to do the papers well or your grade won't look so good. This class is a MUST TAKE course, with Jason of course.

LOVED Nolen. Cannot say enough good things about this man. Easy going, funny, and thorough in his lectures. Cute too. He teaches a tough subject really well and goes over everything in detail. & he shows animal pictures

Very funny and personable. Lightened heavy subjects and really changed the way I see the world. The class content is very easy to absorb and readings aren't bad (about 30-60 pages of text a week). 3 tests (non-cumulative) and 3 essays (3 pages long, each). Very doable, very enjoyable. Highly recommended for ethnic studies credit.

Jason is my favorite professor I have had! He is young and super relatable to students (pretty sure our entire class follows him on Instagram). He makes class enjoyable and you are guaranteed to laugh at least once during class. If you are taking this class, definitely take it with Jason!

Jason is my favorite professor I have had so far. His lectures include interesting content and also can make the class laugh. He is younger so it easier to relate him. I am a big fan of his teaching style and his cats Stu & Lu. This class does require participation in discussion though and papers are not graded at a college level. Take this class.

Jason is very relatable and he makes his students feel comfortable. He presents the information in a very entertaining and easy to understand manner. Plus, he adds a lot of videos in! It's a very interesting class and the material is very interesting as well!

Makes the material understandable and interesting. He finds awesome videos! Professor Nolen is in general very likeable and interesting! I've really been liking his class and his class structure (not discussions)

You can basically pick between reading and lecture, but both will ensure you the A. Reminiscent of a high school class in how you can study. Lectures were engaging, interesting, and informative. Would recommend to everyone and their mother for an ethnic studies class.

Soc 134 was a blast with Jason! I loved going to lecture because he was so funny and informative about the topic. In order to succeed in this class, one must attend discussion and be active in participating to truly understand the material.

I loved Jason as a lecturer, he's laid back and relatable, I had a lot of respect for him and they way he was able to provide perspective on a controversial subject matter. 3 papers and 3 exams which are very doable but certainly not easy A's. Readings can get long, but honestly I didn't do many of them and still did alright. Highly recommend!

Jason was pretty clear about what was expected and what we needed to know. There aren't many grades throughout the semester, so skipping lectures and not doing the readings can really hurt you. The readings aren't too long, so set aside a long afternoon at the start of the week and get them all done, and be sure to take good notes on them!

Jason made lectures interesting and straight-forward. Exams were 5050 lectures and readings. The class really makes you think a different way about the world and how you shape your views of race. Highly recommend taking it!!

Jason was great. His humor and overall personality made the class that much more enjoyable. Only 3 tests and 3 papers to do all semester long, difficult but do able.  The only downside were the weekly readings that could get heavy, but hey, you had all week to do them.
Jason is awesome. He makes lectures interesting. Only negative about the class is the readings each week can get kind of long. Other than that, he's awesome,  and the class is super interesting.
He has a lot of reading to the course. Not really known what will be on the exams.
Just a laid back guy, funny enough to make lecture worth going to

He's a really good lecturer, engaging and funny. His slides are clear and he is very open to helping students and clarifying. There are 3-4 papers throughout the semester and 3 exams, no final. The exams are pretty straight forward if you go to class, take good notes and do the readings.

I do not like math at all and still managed to get a good grade in this. The math is very rudimentary and he explains it in very accessible ways. Very laid-back. Lots of tests, but they're easy and he drops a lot of them. No final unless you bombed a previous test and want to retake. Highly recommend as a basic math class for non-STEM majors.

He's a lovely person and I enjoyed his lessons. He does a great job of making things easy to understand through solid examples and funny word problems. He made me enjoy math which I can't believe I'm saying. Class was easy and TA's were helpful. Going to lecture is definitely the key to success.

He seemed like a nice and silly guy but I couldn't understand much when he tried explaining concepts. The quizzes were super easy, sometimes it'll take me less than 5 minutes to do. The TA's were incredibly helpful and would have separate reviews for us for upcoming exams
Very laid-back professor. Allows redo's for tests during final exam period, and homework assignments are basically free points.

This class is taught by TAs and I couldn't understand anything mine wrote or said. The tests are hard, especially if you're not good at math, and the averages were usually 60%. The TA did not teach the criteria in a clear and understandable way. Class is not run well overall. Lots of people dropped from mine. Avoid this class if possible.

Math 112 is a joke. Class is taught by TAs. My TA  was terrible and honestly the worst teacher I ever had. Quizzes and exams are difficult and do not directly correlate to lecture. 1/10 do not recommend!

Dr. O was is great! Doesn't take attendance, but I don't recommend skipping. One overall test for each unit and two mini quizzes within the unit. Weekly homework, but it's not difficult. Textbook is bundled into your tuition but you'll rarely use it. Lecture slides and quiz/exam review are posted and review sessions for every test with the TAs.

Such an easy class, you have a short 5 minute test every week but got 100% on all of them, there are 4 biger tests throughout the smester but you can retake one of them. No final. Decent amount of homework but it was not hard. super fun and silly guy.

He's a great guy and super cool to take the class with. Even though he might come off as slow initially, he does a really good job at explaining. Make sure never to skip lectures cuz they are super useful!

Truly such a funny guy, he is knowledgable and will answer questions as they come up. 141 isnt a very difficult class but i am terrible at math and still have managed to do pretty well. He also has automatic extensions for homework if you forget to do it within a day of the due date.

Professor Olson was a nice guy, but the way his class is structured is kinda disorganized. You have weekly check ins usually once a week but they are always at the end of class so if you don't finish before everyone be ready to keep getting up out of your seat to let people through. He also never checks his email so you have to go to him in person
Great prof, lots of dad jokes. Make sure you go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've struggled in the past, and he introduced me to amazing resources.

Let me preface this by saying I've taken Calc 2 before. Nonetheless, I found Professor Olson's lectures to be vastly more interesting and understandable than my previous professor's. His lecture style is example heavy, so ensure you're comfortable learning that way, but if you are confused and ask a question he will always explain it for you.

I really liked him as a person, but I think he forgot that Calc 2 concepts are challenging to undergraduates. He went really in depth and got off topic frequently. Lectures were either too fast or too slow. He's the most helpful in office hours in terms of math, and is a very kind man. Overall, I would take another course with him if I had a chance

He was a pretty good professor but he tended to get distracted a lot during lecture and taught it at a bad pace. I felt like if he focused a little more we could have had some review days for the final. But he was good at explaining most things and I feel like I learned a lot.
Math 112 was a difficult experience, without the undergraduate helpers it's very hard to receive in class help. Lessons make minimal sense.

This is for Math 222, not 221. He's a good guy, but I think he forgets these are pretty difficult concepts for people who are first learning them. Goes at superspeed through examples without explaining that well. I am very lucky I have a good TA that has basically taught me the course.

Dr. O is a great prof who provides clear lectures and gets to the point. Provides good definitions and examples. Easy to reach via email for missing class. Connects content to real-world situations. Exams and writing practices were very easy. Exam review sessions are so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr O was always quick to email back and was very accommodating with quiz and WP retakes. The class and the material is next level easy, I got an A and never went to lecture, just make sure you go on Thursdays when he gives little mini quizzes so you can get those easy points.

It's easy to get an A/AB in the class. HW is assigned 2x a week, online, & unlimited tries to get the answer. Weekly in class quizzes are posted the day before. He drops 2 of the lowest quiz and hw scores. The lectures do feel pointless/are overly complicated/too fast, so go to the exam reviews that he has (they help a ton)!

Travis Olson is an amicable professor, but that's all. He does not respond to emails, either on outlook or canvas, and he failed to respond to two emails I sent in regards to missing class due to a funeral and two other emails asking about the final. He does not put exam dates in the calendars, and two exams (50% each) were 14 days apart.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MATH 221's grade is very exam heavy, The Organic Chemistry Tutor is better than Travis Olsen, it's very easy to lose points on discussion quizzes and homework. My advice for an A is to skip lecture, do past exams and ignore all other content and try to attend all quizzes. There are better conceptual explanations on the internet especially areas.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is mainly based on exams and lectures weren't amazing as he goes through concepts quickly, but they were ok. If you study outside of class and take as many of the past/practice exams as possible you'll be fine. Past exams use similar set up and questions so go through them.
This man will not respond to any of your emails. Avoid at all costs.

Olson was a totally solid professor. He's a very clear speaker and is relatively funny. Class is certainly difficult and you will need to study outside of class to get a good grade (shoutout to Professor Leonard on YT). However, the tests are well structured/fair in the sense that they are quite similar to the practice tests. So study those a lot.

He was a solid lecturer, sometimes went too fast but pace was ok most the time and he'd crack jokes or randomly sing which kept me awake. I ended up doing most of my learning from the TA but the lectures were useful for introducing me to the topic. This class is very exam heavy(29% of your grade for each of 3 exams) so be ready to lock in for exams

Professor Olson was great at lecturing, however the way that the class was distributed for grades made it extremely difficult to get a good grade. 87% of your final grade are from two midterms and the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Travis was a decent professor. However, he often gets sidetracked and forgets to thoroughly explain brand new concepts to the class. If you haven't taken calc before, you may struggle with him as a professor. Some things you need to teach yourself.

I don't recommend Travis as a professor if you don't need to. He goes too fast during lecture without explaining himself which almost makes the lecture pointless. You're going to want a good TA if you have him. You need to teach yourself almost everything. Taking calc before this would maybe make it better, but if you haven't good luck.

I think he's a funny guy, and would occasionally make jokes in lectures. He's got a swag dad vibe and I somehow love it. The class is not easy by all means, but I'd say he did his best with the weirdly structured syllabus. Exams were doable as long as you study a lot from past exams as they were pretty similar.

Always cheerful and funny during lecture and makes the content as easy to learn as it can be. Yes, the course is difficult, but that's because it's calculus. He said he's taught calc for almost two decades which is evident by his ability to explain things in the most intuitive ways. The mathematical notations he uses are also helpful and make sense

He's a really nice, personable professor, but he just doesn't teach the material well. He goes on a lot of tangents, you have to look online after class most of the time to finish your notes (which are fill-in-the-blank), and you have a quiz to take pretty much every single class period. Do not recommend.

Like many other people have mentioned, nice guy but not a great teacher. He mainly goes over examples in class and hands out elementary school style "fill in the blank" note sheets. You will often find yourself teaching yourself content that you should have learned in class. Also, quizzes almost everyday which are easy but annoying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice person, terrible teacher! Test content differs from class material, frustrating unrelated questions on quizzes, lags behind in course, slow grader with minimal feedback. Transfer to another section if possible.

Travis was funny and seemed to care a lot, but he was just kind of confusing and hard to follow. He's fine for the class, like you'll do fine, but be prepared to teach a lot of it to yourself. The exams are way harder than anything you go over in class and don't seem to fit the stuff he actually taught.

Average professor. He is just fine for Calc 1 since you are probably better off learning most of the material by yourself anyway. Tests were actually pretty hard with class averages often falling into the low 70s and high 60s. It was curved by a letter grade at the end of the semester though.

Dr. O is kind and funny, but her lectures were not good. She clearly prepared for some topics and lectured with increased insight, while most were simply copy and pasted from the text book with no useful notes or lecturing. Exams and homework were very easy if you did the reading. Fine for an intro class, but you won't get much out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Oaxaca, I had her her first time teaching at UW, but she knew what she was talking about, and she was really nice.

Lectures are pointless to go to she just reads off a slide which is copy and pasted from the textbook chapters you have to read, all of which are VERY long and have to be completed every week. She was always unprepared and seemed to be making decisions on the spot. She relied on TAs but didn't communicate with them well. She was bad at using tech

She is a new professor and did not seem very prepared for the lecture. She gave out so much reading that it was hard to complete before the next lecture. She relied heavily on support from her TAs, but didn't seem to communicate very well with them. Overall, I don't recommend taking this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was great! Super funny and kind. Her lectures were very much review of the textbook, but you should be reading it anyways so it's actually very helpful. Class is exactly what a college level class should be. Exams were extremely easy if you just read the book and know how to compose a decent 1 paragraph argument. She is amazing and very smart!!
She is great! Super funny and kind, and although her lec
She seems unprepared for lecture. Seems to heavily rely on her TA's for coursework and direction. She can make expectations not clear.
Amazing professor, just lots of reading but interesting course work. cares about students and teaches clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are utterly useless. She will assign homework on a chapter and will not cover that chapter until a week later in lecture. She never gets through the chapter in lecture but somehow talks the whole time. Her tests are incredibly difficult for a beginner class. You will never be prepared for the tests. DONT TAKE THIS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not beginner-friendly. Moves fast and skips vital material. Lectures were her reading off slides from textbook (which you must read anyway, there are 2 of them). High expectations. Exams are hard and unnecessarily complicated for an introductory-level class. Doesn't give enough time to complete them either. Work was never graded on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was easy and Oaxaca truly cares about her students. My biggest complaint, however, is her lecturing style (she is new so give her some grace). All she did was read the slides, which were literally just a copy and paste of the textbook. It was boring at times and easy to skip (your gonna have to read the textbook anyways).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were monotonous and useless

Oaxaca was great. Textbook is necessary as she cannot cover all the content needed for the exams in lecture. Very reading heavy. Exams are long and semi-difficult, but home-learning assignments  give a great cushion for your grade. Lots of extra credit opportunities throughout semester. Discussion attendance is mandatory and so helpful for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very engaging in class and conveys information well. She clearly cares about her students doing well, and wants everyone to succeed. There is a lot of reading, but that comes with Political Science classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Oaxaca is an amazing poli sci teacher, her lectures are fun and occasionally are scenario based. The homework takes a while but is engaging. She wants her students to succeed and it shows!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have ever taken. Gets most of the problems wrong in class and makes many mistakes so hard to follow even if you are listening. Also don't know how I am supposed to prepare when the answer keys are 60% wrong every time. Do not take

The lectures are a bit dry but very straightforward and easy to follow. Old lecture notes are provided, but they contain quite a few calculation errors and typos. Attending class is actually really helpful for making sense of those outdated notes. His exam reviews are also very useful.

Do not take a class with him. He somehow makes everything more complicated than it is and does not even know the right answers. The solutions to practice exams are wrong multiple times and he does not explain anything. Don't bother going to lecture unless you want to rage and just learn it on your own.

This professor did not explain things at all. Had to teach myself the entire course. Would just speed through the work in problems and skip steps. Left the entire class baffled. He would make so many mistakes in his own work leaving us more confused, and sometimes didn't even know how to answer questions from students in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MATH118. If you value your mental health, don't risk it. He messed up his own work, never explained, please save yourself. I learned more from the TA's. I swear, I lost so much hair just from stress because of this man. When I asked for help, he basically ignored me. Make this choice for your own sake, live a happy life without him as your teacher.
He's okay. He often overcomplicates simple topics when there are simpler ways to explain them. You will most likely end up teaching yourself.
He is kind.
youtube is probably better than his lecture

He was deeply committed to ensuring students grasped concepts thoroughly, which I greatly valued. His dedication to our success was evident, and he invested significant time in deriving and explaining ideas clearly. I truly appreciated his efforts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Topics are pretty tough, but exams are basically copies of past exams. Study those and you will get an A.

Easy to fall behind in lessons if you miss lectures but note outlines are provided. Lectures are long but include notes and practice problems. Use homework and discussion packets as practice for exams, the more practice problems you complete the better.

This professor is your typical math professor. Lectors are a little confusing and disorganized. He sometimes goes on random tangents about a niche topic that you don't need to know for the test. I was able to combat this by putting in extra studying. I recommend CramBetter. It went over everything in class in depth and explained it all well.

Absolutely terrible professor, if you have him just watch youtube videos and never go to lecture, if you like someone who is so unorganized and just sits on stage and does nothing this is your guy but i would rather have a snail teach me the class then this "teacher". DO ANYTHING you can to avoid this man..
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade you earn will reflect the effort you put in. Period.

Lecture was actually easy to follow. Very little theory but lots of examples.
Exams are harder than lecture or discussion examples, but fun questions.

Oh Hoon wastes my mortal time on this planet by showing up both late and unprepared to class. He makes mistakes frequently because he doesn't show his work on the board. His method of notes requires an iPad, and it's tough to just use a notebook. He shows little care to his students in general and is very awkward. Please avoid at all costs!

Oh Hoon was never very organized, and many times had to erase and redo his work during lectures. The saving grace for this class was the fact that the past quizzes and exams were always identical to the actual thing, so as long as you feel comfortable with those, you should be okay.

Not a good teacher. He spends a lot of time on equations he thinks are fun to prove and then tells you that you have to learn the rest of the concepts outside of class from the book. I would leave class confused on most days. If you have a choice, don't choose Oh Hoon.

Overall he was just not a great professor. He made the concepts much more confusing than they had to be. He said the final was going to be like the review but was not. Usually the review is similar the the exam. Quizzes were all the same as the previous year just with different numbers.

Oh Hoon is a great person, but a lousy professor. If you didn't take precalc in HS you will be lost. He moves so quickly through difficult concepts that you can't even keep up w/ his rambling. He also makes mistakes 2-3 times per lecture, and sometimes a student has to correct him. However, Oh Hoon's exams are almost identical to his reviews.

Math 114 covered pre-calc concepts learned in high school, but Oh Hoon teaches them in the most confusing ways. He is very unprepared for lectures, often times making mistakes throughout problems. Content on homework is different from what is done in lecture and discussion. Very all over the place.

Oh Hoon moves very quickly in lectures, but he will always stop to answer any questions or confusion if you ask. He is very chill. Attendance doesn't matter, but lecture is helpful to be prepared for the exam. He posts all past exams, which are almost identical to exams you will take. The TA's aren't good, but discussion isn't mandatory.

Oh Hoon had very disorganized lectures and did not plan out what he was going to teach for the day. This made lecture unnecessarily confusing. For a class with content that's already confusing on its own, this put everyone at a disadvantage and most people really struggled to keep up each week.

I don't get why folks below had to lie and make him seem worse than he is. The cool thing about his exams is that he lets us use cheat sheets, which is a lifesaver in those super fast-paced summer math classes. He uses gradescope, which is nice, fair partial credits. It would've been cooler if the class was more interactive.

He writes blazing fast in lecture, so its incredibly difficult to catch up. Pretty disorganized, posts grades and lecture notes insanely late (2-3 week turnover during an 8 week term). Overcomplicates things (Prof dave will be ur friend). Exams were pretty easy at first then the difficulty jumped insanely high with obscure trick questions. Run. Now
Apparently this professor does not even know what he is talking about. On the last class, he spent thirty minutes to figure out an old exam question.
He knows what he is doing.

Oh Hoon is funny, his lectures are dry but he'll come in with an off-handed comment that really makes you laugh if you're paying attention. His midterms were straight forward, but his final did throw me for a loop and ended up messing with getting an A. Overall, I didn't put in a ton of work and it turned out fine- just wished he'd curve a bit.

I am usually pretty good at math but this professor made it extremely difficult to follow. He would joke about how he is known for being disorganized. He gave us the prior exam as the main study method without posting an answer key to see if we were studying the correct material and didn't answer my email when I reached out. Drop him.

Overall it is a difficult class, your grade is pretty much only determined by the 3 exams, but Oh Hoon Kwon goes through lots of examples in class that are clear and easy to study from. He has old exams posted that are exactly what he uses to make the new exams and in the lecture before each exam, he goes over exactly what will be tested.

Calc with Oh Noon was way harder than it needed to be. On the first day of class he says "You have probably heard stories about me being boring and disorganized... they are all true". At least the man is self aware. Lectures are hard to follow and the TAs aren't much better either. Overall, did not have a good experience with the professor or class

Oh Hoon is a really poor professor. His lectures were insanely disorganized. We got 3 weeks behind at one point which meant content was cut, which puts any students taking Calc at a disadvantage. Class isn't necessarily hard in itself but becomes hard with a bad professor. Constantly stated that a curve would be applied, but we never got one.

Oh Hoon Kwon is a caring but unorganized professor. I never used the book even though he said that we should. The subject matter wasn't hard but the way that it was taught made it difficult. I recommend going to every lecture as that is when I learned the most. He would give the subject matter of each test and quiz the lecture before the test/quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Well he did not assign any readings but asked to read the textbook because he said his lecture was going to be a brief outline of what we need to study. It was quite obvious which parts in the textbook were important or not. Do not miss his lectures. It was boring because I already knew the stuffs but if you are new lectures would be very helpful.

Oh Hoon was a mostly careless professor who was occasionally funny but not on purpose. Yelled at us for not reading the textbook but never assigned readings. Gave us a good outline of what was on each exam, so not terribly difficult to succeed in the course, but if you're interested in learning, find another professor.

Oh Hoon is a nice guy, but his lectures are a disaster. Lectures don't correlate with discussion worksheets or homework. You will learn this class exclusively through online youtube videos. This is not a hard subject, at least, it shouldn't be. Which is why it is a miracle that half of his class is failing.
He is not the best lecturer, but he cares and will tell you what to study.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM! If you want to be happy, take another class. Everyone leaves lectures more confused than when they came in. TA's are no help either, literally run away. What we're learning isn't even difficult, the way he teaches makes it so much harder than it should be. Look for online classes instead. Do. Not. Take.

He is a good teacher!! Everything he taught was basically in the textbook. He asked students to read the textbook several times during the class because his lecture was not covering everything. Luckily I followed his advice and started to read the textbook. His test questions were basically from textbook examples and discussion worksheets verbatim.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a decent math teacher, not bad but not good. I was lucky enough that I have a pretty decent memory for math so whenever he doesn't teach something correctly or fully. I just do the homework or watch a video to refresh my memory. Exams are fair but only 3, just study the pass exams and you should be decent off. Think it through and keep calm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: OH Hoon is a nice, caring professor, but he's a really poor teacher. We were 2 weeks behind in lectures and we never got caught up. He also was really hard to understand and didn't answer questions very well. Get a different professor if you can.

All Professor Kwon did was write math problems on the board, showed us how to solve, and move on. Homework at times did not align with what we were learning. Whole class was failing and struggling in some sort with the material. This is not how you teach a subject that people often tend to struggle on. Good luck with email responses. Don't take.
His lectures are an absolute circus, I am never sure what to expect next, his work is unfollowable. Test make a major portion of the grade.

Oh Hoon has horrible lectures, they are so unclear and unorganized. Thank God the material is not that difficult, but pray you have a good TA to reteach you stuff in discussion if you don't understand it. Oh Hoon is a nice enough guy and he tells you what each question on the quizzes and exams test, but the tests are much harder than quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized and confusing, even if you go to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture can be confusing/disorganized/rushed. We would fall behind schedule a lot and go to discussion to work on material we had yet to cover in lecture. Discussions were the most helpful place to learn. The actual material isn't that difficult so if you miss a lecture, it's not that hard to catch up + he tells you exactly what to study for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I could turn back time I would've picked a instructor

With prof. Kwon, his lectures are a mess. There's never a clear idea/ part of what topic he is teaching and every day feels like a new class and it felt incredibly unorganized. There are 2 midterms and a final that is 84% of your grade, so that can be very stressful if you do poorly on exams. Kwon is nice enough, but I had to teach myself. E

Oh Hoon Kwon is a fine professor but the structuring of this class is horrible.  Three tests are worth 84% of your final grade and each one is only 6 questions.  Don't bother asking a question in piazza because no one will answer.  There are weekly quizzes in discussion but they are only worth 4% of your grade.

Kwon consistently gets things wrong or is confused in lectures, making everything even more confusing for the students. Also, over 80% of the overall grade is determined by three exams, the first and third of which were IMPOSSIBLE and the second of which was far too easy. Be prepared to self-teach and pray you have a good TA.

He doesnt give good lectures, he confuses himself during them and only goes off of the textbook. Half the time I had to reteach myself and he gives no good opportunities for students who struggle to regain theyre footing. Pray you have a good TA, which I didnt and maybe you will be able to do good if you arent already a natural at math. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reasonable lectures but a bit tricky exams. Overall it was just fine. Make sure to refresh your algebra! He did not teach heavy algebra, but his exams assumed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was beyond difficult. Your grade mainly depends on three exams. The second exam (average 91) was WAY TOO easy and the first (73)and third (70)exams were impossible. He doesn't curve and lectures do not help. If you do end up in his class, my advice is to take notes in lectures and bring them to math lab, it's the only way I passed.

Nice guy but not a good teacher. Avoid taking this class unless you have to. Take 114 and 221 instead. Exams are hard and there is no curve on them. So many people failed the first exam that the second one was too easy (not complaining) but the final was extremely difficult. Class ave. was a 70%. Self taught the entire class and I'm exhausted.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exam 1 was mostly about algebra. Exam 2 was way too easy kinda calculus-ish. Final was like back to algebra plus what you learned from his calculus. It was pretty fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Final is way too hard and he is AWFUL at teaching.

Guys. please dont take this class with Oh Hoon. I am actually exhausted from teaching myself all of the content because none of his lectures ever made any sense. I am actually begging you. The class AVERAGE was a 77. Do yourself a favor next semester.

While sometimes he makes a good joke or two in class, OH HOON DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO TEACH. Not only does he not know how to teach, he doesnt respond to emails or help you. Do not take a class taught by him if you have the option to.

this math class was the hardest ive taken. attending lecture/discussion didnt help as he was confusing and the TAs suck, no offense. i had to teach myself everything. i would recommend any other QRA class!!
His lecture is pretty easy to follow. Worksheets are crazy, but actual exam questions are not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy and he can be funny on occasion, but he explains concepts in a very complex way and will unnecessarily explain the confusing mathematical reasoning behind equations and it's unnecessary. Im struggling so hard yet I have a tutor twice a week. He just copies examples from the textbook instead of explaining what he is doing.

Professor does a good job with lecture videos. Sometimes, his material is hard to understand but he is mostly clear and concise in his lectures. Lot of tests and homework, but with some studying, this class wasn't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very helpful and understanding professor. Made the class easy with his concise lectures. Was available for help frequently outside of class and is a pure gem of a person. Could not recommend him more.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lecture videos were concise and relatively easy to follow. As exams were open-book, I took screenshots of his work and printed them out. His videos are very helpful in learning the concept. I never used the textbook even once. The homework is hard and lengthy every week. Make sure you go over them! The exams are similar to the HW.

The lectures he posted were rather unnecessary and messy but if you asked him for help through email he was far more helpful. The textbook was very helpful, it was the way I got through the course and learned the material. Tests every week and a few things of homework to go along with it, wasnt bad but time consuming

Your grade is heavily dependent on the exam you have each week, each one being worth 7% of your grade. I stopped watching the lectures halfway through the semester and pretty much taught myself the material. Uses honorlock.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Kwon is a really nice professor!!! Since I take his course I feel that I learn a lot in his lecture. Yes, for sure Kwon sometimes teaches wrongly in his lecture but that can be inspirationalHis class will teach lots of fundamental proofs which can really solve my confusion. If you prepare well, you can waive the final exam. How amazing!

To me, his lectures are very messy. But, he's a very reasonable professor. It is possible to pass with little to no work but it is a lot of work if you want to understand everything he teaches. Seriously, he is super chill! :D

Oh Hoon is a very nice guy but his class is quite difficult. He often spends time on things in class that will not even be on the exams and also puts content on the exams that was covered for only a few minutes if at all in class. While he pushes students to think about math more in depth, he can be an extremely tough grader.
A lot of homework and most of it has nothing or very little to do with what we are learning in class
Very fair and reasonable. He cares students.

Oh Hoon is the sweetest man ever. You can really tell that he cares about his students and wants them to do well. He makes this class really easy to do well in. All of the tests cover the exact material that's on the homework sheets given in discussion. Would definitely recommend.
He knows what he teaches. I learned a lot from the course, and it was a good review from the advanced point of view.

Dr Orrock is hilarious, enthusiastic, and knows his stuff. He gives great explanations, and made what I thought was going to be a boring section of zoology very interesting. He writes class notes on the chalk board, which was awesome. His test was not terrible. If you study and know the material, you'll do great.

He strikes a good balance between knowledgeable and funny. His lectures tend to contain a lot of material, but he's good at providing examples. He writes definitions on the blackboard so you'll have to attend if you want notes.

John Orrock is great! He has the most bubbly personality and his excitement for biology shines through with every lecture! He tends to zoom in on more important concepts rather than go through all the topics from the book so make sure to read, but overall I learned a lot from him and he really wants his students to succeed. Would recommend.

He also writes a lot of notes on the board, so attendance is necessary if you want to pass. He's a great guy and he knows his stuff.

Dr. Orrock does his best to make his lectures engaging. He knows his material well and throws in a lot of humorous examples to keep you interested and to help you remember what's going on. He writes his notes on the board, which is really helpful, but that means you also need to show up. Overall, he's a great guy and I look forward to his lectures!

Professor Orrock is very enthusiastic and gives great lectures.  He writes all of his notes out on the board so there aren't any online notes, so obviously you can't miss lectures.  He was able to break down  hard subject with funnyuseful anecdotes.  The passion he had for what he was teaching made me enjoy the class more.

Orrock is one of the best lecturers. He's abolutely hilarious and I often found myself laughing out loud in class at his jokes. Content isn't all that interesting, but his lectures are entertaining and the class is easy. No text book, maybe 5-10 minutes of hw a week. Go to lecturer though because he takes notes on the board. Easy class, easy A.

Orrock is a great professor and a funny guy. It is incredibly important to show up and take good notes, because he takes notes on the board and the powerpoints he posts online are mainly just pictures. There is no textbook and the only homework is to read a short article every week and post a response. Pay attention and you will do well.

Dr. Orrock is easily one of the best lecturers I've had at UW. He makes ridiculous 90s nostalgia jokes and really lets his personality show through. He also does notes by hand which I respected. This also meant that you need to take notes as his PP contains little info. You also need to scour the text as he pulls the most particular bits for exams.
Dr. Orrock was my favorite professor of the three. He always had great examples and made sure that people understood the material he was getting across. I would take the class again just for him.

He actually does his notes by hand! Very clear in explaining the material and let's you know what's important. His lectures are engaging and makes you want to learn the material. Isn't big on detail, but wants you learn the main concept.
An absolute gem of a class required to fulfill the C/D requirement of the biology major. Easy class, phenomenal professor!

He was the best professor I've had so far. He always tried to make his lectures interesting and used great examples to clarify. Very entertaining and very helpful, learned a lot- made lecture worth waking up for.

Orrock is one of the best professors I've had at Madison. He is very charismatic and passionate about what he teaches and connects well to the class. I was in a power lecture and they didn't seem bad. His exams are not bad and homework is easy. Definitely would recommend his class to someone mildly interested in this field!

Dr. O was great, especially for those trying to get their feet wet in an introductory class. Very charismatic and funny and he clearly loves what he does (which is more than can be said for many). He communicated the information in a clear creative way so that you could remember it. By far the best lecturer in this class.
Great sense of humor and understands that students are as excited as he is. Must say study his examples, those will come up on his exams! By far my favorite of the three lecturers.

Generally, lectures were boring outside of a few hilarious jokes he made. He's a great guy and nerdy in the best way.  I didn't really take the final seriously because i thought evolution/ecology was so obvious but it was harder than I thought it would be. Least favorite of the three who taught bio.

He is a nice person. You can tell he's into what he does. His lectures can be really boring though as well as his slides that are most of the time blank, which he then writes the answers on the board which is time consuming and annoying if you want to look at slides online later. Pretty easy, just be sure to take good notes & stay awake.
He's a cute nerd. Makes nerdy jokes and teaches Ecology and Evolution, pretty boring stuff but he makes in interesting.

Seriously, this guy's fantastic. He always uses ridiculous examples on-the-fly, but they're hysterical. Laughed out loud in class daily AND still learned a ton. Information is easy to understand and very interesting. Wish he taught more than 3 weeks of the class. Looked forward to his lectures and would often be upset when the 50 minutes were up.

Orrock is a pretty good instructor.  His lectures were interesting, but required very active note taking.  He answers student questions very well and makes the concepts more easy to relate to.  His exam was a fair assessment as well.
John Orrock is the Man!  he has the most interesting lectures and makes you want to attend class.  he makes the subject matter very interesting and is always cracking a joke.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken. He was often late, gave unclear answers, seemed annoyed by questions, and barely gave useful advice in conferences. Very disorganized too—forgot assignments and once posted homework at 10 p.m. due the next morning. Avoid if possible.

She also made the tests much easier than they could've been which I really appreciated. avoid this lecture. Prof Rycroft instead

Ohm was amazing, she gave a lot of examples and was clear in her lectures. So much better than other professors who teach this class.

Best math professor so far.

You need to have some common sense/basic understand of fundamentals though.

(update from a low score). She adjusted her teaching method, and the content is relevant to the exam! Midterm 2 was a nice exam! But the exam weight is tooooooo high and ignore our effort in quiz! However, this is the matter of math department
She is a kind teacher!
Cares about students; disengaging lectures; 3 exams are 84% of your grade; weekly HW and module quizzes; late exams; mediocre TAs; grading standards are unclear and not shared
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Better than most math professors in the department, sometimes bland lectures but always easy to follow.

This is Dr. Ohm's first semester teaching after her post-doc at Princeton and I'm happy to see how well she progressed with lectures and how to teach content as the semester went on. She does a very good job with lectures and posts the notes online as well. One thing is she doesn't write the exams (the department does) but, they're very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ohm did a good job teaching Calculus in class. She works several examples in class which is very helpful. She is caring and wants to help you succeed. Very helpful in office hours. That being said, you still need to put in the work outside of class to succeed in this course, regardless of what professor you take.

Ohm did reasonably well for her first time teaching; not perfect but also not bad either. Gives many examples during lecture, which is very helpful. She is a caring professor and takes student feedback seriously. People complain about the first midterm but she is not in charge of making the exams (no individual prof is).
She is a good lecture teacher, but the class is very difficult. Your whole grade is based upon the exams which are difficult.

Professor Ohm is a super kind teacher and she really tries her best to help students. The one star review on her page is very misleading because she does not design the midterms. She went over a very similar example in class and well I agree that the question on the midterm was very difficult, she is not at fault for that.

She's just plain bad at teaching. An entire question on the first midterm was never discussed in class, and only written out once (incompletely) in the notes she posts online, which are hard to follow.

Reflecting on the pedagogical approach of Jason Oakley, it was a certainty in every session that one would encounter a heightened state of conceptual ambiguity. He demonstrated his mastery of educational agility by altering exam formats in real-time! I am giving a one-star rating solely due to the lack of a zero-star metric.#EducationalGaps
In terms of getting by in the class he isn't as bad as everybody makes it it seem but if you really want to learn it can be difficult. He also has a poorly done grading system.
Terrible professor and is the hardest grader of all time.
Great professor, you just have to turn up to lecture to really understand the class.

He is one of the worst ME professors that we have. He clearly isn't very comfortable with the content and it shows in lecture. On top of that he demands no respect from students, and people belittled him on Piazza because of it. Unclear formatting, inconsistency, not good all around.

I never review professors, but I needed to make an exception for this absolute gem. He is sporadic and indecisive, making changes to exam formats with no warning. He claims to not know the amount of time that goes into the homework and decided to raise grade boundaries because he felt that grades for his class were too high. Worst prof in MechE.

Uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh

I usually never write anything in this website but holly this is the worst professor I have ever had to encounter in my whole life. my guy does NOT know what is going on, sometimes it felt like us the students knew much more than him and would fix his grading or rubric. I took two classes with him and he doesn't know what he's doing.

He has to be the absolute worst professor I have ever had. It genuinly seems like he is a student with his basis of knowledge on the things he ATTEMPTS to teach. You are left bored, confused, and frusturated at the end of your time at lectures. Gave us an exam worth 24 points where missing a signage would drop you 5%. Absolutely horrible.

Lectures not mandatory but crucial to understand content.   Go to all of his lectures and use his review materials and you'll pass with flying colors.  Oakley is underrated for sure.  He is also really kind and learns everyone's names by the end of the semester.  Textbook is McGraw Hill - pretty normal stuff.

Beautiful, intelligent, game changing. These are words I would use to describe Jason Oakley. I felt like an angel came down from heaven whenever I went to his class. Although I sat in cramped wooden seats, I felt like a roman being hand fed grapes basking in the sun whenever I heard his voice. 10/10 would recommend if you want a god-like experience
Not a good lecturer. I suggest avoiding him if at all possible. Struggles to convey concepts in a clear and concise manner.
Very bad professor in general. The lectures will be useless and a waste of your time if you show up. I had several projects mis-graded that he refused to fix.

bum 







(extra characters to meet the limit)

Professor Oakley is a living legend. His lectures are like a masterclass in both brilliance and charisma, making even the most complex engineering concepts feel like pure magic. He doesn't just teach—he transforms students into future innovators. His office hours? More like sessions with a guru who imparts wisdom that changes your life.

This guy is the worst professor. There is a clear lack of preparation that goes into his instruction.He probably doesn't use SolidWorks and MATLAB on a regular basis for his actual work which is incredibly noticeable during lectures to students who have become proficient in the platforms through internships.
Jason Oakley did not teach the necessary material to succeed in the course. Very dry, non-informative lectures. I had to learn everything from my TA during lab sections.
very boring
He is passionate about what he is teaching, that's for sure. Just isn't the best teacher. His grading criteria is also not clear at all.

Jason Oakley didn't understand the material he was teaching, the lectures for this course have little to nothing to do with the graded work you will be assigned, and what is taught is entirely off topic. Your lab and your TA will be this entire class for you. Show up to lab and the course is a piece of cake, the TA's are wildly more helpful.

Terrible. 

Avoid

He should find a new calling.

Probably the most confusing grading I've ever had. He gives you examples for the homework which dont meet the grading rubric and makes mistakes all over the rubrics and homework instructions. Lecture is absolutely useless so the class is essentially just figuring out the homework yourself and attending lab.
He just did not know what he was teaching and what he should teach.

I've had Jason in multiple classes, and can safely say his lectures are some of the most useless lectures I've been to. I've seen him read off of the textbook in class, and answer valid questions with "I just showed you that". His lectures and homework assignments are riddled with substantial mistakes that make it very frustrating to learn from him

Not as terrible as a lot of people say. His lectures definitely aren't helpful, but you don't have to go and the class isn't hard compared to other ME classes. The homework is long but TAs are helpful and most of us who stay for lab get it almost done during class. His exams were reasonable and open note. Most people I know are hovering around AB-A

He demonstrates passion and enthusiastic during his lectures. The impeccable lecture layout clearly articulates complex ideas. Students are always waiting to see what wisdom and knowledge he will bless us with today. His careful planning and attention to small details makes sure every homework is fine tuned to absolute perfection for his students.

Jason Oakley has a way with words. His ability to give a thorough and thoughtful breakdown of concepts is unmatched. I go into class knowing nothing, but when I leave I feel a sense of euphoria. The only reason I wouldn't take the class again is because he did such a good job teaching the material, won't need to. I can see why he's employed.

It was guaranteed in every lecture that you would either be more confused by the concept or he would not explain the topic at all and then expect you to do homework and exams on the topics he was unable to teach.  Had to learn the entire class from one student who had prior knowledge.  Received one star only because I cant put zero.

It is probably better to just read the text book and show up for quizzes and tests because all Oakley does is take the equations from the textbook and write them on the board. He jumps around, adds things randomly, explains things unclearly and has no grasp of what his own homework is about.

This is the only Rate my Professor review I have ever given because he was that bad. He took over teaching our class for the last 3 weeks of the semester and switched the entire curriculum. He then proceeded to not show up to our final exam. He never sent an explanation or an apology. Just a complete ghost. I have never had a worse experience.
He didn't show up for our FINAL. How does that happen.
He is really thoughtful and caring his students a lot. Great explanation and exams are fair.

This professor's lectures are absolutely useless, and he makes many mistakes in lecture. He does not offer any resources to practice for the exams, nor is he clear about his grading rubric and takes off points for seemingly no reason.  He doesn't hand back exams so students can improve and when help is requested he refuses to offer it.  0/10.

He isn't a bad person but he isn't the best teacher. He can be very monotone when teaching low level courses like ME231 but he does enough to get the point across. I felt confident in my learning throughout the course. If you are willing to put time into lab assignments you will be fine grade-wise.

The class isn't very hard but he is not a very helpful professor and is very boring as well. Try to get ahead or keep up because if you get behind it is hard to catch up because things start to pile on very quickly. Overall, the class is pretty easy.

One of the least passionate professors. Skips class without alerting his students. Gets frustrated when students ask genuine questions. Lectures where he does show up are a useless hour of students watching him do Solidworks. Possibly better for other classes, but not great for ME 231.
Absolute snooze

Literally worst class I have taken to date. Zero guidance whatsoever and expects students to be experts at solidworks and whatever the h3ll the on paper assignments are supposed to be. Absolutely terrible feedback no rhyme or reason to anything and it is almost impossible to not get docked like 5 points on each assignment just because. Terrible.

Has no passion teaching lower level courses. Teaches SolidWorks Concepts but not how to make parts in SolidWorks. This is the part most students get caught on. Overheard him telling a student who took 5 hours to complete the first assignment that he needs to get better at SolidWorks and maybe the course isn't for him.

Jason Oakley was an alright professor. His exams were worded weird in order to, I feel, trick students. His lectures are incredibly boring most of the time since the material is 20 years outdated at best. He seemed like a genuine guy who cares for engineering. He did completely miss 2 lectures with no warning though, so maybe you'll get lucky.
Worst engineering professor I have had yet. Lacks passion to teach the subject and it shows since it seems like no one is paying attention in lecture.

He's pretty dry. The lectures aren't always relevant to the material. He seems like a nice enough guy, but his lectures are not very interesting and he says uhh so much it made my head hurt. He was a fair grader and test giver though. I feel for a harder class he might not be a great choice.

Oakley was really good professor for fluids. I found he did well with explaining the complicated subjects of the course. Office Hours everyday was a plus. Quizzes every week which is heavy but helps with the learning process. Our tests were the same for a different professor, our class scored consistently higher than the other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Oakley often would do example problems incorrectly in class, would not show up to classes and wouldn't tell any students he wasn't coming so we all sat and waited for him not to come, very boring lectures and exams would contain questions with little similarities to course content.

Professor Oakley may seem a little intimidating but he's a nice guy if you ask for help. He's very traditionalist in that all homework is handed in/hand graded which I really appreciated. The Solidworks assignments can take a LONG time even if you know Solidworks because you have to follow the textbook. Tests are pretty hard and worth 50%. He's ok!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures. The homework assigned is not reflective of what is on the exams. The exams are multiple-choice, random pieces of information, that are barely mentioned, if mentioned at all, in lecture. Because of this, the class lacks materials that are helpful for studying. High-grade distribution (94 for an A) and no curve.

Lectures were admittedly boring, but Prof. Oakley was very accommodating, clear, & made sure you had the tools to succeed. Try to make yourself focus during lectures and the class isn't that bad, but you can fall behind fast. He offered lots of office hours & gave extensions if you struggled with something. Not a very tough grader. I'd take again.
He wasn't great at lecturing but he isn't bad either. In general this is a pretty average class. However, some of the more difficult stuff is crammed together at the end of the course.

Mr. Oakley released the wrong final exam for our class (the exam he released was locked in November) which left 100+ students waiting around for 2 hours for ANY sort of update only time receive a new test in a time slot that the majority of students werent available for and he never really apologized or admitted an error on his part that.
Professor Oakley is fine but my TA helped me the most in this class. His SW assignments are fun, in my opinion. To learn the most from his class, I suggest getting a TA as your lab instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sometimes his lectures can feeling monotonous but that's the only negative I have. He is very clear on what he expects and actively tries to prepare you for those expectations. If you even put slight effort into the class, you'll be well on your way to understanding the material.

Reading and online homework due for every lecture, but you're allowed to see the answers and take them multiple times and they help you understand the material. Generally, I'd read the textbook, see examples in lecture, and practice via homework. Oakley was always very responsive and clear via email and office hours. Solid prof for Fluid Mech

Jason Oakley is really helpful in office hours, but he doesn't know the material. This class is taught in a really inefficient way. We needed to design a mechanism that will be 3D printed, but we didn't learn how to be successful. It's worth 15% of our grade. He doesn't accurately represent the tests with lectures or practice problems.
Plane awesome professor

The amount of homework he assigns is pretty ridiculous.  However, you can find the answers online pretty easily.  He writes really fast and therefore has bad handwriting.  That's why I gave him a 2 for clarity.  Not a horrible Professor but I wouldn't recommend him.  Found it difficult to stay awake in class.

While poor at teaching the beginning of the semester, he conducted a mid-semester survey to gauge what areas he was lacking in. After that, his teaching ability went up dramatically and he switched from teaching mostly theory to mostly examples. For a new professor he did a pretty good job.
She is a great professor! Very personable and willing to help you understand. You can tell she cares about biology and helping her students understand. Tests are difficult though.
She puts a lot of effort into the course and is very clear about the requirements/expectations for each day. Also a very lovely person who makes an effort to get to know you.
gale oakes is a very lovely woman. she cares a lot about this course while adding fun a whimsy at the same time. if you pay attention and show up very little is needed outside of class time.

You're lucky if you saw Gale twice throughout the semester, course is completely TA led. Almost all of grade is based in “quizzes” but I argue their difficulty are like an exam. Averages are always low, grading is tough, no curve and no rounding. Take 151/152 sequence.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All depends on your TA, Peter Conowall was great. If you actually study and learn the learning goals you will be fine

Bio 102, managed by Gale Oakes, was a waste of my tuition. The quizzes were 90% of your grade, never returned, were fill in the blank, and took ages for them to grade. Average was a C. Gloves are $$. My TA was also unprepared and never explained topics well. No practice tests/quizzes, makeups, or joy to be found in this course. Steer away.
This class is basically thought by TA's and it really just depends on your TA. Gale Oakes seems kind and caring but my TA was a tough grader.

This class was graded by few things and she wouldn't let me make up a ten point quiz that was the difference between a B and an A for my final grade, even though I hadn't been in the class yet while the quiz was given. Would not recommend she screwed me over after working hard all semester.

Great Professor, her slides were extremely helpful and informative. She brought live speakers who helped get the story from someone who does studies there or is from the area. There are a couple reading and videos to watch for leacture that are important to do, but overall she is a good proffesor just hope you have a good TA.

I've taken a couple classes with Professor Otting. Overall, she's passionate and clearly cares about the stuff she's teaching. I would say that my TA made the class more challenging than Professor Otting did. Regardless, not a difficult class and content is easy to grasp.

Currently working on her final paper, and it does not make sense. The final essay questions ask about policy, when this whole class was based in issues, not policy. Then she asks for multiple sources to be used per answer, when each reading does not relate to the others. It is impossible to give a good response with the given materials. so stupid
I really liked this professor. She seems very nice and I liked her lectures. Assigned many videos as well which was nice.

I was really excited for her course, but she is just not a good professor. Class lectures feel robotic, and she does not provide grading rubrics and will randomly give pop quizzes (was NOT in the syllabus as part of a grade or mentioned as a possibility). She also will not respond to emails, and trying to have a conversation with her is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring professor with surface-level content and discussions. There is an overall lack of grading consistency and clarity - does not provide rubrics or clear guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have the option to take 240 and 300 with a different professor, I would definetly do that.

Very interesting lectures that were easy to follow along. Lots of readings, but most of them were super digestible and intriguing as they were required to be used as references for the midterm and final paper. Group project in discussion worth 25% of overall grade, but it was well-explained and didn't require much time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Otting was great! Our lectures were always very engaging and we talked in groups a lot. There were many readings and videos/podcasts for class, but they were all pretty interesting and easy to get through. We only had 3 essays and a project, and while they were pretty big we had a lot of time to complete them and ask for help.
