reviews.comment: Do not take his course. He does not know what he is talking about
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not useful
Professor Qin may not be acquainted with the course content and exhibits a lack of knowledge in statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized. The syllabus was essentially a suggestion, as deadlines were moved with zero notice. Expect to wait 3+ weeks for any grade to be returned, usually with zero feedback on why points were docked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Reginold has been, by far, the worst professor that I have had. Any clarification question asked during lecture is met with a degrading response. Furthermore, he does not answer emails and tends to prioritize the sale of his "works" rather than the education of his students.
he's got LOADS of attitude. very condescending. he asks us to do tons of reading, watch long films, AND complete linkedin trainings. very harsh grader too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Waited ONE hour for a zoom call that he didn't show up to, then claimed there was a confusion regarding the link. Like.. we all know you forgot. Mind you we had to pay $35 to watch a movie to discuss in THAT zoom call. Canvas is VERY poorly organized, a ton of readings AND films to watch just for a 300-word discussion post, no materials of his OWN!

I have some choice words for this prof. For one, he didn't even show up to a zoom discussion we were required to attend, while we all waited. The course itself is very disorganized and glitchy, with canvas materials written so poorly I question how he could have written his own publications. He's also condescending. Can't believe he is tenured!

LIS500 was an interesting class. Contrary to popular opinion I didn't mind the LinkedIn certifications and they were semi helpful. Participation matters a lot in this class and it has to be like novel and meaningful. Grading criteria is all over the place, max effort usually got you an A but randomly you'd get points off. Not a very friendly guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took African100 and inevitably had to drop the class. I attended every class and still received a 0% for attendance and when I asked to talk about it, he responded with "are you done?" and walked away. It wasn't until I dropped the class that he responded to my numerous emails and said "we were going to accommodate, but you already dropped."

AVOID REGINOLD. Genuinely awful professor. Grading requirements were vague and often required students to read his mind as to what he was looking for. This led to harsh grading, and at times, condescending feedback. "Lectures" some weeks consisted of being asked to watch full documentaries or complete certificates on LinkedIn Learning. Very bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very passive-aggressive/condescending person. He and the TA are also very harsh graders. Make sure you budget lots of time for completing long readings, watching documentaries, and completing Linkedin certificates. Quizzes are very confusing even if you do the readings and watch lectures, but other assignments/projects aren't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. The course modules are incredibly disorganized and confusing. The professor's lectures are just basic overviews, lasting only about ten minutes, but then he expects us to watch three hours of videos on LinkedIn Learning to teach ourselves. It's just awful. It's hard to imagine this person is a professor at UW-Madison.

It is an online course this semester for 3 credits. Really confusing modules including messy assignment and poor organization. Can not figure out why there is prof like him existing in top 50 US universities while we pay them so much each year.

African 100: The course itself was very all over the place and the professor essentially just mooched off several different professors for the course material- close to none was his own. On top of this, he is very condescending. Then, he'd be shocked and angry when no one wanted to volunteer anymore. Finally, our grade was based on unclear quizzes.

He has a demeaning attitude. Lots of reading and you are graded on very few things meaning you better do well on the things you're assigned. His lectures are essentially useless as they never teach you anything new or anything you need for tests. I'm sure he might be a good guy, just not the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: REVIEW FOR AFRICAN 100: Reginold Royston is not only just a terrible person, he's an even worse professor. I've learned nothing about Africa while taking this class. I've never seen such low grades in an intro class.
never again he's rude and so is his TA Dami.

Grade based on 
- attendance (lecture and discussion)
- midterm and cumulative final
- weekly quizzes on reading/ video lectures

He is demeaning, condescending, and very blunt. The readings and videos (if done correctly) would have take forever. The quizzes were said to be "straight forward", but they really were not.

Royston assigns tons of readings, but if you skim them for key ideas you'll be fine in class discussion. A few quizzes and a final project & one longer midterm paper, but assigned with plenty of notice and criteria is clear. Royston actually reads through your work & gives meaningful feedback. Class very easy yet very interesting.

Expectations are vague. Very judgemental of opinions but also wants students to share their opinions therefore it feels that you have to say what he wants you to say. The course organization is a bit messy (old links) and the content is out of date. As someone who talks about inclusivity, he does not foster that environment.

Supremely vague in his expectations. Something is due on one day, nothing else is written, but he expects you to have it done much earlier because it was communicated by ... Idk, osmosis? For someone who's obsessed with effort as reflected by Big Brother surveillance stats, he is certainly dialing it in and using materials from years past.
Dr. Royston is a nice person, but not a good instructor. His feedback is generally vague and grades harsh. Lectures are boring too!! Take someone else if you have a chance

This was my favorite class I took this semester. There are 2 harder assignments for communication B, but for the most part, homework was just readings that you could get away with skimming if necessary. The subject matter is very interesting, and the class is mostly discussion-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class had a rare combination of being incredibly interesting and also fairly easy. There are two major assignments that are on the more difficult side, but the majority of the class is just completing academic readings for homework and discussing them in class. The discussions are all fascinating, and Professor Royston really makes you think.
Sean paul has done such a number to me that when I got the alert yesterday for the tornado I immediately put my shoes on and went outside looking for it

do not be afraid of sean paul!!! (except maybe in OH). his lectures are engaging, if you can understand abstract concepts, but he expects you to come to class having read the textbook– you must read the textbook! exams are fair, normally pretty straight-forward, he practically tells you exactly what is going to be on them if you go to lecture.
describe sean paul in exactly 6 words make no mistakes or u get a zero oh youre wrong  zero that wasn't the six words i was thinking of try again next time :(

His lectures are so abstract that it is almost impossible to follow along for the whole hour and 15 minutes. He told us to drop the class if you got under a 50% on the exam (mind you the average was a 58%). Told us to redo the hw's to study, and then proceeded to put nothing from the homework's on the exam. Lowk kinda mean too.
told us the other day to watch 3 lecture recordings before coming to his class and then I bet I will go to his class and he will say nothing intelligent for the entire period

I did onlyfans to pay for my tuition this semester and now I will probably have to retake this class because Sean Paul is failing everyone. this class is easily the second hardest thing I have ever done.

assigns homework out of a textbook he doesnt teach from, failed more than half the class on the exam and then never handed it back. everything is all over the place with his class. says everyone failing is their own fault for not reviewing concepts from prior math classes that arent even a pre req for this class.
he has a passion for math. but he doesnt teach "real" math he teaches things that have no useful application at all.

he teaches the theory behind math instead of real usable math to his class of engineers. talking about musical isopodpromorphisms like bruh cmon. he talks about how we need to revisit classes we never took like math 340 prior this one. none of us took 340. i wish he could teach real math instead of whatever it is he is doing as of recently

Singled out individual students infront of the class after poor exam performance for everyone. Does not actually know the prerequisites for this class (most of us have not taken 340) Initially was liking him but after the first exam he just kinda ranted to us about “not trying”, many of these people were the same people I had seen in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor assumes everyone has a strong background in linear algebra, which makes his abstract lectures hard to follow. More concerning, though, is how discouraging he is after poor exam scores; he tells students to reconsider the course or even their major. That kind of response is demotivating and inappropriate/unethical from a professor.
Sean none of us took math 340 like literally 5 of us maybe the rest didnt so yeah

In fact it is a very good course. It provides video recordings of each class. As long as you study diligently you can learn a lot and it's not difficult to get good grades. Highly recommend Professor Paul.

Sean Paul's a chaotic teacher. His lecture material often differs from the textbook, and he fails to articulate his expectations. This, coupled with sudden office hour cancellations and random email response times, makes him hard to work with. While he knows and cares about what he's teaching, a little organization would go a long way for his class

day one of class he holds up fabians textbook and says "who here has read this front to back?" and half of the class who is retaking raised their hand. then he said "forget everything you thought you knew because its all wrong!" and the whole class erupted in a jolly cheer. and we lived happily ever after. the end.

Great guy, but man... those lectures were basically useless. Extremely hard to follow and not at all focused on topics that were tested. Realized halfway through the course that my time was better spent going to discussion and studying by myself or getting an extra hour of sleep instead of going to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anyone who has taken his class knows his lectures are a waste of time. At the same time he doesn't have a clear criteria for giving points. So he ends up giving a grade based more on whether or not you have satisfied his vanity in the class rather than your true level.

Irresponsible, no syllabus or grading criteria, and unorganized lectures. You will know nothing about Jacobi fields, the index lemma, or comparison... Instead, he repeatedly talked about his three ways to define connections and his spin group construction from Clifford algebra. It's like taking dental advice from your eye doctor.
other reviews speak on how well he is respected

One of the worst professors I've had at UW-Madison. Tends to ramble on about irrelevant topics in lecture. Disorganized. Showed up more than 5 minutes late a few times. Hard to see him use his fingers to explain concepts. Once, he glossed over a topic in the last 30 seconds of lecture because he would "get in trouble without saying it."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Lecture Summary:
(note we are 3 weeks behind)
Prof gives (through hand movements) a question about something we never talked about, discuss with someone next to you
Prof walks around and no matter your answer, you're wrong
oopsies, 75 min class is over, no answer for you!
