There's two long papers and some short writing assignments that are easy A's, and some quizzes that are simple. It's an easy A if you show up to class and try on the essays. My first essay was graded way harder than the second.

Zumbrunnen is a really great professor. You'll learn a lot about his family and his dogs. Personally I really like his back stories, it keeps the class interesting and he ties it into the material really nicely sometimes. He also managed to boil down really complex theoretical concepts into understandable portions.

One of the best professors I've had at UW. Explains everything incredibly well and wants his students to succeed and leave with a knowledge of important political ideas. Lectures are interesting and he does everything he can to make them as fun as possible. Take PS209 with him if you can.

John is one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes the subject matter, even if it's boring, seem very interesting and explains things so well that difficult concepts become almost perfectly clear by the end of lecture. He is also hilarious, and students really like him! Bi-weekly quizzes are very fair and TAs are caring and helpful.
This man is a saint. Even if you have no interest in political science, he works with you and pushes you. He is awesome and I am so happy I took a class with him!

Best professor I have ever had. It shows that he is really passionate about what he does. His lectures are crystal clear, incredibly interesting, and he always took the time to make sure we understood the material. I really looked forward to lecture every week. Kristen was an awesome TA too.

Awesome Professor! It may be hard to get up early every M/W, but trust me, it is a MUST GO. I barely read the textbook because John was so knowledgable, clear, and to point about everything we needed to know. Great examples, quotes, and stresses on important materials. Only downside is that the TA's grade your stuff completely. Write for your TA.
Amazing teacher! Don't need to buy the book!!!  So helpful and knows what he's talking about!  Really understanding nice guy

Never read the textbook. He explained everything really well. His lectures were always interesting, and he kept your attention. Tests were fair. Our final wound up being online because of snow, but it was a bit tougher than the midterms.
Easily my favorite professor. Great guy; funny. Didn't read textbook once; he goes over everything in lecture.

Professor is extremely knowledgable, friendly, and entertaining. Makes an otherwise dull subject bearable. Exams are short answer/essay, graded by TAs, no other assignments/grades besides participation. Lecture not mandatory but you will not succeed in class unless you attend and take VERY DETAILED notes. Recommend to anyone look for theory credits

Favorite professor so far, the lectures would be really boring with someone else teaching it. He keeps it interesting and easy to understand. The tests are pretty straight forward as long as you attend lecture and take good notes. I barely use my textbook, the readings are boring and long, but he does such a good job in lecture.

Favorite professor by far. He is extremely entertaining and wants you to do well. Everything you need to know for the exam he explains in class and lays it out for you. No need to read the text because he fully explains the text as long as you go to lecture. The only downside is the TA's grade everything.

He makes the class fun and is a very clear in lecture.  Everything you need to know about the reading is covered when he lectures.  However, I would advise taking really good notes.  He lays out everyting you need to know clearly but his slides are mainly just quotes and its hard to go back and figure out what he wanted you to get out of them
A good guy, though I got the sense it was pretty tough to get an A. Covers just about everything you need to know in lecture, which is good because some of the readings can be pretty dense.

I enjoyed this professor a lot, getting up at 8:50 was worth his humor and friendly demeanor. However, there was a great disparity among his TA's. The female TA, Kaitlyn Jones was much more difficult/unfair than the other TA. TA's grade everything.

Really entertaining and easy to talk to. Made class fun and interesting. Didn't need readings to understand class but it helped to do them. Assignment instructions were really clear. Awesome guy who really knows how to connect with college kids. Very chill class.

Great professor. I had no poli sci classes prior and understood everything. The readings seem daunting and hard to understand but you basically don't have to read anything because he explains the material so well. Very entertaining and engaging.
Great Prof
Great Professor.  Cares that you learn the material and why it matters.  Not hard, but you should definitely do the work because you will benifit immensely from the insights he brings to it.

Such a fun lecturer. He always tells funny stories to make the boring topic of political theory enjoyable. He tries really hard to make lectures enjoyable. Great professor definitely take a class from him. The final is a paper so makes it even better!
Good teacher, funny guy. Probably an even better teacher for people who have the slightest interest in political science, which definitely was/is not me.

Zumbrunnen is a really great lecturer; he's interesting and funny.  The class has a lot of reading but all the important concepts that you will be tested on he reviews during class so it isn't necessary to read to get a good grade.  There are 2 midterms, a final paper, and 3 1-2 reflection papers.  Not a super hard class.

Good teacher. He doesn't try to trick students on the tests and the course is taught at a leisurely pace. He's also technologically literate (for the most part) and he likes to integrate videos into lectures to give historical or personal context to the material.
Very entertaining teacher, class not too difficult

I don't care what anyone else says- if you want an A, you need to read the books. The concepts are difficult and Machiavelli sucks, but just memorize the study guide answers (which take a lifetime to write up) by heart. Best part is John keeps the class upbeat (even with the really dry material) and responds to any question on study guide via email

Class runs with PoliSci 502 so I was overwhelmed at first. No need to due readings, but lecture is mandatory. He tells you all the important things from readings. Very interesting class, and GREAT teacher.

Great professor, really knows what he is talking about. The subject material for the class is pretty boring and at times confusing, but he made it all clear in lecture. 2 papers and 2 exams, all doable, but go to lecture!! You will be lost without good notes! Don't bother doing the readings, its really not necessary.

Amazing professor. Class topic would have been extremely boring with anyone else but he was funny, engaging, and interesting.  He was easy to understand and laid out all the concepts clearly.  Not too much work since you don't really need to do the readings.  The class wasn't too hard, either.  Very helpful.  Highly, highly recommended.
great teacher

Zoe Todd is the best professor I've ever had at UW-Madison. She made very challenging material easy to understand, she was accessible outside of class, and she very clearly cares a lot about her students and the material she teaches. Get ready for some cute pony pictures too!
Zoe is the best professor in UW chemistry department!

Dr. Zoe was amazing! She held multiple office hours during the week and extra during exam time. She was extremely helpful and guided you if you were stuck. As other people said, she remembers so many names. She really cares about you as a student and as a person. Would love to take again!
A top notch professor that really cared. She memorized the first 3 rows names in a giant lecture hall for multiple sections. Truly a kind individual

Though she is one of the newer professors in the chemistry department, she was the first professor that made me feel like I was actually cared about in a class so large. She was kind, caring and always willing to find ways to help no matter what the situation was. She taught in a way that was very easy to follow and understand.
Before I took this class, I saw somebody commented here " Zoe is an angel". Now, after having her class this semester, I have to say that student is absolutely right!!

One of the best prof in chemistry department, she is super helpful especially in her office hour, she is always welcome to help you. Btw, she remember every students' name, even if you only been to her office hour at once.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Todd has been fantastic and she cares deeply about every student. The exams are very fair as long as you do the homework and discussion materials and try studying. She is an amazing professor and I wish I could have her for 562
One of the best chemistry professors at UW. She priorities supporting her students and giving them respect.

Professor Todd was the best Chem 104 professor I could have asked for. She cares about her students, tries to learn their names, and was really nice. She taught in a way that was clear and not confusing. If you can get her for Chem 104, you totally should.

Zoe Todd is an absolutely wonderful teacher, lecturer, and person. She'll try to learn your name and major and help more than any other professor I've had. Her classes are wonderful and you're privileged to have Dr. Todd as an instructor. HIGHLY RECCOMEND!!!!

zoe todd is an ANGEL on earth!  trust me... take her class if you want a good grade and someone who cares about you.  go to office  hours once a week and sit at the front of class!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Zoe if you see this legit bless your soul you are amazing

Professor Todd has been the best professor I've had. She genuinely cares about her students and would have several review sessions before each exam which no other professors would do. Her lectures were great and she was very responsive to emails and feedback. She would get to know people's names in the lecture, and overall I really enjoyed class.

Dr. Todd is the best professor I've had so far on campus. She cares a ton about her students success and holds helpful review sessions before each exam. She broke down complicated topics very well and made the expectations for each exam clear to all students. Her lectures helped expand on topics we had learned outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Todd is among the smartest and kindest chemistry professors in the chemistry department. They encourage learning and are always fair on exams and homework. Their support and availability make sure that anyone can succeed and learn. If you see them teaching a class, take it, you won't regret it.

The best professor I have ever had. She is so knowledgable on the topics and extremely helpful. She truly cares about her students and the tests are very fair to the content. Getting a good grade is very doable by going to review sessions and doing the homework.

Professor Todd was an amazing professor for Chem 104. For someone who hasn't taken chem prior to freshman year of college, she was extremely caring and ready to work with me whenever I needed so I could fully understand the concepts. Would definitely recommend her, the class itself is somewhat difficult if you have no previous chemistry knowledge.

Prof. Todd was the BEST professor i have had at the university so far. She was extremely accessible outside of class and she would host 4 review sessions before every exam which shows how dedicated she was to students success in chemistry. She is fair, and I felt like when i studied for chem exams the material I studied actually was on the exam.

Dr. Todd is the best - she actually cares about teaching and her students. She knew almost everyone's name in a huge lecture, was always available to meet, and held lots of review sessions before every exam. She went above and beyond and wanted her students to succeed. Highly recommend!!

Zoe Todd is the best professor I have ever had at UW. She is kind, easy to reach outside of class, and puts extra effort into getting to know her students. Her exams were fair and she often felt sympathy for when test averages were low or students struggled. Best chemistry professor for sure.

Zoe Todd is one of the only professors I have had that made an effort to get to know her students! She cared about the feedback she received and was willing to adjust based on the class's response. I wish I could have her next year too!
Truly cared for her students!

If you have the option to take a class with Zoe Todd, I promise she is worth changing your entire schedule around for.  if you want to get an A, sit in the front and go to office hours.  She will know your name within 2 classes and is more than willing to help at ALL TIMES.  I went to office hours every week and she kept me from dropping out tbh

Zoe is one of my favorite professors that I have had. She genuinely prioritizes geting to know her students and helps them thrive in her class. She is extremely accessible outside of class online, in office hours, and review sessions before exams. It is a difficult course and the the homeworks are hard, but they set you up for success on exams.

10/10 would recommend. Office hours and review sessions were available and extremely helpful before exams. She taught a challenging class really well. I'm not a math person, but she broke down the math in an easily digestible way and walked us through each critical thermodynamic derivative. Zoe cares about her student's success!

Clear and paced lecturer. Immense respect for students. Checks in about understanding and preferences regarding course structure frequently. Puts in lots of personal time. Offers review sessions before every exam. Fair and fast grader. Student success driven. Guarantees success to those who try. Higher grade average due to superior teaching style.

Adam is a well educated entreprenuer. However he is not a good teacher. He has many strict policies that are designed for you to fail. He uses condisending tones and is really bad at reading emails entirely. If you make an honest mistake he will make sure to let you know other students did not. Smart person, doesn't belong in teaching.

Dr. Bock is a solid entrepreneur, a great speaker, and a bad teacher. He's good to talk to, but the class and its' policies are designed to break you. This is his side gig and that shows in his behavior and mindset. The content was awesome, but seriously, take anyone else if you can. You are a number to him and he won't hesitate to remind you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adam Bock was the worst professor I have ever had. Avoid this class if you can. The professor seems to have zero interest in helping students succeed and acts like he wants you to fail. It feels like Adam Bock wants you to get a bad grade and tries to trick you. Don't take him. It's frustrating and feels like a waste of time. DO NOT TAKE!!!

One of the worst I've ever had! He teaches nothing. You watch a lot of videos and read a lot of readings and that's it. A group project with exams and quizzes. Bock definitely doesn't care about this class and his students. He only wants to flex his experiences while adding no value to our learning and career journey. Such a waste of my tuition.

First, this class is a free A, exam questions are REUSED every year, and there are quizlets with the answers. Second, everything that was said in the 2 messages below is true. However, Bock has legit entrepreneurship experience-- and quite a bit. But Bock seems to have a lot more going on outside of teaching, and this to me is more of a side gig

From the first lecture, it was clear Bock was not interested in getting to know his students & he solely holds this position to boast about his successes. Took this class for the entrepreneurship cert, would not take a class from Bock again unless he decides to show a shred of interest in anyone other than himself.enroll w ppl for the group project

I love the class and hate the professor. Never in my life have I had a professor as egotistical and incosiderate as Dr. Bock. He is more interested in power tripping than actually teaching. If I was the department head, Dr. Bock would never teach another class a day in his life. As a professor, you want to help his students. Bock is the opposite.
The class was easy A, exams were not too hard. Bock was, however, pretty rude to students, didn't really learn anything for the class...

Dr. Bock is really nice and approachable. As long as you do the required assignments on-time and actually put effort into your t-shirt project, you will do well. Exams were not bad. This class covered a lot of different topics that are very useful for developing an entrepreneurial mindset. If you have the chance to take this with him, do it!

very strict, no-nonsense. Class only meets once a week, weekly readings and quizzes, one big project. most of the work is busy work. most of the exam questions are from the weekly quizzes so WRITE THEM DOWN. grade dropped 8% for not buying reading material on time, not very flexible with deadlines

Bock is meh. Class only meets once a week with short readings and videos to watch in addition. Weekly quizzes are extremely easy, exams are very fair and pretty much all of the weekly quizzes put together verbatim. T-shirt project is other main component which is just busy work basically. Easy A/AB for entrep. cert.

I am mixed about this class. Bock is a great lecturer, very knowledgable, but he's not a person I would visit for office hours. He's the kind of teacher whose feedback is "you should have read more" or "that's more of a you problem." There are at least 4 tophat questions each lecture which count for accuracy and partic. Good teacher, bad for help.

Relatively easy class, but get ready to read the textbook for his exams. He covers most of the material in lecture. However, if you don't want to wake up that early, you can easily read the chapters that are covered in the textbook and easily pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Adam is very knowledgeable about the entrepreneurial world, and his past experiences coupled with his expectations that all your work has strong data & evidence to prove it, make papers & case studies one of the harder parts of the class. Nonetheless, his tough grading makes you learn a lot about how to write and significantly back up your claims.

The worst thing about this professor is his inability to realize that not everyone has had the same learning experience up until this class. He will bring up calculus 2 or 3 concepts not required for this class, and make simply physics far more confusing. Will skip every step saying that it is "simple algebra", and call the class simple and easy.

Great professor, obvious he enjoys what he teaches Passionate during experiments. Sometimes difficult to understand due to his accent but all his lectures are accompanied by a slideshow that one can look to if they have trouble understanding his lecture. Exam's were(not sure if still are) online.

He mostly just reads off slides and just gives the basic information instead of delving deep into the content. However, he makes expectations clear and provides you with a lot of resources to let you succeed. Often times, test questions are just modified HWs.

He's a difficult professor in terms of he tells you the information and expects you to work out the "learning" part of it, but he really does want to make sure you are learning and he will stop the class for any questions, and encourages it.

Lectures were lazy and were just slideshows with definitions and formulas. He expected everyone to just know everything because we were physics majors, so he would never explain anything he deemed simple. When asked a question, he would start answering a different, unrelated question, so it was impossible to ask meaningful questions in lecture.

Professor Pan is an engaging lecturer, though the pace can be challenging. Staying engaged and using resources like the textbook and Unstuck study make all the difference. Overall, a rewarding class if you put in the work.

Just reads off slides and fails to elucidate derivations of equations. Everything is "trivial" and you never have a fundamental understanding of whats being taught. That said, Pan is very fun. We do demos and I find myself consistently engaged in lectures, though not due to understanding the material. He's passionate, just not a great lecturer.
Almost completely inaccessible online. If you want to talk to him about anything you have to do it in person. Lectures were fine overall, he posts slides.

Though the pace of the lectures is a bit faster than normal classes, Professor Pan is very passionate about teaching and really wants his students to learn Physics well. Gradings and exams are all fair.

He tries (but fails) in lecture, and is completely unavailable outside of it.  He does not teach well, as in, he cannot.  He shows equations, tells us to derive them, and then moves on.  Homework, tests, and all of the actual teaching falls to the TA.

The class format he has made is very dumb. Since everyone gets nearly a 100% on all of the non-exam content, your grade is entirely decided based on exam performance, which is 20 multiple choice questions per exam. Each exam you make a notesheet and try to put every formula you can find on it, since the exams are just plugging in numbers to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concepts are often overcomplicated and only taught conceptually, which is of no help to those whose majors rely on the application of physics.

Physics 201 is definitely not an easy A but Yibin at least made it entertaining. His lectures were sometimes confusing, but he did live demos which often helped with understanding. His tests are all based on past exams and homework questions, and you get a whole paper for an exam notecard.

The professor is a very passionate lecturer, but he makes little sense when explaining complex topics and expects to know how to solve the problems already. The pace of the class is also weird with quizzes not covering anything he covers in lecture and tests being curved very poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pan's lectures were extremely fast and hard to follow. The first few topics were fine since the contents overlapped with what I learned from high school, but it started going downhill from there. My advice for future students would be to avoid him if possible, trust the negative reviews from this website, and be prepared to self study.

I don't think I learned a single thing from any of his lectures. He did not often explain things, even when answering questions. Seemed to just hate teaching. Not at all accommodating, never answered a single one of my emails, least clear grading criteria to date, exams were just terrible.

Lectures with Pan were nothing more than him calling concepts "trivial" even if they were new or complicated concepts. He assigned lengthy multistep questions for homework that was nothing like the lecture examples or the textbook. Going to his lectures is about as much use as throwing a cup of water into the ocean to raise the sea level.

I took the Pan/Sherafati combo for physics 201 and regret it. Pan is absolutely god-awful at teaching. Everything is too "easy" or too "simple" and does not deserve an explanation in his mind, even though this is an introductory course. The tests were full of errors, and the last two were ridiculously difficult. Avoid these professors if you can.

Took Physics 201. Very hard to reach, especially in online format. Wouldn't respond to key emails(on tests, submissions, etc) until 1.5-2 weeks later. And on those replies, all tried to gaslight the student on being in the wrong. Appears that he is also hard to reach through TAs, as multiple times it wasn't until friday our TA would get an answer.

Pan is not the best professor because he always modifies the slides to his liking before lectures and never uploads them early. As a result, when he goes too fast (which he often does), keeping up with his lecture is often hard.

Yibin Pan is an embarrassment to the Physics department and the university. He routinely berates his students for "stupid" questions and is not conducive to a productive learning environment. When taking his course, the one phrase you will learn to hear most is "it is trivial" and "this is easy," this class is anything but. Avoid him at all costs.

While the physics 202 team in general is a mess due to the often horrible TA's. The pan and shiu will take care of you and give solid lectures with some cool demos scattered throughout them. Course is still a mess and was a wretched introduction to the physics department.

Prof. Pan is a horrible teacher. Very nice guy and is willing to work with students to discuss and solve problems/concerns about exam grades, but his lecture slides are dense, ugly, and move way too fast. Reading the book is a necessity to gain all of the relevant information. Amazing that he's allowed to teach such a central course.

This man derives joy from torturing students. The class is curved competitively, with only the top 20% of the class being able to get an A. The lectures are entirely useless, since on top of hating students, Pan is entirely incompetent at teaching. The tests are riddled with mistakes -- the second midterm had an unsolvable problem.
Lectures are very boring. Does a bad job of teaching the material. First tests were easy but the third and final exams were unnecessarily difficult.

He does not appear to put thought into his lectures. The concepts are overly confusing. Worthless labs and worthless discussion sheets. This class exists to demotivate engineers with its stupidity which leads to difficulty
this guy has no clue how to teach. overly confusing lectures and relatively simple high school physics with impossible curves and tests

Lectures were hard to understand and not recorded, so you were screwed if you missed class. Concepts were not explained well and Pan would often contradict himself while lecturing. Inaccessible outside of class and unforgiving with homework and tests. I had to teach myself physics from the textbook

Although he is kind of confusing and hard to understand sometimes, overall he will answer questions and will try his best to make things clear. He also always has good energy and keeps lectures interesting to help you learn the difficult material.

The hardest class I've ever taken. The only time I learned anything was from the textbook, taking notes by myself, or from my TA in discussion. Lectures are confusing and most of the learning is on you. Worked super hard in this class and still worried I won't pass.

Professor Pan made a subject that I love incredibly boring. I stopped showing up to his lectures because he put in very little effort and the exams were based on the book anyway. For the final exam, he released a practice exam hidden within the files on canvas which had half the questions from the final and only told his favorite students.

He has really good lecture content and tells you some of the problems that will be on the exam in lecture. Weekly homework and quiz are not too difficult, and are a good grade boost. Exams are all multiple choice and fair. Overall, take him if you can.
Lazy professor with bad class setup

The semester started with another professor, and then Yibin took over the class about half way through and my understanding plummeted. In comparison he doesn't discuss the process of diagrams or demos and merely just tells you what is occurring. If you can avoid taking class with him, you will likely understand much more of the class.
Only two attempts on free response HW questions, which is questionable. Tests are graded on scantron. Constantly insists class is "Easy".

Not the worst professor but did not do well with online format. Tests curved individually rather than your overall grade being curved unlike most classes. He curved down on some exams (1 exam had a 98% cutoff for an A). Learned mostly from the textbook. Failed to respond to emails, would change exam formats arbitrarily. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maybe Yibin was a lot better before COVID. But he is definitely the worst-adapted professor to online learning that I've ever seen. Doesn't know how to respond to emails. All he does is assign online textbook readings and assignments through WebAssign. I learned 100% of the material for this class through the textbook, not him. Just a bad professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was completely self-taught from the book and the lectures pointless. He just read off slides and skipped every step saying its just basic algebra. Grade on canvas wasnt weighted so a 95% ended up destroying my gpa. Didnt help that most of the people in this class were cheating which screwed all of us who did not. Very poorly ran.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad explanations. Takes forever to reply to emails. Doesn't care and understand his students at all. I felt like he didn't put in a lot of effort into this class. Maybe it might be better in person but I doubt it. The grade shown on Canvas is not accurate, which made me think I was doing relatively well until a couple of weeks before the exam.

Class lacked any form of infrastructure and little to no support was offered to students. I went into this with little experience of physics and it was definitely very painful. Lectures were incredibly boring and lacked proper demos and homework took hours. Very hard to learn from. Maybe in-person it would've been better, but beware.

Do not take this professor if you want a good grade. The language barrier makes it difficult to understand what he is saying during lectures. His class is curved which shows he can't make good tests with most of the test problems being HW prb with numbers changed.I missed the final exam because of the hospital, and he didn't give me a make-up exam.

Dr. Pan was a very average professor at best. He never really did anything outstanding that made him more enjoyable as a professor, but he did okay at teaching the class. The class overall is notoriously difficult, but most of the exam questions are ripped straight from the homework. As long as you work and study hard, this class won't be too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this class to my worst enemy. He is awful at explaining what is going on and takes forever to get back to your emails. I know this is a mandatory class for a lot of people just try and not take it with him.

I can't imagine how UW-Madison can hire such professors who have no idea what they do and do not care how their students do. No motivation for physics and he has no clue how to explain. The worst physics professor in the department. He covers the lectures and puts up different questions on the exams. Not recommended with a little curve.

Grades all semester were unknown as the tests weren't weighted correctly in the grade book. I had this class and another final on the same day at the same exact time and Yibin Pan refused to allow me the alternate time after not responding to my original request sent a month before the final and well before his cut-off final exam conflict date.

I got a grade of A totally depending on my hardworking and smart brain! Reading textbook by myself is much more useful than listening to his lecture. He is a very rigid person and unwilling to answer some simple questions from students. He never replied email and his excuse was "I receive tons of emails everyday".

Online class for physics 201 with Yibin Pan has been awful. He has no clue what he is doing most of the time when it comes to technology. For exams, his approach to fair grading includes no partial credit. Scores are based purely on answer. If I could only say one thing about this professor it would be STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pan: *Spends barely any time on lecture slides and turned off chat so nobody could ask questions *Doesn't respond to his email quickly, if at all *Is generally not helpful to understanding course material *Labs are confusing, stressful, pointless *Exams are unfair, but curved This course was the worst academic experience I ever had.

As someone with no background in physics this "introductory course" is heavily reading based and lectures barely help you understand anything as they are rushed and lack thorough description of content, based on the fact that your already supposed to understand what you're being taught? Also the adjustment to online instruction is disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very difficult, and many of the exams follow that trend. He gives out weekly WebAssign homework, which is lengthy, and some questions may be on the exam, but be prepared for exams on content never seen in class or the textbook. His lectures go through some examples, but he just talks through the process. and doesn't explain concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Pan is a solid choice for Physics 202. Exams and homework focus entirely/mostly on the basic equations and concepts, so you don't have to worry too much about derivations. He is an entertaining lecturer, but all I got out of his lectures (that I didn't already get from the textbook) were some pointers on what would and wouldn't be on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Pan's course Physics 201 course is subpar. He's too lazy to put proper derivations on lectures and makes us look for it on our own time. He makes tons of caught and unnoticed mistakes during his lectures which makes them confusing and pointless. The exams are bad because they are exclusively on webassign so you basically get not partial credit.

Prof. Pan is not great. Exams have mistakes (which he makes) that waste test time for students, but he doesn't care. Exam difficulty and grading is another problem, to get an A you need a 95% (curved)??? This course is disorganized as hell, all the learning is from the textbook. Horribly executed online labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I believe this is Dr. Pan's first semester teaching 202, but other reviews apply. I've never seen such a lazy professor. Lecture is low-effort conceptual examples and he pulls test questions from the homework problems he didn't make. No attempt was made to adapt the in-person labs do something of value in an online setting.

Dr. Pan is an absolute joke of a professor. His lectures are terrible. He gives the minimal amount of examples and the ones that are given are so basic they are totally useless in preparing you for the exams. Get ready to learn on your own because his attitude and effort put into this class are abysmal.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is careless about the course in general and it is evident from his poor organization. The slides are all over the place and are very difficult to read. The exams are conceptually difficult which adds onto the fact that your exam grades are based off of the answer you got rather than your written work (which is much more important in physics).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I have taken. I do not know why other people said Yibin Pan is caring because he certainly is not. He is rude to students who ask questions and doesn't realize that 90% of the time a student is asking a questions is because he didn't explain clearly. Online tests are also extremely hard and poorly made.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His poor english and inability to properly explain concepts makes this already difficult class even worse. Probably his worst quality, he is very condescending to students who ask questions, which discourages participation in lecture.
Pan is a good professor, the class was in great logical. But i wish he could give us more practice exams before the midterm.

Do not take this professor. He can't speak English or teach any physics. The only word you hear is "calculation". Take another professor with whom you can learn it. He has a terrible attitude. UW-Madison shouldn't let such professors teach. I regret I paid Non-resident tuition for this horrible class. The quality of instruction is extremely poor.

Class is fairly difficult unless you have a strong math background. The tests were all multiple choice, although this does not mean they were easy. Some did not like his English, as he has an accent, but I found it easy to understand. Going to lectures is important as many of his examples gone over in lecture show up on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pan is amazing and very funny. You will learn most of the class in discussion so make sure you show up and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lectures- interesting and easy to follow. My only real complaint is that the tests were all multiple choice, so you cant get partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fun guy. I always enjoyed his lecture and Dennis! You can tell he tries his best to make physics fun and easy to understand. Having a good TA is really helpful and understanding the homework is key to doing well on the tests so do the homework and understand it! :)

He is NOT interested in student success. Not approachable AT ALL; will be rude and make you feel bad for asking questions and gets frustrated if you don't understand concepts he as already explained. Lectures are not cohesive and hard to follow. Please, please, please, if you are not a physics major avoid taking a class with Pan at all costs.

First of all you can't understand him half the time, even though his lectures don't make sense to begin with. He did not adjust to online classes well, and clearly is oblivious to what is going on outside of his lectures. Just pray you don't have a bad TA like mine who just hands us impossible worksheets every discussion and doesn't teach
Yibin is a great lecturer, sometimes to the point of geeking himself. Make sure to pay attention and understand what is going on conceptually, as the exams are strictly multiple choice.

Really fun and energetic professor. Tried his best to explain things and did so adequately. The multiple choice format on tests can be annoying because doing one thing wrong leads to an incorrect answer which is often a choice. Test questions are often like the homework so study carefully. Not a ton of work but concepts can be difficult.
Difficult to understand language at first

Exams are so much like the homework, so make sure you actually try on hw. Also, exams are a huge part of the grade so one bad exam grade can screw you over (I got 90, 40, 80, did great on hw and labs, but a BC) Labs are totally irrelevant. Lectures are easy to tune out so I started using Khan Academy, since they made everything easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's enthusiastic and fun to listen to, but his class overall did not give me a better understanding of physics, which is something I look for in a physics class. He was kind of all over the place. A good TA probably helps but mine was truly awful. The best way to study for exams is old homework problems. The book was pretty useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yibin's lectures were straightforward, energetic, and gave me everything I needed to know for the exams. Exams were multiple choice, but easy since he allows an entire notebook sheet for formulas on the midterms and three notebook sheets on the final.
All tests are multiple choice and only test you on how good you are at guessing between options. Came in with a great curiosity to learn physics but ended up wanting to leave the class half the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Don't skip a lecture or you'll miss his funny demos! Exam questions are pulled directly from homework and old exams, an easy A's as long as you study

Yibin's lectures contain everything you need for this class. He makes quite clear what is going to be on exams, which formulas you will and won't need, and how he expects things to be done. The only negative is that the exams are all multiple choice with no partial credit, but the questions are straight from the homework and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was extremely easy. The material isn't easy, but the exams are a joke and very straightforward. Yibin is fine at teaching, not the best though. He is very engaging, funny, caring. I would definitely take him again because of his easy exams. I barely attended 3 lectures throughout the whole semester. Lectures are fun (demos!) but useless.

The grades were pretty solid. Homework is worth the same as an exam grade which is nice. The labs were easy and I didn't use the super expensive textbook. I double blocked and did not make it to a single lecture. Just make sure you study for the exams, they're similar to the homework and the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hes the man for 201. If you understand the homework and do the practice exams youll be fine on exams.

Mr. Pan is the GOAT. I never had so much eneg in a class before. I skip nap class to come see Mr. Pan spin in circles to demonstrate momentum. Mr. Pan has some wack exams but if it aint broke don't fix it.

No one loves physics more than Yibin Pan--it's hard not to get excited about the subject when he's teaching it! The exams aren't too bad: 20 multiple choice questions, most of which are taken directly from the homework. You also get to use full-sized sheets of paper (front and back) for your formula sheets. Not too hard if you put in enough work.

Mr. Pan is honestly one of the best professors here. People who shame him on this site did not try in his class. His exams are straightforward if you actually understand the homework and practice exams. He gives you everything you need to succeed in his class. Just don't be lazy (5 credit class) and an A is very possible. Funny, caring, and a gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Yibin is honestly not a bad prof. He is hilarious when giving lectures and I would always look forward to them. It is important to go to lectures because if you pay close attention, he will literally tell you some of the questions that will be on the exams. For exams, you are allowed full sized sheets of paper for formulas. Not Bad.

Somehow this class made me worse at math and physics. Yibin would just throw equations at you without explaining them and you had to figure them out basically on your own. The tests were all 20 multiple choice questions with e) non of the above as an answer for each one. The only reason I passed this class was because of my TA.

Be prepared to teach yourself everything. He gives you all the equations you need but you need to understand how to manipulate ALL of them to solve hard problems. If anything, his class demonstrations are the most important aspect of lecture. Exams are hard and unforgiving. Beat the average classmate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He was decent at explaining the material, and was pretty engaging. His accent can take some getting used to, but you don't even notice it after a little while.

Yibin is the worst professor I have had here. His lectures are not well structured and you will likely be confused on the material if you don't prepare before lectures. I would recommend going to tutoring hours. Yibin's office hours are the LAST place you want to go! His exams are tricky and will become your worst nightmare bc no partial credit!

This class crams 16+ chapters into 14/15 weeks, which is why it is understandable that Pan might not go into a lot of depth during his lectures. Read the book, it will teach you what you need and Pan's lectures will compliment that. Pan is a great professor, very fair, and his lectures and demonstrations are fun to watch.
Professor Pan loves physics, and is an average professor. His tests are all multiple choice, so there is no partial credit.

I found Yibin easy to understand and his lectures engaging. They aren't mandatory, since he posts his slides online. The downfall is the tests, which are 20 multiple choice questions with no partial credit. The are heavily based on his homework and practice exam. Labs are a joke. He does not budge on grades.

Yibin Pan is a lovable old man who loves physics and he presents his material well, lecture material is always posted online, lets you use plenty of note sheets on exams, and if you have a good TA, labs aren't too bad. The downside of this class is that all exams are 20 multiple choice questions that are super hard with no chance of partial credit
He's really hard to understand to the point where I didn't even go to lectures. Honestly just read the lecture slides and you'll get the same thing out as attending lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Awful class. The lectures are not thorough enough as compared to what is on the exams. Not a class where I learned physics just learned how to take timed mcq by memorizing the homework(which I think are super unfair because how can you grade calculations without giving partial credit?) You will do bad if you are not good at physics coming into this

I had low expectations for this course but this course was far worse than I expected. Yibin is hard to understand and hard to follow. He is a nice guy but he is not good at explaining the material. I would suggest taking this course with someone else if possible. Exams are only 20 multiple choice questions and they are hard to finish in time.

Pretty easy class unless you struggle with timed MC exams. Yibin makes lectures entertaining, but, for those who don't have much physics experience, the information doesn't come across the best.  This class was pretty much a repeat of AP physics but instead of energy we have energe.

Yibin is adorable. I did not take physics in high school, but I somehow survived this class. Labs are useless and frustrating. Test questions are straight from the homework and practice tests. Memorize how to do those problems and make a good formula sheet for the tests and you'll be fine.

Crazy thick accent. Not in a way that's too hard to understand. He's an old enthusiastic man (this and his accent make him really funny) and you can't help but like him, even if he's not a fantastic lecturer. Goes thru a lot of examples in lecture, which I personally find valuable. Tests are multiple choice and you can have a note sheet

He wasn't a bad professor, I met with him outside of class a few times for some concerns I had. The major knock is the tests in this class. They aren't written all that well so it is a huge swing from what is online. The practice exams do not follow what he gives out. I would recommend finding someone who has had him before and using their exams
we only have multiple choice for all exams. not a bad lecturer but need self study.
He is good at explaining knowledge. But his exams are only 20 multiply choices. Take his class if possible.

Overall, his tests are very straight forward. They are basically modified homework problems. Although the tests aren't bad, his lectures are excruciating because he has trouble speaking English, so it is difficult to learn much from lecture. I learned everything in that class from my TA in discussion.

Really the only reason I went to his lectures were to see his hilarious antics. I have literally cried laughing from some of his demos in lectures. I don't think he's as bad as these other reviews make him out to be really, if you can grip the homework material then you'll do fine on the exams.

Yibin is hands down the worst professor I've ever had. He teaches the course like you already know the stuff, his lectures are unclear and he doesn't have office hours. several of my friends( who are physics students) have trouble completing the practice problems for the exams. Tests are multiple choice, no partial credit allowed. DO NOT TAKE.
Another professor that is hard to understand.  Tests aren't too bad, but he does a terrible job lecturing.
He wasn't a good teacher and the exams were a poor format

Yibin basically puts up a powerpoint and talks right from the slides. He teaches topics briefly and vaguely. Hard to understand sometimes. I'd say probably less than 50% of my class actually attends his lectures. You can skip and just read his slides. Tests are straight off of homework and practices so memorize those and they aren't too bad.

I loved AP Physics and got a 3 on AP test. This class was extremely difficult. Yibin is not a good lecturer and his exams are all multiple choice for math questions, which I HATE!! No partial credit given. He always includes on tests an answer (E) non of the above are within 5% of the correct answer. Sometimes this is the correct answer. Ridiculous

Prof. Pan tries his best to deliver the course material to you but he fails most of the time because he expects you to "preview" before the lecture. Tests are from homework and previous exams. However, they have a lot of tricky questions  screwing you over. I feel like the purpose of the tests is to challenge the students rather than teaching
The only reason to go to class is to watch an old chinese dude spinning around on a wheel. Otherwise just get an extra sleep and skip lecture.

Lectures are a joke, you just go in and laugh at him getting confused with himself and doing his funny demos The exams are filled with trick questions that make you feel stupid I taught myself the whole course

Overall average professor. Passionate about the subject and has fun teaching. Claims "you must preview" the text to be successful. Lectures help out a decent amount, but he doesn't teach subjects that thoroughly. Tests are almost exactly like the homework, so review those beforehand. Labs are pointless and didn't help at all.

Professor Pan makes a challenging subject interesting. The tests are all multiple choice and are almost always altered homework problems with a few extra ones he adds in. Reading the textbook isn't a must but it does help. Homework is all online and just beware for the double assignments that get assigned after tests.
Super easy, exams are straight from homework, would take Professor Pan again if I had a chance.

Anybody who thinks Professor Pan is not fit to teach is clearly wrong.  Yibin is an amazing professor who has crystal clear lectures and performs hilarious demos and jokes, all accentuated by his thick Chinese accent.  I would totally take him again!  Midterms are pretty much just slightly altered homework and practice test problems.  In short-easy

His accent is deep, but his lectures are still worth going too. He puts his slides online too. If you want to do well, just do the homework, questions on lectures slides, and discussion worksheet problems over and over again because his exams are literally just those type of problems with different numbers. Also Textbook is great secondary source

I stopped going to lecture after realizing it was no help to me. I just read the textbook and his powerpoint slides afterwards, then attend the mandatory discussion. I've received average scores for midterms. Tests are very much like the homework.

The key to this class is understanding how to do the homework. Many problems on tests are almost identical to homework. Also many of his conceptual questions on tests he goes over in class. He is fairly easy to understand and does hilarious demos.

Yibin really tries to present the material well.  However, I found the lectures quite dull.  I just read the textbook, reviewed the lecture slides, and went to discussion and I feel like I grasped the material just fine.

He was kind of adorable, but that is where the good qualities end. I didn't learn in lecture- my TA told us everything we needed to know. She saved me in this class. The first half is similar to high school physics- but it gets a lot harder. He is not flexible AT ALL with conflicts. Exams are just like homework, and aren't totally awful.
I found Professor Pan extremely difficult to understand. Exams are conceptual multiple-choice for the most part and no partial credit.

Yibin cares about the subject; however, he is not a very good lecturer. Often he flies through material and doesn't go into enough depth. TA's will make or break your grade. If I hadn't taken physics in high school, this course would have been extremely difficult.

I think Professor Pan is really serious about his lecture. He gives us all the details for exams and he really does a good job at preparing us for the exam. Except for his accent he is really a good professor.

He is overall a good professor. He gives a decent curve, he knows the material, and explains it well enough in lecture. I pretty much never had to read the book and still did well. He has an accent but he is understandable. He's eccentric and clumsy, so demos are funny. If you study homework and practice exams, you'll be fine.

Memorize the homework questions and you'll be able to slip by with little/no effort. Going to class was more funny than helpful. Yibin has a heavy accent, is poor at explaining, and is very unorganized. Avoid unless you never plan to use physics.

Not a good professor.  I would go to class only because he would hint at what would be on the exam.  I took notes in discussion and was lucky to have an exceptional TA.  He was rude in emails and tests were all multiple choice with trick questions.  I relied heavily on the book and managed an AB in the class.
Really thick accent. Not a great teacher. Knows his stuff but cannot translate it to the student. Exams are difficult and the homework is not very relevant. Don't take Pan if you can.

I like this professor, although he does like to focus on the ideas behind physics and not pure problem solving, if you put in a little bit of effort the class is not too difficult and is run very clearly and well.
Exam problems come straight from the online homework and are pretty easy.  Overall not too hard of a class, but heavily exam based grading so make sure you study hard for all of them.
His lectures are unclear, very hard to pay attention.

The class was easy enough to understand with some work but pan made it much harder than it needed to be. He uses a lot of trick questions on tests and questions that could be an answer, none, or all of the above. Learning the professor early in the class will help.

This is not a easy class. If you want to get an A, you must study hard and read the textbook at least once before exams. I admit his exam is hard, covering lots of conceptual problems and calculation, but that's what you need to know to master physics and use it as a tool in other subjects. He's a cute professor!

Not a fan of Pan. Awful exams - 100% multiple choice. He is annoying, lazy, and his lectures are nearly useless. Look at the formulas in his online slides & go to discussion to get your information. He was rude during office hours and breathed disgustingly into the mic throughout every lecture. Labs - easy but a waste of life and I love physics.
Never studied once for this class and got an A. Very easy grader and not a bad teacher. Does interesting demos in most classes and is a pretty entertaining guy

From Pan: In particular, I will not consider  arguments such as: --- "For some/any reasons I **need** a particular grade level." --- "The multiple-choice type exams are not fair by nature." --- "I  have had too many other obligations." ---  "My grade did not reflect my efforts."
He was a great physics professor, really enjoyed his lectures and demos.

If you took physics in high school this class seems like a rehash for a lot of the time. There are some higher level topics that are covered in the book probably better than yibin covers in lecture. Honestly I went to maybe 5 lectures all year and did great. His tests can be difficult but the class is curved so overall he's not bad, not amazing.

The very thick accent made me pay attention more and made class fun. The exams are not hard at all if you do the homework, take the old midterms and finals and attend most of the lectures. This class rocked my socks.

Overall, I thought he was pretty average. He accent does make lectures amusing, but I found lecture content to be a bit incomplete. Gaps were usually filled in by the homework. He emphasizes conceptual understanding of material. Tests were mild, but I didn't like the multiple choice. I really like that he gets so excited about teaching physics.

Pan has a very thick Chinese accent but that is what makes the class so much more fun. He is extremely enthusiastic about physics and is always smiling when he lectures. Tests were easy but that also meant that the curve was a bit tough. Overall a wonderful teacher.
Great professor who explain everything clear.
He's really excited about what he's teaching. Exams and HW were easy, and I found the lectures to be easy to get through. Great professor.
Tests are all multiple choice which is good and bad. Tests a lot of conceptual stuff. Homework is alright. Overall just a pretty average experience.

Awesome professor! Very knowledgeable and helpful. Extremely excited about physics. Definitely knows exactly what he is talking about and loves to discuss it. The class is built on understanding physics, not math. Plug and chug will not work.
He always explains each concept clearly. The homework and exams are easy if you go to his lecture (all questions on the exam will be included) and read the textbook. Interesting Demo!

Yibin Pan is pretty nice professor, exams aren't that bad but yeah you do have to study because they are multiple choices. Homework and Lab were a joke. He got an accent but that clearly isn't that bad. The best part is you don't have to be a Calculus freak to do his problems but only if you know the Physics concepts then you are fine.

overall pretty good teacher. like other said, he's very excited about physics. he has accent but still easy to understand. i dont love the class but dont hate it. love when he says "correct" because it sounds like "crap"

Had him along with Prof. Tao Han for 202. He's gets really excited about physics. Homework is easy enough and exams aren't too bad either. Lab is a waste of time since nothing ever works, but they don't care about formal lab reports so that's not too hard. Never read the textbook.

Labs are a big waste of time because a lot of the equipment doesn't work. Hw is pretty easy if you read the chapter before hand. Lectures are also posted online, the demos in lecture are pretty interesting. If you really don't understand something def go talk to the professor.

I had this guy along with another prof as part of phys 103 and frankly he's the better of the two. His demos are hilarious (cause he's the test subject) look forward to the final demo (he almost killed himself demonstrating inertia made it worth it coming to lecture). Sometimes gets caught up in his demos, with funny results.

Yibin: He makes his demos look silly by making himself the object, but entertaining though. The worst thing about his class is just the online homework, which sometimes are very difficult and you cant find the answer anywhere but go to the TA. Some exam questions r pretty confusing, though you should be able to get an A if you work hard.

Kind of a big jerk, arrogant and completely unhelpful outside of lecture. Decent lecturer but not very good english and hard to understand. Maybe I was an outlier but he would straight up ignore my emails to him, when they were about academic conflicts, maybe he thinks that this pointless INTRO class is the most important thing in the world.

He really cared how the class was doing and is really passionate about the stuff.  Accent can take a bit of getting used to but it is not that bad.  His tests are easy in comparison to other physics teachers.

Great guy, makes class fun, little tricky to understand occasionally, but really not so bad once you get used to him. He only taught for the first half of the semester and I was sad to see him go. Recommended.

He knew his stuff, if you can understand him. Sometimes a little entertaining, although you are more of laughing at him than with him. Basically he cares about the subject and tries, but just doesn't connect well to the students.

He is a pretty decent professor. Hard to understand at times, he talks really fast when he really gets into the material, but honestly its understandable and he actually does a good job teaching the material if you give him a chance. Exams are pretty easy as well...he allows a full sheet of paper, double sided for formulas
Decent professor. A little tough to understand right away but it gets better. Exams are fairly easy because you get note sheets and he does a good job of letting you know what will be tested.
Language=bad.  Lecture=bad.  I didn't learn anything from him, thank god for my TA and semi-doable exams.

Great professor!Even though it does take for a whlie to get accustomed to his accent and he occasionally tends to repeat himself too many times, his lecture is very easy to understand, and he really cares for his student!

These people are a bunch of crybabies.  I don't know how you could possible rate Professor Pan low.  Every time he teaches he focuses on making the material as easy to understand as possible. His tests were fair and he prepares his students with very helpful review sessions.  He also has some kickass quotes.  Best physics prof period.

He's difficult to understand in lecture and liked to show the complex proofs behind the equations but is very enthusiastic. Tests are hard and you need to rely the textbook and TAs to do well. However, the difficulty of the midterms usually results in a generous curve. Be prepare to do alot of work outside of class in order to get a decent grade.

I also do not understand all the complaints. I think he was pretty entertaining, way to energetic about physics but funny. His powerpoint slides are very organized and his lectures are incredibly easy to follow. The only thing is he has a thick accent but it is understandable. His tests/curves are pretty easy (and I HATE PHYSICS!!)
Exams weren't too hard since he allowed notesheets, but his lectures were horrible.
I really don't know why people complain about him, probably the hardest-working professor I've had.  Tests are pretty fair and he follows the book very closely.
Do not take the class with this guy. U will not be able to understand a thing he says. U will have to teach yourself everything. Worst professor I have ever taken
I studied about 15 hours a week, and still got a C. I relied mostly on my T.A. to explain everything.
Pretty much the worst prof ive had.  Has a strong accent and when the class average on the first exam was a 51%, his response was "why you no study?  why you no understand?"
He IS as bad as people say. Ridiculous amounts of homework and exams suck!
Lets just say when the class average on the second exam was a 51, his response was "i no understand why you no understand.  do you no study?"

exams are theoretical MC and 100% algebra, no actual numbers. talks quickly w/ thick accent, alternates between board and PPT slides, i'm unable to copy and understand at the same time. later in the lecture he modifies previous eqns on blackboard and you get to figure out what applies at that moment. would not recommend--i stopped going to lecture.
Not as bad as people say. Read the book, come prepared to lecture, do your homework, and the tests are fair. If you're having trouble with this class, good luck in med school.

I don't think hes as bad as everyone says. Sure I hate the theoretical & symbolic stuff as much as everyone else, but I thought overall he was an ok prof. final exam was fair as was the curve. Lectures actually pretty helpful. easier to understand after a while. Not a bad prof. Not great but not bad. cheat sheets VERY nice. homework a bit excessive

Take another professor.  If you can't, you can do well with Yibin by reading the book and making awesome cheat sheets.  He lets you use an entire page front/back for each exam, and 4 for the final.  Write down the book's equations and know how to do algebra and you will be fine for the most part.  Multiple choice "theory" questions suck.
This guy blows, he doesn't know how to teach, exams were a joke, don't take this class or this professor!

Just plain horrible. This class is screwing my pre-med GPA. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! His tests are ridiculous multiple choice "theory" questions and problem without numbers. Honestly, who has physics tests without solving problems with numerical values.               P.S. His English stinks
Horrible. Covers a chapter per lecture.. even the T.A.'s say the tests are rediculous, and his accent makes it hard to follow lecture. Take someone else.

He speaks English with a VERY STRONG accent, so if you don't concentrate really hard on what he's saying, it'll pass by like he was speaking Mandarin.  He seems like a nice guy though, has good manners unlike most professors.
While I thought the class was easy enough, I had no idea what the heck he was ever talking about.  I either skipped lecture or slept through it.  He has a thick accent and talks very fast.

You better read your book, cuz whatever he says that you can understand won't help you much.  Likes to yell into his microphone.  Goes nuts on the chalkboard as if he were beating it to death.  Take someone else if you can.

DON"T choose this prof. For one, your final grade is not shown on canvas until it shows up on your transcript. Your participation grade is heavily based on if the professor likes you, so if you want an A, go to his office hours. I was not aware of this since it was not mentioned in the syllabus, and it was the one factor that dropped me to an AB.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kern was okay. This was a guest lecturer class though so he really didn't actually lecture much. The format was okay, but during this session he was unable to any of the lecturers in person, understandable but sad. When he did lecture he seemed knowledgeable. He also really loves to play devils advocate when people participate in class.

I would rather be tied to the back of the 80 and dragged across campus than attend this lecture taught by a white man who doesn't understand privilege. craziest superiority complex. says the field would improve if all the text was written by him. yeah and maybe if I taught this class, everyone's will to attend this god awful class would improve.

There is an absurd amount of required reading for this class. Upwards of 600 pages in a week at times. But overall an interesting experience and an easy class. The professor himself is kind of an oddball.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: do not enroll this course
Worst
is not an easy A, the class is bland and boring.
Don't take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Asian310 was a super easy but brain dead class (to me). Adam made is really easy to complete the quizzes/discussions without having to attend the classes (tho it was recommended you do). Solid choice of a professor who was not too hard. There was 1 opportunity for extra credit, but it was only for 1%. Take him if you can, but be ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at UW. This class was the single easiest class in my career, and probably at the school. No homework, only 4 quizes. All MC and True/False. Take this class.

Such a chill and knowledgeable dude. This class was my easiest course this semester and it was just something to look forward to. Do note though- its not really a literature course, its Japanese pop culture in case you were looking for something reading heavy.
Adam is one of my favorite professors. He's clearly passionate about Japanese studies.

While there's a decent amount of reading and effort in reading theory and translation, Adam is super helpful and lenient. He's so completely mastered the theory it's scary sometimes! He's funny, easy to listen to, and always thinking about you! I've taken 3 classes with Adam, some easier and some harder, but he's been great every time.

Extremely easy class. 4 online open internet and book quizzes, the lowest of which is dropped. That makes up 60% of your grade and attendance is 40%. It's all manga, but there is just way too much reading. I read one of them the entire course and still aced the quizzes. Helps to take this class w friends. Chill professor but he acts weird sometimes

It's always amazing to watch people be so knowledgeable in something that fascinates them, and that's how the lectures by Adam are. If the material is bland, the sense of humor of Adam overshadows it - make sure you do the readings before writing any papers though.

Kern is a professor that is extremely captivating but also pretty dang annoying (in a good way). I was never bored in his comic class. He had intriguing thoughts about the comics, and the comics he chose were extremely interesting. Class grade is based off of 4 quizzes, attendance, and participation. Show up to class, read, and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kern is an interesting guy with interesting perspectives on everything. Took his classes three times because I was intrigued by his character. I enjoy hearing his take on history, he makes it quite interesting. He will remember you and your writing--take that into account if you want to skip. If you are one who won't argue with the Prof, take him.

This class is about comics, and it's the first year Adam taught it, and I thought it was great! He's such a nice guy and super approachable. He presents thought provoking arguments and is really passionate. The class is graded off of 4 online quizzes (lowest dropped), attendance, and participation. If you show up it, it's super easy to do well!

He is very passionate about Japanese culture and knows what he is talking about. He is quirky, funny, intellectually driven but a little cocky in terms of personality. A great person to get know if you want to pursue East Asian Studies. Do the readings for the lectures because there will be discussion. Interesting topics covered about JPOP culture.

A spectacular and energetic class. Very willing to offer help and is genuinely interested in his students and fostering critical thinking (including opinions contrary to his own). Discussions are thoughtful and interesting for the class size. Difficult to get an A, but unless you're all about maintaining a high GPA, the class is more than worth it.

Kern's Haiku class is wonderful! He is super knowledgeable and cares abuot what he's teaching. Fair amount of reading but it's mostly short poems so it's interesting. No exams but a few essays. Class is fairly easy if you show up, read and take notes. Kern gives high energy, interesting lectures.

Great teacher!  Cares a lot about the course and his students.  The tests can be tricky but he is fair.  Hard to get an A, but also hard to fail.  If you do the readings and show up to class you will do fine.  That shouldn't be too hard to do since he is a captivating speaker and most the readings are very interesting.

Fantastic teacher. Very knowledgeable about everything he teaches. Tests are tough. You really need to keep up with the readings to do well. But once you get the hang of his brand of critical thinking, things will start making more sense. Highly recommend taking Manga class with him. You'll never read manga the same way again!
He's very passionate about what he is teaching. quizzes can be kinda tricky due to his very articulate writing style. Overall though he emphasizes having fun.

Treves turns what is an easy class content-wise into chinese water torture. Your grade relies solely on 3 exams and 3 study guides, which are all harshly graded and he provides zero constructive feedback. To make things worse, he raised the cutoff for a A from 90% to 94% AFTER the last exam. Unless you are a masochist, avoid Treves at all costs.

All reviews from fall 25 are accurate. His study guides are "correct the AI" but then he gets heated and accuses us of using AI. Who is using AI to correct AI?! Study guides must be done EXACTLY how his answer key is or you get no points. The exams carried my grade as they are online, 2 attempts, open book. I would avoid this class and professor.

He changed grade cutoffs on the last day, using extra credit as an excuse. He has an extreme focus on AI detection that penalizes honest work. Grading is harsh and subjective. Lacks transparency. Expect the goalposts to move constantly.
Looks like he is a Researcher more than a Teacher. Doesnt know how to deal with students. Expect anything mysteriously lowering your grade if you got a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, the most self-absorbed and unprofessional instructor I've ever had. Treves cannot accept the fact that people can do well in his joke of a class with minimal effort so he goes on baseless AI witch hunts and randomly curves the grade required to get an A from 90 (as listed) to 94. Shows a complete lack of respect for his students. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Randomly decided to change the grade curve on the last day from a 90 for an A to a 94.

Raised the A threshold from a 90 to a 94 after the final. Lectures were uninspiring. The grading scheme was almost completely removed from your knowledge of the course. Everything everyone else has said from this semester is true. Worst professor I've ever had. I had an interest in ecology, this class killed that
sad excuse of a professor and made his ta grade everything. cares way too much about using ai to even help with the class and flipped out and changed the A requirements from a 90 to a 94.

One of the worst professors I've had. Grading is extremely harsh and unfair. study guides are the worst, if answers aren't worded exactly to his liking, you lose a ton of points. One study guide had a mean of 50% . Don't take any course with him if you want fairness.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had. Grading is extremely harsh and unfair, with an A requiring more (4) points than stated in the syllabus. Exams are overly difficult and poorly worded, so you can understand the material and still lose points. The content is interesting, but unfair grading ruins the class. It feels intentional and discouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor has an obsession with AI. Only has assignments based on hard graded 'study guides' that are done either by yourself or correcting AI, but holy if you actually use AI on an assignment or even google he WILL hunt you down and give you a 0, but if you come forward saying you used AI(or google) you can maybe get a 50% (if you're lucky).

Lectures are a snooze fest and mandatory, literally half asleep for an hour and a half. Easy exams but seemed to try and make the course way harder nearing the final exam. Study guide assignments are ridiculous, you will either get a horrible grade or get accused of using AI and have to take it up with the dean. Terrible experience.

Weirdly difficult compared to actual course content. Baselessly accused various students of AI on the study guide. Very harsh grader on study guides. Exam are online and multiple choice with two attempts. Very self important. Lectures are recorded, but attendance is taken for the chance at a grade bump at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor does not know how to lecture and goes off on random rants about wolfs, dogs, politics, and himself. Obsessed with the idea that everyone is using AI on his assignments. He throws out baseless accusations and gives you the option of receiving a zero on the assignment or he will report you to the dean with little to no proof. Terrible.

Class guidelines make no sense. Has such a sense of self importance (which is expected from professors but he takes it to a new level).
Feel like his lectures are a democratic rally. Uses canvas to tell people how to vote, tell people about lectures.

Very weird fixation on AI. Straight up witch hunt like others have mentioned.

Halfway through the semester, he baselessly accused 30 (of 250) students of using AI and refused to grade their papers, then declared he would be reviewing every past assignment in what feels like a witch hunt. If his lectures were compelling or he showed any interest in students, I could sympathize with this, but he is aloof, boring, and immature.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolute stickler over usage of ai and cares too much for a introductory course that people take jus tto satisfy their science credit. Freaks out over usage of ai on a study guide and rambles on about wolves and dogs in lecture

Exams were very easy but the multiple choice questions were always worded very poorly. The toughest part about this class was the study guides. If not worded to his liking or the perfect answer is not given, get ready to either lose a gazillion points or get accused of using AI. Also, his lectures are NyQuil as they go on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
