reviews.comment: The assignment instructions are often unclear. Even when you reach out for clarification, the response is typically just "re-read the instructions." It seems like multiple students have experienced the same confusion, but rather than using the feedback to improve the course materials, the response is usually to figure it out on your own.

Treves is someone who you can tell is very knowledgeable and passionate about environmental studies, which shines through in his lectures. The course isnt very lenient when it comes to misses/late work but that expectation is made very clear in the start so you cant really complain about that. He also has a cute dog which he brought to class so, W
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The assignments are weirdly laid out. Some are formatted as discussion posts but no actual post is required. Very long winded and confusing descriptions of assignments. No traditional numerical rubrics, literally just descriptions. Most assignment descriptions bounced all over the place and had no clear, transitional formatting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can tell he is super passionate about his subject, so lectures sometimes devolve into tangents. Tests all had two attempts plus an extra credit assignment so its pretty easy to do well. Sometimes he would assign really long videos which were annoying to find time for.

Took his class in spring '23 and the TA runs the whole class. Cannot comprehend an email to save his life. If you have questions set aside 2 hours because he will not be able to answer them without 5 threads and involving the TA anyway. Uses Docs and not canvas so who knows when grades get in. Avoid this professor.

Professor Treves is very passionate about his research, and assigns interesting news articles as readings. However, his test questions are very vague and hard to interpret, often hinging on specific wording. There's no homework, but the class is surprisingly difficuly (ENV260)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Treves is just alright, but definitely knowledgable. Lots of reading, and a lot of the class is online (not my favorite). The exams are hard but you get to take it twice. I did well by writing down most of the words Treves said in lecture. Definitely a little harder than it should have been but manageable. The main words that comes to mind: "meh"

Treves is passionate about his work, and that comes across during his lectures. However, lectures are extremely disorganized, and exam questions are intentionally confusing. Study guides are graded harshly. There is extra credit, but it is extremely difficult to complete. This class was unnecessarily complicated. Avoid it if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was honestly a little worried about the class when I saw Dr. Treves's rating on this site. I was pleasantly surprised when I came to class and he was extremely passionate, inspirational, knowledgeable, caring, and super flexible with his students. He loves when you ask questions! Overall this class is relatively easy and quite interesting.

He does have a passion for the subject, but his teaching style is very disorganized. Learning goals don't line up well with the test, and the textbook lacks clarity. However, the lectures tend to be fun and engaging, and the material is interesting. Many classes are held online. Few study materials are provided, mostly students are "on their own."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT take 413 with Dr. Treves. While he is very knowledgable, he does not know how to properly set up a course and give students information in a way that supports learning. His grading is extremely picky for a class where he does not actively teach. The content was quite interesting but the way the course is structured is very poor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Treves is very knowledgeable, but this course is truly awful. Almost all content is boring readings, and many are on Prof. Treves' own research. It's pretty clear he doesn't care about instructing and would rather focus on his own research. The course is organized well, but be prepared to do nothing but read, and not learn much because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Treves is smart but the class is highly unorganized and fairly boring. Content is interesting but exhausting--hard to comprehend without a legal background. He's incredibly condescending if you ask questions. His exams are poorly worded and grading criteria for assignments is pretty unclear. Very dense readings and very few lectures. Frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Treves is an okay professor. 413 is not that well organized and there is a lot of content to sift through for open-book exams + lots of readings but it is doable if you put effort into it. He is pretty understanding of emergencies if you tell him ahead of time. I do think the grading is a little harsh on exams though (lose more than 45 pts = B).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I normally don't rate professors this early in the semester, but it had to be done. The online course is scrambled and confusing. Grades mostly come from exams, but you can only lose 30 total points throughout the semester for an A. He is condescending in email and talks down to students. Not accommodating. Insurmountable amounts of reading. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was interesting material, but this is not an engaging professor. He talks slowly and has roundabout ways of saying what he means. This is true on homework and exams. As a senior, I could tell this was a class meant for freshmen. He lays out instructions on performing basic scholarly tasks. I attended lecture, didn't study for exams and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Treves is really passionate about his research and course, but it is sometimes hard to follow. His lectures do not relate at all the exams, but they are interesting. If you are interested in this subject I would reccomend going to class and his office hours, but if you are just taking for a credit attendence is not even mandatory.

Treves is an extremely passionate and kind person, and the exams are relatively easy (online, 2 attempts). However, for a 3-credit class, he assigns excessive amounts of homework. A majority of assigned material is his own research, so broad spectrums of subjects and voices are not often covered. Overall, the class is easy but avoidable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've had Prof Treves twice now, for ENVST 260 and 413. He's knowledgeable, passionate, and intelligent, and he's respected for good reason. However, his courses rely a LOT on his own research, and a lot of the readings and info from 260 were used again in 413, despite these not being sequence classes. Take 413 for an easy 3 Natural Sci credits!

Treves is SMART, but his research dominates the class. This is an excellent course if you're an ecology nerd or into systems. Overall 4/5 because it is so test-heavy. The tests are very difficult. Bring your critical thinking skills. However, you get 2 tries.

I would 10x rather have a passionate and informed professor than an easy class.

Adrian's lectures are very interesting because he is extremely passionate about the subject. The exams weren't difficult (they're online, open-note, and you get 2 tries). The study guides were more challenging but those are honestly dependent on your TA. Overall, if you show up and take notes you will do well.

The class grade is entirely dependent exams. There are opportunities to speak with the TA or Treves, but these opportunities are not helpful because exam questions are so poorly worded. Treves looks for very specific answers to general questions. These topics are often are only briefly touched upon during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was not too bad, but the exams and study guides are the only part of your grade so you will want to do well on them. The study guides are graded very harshly, with one of the averages being 19/30 this semester. You get one drop though. Treves is very, very passionate and very knowledgeable about his subject, and is more old-school. E
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. The lectures have no relation to each other. Tests are ridiculously hard, with questions that make no sense. reviews.comment: Introductory Ecology was the easiest class I took this semester. The only thing that worried me was the exams are worth 75% of your grade but there are only three of them and no final.
Not a good professor at all.
Adrian is a horrendous professor! Not only will he completely ignore you and treat you like a lowly creature, he'll do this while teaching you nothing. DON'T TAKE HIS COURSES!

Adrian's lectures are scrambled and not good at all. He jumps around from topic to topic. Not a well organized course or lecture whatsoever

reviews.comment: The class content is very easy, at least it should be. You can still completely understand the content and do just average. Not a smooth lecture whatsoever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Biggest regret was taking his class, he creates ridiculous tests and grades unfairly. Found a way to turn the class into basically a course about his own research

reviews.comment: Super nice, easy to follow lectures and accessible for more explaining if you do not understand the material. Exams are reading heavy but not difficult if you know the terms he highlights. Has 4 quizzes given during random lectures but drops the lowest score at the end. Slight curve at the end (stated by TAs) but he does not state this.

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading for this class, however, the text book and readings are provided online so you don't have to pay for the text book. reviews.comment: Adrian is the best

Most of your grade is determined by 3 tests that use unnecessary, complex vocabulary that makes it hard to determine what the question is asking. Overall the class is very disorganized and poorly taught by him.

reviews.comment: A very time consuming course. Never thought it would be hard like that.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE FOR BIO CREDITS. IT IS NOT AN EASY COURSE AS YOU THOUGHT. AVOID AT ALL COST.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Treves is a good guy, this class is extremely difficult. There is a "study" guide before each of the 3 tests, and the lowest score is dropped. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not a science major? DON'T take this class. I thought it would be an easy science credit & the reviews seemed nice, but the class is awfully hard. Only 3 tests throughout the semester and that's the majority of your grade. Too many readings and tests are worded horribly- very tricky to do well. Avoid taking this at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Adrian was awesome. Before every test, he provided a very thorough study guide that was very similar to the format of the test. He also had office hours and answered any questions students had to ask. There will be a lot of reading but if you attend lecture and skim/ read the readings you'll get by with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is awesome. His study guide is super helpful for his exams. "There is a curve depending on improvement so if you improve by 10% of your score from one exam to another, you might have a possibility of being pushed up a letter grade. If you do that twice, you are guaranteed the bump up a letter grade" quoted from his email.

Adrian is a super nice person and a great professor! I learned a lot in his class, he cares a lot about his students. His lectures can be confusing and there is a lot of reading, but it is important that you do read and go to class. I'm very happy that I took his class and I can't wait to take his next one!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Treves does a nice job of trying to make the class material interesting and to make help available to students (not that you should need a tremendous amount of help). If you just do the study guides and study the lecture powerpoints before tests, this class should be an extremely easy A. Overall awesome way to get bio credit.

There are three midterm exams throughout the semester, five study guide assignments, and no final. The exams mostly cover lectures (80-90%) and only cover readings a little bit. They can be a bit tricky but you should be fine if you go to lecture. Dr. Treves is helpful in office hours and seems to really care about his students.

Lectures are essential to passing this course. Show up and take notes about the slides and that is the most difficult thing you will have to do all semester. There are few assignments and everything is relative to the exams.

A lot of the material was clear cut out in lectures, but for an introductory class, the tests strayed from course work. You must absolutely know the topics through and through, but if you don't, he is there to help and my TA was amazing. If you go to office hours, you should be about to get an A

I really enjoyed this class. The topics and books are interesting (although some of the assigned articles/studies could be a bit dense). Professor Treves is really passionate about what he's talking about and seems like a really approachable person. I would definitely take another class taught by him.

Class decently interesting. Textbook surprisingly interesting. 3 [M.C.] midterms, 2 [extremely easy] homework assignments, no final. Course is not very well organized and seems to skip from topic to topic, but if you know all the study guide terms you should do okay on the exams. Professor is very passionate about his topic, and super friendly.

Treves is very concise in his lectures. He maintains a very professional atmosphere which is fairly intimidating. His tests are difficult, the answers are very closely related and its hard to differentiate.

Treves is a great professor and really wants to inspire his students. He was very accessible and the class doesn't have too many tests or assignments. The class may be a bit disorganized but you still learn a lot. A great way to get science credit!

The class as a whole is very disorganized, skips topics frequently and nothing feels coherent. Good lecturer but quite boring; we watch a lot of audiovisual stuff in class. Lots of readings but the exams don't test you on understanding of core concepts but instead stress on  random details and aren't very well written. Learned a lot about ecology.

The class structure made it extremely difficult to earn a good grade. While the professor was nice, Top hat was graded on correctness in lecture, rubrics were overly strict, discussion was harshly graded on participation, and a few exams determined virtually your entire grade. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly one of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. A concept that should be relatively straight forward and obvious is made to be immensely difficult. Grading never matches what is said by professor or rubric and they find any way to take points off. Lectures are unorganized and mind-numbing. Needs serious restructuring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lecture content is interesting, but was overshadowed by the terrible structure of the class. The exams were not representative of the learning targets at all, and the professor refuses to give any study material (practice questions, study guides) The discussion is annoying and everything is graded very harshly. Tophat is graded on correctness.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professors' lecture slides are very information-dense with no structure. Discussion is completely unrelated to the information from lecture. Many group projects with poor formatting and instructions. No practice material or rubric provided for exams. Exam format is unnecessarily difficult and a poor way of assessing students' knowledge.

Professor makes simple tasks quite difficult. Lecture slides are packed with information and she wont tell you what information is needed to pass the class. A lot of assignments lack specificity which leads to a lot of students doing it wrong. Id say that the exam structure is not the best way to tests the students  knowledge.

Conceptually easy class made needlessly difficult. Exams rely on details barely mentioned. Discussions are irrelevant, and she refuses to provide any resources beyond slides. Other points are deducted arbitrarily to spread grades. Overall an exasperating professor who expects far more from students than she puts into her one weekly lecture.

Best professor I've ever had, very engaging and funny lecturer and incorporates fun stories. He's very smart, well-spoken and breaks down complex concepts so that they're easy to understand. I've taken 320 and 330 with him and wish he could teach all my classes. Very accessible outside of class and happy to help. Can't say enough good things!!

Adam is a great guy and is super passionate about finance. He is insanely smart so he can digress, but he will really give you a deep understanding about finance. Goofy and funny, wants you to do well.
Took the class 4 years ago. Still using knowledge from the class today. Best I've ever had.

Amazing professor - the best I have had. Very caring guy who keeps lectures interesting with his funny comments and stories. Grade consists of 5 exams. Exams are relatively easy, as he releases practice exams that cover (almost) all of the concepts needed for the exam. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had. He makes class interesting with his stories and random comments, and it is clear that he is passionate about finance. Extremely willing to help outside of class. Exams are easy with practice questions very similar to (or the same as) the exam questions. Highly recommend.
One of, if not my favorites in the finance department. Great at explaining the complicated concepts in derivatives, great course administration with online lectures, and fair exams.

Had Dr. Smedema for two different upper-level finance courses two semesters straight. This guy is the best. Records his lectures, gives helpful modules to study with, and will never throw any surprises at you on tests. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it over any other professor. You will not regret it.

Courses grade consists of 12 problem sets and 3 unit exams and if you do the problem sets the exams should be a breeze. Quantity of work was not bad. I did most of my studying the week of the exams and would read the other week there wasn't one. Highly recommend him Adam for this course, and its a shame he doesn't teach during the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall grade is determined by 12 problem sets and 3 unit tests. There are 3 Unit tests and the questions are pretty similar to problem sets and practice tests. If you complete all tasks in the module (read textbook, watch lecture, and practice) , you will get at least an AB for this class! And Dr. Smedema will always help you as you need!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very upbeat and chill dude. He's good at explaining tricky concepts. The class is structured as 4 12 point tests, 2 24 point cases, and 12 4 point problem sets. That's a total of 144 points and 133 is the min for an A. It's an easy class but low margin for error. Tests are similar to prob sets and practice tests he gives you. Make sure to read book

Adam is a fantastic young professor who related really well to our class. The first half of the class was extremely easy and was basically just Finance 300 over again. The second half was more difficult but built off of the first half stuff. I liked Adam a lot and would definitely recommend him.

With a dry sense of humor and a vast knowledge of the time, Stern made up for his choppy (and often silent) lectures with sharp wit that would often make you laugh. That being said, he was not the best lecturer and I often found myself bored despite the interesting topic and readings. He asks for participation, but did not know how to get it.

I really like Professor Stern. I thought the lectures were very informative even though he "uhm" more times than anyone else ever. I got the just of the readings pretty well just by attending every class. If you show up and pay attention, you'll do fine. If you don't, good luck. Also, he gives you the questions ahead of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stern is very knowledgeable and passionate. The lectures were interesting, though the first 15ish minutes reviewed the content of the previous lecture, which became monotonous. He does a nice job of making the sometimes dense readings understandable. Part of his grading is based on 'creativity' but still easy to score well.

Jewish 225 - I will say that Professor Stern is a caring professor. From the first lecture I knew my Jewish 225 class was going to be an interesting one. He cares about your well being if you make an effort to improve and learn the subject. Would highly recommend to those looking to challenge themselves while learning. His vocab is off the charts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly assignments that determine most of your grade, a cumulative final but he gives the questions he's going to ask beforehand, tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very respectable and great guy to have as a professor. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and has a lot of enthusiasm for the course material. Lectures can be monotonous at times as they go over weekly readings, but I found them to be helpful in summarizing and remembering the readings from the week.
Long lectures, can get boring at times but easiest class I took in all of college. Grades based on incomplete/complete and a C or above is complete. Very easy

Graded by complete/incomplete, so if you do your work and take basic notes in class you'll do well. A little bit of a stickler on things -- gave us assigned seats, but that was due to a group of super disrespectful people. Very very very knowledgeable, very smart, fairly engaging. Kind guy, wish my peers respected him more

I loved having Adam as a professor! He's very passionate with his teaching and always come to class very prepared and organized. His class required heavy reading but during lectures he recaps the readings well. We would have small group discussions every class and then come back together to relay what was talked about. Loved his grading scale too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very articulate and skilled with explaining difficult concepts. He tried his best to facilitate conversations online and he's skilled at withstanding silence! Readings were interesting and a fair amount of writing. Learned a lot from Prof Stern. You need to work for your grade.

Good guy and knowledgeable, but as the last post said, this class didn't adapt well to an online format (in-person might be more enjoyable). Was reading and discussion-based, but the discussions were mainly summarizing the readings. Not much debate or deep analysis that I expected from a philosophy class. A TON of reading. Learned a lot though!

I don't think he's a bad professor at all. He seems to care about his students and wants the best for them. He is obviously very intelligent. I just think that his class didn't adapt well to the online format. It was very discussion-based and it's hard to encourage participation over Zoom. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by with skimming.

Best professor I've had at UT. Basically distills research papers and their jargon down into easily understandable terms and the material he covers is super interesting. The only thing I didn't like about this class were the TA/guest lectures, and that's just because compared to Akella they can't explain anything. Exams reasonable, hw easy.

First time teaching an undergraduate class at UT, so the grading was a little odd - only 5 programming assignments (relatively straightforward) and one final exam + participation in class. Fantastic lecturer! Assignments are well explained although a little tricky to set up because of CloudLab. Take him if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aditya is fantastic! CS 640 teaches so many interesting lessons that everyone would be better off knowing. Simply put, Akella is a phenomenal professor. Not only is he extremely knowledgeable, but he is incredibly talented at teaching and makes sure that everyone in the class understands what he is teaching. In addition, he is very humble and kind. Definitely make sure to take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Truly gifted, thoughtful, understanding, and all around great professor. Take any course you can with him.

no textbook will help because none can interfere with classroom teaching - textbooks can only enable and support classes
Very unassuming and humble for someone who has achieved that level of success at that age
A no-nonsense professor, he appreciates the value of his time and yours

Real learning happens only when one steps outside boundaries like 'spend not more than 1-2 hours studying outside class for every hour spent in class' and this is really useful stuff totally worth putting a bit of extra time and energy

Attending classes and paying attention will be your best bet, no textbook will help as much no matter what
If you ever make a request and ask to explain a concept in class he will 100% make sure to clarify it in detail. You really get to learn
Professor has very very high standards but if you put in the effort the course demands, you will positively be rewarded. He is kind and fair.

He is a very good lecturer and provides a lot of clarity in the class structure and in the projects. At least as of this semester, there are five quizzes in place of any exams, which is great.  The projects can take a lot of time (think CS 537) but also make you learn a lot of useful/interesting stuff. Overall, fantastic professor and course.
He is a great lecturer and very good at clarifying your questions. I would recommend him for 640. He is extremely knowledgeable and conveys ideas clearly
hate it
It is a difficult course to take.. The HW's require too much time and effort. Many difficult papers to read. He covers the important points of the paper in the lecture so lectures are much useful..

reviews.comment: Great professor. Definitely knows what hes talking about with respect to Networks. Will help you whenever you need it and is very responsive. Material isn't too tough, the projects are slightly difficult, quizzes are not too bad if you go to lecture and reread the slides, I'd recommend him as a professor.
Good
Good.
She like doesn't elaborate enough in lectures but she's lowkey funny

I actually quite enjoyed taking this class. The lectures can feel long, but they were super interesting. Each exam covers a lot of material, so make sure to give yourself enough time to study. As a professor I thought she explained things pretty well, and overall I didn't have any complaints.

Only ever read straight off the slides with little to no further explanation. Tests were much more abstract and informational then the basic information you were given. Tests were weighted very heavy so very hard to grade up if you don't do well on one exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is tough to say Dr. Addington was a good lecturer, she was fair. I will say do not pay attention to literally anything she says, use the exam review sheet for reference. If you study that sheet religiously, you should be fine. The first exam is extremely difficult, and if you do not prepare, you will get punched in the mouth. DO THE EC!!

Becky moves fast through lectures, so pay attention, and also note the videos and studies she shows because they appear on the tests. Never listen when she says something won't be on the test; it will. She is very reachable by email, even more than the TA. She reads off the slides but provides good information along with them. Do the extra credit!

I personally did not hate the lectures and thought she was good overall at explaining concepts, but make sure that you study for at least a week in advance. DO NOT LISTEN to her when she says something is not on the test and you do not need to study it because it WILL be on the test! 100% do the extra credit because it boosts your grade so much.

I liked the professor but the class was concept based, ALL OF IT. I had to drop the course, it's really hard to go back to a C or above after scoring so low in the first exam.. this isn't a class where you can prep the night before.. good luck if you're taking this class.

One of the better professors to get for this class, even though lectures are pretty boring. There are 4 exams throughout the semester that are not cumulative--literally a lifesaver because this class has A LOT of content. The material isn't hard, but I would recommend at least skimming the reading.
She is a terrible person. She laughs at things like 911 and sexual assault of children. As a victim myself, it makes me scared and uncomfortable. DO NOT TAKE BECKY.

It's so so so hard to get a good score on an elementary course by her. I have reviewed all the key points for each test for at least 6 hours every night before tests. I must tell you for me a person who has never taken any psych courses before. You can only get a B for the most with all extra credits. I got A for all of my rest courses. Be careful!

Professor Addington cares deeply about her students, her lectures can be long and sometimes boring however thats college for you. Do the extra credit, if you do all you have to do is shoot for an 87% for an A.

Lowkey the class isn't that bad, but hope you get a good TA. The TA we currently have is horrific and doesn't do her job well. Addington also just reads off of slides in the most monotone voice. Puts me to sleep

"Teaching" is just reading slides with mandatory lectures. Extremely difficult to stay engaged as learning is purely listening. TAs are harsh with grading short essays and quizzes are either get 100% or 0%. For example, my 0.9/1 quiz was regraded to a 0/1. Midterm was also very specific and exhausting to know every detail despite immense studying

Her lectures are very BORING you could fall asleep. She basically reads off of the slides and attendance is mandatory. Exams are also extremely hard and toughly graded. But she gives extra credit opportunity tho.
This professor read off of the slides that she presented and all of the slides were taken off of the textbook in class. Every example.

If you're struggling, go to office hours and talk to your TA. I had 210, it was tough but if you use the resources available to you it's fine. Very friendly at office hours. Participating in lecture helps.

I really liked her. Her lectures were very straightforward and she even tells you what concepts to study before the exam. I found the exams to be pretty easy. She also does review sessions before the exams which help alot and she records all of her lectures.
She was excellent at explaining the concepts. Class was laid out very clearly.

reviews.comment: she is brutal. Exams do not reflect what you actually learn in class. Had to drop the class because thats how brutal her grading policies are. Please take literally any other professor besides her for 210. Please please please
Very disorganized, slow grading, confusing when walking through problems

Please do not take the class with her! My TA's discussions were more helpful than her lectures. She does not align her lectures with homework bc it consisted of material from the following lecture. She yaps about examples for too long, that it starts to make no sense. She made me hate a class I took a great interest in.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR/you will fail this class regardless of how much effort u put in/she sabotages you/the exam questions are paragraphs/there is no curve/she wastes the whole lecture talking about dogs/attendance is REQUIRED yet you will learn nothing for the whole 1 and 15/seriously take another professor this is a warning

reviews.comment: Falls behind on class content schedule/Gives examples in class that turn into stories not related to helpful material overcomplicating it/Material on tests does not accurately reflect content in lecture/Attendance is mandatory but I've been better off reading the textbook/Explain processes behind everything on tests even if she doesnt explain it.

Take with any other professor if you can. Only way to survive and get a decent grade is a good TA who explains examples during lab. Attendance is mandatory but lecture is unhelpful. Tangents that provide no understanding. Behind in content but still tested on things we haven't covered yet. Have to follow along with her writing on a piece of paper.

Nice person but a horrible lecturer. Every lecture is extremely boring and slow. She overexplains everything. The pacing of the class is really weird in terms of content. The tests were unnecessarily hard (average score was 60% on first test). I took stats before and she made me question if I really knew stats. Leave each class with a headache.

Everything on exams was straight from lectures. You can tell she cares about students & was nice to accommodate me when I was sick. Not the best class, but it's okay. I even took 210 with her which was more difficult but she breaks stuff down. The exams were harder than the homework which sucked, but I did notice she made a point to learn our names

Honestly the TA you get for this class matters drastically. Mine was amazing, while the other I heard was awful and graded harshly. I had Addington for 202, and don't mind her teaching style; however, an AP stats background greatly helped me here. If you don't like stats, or have had Addington before and didn't like her, take another professor.

reviews.comment: Her lectures can drag on but that's a given with the course material. She's very thorough with examples which helped a ton. Lab is pretty useless as SPSS is very simple, but the practice sheets were nice. Homework is easy and short. The tests seemed designed to take the entire time, so study and do lots of practice problems. Overall, she was great.
This class is pretty boring and her tests are impossible no matter how much you read or how well you know the material.
all she does is talk about how she's a dog trainer and makes students fall asleep during power lecture.

I had Becky for two classes in one semester and found that she was one of the best professors I have had. She made lecture interesting with very clear Powerpoints as well as lots of pictures and examples to go along with topics. To top it off, she brings her dog in for examples on learning and Wren was awesome!

Although the lectures and topics of the class are themselves fun, the tests are way unbelievably hard. I'm good at memorizing terms and I understood all the material we learned, but that didn't help at all. Unless you're good at deciphering lengthy test questions and figuring out what she means in every question, don't take the class

The material is really easy to learn, but she will make the class appear more difficult than it actually is by having exams with poorly worded questions that will stretch your reading comprehension more than they will stretch your understanding of the material.  The class averages on the exam can't possibly reflect the understanding of the material

Before taking stats, I was really nervous because I'm really not a math person at all. But Professor Addington made all the concepts super easy to understand, assignments were easy, and exams were fair.
I'm not quite sure why Becky is rated so low. I went on a friend's recommendation to take Psych Stats with her, and I'm glad I took her recommendation instead of taking the rating into consideration!

Really great professor.  She is quirky and funny, and her love of dogs shines through!  I was nervous about this class because math has always been difficult for me, but she takes the time to explain all concepts and makes it very easy to understand.  Highly recommend!

great proffessor, very engageed and interested in the course. Do not read the text book and attend all lectures. Everything on the exams is from lecture. Exams are very straight forward if you pay attention

Overall, she was a great teacher; passionate, engaging and interesting. Her exams were tough but fair. However, she is extremely difficult to get in contact with, she never responded to any of my emails, and I couldn't even leave a voicemail on her office phone, it just kept ringing. Very frustrating. Otherwise, great teacher.
Her class was fairly easy compared to other psychology classes. Her exams are straightforward and fair.

Loved her and loved the class. Exams can be difficult but are sill fair. Professor Addington is more than willing to help students and meet outside of class. Very passionate about the subject and even brings her dog in for demonstrations. Even though I loved this class, I would only recommend it for people who have an interest in animal behavior.
Tests are impossible. Addington will ask you about anything used in the textbook, no matter how seemingly insignificant. Be prepared to read the book 3 or 4 times. Very boring class.

The class is very boring and slow but Addington is very thorough and clear. The tests are hard but reasonable and she is very responsive to students and technologically proficient so email communication is easier and grade postings are relatively prompt. I'd recommend her.

Addington is a great professor and lecturer! She makes everything crystal clear as she goes through lecture and is super-organized.  She's extremely amenable to extra help, too. Tests are only difficult b/c of the bell curve the psych dept makes mandatory. If you have to take the dreadful 225, take it with her; she'll make it less painful!

DON'T take this class! At first I thought the material was very interesting, I did the readings, took diligent notes during lectures, and studied hard. Despite all of this, the exams were unbelievably difficult! The questions were extremely confusing and VERY dense. Would never recommend this class to a friend. Wish I would have taken 450 instead.

Terrible class. Material appeared to be easy but tests were unfairly difficult. Not to mention extremely boring lectures. As someone had previously stated, she is very flakey. Poor excuses for canceling an exam (literally an hour before it was scheduled) and office hours. Was also late for the final exam... Do not take this class!!

No idea what others are talking about, tests were absurdly easy with normal amount of studying!  A joy compared to others in the psych dept, the first straight-forward and FAIR tests given. Fantastic lecturer, takes time to ensure everyone understands every point before moving on. Very helpful when you ask her questions. Awesome class, a pleasure.

Good lecturer and easy to follow but the exams were ridiculous.  The questions were not very clear and as a whole the exams were very dense.  I would also suggest taking 450 with Coe instead.  That class was better.

While the topic is interesting, I would not recommend taking this class. She's quite a flake... re-scheduled one exam (the day of) because she had a migraine... and then moved the second and canceled her office hours immediately preceding the exam so she could "finish working on it". Take 450 with Coe instead - it's much better class

One of the worst in the psychology department. She will not give any credit on exams for answers that are not specific, but she is always vague in lecture. Questions on the exams are not clear, but she will still take points off. Try to tae this class when Addington is not teaching it.
Great 225 teacher. Very clear and helpful! Yes, the class sucks, but Addington tries to help make it do-able.

The class is very interesting but it is really annoying that she never returns assignments. The readings are not necessary. I wouldn't even bother buying the textbook. Overall I really enjoyed the class.

I liked this class. Rebecca is well organized and runs it smoothly. She also brings in her dog to demonstrate and knows a lot about dog training. Exams are indeed ridiculous, as others have said - she is so incredibly picky on the short answer questions. Overall recommended, however.

Exams itself were very hard, but you have homeowork assignments that play a role in your final grade. What I liked the most was that Rebecca was very understanding and made every chance possible to engage the students. She was also very available to meet. Okay class, good prof.

Becky is a good teacher. let's face it, Statistics is extremely boring and there are few people that can make it interesting. Go to lecture it really helps because the tests are mostly from lecture materials. The class is not easy by any means but it is manageable if you put in the time.
Becky was great!  This class is notoriously difficult and boring, but she made it pretty do-able.  Definitely go into office hours for help on papers - she's really great!
Lecture is easy to follow, and then the test comes and it's ridiculously hard. Only geared towards one type of thinker, no room for individualized ideas. Get through it and move on.

You have 3 things keeping your grade down in this class: 1.) The curve is not generous. 2.) The people who drop out of this class who are on the lower end of the curve put the middle portion students closer to the bottom of the curve. 3.) You have to compete with students who retake this class (so they get a 2.75 GPA average with Intro PSY). HARD!!

She explains concepts very clearly if tediously. Lecture is so comprehensive dont really need book unless you want it for review. Tests arent too hard but the curve makes them more painful.So if you want an A study hard. if your at all good with a computer dont bother going to discussion the SPSS manual will tell you everything you need to know.
She just makes you angry.  Normally if you do badly you know you're responsible that is not the case in this class.

She is the worst professor I've had.  She makes the tests so that no matter how well you know the material you cannot finish.  I got a C on a test without getting anything wrong, just couldn't finish. No one can.  She doesn't understand that it is not a test of our knowledge, its a race.  Many tests can be hard to finish but Ive never seen this b4.

Good class. Not THAT easy, but if you go to class and study a little you'll be fine. You don't have to do the readings, but I do the them as a form of reviewing the material. Tests are very straight forward. Gives you a review sheet of what you need to know for each exam. 3 exams and 1 easy homework assignment.

not interesting to listen to. only used animal and wildlife examples for problems. she would go on for 15 min to set up the problem, and by the time you would actually start working on the problem, you forgot what you were trying to solve! showed up and listened but still do not understand any statistics at all!
typical psych course, graded almost solely on 3 exams (1 hw assignment), about the same difficulty level as psych 202.

Had addington for 210 and 225. I definitely recommend her for 210; its boring subject matter no matter how you cut it so her clarity is helpful. 225 sucks no matter who teaches it, especially because of the bell curve, but she doesnt make it harder than it needs to be. exams arent hard theyre just graded hard so the curve doesnt make a 92 a B

Addington: clear, concise, knowledgeable and helpful.  Awfully stern at times but not angry, follows rules, not much room for negotiation.  Exams: require detailed, to the point answers.  Vague answers only recieve half credit. Papers (3): long, be prepared, 15-20pgs plus, research required.  Work/time intensive, technicial more than conceptual.

Had her for both 225 and 449. She isn't as hard on grading as everyone says, you just need to know your definitions. As long as you do the readings and take good notes, you shouldn't have a problem getting an A. For 225, your grade more or less depends on your TA, since they grade all of the papers (and half of each test).

She doesnt like to return emails. takes months to grade papers... if on the exam you do not put the exact word that she wants( just the defenition) she will mark you down! :( like the info of the class, just hated the grading
If you want to memorize stuff and spit it back to her take this class.  Otherwise, dont...Coe is way better- take psych450
hard class no matter what you do. my personal opinion is Addington is a much better teacher than the other options...

Very clear explanations including uselessly long examples.  Review sheet is a gift from God, but she probably won't send it until the night before the exam.  Boring.  Can know all material for an exam, don't give exactly the answer she wants, and get a C on the exam.  Papers and be...overwhelming.  Could be worse, I guess.

She knows her material, but conveys it in an uninteresting manner.  She has to be one of the pickiest graders I have ever had.  Some of her test questions are way off base.  If you want a class on a similar subject taught by a great teacher, take Psych 450 or 451 (not sure which it is) by Christopher Coe (Pysch of the Primates).

I took this class in the summer of 07 and it was not nearly has hard as i expected. I definetly recommend taking it over the summer with Addington as she focuses less on the statistical stuff and more on the experimental process. Although it requires lots of time and effort, Addington cheers you on and gives you everything you need to succeed.
lectures are very clear but tests are very hard

The lectures are insanely boring and she is a nazi with grading.  She will take points off on exams if you do not answer with the EXACT wording that she wants you to.  Not a class worth taking unless absolutely necessary.

Her exams are the same for Psych 225 and 449. I had her for both classes. The exams always have multiple choice, short answer and 2 long answer questions. She lectures off of powerpoint. Reading the book is kind of helpful, she'll put a question sometimes in the multiple choice from the book that she didn't go over in class.
Lectures are pretty boring, and the tests are impossible....not a class worth taking
good teacher, hard class
The class is meant to be a weeder course, so all assignments are predetermined and the bell curve is set.  Addington doesn't try to make it any more terrible than it has to be.
well organized class
Pretty good teacher, just a long boring class with an uninteresting subject.
She makes this class so much harder then it needs to be. The tests are just ridiculously hard. I would try to get a different teacher if you have to take this class as a requirement.

I think Professor Addington was a good professor.  Her exams are fair, but tough.  She gives you all the information you need to know via lecture and she emails study guides for each exam.  Totally obsessed with a few animals :)  Overall, it was a good class, but certainly not an easy A.  Recommendations:  Go to every lecture...book is mostly junk.

Professor Addington, I think, is a pretty good professor.  She tells you almost everything you need to know for the exams.  She emails study guides for every exam, so there is no reason not to know what is on the exam!!  Go to lecture, and study your notes, the book isn't much of a help.

The exams were bizzare, some questions were way too specific, ie. soemtihing you would have had to have ready a tiny blurb several times to know or remember. Teacher is nice, but the class is not an easy A.

I took this class in Fall of 2000. I am not in graduate school and I realize how much I learned. She was a great teacher and I learned a lot. Tough class though I have to say. The tests were way too hard.
She explains concepts well and is easy to approach with a question.
Will not email you back, hands back exams 6 weeks later
Didn't enjoy the class

This is a strange class to beging with.  Tests aren't that bad if you treat them like 225 tests, but she asks ridiculously specific questions.  Not a good power lecture class, but over all I dont hate it, or her.  Just not that impressive
Her tests have nothing to do with lecture.  Extremely boring speaker, nice, but extremely unclear and not worth the D I'm getting in the class.
Very nice!
Strange obsession with dog racing and breeding a'la BEST IN SHOW
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
It is LITERALLY impossible to get an A in this class
There is absolutely NOTHING you can do to prepare for these exams they are like nothing you have ever seen in your life.

Do not take a class with Alex if your able. He literally doesn't use an answer key to grade, instead he lines up 20 tests and grades based on your responses compared to the other students. Had to stop going to class because he would get so off track that I learned more by myself. Tests are unreasonably hard and purposefully nothing like examples.

I took the four lecture/week course Mon-Thurs. Abiral is amazing, he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The class was beneficial and thought provoking. There are two papers during the course, and a paper to read each week. The reading can be heavy and confusing, but if you complete the work you will succeed.

Abiral is kind, smart, and knowledgeable. He creates a comfortable environment in his classroom. The class material is interesting and thought-provoking. The essays are open-ended and therefore not difficult if you put in effort. There is a lot of reading and it can be tough to get through and understand as it's old stuff.

Abiral was very passionate and invested in what he was teaching, but it was easy to get started as someone with little background in Philosophy. He was easy to work with and made the whole class feel involved. This class had a lot of reading, but he gives that disclaimer at the beginning of the semester. Overall a great course.

The best. Super flexible and caring, you could tell she really enjoys both her students and subject matter. If you have a question about her class material or policies, just reach out to her, she wants to work with you! If you have a chance to take a class with her, do it!
LOVED having prof. Letak this semester. If you have the option to take this course please do. She teaches us so many important things about mental health and genuinely cares about all her students.

It is hard to find a professor better than prof Letak. She clearly plans all of her lectures for a long time and makes them very clear and easy to follow, as well as very engaging. She is a very caring professor and is great at what she does

Professor Letak has been my favorite professor at UW so far. She is an amazing lecturer and really cares about her students health. There are 4 quizzes which aren't too difficult and she is always available to meet out of class time. Papers are relatively easy and she makes lectures super interesting. Highly recommend.

Abby is a fantastic teacher and she really is my favorite prof in this school. She is caring, humorous, and knowledgable, especially she is young. She gives great examples for difficult terms and explain them in simple ways. No exams just really easy quizzes. Attendance occupies a lot in final grade. Just go to class and you will be fine!

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Her lectures were very easy to understand and follow, but you need to show up to lecture to pass. She made learning engaging & enjoyable. She really cares about how well students are doing in her class. Assignments are spaced out and she doesn't have midterms, just papers, quizzes, & discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was okay but it was too easy for this level of class. Abby is a nice person, but it doesn't always seem like she knows what she's talking about. I want to give her a pass because she's a doctoral student, but I thought the class would be more.

Professor Letak is great! Lecture attendance is mandatory, but she was always super understaning when I had to miss class due to sickness or other reasons. Assignments are spaced out well so it does not seem very overwhelming for a 4-credit course. She actually cares if students do well and tries to make things more understandable!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Letak was a great professor! She really enjoys social psychology and it shows in her lectures. There was a few quizzes, a few papers, and discussion posts. Overall, really easy to learn from.
Class is a standard physics class. Lecture and discussion are mandatory, even though neither were useful for me for overall exams.

I really liked Dr. Mohammadi for 208. His lectures often went through the conceptual part and equation derivation which most people didn't like but I liked it since it's critical to understand concepts to do well. He passionately did demos while also being accessible outside of class. Don't treat it as a math class, but an actual science class.

Speaks condescendingly and can't comprehend if you don't understand. He writes the exams in a way that are very difficult to understand and to do. He makes the exams be the hardest versions of the topics and words them in a way that makes no sense.

Had him for 207 as well and my opinion of him has only gotten worse. Likes to blame the class for low test averages and enjoys making things extremely theoretical and difficult. Difficulty of different elements of the course and practice materials do not line up at all. Lectures are difficult to follow and his answer keys are hardly useful.

Dr. Mohammadi is a decent lecturer and is passionate about physics. He is funny, cares about student success, and explains concepts to students well, but sometimes focuses too much on the conceptual and doesn't explain how to practically approach problems. Class difficulty all over the place; homework =/= exams =/= quizzes. Can feel blindsided.

Seems very nice, but lectures are not enough to prepare for quizzes and exams. He often spent a lot of time talking about how to derive the equations, rather than more practice questions that matched with exam material. He's very enthusiastic about teaching, but the layout of the course isn't great. One of the better intro physics professors, imo!

Dr Mohammadi is amazing. You can tell how much he cares about teaching. He came in very well prepared, knowing what we were going to cover and how he would cover it. He is very inspiring with how much passion he has. He knew that many people were scared to take this class and did his best to make it approachable. I can't say a bad thing about him.
Professor is enthusiastic in teaching but exams were constructed very horribly as if it was rush in an hour.

He gave lectures very enthusiastically, and seemed to genuinely care how his students did. Tests were difficult and seemed to test on things that weren't on the homework, but if you really throw yourself at the practice tests you can do alright.

Physics sucks.  But you have to take physics take it with him.  He works to engage his class (who don't reciprocate often), give real world examples of concepts (which frequently show on exams), and has a real passion for physics (which I don't).  When I sucked it up and really payed attention in lecture, I learned, and that is all you can ask for.

Abdollah seems like a great guy, very nice, but honestly this course and 207 are so messy and hard to get through. The difficulty of the lecture examples and textbook problems do not at all match up to the test questions. Labs are a slog to get through but graded generously. Pretty generous curve as well at least

Overall, 208 was ok. I enjoyed Prof. Mohammadi's humor and passion during lectures and OH. However, this course is super disorganized. Exams were all over the place, with the final containing ambiguities and even questions without answers. Some topics were crunched on time, and wasn't a huge fan of the mandatory attendance for discussion and labs.

Mohammadi is a great professor for Phys 208, he really tries to have the class engaging with demos and questions. He also makes his slides very easy to follow. For me E&M is a tougher unit than mechanics, but as long as you spend the time to study, it shouldn't be as bad. I would've preferred him as main professor, as he only taught a few classes.

Mohammadi is easily the best professor for Phys 207. Unlike the other professor, he actually tries to engage the students albeit not having the best handwriting. The homework does take a long time and the labs are overall not that bad. As long as you do well on homework and pay attention during his lectures, then you should be okay with the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thought it couldn't get worse after 207 but I was wrong. Lectures were incoherent and made the content more confusing. Exams were absurdly difficult and did not accurately reflect the type of content or questions seen on homework/quizzes. I would not recommend this class to anyone seeking to actually understand physics. DON'T DO IT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, this course was ok. I would say Dr. Mohammadi made lectures enjoyable, going through demos and being funny. However, this 208's difficulty and structure is very disorganized. Especially exams were all over the place, and the final had unclear and clearly not proof-read questions. Idk what happened since past semesters seem more organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content itself was good hell, even the teaching wasn't half bad. But this professor is incapable of making a good exam. He gives a 6 paged equation sheet just for half the multiple choice questions to be some random physics equation he just throws out of no where to solve the problem. This is especially true for magnetism and optics/nuclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Mohammadi really cares about his students and their learning. His lectures go a bit fast and most of the time you'll have to study the content on your own to fully grasp the concepts. His lectures serve as more of an introduction to the material, but his slides are easy to read/follow on your own. Overall, I liked having him as an instructor!

Lectures are rather uninteresting. Although Prof. Mohammadi is passionate about the subject it doesn't translate to an engaging lecture. Lecture attendance is extra credit, which really says something about the class- expect to mostly learn from the textbook and/or your TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
I actually hate this class, if you have the option to not take it here PLEASE do
Mohammadi cannot teach and thinks that concepts that are easy for him are just common sense and it makes it difficult for others to learn. pls do. not. take. this. class.

I took physics 208 spring semester 2025 and it was THE WORST class, second to 207. Professor Mohammadi himself is a nice person, but definitely not a good instructor. He would often kill class time by going over equation derivation and then proceed to give exams that were way more difficult than anything went over in lecture (if any) and homework.

Dr. Mohammadi is a great teacher and I really enjoyed his Physics 207 class. He was funny and explained concepts in simple words so I can understand better. I would Highly recommend his class and I Had lots of fun and good times.

Worst prof ever. Spends more time deriving equations than explaining how to use them. Extremely disorganized course and the exams were unnecessarily confusing. He is condescending, rude, and teaches like everyone in the class has a physics background. I wouldn't recommend to my worst enemy. Genuinely the worst experience I've ever had in a class.

Physics 207 is a hard class and there were many times I was confused in class. But that doesnt mean Dr.Mohammadi is a bad teacher. He goes through problems in class and does helpful tophat like questions that really help your understanding. He also is very funny which is nice. Only complaint is he writes cos and sin very weirdly which is confusing.

I think abdollah assumes that understanding concepts he's been teaching for years is easy so he doesn't put effort into helping you comprehend it. This class sucks overall but going to lecture after reading the textbook actually made me understand the class LESS.

Abdollahs lectures were often all over the place and were way too detailed and overwhelming. Types of questions you'd see on an exam were never talked about in lecture. Content from homework and discussions seemed completely useless as it never related to stuff on exams. He's a nice guy, but it felt like this class sets you up for failure.

I find him so funny. Love his vibes. Kinda a bad teacher imo, but I dont use the lec slides to study so it didn't rlly matter. lots of past exams are provided for practice. discussion attendance is graded which kind of sucks but you get 5 skips. He's super chill and you can tell he enjoys teaching. textbook readings are not mandatory.

Lowkey hated this class because it was super hard and the exams are pretty much the only thing that affects your grade. Lots of homework and problem sets and quizzes but they're worth a small percentage. Abdollah was okay, knows his stuff but doesn't teach it very well. This class definitely requires a lottt of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Awesome professor!
Even though I may not end up getting A or even AB in the course, I really like the teaching style of Prof. Mohammadi. He is so caring, sometimes funny, and explains tough concepts in simple language! I really do not know why he got some negative comments here!

Not sure why this professor got so many negative points.
Dr Mohammadi is one of the best professors I have ever had. Definitely recommend taking 207 and 208 courses with him.
He is so caring, fun, and knowledgable. The demos are in class are great.

Dr. Mohammadi did his best to keep the course engaging. He was clearly passionate about the subject. Learned the most from doing the homework. Lecture attendance gives 2 point boost to the overall grade. Homework would get penalize when you input an incorrect answer to the Mastering website. Labs were pretty useless but a grade boost overall.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Mohammadi is very engaging. The slides are organized well so it is easy to understand as he is walking through the process of solving problems. He is also very responsive to feed back which is helpful for changes being made going forward. The use of in class demos to show concepts was great!

I had Mohammadi for both 207 and 208. I got an A in 207 but 208 was much tougher and I ended with an AB. Overall, he made the course material engaging and at times humorous. Lectures were useful but it's good to sit nearer the front to see the whiteboard and hear him better. Would take again with him.
Useless lectures

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO! This class and its professors are made to set everyone up for failure. Lectures/PowerPoint slides are useless. And no matter how much time you spend studying for the exams, you will NOT get the grades you think you worked for. Definitely take a class that is easier but the equivalent of 207, if you can.

207 was just about the worst class I have ever taken. Lectures are meaningless. Discussions don't prepare you for the exams, nor do practice exams or review sheets. Exams are significantly hard. Instructor office hours were pointless. While his lectures were better than the other instructor teaching it, they were still so unhelpful. Don't take this
Does a good job of breaking complex things down in lecture, and discussions are very helpful
Professor Mohammadi seems to be very knowledgeable about the course and he provides us with useful information. He had a nice lecturing style that made the class very easy to follow.

Take 207 and 208 with Him. Dr. Mohammadi is an underrated professor in the physics department for General physics teaching. Lectures are great and exams are fair. His slide could be a bit hard to follow but if you understand discussion problems and previous year exams, you will be fine.

Attendance is mandatory and is taken via a participation session on MasteringPhysics. He is a nice man but the lectures are hard to follow and rarely cover relevant information. He goes fast and either doesn't elaborate enough, or elaborates WAY too much. Discussion sections are gonna save you, as will your TA's office hours.

Professor Mo's lectures are decent, I can usually follow along with his lessons. It's hilarious when he tries to do demonstrations for the class and they don't work. 207 is hard, however there is a substantial curve, and the physics faculty cares a lot more about their jobs than the people in the Math department. Study hard and you'll do okay.

Physics definitely isn't the best class but he genuinely tries to make it understandable and semi-fun. He's very accessible after class and will help you better understand concepts. Yes, the course is hard, but he is probably your best bet in making it through the semester and passing (just show up and do the homework).
The exams are way too hard compared to the content he teaches in class. There is no additional material he provides to prepare better for the hard exams.
Professor Mohammadi is a great instructor he makes learning enjoyable. Physics is a tough course, and although I struggle with the material I find it helpful that he makes the class less stressful.
Class is hard, but if you keep up with the homeworks and discussions and ask help when needed, you will be just fine.

PHYS 207 is a terribly organized class and the exams are ridiculously difficult. I thought Mohammadi was the better lecturer of the pair that we had and he was very helpful in office hours. My frustrations lie more with the class than this professor specifically, but his lectures were sometimes confusing and often did not match the textbook.

I did an exam with him and scheduled it for a different time and he forgot I had him (and he agreed) for a later time that day.  He said the only way I would get credit was if I took the exam right away in the next 30 minutes (3 hours before my scheduled time).  The class was very difficult, but my TA was the only thing that got me through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ridiculously hard class for introductory physics. Goes over lecture slides super fast and covers a ton of material each lecture. Exams are extremely hard with averages ranging from low 70s in the beginning of the year to low 50s by the final. Homework is also extremely time consuming with very hard problems that are graded by accuracy.

He cares for his students but is not a great lecturer. I'd never taken physics before, so the first half of the semester I taught myself out of the textbook until I sort of gave up. Due to easy labs, doing all my homework, and a bit of extra credit, I managed a B. So while the class was difficult, getting a decent grade is pretty achievable.

He has this belief system that he is correct about everything because he studies major political figures as his job/passion and writes about them. He thinks if you disagree with him it's because you're just not as smart as he is. I approached him with respect on a twitter account he doesn't know is mine and, as expected, he called me a rude name...

Helped me rediscover my love of poetry. Dude is an expert when it comes to literature and literary theory, and also has a pedagogical approach that is a welcome break from usual academia. Seth is a fantastic teacher. If you get a chance, take his class.

Seth is probably the smartest man I have ever had teach me. He genuinely cares about your success. His Metamodernistic spin to the class may be frustrating at first, but once you truly understand it, it's actually very interesting. He is a fair grader and is understanding about late work, absences, tough assignments, etc. You will learn a lot.
He is incredibly kind and very helpful in regards to proper English grammar.
Interesting background with being a lawyer. Course has a criminal justice emphasis which made it interesting.
He's super helpful, not boring, is pretty funny, and makes the class interesting. And you actually learn something!

Seth is by far one of the best teachers ive ever had at UW-Madison.  He puts his own spin of criminal justice into the english class so that the prompts for writing assignment are more interesting.  He has a really interesting background between being a former lawyer and published poet.  I would highly recommend his class, you wont regret it!
different way of teaching. learned more than I thought I would. fun, likes to use games, but they are effective.
He knows what he'a doing and makes English class very pragmatic in nature. I'm very glad I took this class. He even bought pizza on the last day for everyone.
Makes class really interesting and focused class on Criminal Justice.  Always welcomed questions about the outside world and how the legal system worked.  Recommend this class to everyone!

Professor Faisal's class is the best art class I have taken in three years. I took Art 348 Digital Printing (no option in rating). His expertise and friendliness are incredible. He teaches extra skills and field trips, is helpful, and appreciates you. This class forms a community like no other, and you learn about literacy as an artist. 
、

I can't believe Faisal has only 2 ratings, best professor/teacher I have ever had. I was perpetually mind blown by his knowledge, experience, kindness, supportiveness, etc etc. I would recommend to take one of his classes no matter what your degree is. His class changed my perspective and encouraged me to continue pursuing art.

It's a learning community seminar, so he's probably easier on this class than in his true art classes, but it's pretty easy and a lot of fun. It's interdisciplinary, so no one's judged on skill and everyone's encouraged to experiment & go out of our comfort zones.

If you need someone to really challenge your work, Faisal is the professor to go to. He is constantly playing "devil's advocate" which can be a little frustrating at times, but it also sparks a lot of growth. Faisal has turned my head upside down more than a few times and is one of the most complex conceptual thinkers in the program.

(SOC618) Great professor, and a great course! Fabien teaches well, assigns interesting readings, and gives a lot of flexibility with the project. Don't skip readings. Pick a research topic that you love. If you've never done much programming, you'll need to put in more time than most people to learn R.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor who you can tell genuinely cares about the subject and students' understanding. Easy class if you're interested in the subject, otherwise the readings can get tedious but overall not bad.

Super interesting professor and he clearly knows a ton about the subjects he teaches. The class is almost entirely built based on discussion of the readings, and there are a LOT of them, but read them and show up to class and you'll do well.
There was a significant amount of reading for each class, however each reading was fairly understandable and was thoroughly covered in class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Professor Acker is simply fantastic!

The course is difficult due to the material, but she is super accessible and supportive and does everything she can to help you if you seek help.

I would even say UW's Business School is blessed to have her!
Best professor I have ever had at UW
Amazing! very enthusastic and you can tell shes very inteligent

Lindsay is amazing. There's an online textbook but you don't need to read it because she puts everything on the lecture slides (which are fully on Canvas). Lindsay cares a lot and makes herself very available. Great explanations and lots of examples/practice - overall the class was way better than I expected

I liked Professor Acker a lot! She had great material prepared for us and did an excellent job of explaining. Homework was participation-based and exams were open note. I never felt that anything was unfair.

She is seriously the best! I enjoyed the content. At first the class is challenging because it is very different material. If you review and print out ALL powerpoint examples and homework problems, you should do decent on the exams (open note). She is willing to help you learn if ask. She make the class fun and she is a very sweet person!!

Lindsay is one of my favorite professors. She walks through lectures in such an easy to understand way, giving real life examples. She really cares about her students and their learning. I didn't think I would like fundamentals of taxation, but after taking Lindsay's class, I decided I would like to work in tax. She's the best!

Lindsay is amazing. She had to do partnership tax online this semester. Every week it was the same pattern: Monday watch a lecture video, tuesday do HW, Friday take a quiz. Her quizzes and exams were on a time crunch and the averages were always high, so there was little of a curve. But, she is a superior lecturer and very caring and understanding

Accounting 329 with Lindsay was great! You don't really need to read the textbook because certain sections we don't need to know for class. Her powerpoints pretty much contain what you need to know. Beware that exams are a bit hard and you feel like there's not enough time to do calculations. Homework is simple, once a week. Just ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lindsay is great. Tax topics is kind of a random assortment of different topics. Despite this, Lindsay is an incredible lecturer. The workload is fair and nice. She also delivers the material in a concise but clear/understandable manner. Tests are worth a lot. Dont let that scare you. If you put your effort in, youll still succeed

Lindsay is awesome. She's taught the only accounting class I've ever enjoyed and made the material really engaging. Everything seems extremely applicable and she does a great job of taking her time to explain things. She makes sure that we know we can always be in contact with her if we have questions and her exams/quizzes are very fair.

Lindsay is a great professor, one of my favorites! The textbook is useful to have to skim through and refer back to for homework problems. She explains things super well and is very enthusiastic and knowledgable about the material. She makes the class and material interesting. The exams are reasonable if you study the slides and quizzes.

Taylan was a great professor. He genuinely cared how his students learned. The tests were somewhat difficult, as I feel the questions were ambiguous at times. However, Taylan fully took that into consideration and graded accordingly. I found the lectures very interesting and his humor kept the lectures light. I fully recommend Taylan as a professor

He really cares about his students and makes class very enjoyable! He communicates with the class very well and understands we have a life outside of school and genuinely cares about our well-being. Very approachable about grades and works with you if there is a concern. Definitely take another class with him!
Eye-opening class! Though grading not super clear, Taylan handles a tough topic very well. He was very good in connecting his class to relevant issues on campus and beyond.
This course really opened my eyes to the race relations in the United States. It was great to have him as professor for the class.
Awesome professor that is very passionate about the class. He really knew his stuff and I would highly recommend taking him for soc134 if you have the option!

I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned in this class. Not only was the professor never available, but all of the material was so unclear, the entire class relied on each other for clarification.
Not the best professor in a virtual setting. It was hard to learn from lectures as they were pretty proof-based, not many example problems.

Abhishek is great lecturer. He teaches straight out of the textbook, but explains the material very well. The lectures are good for conceptual understanding. It would be great if he could post answer keys for the practice and actual exams.

I took Math 320 online and it was fine. Im sure it would have been pretty hard in person, though. Abhishek lectures straight from the textbook, word for word, so honestly, the lectures aren't super useful. He sends out practice exams before midterms that are super similar to the actual exam, which are super helpful.

Abhishek seems like a very smart guy. However, his lectures are straight from the textbook. I look forward to the beginning of his lectures as he always starts with "alright, let's get started" but after that the lectures are fairly confusing as the material doesn't really make sense. I took this class fully online.
