His lectures consisted of proofs/theorems, and rarely involved actual examples of the concepts we were learning. Although his lectures were the least helpful way to learn, that was not the worst part about him. He refused to release keys for practice exams or past exams, so it was pointless to do the practice exams as you could not verify answers.

Took Calc with him last year. Had never taken a calc class before but listening to his lectures made the class easy. He was pretty easy to understand. However, I worked super hard in the class. My advice: Crush the first exam. I got like a 48 or 49 out of 50 points on the first exam and this carried me as the material got harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have now taken both Math 211 and Math 141 with Professor Deshpande. He is about as dry of a professor as you can find. His lectures, while moderately helpful, are very long and hard to pay attention to. He never updated the gradebook the entire semester until posting the final grades. I would strongly advise against taking a class with him.

He only used textbook examples which made lectures close to useless. He never explained things clearly and didn't answer questions well. For a class that is an introduction to calculus, he made it extremely hard to learn and form a baseline as he didn't give any more examples or resources to find if you didn't grasp the content.

Final Remark: Sometimes Professors can get F's too. To describe Abishek in a nutshell he is a proof-based textbook teacher. In his lectures he covers basic examples of concepts, only to then give you insanely hard homework assignments that are nowhere near the same level. The only way to succeed is to get a good TA and make a study group right away

HE IS TERRIBLE!!! cannot understand him. LATE to his own class!!!!! wtf?! does not know how to work a microphone. i took AP calculus and did not attend a single lecture or discussion and did fine. claims he has a curve but sets higher grading standards than the university!!!!

Professor Deshpande really cares about his students. Those who complain about him most likely did not put in the effort to do as well in the class as they would have liked. Professors who are this smart are bound to make easy subjects seem harder than they are. Go to lecture and office hours and youll be fine!

Professor Deshpande taught the basics covered in the first exam very clearly. However from then on his lectures were confusing and towards the end he started teaching Calc 2 and Calc 3 concepts which should not be in a business calc class. Handwriting can be hard to read at times.

Professor Deshpande did a solid job at teaching this course. Taught straight out of the textbook, yet reading the textbook is a good idea if you want to see a few more examples and be more prepared. He was always accessible and helpful in office hours. Practice exam was VERY helpful for our first of 3 exams. Homework is the other 15% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Deshpande does a pretty okay job at being a professor. He is pretty dry like mentioned in another post and I feel like even though he probably has a personality, he does not show it like ever. He focuses a lot on how to get to a formula when I just want to know what it is. Also, his handwriting is difficult to discern sometimes.

I preferred my high school calc teacher. I had heard that the calc teachers at Madison weren't great, but I never realized they were "nasty". I think the only reason I was ok in this class was because I already had a lot of knowledge in calculus (and it was still pretty tough). Hopefully he starts taking his critiques more seriously.

The lectures are extremely dry and he goes too fast. His handwriting can be difficult to read and his accent is a little confusing. The worst part is that 85% of your grade is based on tests. However, he does post practice exams that have a "similar flavor" to the actual exam; however no answer key is posted. Overall just OK.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He sucks
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Abhishek "is this clear" Deshpande. If you take this guy for a math class, you'll hear this phrase around 25 times a lecture. Even this man's handwriting has an accent. You're better off watching a 10 minute youtube video than you are by attending a lecture.

Literally taught straight out of the book, even every single example he used in class. Claimed that it wasn't a proofs class, then put them on the exam. Asked the class questions, told you that you're wrong, then rephrased your answer as correct. Skip lecture, just read and do homework.

I really liked Prof. Deshpande's Math class. The material covered was pretty theoretical but he put a lot of effort in making it interesting and relatable. The homework and exams were just about the right level for us . He was also very caring and was always available available outside class for questions and guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but not good at teaching. There are lots of proofs in homework and exams. Textbook and TA can save you. If you do the homework seriously and understand every single question, then you can survive from this course. There's a curve because I only get 80% and also get an A... He thinks we are all smart, but unfortunately, we're not...

He was not horrible. The first test was difficult and no one knew what to expect from him. Once he got a better understanding of how to present the material, it got much easier. He likes to focus on proofs which is frustrating; however, he did base his exams off the homework which made studying for proofs and other problems much easier.

For students taking this course in future - The instructor is knowledgeable, patient, and takes care to make sure students in the class understand the concepts. If you put in work, the effort would be worth it. First exam was difficult and his lectures could be better organized, yet I feel I am much better at those concepts after taking this course
Stunningly Bad. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I think university is not high school, so no one should expect spoon feeding. I found his knowledge reasonably high. He solved my doubts in office hours. His lectures were not organized as fall 2018 was his first experience of teaching.
Overall bad experience lacked knowledge on how to actually teach the class.

Every semester it seems like I've found the worst teacher at UW-Madison. But this guy was the worst. He really has no idea what he is doing. He also doesn't bother communicating with students most of the time. The entire course was proof based which made it very difficult and essentially useless.

It was his first semester here and I think his first semester teaching so I'm giving him a 2 solely on that. He will ask the class questions on new material and won't give up until someone answers. He does not understand that this isn't a proof-based course. Just wasted time and was not clear what the exams were going to be like. Avoid him.

He is a new professor who is obviously intelligent, but is severely out of touch with the level of explanation necessary in lecture and is often unorganized. Homework includes very few practical problems and instead has proofs that are impossible to solve without help. He is constantly improving with feedback so future years may be different
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This was his first semester here and I'm not sure if this was his first time teaching but you could tell he would just teach from the book. Repeated himself a lot and very rarely used concrete examples. He was trying his best and he seems smart, you could tell he cared. No study guides. He is nice but this class matters so I wouldn't recommend him

Abishek was the worst professor I have had since I started at Madison. His first semester teaching was Fall 2018. He expects too much out of his students. Homework is challenging and is made up largely of proofs (need chegg or slader). First exam was very hard, second was easier. Take someone else if you can.

Danny Aerts is an engineering encyclopedia. Great professor to have for this class because his expertise don't allow for any lack of effort on the students' behalves. We couldn't get away with any glossing over core engineering principles, and it made us all well versed in the material. Tough course but it was a good capstone experience.

I had Danny for lecture, and he's not a very engaging lecturer (just read the lecture slides and you'll be fine, read the book for extra help). However, I also had Danny as my lab instructor, and that was great. He is kind and very patient. The grading was fair and he graded very easily on the final lab.
The material is very straightforward, labs constitute large portion of your grade and range greatly in difficulty. Lectures are as boring as any and the book is not very useful.
Overall great guy.
Prof Aerts is not helpful and can be rude as well.

Danny is a good guy.  He's easy going and down to earth.  As a ME 368 lab instructor, everyone in our section is beyond thankful to be in his lab compared to the others.  He grades everything promptly.  Feedback is a little vague, but it's not too bad.  In other words, go Danny or go home.

Found the class very interesting. Dr. Wakai clearly is very knowledgeable on the subjects and does a good job providing just enough depth on each subject to where it feels like you're taking something away without overwhelming you. If you pay attention and review the slides the exams are pretty easy.

Nice guy. Lectures can be pretty dull, but you can tell he puts in a lot of effort. Usually brings tissue samples or medical equipment (complete with demonstrations) to every lecture.  Great survey of medical technology for pre-health students.

The class was pretty interesting. Got to learn how all the imaging equipment in the hospital works, so this class is great for pre-meds. Otherwise, the lectures were kind of boring and not that engaging.
excellent

Seemed like an interesting guy.  Many times I got the sense that he felt he had better things to do than teach this 100 level class. I found the class hard but in the end I got a B in it so I can't complain. I got my science credits and didn't kill my GPA.

GREAT CLASS!! Ackerman was excited each day to teach us about weather. He was quite funny and constantly made fun of himself. Test are very easy if you read the textbook, answer the review questions and look over notes. I would recommend the class to anyone!

Lectures were pointless because and reading the book really wasnt that helpful because the exams were hard. One thing I liked was that he gave a review sheet every exam but the multiple choice were too hard to decipher.

The material is not particularly hard, and Ackerman provides some helpful study guides before each midterm - which he then curves upward. The TA's are all very knowledgeable, but if you choose to take the lab section, pick Hester (hands down the best). Ackerman gives little in-class assignments, but they are graded on completion. GREAT CLASS.

The class was fairly easy as long as you attend lecture and read the material. The exams were straight forward and the prof isn't mean or boring. The TA seems a little off but besides that the course is pretty good for a science class. And a lot is done on learn @ uw such as quizzes and slides are posted.

Ackerman himself is a very enthusiastic professor and shows obvious interest in the subject.  His lectures don't really prepare you for his tough multiple choice tests, however he does take 3 of top 4 tests.  Reading the book is a MUST to get a good grade.  The 1 credit discussion is NOT WORTH the extra work.

This class was very hard. Prof Ackerman was NOT available outside of class. He didn't care about the class. VERY hard to pull off a good grade in this class because the multiple choice exams were very challenging.

Steve is a great, enthusiastic professor. It's a college course, of course there are homework and exams that are meant to challenge you. Never felt he or the exams were unreasonable. Great freshmen/sophomore class.

Horrible lectures that were extremely boring, but attendance was effectively mandatory due to stupid in-class, randomly done assignments. One example is when he decided to make us draw a face and turn it in for credit. He is never available outside of class, but the biggest flaw is how disorganized and chaotic the class is. By no means an easy A

The class wasn't as easy as everyone made it seem.  However, if you take some time reading the book, you can pull of a very good grade.  He tends to stay on topics that are really unimportant with respect to the tests.  I highly recommend reading the book and highlighting and or taking notes from it.  It's really the only way you can keep up.

tests not so easy. he spends about 40% of each lecture doing pointless in class exercises and wasting student's time.  it is not worth your tuition dollars to take this class. he is not available out of class and does not care about this class.  for the amount of money we pay for these classes it is unacceptable that he is not available to students
Too much for a 100 level class. His multiple choice are difficult and confusing at times. His TAs are very rude and not helpful.

Steve Ackerman is the man. This has been my absolute favorite class at UW. He does an amazing job incorporating humor into the lecture to keep things interesting. Four exams total in which you take your top three scores. All are pretty easy (36 MC and 2 short answer). I would highly recommend this class to anyone who needs a phys. science credit.
Very enthusiastic.
Awesome Professor! Class was well organized and fun to attend. Best professor I have ever had in college. Great college experience
VERY unorganized lectures. Most of the test material comes from the book but some is from lecture. You have to work in this class if you want a good grade. Interesting class overall.

Class requires work.  Not as easy as everyone said. Unorganized lectures.  The textbook helps a ton for clarity. Lots of easy in class assignments and homework help your grade but make attendence necessary.  Steve seems like a great guy, but he's not helpful to outside of class.  TA's are helpful. The 1 credit discussion is a lot of extra work.

Steve is awesome! He's a little spacey sometimes but he makes lecture interesting. He really cares about students getting good grades though, and lets you drop the final. There are a lot of in-class assignments (SUPER easy) and little online quizzes but you can use you book and they really help boost your grade. REALLY EASY PHYSICAL SCIENCE CREDIT!

Steve is a very confusing lecturer and going to lecture is not helpful (except for the pointless in-class assignments). He knows his stuff but gets confused when he tries to explain it to an entire class. His tests are tough, but he wrote the textbook, so read it to help you on the test. He likes to spring homework on you so check Learn@UW OFTEN!

This class was not hard at all. very straight forward. He wrote the book, so its all pretty much in there. a good lecturer, and a funny guy, you dont have to go to class to get an A, but I enjoyed it.

Ackerman tries to make the class fun, but winds up just wasting your time with clapping and useless in class activities. Pretty easy, but so frustrating! The TA's know it all, and the prof is constantly making errors during lecture.

very disorganized class...he is basically a stand up comedian but he tells you nothing in class that you need to know for the test. Never gave a syllabus, assignments are randomly given, it is a class designed for freshman with little structure and no required thinking. not too easy either.

Going to lecture is pointless except for the in class activities he randomly gives.  On-line quizzes are easy.  Tests are hard- tells you what to focus on, but what he tells you is not on the test.  Thought this would be an easy A or B- it is not.  Do not take this class if you are just looking for science credit- there are better/easier classes.

The class is pretty much an easy AB if you show up to lecture and do some reading. Ackerman is an enthusiastic, down to earth guy that somehow I would trust with anything even though I've never talked to him 1 on 1 before. He just gives off that kind of vibe. If you can take a class with this guy, do it.

This class rocked and Steve rocked! You had to read the textbook to get an A, but that really isn't much to ask. It was important to go to lecture, but you'll want to go because he is so interesting He tells stories about his wife and daughters and is really entertaining. He was really helpful and there was extra credit. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH STEVE!

Not an easy A, but it's definetly reachable. Class attendance is important because he gives random, easy in-class assignments. 7 or 8 easy homework assignments. There are relatively few points, so getting stuff in on time is important. He has incredible enthusiasm for teaching, which makes the class more interesting. His book is pretty helpful.

Never knew what he was going to cover in class, however what he did cover was explained clearly, and he answered all in-class questions immediately.  Read the book on the material he covered in lecture and it's a pretty easy class.  Review sessions are very helpful too.

He is ALL over the place with his lecture.  It's pretty much a waste of time to go because nothing that he says really makes sense. But he does random give in-class assignments so you really can't skip class.  We spent two lectures looking at smiley faces that people drew - waste of time!  An A or A/B is possible, but you do have to study hard!

Ackerman is very entertaining, but is all over the place when it comes to lecture.  Since we use a textbook he co-wrote, read the book before you come to class to try to help with his disorganization.  Overall, OK class.

I wouldn't say it's an automatically easy class, but you definitely have chances to do well. Ackerman is funny and interesting, and he loves what he teaches. If you're confused, you have several knowledgable TAs to help you understand. Go to the review sessions before the exams and read the book!

I don't blame the guy for trying, but his enthusiasm almost detracts from learning. I couldn't take notes worth the paper they were written on. He is knowledgeable but very scattered in lecture. It didn't help that I wasn't that interested in the subject matter.
while I agree that berazow is a good TA, if you really want to know your stuff go see Brian Kaplan, best AOS 100 TA in madison
No Comments

Enjoyed the class, was obviously interested in what he was teaching.  First exam was easy, and then it all goes downhill from there.  Has some trouble explaining himself sometimes.  Did not enjoy the fact that he added more assigned readings after the last day of his class.  Should not screw his students over like that.

He is a really nice guy but the class isn't easy by any means. Its doable but you definitely have to work hard if you want a good grade. I would say easy to get a B but more difficult to get an A. But reading the responses on rate myprofessor before i took the class, a few people just said how great he was and didn't really specify that it was hard
The kind of guy you would love to have as an uncle.  He's awesome, his class is really boring though.  He knows his stuff (he wrote our textbook).

Steve is a great lecturer because he makes the material interesting.  His style works to keep you attention.  However, the power lectures sometimes feel too long.  Beware, he gives in class assignments!
Swell guy. Loves his job.

Makes the class really interesting, and doesn't get too in depth about anything.  No math either, which makes it a really good class to fill your science requirements for non-science majors.  He's really funny and entertaining, too.
He was an excellent and energetic professor!
Fun!  Made an interesting class and steered my studies into environmental science.  An easy "A" as well, which is always a plus.
One of my favorite professors! Extremely interesting and funny --but knowledgable as well!!
No Comments
Weather and Climate was the easiest class
Offers plenty of Extra Credit
very entertaining lecturer.  tests are very fair!
lectures are boring and the TAs suck, but he offers a lot of extra credit that really helps. the tests are kinda hard, but if u do extra credit its easy to get an A
Never there. Funny. TAs sucked, and he knew it but still didn't show up to class.

I had him in a different semester than the rest of these comments and he was very helpful and professional, and maybe missed one lecture the entire semester.  He makes class worth going to with his experiments and overall fun.  By far my favorite professor thus far.
No Comments

Great teacher...when he was there.  By the time of first exam he had been there less than 50% of the time.  As semister progressed he got a little better but still I would say less than 70% of the time he was there. The TA's could not teach for their life.  People would leave if he was not there.
The guy used to do stand up comedy...what more do I need to say.  If you need an easy science course and your normally don't like science, take this class, it makes the weather interesting.

Great Professor.  Very Peppy.  Was hardly there this semester though which made it kind of hard and his TA's suck.  Lenient curve so that helps.  Extra credit opportunites.  Would recommend him, but don't count on him being there more than half the time.
Funny and Peppy
Very nice peppy guy! It's very helpful that he wrote his own text book. That way you could study right out of the book! But this semester he was hardly here.. His TA's SUCK
horrible teacher. if you're going to teach a course, it'd be nice to show up. the TA's are incompetent. don't ever take this class with ackerman.
He's awesome!
HE IS THE BEST PROF. EVER! He made things easy to understand with fascinating demos and was really funny! A great guy and I'd definitely recommend the class!

It wasn't a terrible lecture--I liked him, but I'm just not a science-oriented person, but I managed to get B's on the tests. To be fair, I'm not one of those people that overly studies, so I could have done better.
very good lecturer; tests are fairly easy
Does an excellent job of making a class on weather actually entertaining.  Fun class and the tests aren't as bad as everyone says.
He is funny
His tests have nothing to do with lecture!
you guys are insane. he constantly contradicted the book and was so high on being a cool professor he was not helpful at all.
Excellent professor.  Power lecture never seemed so short.  Tests are a little tricky, but manageable.
A brilliant prof. Really makes the subject interesting. Probably the best I had at UW.
Awesome energetic teacher, class is easy and fun!

Although Ragsdale was very awkward and uncomfortable lecturing in front of such a large group of students, he did a pretty good job of communicating information effectively and making it engaging. Evolution was an easy unit, and as long as you understood concepts, the exam was fine. No major complaints; he was a pretty average professor.
He's so enthusiastic and great!
Very nice professor and little assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ragsdale is a great professor. He is easy to reach both in lecture and during office hours. His readings for the course were interesting and relevant. All of the material was very well organized. While the grading took a bit longer than normal, that seems like it would done by the TA and not him. Overall, I would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The only professor I ever had that was nervous when giving a lecture. He often mumbles, blushes on stage and get nervous, and does not give clear definitions. He will give unclear answers, which is concerning since he is teaching evolution, which does require definitions for terms to be precise and not ambiguous. Get ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have nothing but good things to say about Professor Ragsdale. He truly cares about the success of his students and shows this by providing clear grading criteria and easily accessible (relevant!) practice quizzes.

Professor Ragsdale really cares about his students. His lecture slides were very clear on what we had to know and provided a lot of practice problems. He is a little bit of a nervous lecturer but has all good intentions. The readings for class were helpful but definitely not mandatory.

Dr. Ragsdale was a great professor! He provided many lecture quizzes covering all the content from class that was very helpful for the exam. His lectures were clear and he explained things well. Didn't think I would enjoy evolution as much as I did!
One of the best professors at UW! Class is super chill, has a steady amount of assignments 1 per class.

This class is very disorganized. His grading criterion (no rubric) was not present and not very consistent, and his instructions were super unclear. He changed the three grades in class, 'midterms', shortly before their due dates, and assigned long essays that were never graded. If you are to take a class with him, avoid annoying him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A teacher without a plan, makes you not care for the class. But he will make something out of the blue and make something due by the end of the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not recommend this professor. Tons of busy work with no correlation to projects, and brutal to mental health. Singled me out when I got sick and forced me out of group projects, resulting in an inequity among students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super cool guy. Class is engaging since it isn't your typical lecture. Minimal work in class but still a steady amount of assignments.

TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR BEFORE YOU GRADUATE!! Seriously the easiest professor I have had here and has such a kind, caring heart. He is willing to accommodate you so you achieve success in the class. Attendance is taken each class however you won't want to skip. Small journal entries is the homework for each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS GUY!!!!!! Eng155 is super weird and definitely not a typical English class but he is a really interesting guy who has figured out teaching by immersion rather than through graded assignments. I would recommend the Classical Myth FIG to anyone and I would recommend him to anyone looking for a different kind of teaching experience
Not great - does not ask very engaging questions and does not ask much from the students.

This class was nothing like expected. Being in the FIG was amazing, but the description of the class is inaccurate. He wastes time, you get nothing done, and nothing is really relevant to what I expected. Grading is laughably easy. He is a very odd man. Very disorganized; not prepared. Final was assigned the last day. Kind, but a poor teacher.

Easy but pointless class. He avoids the texts as if he hasn't read them himself. Lots of busywork with vague instructions. I enjoyed some of the plays, but don't expect for him to add anything practical in lecture.

This class was extremely easy but very unorganized. If that bothers you, then don't take it. I was always unsure of what we would do every day before I came to class. Prof Harris was very nice and helpful, and you can tell he cares a lot. Papers are easy and seldom, but you have to do a daily journal (like a paragraph) that's a little annoying.
Nice guy and very helpful.  Kind of weird, but still likable.

Easiest class I've ever had, but Ron likes to draw things out and beat them to death. Class can be boring but attendance is graded. He really wants you to do well and is very helpful, but talks about sex all the time. Very uncomfortable.
this class was very scattered, little organization. show up having done the reading (or not), participate in discussion once in a while, turn everything in, and you'll do fine.
He's kind of weird. He likes to talk about sex. His assignment are odd, but you'll do well if you make an attempt.
He assigns lots of busy work, but if you do it, you get an A.

Amos Ron is an intriguing guy, but possibly the worst professor I've ever had. He rambles on about material unrelated to class about half the time. He has given almost zero examples for Theorems and Lemmas, and his phrasing for Quiz questions are incomprehensible even for native English speakers.

His lecture material on Canvas hasn't been updated since the 90's. Many students in class often confused about assignments, grading, and material. He had no syllabus, only rambles as announcements that discussed vague grading. Lecture's often become rambles and deviate from the online material. Would not recommend at all.

Amos Ron is a very intriguing guy. It is obvious that he is quite knowledgeable in many areas beyond the topics in this course. One of the most complex grading schemas i've ever had, but it's in favor of the students. He is really funny and nice to talk to. Lectures get quite difficult at a point, and the exams are hard but overall I learned a ton.

While the overall content is not that difficult, you will truly never know where you stand in the class. Amos's grading is very ambiguous and he curved to his liking which is somewhat stressful. He also is not the best at understanding specific questions so ask broadly about the topic and just hope he reaches is eventually.

Amos is definitely one of the most interesting professors I have met. He tells joke from time to time, most of them are really funny. The homework and quizzes are well designed so that they give you a comprehensive understanding of the materials lectured in class. Do make good use of them. He has heavy accent but bearable. Exams are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Engaging and eccentric lecturer, gives a decent amount of homework. Biggest issue was communication. Canvas was not updated with correct grades for the whole semester, confusing grading policy, failure to respond to emails, and submitted grades 3 days past grading deadline. Good professor overall, but unnecessarily stressful.

I loved this class.  I took it only to learn Matlab for later use in image processing, but I ended up learning so much, particularly about eigenvalue methods.

My only criticism is that the grading of HWs by the TA was rather arbitrary and not timely.  He started off well, but I believe he got overwhelmed.

Amos is fun and eccentric, but has a heavy accent so prepare for that. You will learn a lot, but only if you really put in the time and effort. The homework is pretty difficult, and the class avg on the midterm was 50%. Definitely make friends in this class to study with. Lots of quizzes (1 during and 1 after every lecture). Hard class overall.

Attendance is mandatory, there will be a dumb quiz everyday in class for it. What he teaches in class are too hard to follow with little to no examples to explain the algorithms. Slides he uploads for references were helpful. If you have other options to learn linear algebra, just go for it instead of taking a class with this professor.

This class introduces some fun concepts, and Prof. Ron is a very engaging and eccentric professor. You can tell he cares about what he's teaching. The projects can be very tough and time-consuming but they are totally doable. You'll have to read the lecture notes pretty often. Grading criteria were kind of loosey-goosey. I had fun though!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent lectures, Amos is funny and charismatic. He doesn't have the best organization when it comes to expectations in the class, so expect a lot of emails with critical information in them. HWs are long, and there is considerable work outside class, so you'll have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Funny, caring( willing to arrange individual OH from 7 pm to 2 am which accommodated students from different time zone). It is not an easy class, you will need to put in the work. But it is not a difficult class either, there are many rooms for improvements.

Amos is great, but you need to be committed to get good grades. Hard homeworks and take a lot of time. Exams are not too bad. If you do the work, you will be fine. Believe me, you will learn a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice, funny, and also eccentric professor. IMO his lectures are hard to follow and require more time after class to review as compared to other professor's lectures. But if you actually put in the time to study after class, you'll do great. This class makes you a better mathematician.

Amos Ron is amazing. Great dry humor, knows material, sends hilarious emails frequently. I did find it easier to email TAs outside of class though. Also, do not miss class! And take decent notes. If you go, spend time reviewing, and try to be as perfect as possible on the homework, it's an easy A. Strong grasp of linear algebra basics recommended.
Don't take any of his course! Homeworks are really tough and always cost a lot of time but no help to exams. He likes to give nonsense in the class and delay when class should be end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amos Ron is an enigma. Sometimes his teaching is brilliant and creative, and sometimes its just hard to follow. He is eccentric, rude, charismatic, and stubborn at the same time. Lectures are 75 minutes 3 days/wk. Attending class is helpful. Exams are difficult. HW is assigned biweekly and takes many hours. Hard, but will make you smarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures! If you pay attention in class, it is easy to understand materials. Also, Professor Amos is hilarious and willing to help after class. Mock exam Exams are not easy, requiring a relatively deep understanding. Don't forget to set aside at least 10 hours for the biweekly HW. Take it seriously and you are guaranteed to learn a lot.

Attend every lecture is very helpful. He is very good at explaining. If you can understand everything in the lecture, exams will be easy. There're lecture notes on the website but no practice exam. Only six homework but each takes hours. By the way, he is humorous and energetic.
Good lectures, explains things well. Provides very additional material to work with, no practice exams, additional readings, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An energetic lecturer who likes making jokes and engaging with the class. Doesn't give many opportunities for students to participate in the actual lecture, instead just powers through and gives answers where there could've been better opportunities for learning. Is really harsh on his attendance policy and is rather rude in emails.

This class was difficult, the homeworks were time consuming and the textbook offered little to no help. With that being said, I loved Professor Amos! He was funny, did a good job explaining difficult algorithms . There will be times where you curse him for having such long homeworks but at the end of it all Im a much better mathematician.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ron rocks. He knows exactly what he is talking about, and gives very accessible introduction to new concepts with examples. The key concepts were explained in an intuitive way, and attending every lecture of his will save you at least three hours of textbook reading. He is also hilarious as a person: his emails are extremely humorous.

While the only good professor for this class, Amos is far from a quality professor. He likes to ramble about nothing of importance ( 5 minutes of every class will be him rambling on how important it is he lectures to the very last minute). He explains things well, but if you don't understand, he will not explain. Homeworks are 10-15 pages biweekly

Fairly easy if you NEVER skip a single class and take EVERY homework seriously. Exams will not be like the exam but you will be fairly outstanding if you are outstanding from the beginning. As he always says: This is life, and you just get over it. I assume.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! His 412 is brilliant. Easy A for everyone
Best professor ever! Take his class! Easy A! Classes are structured in an easy-to-understand manner. Don't listen to those other comments as they aren't true.
Do not take this  class. He is horrible worst teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures and would consider Professor Ron to be one of the best. The assignments require a bit of interpretation, however, the content of lectures and homework are coincident. Lectures are mandatory, and for good reason. The homework is thorough but will only take 4-6 hours, and are assigned biweekly which is plenty of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The assignments are far too long and unhelpful on the exam& the in class explanations are very abstract & CONVOLUTED. Rarely will he walk through an actual problem. The supplementary readings are fluffed,badly organized&written in unintelligible english sometimes. There's a large #of formulas which all differ slightly&you have to memorize them all.

I apologized to the TA for handing in a 70 page homework assignment. He said, "They're all that long." This was a very, very, very hard course. I felt I learned something fundamental, but the cost was enormously high.
worst teacher ever. super rude. homework is insanely long and he doens't give much explanation. outright called a student's question stupid and pointed at the board saying 'duh!' just don't.
If you take this class with this professor, the assignments will be much longer and much harder. This does not mean you will learn the material better

Professor Amos is the worse professor I have had in my academic career.  Compared to other sections of CS412, his assignments are way harder, and his grading scheme is way worse (one 40% midterm and one 40% final). His exams are not anything like the homework we spend 20 hours on and he makes us memorize equations.  He is also incredibly rude.

This professor loves to hear himself talk and will be immensely frusterating at times. Interrupts students before they can finish asking the question, or refuse to answer it at all. Homeworks are excessively long, tests are excessively difficult, and he does a poor job of getting points across during lecture. One of the worst professors I've had.

Terrible professor.  Homeworks are insanely long.  Tests are hard.  He is always sarcastic and mocks everyone to just make you feel worse about yourself.  Squeeks and does weird things in lecture which will freak you out.  Avoid at all costs!
If you like hard concepts taught poorly by a professor and then tested on variations of the concepts for your tests as well as 10 - 12 hours a week of homework then this is the class for you.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!!! I am an electrical engineering student and was required to take CS 412.  He is horrible, the exams are hard as hell, he grades them poorly, and NO JOKE the homework assignments (there are only 6) WILL take you 20 hours per assignment.  HE SUCKS HE IS HARD THE CLASS IS BORING.

Ron is probably one of my favorite professors in the animal science department. He's so passionate about what he teaches and makes it clear what you need to know! Attending this class was always the highlight of my week.

Was recommended to take the class as a non-stem major, seemed easy at first but exams are lecture heavy so you need to go to every lecture and pay close attention if you want to do well. Probably easier for someone interested in animal science. Didn't love Ron as a professor I but respect his passion for animals.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Ron!! He's very passionate about poultry and goes into detail about everything in his slides. If you go to the lecture every day and do well in studying the material, you'll be fine. He's also very understanding, so if you need to email him about anything, don't worry, he's super chill.  Would love to take another class with him! :)

Ron is a good professor. He's been teaching this class for a long time. 4 exams. Discussion questions posted every other week. Attendance in lecture is extremely important, extra credit tophat points are given. He posts the slides and practice exams are nearly identical to the real ones. Solid class if you're looking for a biology credit.
Ron is awesome lol I love his lectures also super chill and cool prof in the Animal Sci dept.!!!!!

Ron was an amazing professor, and you could tell he was super passionate about poultry. I would recommend taking as many classes with him as possible because you literally can't fail. Even though the classes were lecture-heavy due to the nature of the course, he still kept us engaged and gave us as many breaks as he could while staying on time.

Ron is an amazing professor; he keeps you engaged throughout the entire lecture and makes sure you understand all the material. He's open to questions and has easy work to accomplish every other week or so, which is just a discussion post. If you study for the exam, you'll do great on it, and it is very straightforward.

If you want an easy biology credit with a great prof, Ron's your guy. He's been teaching this class for a long time and it shows. The exams are memorization-heavy, but the material isn't difficult and common sense if you like animals. Ron doesn't give homework outside of canvas discussions, and he's always willing to answer questions in class.

Super interesting class, no homework or final outside of attendance and super easy weekly quizzes online that discuss lecture content. Ron is one of my favorite professors and is super passionate about chickens and willing to answer questions. Got to discuss a lot of cool things about chickens and do dissections.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ron is very caring and has fun lectures! I took this class for an easier bio credit but ended up really enjoying it! Grading is based on a few discussion posts that are easy, tophat in lectures, and tests. Tests are a lot of info to remember and so can be a bit difficult, but manageable.

I signed up for this class for easy bio requirements (B.A. req), which is only partially true. Ron has no homework outside discussion questions (which is just asking your opinion), and gives you extra credit just for showing up. However, the tests are A LOT. You need to study every single slide to get an A, but it's a fair alternative to homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class. Everything on the exam is covered in lecture and you can tell Ron really cares about his class. Some memorization but everything is really interesting and explained well with great exam review sessions. He has lots of love for chickens, looking forward to taking more of his classes in the upcoming years.
Very Professional

If you don't go to lecture you are screwed. You are only graded by exams. He offers a fill-in-yourself book that you can get at the university bookstore. 10/10 recommend. It has the same information from the lecture slides.  Because of this I could listen more and write less. There is extra credit (one point per lecture via TopHat.)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found the lectures very informative yet enjoyable from day one. Although there isn't homework or essays, paying attention in lecture is what is going to make or break you in this class! Just take notes! Gives extra credit for every in class Top Hat question answered (around 1 per lecture). This will bump your grade up a few percentage points!

when i tell y'all to never take a class by this man, i mean it whole heartily. his tests are tough for no reason and is overall not a great professor. struggling and seeking help - he wont help you one bit but instead be rude to you (so kind right). when i hear his name brought up or am near his presence i want to literally gag and throw up.
I would definitely NOT recommend taking a class with Ron. He is very rude and could not care less about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron is one of my favorite professors. He is a funny, sweet and a very understanding professor. I will say, he will tell you what you don't have to memorize which I really like and find helpful.
Does not know his left from right about anything. Would not recommend his class at all. Yikes.

Seems like a nice guy but boy look again. Ron's lectures are straight forward but his tests are a different story. He will say that what he spends the most time in lecture is what will be on the tests but that is far from the truth. We studied one topic for days for it not to appear on the exam once, but stuff we don't talk is put on the exam.

Professor was super passionate about what he teaches. I enjoyed attending the lectures. Your grade consists of a couple exams and extra credit Top Hat questions. Exams were not difficult if you paid attention and went to lecture. Oftentimes he would tell you what was important to know. Overall, one of my favorite classes.
Really nice guy. Lectures are easy to follow. Make sure you go to class.

Easiest class I have taken in college, but I love animals and knew a lot before taking it. Otherwise, be prepared because it's a lot of memorization. You must attend lectures to understand, I never missed one. Lectures are not bad though. TopHat questions for extra credit. Tests on paper, they felt like a middle school bio test. Prof is a nice guy.

Ron is a very understanding proffessor. His class relys mostly on the ability to memorize and is quite test heavy. However, he provides very clear lectures as well as being able to talk outside of class. I recommend getting the lecture notes at UBS as they help take the workload off of the student by a lot. Rons lectures are easy to follow!

Ron was a great presenter to class and was very passionate about the topics. While attendance isn't mandatory, and the subject matter is fairly simple to know and understand - make sure you pay attention in lectures as often times Ron will passively tell the class the answer to an exam question, with it not in the slides.

Was a good professor, but you have to go to every lecture and listen to every word or you will not know some questions on the exams, even if you get slides sent to you. There was extra credit through tophat and you will get an A if you take good notes a memorize them.
Ron's wholesome and presents a couple slides per lecture and then allows the class to interact with the university chickens to learn about the day's topic. 10/10 recommend

Honestly don't know why this guy has 5's across the board on this website. He is no where near perfect. The good thing is he's very nice. The problem is Ron makes your life very tough in this class as you HAVE to attend lecture to get the necessary material for the exam. He says specific things in lecture that are not in the lecture slides
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kean is a very good professor. Some think the class is easy but you definitely have to work for your grade, as long as you have time to memorize and attend every lecture you will get an A. Attendance is not mandatory however you get 1 pt of extra credit for attending each lecture, which adds up to an extra 40 points. Overall fun class.

The class is only graded on 4 exams, so attending lectures is essential. Luckily, Ron is a great teacher. He is kind, and his lectures are always informative and easy to understand. The tests are fair and he does a good job of highlighting what topics will be most important. There's also extra credit questions in class and no HW besides studying.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Three 50 min lectures a week, no homework, three exams, and a final.
There is participation extra credit.
The tests are medium- hard, but they are all fair game from lectures. If you skip lectures, tests will be difficult. He gives you a study guide. 
Prof Kean is a bit monotone but also pretty funny.

Ron is a solid prof a little monotone at times but passionate as a prof. The class is only 4 exams for the entire grade so showing up to lectures is a must in order to do well in the class. Definitely a good choice for a bio credit class.

Only lectures and no discussion. Class is always interesting, and I always learn new things. If you skip class, you will have no idea what's going on, because he doesn't post the lectures online. However, he is very responsive to emails, and overall a very nice man. I recommend this class to everyone with a bio requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ron is such a nice guy and so sweet. If you take the time to meet with him and explain yourself as a student, he will be very accommodating. If you just attend lectures and really study the material, you'll be fine. If you don't do that, you will do absolutely terrible. The class is graded only on 4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kean is a really nice guy. Although some of his lectures were quite dry, his tests were always fair game and he was always very responsive to his emails. The class itself was quite interesting. If you are interested in pets take this class!

Ron was a solid choice for "non-sciencey" biological science credit. Your entire grade comes from three tests and a final (Quizlet and his practice exams will help tremendously come test time). All the lectures are pre-recorded, so you need to be disciplined and watch them on your own time. The material was pretty interesting, and EC is available!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: i'm online and essentially it's all lectures with 3 exams and a cumulative exam. he's very interested in birds lol, and his lectures all give the content needed for the exams, and USE THE PRACTICE EXAMS HE PROVIDES YOU!!!!! he reuses questions. overall pretty easy bio class, but you definitely need to study for the exams, but if you do you'll pass

This class teaches you how to raise your pet, it is one of the most interested classes in this university. I like cats and I really want to know what should I do before and after I have one. Ron provided the necessary information for me, I decided to adopt a cat in the future because of this class. It is something more crucial than the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class really requires you to be there since the lectures are not posted online and there is no textbook. But, I did find the classes mostly engaging and Ron knows a lot about animals. If you want a pet in the future, I would definitely take this class. Sometimes you may find class boring and fall asleep, so drink some caffeine before!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If science is not your thing but you need science credit, take this class! It can be incredibly boring sometimes, but all the material is very understandable unlike genetics or chemistry etc. Ron is a nice guy and the work load is manageable. No homework except studying for 3 exams and final. The exams are tricky so take time to study!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not an easy A like I expected. The class is only 3 midterms and 1 final, which does not seem too bad until You do need to attend lecture to get all the information. His exams are tricky in the sense that the T/F questions really get you. Yes there is extra credit but it does not bump you up that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is all lectures and it's all on you to know the information. Ron is a great professor who is very knowledgeable although he does get a little dry at times. So yeah, you MIGHT fall asleep, I sure did a few times. You are only graded via 3 midterms and 1 final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ron is great! ANSCI200 is 100% worth it to get a quick bio credit. Don't buy the textbook, everything you need to know is in his lectures which means you absolutely have to go to class or get the notes from someone else. When you take notes you're basically making your own textbook. Tests aren't too bad if you study and the material is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Kean's AnSci200 is a great class to take for Biological Science credits. The class is clear, interesting, and there is no homework but studying for tests. To pass this class and get a good grade all you have to do is come to class, take notes, and study for the test. He also offers up to 5% of your overall grade in extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is not A EASY A. I am sure about it. You have to study hard. If you are looking for an easy A. You should not pick this class. RONALD is a good person, you can feel he really love animals. If you are interested in this topic, you should go. He knows a lot about animals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't show up to lecture, which I don't exactly condone -- all test material is taken right from it. The textbook is literally just his slides (he wrote it). Do go to the review sessions though; they really helped!!! Ron is lots of fun and the class is a hoot. Big lecture hall though.
Ron is very passionate about animal science, and is obsessed with birds. An sci 200 is a fairly easy class and his lectures are always interesting, especially those about birds.
Really good class and professor. Easy and fun bio credits.

Good professor, definitely a good class to take if you need a bio credit. No homework or reading, but you should go to lecture. If you go to class and study a little exams pretty easy. Not clap for credit easy,  but easy. Extra credit oppurtunities if you go to class, which can be a grade booster if you botched one of the exams. Funny guy too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ron's awesome! Goofy guy and class is pretty straight forward. Go to lecture, take notes, study before test, and you're good. No homework or discussion; it's a pretty chill and interesting class. TopHat points at lecture are extra credit and the "textbook" is his lecture slides, very convenient.
Awesome

the book has all the slide information on it, has extra credit clicker points if you go to class. you do have to study for the test, but not a whole lot. not a clap for credit class but still not difficult to get an A in the course with little effort

I first had Ron for An Sci 200 and loved his class so I took his An Sci 375 Exploring Poultry course and I can't recommend it enough! Ron clearly is passionate about poultry and somehow he managed to make learning about poultry really exciting. His class is also super easy with no homework, just easy quizzes. Can't recommend this class enough!

If you need bio credits, take this class. There are no readings or homework, and the exams are easy if you go to lecture. Although he can be a bit quirky (he really loves poultry), Ron is knowledgeable, nice and surprisingly funny. He also offers up to five percent extra credit for going to lecture. Seriously, take this class.

Nice guy that is very well organized and helpful. Good professor overall, but tests are pretty hard unless you have background knowledge in the topic. Good extra credit opportunities though. There is a text book that outlines the lecture slides almost exactly, however you could take notes without it and be fine
This professor does everything to make sure that his students understand the subject and everything to assure that they get an A. He is an all-around great professor!!!

First day of class I thought, dang he's monotone and super obsessed with poultry, this is going to be a loooong year. But I ended up loving his quirky personality. Kean is straightforward as can be. He literally tells you in lecture exactly what is important and exactly what you don't need to know.  Plus you learn about cute pets. easy bio credit.

I took this class because I thought it would be an easy A, but the tests are so specific and I ended up with a worse grade than I had hoped for. Kind of a funny class, I say go for it and take it if you don't mind learning about quirky animals and remembering the specifics about them.

My favorite professor so far!  The book is a composition of his powerpoint slides, but he mentions 'big ideas' in class that WILL be on the tests.  Every iclicker question you answer is an extra credit point even if your answer is wrong! (about 50 points in a semester!)  If you love pets, Ron loves to teach about them!!  Highly recommend him!

The class was very straight-forward and not terribly hard. Class is optional, but he talks about things that aren't always in the book, and that's what usually ends up on the exams. No homework, only 4 exams. Clicker questions everyday that add up toward participation points.

Tests are really specific for a broad lecture. A lot of information is covered for the exams. I go to every class and pay attention and study a lot and still don't do that well. I was told this would be an easy A class, and there is no way this is an EASY A class. Also, sooooooooooo far away. :( I would never recommend this class to anyone ever.

I don't understand why people are complaining about this class. Yes, it is necessary to attend class because he throws in comments that will be on the test, but he usually makes it very clear that what he's adding is important. I studied for about 1.5 hours for each test and got a 95+ on each one. Kean is approachable and interested in the material
Very nice professor!

Professor Kean is pretty awesome. The textbook is a book of his PowerPoint slides which is great. Al you really have to do is show up, pay attention and write his blurbs. There is extra credit opportunity too
The textbook is a book of notes that he put together. Still recommended you get it, because he goes through the notes pretty fast.

Great Class for a broad look at animals. Pretty simple if you attend lecture and keep up with the notes. No homework just three exams and a final and extra credit clicker questions. Would recommend for anyone with an interest in animals and for people who need a science credit.

This class is NOT easy. I enrolled because I thought it was an easy A...wrong. You have to memorize the entire book. Kean reads the book off his slides, and will add only 1 or 2 comments per lecture so that if you weren't there to hear that little blurb, you're screwed because it's bound to be on the test. This class is only for science majors.

This class was really easy. i would've gotten a better grade if I had gone to class more. Most of the lectures are in your book, which makes this class practically a walk in the park. Ron is a little pretentious, but the topic of the class makes up for it.

Ron's lectures were kind of dry and came straight from the book, but the material was often very interesting and the classes were worth going to for the pictures and added comments. There are 3 exams and if you go to class and know the main points well, the exams are not that difficult

Ron is a little corny and awkward but he clearly loves animals (mainly birds). His textbook is basically his lecture slides so if you can buy a used one you're set. Exams are a bit tricky since he likes short answers that actually require lots of memorization. He'll give you past exams to study from though.

I was told this was an easy A, but failed the course, allong with most of my friends who attended every class. The lectures are extremely boring and broad, but tests are specific. The lecture is read straight from the book/slides. Dont expect a response if you email him. I do not reccommend this class to anybody unless you plan on being a vet.

Really fun class. I enjoyed almost all of the material we learned about. I would highly suggest going to lecture, for he adds in crucial information that is not included in the book. Prof. Kean can be a little dry at times, but he tries to liven up lectures as much as possible. Definitely a good class to take!

if you spend hours studying the material, and attend every lecture this class is still very very difficult. need to be capable of memorizing minute detail to get good grades, if you have a photographic memory you are set, otherwise avoid this class. expects students to have uncanny memory.
this prof is extremely monotone, if you study though, you can probably get an A. need to really memorize all the minute details that are part of biology so if you like bio, take this class
nice guy. The exams are filled with tiny facts that you won't think are important enough to study. This class isn't an easy A. No outside work just 3 exams

I was told this class was easy. I was lied to. It's much harder than you'd expect. There is a ton of random information to know. The textbook is just a compilation of his lecture notes. Ron is a decent lecturer but is rather mono-toned. SORRY BUT THIS CLASS IS NOT AN EASY A.

If you love animals you will love this class. You have to be an idiot to get anything lower than an A in this class, you really do. It's NOT hard, but a simple re-reading of the notes will get you a nearly perfect grade. Ron is great at answering questions and interested in engaging in further discussion if you are. Awesome class!
If you show up to class and pay attention, you will get a good grade.  Ron Kean is very easy going and knows it's a blow off class just as much as we do.  I highly recommend taking it.

Biology and Appreciation of Companion Animals: Very easy class. The book is made of the lecture notes. You could probably not attend class all semester and still get an A. Exam was harder than what was put online but not too bad. Extra credit option. Lots of the info is common sense but he provides other interesting info and shows pictures as well.

It is a very easy course if you put in time to study for exams, but they are much more difficult than you'd expect.  I'd say half the class showed up on any given day, but most exam questions are right from lecture.  There is no homework. Ron is nice and very helpful and really knows a lot. The material is totally useless. Good for bio credit.
Ron Kean is awesome, easy A class, pretty much all the stupid athletes are there
the tests are WAY harder than they ever need to be. i studied all the time went to every lecture and still got a c in the class, and i usually get pretty good grades.

very easy class, easy exams.  Come on, the football team is in there!  I rarely went to lecture and NEVER studied and got the easiest A of my career.  Ron is very helpful also, answers all questions (no matter how obvious) and covers topics people ask him to.
Ron is the coolest, cutest man ever. His jokes are hilarious. I know know all about ferrots and i love Ron Kean.
Class is sooooo boring. Oh my GOD I wanted to die sitting in that class. Tests are picky and dumb as hell. The class is useless.
Very nice guy, kind of awkward, but in a cute way.  Tests are picky, but class is interesting and fun.
He's a nice guy and loves his job. Go to class and the tests won't be hard
Pretty boring class
No Comments

Very Boring...take a nap before hand or you WILL fall asleep. He does make the best effort to make it interesting though..guest lectures are worst. exams are based on lecture, so take good notes and study everything...if you don't you won't do so hot on the exams.
Really easy class.  Have to study for tests but everything from lecture.  Good class to take.
BORING.
The class was much harder than I figured, but Ron did his best to make the lectures interesting. Don't blow off the lectures, the tests are challenging.
The class is pretty easy and there are good opportunities for extra credit.  Just don't think that you can completely blow off the class, the tests can be a little challenging.
Raising Sea Monkeys is probably more entertaining than this class...Review sessions are pointless because he will not elaborate on what he is and is not going to test on.

Prof Hoskins is one of the reasons Nobel Prize is leaving academic biochem and chem towards industry companies such as google. His students struggle finding a job or even a postdoc. His lack of communication skills and his preassumptions and judgement about students along with his fear, makes him small.

One of the best professors I had in undergrad! Extra credit opportunities were available for attendance, which was nice. Tests were "unpredictable" in that anything from lectures was fair game (it was a lot of content) but also not terribly difficult as long as you put in the work. Lectures were interesting/engaging, and very relevant.

His lectures were interesting but very complicated. He did the second portion of the course which covered more difficult content and the exam averages went from 75 on the first two exams to 60 and 66 on the 3rd midterm and the final exam. Very specific things are tested, which is hard since midterms are 50 min. He was passionate about biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hoskins tries to teach but avoids giving the necessary background. I didn't expect that considering his age and experience in teaching (I think he is going to retire in like 10 years or so). He gets exhausted, and takes that frustration to himself, first, and then to the student who asks for help. Maybe he is unhappy with who he became.

Professor Hoskins is a caring and intelligent teacher. He was my favorite professor of the course. The only thing I would encourage is to watch the lectures online (if they provide them in future semesters) for the glycolysis, krebs, beta-oxidation, and urea cycle lectures instead of going to lecture in-person. They are VERY content-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Aaron is a super nice person. He cares about his students, and he clearly explains the materials really well. The exams are challenging, and it is super easy to lose points on the exams even if you study well. I didn't read the book. however, it is highly recommended for getting an A. Previous exams are helpful too, and many recycled ques
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hoskins is a great professor, who clearly cares about how well his material is reaching the students. The study guide he provides is very useful for studying for the exam, and he also takes questions from the problem sets. He does a great job teaching his section of the course. I liked his teaching much better than Professor Cox.
Dr. Hoskins is good about helping in office hours. He lectures very clearly and obviously cares about students. Exxams are fair but tough.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, really interesting material. Would take again.

Hoskins did a good job. Everything is based off the lecture slides, unlike Cox, so make sure you go to review lecture. 507 is one of the hardest classes at Madison. There is an insane amount to memorize and Hoskins does a decent job presenting the material. I've had better teachers, but he did a good job.

Well, what can I say... this class is hard. They expect you to know a lot of material, more so than what they elaborate on in lecture, so be prepared to do extra work outside of class. I thought Hoskins was okay. I just wish they would explain how to do certain problems and ask more clear questions.

Aaron Hoskins is a fabulous professor. His lectures are crystal clear and, although he's not the most animated lecturer on campus, he genuinely tries to keep things interesting by throwing in fun little references and factoids into his PowerPoints. Would highly recommend taking his class.

The entire semester is group project based and you are with the same group for the whole semester. If you get a bad group the class can be very difficult but doable. Ron's lectures are slow, but contain good information. He is available outside of class every week for online office hours which is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class sucks. Ron is a good guy, but basically if you get a bad group in this class you are screwed cuz you spend the entire semester working with them. You consult for a real business and try to come up with solutions for their issues. Ron was a very nice grader and very understanding of issues with the group and the business.

Ron is a cool guy, his lectures are kind of boring as they are mainly reading off the slides, but he is a master in his field of knowledge and it really shows. His expectations and course guide are very clear and helpful so you can complete things on time. The first half project is confusing at first but he answered my questions to clarify.
he is good teacher and helpful

Yes his lectures are very boring, but the material is very relevant. Random groups for the main project, but my group was amazing and creating a brand was so fun. He's an easier grader and there are opportunities for extra credit. Not my fav class but definitely not the worst considering i almost got a 100 percent in it lol
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took CNSR SCI 567 with Ron and the course content was really interesting but the way he presented it was definitely not. Lecture attendance was mandatory but he just read off of the posted lecture slides verbatim. He did not do a great job explaining assignment expectations which left students confused. However, he is very knowledgable.
SOOOOO BORING. SOSOSOSOSO Boring
Super boring lectures but a nice guy. This whole class is a group project so if you have a good group you'll be better off.

Prof. Rock-Singer recognizes students are human and have a lot on their plate. I probably made his life as a professor difficult by having spotty attendance/ turning in things late. Yet, he still acknowledged my effort. I ended up with a B though I honestly probably deserved a BC/C. Grades are not his God and I really respect that about him.
Prof Rock-Singer is kind and compassionate. His lectures are clear, and his knowledge is amazing! The students who have trouble in his class generally just don't want to work hard.

Somehow expects you to understand everything from dense readings before class. Uses lecture time as a way-too-fast review session w/ poorly made slides that don't help you in any way. Says tests aren't made to trick you, that's debatable. Also has an arrogance about himself that rubs you the wrong way. Overall, an unpleasant experience.

I think this professor's ivy league pedigree and big passion into 'salafism' says it all. He is way too concerned with power dynamics which eliminates the possibility of being able to communicate properly and develop any sort of relationship. Not very clear with format of midterms ahead of time, doesn't set up test taker for success.

Prof. Rock-Singer was a really good professor and a great person to work with in general. Only two tests, the content was complex and at times difficult, and the readings personally buried me however, he was super understanding if you ever had a problem. Explained everything pretty well, available to students, would recommend him as a prof.!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Rock-Singer is very passionate about the content he teaches which makes his lectures very enjoyable. He is a fair, if not generous, grader and really cares about his students and their success. Only gripes are that you're graded on very few things and that he doesn't update Canvas. That being said, he is still one of my favorite professors.

Very engaging and passion. He covers issues in a fair a balanced way that leaves the student with the opportunity to form opinions. If you come to lecture ready to learn, he will not leave you wanting. Overall and amazing professor

First of all, one of the smartest professors I've ever met, he's young, but his CV speaks for itself, UW is insanely lucky to have him on the staff. Second, he's engaging, critical, knows how to bring the best out of everyone, will make you a better writer, and is overall just a good guy. You'd be really lucky to have him as a professor.
Prof. Rock-Singer's teaching makes history fun. He is serious about work, but also very thoughtful and caring. You won't regret taking his class!

He is a great professor. He is ver passionate about Islamic History and make the lectures really fun. He really tries to know his students and incorporate fun activities in the lectures which makes it more interesting and helps you understand the concept. His exams are mostly writing but if you study well you will definitely do good.
I mean, Prof.Noyce should definitely learn from Prof.Ahn about how to teaching students. She is no doubt one of the best lectuers in UW-Madison
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I've had! She presents lecture material well and is very personable overall. Exams can be hard so make sure you comprehend material well.
This is the best class I have taken in the Civil and Enviranmental Engineering. It should be the template class for all lecturers!

Absolutely great professor, I loved her lectures so much and she got me into transportation as a whole. Tests weren't impossible, lectures were recorded, extra credit was given, literally everything was there for you to succeed and she very clearly loves what she does. Highly recommend!

Sue is very friendly and understanding. Civil Engr 370 is not super difficult in terms of content, but the exams are relatively difficult and not easy when it comes to timing. The more practice you do, the better you will do in the class. Pretty easy to get a B in the class, but if you want an A or an AB you will need to work for it. E

Pretty straightforward material and is generous with grading exams and homework. Lab is essentially a discussion and Sue wants you to do well in the class. Quizzes are short and only based on lecture material for concepts. Exams can be difficult still, so be prepared.

Wanted you to do well in her course and was accessible outside of class. Had a fantastic TA and clear grading scheme. Generous grading on quizzes and gave extra credit quizzes. Material was clear and comprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Classes not hard but you can learn a lot. Mercy homework grading but very clear feedback. Exams could be a little challenging but you Would hardly miss any point if pay attention in class and do homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ahn was great. She answered questions very clearly and had interesting, understandable lectures. While there's a lot of homework, none of it was busy work and all of it further built on what we learned in class. I'm so excited to have her again next semester!

Professor Ahn was so much fun. She is clearly very knowledgeable and makes her lecture easy to follow. She uses Korean and English in her lectures so it is always easy to understand what is going on. She is also very easy to contact outside of class and was very understanding of me. I will be taking more classes with her for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is the best! The class is really fun if you are interested in learning Korean. The way she teach or the TAs is very helpful and understanding, you just have to put some effort for the quizzes which is based on the vocabulary you take during lecture. Overall, the class worth it. I would definitely take another class with Professor Ahn !

I love Professor Ahn! She's super caring, makes lectures interesting and engaging, and really listens to feedback. Korean can be pretty difficult, but Professor Ahn made it fun and easy to understand. I hope I can take another course with her again soon!

Professor Ahn is incredible! I enjoyed her lectures and she's always so kind and understanding! TAs were also awesome! Definitely should attend lectures as the notes are pretty important but as long as you attend lectures, discussions, do the homework assigned, and review your notes, you should be fine! Would take a course with her again!
An amazing Korean professor. Notes are well organized, and quizzes and tests aren't too difficult. Just put in some work to learn and you're set.

Professor Ahn is a wonderful teacher!  She breaks down difficult grammer/vocab in interesting and easily digestable ways. Both TAs are very kind and helpful as well. Attendance is mandatory, but they're very understanding if something comes up. Don't take advantage of this though, as lectures are fast-paced and it's easy to get behind.
