I found the class to be fairly difficult, but Professor Jaerin is very talented at helping you understand the content and it shows in her lectures! She always brings a bright bubbly energy to class and it never fails to make my day! Lectures are a little fast-paced sometimes but other than that no complaints! TA's are very knowledgable also :)

Professor Ahn is incredibly kind and willing to help her students succeed in any way possible. She is by far the best professor I've ever had on campus and I was glad that I got to take her class in both the Fall and Spring. The workload is definitely not too much and everything is very manageable. Highly recommend!

10/10. She is very kind and sweet! Only complaint is that the TA's and Instructor do not speak at natural / daily speaking pace. I get it is a introductory course, but for those who want accelerated learning, you will learn much faster self studying.

Professor Ahn is one of my favorite professors I've had; she's very sweet and cares a lot about her student's success. Grading is based upon several different factors, so if you have one rough test or quiz, it's pretty easy to make up for it and still get a good grade. Discussion attendance is mandatory, and you can only have a few absences.

Jaerin Ahn teaches introductory Korean (2020). She's sweet, straight forward, and gives that gentle nudge rather than a slap on the wrist when you make a mistake. Class work is simple, not much is expected in ASIALANG 105, in comparison to JP or FR. She gives lecture notes +++, speaks slowly + or - depending on what you want in a language class.
Ahmad is one of the most caring professors I have had. He really works hard to help make learning Arabic less daunting of a task. He is funny and keeps the class energetic and enjoyable.

I really enjoyed taking Ustaad Ahmad's class this semester. You can tell that he really cares about what he teaches and he never fails to bring a lot of energy to the class. There is a lot of homework because it's an intensive language class, but you end up learning a ton of Arabic by the end of the semester. I would definitely take his class again
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He gets angry quick and it is extremely noticeable, he actually highlighted the sybllbus and spent half of the class reading it because he was angry about students emailing him because of unfair participation grades. The participation grade rubric is very unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very intelligent guy. He knows his stuff. Lectures are very interesting and I liked it a lot. More than willing to take questions and have a discussion with his students. His assigned readings matter so if you do them you'll do well. I didn't so I didn't do well but I still enjoyed his class. Exams are difficult. He doesn't give you a study guide.

Prof. Ahlquist takes a salient issue in the American psyche and asks you to think critically about the data. Coming from a poli sci background, I really enjoyed getting to look at inequality from a neutral position and then check in to see how the data affected my view of the world. You can tell he has a passion for the subject.
Yay for Prof Ahlquist!! Challenging material, but if you work for it, you should know the material by the end of semester. Also, prof Ahlquist is always willing to help you understand more.

One of my favorite professors.  His lectures can get confusing because he uses a lot of math to explain but he will gladly slow down to re-explain things and take questions. Also very helpful in office hours. Read his textbook. One of the few professor where his readings are actually helpful. I was challenged but I feel I learned something new.

Good professor. Appears a little difficult to approach but very willing to talk during office hours or after class. Very clear expectations and well executed explanations of US Inequality. It's pretty clear which side of the spectrum he falls on (left) but the class did not seem terribly biased.
He's a very clear and knowledgable professor. He helps make interesting subject matter more interesting.

Ahna is a great professor! She genuinely cares about her students and is beyond helpful. In my honest opinion, probably one of the best faculty members in the genetics department. And as a bonus, she likes to bring in snacks for class. Take genetics 564, you won't regret it!
She is super nice and her classes are one of the most interesting classes I have ever had. Her presentations and explanations are pretty clear.
Ahna is the nicest professor I've ever had.
No Comments
No Comments
Very good professor. A bit hard to understand at times, but writes very clearly on board. Lecturers aren't required but help immensely in understanding the material.

He is one of the best professors I've had. His classes are at a great pace and he writes very neatly on the board. Math isn't my strong suit but I didn't find this class challenging because of the professor. I would definitely recommend him!
Really nice prof, and is very open to questions.  He takes his time explaining things and writes really clearly -- best handwriting I've ever seen for a prof.
Excellent notes, very helpful. Some accent.
Excellent notes, very accessible and helping professor - always ready and eager to help
Cool and awesome

He's hard to understand and goes through lecture slides really fast.  I found it best to look at slides before class, take notes, and then take more in class.  Exam is difficult, but if you go to his review session and study A LOT, you can get an A
Excellent teacher; knows his subject. Only problem is accent (sometimes).
Lectures are straight out of the book, he reads off the slides, no point in going, just study the slides and memorize them to get an A

He was not a very good professor at all. Read directly from the slides and was a very boring lecturer overall. You would ask him questions in the review and instead of answering them he'd just say "Oh, you don't need to know that."

Aight, here's the deal... this guy teaches very poorly. going to lecture is worthless because they're posted on the website, and he doesn't say much more than what's written on the slides. his exam is very easy! you get to write on a note card, and his exam comes directly from the lecutures. take the class, don't go, and ace it.
Powerpoints are identical to book material.  Makes the subject dull, and is hard to understand because of accent.  Tests are very hard, even if you study.

His exam was extremely specific and his review session was a joke.  His lectures were simply him reading from powerpoint and he was very difficult to understand when he didn't read from them.  One must rely heavily on the book and know most of the material on his slides.
He gave excellent notes and is a good teacher. However, reads too much from powerpoint directly.
No Comments
AF 703 is one of the best class I took in UW-Madison. Professor Agoke is excellent at showing the step by step process of teaching methods. Her class is one of the best.

Class is based on discussion and class participation. Adeola is a sweet, caring, and intelligent woman I loved her as a professor! She explains each discussion topic in class so discussion/debate was always in-depth. The final is a research paper, was not hard at all and we worked on it throughout the semester. Overall the class is super insightful

Dr. Adeola has to be one of my favorite professors at UW-Madison hands down. She really wants to help you become a better writer, and offers great feedback. She also comes to class with a smile which creates a welcoming vibe. I have developed my critical thinking and communication skills while taking this class and have learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: More than any other course I have taken at UW-Madison, this class made me a better student and person. Dr. Agoke genuinely cares about her students and wants them to learn and succeed. Participation is mandatory but she is understanding and assists you if it is difficult for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Participating in class is necessary in order to succeed. Adeola makes it clear what she does and does not like so you can take that information going forward with papers. She obviously cares about the class and tries to make it engaging but there is not always much to discuss from the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Adeola was my favorite professor at UW, and I'm a senior so that's a huge compliment! She is CARING and compassionate. She expects students to engage in the course content, and if you don't participate or do the readings, you will get nothing from the class. I would recommend her to anyone. Daily discussions, 1 big research paper, attendance is key

It's clear Prof. Schmidt knows her stuff about H.C. Andersen and she conveys her enthusiasm to students. That being said, the class themes seemed to repeat and lectures got boring fast; I spent a lot of time on Twitter. If you show up to most lectures and do the reading you should get at least a B.
Very condescending to students. Not very helpful or responsive.

Very enthusiastic about the subject and pretty clear for being a lit prof! Lays out in simple terms what the meaning of each story is. No essays, no participation grade, just exams. Expect to write a lot on the exams.
Nete is incredibly helpful and awesome. She's one of the best teacher's that I've had at Madison and I loved how enthusiastic and nice she was.

I had her for Lit Trans 275 last semester and I have her now for Lit Trans 324.  She is the sweetest lady ever and she is very knowledgable.  She truely loves what she does and is very willing to help.

I got an A but it wasnt as easy as I would have predicted. Class is not curved but questions on exams can be tough. Exams are graded by TA's so talk to her about them afterward and she will award you extra points. Very nice teacher.
easy prof. read the book and you will get an AB at least. no need to go to class.

Her class consists almost entirely of guest lectures, most of which are quite interesting. If you have any interest in Scandinavian culture or history, I highly recommend this class. There was only one graded assignment all year, a book report on a novel. There are two midterms that she graded pretty harshly, just make sure to study a lot!

She is a really nice lady, but she only lectures like 3 times over the semester.  A guest lecturer on a different topic every day, with readings for each.  Read one book and write a 2 page book report, one midterm (short answer and essay), and one final. It's a lot of info to take in, but study and you'll do alright. Wish she would teach more tho!

Probably one of the easiest classes you'll ever take. I sat in class and did crossword puzzles. Tests are really easy. She teaches a lot of history that is pretty much irrelevant. Just read the stories and you'll do fine. Comm b is like a high school english class.
Hans Christian Andersen...easy class, dont have to go to lecture, just read stories, tests easy...take for easy good grade

Her overall rating may make her look bad, but she is simply neutral/okay. I found lectures very boring and the textbook readings a drag, but she is decent. Grades are based of multiple choice quizzes and a few bluebook tests. Not hard to do well in, and she clearly is very knowledgeable, but just not an interesting class in my experience.

Tripp's lectures are very fast paced which makes it difficult to take notes, which she requires are written by hand. Doesn't slow down or explain complicated concepts. Not a great introductory teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tripp is an incredibly knowledgable person, but her lectures were simply just regurgitations of the textbook and very boring. You don't need to show up to learn the course content, but attendance is mandatory. Would recommend if you're someone who wants an easy A while shopping online in lecture, don't take it if you want to learn.

Professor Tripp is very accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. Even though she can get behind on grading, if you put in the effort you should not worry about getting good grades. She will go out of her way to help you succeed.

SKIP THE LECTURES. She just reads off a slide and regurgitates stuff from the textbook. The textbook is also pointless mostly too. If you have common sense, you can do very well in this class by reading some wikipedia and news articles.

You can tell she's super knowledgeable about the course and cares about her students, but lecture wasn't super engaging.There's 5 quizzes that are pretty easy and she gives you clear study guides for all quizzes and exams. Assignment directions can be a little confusing.  Would recommend if you like international relations, otherwise maybe not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mandatory attendance even tho she just reads off the powerpoint. The other posters are correct... she has a tendency to ramble about her life. Class isn't crazy difficult, but lecture was boring and long. 6 or 7 quizzes, and u drop the lowest score. Doesn't put in grades???? U don't know until after the final exam how u r doing in the class.

This professor is extremely boring. If you love international relations, you'll enjoy the class; if not, it may feel like naptime. It's an easy course but attendance is required. You get a basic poli sci foundation, but I wish lectures were more engaging and less focused on off-topic travel stories.

(I took PS 120 fall 2025)
Disorganized. Attendance was mandatory but in lecture when she spoke was disengaging, disjointed, non-linear, and she rambled about her own experiences, which was cool to hear, but didn't pertain to the lecture at all. My TA had no idea what they were doing and she had little communication with him. Don't recommend.

(I took PS 120 but it's not an option)
So incredibly disorganized, she constantly changed due dates and assignments
The readings were interesting but you didn't have to do them. Idk if I learned anything this whole sem
Midterm and final was writing essays but we get a notecard for final, grading isn't hard but frequent quizzes and assignments

Aili is a pretty good prof. Attendance for this class was manditory, but there wasn't a discussion either. Assignments are super light, and the 6 quizzes are super easy, and we're allowed to miss one as well. Only drawback is the 10-12 page research paper due before thanksgiving, but we do get to choose the paper topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Tripp definitely knows what she's talking about, however, she's much more of an academic than a teacher. Unclear expectations, you basically have no grade until the last week of class. Lectures are incredibly statistic-heavy and can be very unengaging. Wouldn't recommend.

I don't agree with the majority of these negative reviews. Perhaps Prof. Tripp changed her teaching methods from student feedback, but we definitely used the textbooks and changes to the syllabus were well-communicated. Prof. Tripp is incredibly educated, experienced, and well-connected. Her lectures were bursting with knowledge. I loved this class

This class was the most unorganized class I have ever taken on campus. We frequently had due dates changed last minute or sprung on us last minute. She is passionate about the material but does not know how to convey it in a way that makes sense or flows from lecture to lecture. I can honestly say I wish I never took this class.

Attendance is not technically part of the grade, but the class is small and she KNOWS when you are not there. Show up, or you will lose her respect. Her class and research are fascinating and the class is not difficult if you show up and do the readings. She can be a confusing communicator at times, but her passion makes the class well worth it.

This "Women in Politics" class sounded interesting going into it, and Tripp is such a nice person, however her lecture style is unbearable and boring. Do not buy any textbooks, they are unnecessary as exams only cover lecture material. 4 quizzes, 2 take home essay exams, 1 8-10 pg research paper, participation and attendance counted in grade.

Most worthless course I have taken as a PS major at UW. No direction, completely unstructured and you learn nothing (besides about her own personal accomplishments). On the bright side, easy A if you have prior knowledge. But don't take this class if you want to learn anything or feel like there was some reason you went to class.

Professor Tripp knows a lot about this field, she was especially great with quotas and women in legislature, but outside of that she isn't great at teaching the other material.  Interesting stuff but class sometimes was pointless when she'd ramble.  Assigned about 800 pgs of reading the last month of class.  Took attendance to force us there.
Do not take this course with her, you won't learn much at all. Lectures are extremely scattered and really elementary level.

A nice, friendly woman. Lectures are okay,sometimes a little scattered. Overall the class is easy, easier than I would have liked for a 600 level course. Material is pretty elementary and doesn't dig too deeply. Exams are essay take-home and not difficult if you do the readings and pay attention.
Terrible lecturer. Does not convey information well. She seems like she knows what she is talking about though. Gets easily distracted and flustered.

Horrible. The class should have been great, but her lectures are incomprehensible. She is a very nice lady, and she really means well, and she is a great writer, but she just cannot lecture.  She also gets very upset when students need clarity on a concept or when students are trying to discuss class problems. Never again.

Unless you've studied in Africa, do not take her African politics course.  You're at a strong disadvantage if you don't have an African politics background.  Lectures aren't always that clear.  Very general course - you really never get a chance to learn about specific countries...

Dr. Saatchi is super caring towards his students. If you're struggling in this class, talk to him and he will kindly help. The grading system is also super lenient because this is an introductory class. Pay attention to example problems discussed in lectures because they are the ones that will be in the exams.

Quite possibly the worst professor Ive ever had. His lectures are absolutely useless, and you will need to learn everything from the book, which is by far the most useful resource in this class. The hw and exam questions are similar, so I have to give him credit for that at least. The pace of the class is very inconsistent too.
Genuinely kind lecturer that really cares for you.

I took MSE350 over this past summer and it was all online. Although Professor Saatchi wasn't the greatest at using technology, he was always online for office hours and even got online late at night to help with difficult assignments. His lectures are boring and didn't cover the material fully. I recommend reading the textbook over the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't of much use, but he is a fair prof. If you're alright with reading and reviewing slides outside of class, he's your guy.
He is a great guy, you have to work for your grade.

Overall he is just not great at lecturing but the way the class is organized is what is really flawed. He will basically just read off power point slides that summarize the 30 page readings he expects you to do between lectures. I eventually just took notes on the slides. Homework is can be hard since very few examples are done in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Get ready to learn almost everything yourself and then go to lecture and talk about what you just read the previous night. The material isnt insane but lecture for me is nearly pointless aside from the quizzes and tophat activities.
The most boring and unmotivated educator that I have ever met

Dr. Saatchi is obviously passionate about his field and a nice guy, but unfortunately he isn't a great lecturer. He is a fair grader , but not clear in his "mini lectures" and you are forced to learn everything from the book yourself. The semester I took it, they switched it to an "active-learning" course and he didn't know how to teach that way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The living meme and legend
THE REAL WISCONSIN EXPERIENCE
Awful!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Saatchi is very hard to follow. His lectures are almost useless. I learned 80% of the material myself. Readings are insane and the quizzes can trip you up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's hard to understand while you manage to stay awake. He gives quizzes every day to see how everyone is doing, but when the average is 37% he gets mad and doesn't explain much more. The best way to pass this class is to read the book often, make sure you know how to do the homework and if that doesn't work ask specific questions.

Worst professor ever. Lectures consist of a daily quiz followed by random primitive noises, lip smacking, and mumbling as he attempts to explain the correct anwers to the quiz (with averages typically falling around 60%). After this mumblefest there are 15 min left to do 1 - 2 tophat questions, meaning no course content is ever covered.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: wow..... just wow
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures sound like he is mumbling a memoir to himself. You are much better off taking this class online with some friends so that you can cheat on all the exams.
Ahmad is a really nice guy but his lectures leave a lot to be desired. Quizzes are worth way too much of the grade, but if you do decent on them and the exams you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sure he has an accent and lectures are pretty boring, but the class isn't all that difficult and his grading scale is very generous. Also, he is very responsive to emails and accessible in office hours. The textbook isn't required, but it definitely helps.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you want a professor that explains anything and gives fair quizzes, I suggest you find someone else... terrible professor
When I tried my best reviewing everything before exam and still couldn't do well, I realize there's something else wrong besides me being stupid.
The absolute worst. If you can take this online I would recommend that option.
Honestly less useful than sleeping through his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awful, hard to understand what he is talking about

Saatchi's lectures are uninspiring in every respect; almost all information is read directly off the textbook's PowerPoint slides, and his speaking presence leaves a lot to be desired. However, I will say that he comes off as a kind person, and the grading scale allows you to neglect the class outside the weekly assignments and practice tests.
OK this is a bad class. But Prof. Saatchi has made it passable. He's helpful in office hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Saatchi's lecture style is awful. You'd be better off watching online later at 1.6 speed and skipping to the useful parts (if you can find them). On the plus side, he teaches straight from the book so you can teach yourself from the book if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very good. He knows the material well and is very helpful in office hour.

Professor Ahmad Saatchi knows his stuff and is honestly a very good teacher/explains everything in a clear manner. Please get past his kind of monotone voice (feel free to just watch the lectures at 1.4 speed). You can tell that he knows exactly what hes talking about and how to show it. Homework is fair and tests are fair, just put in the work.

It's true Dr. Saatchi's lecture is a little boring, but he is a very good instructor. He is very helpful and easy-going in office hour or if you talk with him after class, and the course itself is not that hard. You can't expect an A without any time spent on it except for copying homework from the solution manual.

These lectures are SO boring. He reads straight from the power point slides. The exams are half just memorizing vocab and the other half is memorizing how to solve the problems. The quizzes on monday mornings are ridiculous so learn how to use the "control/command f" function

His lectures consist of accented mumbling about the material in a way that's not much more helpful than the textbook. Tests and quizzes (all multiple choice) are very hard until you realize that the quiz questions are taken verbatim out of the multiple choice-type questions at the end of each chapter, and the tests are extremely similar to the practice exams he posts. Additionally, quizzes were Monday mornings at the beginning of class and were only open for 45 sec per question, so if you're late to class you'll get a terrible quiz score. Essentially, you won't learn much from him, but you can get a good grade if you can catch on quickly to how the class works. Do yourself a favor and take a professor that can teach instead. You're in college to actually learn, after all.

Very boring lecturer. Rambles through material for 50 minutes. Teaches straight from the text and reads exactly from slides. Tests were fair and heavily based on past exams. Homework was reasonable. Quizzes are taken verbatim from the end of chapter questions. Nice guy who is very fair with any personal circumstances you might have.
Hard to understand, gives impossible quizzes, doesn't fully understand what he's teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have to work hard for it, yes he might have an accent but he knows his stuff.

I took the 3-week, 3 hrs a day summer session of this because of the course's bad rep, this is the best option. Poor lecturer, thick accent, but teaches STRAIGHT from the textbook so teaching yourself from the book WILL happen. Summer class quizzes are daily and NOT ONLINE. Tests are mostly theory based. Ask around for textbook solutions, they help

First off Saatchi is an amazingly nice guy.  He really is quite accommodating to situations, and will help you in any way he can.  The main problem with him isn't really him at all, it's the class.  It's a very basic course, and you can tell that he loves this topic, but because there is so much material, he cannot focus on one subject for long.
Professor Saatchi is the worst professor I have had at UW.  He is essentially an audio book for the textbook.  You will go through this class and have no idea what you are doing the entire time.
Just a good guy
In his lab section he was great. He could be a bit ramble-y, but it was all useful information for the lab. I highly recommend Saatchi's lab section above all others
Gives time in office hours.

Saatchi is basically just a bad tour guide for the textbook. He points at a few pictures and then mumbles around for an hour. As long as you show up for the in class quizzes having done the end of chapter fill in the blank questions you will be fine. The tests are a combination of those and the practice exam. Inspirational was a joke.
Great professor, just memorize the questions because it's pretty much word for word that's on the tests.
good guy

Saatchi blunders through his lectures like a confused lemur. He mumbles and loses his train of thought with ridiculous frequency. There's no reason to go to class. The average grade is an AB and if you put in an hour or two of work before the exam you'll get an A. Exams are word for word the practice exams.

Saatchi is the worst thing to come through campus since the blizzard of '78. Definition of a joke class. Could have been interesting, but instead this dude (who is very smart, btw, just can't teach to save his life) just stands there an mumbles off slides.

He's a great guy, but his teaching style is just bad. Mumbles, writes in hard to read cursive, doesn't talk loud and is very confusing on his expectations. Although, his quizzes are straight from the book and the exams are the book's homework problems too (and he gives you the answers ahead of time).

I can't believe some of the comments here. Prof Saatchi has inspired me to go further in materials science. He was always available for deep discussions of the course material, and I actually felt that he illuminated some of the drudgery of our boring textbook. His English is a bit rusty, but his dedication and desire for us to learn was huge...

Be prepared to spend at least half of your time deciphering what Saatchi is mumbling on about in lecture. If you don't read the book, you will likely fail the course. So far, all of the quiz and exam material has been copied word for word from the book. Material science is actually an interesting subject, but this guy makes it nearly unbearable....

I took this class expecting it to be one of the more difficult ones, however; it turned out to be one of the easiest. Just read the book before lecture and do the homework assignments on a weekly basis and you'll pass with an A-B. That being said i rarely attended his class, but i did use his office hours and the TA's as well.

Very nice guy, he just can't teach. Mumbles throughout lecture. The homework expects us to know much more than what was taught, and they are not very helpful to your overall grade. Halfway through the semester, he announced that TAs are hosting review sessions every week. I learn more from those than I do from lecture; they're what saved my grade.

Based on the tags I used above, it may seem like this is a great course, but I'll be honest: Saatchi inspired me to never take a Materials Science class again. The fact that I sat through lectures three times a week was hilarious, as I didn't learn a thing in the four months of classes. The lectures amazed me as they were regurgitated PPT slides

To call Ahmad Saatchi a professor would be a gross inaccuracy.  He is more of a guide whose sole purpose is to tell you what chapter to read in the very non-descriptive textbook.  A solution manual will go a long way in this class. Best of luck, you're gunna need it...

Lectures: You may rather want to hit the bar at 8:50 on Monday morning.  Homework: Really only helpful for the quizzes. Doesn't help for preparing for exams.  Quizzes: Usually copied straight from textbook, sometimes still has the answer accidentally circled.  Exams: Buy a magic 8 ball.  Overall nice guy, cant teach

Saatchi is very clueless in this course. He is very unclear about what homework is assigned and you end up doing whole chapters anyway which take an absurd amount of time. Mumbles through power-points during lecture. The quizzes come straight from the books homework so if you memorize the answer  you can get those right. Tests are random and hard
If I could give him zeros I would. Everything said in previous reviews of him are all accurate. I go to lecture everyday and I could get a D.

He wants us to learn the material and he's trying but the man doesn't know his head from his feet. Too much homework. You have to read the book to learn anything and his quizzes range from obscure information you skipped over while studying to a copy of the homework.

Bad professor! Doesn't teach material at all. He is just awful at answering questions. Doesn't follow any sort of logical progression and expects students to memorize book. Gives insane amounts of homework and tests on very obscure and useless parts of the text. Absolutely the worst professor that I have ever had.  Just Awful.

Okay, I know he was hired after the semester started and he had to just jump in. That is fair. Since then though he does not understand how much work he assigns. This chapter 8 due had 126 questions plus 5 others. You really have to memorize the book. Many people have dropped this class. I wanted to really like this class but very disappointed...

Clueless... All the info he spits out is right from the PPT slides provided with the text. And if a student asks a question, he tells us to look in the book 50% of the time. Plus the book is useless and nearly impossible to understand. He never makes clear his expectations for HW. My only advice is do the online HW cause quizzes are based on that.

He is an awful professor. He has no idea how to teach or even what to teach. He simply reads off of the provided powerpoints and he is impossible to understand. Whatever he says the TA's say the opposite. His tests are impossible and there is tons of homework.

Saatchi may as well be a text-to-speech robot. He stands at the front of the lecture hall mumbling through powerpoint slides.  He is also not helpful when you ask questions, and often can't understand what you are asking. The TA's are just as clueless as the students as to what we should be studying or learning because of his lack of communication.

Terrible. That is the only word I can use to describe this professor. Do whatever possible to avoid any association with his teaching.  He assigns almost every single end of chapter question on a weekly basis (50-100 questions). His lectures are impossible to follow, and in no way does he prepare you for his impossible tests.
He is the worst professor anyone will ever have. Doesn't know how to use the internet so you cant keep up if you don't go and he can not teach.

Saatchi is without a doubt the worst professor I have ever had. Test questions are very specific and very hard to study for. Mumbles through lecture and reads straight from slides that he got from the book.  Lecture is basically useless. If you can avoid him do it at all costs,  this class is a nightmare!

Saatchi is the worst professor in the entire school. He is rude to students. He fails to answer questions asked in class. His tests are ridiculous unless you can memorize 150 pages of material in 3 weeks.  He flat out doesn't care about students. Good luck in this class as he is the only professor...

Very quiet and mumbles through lectures which are almost useless. He talks about very broad topics in lecture and then asks very specific questions on the tests which are hard. He is hard to get a hold of and I still have not left a lecture with a sure picture of what the HW was and what was going on the class. He tries, but he is still bad.

Professor Ai is always patient and caring. He writes math proofs on board carefully and rigorously. He often provides the motivation for the mathematical concepts and has a good organization of course content.

Honestly, one of the better professors for math 431. The material is relatively easy, but Albert tries to explain the deeper reasonings for each problem to prepare for later problems in the book. Realistically, any professor would be the same in the course since they all teach directly from the UW-licensed book in order.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: actually garbage, avoid at all costs. the problem is the class is relatively easy but its explained so poorly its impossible to know what's going on. Literally lecture is watching professor ai fill 2 entire pages with greek symbols and random syntax to "explain" something like flipping a coin. The worst professor Ive ever had.

Not responsive to questions on online forum. Doesn't present challenging topics clearly in class. Doesn't have a strong handle on the material he's teaching. Homework is not representative of what's covered on exams. Don't take the course with him, seriously.
The exam is very difficult, Fast progress. Suitable for students who like to challenge themselves

Aida is AMAZING! Best professor I have ever had at UW-Madison. She is brilliant, creative, articulate, and generally lovely. 574 covered super interesting topics related to feminist literature, which is obviously one of her passions and something she is extremely knowledgeable about. I could listen to her lecture all day. Class with her was a joy!

Aida gives incredible lectures, is absolutely brilliant, and is very down to earth. I would highly recommend taking a class with her. In fact, if you don't take a class with her, you're missing out on the best professor and course of your life. There aren't many people or professors like her!
Although she is not good at giving lectures, she is very intelligent and the course material is interesting.  A lot of reading but otherwise manageable work load.

reads straight from lecture notes which use overly complex language to explain simple themes throughout the books. lecture is only mandatory to take pop quizzes and is almost useless for the midterm. Grading is strictly based on TAs and some are much easier than others. Class isnt that hard if you have a good TA but a struggle if you have a bad one

Aida is one of the best professors I've had. The course material was challenging, but Aida provided a learning environment where students' ideas were never shot down. Her intelligence is remarkable and her passion for the subject made learning enjoyable. Class is mostly focused on discussion, so be prepared to analyze theories presented in the text

Discussions & lectures rarely had anything to do with the content of the readings, even though the midterm was based solely off the readings. Reads off pre-written speech for lectures, uses unnecessary complicated language, but stutters when asked a question & has to go off her script. Nice lady, class left me disappointed.

She is very clear and concise with her lectures and makes sure not to waste any time. She is also very nice and understanding when it comes to misunderstandings or time conflicts. Take her classes if you can!

Aida is incredible. It is difficult, being an upper level English postmodern lit class, but she is so passionate about what she does and is always willing to help anyone. She is remarkably intelligent. I would recommend this class to all lit majors

The lectures were somewhat interesting but not very relevant to the class as there was only one exam and it was based off of the assigned readings. Discussion sections were much more helpful as they discussed the book rather than the history of the author.  Relatively easy class as long as you got a good TA as some were tough graders.

Prof Hussen is very passionate about what she is teaching in class, but she also keeps class light and will joke around. You need to read the books because each one has a pop quiz or short assignment, but they're all great. I'd attend lectures because powerpoints aren't online and only list main points. TA graded, get Karolyn Steffens if you can!

This class was really challenging but in the best way possible.  Aida really makes you think and won't give you answers but is so willing to meet to talk about questions.  She is easily the nicest professor I've had on campus and you can feel her passion for her work.  I would LOVE to take another class with her.

Has well designed powerpoints and interesting lectures but doesn't upload them online. You have to be a good note taker to be successful in her class. Reading is about a book a week with either a small quiz or assignment.

This class required a lot of reading, but most of the books were easy reads. The assignments were very straight forward.  Lectures could be long at times, but she was very into what she was talking about and very funny when you paid close attention to what she was saying.  A lot of this class depends on your TA.

Wonderful and intriguing lectures. Her readings and interpretations of the novels are very straightforward and interesting. Gives pop quizzes in lecture to make sure you're attending which keeps you accountable for the assigned reading. Overall, wonderful professor! Highly recommend.

Although her lectures could get long at times, overall Professor Hussen's lectures were interesting. She was passionate about the subject. There was a fair amount of reading, but the books were pretty easy to read. Assignments and essays were straightforward and not too difficult. Overall, I enjoyed the class.

Lectures are useless. She literally just writes essays for every class and reads from them. A lot of people would get up and leave. Her powerpoint slides are useless as well. Assignments aren't hard, it just depends on your TA.
An alright teacher. Really boring lectures, but an easy class. A lot of reading.

Course name in class search is very misleading, but it still turned out to be an interesting class. There are three papers, a book report, and a presentation, besides that, there's no homework. There's a lot of reading, but you can definitely get by with skimming. Know the concepts, take good notes. Professor is very nice and approachable.
Great professor with high standards and interesting lectures. Has a really good BS filter for papers, so you actually have to make them good.

The class was interesting and so were most of the readings.  Her quizzes are horrible, which I think she realizes and may change for future classes.  I missed class a couple times and failed the quizzes, but I still got an AB.

She's a pretty cool professor harsh grader on papers so make sure no grammatical errors and you put in your own ideas/thoughts about a topic. A lot of reading at the beginning of the semester. Take home exams are super nice
harsh grading, not interesting
She was excited about the thing she taught. But honestly a really strict course and grading with mandatory attendance for some of the weirdest assignments that don't bring value to anything at all.

Lectures were interesting but her class was disorganized and her expectations too high. She gave many creative assignments with vague instructions, and would then tell the class that she was 'underwhelmed' with the submissions. Assignments were graded pass or fail- not in the syllabus. And I bought the books just for them to feel brushed over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking this class. The assignments were nearly always unclear and the readings were utterly useless as we never went over them in class. She is also very strict with attendance at all lectures and discussions.  It is an easy A but entirely made up of busy work. Overall this course is very disorganized and unproductive.

All i will say is , if you are looking for a class you can get an A in , do not take this one. 
Horrible professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was a disaster; the professor was unclear about the assignment, and even got the due time wrong. There is a final exam for this course, but until week 13, she had not decided on the format of it. The assignments were interesting, but the workload is too much. She doesn't allow for any emergencies. You will not get any extension.(EASY A)

Prof Edoro was consistently disorganized. She took over for our class when our original professor quit and taught us the ENG 178 material, but she just never picked up her feet and constantly miscommunicated about assignment requirements AND EVEN FORGOT ABOUT OUR FINAL EXAM. Woke up at 7:00am for nothing. Fun class project, careless teaching.

I adored this class. Ainehi is one of the most intelligent lecturers I have had, and I was always captivated by her lectures. Attendance was mandatory with 2 absences allowed. Grades are made up of weekly hw where the lowest score is dropped, one essay, an Instagram project and a final exam.  Awesome class that challenges you to think critically!

Super smart and intelligent professor. This class however sucks. Graded by few things and insane attendance policy (2 freebies and if you miss 1 your grade drops half a letter grade). Prof. Edoro has super uninteresting lectures and awful communicator. Only thing I really liked was instagram project at the end of the semester.

Easy class. The professor is intelligent but takes a ridiculous class way too seriously. She has an extremely strict attendance policy (2 lecture drops, each absence beyond drops a letter). Despite her intelligence, the lectures are completely worthless. It's the last week of class, and assignments from the first weeks have not yet been graded.

Course itself is a cool concept but taught horribly. I enjoyed the lectures but didn't learn much. Ainehi is passionate about social media but her passive-aggressiveness and lack of communication really spoil this class. Attendance policy is harsh and material is disorganized. 1 essay, 10 weekly notes, and an Instagram group project. Easy A or A/B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely strict attendance policy and worthless lectures make this the worst class I've ever taken at UW. It is obvious Ainehi idealizes social media and loves talking about it, but that doesn't make for an interesting class. Pray you don't have any emergencies during the semester as Ainehi won't care - it's half a letter grade per missed lecture.
One of the smartest people I've ever met. She really wants people to think, not just recite what we've memorized.

Prof Edoro is one of the kindest professors at UW-Madison. She truly cares about her students. Lectures are required even though there's no exam. Readings & questions for the first half of semester (graded by completion). Group social media project for the back half of the semester.

She is very passionate but the lectures are not useful at all to the assignments. There is a strict attendance policy through tophat. If you have to make attendance mandatory that means they are probably not useful or engaging. The lectures are more for her (she likes to hear herself talk about what interests her) than the students.

The class overall was pretty easy and interesting if you did the work (small writing assignments, two papers, and a group project), but I would agree that her attendance policy was quite unfair and annoying. Edoro is very smart and passionate about the topic but the class itself was a bit disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Prof. Edoro's class very much, but her lectures are a bit dry at times. Attendance is tracked via TopHat. The papers are very doable and she provides a good amount of extra credit opportunities to boost your grade. Overall, a very interesting class and it is obvious that she is very passionate about what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Edoro is not a good teacher, but she is very knowledgable in African feminists. Her attendance policy is extremely rigid--you cannot miss any days of class, and she emphasized that we must come to class even if we are sick. She is also extremely unorganized and gives very unclear directions. I would not recommend this professor at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Edoro is kind but too unorganized. It took a month and a half to grade a 3 page reflection paper! Super frustrating. At the end of April I knew only 30% of my grade and didn't know where I stood in the class. She was unclear with communication and I always felt in the dark (assignments, grades, etc.). Didn't do much work for this class--easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Professor Edoro is a very wise woman, she is perhaps one of the worst professors I've ever had. She is super unclear with her directions, and blames you when she messes something up. She's very cold and unwelcoming, and not super accessible outside of class. I am sure she's a good person but she's a terrible professor. Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you miss any class points immediately are taken off, otherwise a good professor, but I don't like the lack of flexibility.

She was absolutely amazing. The class itself was super easy. I think we had two papers, two group projects, and a couple note taking assignments. She gives you time in class to work on it all though. She really cares about the class and makes it really interesting and innovative. Our final project was a twitter thread if that says anything.
Super dope guy and fairly interesting class.

Very nice and chill guy. His lectures were very engaging which made class fun to go to. Would definitely take a class from him again if I had the opportunity, and would encourage any individuals looking for an introduction to philosophy to consider him.
great professor
W prof. Would recommend

Boydston is an really good professor that makes a tough class like Ochem 1 much easier to learn. The class is graded mainly on 3 take home quizzes and 4 exams. Professor Boydston is one of the nicest professors I've had. He is funny, caring, and very smart. He keeps lectures interesting and I would definitely recommend taking his class.

Best professor Ive had at UW. Cares so much about his students and is extremely accommodating. Professor Boydston is hands down the best professor you could ask for when it comes to O Chem. He provided countless opportunities for students to receive extra credit and was very accomodating.
