Kurt is a nice guy with a clear passion for what he teaches. Attendance is necessary because everything you need to know for the exam is either written on the board or explained during class. His exam was much easier than any of Will's; however, there is a lot of math, so make sure you know your cell dynamics calculations well.

wonderful professor! kept me engaged during every lecture even when scrambling to write down everything he'd sputter. attendance is crucial as there are no notes online. i highly, highly recommend taking a class with him!

Kurt was a really fun professor, but he also came up with odd questions for the exams.  For example, he always asks "what does the inner cell most resemble?" and the answer is chicken noodle soup, not lasagna.  He also likes you to do mental math- no calculators allowed when it comes to testing cellular dynamics.

Enthusiastic lecturer but he writes fast and messy.  You should attend every lecture, but that won't translate to a good grade.  His practice exam was much easier than the one he wrote, which had all this random math that was never covered.  Luckily, Bement teaches the rest of the class.

This class was ridiculously easy. Tests were of rote recall rather than application of fundamental concepts. Lecturers (Amann and the other one) goofed off a lot and did not give particularly inspired lectures.  Only two pieces of assigned literature, and they were not seminal in any way.  Steer clear and read a textbook instead.
He's one of my favorite professors, he's very enthusiastic and it's kinda contagious. You have to go to class and pay attention to what he writes in order to do well.

He is really hard to understand and his drawings on the board are a mess. He went on a great length about actin, but I was expecting more from a cell biology class. His exams are fair, but some questions are about silly things he mentions once, and then expects you to remember.

He does an amazing job with this class.  His enthusiasm for cell biology is contagious, and he explains recent experiments that help explain the material.  Don't bother buying a book, and don't plan on skipping class. Everything you need to know is written on the board during lecture.  Also there is a contest with a prize of a Gold Squid.

Very passionate.  Not always clear.  Fairly easy but I didn't always know what to expect as far as grading.  The class was usually engaging but some of the assigned reading was terrible.  If you do the reading the class should be a breeze.  He changes it every year though
great teacher

He is an awesome teacher and is very good about keeping your interest and attention..could be a bit clearer since just tries to draw complex pictures on the blackboard...but still better than staring at a powerpoint while they read it off
Kurt Amann is the greatest teacher! He's very passionate about his work, and projects that in his teaching. I suggest this course to anyone, even if you are not interested in science.
He is a very nice guy. Good teacher too. Lectures are very well prepared.
Kurt is passionate about his profession, and it came across in his teaching. He uses very subjective tests, but I actually learned while taking the tests.
No Comments
Ironman Prof rocks the house!
He wasn't stright forward and has an attitude
No Comments

Ridiculous! What could have been a very interesting class degenerated into nothing but the discussion of Amann's reason for living (actin).  The class had no direction and unnecessarily large amounts of work with little guidance.  Avoid at all costs.
No Comments
If you want to learn science or get excited about it, Prof. Amann is awesome.

Very confusing, the material is irrelevant.  He is inconsistent, usually says what he is lecturing on is not going to be on the test, but it always is.  His grading procedure is very subjective, and assigns very long writing assignments without guidelines

Treats you like a high school class, but he does his best to make sure you learn well. The class is super homework heavy regardless of professor and most of your learning will be done outside of lecture
does not care about students and stresses them out. And oh also falsely accuses you of cheating DO NOT TAKE HIM.
bad dfdffdfdf

Honestly, this is one of the classes where the professor does not really matter. The lectures are pretty useless since this class is homework heavy, you know almost everything they cover in class before itself. I would suggest taking the homework and the readings seriously to do well in this class.

I am taking cs200, which is really difficult, we need to write 20 hours of homework every week, but we only have one lecture every week, and I am about to learn autism. Why is this most elementary class so difficult, and I got an f directly at last, I thank you, professor.
We only have one lecture a week, we can't learn anything, and we are all novices, zybook is not so easy to understand, we learn very painful, I hope we will not meet this teacher again.

The professor's teaching level is not bad, but he seems to dislike class very much. He did not come to class for three times, because the teaching assistant taught the class for him. On this point, I think he lacks respect for this class.
Class is a bit unorganized and one of those where you get what you put into it, but he's a fun and caring professor who engages the class.

This class is a scam. The CS department wants your free labor. All that happens in lectures is a 10min ice breaker and then another 40 minutes where he throws out random buzzwords to make it sound like were learning something. Then you have to spend 2-3 hours weekly doing study groups and teaching, in which we are offered very little support for.

My absolute queen. She is an engaging speaker so lectures were more interesting because of how she tells her stories. The projects are creative and not too hard. The reading pace is fast but like lowkey not mandatory and she does give little breaks so it's chill and she kind of makes up for the fact that the books can be boring.

Easiest literature class you could take. Lectures were overall pretty engaging, even if you didn't read the novels ahead of time. It is clear that Anja cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Anja is a very kind professor, her lectures are based on the books but also her life expierences and helping her students. Attendence in discussion counts towards most of grade. The classload is light, mostly reading along with 3 easy writtings/projects. Final exam :10 reading questions(basic comprehension).

Professor Anja is super sweet and her lectures are very inspiring. Readings were assigned but not checked and there was hardly any homework at all; if there was any, it was lightly graded. Super cool teacher and super cool class!

Anja made this class very fun and enjoyable. She also made it seem very chill which is good if you are taking a tough semester load. It's quite easy to do well and she shows a lot of funny videos in class. The only problem I would say is she sometimes called in sick and would let us know like an hour before class started which isn't fun.

Anja was a very engaging lecturer despite the readings being quite boring at times. The class can be somewhat disorganized at times and there were multiple lectures cancelled. The class is easy and I would take it again if I could just because Anja is great.
great professor. also shoutout TA miranda
great lecturer. good choices for books.
Anja is one of the best profs here. Love her so much and would recommend her over any other english class. She once brought her daughter to class and had her read a poem in front of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anja was one of the best professors I've ever had. As someone who's religiously hated English classes, she turned what was typically a miserable class experience into something I would actually look forward to attending.

Anja's class was the highlight of my semester! Her lectures are so moving and she offers such valuable insight into life, the world needs more people like her! The workload was super light and assignments were graded easily. If possible try to avoid Arijit Banerjee's discussion section, he's pretty snarky towards students.

Love her as a teacher, would totally recommend. Lot of readings but you don't really have to do them if you go to class. She gives great advice on life in general. At first I was a bit apprehensive that she wouldn't be too serious as a professor but she ended up being super insightful and funny too.

Anja is one of the greatest, most memorable professors I have had. She's super caring for her students and very understanding. I come out of every lecture with new insights, and I've found myself applying her teaching to my everyday life. DEFINITELY recommend taking her class!!!

her lectures are very thought provoking and she helps you understand the readings on a much deeper level! i ended up falling behind on our readings and i still ended up understanding them just by going to lectures. assignments give a lot of creative freedom. she is a very caring person, and a flexible professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anja is an amazing + grounded professor. Her ability to engage students in the work that they are doing allowed me to complete assignments without stress and the pressure of being "wrong." I recommend going to lectures, although attendance isn't mandatory, as she speaks to everyday struggles of life and provides unique perspectives to living.

One of my favorite professors at UW. Didn't realize I was taking a comedy class until the first day and thought about dropping, but I stayed and this is the only class that I actually look forward to attending. She is so funny, makes an effort to get to know students, and actually cares what we have to say. Looking for another class to take withher

Amazing! I took the course Honors Only and Anja led very inclusive and engaging discussions. We read 4 novels throughout the semesters with a few other short readings. Super easy, quick final, and if you blanked on a question she would just tell you the answer if she recognized you as having attended lecture. Caring and awesome person!
Anja is an AMAZING professor. You can tell that she really enjoys the content and cares a lot about her students. Would 100% recommend both her and this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would recommend Anja 100x over. Her lectures were engaging along with very helpful. The books required in the course were hard to read, but lectures got me through them.

The final was only questions about facts from the books/readings which was really weird? The final was also printed wrong and only 10 questions. The papers are fairly easy, and lectures are important, but she cancels lecture at least once a week. My TA was amazing though, shout out Brittany
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For me, this was a life-changing class. Twice a week, I felt like a learnt a lot about the world and myself; about relationships, friendship, life. Anya is brilliant and funny and honest in a way that none of my other professors are; I'll remember this class forever.

One of the best professors I've had at UW so far! Participation is not needed, but it helps a lot if you go to class. A decent amount of reading is necessary, but besides that, the class is very easy. The books are also somewhat entertaining, so it's not that bad.
Pretty cool professor, she's funny and relatable. Lectures were chill, and showing up basically meant you aced the final.

She was genuinely amazing. You can tell she loves her job and her students. Took ENGL 169 and all we did was read (but you really don't have to haha). The final exam is so so straight forward and simple. I would recommend going to lecture because she remembers faces. So if you don't know an answer on the "final exam" she will literally tell you.

I'm at math major and I usually hate English classes. That being said Anja is without a doubt my favorite professor i have ever had. Her lectures are spent are spent pondering interesting moral questions and giving life lessons. Grading is very easy. Highly recommend

At first, I wasn't sure I wanted to take this class. After I finished it, it's one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. She is an amazing professor. Take this class if you need it!!! You will be very happy you did!

Professor Jovic-Humphrey is an awesome professor. She is caring, helpful, and wants to make genuine connections with her students. Though she is super laid-back and jokes around in her lectures, the lectures are still very informative. She does not assign "busy work." The class is mainly graded on two essays and a presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anja is easily one of the best professors I have had at UW-Madison. She is very caring and thoughtful and you can tell that she is very passionate about the subject. I recommend taking Engl140 if you need a literature or Comm B credit because the workload is very manageable, the books are interesting, and the lectures are fun to attend!

This is for 248 and 140. She's a really unique person, she's cool, interesting, funny, and she has really unique ideas and thoughts about life. Take her classes if you want to invest time in coming to lectures; that was the biggest benefit for me - they impacted me in making my life better beyond any grades or credits.

Amazing; prob my favorite prof at UW. Kind, funny, engaging. Her class doesn't feel like a traditional English class but instead an open space using ideas in readings to talk about art, philosophy, social issues, how we live life, & more. Lots of freedom in written assignments. Take honors if you can: more freedom, great discussion, no extra work.

Anja is the sweetest, kindest professor I have ever had in so many years. She cares about her students and recognizes every student who come to her class. For the most part, her lectures are engaging and during her discussion, she likes to hear every student's thoughts and opinions on the topics being covered. Highly recommend her for English!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Jovic-Humphrey is a unique professor who actually cares about her students! Her lectures are usually interesting and inspirational as well. During discussion, she is super friendly and open-minded! Highly recommend her as a professor!
Highly recommend taking a class with her, she obviously cares a lot about her students and provides a lot of support.

This class was incredibly fun and I found myself more engaged than I was expecting to be. The lectures were compelling and thoughtful, and the reading wasn't excessive. Participation and clear effort matters. When Dr. Jovic-Humphrey says she wants to hear your thoughts, it turns out she really means it.
Wonderful professor, hilarious material. Take this class!
This is actually for Eng 100 but she was extremely nice and the best English teacher I ever met.

she's the nicest person ever! I want her as a professor again she's the best. she's so funny and kind and you can really tell she likes her job. her personality is also golden and she is so interesting!!!! TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU CAN!!!!!!!
Read high-quality literature, have only 3 writing assignments, and be treated like a human being by both Professor and TA. Whats not to like? Professor cares, she really does.

She is amazing! I took an honors course with her and it was super easy yet still extremely valuable. She is so, so kind. Easy A if you put in a little effort. She is a gem of a professor and genuinely cares about her students.

She was AMAZING!!!! I thoroughly enjoyed her class and everything that I learned from it. There are multiple books that you read pretty fast but most of them I liked. Her essays were not difficult at all and there was one where you could do a project instead of an essay. She really appreciates all her students and makes you feel valued.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: All you have to do is show up to discussion and participate (I was able to participate pretty easily even without reading the book assigned), and write two papers. For a Comm B class, this one was very easy. And Anja was incredible, passionate, and ridiculously smart. Highly recommend any class she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class, and her! Seems passionate about the material and her recorded lectures are soothing. She posts weekly modules with a warm-up, lecture, reminders for the discussion section, and a reflection. There are two papers and 1 project. This is definitely a class that is not too hard to do well in. Would recommend for a gen-ed!
10/10, such an amazing professor/instructor. Her discussion classes are very insightful and I can't her classes less.

I took the course this summer by accident - I wish they called it "humor and comedy." I do creative writing, and at first I thought - how much is there to say about humor-writing? - but this course was really eye-opening. The Prof was hands-on and tracked our progress every week in the gradebook, which I appreciated. The lectures were awesome!

Anja is the sweetest professor you will ever meet. My only complaint is that the semester ended a week ago and I have zero grades handed back to me for this test, which has made me nervous. The books are interesting and she incorporates outside material into the lectures when appropriate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Anja is one of the best professors I have ever had! She was so sweet, and really cared about all her students in the lecture and discussion. She focused more on our own journey through literature instead of just doing stuff to pass the class which was wonderful. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very open, caring and personable professor, if you make time for her she will make time for you, and is very accommodating. Although 140 is listed as an elementary class, I felt thoroughly challenged by the readings and the final analytical paper, so I will say that her class takes effort. Overall, I had a great experience with Dr. Anja!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing. Profound. Lovely. Incredible. Best professor I have ever had and ever met.

Anja is a straight gem. The entire course is reading the books and listening to her talk about profound, incredible insights she has about life that relates to book and she's a dawg; very nice lady, passionate, and funny. You don't need to read. Two papers, a creative project, and a test, all easy af. Easiest and most interesting class I've taken.

Super sweet professor! Sometimes she was scatter-brain during lecture but always had good content to go over. She makes you read a lot but it is a lit class so what do you expect. She chooses good books to read at least. Discussion attendance is mandatory but not lecture.
She is an interesting person full of intriguing ideas. Assigns a lot of reading but choose things that are enjoyable. Overall I highly recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Anja was a great professor and really cares about her students! There was a ton of reading for the course, but not many assignments which made it easier to handle. The amount of reading is the only thing that made the class challenging, in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She's the best of the english teachers at Madison, in my opinion. Caring, passionate, and funny as well. If you get the chance, I highly recommend you take her class.
Engaging professor, she connects the books we read with contemporary issues so the books are never boring. Her discussion sections are helpful and thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Perhaps other professors can teach how to read/write better than Anja, but Anja is the best at making people passionate about English. Fun class, LOTS of reading but still overall easy. I would focus on choosing a good TA since I think they grade the papers. Would highly recommend.
Anja is very nice and cares about the material she teaches, only 3 papers and a final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved English 167, not just because of the great literature I've always wanted to read, but especially because of Professor Jovic's teaching. She is a very caring and invested individual, who made our 3 hour night lecture more bearable. I heavily appreciated her teaching/lectures, she is my favorite professor at UW Madison.

I took this class to fulfil a lit requirement and I was completely blown away by it. The professor said she wanted to give us intrinsic (as opposed to extrinsic) motivation, and she really succeeded in doing this. She managed to say something really profound about life (and not just books) in pretty much every lecture.

There were 9 assigned books for the semester, and most of them were easy to get through. Anja fostered good discussions and is kind, understanding, and laid back. The course is graded on a 12 page midterm paper, a creative project, a 12-15 page final paper, and participation. Students were given a lot of freedom in their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Homework rubrics are never clear; grader takes petty amount of points off. Class exam should have been online or given more time. The exam practice question was way too simple for the midterm. The class is based on an outdated program that doesn't match what industry uses. I wouldn't recommend it for ME students.

I did not have Mikkelson as my professor, but after the first midterm, I started attending his lectures. And they were way better than my previous professor. He gives lots of examples, explains concepts well, and is a great lecturer overall. Exams are hard, but reasonable. It was well worth waking up early and attending his lectures.
Fun professor just a difficult class
Engaging lecturers. Fast talker. Recorded lectures. Funny. Exams are hard, but for the most part fair. Required attendance in discussion.

Very good prof, he did a good job with example problems during lecture to explain the concepts.  Exams were very difficult and required a complete understanding of material.  He records all his lectures which is very nice.  Difficult material.

Lecture slides are heavy and dense with not a lot of explanation of why things are the way they are. Often not at scheduled office hours so receiving help is hard. When at office hours he responds to questions with rude and demeaning responses. Isn't very understanding when problems with ANSYS software arise on exams and homework's.
Andy made getting up at 7am bearable because he has a good dry sense of humor. He is also a beast. He knew what he was talking about it mechanics, and my god this guy can draw.
Solid professor. Engages lecture halls, teaches things well, likes to use real world examples to demonstrate concepts, one of the better engineering professors I have had

Overall this professor was good for the class, he was engaging and helped make the class interesting. The professor does go through examples in class pretty quickly, however he goes pretty detailed with them. The class is tough but the professor clearly explains topics and answers questions very frequently.

Really enjoyed the way that Professor Mikkelson taught this course. I ended with a very high AB and was very close to the grade cut off, but the class wasn't curved at all. This is no fault of Mikkelson's- the course is taught by 3 professors but rather something to be aware of. Overall, Mikkelson was one the best (and funniest) professors I've had
Andy is a beast

One of my favorite professors ever! He has a great sense of humor and genuinely cares about his students and their understanding of the concepts. He explains everything clearly and uses a lot of examples in his lectures.

He is great. I didnt do well in this class, but that was due to me and outside commitments. I don't think I would have passed at all had he not taught the course so well.

I have used the material professionally since taking his course and I had a good grasp on the subject. Dude has a dry sense of humor but he's a great lecturer and a good person.

Ok lecturer, but not much passion for the subject. He's not very good at answering student questions. Everyone agrees the book is bad, but they keep using it. Exam questions are not very clear and the group project is time consuming. If Zhiyi Jiang is still a TA, choose him, he's more experienced with the course.

Andy is a down to earth guy and a good professor. He mixed some jokes and videos in with his lectures to give some relief from the content. I think he explains concepts well and emphasizes the most important ones. He asks a lot of questions during lecture, and I would recommend participating even if it's just thinking of what the answer is.

Mikkelson's teaching style is fun and relaxed mainly owing to his dry humor. Lectures could be tedious and sometimes felt they contained more information than needed, but he was able to convey ideas well for the most part. Very helpful and accessible outside of class. Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andy is relaxed and has a good sense of humor. He is a little monotone and goes through lectures fairly quickly, but does a good job explaining the material. The course itself is rather boring but he does a good job trying to make it interesting.

He does not explain concepts very well and lectures are not very organized. Sometimes acts like the stuff he is teaching is "common knowledge" when they are very difficult to understand. Highly recommend professor Detlor for mechanics of materials over Mikkelson.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent engineering professor, gets the lecture hall to participate and isn't a bore. Helpful and accessible outside class. The group runs the class between 3 professors so there was disagreement when it came to if they should curve or not.

Mikkelson gets a bad rap but I really enjoyed his lectures. He has a dry sense of humor that is fun to engage with in lectures. His lectures explain the material clearly and his worked examples help you understand the material.

He does his best to make an extremely boring topic manageable. If you can get Zhiyi Jiang as your TA for this course do it, he is amazing. Exams are open book, closed notes which is weird but you can just write everything from your notebook in the textbook for the exam.

Mikkelson is a professor that gives zero additional effort beyond 2 lectures a week. I would assume he has more important research to worry about. He is extremely lazy when it comes to assisting students, puts zero effort into helping beyond one sentence. Zero personality and a terrible lecturer. Class taught by the textbook and TA's.

He is so mean and his class is super boring, and his teaching is like telling a story before you go to bed, and u would fall of sleep u don't even know that. He is a super super suck professor. Please do not take his class if you want a happy colleage life. The most important thing is his sample exam would useless, and his exam is super hard.

If you can take the course with any other prof, consider it. Puts very little effort into teaching beyond just reading off the slides and doing problems, but grades as if you had a thorough teacher. The textbook is the only way through.
Andy is awesome he is accessible outside of class and really cares about his students. Exams are fair and gives plenty of partial credit. Awesome prof, really recommend taking his class!
Good guy, means well with the class. Does a lot of examples in lecture and covers the material pretty well. Homework is long and the tests are tough though.
I dubbed him the terminator. He comes into class and kills material. Good professor as he is clear and entertaining. I just like the guy.

The most boring professor I have ever had. He reads the presentation to you word for word and is not interested in engaging with students or the subject matter. Avoid this professor if possible. Exams are incredibly long.
Andy is a great instructor with a good sense of humor. Classes are not mandatory, but help to understand the material for the homework.
Lectures are fairly dull and boring, but contain essentially all the information you need to do well in the course
Bring coffee to lecture, he is drier than the sahara desert. But he is clear and the dry info is actually helpful. Homework and practice homework more then prepare you for the exam.
Exams are hard and different from the hw.

Didnt mind the class. Pretty interesting guy with a dry sense of humor. monotone. But I really wasnt happy with my end grade, even tho i was in contention for an acceptable one all semester. not sure what happened.
Does a lot of examples from the book and all lecture slides are put online for review.
Just stands at the front of class and reads lecture slides off the screen. Extremely monotone and boring.
not bad
Great professor,  very passionate about the subject which was reflected into interesting lectures.  Took French 211 just to fill a credit but it ended up being the best class I have taken.

Prof Armstrong is awesome, hes got the right blend of uplifting and charming energy without being overbearing and annoying. Hes funny as all get out which helps break tension. In terms of grading hes a fairly easy grader, and is very reasonable and understanding when it comes to missed class days/assignments.

I took French 211 last semester, and I loved it! At first, I wasn't very enthusiastic about taking the class since it was only to fulfill a requirement, but it ended up being my favorite. Professor Armstrong is a genuine, chill guy, and he is knowledgeable on the topics we covered. The class was manageable, and I would definitely recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super chill dude and a great professor. Funny but very knowledgable about the class content. Easy A if you attend class for attendance points, I never did the readings but could still do well on papers. Honestly what made the class was my TA (shoutout Fabian) but there's another who was awful. Usually didn't pay attention and was completely fine

Armstrong was a good professor overall, didn't make things too difficult for students. Had around 5 quizzes total, all based on what was taught during lecture -- attend lectures if you want to pass the class! Midterms were fine, mostly just papers.

Josh is an awesome prof! His class is very simple, the readings are straight forward, and the quizzes are easy if you do the readings and pay attention. This is a literature course, so expect quite a bit of reading, but I was shocked at how little writing there was for this class. Only one mid-term paper (1 page) and a final paper (2 pages).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Armstrong is a great professor. Cares for his students and his thorough in directions. Would definitely recommend for a lit credit.

As of now Josh is my favorite professor I've had. He's a genuine guy that cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. He has high expectations for you, but they aren't unattainable. I took another class from him just because he was the professor. Would definitely recommend!

Readings, assignments, and grading in this class were all fine. But lectures were very haphazard - a lot of the time, Josh just talked about the readings with no slides or structure and I found it hard to participate, take notes, or even pay attention. I did not get much practice speaking French from this class. Maybe it's better in-person.

DO NOT TAKE A COURSE FROM HIM. First of all, he expects everyone to participate every day in a class of 35 students, and if you don't, you'll get a B-/C range for participation. On top of that, he grades RIDICULOUSLY hard on essays. Get ready to get a B- or a C if you're used to getting A's.

Josh is one of, and I cannot stress this enough, the BEST professors I have had at Madison. He loves his students, he loves the material, and he's reasonable. Get ready to put in the work, though. You get what you work for.
This is a fun class. He won't overwhelm you with homework. Fair grader and easy to talk to!

Josh is a great guy, has clear guidelines and expectations, and is a moderate grader. If you put in the work and show up to class, you will get the grade you deserve. Excellent command of the French language and so nice. Occasionally cancels class for a conference. Totally recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Josh is by far my favorite prof that I'd had yet, especially in French. This class does have a lot of reading (that you pretty much actually have to do), but it doesn't feel so bad because coming to lecture is enjoyable. He discusses the material thoroughly and keeps it entertaining, and will make sure you understand what's going on.

Josh is great! His class is just the right amount of work. He assigns homework every night, but he doesn't usually check for completion and you can definitely get by not doing it a lot of days. He's a very easy grader, but participation is definitely a requirement- he will call you out if you don't speak. Overall, it's not hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Reading-based class - very little homework other than to do your assigned reading which he doesn't check. Tests are based mainly on concepts discussed in class. Be able to at least B.S. your reading and you'll be fine. Couple papers. Very kind and understanding but reasonable teacher. Easy to understand. Would definitely take again

Very disorganized, which markedly affects the quality of the class. I would not take this class again. It is very difficult to meet with him in office hours. He's not a bad person, and he likes his subject, but he's just not a good professor.

He seems like a coolgood person but he's definitely not the best professor. He was really unorganized, slow at responding to emails and putting the homework assignments up on Moodle. The class seemed to be very unengaged throughout the semester and there is just a general air of disinterest in class which could also be attributed to the books.
Love him, he's so fun and dances were somewhat difficult for beginners but he posts videos so you can practice outside of class.

I took Dance 107 with AJ, and it was great! Show up to class, participate, and have fun! He is a very talented dancer and a great teacher. Canvas assignments weren't very organized or clear, but it was okay; he didn't grade hard.

Fun guy. I took hip-hop with him and then Latin social dance. Have fun, make friends, and definitely don't worry about the in-class practicals. You probably won't ever need to practice outside of class.
He was not responding to emails, and the grading was not clear. Dance was difficult and hard to follow for beginners.
AJs hip hop dance class was so fun! All he expects is that you show up to class, try your best, and work hard! Youll do warmups, hip hop technique, and learn fun combos.

Eduardo is a wonderful professor and lecturer. ECE 330 had a semi-flipped learning style when I took it, and his video lectures and in-person lectures always left me prepared to work through the in-class activity and learn the concepts required for exams.

This professor is amazing! I had him for 330 his first semester teaching the class. Attendance is incentivized and he does everything in his power to see you succeed. Does a somewhat flipped learning style with only one video prior to each class and then goes into a lecture to start each class.

I have taken three classes with Eduardo (331, 204, and 532), and he has been amazing in all of them. He is passionate about the topics he teaches and really cares about the outcomes of his students. If you have the chance to take a class with him, I would highly, highly, highly recommend taking it.
Took it over the summer, contents are crammed and intense, but prof Arvelo is one of the few reasons I keep showing up and not giving up on this class!

Eduardo does an excellent job distilling the ideas of matrices and their applications in ways that are easy to understand for folks like me whose background in linear algebra is shaky. Exams were split into units and were not cumulative; workload was quite reasonable. Definitely recommend before taking CS760.

This class is really amazing and so well designed. It's my first flipped classroom but i thought it actually helped me learn better. He's always open to help students, very knowledgable, and explains things well. He makes an effort to learn student's names and get to know them which is rare! One of the best cs classes and professors that I've had.

Prof Eduardo embodies what a world class faculty is. If you've watched Harvard's CS50 lectures, the gold standard of teaching, Prof E's lessons and energy is on par.
I'm an exchange student from a global T20 and Prof E's teaching is better than anything I have taken. 
The online lectures however isn't as great, was done by another prof years back.

Eduardo is a kind and fun person. The flipped format of 532 wasn't ideal but Eduardo made the most out of it. The exams were fair and slightly curved for the last ones. All in all great professor, but 532 should really be cross-listed to the math department because it was all linear algebra. I'm glad I took math 340 before.

532 is hard, but Eduardo makes it as manageable as possible. Reverse format, and non mandatory attendance, plus activities are graded on participation. Homeworks are long and hard but are graded generously. Tests are not too difficult, you'll do well if you know your stuff decently. Very clear grading criteria for everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is somewhat useless. The lecture videos are created by someone else and are very boring. In class you do activities that are designed to take the class length, but they are often very complicated and take longer than the class. Yet they are due at the end of class and thus you lose points. This class is all theory so you won't learn applications
Eduardo the goat

I had ece 203, ece 330, and ece 334. He is a legend. He is in my top 3 prof that I have ever had. Super good teacher, his exams are reasonable, and he is also just a very likable and down to earth guy. I know many people who took a class with him just for the experience and to be in his presence. 


I would kill for him.
Awesome
One of the best professors I've ever had

Prof Arvelo is really helpful and very accesible. He would often overstay his set Office Hour hours before exams and during difficult content weeks during the semester. Must take if he's teaching a class you're planning to take.

Most of the learning in ECE 203 comes from the exercises and the labs (which you need to attend). Professor Arvelo is amazing because he answers Piazza (online forum) posts very frequently and provides detailed explanations. Can't say anything about him as a lecturer, but he's a really great guy who cares and is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Arvelo is an amazing professor. He is very friendly and dedicated to his craft and answers questions till you get the concept entirely. Very responsive to emails/messages. Highly recommend him for ECE 203.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class content should be interesting and enjoyable in theory. However, the lectures are very slow and boring, and a majority of the class won't pay attention. This is all manageable, however the canvas page is a mess. No modules done correctly, readings are always posted in weird spots and with broken links, and just super sloppy!

One of my favorite professors at UW. Canvas was perfectly organized, lecture topics were valuable and focused, and optional readings were always really well picked. The midterm and the assignments are pretty hard and you have to problem solve some things on your own, but you're supposed to.

Convinced me to do a career in UE, so honest 10/10
Very disorganized and rambles. Doesn't use any structure and not good at explaining things. Difficult to understand as well.

Gave no guidance on grade breakdowns. End of year grade stood at 94.94%, below the un-communicated cutoff of 95% for an A. No communication from her about grades and she ignored my emails. She seemed very nice, making this lack of communication very disappointing.

Attendance and participation are graded. One midterm and a big final group project. She was a nice caring professor but the class was disorganized in terms if her explanations and the final project criteria. Also her grading scale was wack a 85 was a BC. Overall easy manageable class.
Alina is a really nice professor. She is always accessible outside class even at midnight. Great passion on teaching and always encourages you to go further. Exam is really fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Arefeva, but I hated the class. The grading scheme was obnoxious which makes me regret taking this class. Attendance is mandatory, and as much as Arefeva tried, the content wasn't that interesting. This class is also cross-listed with Econ, but Real Estate students had way more of an advantage than the Econ students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Alina is a really intelligent person and has a lot of great research however her teaching skills are lacking. Not graded on much and the work isn't very hard either. You get a cheat sheet for the exams which is nice. Attendance was mandatory. Class is very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's alright. The class is crazy boring. It's cross-listed as an econ class but I would recommend not taking it if you don't have a background in RE because I was lost for much of the class. Only two power lectures per week, graded on participation in class, one midterm and a final, and a huge group project. It's overall easy but not fun at all.

The BEST professor ever. He makes the most boring topics fascinating. Class is super easy to get an A in, you decide how much work you do, and as long as you get most of it right, you get full marks, plus unlimited retakes. If you actually do the work and make an effort you will learn so much and leave a better person. I cannot recommend him enough

Professor Mobley was amazing! Not only are his lectures really interesting, but the specifications grading system meant you could get an A without having to stress yourself out about doing perfect on everything, which really helps with learning. Make sure to go to lecture because there are 'focus questions' at the end which you need for credits

I loved Professor Mobley! Very accessible outside of class and always interested in student feedback. His specification grading system makes it very easy to get an A in the class as long as you show up to class and put in some effort.
Super nice and chill, work's pretty easy with unlimited repeats.

Arguably the best professor I've ever taken. His lectures are straightforward and interesting. The minimal homework and quizzes are extremely easy if you pay attention. You have unlimited retakes on all assignments to obtain credit for the assignment, which is 100%.
Professor Mobley truly cares about each and every student and wants nothing more than them to succeed. Try your best and it'll work out.

I was a little nervous going into this class, since he's the CO of the NROTC, but I absolutely loved this class. He's got a great charisma and teaching style. I'd take any of his classes in a heartbeat.

Prof Armstrong is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about linguistics, and he manages to convey a ton of information while also making difficult concepts accessible and comprehensible to students. This is the second class I've taken with him and I've loved both of them!

Dr. Armstrong is hands down my favorite professor I've had. He knows so much about this topic and teaches it so well. Exams can be a bit difficult, but as long as you study, you should be okay. He was really good at keeping class interesting and engaging. I would highly recommend.

Professor Armstrong is one of the most passionate professors I've had. His lectures are pretty clear, and he's always available to answer questions. Homework is about 30-40 pages of readings per week and answering a few questions that weren't graded for accuracy. I really enjoyed his class and would highly recommend!

Grant is my favorite professor, I have taken multiple classes with him, and his passion for the topic always shines through in his lectures. He presents topics in a clear straightforward way and grades fairly. He provides consistent support for students and gives great help during office hours. It's clear that he actually cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grant was such a nerd about Spanish linguistics in the best way so he really knew what he was talking about! For what the content was, he made it somewhat interesting. Also, he graded fairly.
Solid lecturer who explains things well. Overall the class has been fairly easy, but I still feel that I learned a lot.

I liked the class and the professor! You could tell he was knowledgeable and genuinely liked the topics. There are two in-person exams and two take home "problems" that are the midterm and final. Discussion participation is worth the exams combined, so make sure you go to discussion and participate at least once.  Pretty straight-forward class.

Very clear and understandable, manageable expectations. There is one discussion assignment each week. Slides are posted. He is very willing to help you if confused. There are discussion quizzes every once in a while, and a mix of exams and take-home problems. I thought lecture was great and he uses lots of example problems. Not super difficult.

Professor Armstrong is a witty, passionate guy who loves linguistics. I took this course slightly frightened by the comments of others on here, but mainly found them to be untrue. He assigns a lot work and there are many exams, but if you attend and participate in his lectures, this course should be no trouble. Great professor and great guy!

I found the class to be super clear and easy despite having no background in linguistics. He honestly doesn't ask much of you, the grade was just based on weekly quizzes, discussion attendance, and four written homework assignments that were due once a month. I also went to his office hours and found him to be kind and helpful with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would not take a class with him again. 225 was challenging and he graded very harsh.

This is supposed to be an INTRO class. He is the pickiest grader, he will never give an A. Whole class is graded on 3 homeworks, 2 exams, and 1 final; no participation grades. His "class" is just him reading off a slideshow for 1hr 15min. His exam questions are SO specific, nothing you can study for. Grading criteria/feedback unclear. STAY AWAY!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grant was the scariest professor I have had on this entire campus- he was so intimidating and this class was the hardest class I took during my entire Spanish major on campus. His tests were very difficult and the assignments were absolutely exhausting to complete. If you want to learn A LOT then take his class, but it's a real challenge!

Grant grades HORRIBLY. I am a native speaker and he always finds something wrong in your writing even if it's grammatically correct. He only accepts certain grammar styles and if it doesn't meet his style then your grade will suffer. Do not recommend this professor!

Grant is a very good professor for this class. I really enjoyed going to class every day and learning from him. He gives weekly quizzes and there is a writing assignment (essay, composition) due usually every week. He grades subjectively off your first assignment, but gives good feedback that allows for growth and improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clear expectations and a pretty straightforward class. Grant speaks a very slow and clear Spanish which makes understanding everything easier. The book is definitely not needed. Make sure not to skip much or you'll receive a grade lower than you actually deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was the worst Spanish class I've ever taken. We didn't speak Spanish throughout the semester and then were required to do a 20 minute presentation all in Spanish with no notes at the end of the semester. Huge waste of time and will decrease your Spanish-speaking skills.
He is a teacher so good. He is very smart and really teach you. I like so much his class.

This is my third class I have taken with him. He's my favorite professor of all time.  I don't like small classes, but his I can handle.  He's very, very organized and precise.  He does grade toughly, but he's respectful and super nice to all students.  I would absolutely recommend taking at least one of his classes.

Out of all the Spanish classes I've taken at UW so far, Grant's has been my least favorite.  His directions are always on his assignments, but tends to be somewhat vague for some of the compositions and for his quizzes.  Haven't been a fan.  If you don't have to take him, take a pass for someone else.  Hasn't been horrible, but at least no final.

Prof. Grant teaches pretty clearly in class but when someone has a question he doesn't know how to explain things in any other way than he already did. Goes through slides way too fast. Went to office hours multiple times and he was very unwilling to help. If you ask a question he thinks is dumb he will be condescending.

Excellent professor. Very dedicated to the subject matter and willing to communicate knowledge to students. His explanations were generally clear and precise, although when the class did not understand a specific topic, he would continue on. Homework and exams were challenging, but fair in relation to the level of the course. Did not use textbook.

He's a great professor and engages a lot with the class. There are 3 exams throughout the semester, which are open notes of 2 pages. Lecture and discussion are mandatory. There are two readings per week, which are pretty hard to comprehend, but he goes through each reading during class. He cares a lot about his students and is very understanding.

He's very nice, has good humour, class sometimes drag but he tries very hard to make it engaging, and tests aren't that hard, class should be pretty easy to get an A in, class uses perusall right now for homework but it's decently doable twice a week

I really enjoyed taking this class. Participation matters but the lectures are very interesting to attend. Created an environment that was very encouraging to students who were just being introduced to philosophy. Although if you are looking for an introductory class that teaches the basics of writing philosophy papers, this may not be the class.
Super cool, easygoing, british guy. It is hard not to love him. Easy class. Attendance is heavily mandatory and lectures were sometimes boring, but so hard to not get an A. Def take for credit.
He was a super kind guy and I found his lectures super interesting! I would 100% recommend him to anyone looking to take a philo class.
That is a really great professor with amazing lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super nice guy with a good sense of humor. I strongly recommend this class to anyone who wants an enjoyable, manageable, and engaging class. The discussion sections are probably unnecessary and attendance is mandatory but outside of that, you have to be comatose to not get an A. Plus he's British so that's kinda fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this professor and this class! He's tough but funny and cares about his students. Class has a lot of material, but it's interesting and the labs are fun! Exams are hard, but if you review all the lecture material you should do fine. He grades harshly at first, but you'll understand what he's looking for by the middle of the semester.
The worst professor on campus. Has a huge ego and refuses to accept help when he clearly needs it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the GOAT

Arnoldo is hilarious and incredibly caring and understanding of the students. He does have very high expectations for grading, but is incredibly accessible outside of class for homework/lab help (or just to talk about life). My biggest complaint is he can be a bit disorganized on the account of him teaching several classes.

Arnoldo is an amazing person and professor. I am finishing up my 3rd class with him and it's clear he really cares about his students. He is always available for questions and will often work through things with you. His exams are hard but if you engage you'll succeed. Curves the class so that you pass if you tried at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are 2-3 hours and grading criteria is strict. Lacks student-teacher transparency.

He's very approachable and caring and enjoys answering student questions, even when they seem bizarre or dumb. My major complaint is he writes exams that are way too long. He does take that into account and chooses exam times/locations that allow for students to work late, but midterms and finals take most people 2.5-3 hours.

Very personable and caring. Exams are very thorough, but fair. Lots of work from weekly lab assignments, but labs are usually fun, and many end with food you can take home (bread, poptarts, etc). Overall, more enjoyable than I expected. Lectures were engaging as were labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arnoldo clearly cares about his students and tries to help them out with the grading, but his exams can be pretty specific, like an offhand mention in lecture can be a whole question in an exam. Labs usually are completed early and the reports are almost freebie points. No textbooks or readings which is nice, everything is lab or lecture based
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Arnoldo is an amazing professor, he always makes lectures engaging and is very approachable for help.

Professor Asif was a great professor. He didn't assign very much homework at all for a 4 credit class, and when he did he would give a good grades to everybody. He says there's required textbooks on the syllabus, but he provides everything you will need. He also does care about how people do in the class and will help you if you ask for it.

He is a knowledgeable and supportive instructor who explains the material clearly and creates a positive learning environment. He is kind, organized, and always willing to help students understand the coursework. I truly appreciated their teaching style and would highly recommend their class. He is easily accessible outside of the class too.

He is an excellent instructor who explains concepts clearly and supports students throughout the course. I truly appreciated his teaching style. He is patient, knowledgeable, and always willing to help. He creates a positive learning environment and makes difficult material easy to understand.
One of my best professors, highly recommend taking this class. He is so kind and makes learning Hindi-Urdu so much more fun!

I enjoyed Professor Asif's class and have greatly improved my Urdu skills! He's very caring and wants you to succeed. He is patient with you and works at your own pace. I'm excited for next semester when the classes aren't so early. Participation and attendance are important but that's the only way you can really learn a language. Great prof!!

I started Urdu feeling very nervous, but Professor Asif was great. He really focuses on where you're at with your learning. Approaches the language to help you understand without feeling rushed. Fair amount of homework, but as long as you put in the effort to try, you'll succeed. Probably one of UW's best profs. Only downside is early morning class

While I found this content very interesting (comparable to Child Development) I found the professors policies to be harsh. In addition, the lectures were sped through so it was extremely challenging to get all the information down.

Pt2: the extra credit assignments are only for missed attendance or discussion posts. Unless you REALLY need to or just love social development, I would NOT recommend this class. It's not engaging or really that interesting. You have to put in a lot of work, but really only get half the output. Save yourself some time and take a different depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Part 1: While Professor Jordan is very kind and knowledgeable, her lectures are not good. She flies through the material while reading a very wordy script. To really understand the material you must go back and watch the lecture videos which can be VERY time consuming. There are extra credit opportunities, but...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jordan was an efficient and engaging lecturer. She goes fast but posts lecture videos if you miss anything and offers time for questions at the end. Exams were multiple choice and short answer and focused a lot on research study content that is covered in lecture. Make-up assignments are available if you lose points. Would recommend!

I liked Professor Jordan. Lectures moved quickly but were interesting and efficient. Exams and lecture content were very focused on research studies. Expectations are very clear and rubrics for every assignment are available. She even offers assignments to make-up lost points.

Pt 2: …”you will not be able to earn more extra credit points than attendance/participation points you missed” straight from canvas announcement, not in syllabus. So you can't really earn extra credit. Because you can only get up to the number of points you missed. Overall, this class was unnecessarily hard. I dreaded going to this class-DONT take.

Part 1: DO NOT take this class or professor. She reads off a wordy script and her slides have very little words. You will likely have to rewatch lectures as it's extremely hard to get everything down, even if you are writing directly on the slides. The exam questions are so wildly specific and hard for no reason. She does offer extra credit, but…
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jordan was very kind and cares about what she was teaching, but this class was difficult! Lectures had so much content and went very quickly, slides had minimal words, and she read off a script the entire time. It was difficult to keep up with anything going on, and exams were very specific. She did offer extra credit. Would not rec. :(

Professor Jordan is very kind, but her lectures are not good. She reads off a wordy script, and you have to fight for your life to get down anything she says. She does not put many words on the slides, so you must re-watch the lecture if you miss anything. The exam questions are wild and very specific. I would NOT recommend this course to anyone.

Professor Jordan is amazing, lectures move really quickly but are engaging. The content is very focused on learning a bunch of studies to understand broader concepts, but it is taught very effectively. All criteria and assignments are clear and actually help you learn. She also offers assignments to make up missed attendance/participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her online course system was confusing, too many little assignments here and there to keep up with per week, and a random group project. For a 3-credit? This's doing too much. She would not let you make up anything you missed, not even under serious circumstances. Very heartless professor. Would not recommend taking any course with her.

- She was my only teachers that didn't let me make up work or extra credit
- Used reasons like how I would address her in emails to not give me a certain final grade
- She always thinks she's right & won't listen to you.
- She said I could get a C if I got a certain score on my final & I got that score she didn't give it to me
- Not flexible at all

She will not respond to any emails or posted canvas questions. Her syllabus was outdated and the TA listed was the TA for the class last year and isn't the current one. The current TA's email was not listed anywhere on her page. Go to class or you'll never hear from this woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Ashton is super nice and caring! She loves giving out extra credit so go to class and participate in the activities. She's not a great lecturer but there weren't any exams for online so it wasn't a big problem. Most annoying thing is all the group work, every Thursday was group work and if you have a bad group it sucks.
Do not take this class. She is horrible at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If I would have read the reviews on here first, I would not have taken this course. I can't believe this class happened to me... harder than Econ 101/102. This class moves SO quickly and the exams are impossible to finish in time. I do not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I do not recommend Lydia as a teacher. She reads off the slides word for word which leaves me with unanswered questions a lot of times. On top of that she goes through her slides very quickly. The exams are very long. I did not finish one of them within the class period. Overall would take different teacher if possible.

Avoid this class! I did fine, but seriously taught myself the majority of the material on my own. Prof is boring and just not good at teaching. I left most lectures confused. Her test grading is very lenient which is nice, but that was about the only good thing about the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Ashton flies through lectures and half the time, I don't understand anything that goes on. I have to set up extra time with the TA and attend office hours to really learn the material. Because this class is math based, its hard to learn math through a textbook, but in class, the math is not well-taught and steps are not clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a very fast/nervous lecturer and does not communicate the material well at all. Nearly everyone in my class leaves with a befuddled look on their face, just like me! Also I took an 8am class with her, showed up at 8:04 one day (no exageration) and was marked absent. Avoid her if possible.

It was very easy to get an 'A' in her class because she handed out extra credit at every turn. Her exams are very difficult and the material covered is not usually well-taught, but there a lot of other ways you can make up points. Don't worry, you will do just fine. Show up to class, and you will pass.

She flies through her slides and doesn't explain anything clearly. You have to read the book to understand the class. She blames the low exam averages (64) on students not going to office hours even though she only holds office hours once a week for one hour in the middle of the day - not that she would be able to explain things anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Half of her notes and exam reviews were incorrect, which makes it hard to learn. Assigns discussion posts and articles to read very last minute, if you don't check the class site frequently you can miss an assignment! Don't take unless absolutely have to!!!!

Professor Asen's lectures can run a bit dry and he is quite wordy when explaining concepts, but overall this was a very interesting course. Your grade is determined by lecture and discussion attendance, a few (pretty easy) speeches, exams, and papers. Be prepared to write, but it is nothing out of the norm for a Comm B course.

The assignments are well defined and really help you learn the content. It's a lot of writhing but not out of the ordinary for a Com B class. Lecture attendance is mandatory and it's important to take good notes, but you can tell that Professor Asen really knows the content and cares about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Asen's lectures are quite dry at times, but the content is important to know for tests and essays. He genuinely cares about the content and his students. However, they do take attendance at lecture which I found to be quite annoying at times. I would take a course taught by Professor Asen again!
Do not take his class
Interesting lectures and caring guy

Is a good professor, but sometimes he's a little fast with lectures and doesn't record so some of his important comments on the lecture slides can be hard to get. Overall if you just go to lectures and discussions you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brown does a wonderful job with this course. Attendance is not required, but I highly recommend going to every class. She makes lectures very engaging, and if you attend and take notes, it is much easier to complete the 2 papers and 2 exams. I highly recommend taking this class, especially if Professor Brown is the instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer and I really appreciated how she implemented class participation into lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but she doesn't post slides and you need the info from the slides in order to do well. All exams are online, open note and the class is graded by 2 essays and 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent amount of reading for required discussion section. No lecture notes posted. Exams were all online and fairly easy. Two papers and attendance made up the rest of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hernandez is very kind and cares a lot about his students. The class itself is challenging and it's definitely difficult to make interesting to learn about. I'd recommend going to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is particularly hard for being a freshman level class. It is not really his fault though because the content is hard and it is used as a weed out class. He is really funny and I appreciate how focused his lectures were on practice problems.

Antonio is a great professor for statics. He is interested in the topic himself, and therefore it is clear that he enjoys teaching it. 
He makes the course challenging, but not impossible, where you can still pass the class if you don't attend any of the lectures or discussions, but if you attend everything, then an A or B is not difficult.
One of the best professors in UW-Madison.

Antonio slows down his lecture a lot and cares a lot about his students. He also explains students questions very patiently, and gives a lot of extra credits in the end. His exams from my opinion are not hard as long as you fully prepare yourself.

Antonio is a great professor. He truly cares about his students. If you put in the work, you will get good results. He is available to help and provides numerous resources to support students' success. Exams are reasonable. Do the homework and show up, and you will do just fine.

Statics is a hard class. Hernandez does a good job in my opinion teaching this class. He cares about students understanding the material more than knowing how to do the problem. He really cares about students succeeding outside the classroom and in their future careers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good professor and seems to really care about his students. the class is hard and homework assignments are long, but the exams are relatively straight forward. lectures were recorded. i wish i had gone to more office hours, he seems very knowledgeable and eager to help

EMA 201 is one of the first challenging classes engineering students take, and Hernandez gets a lot of flak from that. Hernandez genuinely wants his students to succeed and has many opportunities for students to get help. Lectures can be confusing, but skimming the textbook beforehand helps a lot.

Antonio gets a lot of hate but I think a big part of it is this class is often people's first real college level engineering course and they haven't learned to properly study. The examples in lecture are really helpful, homework takes forever and is impossible without Chegg, discussions are useless. Content isn't actually that difficult though.

Dr. Hernandez is a nice professor who cares about the success of his students. The lectures can be confusing and jump straight into difficult material without a foundation. However, he is very encouraging of all students, and he wants everyone to succeed. The class is usually curved at the end. Lecture is mostly examples, but they are recorded.

Professor Hernandez cares about his students' learning and understanding of the material. He does move quickly while lecturing but does have practice problems in lectures to introduce material. The exams were fair and focused on material heavily covered in homework and lectures. There is also a lot of opportunity for extra help in the course.

I loved Professor Hernandez! This class was challenging, but Antonio made it more bearable. He cares so much about his students and although the homework takes a while it is worth taking your time with it to succeed in this course. Go to the study tables and do the practice problems and the tests should be fine.

Goes out of his way to create relationships with students. Very caring when it comes to students success as he spends lots of time at the weekly study groups. Exams are hard but can be predictable. Handwriting can be hard to read at times. Appropriate amount of homework for the class. I would definently take him again!
He's a pretty good professor, very funny but I don't think he's trying to be. The class is difficult but if you put in the work you'll get a lot out of it.

Professor Hernandez's ratings do not reflect how good of a professor is, statics is a tough class and I think he does a good job teaching it. His lectures had lots of example problems and to me it seemed like he truly cared about his students by being available. The one negative thing is his exams were always too long for the allotted time.

Very difficult class, but Prof. Hernandez is so kind and truly cares about his students' success. He tries his best to help everyone understand and he's very accessible if you need help. Do the homework and practice problems, pay attention in lecture, and take the preps course, and you'll be fine!!
Hard class, but Antonio cares about students and only makes the tests hard so we can be better.

Professor Hernandez is a nice guy but he does not care about student's success as much as he should. EMA201 is very much a weed-out course and he is the perfect professor for this position. The exams he creates are tough, usually require more time than given and graded hard. He also very rarely offers any sort of curve even with low class averages.

Statics is hard and certainly tested me but Hernandez clearly cared for me and other students.  It is clear he wants his students to pass and even stays after class to answer all questions outside his office hours. His exams are clearly defined on what's going to be on it and he provides plenty of prep materials each exam.
Students will ask questions and if the professor will dismiss or say rewatch the lecture as a response to confusion

Statics is a difficult class but Hernandez's lectures make the concepts very clear. He does 1 or 2 problems throughout the lecture which really helps you to understand the concepts and process. Exams were very fair. Most of his bad reviews here are students that are mad about things that are their own fault. Hernandez truly cares about students.

His lecture are straight to the point. He reviews what you read for 10ish minutes and does 2 tough problems in class. His exams are fair, if you put enough work in you'll get the results. Don't listen to the negativity about him since he does his best. Please get to know him during office hours as he truly does care about helping you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hernandez writes fair exams and assigns relevant homework that should help you prepare. However, his lecture style is very quick and doesn't expand on the conceptual aspects of the class. He spends most of his time working through the math rather than breaking down how to approach each problem. If you put in the work outside of class it is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It seems like Hernandez has improved over time. Despite the workload, he's dedicated and knowledgeable. Preparing before lectures is essential, and his availability during study tables is a plus. Past reviews do not reflect his current effectiveness. It has a heavy work load for only a 3 credit class, but it sets the groundwork and is essential.

Antonio is a great professor. The course is difficult, but he genuinely makes an effort to connect with students over the materials. If you are worried about your grade try to enroll in PREP (or get Chegg like every other student).

I enjoyed Professor Hernandez and I think people are too harsh on him. His lectures are clear and easy enough to understand, provided you actually put in the work outside of class to understand the material (which many do not)

Hernandez definitely cares for his students but overall is a poor professor. The amount of homework assigned is ridiculous for 3 credits and tends to take 4x the time of my other 3 credit classes. His lectures are useless and I stopped going. Do all the old exams a bunch of times and you'll do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a caring prof, and you can tell that he tries his best to explain concepts. He goes a little too fast as he tries to get in as many examples as he can. When going through examples, more or less explains how he got from point A to point B. Statics is hard and you need to try, I feel that people take their anger out on him :/ the tests are fair

Professor Hernandez, in my opinion was a good lecturer. Very cut and dry. He tells you exactly what you need to do. he goes through examples kind of fast, but lectures were only 50 mins so not sure if he could really control that. The homework study group he held was always helpful. He provides a lot of ways to get assistance in the class.

Statics is not a 3 credit class, expect a lot of outside time spent studying the materials as you will learn little in lecture. The lectures themselves were fast paced and it was really easy to fall behind. The homework was much harder than what you would see on an exam, and had few attempts to check if you got the answer right.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of people talk badly about Prof. Hernandez, but I felt like he was one of the best professors I've had. People need to go into EMA201 understanding that it's hard, by no means is it a piece of cake. Prof. Hernandez gives you everything and more you need to succeed while also making the exams fair. His lectures really help you get the concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Hernandez is a solid professor. He moves quickly through lectures, but it's only because he is limited on time. Outside of lectures, like in office hours, he's more than happy to help students with homework and practice problems. Hernandez seems to strive for keeping the material interesting and keeping the exams fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He's very articulate and teaches well. People just don't like him because the class is hard and he has to go at a decent speed to get through all the material. He's a goat tho fs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hernandez while being an amazing professor gets a bad wrap from the difficulty for many freshman. The course itself is harder than most and sometimes unintuitive, but Hernandez does try his best and is always open to answering questions to help you better understand the subject. Don't let his rating push you away from taking the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Before taking statics I heard that it was one of tge toughest courses I will go through as a mechanical engineer, but with Hernandez it wasn't as hard as I thought.
