He made understanding easier, and his lectures cover all the material. The homework also help in understanding. He is just amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Okay lecturer but material is presented right for how hard class is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The guy cares a lot. He really wants his students to succeed. Although he sometimes teaches in a slow way, he drives the important concepts and sets up a good foundational understanding for my remainder academic career.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wow. Just wow.

Statics is already difficult and this class is not curved. He makes it harder because he is not good at explaining and his quiz questions are often unclear and ambiguous. He very much gives off the impression that he doesn't like teaching entry level students and gets frustrated when he has to explain simple concepts.

Overall I think prof. Hernandez did a good job teaching this class. It was a little rough at first but he listened to student feedback and changed things for the better. Lots of homework, and exams were worth a large portion of your grade. Partial credit saves you on the exams. If you watch the lectures, do the homework, and study, you will do fine

This is a very difficult class, but it was even harder with his teaching. Lectures were very hard to pay attention to, and discussions & OH were not very helpful. You're going to have to rely on the textbook and find other lectures on YouTube. Homework takes forever and exams were very tough, but they were graded pretty generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: EMA 201 is extremely challenging, and teaching this class is not easy, but I could see that Professor Hernandez gave his best. The start of the semester started rough, but the professor was willing to receive feedback from his students and fix the problems. He deserves a 5 because of his effort and improvement throughout the semester.

The form of honorlock he used throughout the semester was the most invasive form possible. You were required to show the entire room in which you were taking the exam and you were not allowed to take it in public areas. I felt like he invaded my privacy and it added an extremely unnecessary amount of stress to the exams in this class.
He does seem to kind of care about his students but the problem is that he just sucks at teaching. Lectures are monotone and cover the material but the book itself does a better job.

Professor Hernandez definitely cares about his students and gives them resources to be successful, but seems to get a bad rap because statics isn't easy. Even though his lectures aren't the most interesting, they still help to do the homework and his grading on tests is pretty lenient. Tests are basically like the homework questions.

Yes, his lectures aren't the most interesting, and this class is a lot of work. However, like some other reviews have said, he clearly cares about his students. The grading when it comes to exams is generous in my opinion, based primarily off of your approach and steps vs numerical values. Not as bad as everyone says.

I agree with a lot of the crap this guy gets. Hes very monotone, and when someone asks a question, hes never concise or clear. However, the structure of the lectures must be exactly what I need. 10 minutes explaining the concept directly, and 2-3 practice problems that he explains very in-depth. Ive only used textbook practice problems once

Often tries to belittle students during Friday lectures. Many tests are purposely confusing so he can have gottcha questions which do nothing to help learning. You have to just learn the equations and do everything else yourself. It is the work of a five credit class for only three credits.

Hernandez is a smart guy but he is very obviously not ready for an online format. His lectures are horribly boring, he just has white slideshows where he goes over content from the book in monotone. If you have to take the class for your major, read the textbook, go to SST to do homework, skip lectures because they're useless.
Worst professor I've ever had.

It is ridiculous how little effort someone can put into their job and still keep it. He sounds like he wants nothing to do with his students as well as the school whatsoever. I have never seen someone so unmotivated not to mention his massive ego which gets in the way of his teaching.

Just because you went to MIT doesn't make you a good prof Hernandez stop trying to use how smart you are as an excuse for why the whole class is failing and making us feel dumber than you. YOU are the problem.

Whenever a student has a question, he always finds a way to avoid answering it halfway through because he is such a poor communicator and can't manage his time properly when lecturing and just ends up making everyone more confused with his nonsensical and broken explanations, if he even bothers explaining at all. So arrogant and condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Maybe not the most interesting class but he makes in 10 times more boring than it has to be just with a lack of enthusiasm. He will give you such a headache. Just look at all the ratings he has since going online, not one good review.

He cares more about being right than being clear. A student found a direct contradiction between his quiz question and the textbook and he ignored this completely. He words all of his questions in a way meant to trick his students, he doesn't care how much you struggle in class and is too impatient to answer questions.

Professor Hernandez is the most frustrating educator I've ever experienced. His weekly quizzes are written to trick you, testing you on your reading comprehension more than anything else. Unfortunately, his ego prevents him from communicating the material clearly. Beware, you will be teaching yourself this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is the only option when it comes to choosing an instructor for this statics class. He gives weekly quizzes which are worded terribly. Each week he constantly makes mistakes and students make valid arguments, but he simply doesn't listen. He also doesn't put effort into his recorded lectures, he could not be any more boring than he actually is.
All of the quizzes in this class aim to trick students.
I have never heard someone talk so much and yet say so little...
Hernandez teaching statics is like an annoying boss battle you have to beat to before accessing the rest of the college of engineering.
He is the most useless ad careless professor I have ever seen
What a horrendous professor and just person in general
Wow. what more can I say about this guy that hasnt been said yet

When he's not bragging about how he went to MIT during his pointless lectures that are mostly nonsense, he tells us how dumb we are when the test averages are too low and offers no solution. Not the type of person you want teaching a class like this, he is so egotistic and narcissistic. I wish he put as much effort into teaching as he does bragging

He is a very bad professor, after watching his lecture videos I was tremendously confused. He teaches as if we all knew the concepts coming into the class. If you ask for help he tells you to try harder and calls it a day. Everyone does very poorly on most exams and he seems not to care or change his teaching.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS

You should see some of the emails this guy sends to the entire class. If there is ever an exam that the class does poorly on as a whole, he sends an email immediately after asking people not to contact him about grades and usually adds a passive aggressive comment where he blames the class. Its really unfortunate he's the only statics professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worse professor I have had yet. He talks like the human version of Eeyore. It boggles me that a man can show so little enthusiasm in the content and show even less care for his students. Any questions lead to condescending answers to make you feel dumb. In his mind, he's never wrong. Lectures only make you more confused than anything.

This guy thinks he is such a great teacher and talks with such a high sense of pride over his knowledge and thinks he has some type of power over us as a Statics professor, but in reality he is so unaware of how poor of a communicator he is and never seems to get the point across in a sensible manner. Should be fired, shame on him and CoE
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have had. This class takes a ton of time and he is such an ineffective teacher that I still learned very little from him. He is extremely harsh and condescending. Told my lecture (250 ppl) that the exam average was bad because of our collective laziness. He is a horrible teacher on a massive power trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Long Homework, pointless lecture, terrible class all around, Hernandez makes the entire thing so much worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For EMA 201 I found that professor Hernandez cares about his students, but I found that the way he presents material tends to be over complicated. If you like learning every small detail about something instead of learning the essentials, then this is the professor for you. Overall, not bad, but not the best professor Ive ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely nothing good to say about him, avoid

Very bad communicator, takes the simplest concepts and tries to explain them in the most complicated way possible, really unnecessary for such a fundamental class. Also arrogant and condescending. Perfect example of how going to MIT doesn't mean you're a good teacher, go back to MATC and learn how to teach, that place suit your skills more than UW

He's a nice guy for sure. Unfortunately, that's not all being a professor is about. He is very unspecific/unforgiving on grading criteria and you can't miss even one lengthy homework assignment because they are worth so much. He is very condescending at times, also getting mad at students quietly explaining problems to their friends during class.

Prof. Hernandez clearly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are helpful but not necessary, most of the learning is done through the homework. While the homework is difficult, it is so important. He holds SSTs which are helpful and also allow him to get to know your name- I recommend going.

EMA 201 is originally a tough class to teach. I'm not sure if he teaches really well, but what I can assure is that he really tries hard to help students. He is even available during drop-in tutoring, and enjoys explaining things to students. Even when he fails to explain things, he remembers it and later sends scanned paper work through email.

Hernandez isn't the worst professor you could have for a hard class like this, but he's not great. His lectures move very fast and it's easy to miss things, and he spends little time explaining core concepts (he covers examples in class and expects you to learn concepts on your own). Tests are hard, discussions are unhelpful, homeworks are long.

He's a great prof! Very clear and works problems in class. He always helps calm us down before tests and has quickly become one of my favorite profs. Do yourself a favor and talk to him before or after class even just to introduce yourself, very personable guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He really tries his hardest for students and cares a lot he's just not the best teacher and lecturer ever. He over explains simple concepts and can be confusing. It is probably a very hard class to teach, but sometimes he can make it harder than it needs to be. Chegg is really useful. Be prepared to put in the work if you want to be successful.

He messes up quite a bit during lecture which is frustrating and leaves you a little bit lost. He only does examples in class and expects you to watch 3 hours of lecture videos outside of class. Test are tough and discussions suck. However, he's a really sweet guy and cares a lot about students succeeded. He will help you if you ask for it.

Antonio had little quirks that made him a bit annoying as a professor but seems like a good guy overall. He often glazed over what he thought was easy, but also would write out ALL of the steps in lecture. He was pretty set in his ways in terms due dates and class structure. Discussions sucked. Lectures put me to sleep. Watch the videos!!!

Checks all the boxes to be a good professor: accessible by email and responds timely (I once emailed him at 1:05 AM and he responded by 1:15 AM), cares for students to do well, and makes content other than his lectures available to students to learn more on their own. However, he just sucks at teaching/lecturing, is very boring, and messes up a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is a very hard class. He expects you to watch 3 hours of lecture video each week which is just too much. You can tell he really cares about his students and tries to help people succeed but doesn't really explain the concepts in lecture and just does example problems in class. If you want to succeed I would strongly recommend preps

Messes up a lot in class making the material more confusing. Not very good at explaining things, just kinda assumes you know stuff and skips over important math steps during class. Tries to tell jokes during class but they are just annoying. Sadly, he is the only professor who teaches the class at Madison so ur just stuck with him. Sorry in advance

Great teacher! Connect homework questions are tedious and obnoxious, It takes sometimes 3 hours on a set of homework questions every week but at least they help you master what you are learning. Antonio genuinely cares about how you do in class and he is willing to help as long as you show that you are trying. The class is tough, that's engineering

Antonio was great! He made sure to clearly show every little step in his solutions and the thinking behind his process. Many people said statics was an incredibly difficult class, but taking it with Antonio with his first semester of teaching the course, I think it was an average difficulty. He really cares and wants to see his students succeed.
The class is extremely difficult and you must be ready to spend hours on the homework but he is very helpful and is always willing to put in the extra time to help you.

Was a 5th-grade teacher and it shows, doesn't speak up, and doesn't provide clear instructions. Often rambles. Not professional. Uses derogatory language because its 'in the legislation', also stereotypes. skipped entire disability groups because 'lack of time'. However, the workload isn't too much and exams are open resource unlimited attempts.
The single worst class and professor of my life. Didn't learn a thing, all questions, homework, exams, and quizzes were horribly constructed, and every lecture felt like the same material. STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this class and Professor White. It wasn't difficult and she seemed like she cared about the material. The only thing is that I don't feel like the CBL was integrated well into the class. You're only required to do one discussion post a week and there's only a few quizzes that are pretty easy. I never read the textbook and was fine.

She is super nice and the class was actually so easy. She cancel class a lot. Best part of class is when people come to speak. Lectures are super short. She means well but seems to not really know what she's doing. Basically always graded on completion I ended with a 100%. If you're an education major def take this class its a breeze.

Dr. White is very kind and very intelligent, but there really isn't anything to glean from her lectures. She won't record class if you're ill or offer virtual options, even though her class is on accessibility for those with disabilities. The CBL component is poorly integrated with the course as a whole, but it is the only redeeming factor here.

Might just be me, but I felt she was sometimes disinterested in being there, a little disorganized, and was gone way too much. Don't miss a lecture - she doesn't take attendance but it's hard to keep up if you aren't in class - you won't do well on the quizzes without the little nuggets of info you get from lecture.

He puts whole essay's worth of information on every slide. Not easy to keep up since the exams will cover everything in the slides. I took this class early on in my undergrad so my study strategies had room for improvement. I recommend taking this class later if you can, even if you are on the biomaterials track.

Long readings are assigned with reading quizzes before each lecture and the readings are pretty dense. Three exams make up most of your grade. Dr. Ashton is a nice person and very passionate about his research in biomaterials, but he goes through lecture slides quickly considering how much information they contain and lectures can be a bit dry.

Hands down worst BME class I have taken. The first day he tells you the only way to succeed in the class is to memorize the slides. Then, he proceeds to give you a 50 page reading assignment every lecture. I spent days studying for the exams (which make up the entire grade btw) just to get average. Lectures are boring, he just reads off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you are interested in biomaterials and tissue engineering, you wont be after this class. Dr. Ashton doesnt explain any background information and spends the entire hour and fifteen minutes talking at you about concepts you dont understand and refuses to clarify them. The reading makes no sense and he tests you on it after admitting its hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes you read A LOT. The exams are all short answer and essay, but he tells you the possible topics ahead of time. Also on the final we were allowed to have a "notecard" which was actually a full sheet of paper. I don't like history and I thought this was an easy class

Need to attend lecture to pass. A lot of outside reading and homework assignments that are grades pretty toughly. Essays are graded extremely hard, so the finals and midterms are easy except for the essay portion which get graded tough.  Gives pop quizzes on random classes usually every other Friday so you must show up. TAs arent helpful either.

Professor Biss was a good teacher. His lectures were straightforward and his tests were easy (Pretty much like vocabulary tests). Lots of reading assigned but it's usually just background for the information in lecture. Read the textbook if you need more info but I really enjoyed his class!

I have taken 2 classes with prof Atis and she is probably my favorite professor. Sometimes she seems distracted but don't let this fool you, she knows what she's talking about and is incredibly smart. She's very clear about what's going to be on the test, her lectures aren't super structured but I enjoyed class and what she had to say.

Nobody pays attention, all you have to do is read all the stories and readings for a few days before the final, memorize those pretty well, and you will get an A on the 20% final. Papers are graded fairly easy, 20% of grade is a comparative paper, 40% is research paper, 10% is oral presentation of said research paper, 10% is attendance

I am not exaggerating when I say that 3/4 of the students sat in the back of class and read the newspaper or did other work. Nobody has any idea what is going on half the time. Prof. Atis is a poor lecturer. However, she is extremely knowledgeable in the field of Turkish studies and has written alongside other renowned Turkish researchers worldwide

Took this class on a whim, great bc it knocks out lit and comm b credits. Atis is a funny old woman, very knowledgeable and important in the field, however the class is scattered and hard to follow. Her stories are wheezy and cute though, you can't help but chuckle. Easy A though, I 'd take it again

Took this class on a whim, great bc it fulfills lit and comm b credits. Atis is a funny old woman, very knowledgeable and important in the field, however the class is scattered and hard to follow. Her stories are wheezy and cute though, you can't help but chuckle. Easy A though, I 'd take it again

Not really sure what to make of Prof. Atis. It's a good class to take if you need to fulfill requirements, I guess.  She is helpful and will go out of her way to answer questions and make sure that your papers are coming along well.
Very nice professor and very interesting class!
she jumps all over during discussion, her notes were about 9 random words on the board, and i could never hear her...so basically i sat in back and read magazines and i didn't really miss much

I signed up for Turkish folk lit. not really knowing anything about it and I ended up loving the class! A little hard to hear at times, but just sit up front or better yet stop by office hours. She'll be more than happy to work with you, she's extremely nice helpful and encouraging. Really cares about students.
could never hear her

She was the main lecturer for my course. She did a terrible job, the TAs didn't even know what was going on in class half the time. The class was poorly organized. Since the TAs made the test and told us what was going to be on it, I did good in the class.

She seems like a nice lady, but her lectures are so boring because she wanders off talking about her life experience insead of relating to the readings.  A lot of reading required but the tests weren't that hard if you study enough, I never paid attention in lecture and still got an A

I had this professor for a seminar on travel writing.  The course is very writing intensive but Prof. Atis offers excellent feedback.  Her style is very casual and perfect for those who are engaged students.

i had her as a guest lecturer, and i had a very hard time following her train of thought, her notes.. i had no clue what i was supposed to get out of the lecture. so if you have her as a guest lecturer, consider skipping the class if possible. i must say, though, that she seems like a very sweet lady who probably does better in smaller settings.

Taken in the summer. The class was interesting, though a bit preachy. Attendance was mandatory, and reading responses were required every evening. Easy material, though the lectures were very long. Prof was able to break up the monotony of the 2.5 hr lecture with movies, music, stories.
No Comments
it was an awful painful experience, will never take Persian in my life ..... hate the Prof and the course

One of the Best teachers Ive had in every aspect.  Teaches well, and even caters to your learning style.  Gets everyone to bring delicious food.  No one really falls asleep during class because she keeps it exciting.  However we call her crazy atefeh because, well shes just plain crazy.

The best class I'm taking this semester is her class. I can not miss any. She is the best ever. I like her style. and all of what she says is great. I hope she can be my prof. for all of the subjects, so  I will be able to learn everything.
Extremely nice and caring woman.  Every teacher should be like her.
Atefeh is such an awesome teacher!! She makes the class fun, no matter what we are learning.

I had 492 and 498. Did not see him once during the semester. Lectures are recorded with little to no flow/connectivity. Important concepts quickly glanced through. Quizzes and exams are oddly specific. Seems to enjoy saying he's a prominent part of the research in the construction field rather than teaching tangible content. Unavoidable though.

He seems like a nice guy and knowledgeable on the subject, but the class has little flow and is ambiguous. It's hard to tell what's really important and what's not. The quiz and test questions are extremely ambiguous and specific. A lot of busy work in the class too. No real guide for what the most important takeaways are.

Professor Hanna is an unavoidable part of the Civil Engineering department, which is unfortunate. All quizzes are based upon vague lectures from 2012 that Professor Hanna recorded, but there are many important topics that he glosses over in these lectures. He spends hours on things that don't matter, and quickly runs through the important stuff.
Great at breaking concepts down in an understandable way. He's got a good dry sense of humor as well.
Not a good professor to take compiler course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You wont just learn how a compiler works, youll build one from start to finish! This is no small task, which is why its split into 6 projects (20 hours/project) that build on each other. Can still be quite nerve-racking. Aws is a friendly fellow. TL;DR Not easy but highly instructive

Lots of info in one semester, but definitely manageable. Lectures were engaging, projects were good, but some used tools older than the students with bad documentation, which was frustrating at times. Midterm & exam weren't too bad, but definitely required some studying. I'd take a course w/ him again for sure.

Aws is pretty fantastic. I'll be honest, I am not particularly interested in Compilers, but he found a way to make it interesting. I feel like a learned a lot of useful knowledge in a class where I didn't really have that expectation. He does a great job in lecture and has clear and fair assignments and tests.

Excellent professor with engaging lectures. Cannot recommend him higher. Reasonable workloads, values quality of work over quantity, very available for questions and concerns, course was strong in theory but his lectures were in plain English and he did a great job of making it easy to grok the abstract.
Good at breaking down concepts in an understandable way, always willing to go back and answer questions to make sure everyone understands the material, holds useful review sessions before tests.

He is passionate about both the subject and teaching and it shows. While I recommend going to lecture, he publishes full notes online and they are amazing. The projects are a bit repetitive but make sure that you understand the material. Overall a really solid professor.

Programming projects were way too long and complicated, and often failed to reinforce the information learned in class. I found the professor's homework assignments to be very tedious, and left way too much room for interpretation and contained plenty of vague wording, which is what you don't want on a programming project.
He's not a terrible professor, but the class is kinda boring and he doesn't really change that. Nice in office hours, though.

This guy came in and copied everything from the previous professor. Course page, homeworks, lecture slides -- you name it. Didn't even bother to update the assignments to change info from last year's class to this year's. My partner and I submitted buggy code and somehow received 100%, seems like he just wants to look good.

Aws was fantastic! His lectures were really clear and helpful. The course had a lot of material online that supplemented what we covered and was great review. I visited office hours once with him and he wasn't super helpful, but the TA's were fantastic. He was also willing to adjust my grade at the end of the semester. Would definitely recommend!

You can tell he knows the material but he just flat out can not teach it. Therefore, going to discussion and having a good TA is very important. He stutters a lot during lecture and often times talks very fast but essentially reads off the slides.

If you want to pass the class with a good grade, you need to have a really good and passionate T.A(which I had) for Richard's section. Richard, most of the time, stuttered a lot, on top of that, he was unprepared for many lectures. I believe he is a good teacher, but there needs to be a lot of improvement.

AVOID HIM!! He mumbles horribly, You can't understand him at all, and he is VERY unhelpful. The tests took 3 weeks to get a grade back. I went into this class thinking it would be one of my favorites but it was absolutely terrible.

Avoid him! Explanations of material = incomprehensible. Moves through material wayyy too fast but yet was so uneven that @ the end of course, left out 3 chapters of the book when he ran out of time. Really put me at a disadvantage for my next stats course. Vague guidelines for papers but then grades like you're a PhD student. Take w/ someone else!

Horrible, horrible, horrible TA/prof. Full of herself, made students feel stupid, regardless of whether they were also native speakers or not. If it wasn't Mexican Spanish, it was wrong. She is impossible to please, a horrible person in general & had too high of expectations. For the love of everything holy, TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR OR WAIT FOR ONE

Very very difficult class. Heard from friends that other 311 classes were a breeze! I worked my butt off and only ended up with a B because I needed the retro credits. She has impossible expectations for students.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. she does little to nothing to help you do well in the class. even if you ask for help, she will not correct anything on your papers and will wait for u to turn it in so she can give u a C. I've gotten A's in every spanish class I've ever taken. Avoid her at all costs.

Doesn't give clear instructions for hardly anything. Expects you to read her mind. Grades unfairly and expects you to be visiting her during office hours constantly. Gives excessive homework. Nevertheless, I feel like I did learn alot altho she is a terrible grader and even though I'm doing everything I can I probably won't get the A I deserve.

Horrible professor with ridiculous grading scale. She had ridiculous expectations that she never clearly states, but rather expects from students. She's helpful if you go to office hours but you have to put in a lot more effort than the class is worth. Avoid her if you can!
Terrible teacher.  Impossible to get a good grade.  Don't take her if you can help it.

This semester was horrific.  I'm fairly positive this was her first time teaching 311 and it showed.  The textbook we used was great, but her expectations were absolutely ridiculous and the amount of homework was insane.  There are currently no A's in at least 2 of her 3 sections.  We're taking a petition to the Spanish department head about Maria.

She was tough...I had to work hard...But this class was the BEST Spanish class I've ever taken...I worked the hardest I've ever worked in a Spanish class but I also learned THE MOST Spanish I've ever learned in a semester...HIGHLY RECOMMEND for anyone seriously interested in learning and truely understanding Spanish grammar, etc.!
She was ok...pretty much no personality though and always seemed a little pissed off. The tests are hard, but the rest of the class is pretty easy.

Maria was impersonabe at first, but after getting to know her you realize she tries to help. However, if you don't ask, she won't go out of her way to make sure you are not struggling. The tests are difficult but consistent. Not the most fun or exciting professor, kind of a bummer, but if you get used to her and ask questions you will learn.

Maria was definitely tough - the exams were nearly impossible and she's a VERY strict grader on papers - but by the middle of the semester, I knew what to expect.  She was ALWAYS available for her students - she even ran a study group for us once a week.  I definitely reccommend her to anyone who wants to learn a lot and work hard.

I didn't like her that much during the class because she wasn't the most helpful HOWEVER after seeing her around after the class had ended, I am very glad I had her. She is a very nice and perfectly willing to help you out. The tests are hard, but they are consistent and predictable. Nothing was a surprise..we knew it was going to be hard.
she is terrible teacher who doesn't clarify anything and doesn't teach you anything. You listen to music and then get hard ass exams on stuff you never went over in class.
No Comments
She didn't treat everyone equally.  She had the students teach and she didn'e explain things at all.  I would never take her again.
No Comments

Professor Zhu is a nice guy, but his class is way too hard for how it should be. Labs are hard to follow and I'm rather chasing the way too general instructions most of the time instead of learning GIS skills. No clear lab grading criteria, which is rough when it makes up most of your grade. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A-Xing seems passionate about his field, but this does not translate well into his teaching skills. Online lectures are extremely dry. His accent is difficult to understand, and no reliable subtitles are provided. Exam questions had many grammatical errors and some did not make sense at all. Lectures also haven't been updated since 2020.

The class is fun and the material that he presents is very educational. The lecture videos are also pretty solid. However, his English writing makes it very challenging to understand the exam questions and the written lectures. In addition, a lot of the class is just memorizing what he says is the correct answer in his lectures.

He is obviously very passionate about GIS and really wants to make sure his students know what's going on "under the hood" with many of the spatial methods and tools that he covers. The broken English that he uses in his readings and tests can be irritating, but as long as you understand the material you'll do fine. Very nice guy and truly cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He seems to be a nice guy, but with broken English in lectures and quizzes, which make it so hard, boring and despair for me. The quiz is like choose the most correct but with the broken English (you know it's gonna be nightmare).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy, but his lectures were so boring. It takes days for assignments to be graded and you don't really know what you have in the class for the whole semester. Exams were pretty difficult and the grading for them is pretty harsh.

He is terrible at explaining things and hard to understand, lectures put me to sleep even though they were online.  Lab directions were clear but are extremely frustrating, especially if you have never used ArcGIS before.  I would recommend taking 370 before this class.  I love the topics but he made it so boring.

I had him for 377 and currently have him for 579. There's an online textbook which I believe he wrote himself, since he always credits his work in it. You must read this to understand what's happening in class. He's obviously a smart guy but the content is incredibly boring and there's a lot of broken english in the textbook, which makes it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Zhu is a great professor who is passionate about GIS. He presents topics very clearly in lecture. Lecture is not required, but you will not do well in the class if you do not go. You need to do the work to do well. The tests are very difficult, there are pop quizzes, and lab attendance is required. The class is slightly curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A-Xing is super nice and really cares about the subject. He get's really into the lectures and his mannerisms are very cute. The topics can get boring, but he tries to simplify them as much as possible and tries hard to get them across. Has a good attitude about learning and school.

Labs very useful and applicable but lectures suck. 2 power lectures (75 min)/week and eventually stopped going. Very enthusiastic about the topic however usually strays off topic to boast how the U.S. has much better GIS than the rest of the world and he is often wrong on these tangents. 5 pop-quizzes worth 5pts each. Exams have obscure questions
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams are tough. He is passionate about the subject. Most of the time lectures are good!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty good because he is very passionate about his field. However, sometimes his lectures can be a bit boring as he goes on in excessive detail about things that often you are not interested in related to GIS. The exams are tough. He grades them hard. Labs are time-consuming but easy.

An excellent professor. There's a lot of class material and it can get dry at times, but he explains it clearly, enthusiastically, references real life examples/relevant stories to make it more interesting, and is happy to help during office hours. His accent is about on par with Martin Yan(TV chef), so its nothing to worry about. Solid overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had Axing for 579 and 377. I think he is a good professor and disagree with the reviews that say he is unclear. He explains most concepts very well. The issue is that there is a lot of material to cover and some concepts are just difficult to grasp. Go to class, think through the labs, and study for the exams and you will easily get an A.

A-xing is friendly, yet is truly a terrible teacher. His accent makes him difficult to understand and he has a very rambling way of lecturing, so it's very difficult to follow. He's incredibly bad at explaining complicated topics. Had him for Intro to GIS, Spatial Analysis, and GIS Apps; had to teach myself.  Wish there was a different professor.

Great Class - Very insightful abt the process of GIS applications and scientific thought, Had a lot of cross over into other course work. He is a very enthusiastic instructor about his topic. Labs were a bit long but the lectures were great.

Great instructor. You can tell he seriously knew the material. He was difficult to understand at times because of chinese accent but it never got in the way. Very comfortable with questions and always willing to help. The class was challenging, not because of Zhu, there was simply a lot of material. Definitely not a class you can skip often though

The only part I liked about this class was the lab. The lectures were boring and sometimes hard to understand because of 1-A-xing's accent and 2-the fact that he is just bad at explaining things in a way that can be understood. I would NOT recommend taking 377 if A-xing is the professor. It was painful.

It's unfortunate that Dr. Zhu is supposedly a great UW prof, when he's never there.  Seriously, he's never around.  Our TA taught our class way more than him.  But, our TA was a better prof than him.  The classes could be interesting , but he has a way of making it seem like you actually don't want to learn this stuff.
No Comments
Axel is INCREIDBLE!!!! You will adore him, he is funny and great and you learn a lot from him!!! He is great I highly recommend taking him! He will make sure you pass
Great TA. helped me a lot during his office hours, very accesible. Funny as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Axel is a great guy. He's funny and makes the class really interesting. As long as you do what is expected of you, there is no reason for you not to get at least a B in his class. Excellent professor and I definitely would recommend to take a class from him if you get the chance!
Charismatic guy who knows his stuff.

Funny and entertaining professor! Will work with you one-on-one for papers, which I highly recommend. He enjoys students who are outgoing and put themselves out there. However, don't ask a stupid question or he will call you out in front of the class.
Axel is awesome. He is a crazy Cuban that does not care what you do in class. Very little work and quite easy to get a good grade.
THE WORST.

Axel is really nice and makes class very interesting. He basically tell you exactly what will be on the tests/exams. If you go to class you will be fine but missing one you won't get the material because he can't really further explain some of the grammar material. Overall his class is not hard.
Axel is an awesome teacher. He is super helpful, extremely nice, and it is an easy class. If you are willing to learn in his class, you will.

Axel is a huge linguist, which makes his class pretty awful because he spends a ton of time talking about what can used here or there, and as a result we do almost no speaking in class. Very nice and friendly, but my Spanish is not any better after this semester. He sends us home early a lot because he is "tired." Avoid if you want to learn Spanish

super charismatic as well as clever and helpful TA. Knows his subject well. the way he teaches is amazing - he actually made me want to come to class. there were no classes that were boring in his course.
Not recommended. Stay away!

I took ILS 205 Fall 23 and would highly recommend it. He's a fantastic lecturer- I always felt like I really understood the dense readings after lectures. I had Avramenko himself for discussion and liked it- he really pushed students to think more about the texts and truly listened to everyone's personal thoughts and philosophical ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't take class if you want easy humanities credit. Grade is entirely dependent on TA and A's are hard to come by. I didn't read a single of the 7 assigned readings, all I did was show up to every lecture and take notes. He doesn't post anything so lectures are crucial. Finished with an AB.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing prof. Definitely recommend to any incoming freshman or even sophomores. Lectures are usually entertaining and hilarious. Classwork is tolerable, lots of reading, but even if you don't do the readings you'll be fine. Great class and great guy overall.

ILS 205 is very reading heavy, so if you don't have the time to either read the 7+ books, or at least their summaries, I would not recommend. However, if Plato, Aristotle, etc. are people you are interested in, I would absolutely recommend. He is an amazing lecturer. Def my favorite professor I've ever had. Super funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avramenko is an incredible lecturer and person. I almost dropped the course after seeing the reading list, but his lectures made me stick around. Really interesting content, and discussions are worthwhile and engaging. Show up/pay attention, do the readings, and study a little, and you should do just fine in the course. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The reading is terrible - it's dry and there's A LOT of it - but Avramenko is a good lecture and tries to make class interesting. The exams aren't too difficult but the papers can be. If you go to class everything's pretty straight forward, if you don't you can still get an A you'll just have a lot of work outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer and very intelligent. He does come off as kind of pretentious and arrogant but he knows the material inside and out. Everyone definitely needs to come to class because nothing is posted online. The readings are very heavy . Attendance to lectures aren't necessary but you will have lots of work outside of class.

There is a lot of classical reading involved with ILS 205! If you don't feel comfortable reading Plato, Homer, etc, then this class is not for you. Prof. Avramenko can seem a bit pretentious at times but is overall an excellent lecturer. His lecture outlines are not posted online, so take good notes in class. The exams and 1 paper are fairly easy.

This class is ridiculously easy if you read what's assigned (and have some interest in it) and show up to lecture. Like Avramenko says, he's not trying to trip you up at all - all exam questions are very fair and straightforward. Lecture is so important!! He explains literally everything that could be on the test thoroughly

Avramenko makes an otherwise fairly boring class topic so interesting. So much required reading that I would usually hate, but because he's so entertaining I'm obsessed. Taking 206 next semester because I just love.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Avramenko is an okay professor. His sense of humor comes out during lecture, but can come off as arrogant at times. Overall, the class was easy if the reading is done.

Professor Avramenko is a very smart man, he speaks very clearly and he makes things interesting and easy to understand.  One bad thing about his lectures was his talk about his political beliefs.  Since it was election season I understand it was hard, but it definitely took away from his lectures.

I enjoyed this class, however I found Avramenko's lectures a bit hard to follow at times. Maybe it just didn't vibe with my learning style. I felt that he kind of jumped around on subjects and that made it feel unorganized. He certainly knows what he is talking about though!

I'm in love with ILS 205, I actually signed up for it on accident and it was the best mistake of my life. Avramenko is very funny and engaging. I can actually understand Plato's Republic because of this class. I'm already looking forward to signing up for ILS 206 for next semester.
Hes lectures were very interesting, I learned a lot from the class. His tests were straight forward and you did well in the class if you showed up to class, went to discussion and read the books.

Honestly, I did not like the course material a ton, but Avramenko really makes lectures engaging.  The tests do require some thought, and you need to be good at writing.  Your grade is really up to your TA as they grade everything in the class.  If you are unclear about anything in the class, go to Avramenko's office hours; he is fun to talk to.

Avramenko is awesome. His ILS 205 and 206 courses actually steered me in the direction I'm heading in. Arrogant? Not really. Some people here mistake brilliancy with arrogance, and that's sad. Don't let those reviews turn you away. He's so smart, clear, and hilarious. Take his class!

Prof. Avramenko is an amazing lecturer as he is very funny and interesting. The subject matter is very thought provoking and the readings can be enjoyable if you are into that type of stuff. Show up to lectures, discussion, and read the readings and you'll pass no problem. Would recommend to anyone looking for a humanities.

Hes lectures were very interesting to listen too and i learned a lot from them. His tests were straight forward and you did well in the class if you showed up to class, went to discussion and read the books.
Makes his class very interesting and plays music before each lecture, but assigns a lot of reading.  If you go to class and do the readings, his class is not that difficult

Nice guy, but unnecessary amount of reading and he pulls small vocab out of the text to test you on the final exam. TA completely determines your grade as he grades your paper, and all of your tests. When i had it one TA was noticeable easier so it kind of depends who you have as a TA. DO NOT TAKE UNLESS YOU ENJOY READING BOOKS FROM THE 13t century

Awesome professor! Avramenko is clearly very passionate about the subject and relates things in class to the world. He plays a song at the beginning of every class. Tons of reading, but you can just skim and he'll explain what you need to know.

Engaging lectures that keep your interest. Read the material and the test will be easy. Don't read and struggle with the tests. Highly recommend him and this class for any student no matter the major.

I would've loved this class if not for the fact that the TA determines your entire grade.  Professor Avramenko is one of the coolest, funniest, most knowledgeable professors I've had but the course involves a lot of considerably superfluous reading assignments and an inevitably less qualified TA. I'd rather audit this class than take it for a grade
great class! it is very clear that avramenko loves this subject. the tests aren't that bad if you study and discuss well in your section. taking 206 next semester and i'm excited!

I did not expect to like this class, but I LOVED it. The readings were great and Professor Avramenko was awesome. he played music at the beginning of class that tied into that day's discussion, and it was obvious he loved the topic. if I have a chance to take the "sequel" of this class, I am definitely going to.

Great lecturer. His lecture material is important, since 30% of the tests are from the key terms he defines in class. The rest is on an essay with prompts that are interesting and graded rather easily. Overall good professor, 205 is a take if you need to take some more credits.
Exams have very little to do with what you read.  Go to lecture, study the terms he gives you and you'll do fine.  He maybe a little bit haughty but not to bad.

Great lecturer, so much fun. But his exams suck. Gives you key terms to study, then doesn't use them and expects you to know completely random phrases. So go to lecture and make sure you read everything.

the greatest and most attractive professor probably ever in the history of UW. very interesting lectures, but doesn't post them on the internet so you have to go to class... it's worth it, though - ahh just love him

He gives such great lectures. It's as if he tells each one as a story. The connections he makes are insane and really opened my eyes to what I was missing in my thinking about the world. I guess some people think his intelligence comes off as arrogance, but I don't see it.
Awesome Professor, makes you think and conveys things in a new way that open new ways of thinking

theee best professor ive ever  had. interesting, thought-provoking, abstact. he sarts each lecture with a son, and then relates it to the lecture. can you imagine comparing aerosmith and plato? amazing class; i suggest that everyone take it. a lot of reading, but h explains everything in lecture. grades depend on your t.a. (get a good one!)

He speaks dreadfully slow. Considering the material is interesting, he could have done a lot more with lecture. He comes across as really pompous, but some people dig that. I found it annoying. Since the tests were stupidly constructed, you don't have to read. You should though so you get something out of the class.
Definitely keeps lecture interesting.  Great professor, but your grade really depends on your TA...

A really great class and amazing professor, truly recommended! There is a fair amount of reading, but he basically summarizes most of it in class. After the first 2 or 3 lectures, it really easy to get into the swing of things and understand the style in which he teaches. Any comments on here about how he is pretentious and arrogant are just false.

ILS 205 is a great class.  Yeah, it's hard and you may not get Intermediate credit but it's interesting stuff and relevent to those interested in political science.  You WILL read a lot so keep this in mind but it's a lot of fun.  My favorite class.
He is an interesting guy.

He is really terrible. Just going to say. Within a month, I found him to be a pretentious, self-preening, ass who spends most of his time glorifying his own ego. The class is way harder than the 200 level describes, AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!
he's so cute and funny!
ILS 205:  A 200-level, 3 credit course, that does not count as being "intermediate".  Yet 3 weeks into the semester you are tested over 750+ pages of reading material... Avoid!

I took the Poli Sci Equivalent that meets with ILS 206 and was interesting but ID's were extremely difficult for the Poli Sci Exam. On every exam at least half the IDs I had never seen before. But TA Brandon was amazing.

He is such a funny professor! His tests are mostly identification questions and short answer, and I've never really had a problem with the class. He's also really funny and easy going. I'd recommend taking the class
Some of the best lectures I've been to, hands down. Makes jokes, listens to good music (usually) and relates topics to everyday. The only class I wont skip!

OMG he rocks!  If he hadn't taught the second half of this class second semester I wouldn't have taken it.  You MUST do the reading because he likes to refer to it alot.  He explains things really well, so in discussion there usually aren't too many questions, just review.
Avramenko is the man.  Class is really interesting and not too hard.
He is very interesting and fun to listen to for lectures. Discussions are pointless, and you need to determine the 2 good TA's. THEY determine your grades. Do the readings.

Best class I had all semester. Avramenko comes off as arrogant at first, but then you really start to understand his sarcasm and his reasons for it. Readings are very interesting, and you will learn so much, not just about political science or history, but about life in general. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Full of Youth, fun, tells great stories, and relates to younger generation. Still watches south park. Best prof ever, clearly states ideas in a way that MAKES you want to learn with him.

He is a very enjoyable man. It was always worth going to class. I thought the exams were tough, and my ta was not very good. Try and figure out who the good ta's are because they determine your grade.
Avramenko was my absolute favorite professor. Smart and funny his class was my favorite all year.

Avramenko is the man!  As a repeat student, I think someone needs to spread the word.  Get to know him -- it's worth it and he is incredibly helpful and knowledgeable!  He is awesome and despite his sarcastic exterior actually DOES care about his students -- especially the ones who care about the material.  My favorite prof!
A tough but fair class. Definitely get to know your TA, they can be really helpful in getting the best grade possible in the class....

Interesting lectures.  You have to do A LOT of reading.  A TON of reading.  Some of the reading is interesting and some of the time it is impossible.  Don't expect a cakewalk and your grade is heavily dependent on how your TA likes your writing style.

He's a very good professor. He definetly knows the material and it's clear that he wants everyone else to love it as much as he does. Reading is a necessity. Sometimes it's hard to understand but section can clarify things. Exams are hard but if you read and go to class you're fine. I definately recommend this class.

Avramenko is a really cool guy.3 Tests and a paper, a lot of ways to do well. He keeps lectures interesting and its easy to understand the topics if u can sift thru his lectures. A lot of reading but most of it is very interesting. Get to know ur TA, ur grade is heavily dependant upon how they view ur writing style. Definitely recomend this class.
Tough but fair.
Interesting class, don't have to do the readings. Studying necessary for exams, but a good grade is not hard. Overall, recommended. TA Brandon is by far the best.

He's a good teacher, he thinks his jokes are hilarious (which they usually aren't) but that in itself makes the class more interesting.  He can come off as a jerk, but his lectures are very entertaining and as long as you aren't easily offended he's a fun professor to have.  He gets the info across without boring the**** out of his students.

Good class, young & cool professor, easy to follow.  You can get away without reading but you'd have to study really hard.  T/A's are really good, especially Brandon.  There's one paper and 3 tests, not too bad.  Avramenko is HOT.

Great lectures! As long as you have a general interest in the topic in the first place, not hard at all to enjoy this class. He's brilliant and clearly knows his stuff. He's funny and very relatable to the students. Kind of intimidating to ask questions - he might make fun of you, but he really is a great professor. Loved the course - an easy A
Very good at relating everything to the students
This guy is pretty much my favorite professor. He is a very good lecturer, I never have a hard time paying attention. He's also really funny which always makes class more enjoyable.
In Avramenko's defense: some people need mocking.  His swagger can be a little off-putting, but I don't think anyone can really argue that he doesn't teach well or doesn't know his stuff.

OMG! he didn't care what he said to anyone! anytime someone asked a question, he made fun of them. he spoke too fast in lecture and it was impossible to take notes. don't take a class that he has anything to do with.
Very good lecturer for the most part. Can be a little disorganized at times but usually keeps things interesting. Get Brandon Turner for your TA. He's pretty much my hero.
He's good
Good teacher, sometimes he thinks he's really funny but it was a pretty good class. TA Brandon is the****!
Avramenko is great instructor, sexy and intelligent! willing to teach the materials to you.

In rare fashion, I took 206 before 205, so I had a small leg-up in the class.  But for a  young, new professor, I found him very effective.  Confident, smart, funny/witty, and comfortable up front.  One of the better professors I've ever had - I would suggest his class to anyone considering taking this course.

I actually like the readings, but even if you don't do them he breaks down the topics clearly. The 205/206 courses are interesting, especially if you haven't had philosophy before. Furthermore, he's Canadian and he doesn't mind knocking Bush a bit. Always welcomed. From experience, TA Turner grades harder than Moore, but is a fun guy.

I think the applause he got after his last lecture speeks for itself. Students love this guy, his lectures are interesting, lively and you really don't have to do the reading cuz he summerizes it all for you in lecture. The class was farely easy as the exams, and paper topics were not that challenging whatsoever
He is a great lecturer, very interesting and makes you interested in what he is talking about. He is also really funny!

While the class is interesting, he's a pompous ass. I'm not a big fan. He thinks way too highly of himself, obviously thinks he's attractive and therefore can saywhatever he wants. He thinks he's way funnier than he actually is. I find him annoying, which is unfortunate because so many other people on this site seem to adore him.
I think I'm in love with him.  Enough said.

One of the funnier, better professors. I sat around a lot of people who didn't appreciate him, but I think this is a good prof for a sort of lousy class. whoever said he made this class, they're right. Without him, this would be an awful class. Take him for something like Poli Sci, it would be infinately smarter.

Best class I've ever taken...or I guess best professor I've ever had...he's really funny, liberal, witty, and the lectures are incredibly helpful- the tests are fair also. Plus, as far as professors go, he's not too bad to look at either.

He makes the class.  Without him as the professor, this class would suck.  he is amusing, smart, liberal and an overall great lecturer.  I would recommend this class to anyone and plan on taking the sequel.  Not to mention hes soo CUTE with that canadian accent.

He's really fun and you learn a LOT.  You get to read all the classics that you feel like you SHOULD read at some point in your life, but wouldn't unless you had to.  Prof. Avramenko does a nice job keeping things interesting and relating ancient seemingly obsolete things to modern day.

This is the most raunchy, politically incorrect, and as loud as a professor can get, not to mention that he is unbelievably funny. Not a single lecture goes by without him moking bush or whoever he feels like mocking. I loved this guy's lectures. He's one of those rare professors who actually make you want to come to class. Highly recommended.

Audrey is like the aunt you always wanted. The cool aunt. She is very kind and considerate when it comes to her students. Her classes feel like a family unit. She creates a space where everyone belongs. I just really admire her and I think UW is lucky to have her. Take a class with Audrey, you won't regret it.

Audrey will push you has an actor and will always raise the bar. 250 is a big step up from 150. She did not make herself very available outside of class time, if so it was very rushed. Feedback got repetitive into the course, not much personal student-to-professor investment. But super fun course with so many talented actors.

I am a Standish fan. She is so kind and cares so much about her students. I had her also for 150 and she just inspires the room. I think she's the best professor at UW Madison in theatre. I took 250 in the fall of 2024 and she would buy the class coffee, get to know us, and really inspire us to go further. I grew tremendously as an actor.

Audrey is by far one of the most caring and loved professors we have at the UW Theatre Department. I have also taken 360 with her and have never had a more organized and thoughtful director in my entire acting career. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Audrey, DO IT! You will be a better theatre artist after just one class.

I have had Audrey for three classes and I would take classes with her 7000x over. She is an extremely dedicated, organized, caring, and fun professor. You can get so much out of her classes if you do the assigned work, pay attention, and participate. The participation is not at all painful, and she sincerely cares about your growth. I

This is the second class I've had with Audrey and I registered for a 3rd next semester. She tells everyone to find what they admire in one another and that resonated with me. She radiates love and care. Her classes aren't difficult but she challenges you to be a better human.

I'm in Audrey's 150 class right now and I love it. She makes class fun and she cares about us. Homework was a lot for the first month, but it eased up greatly. She does warn that the class is front loaded. I really like her and now I'm thinking about majoring in theatre. Don't hesitate to take a class from Audrey.

Come to class or you will fail - very harsh attendance policy. Professor didn't make herself that available outside of class, but did respond to emails. Participation is necessary, and the class is fun and informative! But she kind of goes through the motions - ultimately just make the most of the class yourself because she won't help with that.

Fun class that inspired me to pursue acting!  Audrey was a nice professor, but she took little interest in her students. Theatre requires growing and connecting to the industry, Professor Standish had little focus on advancing the careers of her students. The theatre department here just lacks resources. Classwork should have been more in-class.
Attendance really matters!! Also sometimes she expected a little much from a beginner class.
She was a fun and engaging theatre teacher. I would definitely take her class again!

I really enjoyed taking class with Audrey. She is understanding, kind, and funny. I have accommodations and she worked with me outside of class so that I felt confident while in class. She makes odd jokes but sometimes it's fun to laugh at a mom joke. I have zero complaints.

Audrey's class is life changing. I had never taken a theater class and now I am working towards a certificate after completing 150. She really works with you and helps you grow throughout the semester. I thought the quizzes were easy and the exam was nothing, she gives you a review sheet with everything on it.  Audrey is so kind and cares.

I liked 150. Audrey was really kind. She gave written feedback on scenes/monologues and I felt I grew a lot from her notes.  I am a computer science major and had little background in acting. Audrey met everyone on their level. Overall, the class was great and Audrey was fun to have as a Professor.

I really liked having Audrey as an instructor. She seems to really care about the craft and wants students to do well. There is a strict attendance policy (you can miss 3 times) but I get it since we work in groups. Audrey really helped me when I was hospitalized. She got me up to speed in no time. I plan to take 250 with her as well.

Lacks empathy for students, especially those who are shy or beginngers. Her attitude during class makes attending sessions dreadful. Doesn't encourage students. She lacks understanding when sickness arises, which can be frustrating during a pandemic. Far too intense for a beginner level acting course.
had her last semester . just kind of rude personality made theater unenjoyable

I didn't like the final exam that came with this class, as well as having a long scene performance. It's hard to meet your partners outside of class, especially with Covid, and Audrey doesn't really make exceptions for this. There are also a lot of unnecessary readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She has a very bad attitude in class. Can be rude towards students. I'm not sure why there is an exam in a theatre class? Makes it very difficult for first-time learners in acting. Would not take it again!!! Has no empathy towards students and if you skip class for an emergency she will punish you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His test questions are easy to understand and his exams are fairly easy. He is a good lecturer and helps break down the complex aspects of hormones and the brain. He is also really sweet and is pretty engaging.

He sometimes flies through dense/difficult course content, but would often end lectures 10-20 minutes early so it wasn't too overwhelming. His tests are very fair, and he is definitely very caring. I would not recommend taking this course if you are not a neurobiology major. The class is far more biological than any psychology class I've taken.

Loved this course! Anthony can move a little fast during his lectures so you make sure you're taking notes. Three big exams are each 25% of your grade. Exams were a lot easier than I expected since the course materials were pretty heavy. Overall, lots of memorization but interesting topics. WATCH THE REVIEW VIDEOS FOR EXAMS! SO HELPFUL!

I absolutely loved this class. Multiple topics were brought up that were never even mentioned in other classes I have taken at UW, and there definitely was evidence used to support his claims as this is what we were tested on! Professor Auger was extremely kind and understanding towards his students and I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

A lot of the topics in this class were presented without evidence.The professor would often make bold claims and then present graphs that didn't support his stance or present a graph then say "but I actually disagree with that".The class was easy to pass and Professor Auger seems like he cared about his student.I just didn't learn anything.

He's a really nice guy, but he wastes a lot of time explaining that he doesn't want to offend anyone when talking about sex/gender. I'm not conservative by any means but his lectures can be politically charged to the extreme-- he makes bold statements about transitioning (especially for children) with little evidence to back them up.

I took this class in Spring of 2021 online. The content (for me) was a bit difficult but Anthony explained everything very well. He has a professional aura to him but it is apparent that he cares about his students. I really liked how organized his lectures were and always looked forward to them. Just make sure to pay attention and take good notes!

This is Tony's Epigenetic class (its changes class code frequently). He is an amazing guy, very personable. I took this class fully online, and not to his fault (I still really enjoyed going to class), but I think this class would be much better in person. This is a small class, so having natural conversation with him would have been super nice
Professor Auger has been my absolute favorite professor at UW! He is SO sweet and incredibly caring. If I could take all of my psych/genetics classes with him I would.

I took the Epigenetics capstone with Auger. Discussion felt more like a comfortable conversation than a forced discussion. He is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about epigenetics. Guy is hilarious. Grades were based on two presentations of research, an exam (which was very clear), a final paper, and easy participation. Amazing class and prof

I took Tony's capstone course on epigenetics. It was difficult since I had no genetics background, but he made the material easy to understand. Assignments seemed difficult but he is very helpful and wants everyone to succeed. He's an all-around great guy and great professor. I learned a lot in his class!

Auger was a brilliant professor. You could tell he was passionate about his research. Though he talked fast at times, he was always very clear and his TAs always did a great job explaining things during discussion. Everything you need to know in order to do well on exams gets repeated and emphasized in lectures. Pay attention and come to class!

Tony's a great professor. However, the class was somewhat unorganized and lectures were taken from the textbook.  Exams were easy, but the class was moderately hard because everyone always scored in the AB range. This was the only class I've taken that had to reverse-curve an exam.
Knowledgable and clear, seems like a great person

The best professor at UW-Madison. She's extremely knowledgeable about the field and is willing to guide students not only through her class, but also grad school applications, interviews, and more. She's also incredibly kind, caring, and accepting. I also took CSD 481 and it was lovely. 100% would take her classes again.

Audra has been one of my favorite professors in the CS&D department! She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the material that she's teaching. She is very clear about what she expects you to know for the exam. She always has her student's best interest and is more than willing to help/meet with you to help you succeed!

Popping in here to give a recent review of Audra! She is the BEST and widely respected among her faculty and students for a reason. Super straightforward lectures and exams are exactly what she says it will be. One of the sweetest people and very aware of her subject area. Clever and kind
She is an amazing professor, she works with you, gives no BS work and her tests are super straightforward. TAKE THIS CLASS

Audra is AMAZING! You can tell how passionate she is about her research, and all of the topics she talks about in her classes. She is so personable and you can talk to her about anything. Oh, and this class is easy as pie! Her lectures are really interesting, so even if you hate lectures she's really good at grabbing your attention!
Great professor-know the material in her slides and you'll pass. She's passionate and makes you interested in the material she's teaching.

She is so sweet and loves talking about her research in this class! She is very approachable for all things CSDgrad school. This was a super easy class and I really enjoyed getting to know Audra! Recommend going to class for pop up assignments, but all the info is on the slides.

I was surprised abt Joe's rating. I thought he was entertaining and prepared students well. The content isn't super interesting, but Joe tried his best to make it more interesting. He made his exams easy (open note/book), & the lowest exam score was dropped. He also only required students to do 8/12 discussion posts. I feel like he is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: PSYCH414-Class was unorganized and uninteresting, expectations were unclear. Exams were unfair and Joe was unwilling to hear out students, he was quickly defensive and never held himself accountable. DO NOT TAKE any class offered by Joe, you will not be the one student who enjoys him or the way he teaches.

Joe is a kind and sensitive person, but he shouldn't teach. His lectures, assignments, slides, and the whole class in general were extremely disorganized and uninteresting. The slides were 80+ pages long and filled with way too much text (how are you a college professor and you do this???). Class is NOT related to cognition in health and society!

Course is soooooo disorganized. Even you go to every lecture, you still don't know whats going on. Countless mistakes in class. Slides are extremely hard to follow. Some easy concepts were taught in a very complicated way. The grading criteria was very unclear. I really don't know what this has to do with health even the course was named like that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I don't know where to start with this one... Just got out of final exam and doing this for closure. He is kind BUT ALL OVER THE PLACE. Tries to be relatable making jokes about his anxiety yet induces so much anxiety onto his students. Assignments not clear, grading not clear,  NO COMMUNICATION WITH TAs. Waste of time unfortunately. MADGRADES WRONG
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joe is a nice person but that doesn't excuse how much of a dumpster fire this course was. Lectures were hard to follow, his thoughts were disorganized, we were immediately quizzed on knowledge that HE COULD NOT EXPLAIN throughly. His MCQ are worded oddly, often had to provide additional explanations so students could TRY to field them. Just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: god i hated this class so much, prof is somewhat a nice person but lectures and content is super confusing, TAs don't even have to run discussion but still can't get grades in after months, terrible communication between profs and TAs, confusing and irrelevant "quirkiness" on pop quizzes. not sure what makes this class about health at all. AVOID!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Simply another cognitive psychology class- not much actual information on society or health? The class was so disorganized that it was probably three times harder than it was supposed to be. Seemed like a nice guy but the lectures were often difficult to follow and you'd have to teach yourself the material. Take a different level 500 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the second worst psychology class I've taken here. He's very obnoxious and would yell at the beginning of class to get everyone's attention even though he has a microphone. The class and weight of the assignments make no sense. In most of the lectures, he gave examples for the topics but no real definitions, so you're left confused.

Just don't take this class. He is a mess, slides don't make sense and always have typos that affect the information and he doesn't even know whats going on. Quizzes are misgraded, and also you have no time to study or know what is going to be on it. The discussion section doesn't even help you its just paper presentations and is pointless.

I go into every class with an open mind and a willingness to learn. I attend every lecture, rewatch them after class, do every reading, and take every quiz for this class and am barely getting by. The content feels impossible, the exams and quizzes even harder, and there is little to redeem yourself with. An unreasonably hard class.

Content has the potential to be straightforward and easy to understand, however Professor Austerweil makes things incredibly complex. Severely disorganized lectures, contradictory content filled with mistakes, and definitions are not made clear. Nice professor, most of the time, but it's poorly taught. Not a good depth course, would not recommend.

Please do not take this class. It will drive you insane. You basically have an in-class quiz every lecture, I can't see what my grade is, and his lectures are incredibly frustrating by only showing you studies rather than teaching. He is kind, but it does not excuse how disorganized and impossible this class is. This class is a terrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are very chaotic... as well as the grading and quizzes. BTW, he does not give enough time to review previous knowledge but asks students to take a relatively hard in-class quiz. It is hard to understand the class content because there is often no logic. This course has in-class quizzes this semester and has midterm and final exams.

Never been more frustrated with a professor in my 4 years at UW. Extremely disorganized lectures, countless mistakes, and jumping around. It has been 5 weeks and I haven't received a single grade for my weekly reading responses yet. No one can calculate their grades, when asked about this on Piazza he responds by saying that isn't a "priority".

This class was so confusing and I genuinely had no clue what was going on. If you WANT to learn, don't take it. If you want an easy A, take it I guess. He was cool but not easy to get in contact with. The TAs were awesome though, they carried the class and made it bearable. Genuinely disliked the class.

One of the worst lecturers I've had at UW, definitely the worst in the psych department. Class is whatever Joe wants it to be, which is usually unorganized and boring. Class material did not relate to "health and society" as it was supposed to according to the class description. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Hes a bit chaotic in his teaching and speaks without thinking at times which can come across as offensive. It is clear he has pure intentions, but he can be a bit rude at certain moments which makes him less approachable.

Joe is nice but is not a good lecturer. His thoughts are unorganized, so the lectures are hard to follow as he goes on off-topic rants. The class had nothing to do with what its listed as (Cognition in health & society). It was just another cognitive psych class.
