I was excited for this class, but it ended up being my least favorite class I've taken
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Austerweil was so nice! He gave us a couple mental health days throughout the semester which was so appreciated. I had issues during a group project and he was super accommodating and understanding. The class isn't easy, but he explicitly says what's on the exams and makes the lectures as interactive as possible. He's hilarious, too.

This course has improved a lot! The course is now flipped, i.e., students should watch videos before class. These videos are helpful and clear. We are required to read papers that are relevant to the topic for that week. The classmates have a very diverse background (psych and computer science etc.) and make the discussion inspirational. Reccomend

Prof Austerweil was really nice and you can tell he cares about this stuff but he is really frustrating to listen to. He is super disorganized in his slides and often contradicts himself. He is very socially awkward. Some of the test questions were super confusing. Only one exam but only worth 20% of your grade. A lot of projects for the grade.

I think Professor Austerweil is a very successful professor. While he struggles sometimes to correctly articulate his thoughts, he is always very quick to correct his errors and explain things further. There is no textbook, only articles for homework and a few mini projects. Only one exam worth only 15% and a final project. Easy A if you do the hw!

Her lectures were mainly just review from video lectures but were mandatory for participation points. A general knowledge of plants is probably best but it's not too hard to pick up. Three midterms but no final.
Lots of work for an intro class, but overall a good choice if you need the credit. She's very nice and accommodating.

Dr. Rakotondrafara's class was fun and informative. Most lecture material was review of high school biology and environmental science, yet I appreciated learning about plant pathology, agricultural disease management, and how to be a conscientious consumer. I enjoyed the labs; most were self-directed with a small lab group, and the TA helped too.

Good professor and a fun class. Definitely catered towards nonscience majors, so if you have taken literally any biology class before it will be mostly review and not much work. Labs are often quite self-guided and therefore a lot of fun. The class is not difficult and the professor and TAs do a great job explaining everything.

I absolutely LOVED Plants, Parasites and People! Professor Rakotondrafara is passionate about the and explains concepts thoroughly. Most of the course is online with 3-5 lectures per week followed by a quiz. As long as you take the time to thoroughly understand the concepts, the quizzes are a breeze and the exams should go well. Take it!

The content itself is not that hard, and if you want an easy biology class I'd say take it. But the professor doesn't seem like she knows too much about what she's teaching. It's a hybrid class so a lot of the lectures are online. Many of the concepts are poorly explained and you can tell she's reading off of a poor script. Easy grade, bad class.

Lecture and lab attendance are mandatory. In person and online lectures with a quiz each week. Lectures aren't bad, just redundant and not helpful. 3 in person exams and all lab assignments make up your grade. Opportunity for extra credit, but more work than it is worth. Expect to get no direction in lab and to be left without much instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you do not like biology, this class is a great choice. The workload was practical. There were only a couple of times where there would be lots of work. I joined the class a week late, and the professor was very welcoming. I am glad that I took this class.

I personally thought there was a lot of work involved with this course for an intro level class, but Prof. Rakotondrafara was very helpful if you asked a question in person after lecture. Lots of work and sometimes the TAs were confusing and didn't clarify questions very well. I don't think I would take this class again as I didn't take AP Bio.

I took Botany 123 and it was such an easy A. We were online this semester and lectures were asynchronous. As long as you watched the lectures and took notes, you were guaranteed an A. The weekly quizzes were easy and the exams weren't very hard either. I would definitely recommend you to take this course .

I absolutely loved Botany 123! I took this as honors optional and the honors project was super interesting! The class covered many interesting topics and the labs were super engaging! My TA was amazing and I've heard good things about all of them. 10/10 would recommend this class and Prof. Rakotondrafara!

I loved Aurelie! She is hands down one of my favorite professors, period. She always showed up with a smile and you could practically hear it through her lectures. She is very passionate about the topics she teaches, which makes it all the more fun to learn about. The course format is very digestible and easy. If you can take PLPATH123, DO IT!

Prof Rakotondrafara is passionate about DNA and genetics that's very clear in her teaching. She asks for a lot of in-class participation to gauge the class' understanding of the concepts and was really useful. She also welcomes questions during lectures. FYI, she has a thick French accent and sometimes speaks quickly. Tests are MC and very fair.
doesn't explain anything clearly and expects A LOT in case studies. Also, did not allow us to use a notecard on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is by far the easiest class I've ever taken at UW. The concepts are very similar to a high school biology class and you would be especially fine if you took AP Bio. The TA's are all so nice and host review sessions before the tests. The exam average was a 94 or so on 2/3 exams. The lab is ok and requires group work, but very easy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Interesting course, not recommended if you already have a heavy course load. Far more work than a typical 3 credit 100 level course. Expect 2-5 online lectures per week paired with a weekly quiz, HW, discussion, lab and reports. The material isn't difficult, there's just a lot of it and often feels disorganized. Professor is passionate & talks FAST

Was really hoping this class would be a bit more exciting but it was not. The concepts were but the way it was displayed in lecture and in dense readings was not enjoyable. She is very passionate about GWS but too many dense readings and details for intro class. Easy A if you can participate in discussion and write papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were a lot of jargony readings but you didn't really have to read them to excel in this class. The class seemed kinda repetitive and I just wasn't a fan. She also talks really fast and is hard to pay attention to. Overall, easy A but really boring

The professor is so knowledgable about the content she is teaching, that I think she forgets that this is an intro class, so people are not going to pick up on the content immediately.  However, getting a good grade is not hard as long as you can write a good essay for the final and turn in your work on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was very interesting but was too difficult to be considered an intro-level course. Professor is knowledgeable and cares about what she teaches, but readings are usually long and difficult. It doesn't help that instead of breaking down the readings she just copies and pastes quotes from the readings onto 50+ slide powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I went into this class with high hopes but was severely disappointed. The entire course consists of pretty much only dense, difficult, and jargony readings and pointless lectures. All she does is pluck quotes from the readings, stretch it out for fifty+ slides, and provide pretty much no additional content or her thoughts about the subject.

Assigns dense readings which would be okay if she took the time in lecture to break them down to help students understand the material. Instead, she speeds through 40-50 slide lectures where she just regurgitates long quotes from the readings without really adding any commentary or encouraging discussion. Take this class with a different prof.

Professor Santiago Ortiz is knowledgable and passionate. However, the course is poorly organized, we often don't have clear instructions on assignments and the canvas page also lacks specific guidelines. She assigns very difficult and advanced readings and does not really break them down in lecture.

She is a very educated woman, but her lectures are terrible. she has over 25-30 slides each day, and the slides are packed with information. She skips through before you have a chance to take notes on it. Not only that, but she is oddly aggressive. On top of that, for a 102 intro class, the readings are hard to understand and takes hours.

Although she is extremely passionate about lecture content, her lecture slides are horrifically long. One of her presentations was 46 slides long, loaded with content. She will often remark "i'm going to speed through", which isn't how lectures should be. She overwhelms students with content and simply copies paragraphs of text into the lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goated professor for Spanish 203!! 10/10

Kendall is an awesome professor. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to succeed. She is passionate about Spanish and wants to help you. Also, she is pretty cool. Definitely take a class with her if you can .

Kendall is an amazing TA. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The class in and of itself isn't very hard, and Kendall does a good job of answering any questions that students have. She explains the material well.
Lectures can take time to get used to but shes very helpful in her office hours.
She means well, but she isn't the greatest at teaching the course material. Tests and exams cover content that was brushed over in lecture, and is pretty difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She cares about her students; she is easily accessible after class and at office hours. After class, she stays and is more than willing to look at homework issues, answer questions about lecture, or answer any other questions you have. The exams are relatively similar to the lecture material, and she posts notes from lectures to review.

Professor Mouna is an extremely kind and dedicated instructor. She is easily accessible outside of class and provided clear and useful information. Her lectures also typically include information directly pertaining to the assignments.

reviews.comment: dude her lectures GPA speaks for itself, doesn't prepare you for the tests

reviews.comment: She is very accessible outside of class. Many students find that she is very caring and understanding. Sometimes her lectures are slow, but they will prepare you very well for exams. Go in for office hours whenever. I've never had a better professor. She always makes sure that everything she says is clear for everyone.
Poor

Professor Kacem is very nice, approachable and willing to help you if you ask questions. The logic of the class is clear and she talks about some of the complicated algorithms used in each program before the due date. Overall you can understand her lecture and get the help you need.
Decent

I would only tell people I hate to take a class with this professor. She does not explain well during lectures. I've asked people around me in lectures and discussions, and they haven't understood what was going on either. I ended up dropping the class and had to retake it next semester.

reviews.comment: Would you like to go to a math lecture and come out more confused than you were before? This professor is your guy!! Seriously, this professor did not explain anything and just solved problems that had nothing to do with the curriculum
Bad lecturer, made numerous mistakes throughout the year, frankly nearly every lecture. The TAs or students in some cases had to help in correcting many issues
worst lecturer ever. very hard to understand and the examples she tries to use make sense maybe 50% of the time

Dr. Kent is a great person, but not a very great professor. Her lectures are all over the place, and it was almost better to skip lecture and teach yourself. There are two midterms, which are very manageable with the provided practice exams. However, the final was not representative of the previous exams, and ended up dropping my semester long A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures felt disorganized and the professor is confusing and doesn't teach well. She went on tangents a lot and often took forever to get to point. This class with this professor would very difficult for someone without calculus experience. I found myself learning the material by either studying for tests or in discussion, but rarely in lecture.
She knows what she's talking about but only explains through examples, and doesn't actually explain what you need to do to solve the problems.
Overall, not the worst professor ever, but very confusing and doesn't teach well at all. She has very dry humor and does nothing to engage learners/make the class interesting.

Lectures were disorganized, making it difficult to follow or learn the material in class. I often left the lecture more confused than when I arrived. The final exam felt unnecessarily challenging for me, even though math is my strongest subject. I would strongly encourage you to avoid all classes "taught" by this professor.

Professor Kent was not particularly engaging or clear, but lectures were fine as long as you paid rapt attention. My main critique of lecture would Dr. Kent's tendency to spend way too much time on activities. In general lectures were not particularly organized, but she is not awful as some of these reviews make her out to be.
Don't do it. The exams are nothing like the practice exams. You'll end the class knowing LESS calculus than when you started.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overexplained easy concepts by going too deep into stuff that didn't matter and never actually getting to the point. I took calc in high school and it was taught much better than what Kent did. Poor organization overall and had a confusing all over the place structure. Avoid Kent if you can.

The professor taught very generic calculus, and did in class examples that were very basic and easy compared to the midterms and especially the final. I will say lectures are easy to follow, but expect much harder questions during finals and midterms.
She trys to keep class interesting, especially on heavy math days. Tests can be hard, but practice exams help.

The lectures have no outlines and the professor does not make sense. The discussion was all group work and we were not taught anything we had to figure it out ourselves. Lowkey confused how they thought we would learn anything from the structure and random ideas brought up in lectures.

Nice and lenient in terms of grades, but very confusing teacher. Lectures are very difficult to follow, even easy topics are explained almost incoherently. If you end up with her, highly recommend getting a math tutor or being prepared to put in a lot of work independently studying the course work.

I took calc in high school and when I tell you she literally explained things in such confusing ways when it could be wayyyy simpler. She was all over the place in her lectures very hard to follow. The only time the material would make sense is when my TA would cover the topic.
Note that you'll have to study by yourself without even thinking of taking a look on his lecture notes.
Clearly has no clue how to give an engaging lecture. If you struggle with math avoid taking her class at all costs.

She has a very obscure way of teaching. She explains concepts in a very abstract and confusing way. Attending lectures leave me more confused than when I came in. I took Calc in high school and I had to rely on what I learned then instead of her lectures. ]
terrible professor and i took ap calc ab in high school. cant explain anything. goes way to fast in lecture but makes no sense so its like shes skipping around stuff. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.
Never take this professor for this class.  She does not teach well.

she is never on topic. we never learn what we need to know. I teach myself everything and the discussion sheets are never ending and super hard because I don't know the content bc she doesn't teach. if you're gonna have her as a prof switch immediately.
sos i am not gonna make it out of this class

Genuinely so bad, AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Always talking about random shit and I genuinely crash out every time I have to sit in lecture. I am so sorry if you have to take this prof because it's miserable.

reviews.comment:
if you're taking lower-level math courses like calc 1 or 2 good luck. this professor is TERRIBLE at teaching. You're better off attending a different prof's lecture. 

0/10.

I skipped every lecture after attending the first one, Kent does not explain concepts clearly and oftentimes will go on tangents not related to course material. He takes too long on unimportant topics. I geniunely believe anyone new to this material would easily fail this class if they only attended leture and discussions. Do NOT take her.

findpassword.

reviews.comment: This professor was awful, their notes are not readable, they have weird verbage for lecture, literally find yourself someone else because this professor is terrible. I will not wish this on my worst enemy.

Lectures are very confusing & they have a reputation for just chatting and making weird analogies no one understands unless you are a math mathematician. Worst of all, class is test heavy & has no actual study guide, just old tests that have inaccurate examples of what will be on the exams. Find a different teacher if you struggle with math
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly hard to follow, very all over the place and not much of actually teaching the material. You will need to teach yourself everything or pray that you get a good TA who can (re)teach you the material. Honestly dont need to go to lecture as you wont get anything out of it. My TA even said professor was confusing during lecture.

I believe topics were not very well explained or taught. She very often went into great detail about example problems that had little/nothing to do with the topics we were covering in class. Was not very well coordinated with homework assignments.
Lectures are almost impossible to follow and understand
The lectures were very unclear and tiresome

If you get this professor drop the class and try to join another one. I already took calculus 1 and 2 and I still didn't understand what this person was talking about. Save yourself the headaches and drop the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Topology's not an easy subject, but he teaches it well and his lectures are helpful since he offers plenty of intuitive examples and doesn't mind taking time to answer questions. The only annoying thing about this course was that he never provides HW or exam solutions, which kind of suggests a lack of effort.

Great professor. Very entertaining and charismatic person. The exams are somewhat difficult in content but they're all take home tests and she grades very leniently, which makes the class relatively easy overall. Only downside is that she is kinda disorganized when it comes to pacing the class and syncing lectures with homework.

Professor Kent is overall a solid professor. Lectures were practically right from the book, so it was easy to reference. This course overall delves heavily into theory and there was a lack of grounded examples at times. All exams were take home and open note. Grading is quite lenient with most students being freshman. Great class, great professor!

Ms. Kent was an amazing professor. She focuses heavily into the theory rather than the application, which if you can work with is great. Only slight criticism, which isn't particularly valid considering the point of the class was to be proof based, was the lack of grounded examples of how to use mathematical tools.

Beginning of the semester was great, but as the semester went on the quality of lectures decreased steadily, I was learning nothing from them. My friends that did well in the class only managed to do so via youtube & lots of studying.

This was an extremely fair course. Exams perfectly reflected the material covered in lectures. It's definitely possible to self-study using the online modules provided. You can succeed in this course if you take the necessary steps to study efficiently. Kent's lectures specifically were a little difficult because she has poor handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: MATH 234 was a hard class. I went to professor Kent's lecture and to be honest I didn't pay much attention lol so I wasn't able to follow professor Kent most of the time. But she did go into the topics in-depth and explained things nicely. So if you listen and follow you would be fine. Exam worth 84%, be ready to study by yourself a lot.

pretty good professor. most of the time she explained things in a clear way and would go over a few examples. you know exactly what to expect for exams because she provides questions and solutions for past exams. as long as you stay on top of the homework, you should do well on discussion quizzes and exams!

Great lectures. She explains concepts thoroughly and in a way that is accessible to students, and adds pop culture references and jokes that make class fun. She walks you through how to do multiple problems step by step, so if you go to lecture you'll have a solid handle on material, and exams wont be surprising. Exams are 84% of your grade though
Exam expectations are very clear. Lectures aren't great, did most of the learning outside of lecture.

The lectures are useful at the beginning of the semester but as you approach closer and closer towards the end, you should be ready to prepare mentally for watching tons of YouTube videos and reading numerous online articles. Test are not hard though, what I felt this year is that collective complaints lower the difficulty of the exams. Best luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Boring lecturer, with very few examples given. Almost all learning needs to be done from homework, textbook, and discussions. Would often be late and be unavailable for connection outside of class. 2 midterms and a final account for 84% of the total grade in this class. Exams only have 6-7 questions so really no place to mess up if you want an A.

Seems like a great person, but mediocre prof. Lectures were hard to learn from: she jumps around alot, does not explain the math often & just demonstrates, and the lectures are for the most part very boring. Provided little information for exams, often showed up a few minutes late, handwriting hard to understand (rpi, 2integral, 5S etc).

Professor Kent seems like a nice person, but lectures get very boring and they often don't make sense. I learned mostly from discussion worksheets and homework. Take this class with another professor if you can. (Brian Street covered her lectures once and I found his lectures far more enjoyable.)

Professor Kent was one of the worst teachers I've ever had. While she is nice and tries to make lectures entertaining they were extremely unorganized and made little to no sense. It got to the point where I'd read the textbook during lecture instead of listening to what she said because her explanations left me feeling more confused.

Dr. Kent is just okay. If you're really into math, you will love her. Her lectures are a bit abstract for what the class calls for but still useful. Personally, I learned from my TA and the homework assignments. EACH EXAM IS 30% OF YOUR FINAL GRADE (same for all MATH234 classes) so study harder than I did...

Lectures are not mandatory and I don't recommend going since it only makes it more confusing. I still went to lectures and it was a big mistake, as youtube videos taught me way more. If you want to do good on exams, expect work outside of class. The lectures are so poorly organized that you won't get an A if you don't do extra studying.

She's a very nice professor, however, her lectures are extremely disorganized and some of her exams had poorly written questions. Overall the hardest math class I've ever taken due to lack of clarity in lectures and a weird first exam.
Kent is a nice person, but an awful teacher. She is very disorganized
Lighthearted and entertaining in her teaching. However, her lectures and notes are extremely unorganized, so it's hard to follow along because there is no clear train of thought.

She gave a midterm makeup exam that was way harder than the original exam given. I wouldn't advise taking her class because she grades harshly and has no respect for her students or their time. She doesn't understand our whole aren't school. She doesn't get that we aren't on her level of understanding. DONT TAKE THE CLASS
Not good at her job
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She just sucks

Psychologically easy to take. Mathematically lots to think. Responsible, caring and specific. I watched the lectures 3 times longer online to pause and think. The rating is low because her students have no time to deal with ratemyprofs. Elegant writings (even via notability). Professor is not judgemental and is quite open to ideas. Take 375-6 yyds.

Professor Kent is a decent professor who defintiely wants to see her students succeed, although in the online format her lectures often dragged or were hard to follow when demonstrating proofs. I would have preferred more examples. Exams were fairly difficult due to short length, but there was a curve at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This class as a whole was not that hard. Prof Kent was good at making sure everyone was aware what was going to be on the exams so there were no surprises. No homework is collected so grade is made up of exams/quizzes. Review problems are taken out of the book. Class moves fast so sometimes more effective to read out of book than rely on lectures.

The material/tests are not that hard but it could feel hard because lectures are dry and not super helpful. Still go to lecture but you don't need to write down 90% of what she writes, just casually take simple notes on concepts/types of problems. This is definitely a class where you learn most of it on your own through the textbook/internet.
She is really nice in office hours!

Really appreciated the straightforward exams. She told us what problems to expect and that was essentially what we were tested on which is refreshing given many professors act all secretive about what exactly will be on the exam. Minimal amount of proofs and more focused on applications. Overall not bad.

The lectures are way too dry and she gives little intuitive instruction on how to understand the abstract concepts. Not available through emails. Hard midterms. No homework solutions are provided. Hard to get an A.

It was an easy class which she could've explained things in much simpler ways but overall, her explaining will do the job. Her exams are really easy but I mean the class itself is super easy. Attended classes at the start but honestly doing the homework alone using chegg was all you need to get an A.
I took her math 340 and math 240. She is good at explaining things. Exams are fair, not very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Professor Kent for Discrete Mathematics. Admittedly, I rarely attended lecture, but the lectures I did attend were excellent. Professor Kent made the material both accessible and engaging. Midterms were easy with a basic knowledge of the concepts.

One of the greatest math professor in the UW-Madison. The homework is not heavy. Midterms are not hard at all. Final is tested some specific topics instead of the whole book. She cares about us a lot and is not a strict grader. Try to choose her math 240, you won't regret.

This guy was absolutely brilliant.  He did a great job answering any and all questions.  Lectures were always interesting, and it really helped that he showed such enthusiasm for the material.  If you get the opportunity, you'd be a fool not to take his class.

Probably the worst professor I've come across at Madison so far. Doesn't try at all to be helpful, he is inflexible when it comes to make up exams even if for GOOD reasons and his exams are extremely awful. Would not recommend to anyone. ever.

He never actually teaches anything. It would be helpful if he went through a few problems but no. He does these abstract things that no one cares about and doesn't explain anything thoroughly. His exams are ridiculous and unfair.
This man has no business teaching calc 221. Unclear, unhelpful..just horrible..RUN FOR THE HILLS!
He is so miserably terrible I want to cry.
His first two exams were easy and extremely fair and then came the final. He is extremely inconsistent and overall not that clear. If you work hard and go to discussion you should be fine.
Dr. Kent really tried to teach us the material, but my TA was the one who showed me how to do everything.   Pray to God that you get a good TA or else you will need to get a full-time tutor.

By far the worst teacher I have encountered in my years of schooling. He is not helpful at all and makes sure to put the hardest possible questions on the exams. The book doesn't help one bit because its just a bunch of loose leaf paper. Stay away from him at all costs. He is horrible
He just writes proofs on the board and doesn't show the class how to actually solve a problem that will be on an exam
Impossible to read his hand writing and makes the material way more confusing that it needs to be.

This guy is horrible! He's really not funny and 2/3 of the time I am teaching myself calculus. In the beginning I went to his office hours and he's really not helpful!! Lecture I am lost, so I just read the textbook which is just as bad because it's custom. Avoid this guy, the TA is really helpful.
no homework required, learned everything in discussion section but tests were pretty straightforward only a couple questions were really hard most were the same ones we did in class or in disc.
I really enjoyed going to  his class. He cracked some entertaining jokes in class and explained everything very clearly.
Awesome teacher. Don't listen to complainers. He teaches to actually teach, not just to get through the planned lesson.

this guy is an awesome prof for math 320. his style of teaching is a little different, but you'd learn to get used to it. easy exams if you like math, not too much homework. he's the cool, young teacher everyone always wants.

Professor Kent was awesome! His class was just like he said it would be. 3 midterms, no final, and homework. 6 quizzes in discussion sections. His lectures were very easy to understand, and he explained things in different ways so everyone could understand. Very fair, good curve, overall a great prof!
Handwriting is just terrible!! I, as an international student, cannot read anything he writes!! I would avoid him.

Pretty good professor, but exams were tough. I found the TA-led review sessions to be the most helpful form of studying for a test. Also, try to find some previous exams to practice off of. They might not be perfect, but some of them are representative of Kent's exam questions.

HE'S CRAZY! his hair looks like he tried to cut it himself and his clothes were always too tight. His lecture's were pointless and I don't believe that he looked at the problems he was assigning us either.
Exams were tough not always related to homework. I did the assigned homework 3 times for the final and studied 30+ hours, and still got a 50%.

Great professor. His math 234 exams were just what how he said they would be, and overall the class is pretty easy with him teaching it. His lectures are very clear, and slow paced, so they are almost relaxing.

He wasn't the best presenter of the material, but he usually gave enough examples that you got the idea.  Cool guy though, has a quirky sense of humor.  I disagree that his exams were unrelated to what was taught in lecture, if you paid any attention at all you understood at least what the exam questions were asking.
Cute Professor, no need to attend lecture.. exams are not easy...but overall good professor.
Overall decent. Lectures are hit or miss, but more often than not tedious. Exams are fair. Understands the material but too much theory for my liking.

Clearly knows what he's teaching.  Lectures can be frustrating because he's really into deriving the formulas you end up needing to use.  It was frustrating to pick out what was going to be useful for tests and quizzes from his lectures.  Exams were fair, curve was generous.

His lectures are completely pointless. I don't know if he knows what he's doing half of the time. The homework is related to quizzes but not the exams. The exams are pulled mainly from material not covered or not explained in any lecture. Overall I wouldn't even take basic Algebra from this professor.
The exams were very fair.  Everything on them is a main concept and isn't an extremely specific case that is almost never seen.

This was Prof. Kent's first year here, so it was understandable that he was a little disorganized. Lectures started off sort of badly, but they got a lot better. His exams are challenging, and his grading system is different because he doesn't tell you your grade until the end of the semester. He obviously knows what he is teaching.

Professor Bal is fantastic, he is hilarious which makes class enjoyable. Informative, but super easy class. He lets you know exactly what is on exams. pre-class readings and videos can be long but are needed for in class group discussion which is ~1/2 of each class

Lectures were interesting, didn't cover the textbook during them. You're expected to read it on your own. I enjoyed the volunteer work, there are great opportunities. You had to read a chapter, watch 2 videos, and submit a reflection answering 1 question of your choice about the chapter each week. 3 exams not cumulative & get test questions before.

This class is pretty easy. If you do discussion posts you get 100% on them. Attendance is mandatory which I don't like because I don't learn anything during lectures. It's more discussion based and I wish he would talk more about the textbook than the two media pieces we have to watch/listen each week. He does give the test questions beforehand.

Very nice professor and is very fair in grading. Gives the questions for the exams ahead of time which is really nice. Lecture is pretty much mandatory but I don't think I learned anything within the 3 hour lecture which was annoying. Easy class if you need service learning.

This was very much a class that was dependent on your work outside of lecture. 3 hours is really long, even though there are breaks every hour. His lectures did not go into any detail beyond what is in the readings from the textbook. If it weren't for in-class activities almost every class, attending lecture really wasn't important for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bal's RP&SE class was amazing, and my favorite class ever. It was very stress free and gave me a new perspective on things. It required a service learning component to work with individuals with disabilities, and that was a great experience and looks good on the resume. I highly advise taking it, and he is the nicest and funniest guy!

Professor Bal is a really nice guy. The three hour class was a bit frustrating though. Having to sit there and listen to a dry lecture without taking notes or having any other stimulation was incredibly tiresome. It made the lecture feel like it lasted three days instead of three hours. Service learning is amazing and easy to get an A. Ok course.

This class is really fun! The service learning was easily the best part of my semester. Everything is laid out really clearly and he goes over it every class. The class is long but he gives breaks which is nice. The tests are easy and the weekly assignments are too. Attendance is mandatory and there is sign in 2x a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome prof! knows his stuff and interesting... easy class if you do the work. If you have time for 25 hours of volunteering then take this class. Great opportunities! Favorite class of this semester.

This is a 3hr lecture, but he fills the time well. He gives lots of breaks that usually go longer than he says they will. Everything is given to you before hand, so it's pretty hard not to do well. There are lots of in class activities, & attendance is taken 2x a class that count for a chunk of your grade, but do the weekly questions & you're good!

Overall Professor Bal is amazing!! Although the lectures are pretty long, he gives plenty of breaks and keeps the class interesting through guest lecturers, Ted Talks and other videos. The tests are very straight forward and he gives you all of the questions beforehand. He makes sure everything is well explained. Loved the service learning project!

Favorite class of the semester. It's one three hour lecture per week, with a 25 hour service learning requirement. Lectures have plenty of breaks, and are usually accompanied by a  guest speakervideo clips. Assignments are clear-cut and easy to do well on. He's compassionate and helpful, and values discussionengagement in the class.
Amazing professor
Brillian man!
great

Go to every class-you get points, you have to do 25 hours of volunteer work and write a paper about it. Tests are pretty easy just make flash cards from book and  take Myeducationlab.com quizes (the disk comes with the textbook). He uses many questions from it!. Overall, he was OK and class was decent. I would take the other professor though.

He's about experience, as long as you have some input, he'll be happy with you! His tests are solely based on the text, so do the readings and quizzes that comes with the book.  Also, if you remember to do all the assignments, there mostly "give me" points and stay for the whole class, the second 1/2 always has in class assignments.

Tim is a fantastic professor. He truly loves the subject he is teaching and makes the class interesting for those who don't.  He is helpful and always willing to accept your opinion even if he doesn't agree.  Readings are not necessary because he will review them in class. He assigned a couple response papers and one three page paper, all easy.

Truly one of the best instructors I've ever had. A pretty easy A. Readings were pdfs of articles and excerpts, they were unnecessary though as he makes sure to cover them in lecture.  His own passion for the subject was imbued in everyone, kids who normally would be apathetic to philosophy found themselves engaged in his discussions. Great teacher.

I'm an engineer major who took philosophy just to satisfy my humanities. Not only was it an easy A, but it was so engaging.  Even without reading the texts (all posted online, no textbook) he managed to make a lecture class of 75 all participate and take interest in the subject. He was always open to our opinions and encouraged them. Def recommend!

Take Philosophy with Tim!

I really enjoyed having Prof. Jones. She brings in real clients for a real campaign, and you can list this as an internship on your resume. The professor is great! I really enjoyed his class and I learned a lot. He did a really good job at explaining complicated topics and is overall a great professor. This class was really interesting and applicable to the business world. Would definately reccomend!

reviews.comment: Carl really cares about his students. He is very hyper while teaching but very intelligent. If you take the time to talk to him, he will help you and go extra lengths to check in and make sure that you're doing well. His tests are all about 'real-world' scenarios they are incredibly useful. Overall great guy and great professor.
so awesome, you can feel how passionate he is about the material and he genuinely cares about the success of his students. went above and beyond to answer questions, just a fantastic professor
Pretty chill. He just talks about evolution, and the test is light. Just focus on the codon and review the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Good professor
Brilliant guy and you can tell he really cares about his students.
Thee Best !!!!

Baum is one of the three professors for Bio 152, and he makes the content very engaging and easy to learn. Participations during lectures are required and you will need to get them right. The labs for this class are not as hard, but instead you will have to do a semester long research project that will be presented at a symposium so be ready!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had him twice for BIO152 & ZOO410--Dr. Baum is maybe my favorite professor from UW. He genuinely cares about students and is very accommodating for McBurney Students! SO knowledgeable, respected, and always making sure students understand the bigger picture of their education. He is accessible and encouraging, as well!
Awesome lecturer
He is very friendly and eager to help but sometimes I couldn't hear what he's saying.

Dr. Baum was a good lecturer! He gives lots of practice materials for the evolution module that are really helpful to study for the exam. Sometimes his answers to questions weren't the most clear, but usually his explanations of the content were clear.

I liked Dr. Baum as a person, he made lectures/slides funny. He was kinda hard to understand,which is not his fault at all, but he was incredibly helpful in office hours. He did a good enough job explaining the content. In my opinion, Evolution was the hardest 152 module, but that also could be because I barely paid attention in lecture.

Dr. Baum taught evolution in BIO152. Overall pretty good, and offered plenty of practice for his unit. He was slightly difficult to understand at times, though through no fault of his own. He was energetic during lectures and encouraged student input.
Pretty good lecturer! The content is very theoretical but overall okay

Baum taught the evolution section of Bio 152. His lectures were insightful and useful, but it is hard to understand him most of the time, in part due to his accent and slight lisp. He has real-time subtitles in his lecture that never work, but his lecture recordings have a correct transcript that highlights his effective lecturing.

Dr. Baum was a great professor and truly loves his job! He constantly asked students to reach out to him and provided many resources to help anyone with questions. He also had practice quizzes for every lecture which was very helpful when reviewing.
David is very passionate and is way better than the 151 and 152 professors. He cares and also provides a lot of practice resources which others don't.

Dr. Baum is clearly passionate about the concepts within evolution (the module he covered in the lecture. He provides many practice quizzes to help students obtain and practice the knowledge. However, he was hard to understand and not very technology savvy leading to having to rely on the textbook and the lecture recordings.

Dr. Baum is one of my favorite professors I've had at UW! I had the pleasure of having him as a professor in both BIO 152 (intro biology) and ZOO 410 (evolutionary biology), and he was exemplary in both courses. Dr. Baum is an excellent lecturer and very accessible. He goes above and beyond to help make sure students succeed :)

Over qualified for lecturing an introductory Biology course (I mean this is a positive manner). Inspiring and clear in explaining concepts.

Provided a helpful review lecture prior to the final exam for his section that covered student-suggested concepts for clarification.

Dr. Baum is a knowledgeable and highly qualified evolution professor. This was one of the few times that I felt there was more than enough practice material and help sessions for one to do well in the class. He cares about student success; if you put in the work, you can definitely succeed in his section of the class.

Dr. Baum is a solid lecturer who obviously cares a lot about his students. He's very available outside of class, and provides practice quizzes for each reading which are perfect for preparing for exams. His lectures are organized. He also obviously knows a ton about the subject, since some of the concepts are things he's worked on personally.

Davids lectures are boring compared to Simon and Johnathan, but all 152 lectures are slow. He gives WAY more practice questions than the other 152 profs, which allowed me to easily get 100% on his exam. If you can listen to his lectures without falling asleep you'll be fine.

His evolution module was my favorite out of the 3 in 152. He had multiple help sessions per week and also created lecture quizzes after each lecture to make it easier to review. He made the course content very interesting, and is ultra-qualified.
Dr. Baum showed that he cared about the topic he was teaching, evolution and in his lectures he often explained the topic clearly.

Baum is a decent professor who is clearly passionate about what he is teaching. Lectures were taught at a slow pace making it hard to stay engaged, but plenty of outside resources were provided to help study for the exam. The exam was fair and very straightforward. Overall, I personally wouldn't want to take from him again but not bad nonetheless.
Lectures were definitely fast-paced and full of lots of information. If powerpoints were a bit more detailed that would really help with the fast pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Baum is very passionate about biology and also about iClicker. He will call on people who raise their hands in the front row to answer questions, too (if they raise their hands). While I struggled majorly with the evolution module, 
he is accessible for answering questions during office hours which helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Baum is definitely one of the best professors I have had so far. He was accessible outside of class and his exam was super fair. If you studied it went well. Having said this, Baum gives out practice quizzes for each lecture which are just like the exam. Overall, his section was well organized and had plenty of resources to succeed.
Snobby and arrogant. Makes students explain their answers to iclicker instead of him. Impossible test and quizzes. Also forces you to learn about his own research and tests you on it. Avoid.

I found his lectures not very helpful but attending them is mandatory which just meant that I had to do extra studying for the content covered during class because I couldn't understand the way he presented it.
Absolute Goat

Professor Baum gave great lectures that made the content simple to follow. The material was really dense but definitely manageable. Accessible outside of class and will answer any questions to help you understand the material
Professor Baum is a super great lecturer who makes sure to give plenty of practice quizzes, practice questions, and opportunities for students to ask questions. Hes a good teacher and a funny guy.
exams are just like the given non-mandatory practice quizes

Great Professor. Genuinely nice, funny guy who wants his students to do well. He answers every and any question you ask and never makes you feel dumb for asking them. Bio 152 is a hard class in my opinion, but I don't hate it so far because of how good of a professor he is. Wonderful person.

The transition to online happen during his module. Personally, not a fan of Evolution and found some concepts really hard. Gives a lot of quizzes (not graded) to help students. Exam was challenging. Had multiple office hours. Loves iclicker.
He really knows his stuff and manages to make dry material very interesting. He is totally respected and actually pretty funny. I would take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took his Major Transitions in Evolution FIG and absolutely loved it. He is a great guy who genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are fascinating and he's passionate about his subjects. I will be taking more classes from him in the future.

Wonderful lecturer. Abandoned his students in this class and let his TAs make promises that impacted everyone in the end. Take his classes in person where the grades are handled by people who know what they're doing instead of the unqualified TAs he selected for this course. If anything takes Genetics instead of this online class.

David talked about a million things per lecture. The slides were packed with information that was hard to get all the information out of them before he moved on. He seemed to care about the success of his students but test questions were often written poorly and were pretty tricky sometimes. His sections requires a lot of understanding.

David is a really great professor who genuinely cares about students and their success. His lectures can get pretty detailed so reading the book is important. He encourages questions during class and loves to engage with students. Honestly just a wonderful human being. I would definitely take his class again. Exams are not super easy so study!

Dr. Baum was a wonderful professor who is very engaging and has a lot of fascinating material. That being said, his lectures are often too detailed and complicated. Verbal feedback/Questions from students during lecture are too emphasized, and frankly not conducive to a productive lecture environment. Exam much harder than previous material as well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The beginning information was clear of the section. However the last three lectures leading up the exam were very detailed and were asked in detail on the exam. Sometimes the wording was confusing as well. Exam was hard so study!

Dr. Baum was a fun professor to have. He cared about his students and wanted all of us to succeed in his FIG. The subject matter itself is a little difficult to understand, but he does his best to make the students interested in it and experts on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Baum is a great professor. He is passionate about the course material, and more than ready to help you if you need it. He genuinely wants you to succeed, even outside of his class, and helped me understand how undergraduate research works, and what to expect out of interviews and the like. Don't be afraid to ask him for help outside of class!
Dr. Baum cares about what he is teaching, and his lectures reflect this and are very interesting. His FIG is awesome!

Professor Baum is a great instructor! He knows his field very well (even incorporated his own research into the lectures--how cool is that?!) and it's fun to listen to him present. He's extremely accessible outside of class, whether online or in person. He genuinely cares about student success and is willing to go the extra mile.

My favorite teacher so far, had him for a seminar class and he was so caring about every student's needs and individual pace. He's very into the material and it's clear that he loves teaching and everything evolution and botany. If you have the chance to be his student you are lucky and will see why he is such a great professor!

Such a great professor!! Its clear that he really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. His exams are not to difficult if you attend lecture and study the lecture material. Consider yourself lucky if you get him as a professor!
Best professor I've ever had... At madison :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Baum's one of the best lecturers across the Biology department, he explains things very clear and actually cares for your grades. His exams are fairly okay, quite easy if you study and do a lot of the practice questions provided by him. Questions could be tricky in the exams, so make sure you read it a few times. But overall, his classes are great

Dr. Baum is a caring and patient professor who is nice to students. He is always willing to explain the questions to us. Some of the questions in his quizzes and exams are pretty tricky and confusing, and the exam is harder than sample exam even he said they would be equally difficult. But overall, he is a very nice and clever professor.

Dr. Baum is one of the reasons I saw the true value in going to a well respected research university. He incorporates his research into the lectures - which may sound intimidating, but it actually made the lecture more interesting. He is invested in helping. His exam was very wordy and 3x as difficult as the practice test, so beware of that.
I have never met a professor who is more involved or caring. Prof Baum makes class time enjoyable and really sparks my interest further into biology. 10/10 recommend for sure.

Baum is so knowledgeable and is such an effective teacher! He does a good job encouraging student participation which really helps everyone engage in the lecture material rather than just absentmindedly copying down slides. He clearly explains all important concepts and what will be on the exam, with practice exams provided.

Baum is a sweet professor who is good at explaining concepts. He really encourages participation in class through TopHat questions. His quizzes and questions are very similar to the exam questions which overall makes his portion of the class very easy if you pay attention in lecture.

Professor Baum is an awesome guy, full of energy and very knowledgeable. He can explain complex ideas clearly and is very willing to let students understand ideas. His lecture is interesting and inspirational. Definitely do not miss the lecture (also because of Tophat). He seeks feedback from students about the courses.

Had Prof. Baum for 1/3 of a semester during which he covered evolution. As a lecturer he is engaging and fun to listen to. He has occasional funny remarks to make about what he is teaching and that is a gem. The only problem was that at times the Tophat questions in lecture or those on the exam were phrased in a confusing manner. But it isnt toobad

Professor Baum is a great guy. He was able to make the lectures interactive in a class of 300. Very good at presenting material in an understandable way and good at answering questions. He does write somewhat tricky questions for quizzes and exams, but he was clear on what you need to know for them. Reading the text is helpful, but not necessary.
David is amazing and funny and adorable and i would suggest him to anyone because he is the best. He explains things well and asks students for questions very frequently during lecture.

He was a decent professor and a nice guy, but his tests are designed to trick you. There were numerous problems which made you second guess on, or just have 2 or 3 answers that seemed right and you needed an encyclopedic understanding to answer it correctly. Steer clear if you're looking to get an A, it's extremely difficult with Baum.
Not much to say.  He is a very passionate speaker, and is very clear in his lectures.  The class itself can be challenging, but Baum makes it worthwhile.

David is one of the best professors I have ever has. He was really excited about his teaching and worked to make sure that students understood the material. He came to our discussion sections and talked to everyone. He was approachable in and out of class.
He really enjoys teaching and makes the class enjoyable. The exams are kind of tricky so pay attention in lecture. The IP project will take over your life so be prepared.

David is a great professor.  He is very enthusiastic about his work and material is very clear.  He is extremely willing to answer your questions and is very approachable.  Test questions can be a bit confusing though.

David is a really nice guy!  He attended lab sections in an effort to get to know people, and learned a lot of names in our 200 person lecture.  Reading is not mandatary or necessary, but it's helpful for clarification.  Printing off slides is a good idea.  That being said, he does like to trick you on exams...be sure to read carefully!

Baum is a great professor. He is such a nice guy and really understands what he's talking about. Tests can be kind of tricky, but he holds review sessions and is very helpful in them. And he has the best accent!

Baum is a great professor. He is very nice, and very helpful. Sometimes he gets so caught up and excited about what he teaches, he often confuses himself. His tests were long, and tricky. Labs are jokes jokes jokes! This class is like an english com arts course but with some science. Dont skip, he uses materials outside the book too.

Baum is a decent professor. He uses a lot of iClicker questions for credit so make sure to go to lecture. His tests are tricky. Lots of long-winded conceptual questions so you should study quite a bit. It is easy to get a B in this class. Getting an AB or an A is a little more challenging. Lab write ups are a lot of work outside of the actual lab.

Professor Baum is a great professor. The multiple choice exams are difficult but that is a personal opinion. Very helpful during office hours. He's very passionate about the material he's teaching and wants students to understand it also. Slightly unrelated, the lab section is very frustrating and monotonous with pointless time consuming write ups.

LOVED Baum! He expects a lot from his students but he makes himself available for questions and is amazing at knowing what his students don't understand. He teaches his students in a way that really makes them learn the material. If you can, take a class with him!

Prof. Baum is adorable.  He's passionate about what he teaches, and explains himself well.  He's great at interacting with the class and always encourages questions.  The course itself wasn't fun, but he was a great professor.

Baum was fantastic. I was really bummed with 151 until the evolution section w/ Baum. Great lecturer. Really showed the beauty of evolution. He was so enthusiastic and really passionate about teaching all of the fascinating aspects of evolution to us.  Encouraged asking questions and encouraged thinking.  Seemed like a really nice, intelligent guy.

Awsome professor. The class isn't curved, but he wanted to make sure that everyone understood the material. If you're confused about something, all you have to do is ask- he's more than willing to help.

Of the 3 lecturers, he was the best! explained evolution well, made lectures more enjoyable than the other two professors did, and has a great british accent to hold your attention if evolution isnt your thing. uses slides and gives practice quizzes and exams. encourages participation by having students write out questions that he answers via emial
He's adorable. I love this guy.

You have to be really organized with his class.  Note taking is easy enough when he gives you the print outs with holes to make sure that you are paying attention and coming to class.  On the other hand, it is really difficult to fill those gaps when you are sick and can't find anyone who can fill those gaps.  Love the plant of the day.

Dr. Baum rocks! His lectures were almost always interesting and even entertaining. They include everything from Harry Potter, to tea making, to Guiness commercials, to the "woad" song. Even with these fun elements, he presents excellent material and is a great teacher. His tests are not the easies...studying and class attendance is a must!

prof. baum is the cutest little guy with an english accent and an awesome teacher!! WAYYY better than Hernandez, so if you can put up with her, you'll do well with baum. his powerpoint lectures are very organized and clear.
This professor rocks!! His lectures are so much fun, and he even taught us how to make tea.  I just wish he taught more Botany classes for undergrads!
Very helpful, very passionate. He incorporated lots of fun stuff into the lectures. He really loves what he does!
Great professor, very dedicated and doesn't try to trick you on exams.  Good guy!
Nice guy, easy to follow.
hes a really nice guy and the best of the three. his material seems easier than the other two, but his tests are kinda hard. he doesn't test on stuff out of the book, so don't even bother reading it

He is the reason I go to lecture.  He's a lot better than Goodman and Perna, and allows everyone to write down a question after lecture, and then responds to them via e-mail!  It's really helpful.  He also is a cute little man, his accent is fun to listen to.

an average professor. teaches from power point, never takes test material from the book, so don't waste your time reading it. easy class if you go to lecture. tests are MC, not too bad. he has a thick british accent with a lisp! entertaining sometimes.
Nothing good to say about him!

Nice person, but lectures are a bit old fashioned(talk a lot about historical stuff and physical layer) and not recorded. Must read textbook in great detail and take notes carefully.
This isn't a surprise if you look at his research focus, so decide yourself if you want a more modern style & content (take with Ming Liu) or Barford.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fairly big class, but Prof. Barford makes it feel like a discussion and the focus is on understanding the material. Really interesting, and Barford is so willing to go into in depth explanations during lecture. Extremely nontechnical course, tests are easy if you just listen/engage in lecture (do not skip class), plus 3 month-long Python projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gas professor. Definitely the best CS professor I've had.

Amazing professor! Teaching a class as difficult as this and making it easy to understand is his specialty. There are a lot of big projects you work on and they are pretty difficult but he delivers lectures like Steve Jobs and his very passionate about his job. Would 100% recommend.

He's a great lecturer but in every other aspect the class was kinda meh. The projects are fine. The quizzes are not super hard. This class is great for undergrad students who want to learn stuff from scratch but probably not as helpful for grad students who know a lot of this stuff and are really trying to get into the details.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Never choose his course. It is not a CS course, it is a history and literature course, never show codes or PPT, just the blackboard.

Absolutely amazing professor, it hurts me to see such poor reviews on here. His lectures are so captivating and interesting, imbuing his passion for the topic in his students. He truly does know how to teach a class, and actually cares for his students. He takes things very casually and the overall vibe of the class is super chill.

Fantastic lecturer; the best professor that I've had and probably will have during the course of my undergraduate degree in college. Lecture is behind schedule because he loves answering questions and does not like to read off slides. A pleasure to have him as a professor. I average around 50% attendance maximum in cs, i will be at all his lectures

As other people said, projects and quizzes are not related to the lecture. Quizzes questions are very detailed. Besides, we are really behind the schedule. I regret taking this course with Prof.Barford.
cool af

Lectures are fine but too bad they are not very related to exams and not at all to projects. The professor asks super detailed questions on the quizzes. Don't take this class with Barford unless you want to memorize every single piece of the notes.

You can tell Barford not cares at all about his students, especially when the class is now moved online amid this pandemic. He just offers a bunch of pre-recorded lecture videos he had last year at Epic and leave all learnings for the rest of the semester to the students so they have to sit at home and watch a 3-hour-long recording every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Barford is a decent lecturer. There wasn't a time where I was confused about anything. He's average when it comes to explaining algorithms. However, his quizzes are rather unfair as some questions have very subjective answers, and every 2 pts lost makes you lose 1% of your grade. "You have to choose the best answer". Ugh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Barford's lectures are very interesting and inspirational and have a very good flow in them, but he is not very good at explaining details of protocols and network algorithms. Explanations are normally inefficient and redundant. Projects are helpful in understanding materials (somewhat). So read the book before lectures if you take his class

Not a college level computer science course. Lectures are low-quality and incoherent. Projects require using a contrived python framework called switchyard which has little real-world relevance. Avoid cs640 with Paul Baford if possible, instead try to take it with Aditya Akella if available, or just read W. Richard Stevens' TCP/IP illustrated
Good lectures, but too bad theyre irrelevant to projects/quizzes. If you think this is a CS class, think again. Its everything but CS (mainly history, physics, with a hint of EE)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: TLDR: Never, ever take a class with Barford. He often snaps at people who ask questions or makes fun of them, if he even takes questions at all. He is lazy and does not update course materials, so you are left guessing on exams. Always cancels office hours. Projects unrelated to lecture material. Really disappointed. Needs to be audited.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Engaging and solid lecturer. Does a great job explaining introductory topics in Networking. Exams and Quizzes were multiple choice for the first time and require a decent amount of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Barford is highly knowledgeable in advance networks topics. His classes are very interactive, creating a healthy discussion environment for students to express ideas and ask relevant questions. His lectures in general are very inspiring.

Professor Barford is very knowledgeable and this comes across during class. With that being said, he can also be intimidating and rather flippant about comments/questions asked during lecture. Tests are very lecture-heavy, so make sure to take good and specific notes--and this shouldn't be too hard because he does explain content clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Barford does not respond to questions in lecture. He is sarcastic and unhelpful.
Very good lecturer. A lot of details are presented in this course, and he makes them all crystal clear, though it is difficult to keep track of them all. Quizzes/exams are difficult.
Super difficult quizzes and exams which focus on memorizing small details on subjects. Lectures were interesting for the most part, but a lot of information is presented in the lectures.

Barford is very knowledgable in the material.  He takes difficult topics and makes them easy to understand.  He teaches them so clearly that I rarely relied on the book to reinforce the concepts.  He lectures on everything you need to know in the quizzes and exams, and he makes clear what to expect on them.

Barford is an unbelievably good resource for students. His copious amount of knowledge in the field as well as generally phenomenal insight into any situation made this class phenomenal. Genuinely cares about your product and your learning.
He is a good teacher. But the exam is too weird that you can only know what he is asking after you see the answers. If you would take his class, then good luck.

Excellent teacher and very knowledgeable in the field.  A high-level mover and shaker, so it's exciting to having him teaching an undergraduate class.  On the down-side, the guy cannot write exams and his exams can be extremely hard and pedantic with an emphasis on memorization of minute details.  Study hard, do all the work and you may do well.
He grades way too harshly for an online class.
Bart is the kind of teacher that I wish I had more often. He pushes you to think critically and perform to the best of your ability. Not afraid to throw some humor into class.

Gave good and useful feedback, and grading was clear once he had graded it. However, before having graded it we were often not given instructions on what to do or what was expected and then had to learn this class "in hindsight", which was incredibly irritating at times. Was kind and connected to us despite being online.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absurdly harsh grader and isn't an engineer so gets lost in technical details. Rude when grading as well.
This professor is not compassionate, and quite of a harsh grader.

Overall a solid choice for 397. Didnt get as good of a grade as I would have liked, but the class was taught well and graded fairly. What made the class difficult was that the grade is based on a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is like that weird cousin you have. You know they are part of your family but you try to pretend they are not. So yeah, there is some important stuff in here but because it is engineering they lay on a ton of material.  Bart puts a lot into this class and is very well spoken. He is a good instructor. This class should only be in the AM!

Great professor. He teaches a required class that no one wants to take but somehow having him as a professor made it better. He will not give you an A for fluff, and you have to participate in his class. He isn't going to give you a good grade without putting in the work, but he teaches the way classes should be taught. Very highly recommend him.

I came into this class with no interest, it was just a required class I had to take. But Bart knows his stuff, is well spoken and the class turned out to be incredibly useful for me. He's a tough grader and expects a lot, but if you put in the work you will come out far more prepared (especially if you're an engineer) for the business environment
She's truly awesome and you can tell she really cares about her research and teaching.

Lecture slides pulled almost directly from the book. For this reason, I rarely attended lecture. The book is dense, but read and you'll know everything to know for the tests (plus examples in the slides). The 2 noncumulative exams were designed to make you succeed (MC, T/F, matching) with EC. Discussion attendance is required. Would take again 100%

Professor Bates was amazing! Her exams were straightforward and as long as you knew the reading material and went to most of the lectures you were fine. In office hours she is so engaging and kind and went out of her way to help me find resources to add to my understanding. Would absolutely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Principles of intl law w Professor Bates and I loved it. The class is relatively easy if you show up, take notes, read course materials, and study for the exams. Both the midterm and final exams require intense studying if you want a good grade. Also, she is very knowledgeable and makes the lectures engaging and informative. Would take again

Annie clearly has no background knowledge about what she's teaching, cannot answer in-depth questions about the content, and doesn't care about helping students or seeing them succeed. Truly astounding that she even got hired to teach at UW.

Dr. Baur has interesting lectures and is willing to help. She is willing to help you understand concepts in office hours which her counterpart is not. Her lectures are engaging but she talks very fast.
Professor Bauer did a careful job making the points clear. I enjoyed the class and her lectures

Professor Bauer and Zoet co-taught my class, and there was a big difference between the two. Annies lectures were hard to understand and very much more difficult to process and take notes on. I would not recommend to take her class, it is not as  is advertised as an "easy science for non science major" Bauer made it so much harder than it should be

I went into the course thinking I would enjoy a class on national parks, but it ended up being overall stressful because of all the different topics that are covered in such a short time period. It heavily relies on memorization, but the exams were luckily MC. Two professors taught this class and I preferred Prof. Zoet, but that's just my opinion!

There were two professors for this class, and I preferred Bauer a bit more. Knew what she was talking about and answered every question that was asked in lecture. Interesting lectures. I did take Geosci100, which definitely helped me, class would've been harder if I didn't have the basics down already. Exams more difficult than they should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are interested in this course, don't let other reviews scare you.  I always looked forward to attending lectures, found them very interesting, and feel like I learned a ton over the semester.  Professor Bauer is very kind and knowledgeable, and clearly has lots of experience in the field, making her a great source for further questions.
Dr. Bauer made geochemistry interesting with every lecture. She was always engaging and her lecture slides were visually stimulating. She is stickler for due dates though.

I didn't find this class to be as difficult as many are saying. It's online, so quizzes and exams were easy enough if you knew where to find answers, never once did I study or stress for an exam. Overall I found it pretty interesting and I learned a lot.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. Dr. Bauer is very clearly proficient in geology, but her class is not suited for an "elementary" level course. A lot of effort was put into succeeding, but nothing paid off. I would not recommend this course for anyone who does not plan to use geology in their future.

This class is almost impossible. I did everything for this class, I watched all lecture videos, took notes, and reached out for help when needed and I still did terrible on almost all tests/quizzes. I do not recommend this class if you don't need to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was so hard for no reason. I thought I would take it for fun coupled with the harder intermediate courses I was taking. I watched all the lectures, took detailed notes, and completed the study guides. I still would get Cs on every test. I never once got 100% on a test or quiz. Also the lectures are hard to follow.

For a 100 level course, this might be the most unnecessarily hard class for no reason. You could go from getting a 9/10 on the quiz and have studied the material, watched all the lectures, done all the reading and still get a D or F on the test, which by the way, is most of the averages on the exams. If you are taking this class for fun, don't.

This was the hardest class I've taken in college. I thought this would be an easy and interesting 100-level course, but I read/watch everything, take notes, and for some reason started with an A but have been getting Fs or Cs on the most recent quizzes - which you have every week. This class caused so much unnecessary stress - do not take it.

Annie is nice but her class was painfully hard. I was initially excited for the course because it covered National Parks but I found myself so stressed that I never enjoyed the content. The quizzes/exams are atrocious. I always watched lecture, went to office hours, asked her for advice, etc. but still got D's every time. Tears were shed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: GeoScience109 was SO hard, especially for an "elementary" level course. At the beginning of the semester, I, along with other students, expressed to the professors how difficult the content was to follow and they basically ignored the situation. They adjusted what was "passing" THREE times because so many people were doing poorly in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Prof. Bauer's GS109 class, particularly in an online format. For an elementary level class, it was extremely difficult and the lectures seemed disjointed, trying to pack a LOT of content into a short window. I did appreciate that she made herself available outside of class to answer questions, and she was very kind.

The instructor really does not understand deeply the subject he teaches. His lectures are a hotchpotch of stuff that you can just learn by yourself. It's not a good use of your time taking his course.

I am greatly disappointed with his special topic course. I thought such courses are for graduate students to learn something that they can use for research. His course is so low level that it does not prepare you for research. I would rather take another advanced course that other professors offer.
