Baha is a funny guy, but this class was absolutely impossible to follow. I've been successful at physics in the past, but I had absolutely no idea what was going on in this class. The only reason I passed was because I was able to slightly tweak the homework solutions to fit the test questions. He made me seriously consider switching my major.

This man made me love physics even more. Take his classes! He is extremely intellectual and knows SO much. He will make lectures entertaining with his stories. 

That being said, you have to do some work on your own because you learn only so much during lectures. If you spend 2 hours every day I am sure you will do more than amazing in this class.
Taking a class with Baha Balantekin is my worst experience at UW-Madison. I learned nothing from him. Avoid him at all cost.
An old professor who does not know how to teach. He does not make an effort to help students learned. Worse than Pan.
I learned absolutely nothing from Baha. He is an old obnoxious guy who does not know how to teach. He couldn't care less about his students. Take this course when it is taught by another professor.

Baha is a funny guy. Did I learn anything from him? No, absolutely not. Did I show up to class just to listen to him ramble about unrelated things, yes. He goes off on tangents a lot, and is nearly impossible to follow, but the class is entertaining.
Baha is unspeakably rude to the students. He offers no help and is never available. He does not have passion in what he does.

Baha has got to be the worst professor I have ever taken a class with. He put no effort in teaching and his teaching skills are lacking, despite being a very old professor. I wanted to be a physics major but became very disappointed after taking his class.

He was a very unenthusiastic professor. I came to Madison wanting to major in Physics but going into the next semester I can safely say that my major is switching. This class is completely boring and the method of teaching really wasn't great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is teaching half of the course with Pan. I thought Pan is bad but Balantekin is worse. Lectures are dull and uninspiring. He is never around and is unwilling to offer help to students. He should learn how to teach.

The most awful professor I've ever had. I lost interest in physics after taking his dull and uninspiring classes. He does not know answers to simple questions. He is never available, and refuses to meet with students to help them cope with their struggles.
He has taught the second half of the course, and it is just awful. Everyone complains about his teaching style or lack there of. Just not a good professor. I strongly advice against him

Baha makes no effort in teaching. He is the lazest professor I have seen at UW-Madison. Not answering emails and does not make himself available when students are struggling to learn from his poorly prepared lectures.

Awful professor. Very lazy and never responds to students' emails. I have heard him mocking us in front of Professor Brar who split teaching with him. Baha Balantekin is the most awful professor at UW Madison.

Split class lecturing with Professor Brar; lecture slides weren't very helpful and attending class was important. Textbook was good help. Homework was usually due once a week and relevant for the exams -- the TAs were by far the best resource and very helpful for both homework and exams. Labs could be confusing, but grading was workable/reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Creepy old man. Superlazy and did not respond to students' emails. Learned absolutely nothing from him. His lectures create more confusion than knowledge. He got concepts completely wrong and his lectures were disorganized.The other professor is better but not great either.

His lectures are so frustrating. He is terrible at explaining things and is completely flustered and unorganized. Tests and labs aren't terribly hard, but the homework gets difficult at the end of the semester. I didn't feel that the lectures gave me enough info to do the homework.

As somebody who is NOT a math person.... the second half of the class with Baha was much more difficult than the first half, but it was still pretty simple. The math isn't complex and there really isn't that much material being taught. There's a few concepts that he goes over again and again. I thought he was very clear + liked him a lot.
Baha taught the second half of the semester and I did not enjoy it as much as the first half of the semester. It was not an awful class but his half was harder for me and I struggled a lot more.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He seems to be teaching this class repeatedly for many years but to my surprise, he does not seem to know the materials well. The other instructor is better in comparison (though not great either). Never learn anything from his lectures and he does not want to spend time outside lectures explaining concepts to you if you are confused.

Baha is by far the worst professor I have seen at UW-Madison. Lectures are useless and are disconnected from the homework and the exams. He is not willing to help his students. He would rather leave you confused than to spend any of his time. Avoid him at all cost.

Baha is a very nice man to talk with, but the class itself should not even be offered as an option for non-majors. You'll go into the class on the first day, and they'll reassure you that you'll learn the material easily, but that's definitely not the case. The labs are really long and boring. Tests are hard and weigh heavily on your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: baha is way overqualified to teach this class. it just kind of shows. but if you truly understand the material (easy) you'll be fine on exams, which are 75% of your grade. no major curveballs or anything that's impossible to figure out if you actually studied. the labs were very poorly written and designed (not baha's fault) but you can do it!
Hes an alright lecturer and his homework is quite easy but his exams are much more difficult than any of the material he presents. Definitely a disappointment to the faculty at UW-Madison.

He was not always clear on what he meant during lectures. He says one thing and the textbook another. Wasnt great at responding to questions. I found professor Gilbert's lectures to be more informative.
Baha LOVES what he teaches, which really helps make the course material easier to understand and learn. His exams are tougher than I expected, but fair.

Teaching style that only caters to people who are good at physics. The tests are tricky and he does that on purpose. He does respond to emails somewhat quickly so that is a plus. Overall this course is brutal and he does not make it any easier.
Baha tends to go through the lecture slides very quickly and does few practice problems.  I didn't find the class hard but I didn't end up learning the material until I did the homework.

This class was co-taught by Susan Coppersmith. He taught most of the second portion of the class, which was the sound section. The homework was much more difficult than what we discussed in class. I always felt I understood lectures, but he should have done example problems. Tests are easier than the labs and homework. Seems like a nice guy.

No help from this guy. When asked to schedule an office hours appointment, he came up with all kinds of lame excuses like he has other important meetings. I talked by his office and saw him just gossiping with his colleagues.  I was greatly disappointed.
He has no patience with students. Does not want to spend any time with you to help you understand the material. Lectures are unclear. The other prof is better.

Good lecturer that is very passionate about his field and extremely knowledgeable. Test are kind of brutal, but the other professor (Winokur) was more at fault for that. He's a nice guy and a pretty decent professor.

Honestly his lectures were a bit hard to sit through. Just because I would get bored and it's hard to take good notes because lecture was all about applying the reading material to real stories and examples. Super easy to pass though. Mostly essays. Nice, funny person.
Grades too harshly and assigns too many readings that are unnecessary

Very interesting lectures, you can tell he is very knowledgable but the class itself ended up being very repetitive. Majority of the grade is based on four papers graded by TAs, so you need to have a good TA to succeed in this class. Content is easy enough, but grading criteria is very vague. I don't recommend this class at all.

great lecturer and cares a lot, but you need a good TA because there are 4 papers that make up 65% of your grade. my TA was way harsher than the others and it's hard to raise your grade if your papers get scored low. the lectures ended up feeling super repetitive, but the content was interesting. some of the concepts were kinda abstract.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be hard to follow, but there aren't many assignments, and your grades are focused mainly on the papers. Unfortunately, the papers are hard to complete as there isn't much direction, and the prompts can be confusing. TAs also grade very inconsistently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Prof. Beattie; he was super caring and passionate about his field. The class itself was easy, yet you are graded mainly by 4 essays. The essays have many requirements, yet are limited in word count. Additionally, there is not much direction in the papers, so you lose points on things you didn't know you needed. Great guy, not great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is passionate and interesting to listen to in lecture if you are also interested in Envir. Studies. The class is test heavy (4 main papers) but that is because there are only a few multiple choice quizzes and a final that make up the rest of the grades. The grading is relatively easy so the papers weren't bad. I would totally take his class agai
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class thinking it would be relatively simple since it was just for my social science credit, but there are a lot of readings assigned for lectures, and papers are big. But they are helpful for the four papers. It's a little annoying when the paper prompts are posted two weeks before it's due, and future lectures are important for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: No tests except the final and he prepares the lectures to match the quizzes and papers. Cool dude
He was so boring. Nice guy but really boring and the TA's graded so inconsistently. His exams were really easy but lots of reading.

Great professor! Funny and engaging lectures..you don't HAVE to go but is beneficial. Discussions are easy to participate in. You have 4 BIG papers: if you read rubric and textbook you'll do good on them. Final Exam was SO easy: short answer given beforehand and multiple choice VERY similar to quizzes ;) Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing prof and perfect level of breadth and difficulty for an intro ENVS class. It is clear Beattie is both knowledgable and cares deeply about his students. Lectures/papers are engaging and thought provoking but course is overall low stress. 112 was well-structured, interesting, and forgiving if you need to miss.100% would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Beattie's lectures were engaging and you can tell he is very enthusiastic about the topics. The module essays are useful for understanding the content and make up most of your grade in the class.

I loved this class and the way he taught it! Heavily graded on papers but we got time to work on them during discussion... easy to do well on, integrated lots of course content. Had quizzes which were a bit challenging because some questions were very specific but still manageable. The final exam was composed of quiz questions. Highly recommend!

Beattie is such a nice professor. Always helpful and genuinely cares about his students. The class was an easy A, and our essays were graded very clearly. You do have to go to discussion (attendance points), but in all, this class was not stressful at all. Had about a week to do an essay, quizzes were open note, and the final was old quiz questions

Had him this fall. Easy  A. You get 4 essays and 5 open note but timed canvas quizzes and a final exam that is word for word the quiz questions and that's about it. No homework except reading, which tbh I didn't really do at all unless I was researching for one of the essays. His lectures are interesting and he's nice, would take again.

I switched into this class after the first week and Beattie was very helpful in getting me caught up. Whenever I had a question he was quick to respond and always available during his office hours. I greatly enjoyed his lectures and the way he challenged us to think. Asked him to be a reference for an application and he was very excited about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He clearly loves what he is talking about. This may be the easiest class I have ever taken in my life. Graded on 4 loosely graded papers, easy to get 100% on. Sometimes lecture gets a bit boring. There is not much takeaway from this class but trivia and a gpa boost. I would highly recommend.

Discussions mandatory (can miss 1-2). Graded based mostly on 4 papers, a few open note quizzes, and a final (worth 10%). He is fun and passionate about the topics he teaches and cares about students, but it can get boring and repetitive at times. Spent a lot of time talking about race/politics, wish we would have focused more on environment itself

Professor Beattie is funny and clearly passionate about the material he teaches. Homework will consist of optional daily readings, very few online quizzes, and 4 essays. ENVIR ST/GEOG 139 is extremely similar to this class, but I recommend taking this instead of that if you are debating. If you are curious or need the credits, take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: I took beattie's class during covid and loved it. Super interesting and when I tested positive he is very caring to give extensions and help out. There's a lot of readings but nothing that's stressful and most is to the point. He's really passionate about his studies and makes it known that he cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved learning from Prof Beattie; he's caring, understanding, and interesting. He livestreams all of his lectures to make it accessible to everyone. Quizzes are online and open note so theyre usually manageable. Writing assignments arent bad either, very straightforward. Exam was a breeze since he basically tells you everything you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Beattie's passion for the subject shines through during his lectures, which are interesting and cover a wide range of topics relevant to current issues. The text is easy to read, and attendance is mandatory in discussion section but not in lecture. Grades are heavily based on papers, which are easy to score highly on.
Okay take this class if your passionate about the environment and you understand deep thinking about ways to fix/understand the environment but ur pretty much on ur own for this class

Dr. Beattie is a really nice professor that gives great lectures. Some people might say that you need to do the readings, but I literally almost never read any of the textbook and still got an A on almost every quiz. Just have your notes out before the quiz and you'll do fine. Essays should be pretty easy if you put effort into them.

Robert Beattie cares about what he teaches and his students, the class is super interesting and if you show up and do the readings you will do well on the papers for sure. Prompts can be a little confusing but you can always ask for clarification

4 1000 word papers make up most of your grade, but they are extremely easy to get an A on. 5 10 question online quizzes are a small part of your grade. The final is open note and only worth 10% of your grade. Beattie is a good lecturer and and always seems genuinely excited to teach. Read the textbook but skim the other readings.

Prof is really sweet but lectures aren't engaging and really boring. If you took APES in high school this class is pretty much a repeat... I've taken maybe 5 pages of notes all semester. Stubborn about Dec. 21 final and has started cold calling for some reason? Good guy but this class is the reason I'm changing my major.

Although some of the class material is interesting, Beattie does not really get straight to the point and rambles a lot. The prompts for papers are excessively long, and directions for how to go about writing the essays are vague. The quizzes can feel demanding- asks very specific questions regarding lectures & readings. They aren't terrible though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice professor, the workload is light and the papers are slight work. The only challenge I faced was that I did not understand how to study for his quizzes. I did fairly well on the quizzes but there was no organized work to study off of.

Dr. Beattie is super passionate about environmental science, and very caring/understanding as well. I got a great TA, but the discussions could have been very boring if that wasn't the case. There are a bunch of readings, but I literally only did one the whole semester and I was fine. He's great at helping you learn from different perspectives!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class, great professor. 50/60 of the final exam questions were taken directly from the quizzes so it was super easy to ace as long as you go back and study the answers. Topics in the class were engaging and interesting. The papers are straightforward and easy to write. The only thing that brought down my grade was the quizzes, but not by much
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes knowledgeable and easy-going. Cares about everyones input, and gets you to consider environmental issues from unique perspectives. The only major grades are 5 1000 word papers, which combined are worth 60% of your grade. You should attend lecture in order to know what to write about in these papers. Participation alone is 15% of your grade.

This man found a bee in the lecture hall and carried it out throuh the building in his hand and let it go outside. He is a legend. He is obviously passionate not only about bees but the environment as well and it shows in his lectures. He teaches in a moderately impartial manner and he acknowledges his own possible bias.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Take this class if you're looking for an easy A with minimal work. A one page paper is due almost each week, along with two five page papers as a midterm and final. No tests, and easy grading. Approached as a survey class, so very little of anything is covered in any detail.
Great professor. Boring class with a moderate amount of work, but a pretty easy A. The content is interesting too!

This class is absolutely boring. VERY easy A though if you actually show up. Discussion is basically pointless and painful if your TA sucks. 11 reading responses and a midterm and final paper. Half the grade is just for showing up to class. I rarely listen to lecture and just sit on facebook for 50 mins. Would recommend for easy SS credits.

The class is basically an open discussion, he doesn't lecture or teach you anything in general. I spend most lectures doodling or playing tic tac toe with neighbors. Don't go unless you want to listen to the same 6 people continually discussing things you already know. No tests, but attendance is mandatory along with weekly essays and projects.
Awesome guy, recomend taking him! Total bro!

Kata is a pretty easy grader, but the readings are very dense (10-40 pages each, 2x/week). The majority of your grade is based on 5 short responses and 3 medium responses to the readings, but you get to choose them. Participation is also very important, you need to participate pretty much every class to get full points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kata is the top professor in the entire language department. We did not have any exams. Most of our grade came from 300-400 word responses to the readings (graded very nicely), and a final essay written as a group. Rather than smothering us w/busywork, Kata focused on creating lively discussions and making us think critically about the world.

Kata's take on environmental studies in the hispanic world is one of the most engaging Spanish classes I've taken at UW. Great balance of readings/documentaries for pre-class preparation; the class is mostly discussion based. Kata is both passionate for the material and compassionate for her students. Truly wonderful class, even though it's online.

I like Professor Beilin! She's kind of vague in what she wants you to do/when you should turn in your essays/even the topics you can write about, but she's very sweet and doesn't put too much pressure on anything. She accepts all types of participation, I never felt like I couldn't participate because she was judging me. I'd take her again for sure

It was a pleasure to have Kata for SPAN224 this semester. She tried her best to make the class minimally stressful and did a wonderful job demonstrating her knowledge of the material. All you have to do is show up ready to discuss the readings and have at least one written essay per unit (3 units total). I would take this class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I've studied at 4 colleges in 3 countries and Kata is one of the best professors I've had. She is fun and dynamic with her lectures and reading materials. She is clear about what is expected and if she sees you putting in the time and effort you will do well in her class. Make sure to participate in class because that will help a lot. Great Profe!

I took the 468 topics course in Environmental Cultural Studies and loved it! Kata was really flexible and obviously really into the subject matter. The class was discussion based and there was a lot of reading. There was no textbook to buy, just mountains of articles to read but they were all really interesting so I never really minded it.

Kata is an amazing professor with a lot of knowledge and wisdom to share.  She is good at engaging the students and is very willing to be a learner and not just a teacher.  She has a great teaching style that is fun and easier to learn from. Definitely recommend her!

Kata is an amazing professor with a lot of knowledge and wisdom to share.  She is good at engaging the students and is very willing to be a learner and not just a teacher.  She has a great teaching style that is fun and easier to learn from.  She is friendly and seems to genuinely care about her students.

Profesor Belin is a great teacher. She attends to the level of her students, sign of a true educator, and brings a well-rounded knowledge of her subject to the students. History comprises art, literature and all human endeavors. She brings this wealth to the students. And her passion for justice. Lucky students. I am eager to take another one.

First impression of Kata is that she has a strange accent, and after some more time in her class, you'll realize that's the least of her problems. She doesn't give guidelines about what she expects of her students, and she's highly disorganized. Definitely take someone else for 223.

I had this professor 11 years ago but she was the most stimulating and dynamic professor I had in undergrad. She got the students to come up with ideas in class which led on to the conclusions she wanted to make, always encouraging creativity on the part of the students.

I studied with this professor 11 years ago but she was the most dynamic and stimulating professor I had in undergrad.She encouraged the students to come up with ideas instead of stating all content herself and moved the lecture on by getting the students to make the logical connections leading to the arguments she was presenting in class.

Honestly the most unorganized class I've ever had. I feel I could confidently say that about 75% of the class didn't know what was expected of them. A whole bunch of stuff was shown in lecture that would never be brought up again so you didn't know how to filter out what was important at all. Plus there are the readings which are pointless.

The first couple weeks of lecture are tough to get used to for sure. She has an interesting accent, goes through her lecture slides extremely quickly, and the reading can pile up. But once you get used to her style of lecture, it is not too bad. Just make sure you keep up with the readings, pay attention in lecture and don't worry about copying eve
She goes through her presentation way too fast for students to clearly understand the material.
terrible dont go to class the test is so easy and you dont use your lecture notes.

She manages to turn an interesting subject into an arduous journey through monotony. Her accent cuts right through you and trying to take notes is beyond frustrating. Ridiculous amounts of reading that really doesn't provide a relevant look at current culture.

There is so much reading required for this class, but it ends up not counting for much.  You write two essays that are not necessarily related to what we learn in class, and you take two tests.  The tests are too simple after all the analysis you do in class and discussion.  The professor is very unclear and hard to understand.  Frustrating class.

THIS IS NOT A CULTURE CLASS IT IS A HISTORY CLASS. What I thought would be interesting ended up being super boring. I skipped class all the time and when I did go I never took notes because she went way to fast. Her tests are pretty easy though. Get the english version of the book if you can...that saved me in this class.

Very bad. The class is supposed to be aboud culture, but she ends up teaching mostly history. Is unclear, lectures have little to do with exam material. Without discussion sections, the exams would be utterly impossible. Accent sometimes hard to understand (she's Polish) and rambles in lectures on nonrelated material.

She is a horrible lecturer. She seems like she has no idea what she's talking about, her presentations are not organized or helpful. It's like she can't decide whether to teach a cultures or history class so she asks vague questions that are more conceptual but the exams are just names dates and facts. Also has a terrible accent. She's just baaad
Lecture is a waste of time, she just rambles with no apparent structure.  Very difficult to understand and really bad at teaching intro culture course.
Often late to class, then reads from notes, rambles, asks for participation in a big lecture but asks really stupid questions. Discussions are ok but lecture is a drag.

Buy english version of textbook. Very stingy on participation points (40% of grade). Assumes we are all taught about Spain in elementary school and that we know info that isn't in the book but we're not from Spain like her. Asks opinion on things but essentially makes dicisions for you. Very boring. DO NOT TAKE IN SUMMER!
Horrible professor. She is a very hard grader and makes you hate Spanish literature. Her lectures are dull and boring and I didn't learn a single thing from her.

Deceent professor, fairly friendly and can be funny. She knows her material and is understanding of students, but often fails to stimulate them. She has a strange accent (Polish, studied in Spain), but is generally understandable. Easy grader.

I really enjoyed Professor Bhavnani's lectures, you could tell that he knew what he was talking about and really enjoyed the subject. He is very clear before the tests what to expect, and is very fair in writing the tests. I found the readings to be optional, he goes over everything you need to know in the lectures.

Probably the best Professor I have ever had and will ever have. Rikhil teaching style is the most organized and easy-to-understand I could imagine. He makes every topic in the class interesting and every reading if fruitful and serves a purpose! The exams are fair and did not spend a lot of time studying for them. Would 100% recommend Rikhil!

This class was fairly easy. He did not clearly outline the first of two exams and I did not know that he would expect us to be able to attach the names of the authors we had read throughout the course to their ideas. There is a very small sample size for the evaluations in the form of 2 exams consisting of 5 IDs and 1 essay. Do the readings.

Great, real world examples. Clear instructor who is very well prepared. Professional. 1 midterm, 1 noncumulative final, one group project. Attendance is mandatory. I had an average level of interest but the class was engaging enough to go by quickly. Fair, clear grading. Great experience, would take again.

Rikhil was a great professor. He clearly knows what he's talking about and everything I learned from this course I feel like I can apply to real life. I'm glad I took his class and would definitely recommend it.

Lectures were interesting and material may be applied to real world situations. Professor was very knowledgable and has a background in development. I looked forward to going to lecture. Tests are IDs and an essay but nothing that isn't difficult. Readings are long but may be skimmed. Recommend to anyone interested in the topic.
Chill

Absolutely amazing class! Started the semester not caring about Indian Politics and left fascinated. Easily my favorite professor, and I am a senior. made a 2 hour class super fun, and he  was really helpful outside of class. Take a course by him!

Course title "Indian Politics in Comparative Perspective" was hands down one of the best courses I've taken in Poli Sci. Professor Bhavnani is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject (he studied at Yale and Stanford, from Bombay originally) and is a fantastic seminar facilitator. Not necessarily an easy A, but worth it.

Professor Karunakaran is a nice guy. He was caring and his lecture is not test heavy. He really wants students to learn practical skills that can apply to your working area. I would say his lecture and slides are helpful.

Bipin was friendly and patient with the students. He was very patient, going back through steps that students missed or misunderstood multiple times. He was also always upbeat, he was passionate about data visualization, data analysis, and machine learning / how gen ai will affect our lives, but kept it simple and achievable for the students.

I really appreciated how hands on the course was, it was fun to actually code, run through machine models, and play around with data. I also appreciated that the professor made it easy to succeed in this course-- hard skills like coding aren't familiar or required for many post business school jobs, so making it easy to succeed in the course.
This prof is unorganized, his code is random and hard to follow. He's more a tech guy than a good lecturer. The course is overall easy but no way I'll take his course again.

Course work is based on practical application in real world business. I found the lectures and projects very useful. They helped in fetching summer intership. I have registed for another class taught by this same professor.

Bipin is extremely unorganized; most of the time, the programs he was "teaching" would go haywire/not work because his data/processes would be invalid, leaving the class confused and frustrated. He also loved to sidetrack on the unnecessary. Albeit, 308 is an easy class, but from this experience I would never take another class with him.

He does a great job at teaching the course. There is a lot of content, but he makes lectures as fun as he can. He mentioned many interesting facts about Wisconsin, which I found cool. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the slides are vague, so you won't learn much just by reading the slides. I would recommend the class to anyone looking for a gen ed

pretty basic concepts of ecology, overall very easy to learn. test questions are multiple choice, but very specific questions, which makes it hard to prepare for. Kind of a boring lecturer, he gets on tangents once in a while, and has a monotone voice. But overall pretty easy class if you are looking for an easy natural science credit!

Jim has been my favorite professor here so far. He seems genuinely passionate about what he is teaching and workload is completely manageable. There's one discussion post per week and two nature walk activities that can provide a good amount of extra credit. Tests do require a fair amount of memorization, but they aren't too bad.

Prof. Berkelman is a very nice guy. The lectures are a little boring content-wise but he is pretty funny and tries to make them more fun. Very easy content just kind of boring. Grading was super lax, all the assignments were essentially full points if you do them on time.

This class is low-key a little boring, but the professor is super nice and passionate. The material is not hard to grasp however the tests are actually pretty difficult compared to what you would except because most of the questions are super niche and nit picky so that is a little tough. DO THE NATURE WALSK EARLY it gives you extra credit
Jim is a great professor, he made me excited to learn about the topics he was teaching and he is very passionate about his work and field.

Honestly, the class is boring. However, the tests have been mcq and there hasn't been much homework. The professor speaks in a very monotone voice. The slides are pretty long but don't a lot of words.

Jim shows an incredible amount of enthusiasm and passion for what he teaches and how he interacts with his students. He really wants everyone to succeed, and if you're paying attention. He gives many hints about what will be on the test during lectures; if he says "maybe," it will probably be on the test.
Jim is a great teacher who is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about forest and wildlife ecology. He is fun in class and makes lectures interesting.
He was fantastic in all 3 of the courses I've taken with him. Really a fantastic lecturer and one-on-one educator.

Jim is easily one of my favorite professors I've had at UW. Having taken three courses with Jim (FWE318, FWE306, FWE424), I cannot recommend him more! Even if you're not a student in Wildlife Ecology and looking to take an elective course with him, his classes are well-organized, well-taught, and incredibly interesting.

I really enjoyed the lectures and Jim's passion for ecology. The field trips are fun and there isn't much work outside of class. The lab and lecture exams cover a LOT of material (study as you go, don't cram). Exams are very memorization-heavy, including Latin classifications. Labs are low pressure (no pre/post lab report) but don't rush them.
Amazing prof. Go ahead and take his FW110 class!

The class wasn't too bad if you studied pretty well for the tests (definitely review Quizlets and his learning objectives), but they're basically the only grades in the class. Submitting nature walks early (for EC) help, as well as discussion posts, but you have to know your stuff to do well on tests. Berkelman's a nice guy though and passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy hard working. His exams are straightforward. His lectures clear and gives good hints.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall, pretty solid course. The nature walk assignment is annoying, but I would get it over with as early as possible bc ec is offered for turning it in early. Grade is pretty reliant on the two midterms and final, so be prepared for that. Lectures could be a little boring, but a pretty good course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally think that he is awesome! He is a tad bit preachy since there is a lot to talk about within this course, but other than that, he is super approachable and really nice to his students! He is also a fair grader and gives you multiple opportunities to get your grade up if you're struggling.

Jim was a great professor. His lectures were a little boring, but the content was interesting and made me appreciate a lot about wildlife. I loved the required guided nature walks, and it allowed me to appreciate nature more. Exams are multiple choice and cumulative, should do fine with a little bit of studying. Weekly online discussions not hard

Berkelman is very informed in the ecology area of study, so he was a great prof to have for FW110. My only complaints are that during exams he often just starts announcing random things, which is distracting and annoying. During lectures he goes on tangents and then doesn't finish the content in time, which takes away from the next class' content.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was fairly heavy on lectures, but all the exams and projects followed the information from class. An interesting speaker, and very knowledgeable about the topics, which made lectures enjoyable. He was very accessible and helpful outside of class, and did offer extra credit opportunities. Overall, a solid choice, I very much enjoyed the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a pretty solid lecturer who has a mix of good lectures and boring lectures. The nature walk assignment is annoying to deal with because if your nature walk leader doesn't show up you have to go to another one, and most nature walks are far away from campus if you don't have a car/bike. Tests aren't that hard, but there's no curve.

Berkelman is a great prof who's clearly passionate about wildlife conservation and all the material. Lectures can be a bit dull, but overall I enjoyed this class and found it easy if you show up and do a bit of studying.

The skull lab was the hardest of the class, but still passable. The second lab was easy. The lecture exams and essays are really good if you know your animals well or at least study right but not too hard.
His lectures are good and clear what will be on the exam. His quizzes can be tough but very doable.

He is a very nice professor and understands the material, is very accessible. All of the information is in the lectures and he tells you exactly what you need to know for exams. The material was very easy for me but if science isn't your thing it may be helpful to take a lot of notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are many easy quizzes throughout each module, yet they trick you into thinking the exams will be just as simple (they are not!). I am not a science person so I found many of the lectures to be lengthy and dull. However, Professor Berkelman's passion on the subject shows, which makes the class worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and I would definitely take a class with Berkelman again! This fall it was all asynchronous and the quizzes are comprehensive, just pay attention and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Berkelman is a great professor. He always responds to emails so quickly. The class is interesting and you learn a lot about wildlife conservation and its importance in our society. His online lecture is fine but the tests are doable if you watch the lectures attentively. In short, he is a good professor.

Very easy to do well in this class if you just take notes on the lectures. There are 3 exams including the final, easy checkpoint quizzes after the lectures, and discussion posts that are all very straightforward; he grades all of them with clear criteria. He is a very knowledgable and wonderful teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: textbooks not mandatory, but helpful. lectures and lab not mandatory (but best if you go because he explains things in more depth in lecture, and lab is important to go to because you look at skulls and skins and need to identify things that will be on the lab exams). I had this class during corona, so the second half of it was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Jim was a very nice prof and you could tell how passionate he is about his field. Unfortunately, his lectures are incredibly boring. He is a very monotone speaker and gives very dry lectures. The lectures he gives have a large amount of slides, but he speaks so slowly he takes two class periods to do one lecture.

Really nice guy. You can tell he is very passionate about ecology, but an extremely dry lecturer. I've never seen such boring presentation before. He speaks in a dull monotone most of the time and loves to ramble extensively on simple topics. Gives lots of opportunities for extra credit

I really liked having him as a professor. Interesting class, clear he enjoys the topic, not too hard. He's a really friendly dude and will remember your name if you talk to him. Willing and able to answer any of your questions. Overall, would definitely recommend this professor and class, especially for non-majors.

This class kinda sucks. It's like an hour of just ridiculous amounts of notes half of which are irrelevant for the exam. Exams are just memorizing terms from lecture so if you like that then this class will be an easy A. He is very funny and a good lecturer but this class just wasn't for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jim Berkelman honestly cares about the subject matter and it shows in his teaching. His homework and grading are reasonable and is flexible towards students missing discussion, allowing them to make up points through extra work.
Easiest class ever.
I learned so much about th extinctions and how to help the animals from this class.
Easiest Ecology class I have ever taken.
He is the best professor ever. This is an awesome class. You will learn how to protect species.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easiest funniest and nicest biology class ever.
Easy class to pass just pay attention in lecture and do the write project and work hard on the essay.
He makes us work in groups in class and make in class activities which are easy the essay helps boost grade and his quizzes and final are great.
He was a very helpful professor. I really liked taking his class.
I learneed so much on how to be nicer to nature and my paper really helped on why I should protect my species. His class was awesome.
What can I say he really is a great professor with good lectures.
He made his 300 level classs more like a 100 level class. Great guy.

His power points are the best out of all UW bio professors. They are great to study from for the exams which are really easy but also educational, I wish all the bio professors gave tests like his. His dull lab was not so hard like I had thought. His essay was great and so were the discussions online easy points. You'll love the field trip.
He really makes sure that the students really know the stuff in class. His essay is one the easiest I had ever written.
His labs had some good quizzes the first was not as hard I thought his tests really good he is very helpful..
He was very helpful and cared a lot about his students and good heads up for the exams. The reports were graded fairly. Really good guy.

The grading criteria for essays seemed pretty vague, but the EC for field trip reports balanced it out. Exams were more about fact/statistic memorization then general concepts, so beware of this before deciding to take the class. If you don't memorize well, choose a different class, but it otherwise felt like a pretty easy course to take.

His forest and wildlife class was super easy and very direct on what we were learning. The tests can be a bit tricky but it's easy to study and there is a TON of extra credit offered if you turn in your essays early
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The most boring class EVER. Do not take! Yes he is very sweet and intelligent guy, that does not mean he is a great professor. Lectures were unbearable, tests were unreasonably hard, and it was just an overall very mediocre experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's very smart, but Berkelman is a subpar lecturer. There were too many topics covered on the tests. If you can memorize facts and the like, you'll be okay. If you're looking for a biology course that's interesting, look elsewhere. If you want something where your grade is determined by your ability to memorize LOTS of basic info, 110 is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, passionate for sure. Lecture slides are posted online. Boring lectures, can get away with skipping. I went to all of them but was on my phone(not paying attention) most of the time. Fill out the test study guide and study it for a few days beforehand.

Boring lectures. The exams are long and too many details to remember. Random facts tested in multiple choice that are not even mentioned in ppt or the study guide. Easy to pass and get a B without going to class. Not recommended for bio credit if you want an A.

I really did not enjoy this class, he's not a great professor (not the worst, but not good, either) and he tests on things that were glossed over, if they were covered, in lectures. Maybe if you're really interested in ecology you'll like him more? I don't know, but he shouldn't be teaching an intro ecology class.
Certain lectures are really engaging, others are boring but this is mostly due to the material. Guest lectures add some variety and make up for the more lackluster days.

Went to class 3 times all semester and got a B. Study by filling out the study guides with the online slides and use Wikiquotes for the Leopold paper. Study at least 2 days in advance (after you've filled out your study guide before each exam). Nice guy, interesting stuff, just easy to get away with not going. Treat it like a free period. Simple.

I think I went to 7 classes total. 3 of which were for exams. I stopped going because the lectures seemed pointless and extremely boring. He sends out a study guide before the exams with all of the important terms on it. All of the slides are posted online. There is a lot of material that you have to know for the exams, especially the final.

Boring but decent lecturer.  Lectures more or less directly off the powerpoints, which are posted online. Lots of readings and homework, but they're pretty easy.  Useful study guides. Reasonable but long tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His class is super easy, all you have to do is put in a minimal amount of effort. Tests are half short answer and half multiple choice. Mostly memorization of things he puts on the slides.

Berkelman is a great professor and really cares about his students. Slightly boring because  he does basically read straight from the slides (available online). Going to class isn't necessary but the tests are pretty tough, you need to study a lot for them. Recommend this class.
He's a great professor. Tests are fair, he likes to joke around, always open to questions and provides advice outside of class. Great FWE Instructor all around. Do go to class and pay attention.

Jim is very available to his students, and even takes the time to learn some of their names in a large lecture. Lectures were a bit long  and his tests were partly short answer and a bit tough at times. However, the amount of extra credit you can earn by going on field trips early makes this class an easy A if you put in the effort.
Reads from the slides, so it's not a big problem if you miss lecture. He's a really nice man.

Worst class I've taken at UW - material either interesting or painfully boring, and there's a lot of it. Jim's nice enough, but is a bad test-writer and paper grader, requiring memorization of random facts to get an A. Don't need the book, but assigned papers to read are tedious. Getting an A is possible, but you'll have to work for it.

Lectures can be boring as he talks off of the powerpoints, but the content is interesting. You have to go on at least one field trip for the class but it's pretty open ended as to what the field trip is. You have to write a couple of papers too but they're graded really easily.

Although he may not be the most gregarious professor at this university, Jim is passionate about this subject and is apparent through the way he lectures. Overall, a good course to take for the bio requirement in L&S and I felt the grading was reasonable.
Decent class, very easy biological science credits. Make sure to do the study guides before exams and you will do fine. Use wikiquotes for the leopold assignment and you don't even have any homework!

Not very exciting, reads off power point but he knows his stuff. He also cared about the students learning everyone's name. Some test questions were meant to trick you but overall was not a hard class and the subject is interesting.

Very helpful and friendly; made a point of learning all ~50 students' names within the first week of class. Not the most captivating, especially for 10 hours a week during the 4-week summer session, but the content is easy and exams are really just memorization.

Exams are completely memorization based so they are difficult if you have no interest in the class. He does provide a way to get a good amount of extra credit. If you're looking for an easy science to fulfill a requirement, pick something else

Very difficult exams, final being the worst. Way too much information to have a cumulative final. Uses "sim-u-text" text book which is a lot of work/reading and easy to do poorly on. Intelligent guy, very very boring lectures where everything is read straight off powerpoint and ridiculous tests.
Nice guy. Reads off of powerpoints that are provided online. No point in going to class, but much studying is needed for exams. Wicked hard finals compared to boring lectures. Stupid class

I took Extinction of species with Jim over the summer, and it was a lot of fun.  We even went on a field trip to the international crane foundation before the last exam.  He teaches clearly, insists on class participation and group work, and gives pretty easy quizes.  Just pay attention to the lectures!

Jim definitely knows a great deal about the content. Admittedly the lectures were at times very dry, he was very clear and it was easy to make up study if you didn't pay attention. Discussions were interesting, better than most. He is very clear, and his passion obviously lies in this area. I would recommend taking this class.

borrrring lectures...he basically just puts up a powerpoint and reads off of it, stumbling through phrases and misprouncing words such as "fungi" and "cacti".  exams are much harder than what the content suggests, but study & you should be okay.  lot of trick questions or multiple answers where the difference is one word.   nice guy, but lame class
Exams are overly hard given the material.  Lots of vague questions on the final.  Make sure you study.  Otherwises, pretty typical class.

He's a pretty nice guy and his class is fair.  His lectures are a little dry sometimes but mostly very clear.  Overall the class is easy; just go to lecture.  Make sure to study well for the exams tho, because they are a little harder than you might think.
He seems like a very nice man.  Lectures are about as boring as any given lecture at UW, but they are clear.  The exam questions are trickier than you will expect, but I didn't mind this course.

I had him for summer school, 1 month of class, every day for 2 hours.  Lectures were very dry and it was hard to stay awake, but Jim is a really nice guy, and you can tell he cares a lot about students.  Overall the class and discussions were interesting and interactive.  I don't know how the class operates during the regular semester, though.
Hard exams, but fair overall. Obviously puts a lot of effort into the class. Lectures were pretty interesting.

This class is very easy in concept, the material is pretty easy to understand.  However, the exam questions are very ambiguous.  Choose the 'best' answer, though sometimes there can be multiple possible answers.  Also, the wording can be very tricky, and sometimes confusing.  The exams turn this relatively easy class into crap.

Wildlife Ecology 318  This professor is not only extremely boring but he also has some major misconceptions on how the animal world works!  The class is extremely easy but I definitely feel dumber for having attended it.  His test questions often remind me of a high school teachers'(poorly worded and ambiguous). Overall worst class I have had at UW
As long as you did your work (which was very manageable), you were able to get a very high A. I loved his class, it was fun and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SOOOO MUCH HOMEWORK

This class is marketed as a literature class, but it can be argued that it is more a creative writing class. The main focus of this course is to write in a journal (almost everyday), along with in class discussions about the readings, among other things. You do not have to do everything to get an A and Sean is an amazing professor. 100% recommend!

I took "The Writer's Notebook" section of ENGL 169 with Sean. It was a creative writing class focused on journaling and it was amazing. You did not have to do every aspect of the class to get an A. Sean was an engaging teacher who didn't care about the quality of your writing, but focused on making you a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sean was a great professor for our class on Literary Publishing. He cared so much about helping us succeed in this field. He really wants us to do well. The content was super engaging and interesting. He always made us laugh, too. I appreciate how realistic he was, but how much he believed in us, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Bement is a really nice guy and wants his students to succeed. He has additional office hours before exams which is really helpful. He has everything you need to know on his lecture slides. If you understand the highlighted writing on the slides and do the practice exam, then you're good for the exam.
He was my favorite professor out of the three. His slides are very word heavy, but pay attention to the notes written in blue.

The slides were so bad to look at. There was so much information on them. The nice part was that the key concepts were in blue, but it was very hard to follow along, especially if you missed just one lecture.

Dr. Bement is a sweet guy though his teaching felt sub par. You can pass by reading the words in blue font on the slides without going to class, which may help some students, but I prefer lectures that reshape ideas clearly in a digestible way. An A is doable but takes more work than the other units because he doesn't really elaborate in lectures.
I actually really liked his slides because everything you needed to know was in blue print, and his test was honestly really easy; some of the questions were the exact same as the review.
Terrible lecturer, slides used in classes are way too over crowded and he just reads everything on the slide instead of explaining how things actually worked.

So funny and maybe an unpopular opinion but I loved his lecturing style. Yes he read off the slides but it meant that as long as you study off of them you are guaranteed to ace his test. Respected, genuinely interesting and overall a great prof. If you are ever going to skip this class, his lectures are definitely easiest to miss.

Prof. Bement is very nice and funny but he reads word for word off the posted slides, making his section of the class very skippable. He goes through the slides pretty quickly but his test is much easier than the other tests.

Bill Bement seems like the sweetest guy ever, a boring lecturer but he is so sweet. He loves to show funny animal videos and dresses like the early 2000s. His slides for lectures are easy and everything important is written in blue which is helpful. He prefers to just read off the slides word for word. His test is easier than the others.
His lectures were straight to the point and his exams were arguably the easiest of all 3 professors (This class is taught by 3 professors)

Dr. Bement is very knowledgeable but doesnt necessarily know how to communicate his knowledge. Lectures are all on the slides, not room for note taking or for elaboration off the slides. Nice guy, hard exam.

Man does not know how to present. basically reads off the slides. Most boring out of the 3 profs for bio/zoo101. he also puts way too much information on the slides. I did not enjoy any of the time he spent lecturing.

He's a great guy but I don't like his teaching style. He's entertaining during lecture, you can tell he loves teaching! BUT I didn't learn a THING... his slides are too word heavy, he goes way to fast so I don't even comprehend what he's saying or get to write down everything down. Slides are given but that's not a good method for ACTUALLY learning
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor bement is kind of boring. He reads off the slides which makes it really hard to understand the material. You dont have to go to class during his part of bio 101 because youll just end up teaching yourself. Funny guy tho.

Bement tries to be funny. His lecture slides felt less organized and were much harder to take notes on plus he moves through them very fast. His slides also have bad graphics and feel like they're from the early 2000's. Overall he seems like a nice guy, but not really my style of lecturer. Don't buy the textbook, never opened it and got an A

Bill is a funny guy but he goes through slides pretty fast. By no means is he a bad professor, just not really my style. He was probably my least favorite out of the 3 professors for the class, but also the most entertaining. I never interacted with him but he seems nice. If you go to lectures and do the quizzes, you'll probably be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's very funny, but he goes through lecture slides way too fast. You can't get anything down and he didn't post the lecture slides online. Luckily his exam was mostly common sense. He isn't as bad as people say, but he does go through lectures very very fast.

Professor Bement was fantastic and probably my favorite of the 3 lecturers. He was very nice & approachable and made his lectures interesting. I really appreciated that he did not just copy material from the book into his slides, but rather covered interesting topics that the book didn't hit. Would certainly recommend.
He is very nice and makes the model organisms, like the amoeba, very interesting, which adds more fun to the lectures.
He was very funny and probably the easiest professor of the three because his exam and information was very basic and not as in depth. Very funny guy
Bill is wack but in a good way. love that man.
Bill was the lecturer for the third portion of Biology 101, and at times he talked really fast and was unclear in what he wanted us to know for the exam. He got better as the portion progressed.

Dr. Bement is a helluva guy. He's charismatic and pretty funny, and lectures are very engaging. He's extremely helpful outside of class and good and answering questions. Only downsides are since Bio 101 is often packed, it can be hard to hear him in the back of the hall, and he moves pretty quickly during lecture so you have to pay good attention.

Agree with next poster. No notes posted online, and he writes faster than any professor I've EVER seen. So hard to keep up taking notes, and exams are also very very difficult. He's a great guy, but a horrible professor.

I don't understand how everyone likes him. This is by far the worst class I have taken as a biology major. He writes on the board very quickly with his back to the class most of the time. I went to every class, wrote down everything he said, and memorized my notes and never did better than a 75 on an exam. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Bement is a stud! His teaching style at first is awkward but after he is done with his portion of the class, you will forever hate powerpoints for the rest of your life. You have to go to lecture because nothing in online, but every class should be taught this way. Not an easy class, but tests are basically note recall with a couple application ?'s

Amazing professor - the best I've had. Every lecture is entertaining, informational, and interesting. It's professors like him that make UW such an elite institution. His policy to only hold the students accountable for what he writes on the board is very fair and quite entertaining due to all the running around he does.
Awesome professor! Always entertaining, just know everything and you'll be fine!

Do not take this class unless you are *seriously* motivated to learn cell bio. Bement is nice, and a funny guy, but his teaching style is awful. You'd learn more reading a textbook to yourself in a funny voice. I gained maybe two weeks' worth of actual knowledge from this class, the rest was useless details, forgotten the instant the test ended.

Bill Bement is one of the craziest and most intellegent men I know.  I worked for him in his lab for 8 months, and took 570 with him.  His teaching style is eccentric, but he's also very easy to listen to in lecture when you get to know his style.  His tests are ridiculous, yet entertaining, and every day in class was totally unexpected.  Loved it.

Entertaining and great lecturer.  Must attend every lecture and memorize all the details to do well on the exams.  He writes everything on the board really fast so be prepared to keep up.  Though the curve is a pain since you're competing with grad students, the material in the class is interesting and applicable to other science classes.

Awesome professor with a fantastic interest in the material. Incorporates 'real world' scenarios in the form of literary reviews relating to pertinent concepts in order to demonstrate strengths and weaknesses within the field. He's helpful outside of class, and has a genuine interest in his students. Tests are fair are based solely on lectures.

My main concern with Professor Bement was that he writes on the chalkboard extremely quickly, so it's very difficult to keep up with him and concentrate on what he's actually saying unless you write quickly in cursive.  I like to write in print and make it very neat, but I had to give up on that.  Bring your laptop to take notes, imo.

Highly recommended professor.  Attend lectures and take good notes.  Extremely helpful outside of class...actually listens to your whole question before he says anything in addition he is pretty funny

Excellent professor, excellent guy.  Highly recommended.  Do NOT buy the book.  Attend ALL lectures.  Take good notes.  Re-Copy all notes, ask questions where necessary, then get to memorizing.  He made Cell Bio very interesting, and always provided you with what you needed to succeed.  Low-tech (chalk + board) - too many get lazy w/PowerPoints imo
I took CB 570 8 years ago and still think of it as one of the best educational experiences I've had.  Bill's a great prof, a great (unofficial) advisor, and a great guy.

Bill was the best prof I've ever had! He really made cell bio so much fun for me. Inspired me to learn more about this area he was so passionate about. Yeah...I guess I had a little crush, but it only made me work harder! He's an awesome teacher and I'd take his class again just because it's him teaching it.

I LOVED this class and professor!  He is hilarious and that carries into his exams.  The exams are not hard if you memorize your notes, and the book is not needed at all as long as you go to every lecture.  I would definitely recommend taking this class with Bill!

Bill was a great professor!  He writes very fast and everything you need to know for exams is covered in lecture.  DO NOT BUY THE BOOK!  I got an A and I never even opened it.  His notes are very detailed, so don't miss lecture and you'll be fine.
Very interesting lectures, but the exams are very difficult.
Best professor I've had thus far!
By far the funniest professor on campus. He is a very good teacher, not the easiest exams, but an awesome curve! Definately worth taking cell bio from him
very funny guy. I highly recommend takin cell bio from him.
Very good professor, willing to give help when needed. Difficult tests, but a good curve.
Great guy, very funny. Exams are difficult and very detail orientated.
Funny as Hell
Bement is hilarious... no one else can pull off a Meatloaf concert t shirt
Excellent teacher
write all notes on the board

Dr. Schrage is very knowledgeable in exercise phys, but his lectures were difficult to follow along. I often found myself having to teach myself a lot of the material, and looking back at lecture slides to study was very difficult and confusing. Nonetheless, exams are straight forward and cover the big picture without any small details to memorize.

Dr. Schrage is very knowledgeable and cares about his students, however his lectures were often hard to follow because he moves very quickly. It's also tricky to study for tests from his slides so I often had to use outside resources. The exams are fair but must be able to conceptualize the material and understand it fully.

Dr. Schrage is a good guy. He really forces you to think about the material critically, so if you don't spend a lot of time with the material or aren't very interested this class could be VERY difficult. Even as someone who studied a LOT his tests are super confusing and he's a little unforgiving with points back. Overall great guy though.

Agree with the previous reviewer - lectures are not clear and he moves extremely fast. His exams are more straight-forward than Diffee's but are still almost impossible to manage in 50 minutes given. I love the material, but did not get the grade I wanted in this class because of lecture exams.

Really nice guy, but lectures all over the place. He provides a lecture outline but jumps arounds without really telling you. Class is fairly difficult, only about 10% get an A. But overall a really, really fun class.

Dr. Pattnaik is a great person, but his class was frustrating and left most of the class confused. There was little organization of learning and material was hard to follow. The most perplexing part of the class was exams. Taking exams felt like solving puzzles and a lack of graded materials made doing well on exams pertinent to doing well overall.

Very poor teaching methods and grading in class. The professor offered no resources to learn, and all grading was based off of his very muddled lectures. Additionally, he writes very ambiguous and unclear exams that can be difficult to understand what any given question is asking for. Would not recommend as you have no control over your own grade.
Bikash is a really good person, his class is interesting and fun. Not a lot of effort is required for a good grade.

If you're reading this, you're probably in Professor Pattnaik's FIG. He is very passionate about what he teaches. He's a super sweet guy, though at times grading criteria was unclear (I would venture to say this is because he cares more about learning vs grading). Ask or email him your questions and he's happy to answer. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors. Very understanding, kind, and puts students first. Pay attention to lectures because mid terms and exams are based off of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best intro class I ended up having at UW
Guys, she is absolutely incredible. Please don't think about the reviews. This is one professor you WANT to have at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this professor. She definitely relies on your participation, but the course material is super interesting and easy to understand and create your own opinions on. She is caring, flexible and a great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was the best!

This professor is not what her reviews say!!! She is absolutely amazing, and it is a privilege to take with her!!! Her knowledge about the subject is actually astounding. While yes, the class is discussion and challenging, it will teach you to be more confident in your ideas. Her classes are enriching.
She taught me to think critically about literature and challenge opposing views. She's very knowledgeable and always pushes her students to learn. She is overall an amazing teacher y muy amable!! :))
She is very caring and is always willing to help with any questions. She is very passionate about her job!

I really like this class; Ksenija is a very smart professor and really cares about your success in the class. She wants everyone to succeed and learn. Don't hesitate to ask questions, she's helpful and good at communicating.  She brought us candy and was willing to adjust class for students travelling for break. Overall, she is a lenient grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ksenija is an awesome professor! She cares about her students and is accessible outside of class. During her lectures, participation is super important so make sure you're contributing at least once or twice a class. Her grading is relatively lenient as well. Do not be put off by the other scathing reviews. Her class is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking a class with her unless you are interested in literature, or are planning on being an active participant in class. She will correct you and tell you that you're wrong in front of everyone. However, she was a really easy grader on written assignments and projects. Exams were online and MC. Bad vibes, but an okay plan C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance counts a ton for her. I missed a few classes and she gave me a 0 on attendance halfway through the semester so I just stopped going. I still did fine on exams and papers. She will interrupt you mid sentence to correct you or argue with you (in front of the entire class). She assigns a ton of readings, which are long and complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She assigns a ton of readings, and then judges students for not knowing everything. You have to agree with her on your analysis or she will argue with you infront of the entire class. She will correct grammar and judge students for pronouncing things wrong. She doesn't use powerpoint so she just talks at you. Worst Spanish professor i've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Based on the reviews I read on here, I was terrified to take this class, and I won't lie, she can be pretty brutal. In class, she is quite scary, but she's very kind in communication. She genuinely wants to help you learn, so as long as you show her you're committed to her class, you should do fine, and she's a fairly lenient grader, which helps.

Honestly not the worst prof I've had. She's actually pretty sweet and mostly just wants students to participate. If you do the readings and talk at least once every class you'll do fine. Her class was fairly easy you just have to be prepared because she can ask tough questions and be intimidating at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While I think she has good intentions, she is not a great professor. Spanish should be a subject where you can have opinions on literature but if you don't agree with her, she thinks you're wrong. She is very inconsiderate and rude, while also doesn't give clear guidelines on what she wants in assignments which makes the course hard.

Professor Bilbija is the worst professor I've ever had. She was extremely insensitive, assigned impossible amounts of readings (sometimes 2 Spanish novels in a week) and she consistently publicly shamed students for not knowing every detail of the readings/grammar. Her attitude towards students was so negative, it felt like intentional harassment.

Professor Bilbija has a very aggressive attitude towards students and generally speaks down to them. She assigns an impossible amount of pre-class reading which would be difficult to complete if we weren't all taking 3-4 other classes. She would also put students on the spot and criticizes them if we were not able to complete this work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was fine, it was Ksenijas attitude towards students that was disheartening. She was extremely rude when I reached out for help and began accusing me of cheating (which I hadn't) when I was simply asking for help. Shes intimidating, which made me very anxious and instead of helping me, she chastised me for being nervous to ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are multiple novels and documentaries that you are expected to read and know in detail EVERY week. She calls on students randomly to quiz them, interrupts student presentations to critique, and makes the class scary and uncomfortable. I have never had such an unapproachable professor and had lots of anxiety over this course.

knowledgeable, poor teacher, bad personality. My grandfather got a rare cancer, had 6 wks to live. I asked if I could visit him for 1 wk & miss class, but Id send all my assignments early. She said well if my father died, I just cant fly to Europe, and something about how I need to learn to deal with disappointment feeling entitled to leave

I took this class over the summer. It was ok. Tons of reading and lectures. She gives good, critical feedback. She seems very intimidating, but it wasn't really that bad. This class had only 75 total exam points, so if you bombed one exam, your chance at an A is out the window. Overall, the class was average.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ksenija won't hesitate to correct your grammar midsentence, which throws some people off but I found it very helpful. She expects you to participate and doesn't accept vague answers. As long as she can see you are genuinely trying in class you'll do fine. Great lady

I learned so much more than I thought I would in Ksenija's class. She is extremely smart and knows what she is talking about; however, with that, she is very opinionated and she makes it seem as if there's only one way to interpret literature. However, despite her verbal comments during presentations, she is a very generous grader.

Ksenija is THE BEST! I almost didn't take her class because of the reviews but I am SO glad that I did. She's definitely tough and will correct you when you're wrong (even if it's in front of the whole class) but she does it out of love. If you're a good student, she is so helpful if you need anything (other classes or professors or just advice).

The literature we read in 461 was super interesting and I learned A TON in this class, but Professor Bilbija is horrible and very condescending. If you are shy & don't like to participate much, don't take this class. She will humiliate you in front of everyone, & make you feel stupid & insecure about your Spanish. I was uncomfortable everyday :(

Ksenija was a very difficult professor to have as a first semester freshman. However, I do think she had good intentions. It's a lot of reading, the expectations are high, and she can be kind of harsh. But if you attend classes, give 100% effort in and outside of the classroom, and have the desire to learn Spanish, you will succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love Ksenija! I almost didn't take her course because of some of the comments on here, but am so glad that I did! She's incredibly knowledgeable, has a great sense of humor (yes, I speak sarcasm), and was more than willing to make accommodation for her students! If you do the readings and show an interest in the class, you will get an A no proble

She is very opinionated. She is also very particular about what she expects out of her students. If you are ever in need of help, I'm telling you, ASK! Don't be afraid of asking, because the fear of asking will build up, you'll become more and more confused, and then it just gets harder for you. Be respectful, be attentive, and participate.

Avoid if you can - unclear grading criteria and a ridiculous amount of assigned reading create many headaches. If you have the chutzpah to talk to her after doing poorly on an assignment, she'll probably let you re-do it. Participate in class and be confident in your answers/opinions to avoid being steamrolled. Watch out for her cynicism.

Spanish 460 (Literature and Human Rights) is the hardest class I have ever taken at UW, but also the most rewarding.  Ksenija is extremely smart, very funny, and very opinionated - but who isn't?
