You can make a real connection with her, which is awesome.  The class, though tough, was extremely interesting and I would take it again in a heart beat!

Very intimidating and her opinion is always right. If you can just accept she's always right she will tolerate you. Do readings and delegate time to study before tests and you should get an alright grade. An A is achievable but probably from native speakers due to complex readings she expects you to dissect as if spanish was your first language.

Very intimidating professor who tends to scare students from participating. Often gives unclear instructions or changes them often. Greatly improved my Spanish skills, however. Need to work hard in the class to get an A.

A very knowledgeable professor who inspires students to think critically and analytically about all subject matter. The one drawback of this professor is that her perspective/interpretation is the only correct perspective/interpretation. People who disagree with her will not do as well in the class.

She was a tough professor. If you didn't do the readings before class, she would be able to tell and would make it clear. Sometimes, her lectures seemed to be all over the place and tended to be one sided. But, she was very nice and helpful if you put the work in. She was very knowledgable, and overall I enjoyed the class.

never had a teacher that made me feel more uncomfortable.  I asked her a question once, and she told me that that was a first semester spanish question and maybe i shouldn't be in the class.  lit classes are supposed to have room for interpretation, but she won't allow anything she doesn't agree with.  very brash, and shouldn't be a teacher.

Incredible professor.  Yes she is tough and yes she makes you think, but isn't that why we're in college? To learn?  She was funny and discussions were very productive and helpful in learning the material.  The stories that we read were interesting which made it easier to get everything done on time.  Stickler for correctness which was helpful.
She is amazing. I learned so much from this woman.

incredibly interesting class.  read lots of shorts stories that make you think. her discussions in class are helpful; i learned a lot. very cool but doesn't let you get away with crap. she expects you to read & do the work required for this level class....what else would you expect.  very refreshing professor. i really enjoyed her class.

incredibly insightful & smart professor. i liked the class & learned a lot. if you do the work (3exams, 1paper, 1presentation) and talk some you'll be fine.  she's got her own style, will try to get you talk, which makes some uncomfortable since she doesn't coddle. very refreshing teacher, just asks what's expected of you. i learned tons!!

Lit class w/ 3 exams, 1 paper, & a presentation. Offers a lot; really made us think. I learned a lot. She's not harsh, she just likes you to talk and explain yourself and will correct mistakes.  I really liked her.  She was real and doesn't coddle, very refreshing & nice professor. If you do the work and talk you'll be fine.

She expected us to read an insane amount of books, which I don't think anybody in the class actually finished. There's 2 exams, a paper, and a presentation, so your grade doesn't ride on very much. She does pick on people and I didn't think her teaching style was very clear

How this lady is still teaching is beyond me. She needs to stick to her LACIS job, because she definitely doesn't belong in a classroom. Intimidating doesn't begin to describe her.  She's vicious. I wouldn't mind telling her something but the work load is too much and I can't keep up. This is the 1st eval in my 4 yrs here at UW Im excited to write.

The teacher is intimidating during class discussions, and she sometimes chews people out; seemingly unapproachable although she is intelligent. The subject matter was not interesting to me whatsoever in her special topics class and she is a tough grader; she likes things to be extremely exact. You have to buy about a million books too which sucks.

do yourself a favor and do not EVER take a class with ksenija. she is mean and evil and often made students cry in front of class. my roommate took spanish 224 with a different prof and had a very easy, painless semester. ksenija makes this class way too difficult for an INTRO to literature class most students take as a requirement.

Spanish and literature are my two favorite subjects, but I began to despise them both in 224. She's only open to one interpretation of literature: her own. Often ridiculed students who offered diff ideas in front of class making an uncomfortable environment for participation. Very frustrating class for anyone who loves lit.

if you don't know an answer to something, she'll tear you apart in front of the class. awful. doesn't believe that things can be interpreted differently by different people. believes her answer is always the right one. if you dont like participating, don't  enroll in one of her classes.

amazing, intelligent professor. you have to work, but she really makes you think outside the box. if you don't like participating, don't take a class with ksenija... but if you don't mind sharing your thoughts and discussing the readings, you'll be fine. you only get graded on 3 exams and a paper... and she's a fair grader. great professor.
She is harsh and brutal.
She is tough, but if you go to class and do the readings, she will give you some breaks.  Participation, three exams, a paper, and a presentation make up the grade.
She is difficult and she makes you think. Make sure you do the readings before class or you might get chewed out in front of everyone. You do learn some valuable stuff in the class though.

This was one of the most disorganized classes I've taken. Expectations and grading were unclear, and communication felt minimal throughout the semester. I often felt unsupported in understanding the material. I would recommend other instructors if you prefer clearer structure and guidance.

Very hard to follow lectures that don't exactly correlate with exam materials. Lots of talk about topics he finds interesting rather than course relevant. Easy grader but having him actually grade anything is rare, as on the day of the final the midterm grade wasn't even visible in Canvas. Course is decently interesting but hard to take from Eraker

Professor Eraker taught an interesting class; however, the lectures were difficult to follow and take notes on due to tangents and frequent back and forth between slides in class. It's incredibly important to pay attention to detail in the slides, and reference them frequently for studying and assignments.

He is very smart but lectures can be all over the place. I have no interest in the subject so they were boring to me, and I taught myself everything right before tests, but that's not really his fault. Midterm was difficult but he provided lots of practice materials and graded generously. This class could've been torture but he made it manageable.

Bjorn is polarizing. Yes he may be disorganized, unprepared at times. He doesn't update grades on Canvas. However, he is the most passionate prof in finance. He LOVES his subject and that is infectious. Take his course if you actually care to learn about derivatives, not to ace exams. However, his exams are always very easy if you pay attention.

Bjorn is the best professor I have had at UW-Madison. You can tell that he truly cares about all of his students and that he is deeply passionate about the course material. He is very approachable and makes students feel understood as well.

Professor Eraker does not do a very good job at giving lectures since he likes to read off slides and then proceeds to deviate from what he was lecturing to a completely different topic than what he was discussing. Lectures are boring, material is dry, and overall a poorly structured course. Take it with a different professor if you can.
Really good professor. The material is very interesting, and the exams are not very hard.

Intelligent and passionate in derivative and asset pricing. If you are truly interested in derivative and its practice in market, I would recommend you to take this class. Be sure to ask questions in details and go to office hours when you come up with confusions and problems. You will be getting deeper than just going for lectures.

Always recommended to take FIN 330 with Bjorn if you truely want to learn something about trading and derivatives. You will get a paper trading account for practicing the concept in class. The exam is not hard as long as you go to the lecture and think aloud.

Bjorn is super passionate and knowledgeable about derivatives so you get as much out of this class as you put into it. If you are genuinely interested in finance, it is definitely worthwhile to take 330 with Bjorn. You also get a paper trading account with Interactive Brokers to practice lecture concepts with real-time market data which is cool.

Bjorn is the man. He loves derivates (somehow) and really cares about his work. He is a bit unorganized, but he's always willing to help and wants his students to do well. If you take all of the practice exams he gives out, you will pass with flying colors.
He was very unorganized and wasteful of time. It did not feel rewarding to go to lecture and many of the homework assignments felt tacked on and irrelevant.

Bjorn is the most unorganized professor/lecturer I have ever had. He doesnt know how to give a fluent lecture, all his material is old and dry. This is the reason why no one came to class. He then got upset that no one came to class and everyone still did well on his midterm so proceeded to change the syllabus to include participation as a grade

Without a doubt, the best professor I've ever had. Bjorn eradicates the stigma that "large university professors aren't helpful." He truly cares about whether or not you understand the material, not just what grade you get on an exam. You can always ask questions without any judgment. Outstanding, entertaining, and thoughtful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bjorn is a good guy who is very interested in Derivatives. He teaches the class in a very modern way using live markets and data in his lectures. However, he is extremely unorganized and would add homework assignments and quizzes at the last minute that barely related to lectures or exams. Good guy, poorly run class.

Bjorn is an awesome professor. Hes clearly very intelligent and teaches many current, relevant things rather than purely theory, so the class seems much more applicable than many do. Go to class, he doesnt follow a book. Hes also hilarious and class is entertaining. I recommend him for Finance 330 or any class he would teach!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: Bjorn is by far the best professor I have ever had. The class is at times difficult but it is certainly do-able with a genuine effort to understand the material he provides. Lecture notes are high level but problem sets and other assignments help to clarify. He is not only very evidently intelligent, but also consistently entertaining and helpful.

Bjorn is hilarious and enthusiastic about his work. Very intelligent guy and can relate to students well. 330 is the hardest class in the UW Finance curriculum, so no way around taking this class. Bjorn is a great option. Trading assignments are real world, so it's not just theory and models. Can come across as intimidating but definitely isn't.

I thought he was a pretty chill guy, and the lectures were fine- he was just kind of held back by the early time slot. It's hard to pay attention already if you don't care about stats, so trying to do this tired is a bit challenging. His study guides are helpful. Don't be intimidated by the coding part, it's just basics (I've never coded before).

Maybe I just hate math, but I despised this class. Lectures were tedious and boring, you had to learn how to use R outside of class to use on the homework and then you don't get to use it on the exams, the homework is long and the exams are hard.
I wish I could give a lower rating, lectures all of class with slides. Does not engage the students AT ALL, nor does he try to connect with them. Very strict and lacks understanding for students.
Dr. Bloss was very approachable and kind, past exams were available and much more helpful than practice problems.

His rating shocks me.  I assume these people hate stats and never talked to him, because despite an 8am power 2x a week, I found myself enjoying Dr. Bloss' class and coming nearly all the time (I even surprised myself with that).  He obviously cares deeply about his students, and while he can be a bit eccentric, I personally grew to enjoy him.
His lectures aren't that entertaining or informative, the final was unnecessarily lengthy and there were no relevant practise materials provided
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had, he yells when students go to class late and locks the door at 8am sharp. Gives random pop quizzes and struggles to explain concepts properly and thinks everyone can follow along. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awesome guy, you'd like him

He is a nice guy, and he seems to be passionate about the topics he teaches during lecture. Maybe the class difficulty makes a big impact since I only took him for a leftover intro stats class I needed for DARS. But for how he lays out the course work the grading distribution is extremely generous and makes it almost impossible to fail.

Nowhere near as bad as his rating makes him seem, super sweet guy who genuinely cares about the material and his students. Lectures can be boring at times (especially at 8am), but not terrible. A lot of homework, but manageable. Lots of resources/very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't know why Professor Bloss has such a bad rating on here. I thought his lectures were pretty good and that he explained concepts well. His lectures can be a bit boring if you are already familiar with the material, but for the most part, he seems like a very sweet guy who holds a lot of respect for his students.

Pop quizzes were common. 8am class, he would be very upset at people who were late and started locking the door at 8:00. Lectures were good enough.


I got the impression over the whole semester that he isn't very understanding of his students. I didn't particularly enjoy his class or my interactions with him.
Terrible in lecture and did not cover homework content. Final exam was extremely hard.

I wanted to like this professor, but I can't recommend him. Despite 10+ years of teaching, his course lacked consistency, with uneven content across sections. Exams were poorly balanced—an easy second test inflated grades, followed by a harsh final that felt more like an English exam. These issues shouldn't happen at this level.

I had this 8:00am MW and the second lecture he started yelling at the people walking in 1-5mins late. Scary!! He locked the door at 8 after that. Anyway, I thought his lectures were good and he had nicely typed up notes most of the year. Once I only turned in 1 page of a 10 page hw and despite having timestamped photos he didn't take it :(
don't take this if u don't have to. worst class i have ever been in.

Changing textbooks halfway through the course was kind of annoying but lectures were pretty decent and fair to learn from, he seems like a pretty nice guy but sometimes did weird things like lock the lecture room door at start time for class. Better than a lot of other stats professors though so take him if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr Bloss changed his lecture material halfway through the semester. He went from using nicely typed up notes in PDFs to just posting huge bunches of slides from the textbook which were annoying. Lots of homework each week and gave only two attempts on webassign before you got 0 points. Boring lectures. 1 extra credit opportunity. Hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bloss seems like a nice guy. Didn't love having to code but it wasn't TOO hard to learn. The final was pretty rough even with three note pages. 25% for each exam (2 midterms, 1 final). Inconsistent teaching style. Skipped disscussion after the 1st. I just don't love the subject so the lectures were pretty boring. LOTS of homework some weeks
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were slow moving so sometimes hard to pay attention but he's very passionate about teaching. First and second test was easy but the final was a lot harder. Homework was challenging at times and lots of points would be taken off for small things like rounding. Overall good class but challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was experimenting a lot with his lecture style and format considering it was his first year, so he was a little meandering and unclear in lecture. Very accessible outside of class as well. Exams were challenging (doesn't give practice exams) but if you pay attention in the lectures and take the time to find additional practice, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bloss was a very sweet and genuine guy, but sometimes I felt like the lectures were very disorganized. The lecture material was no where near the difficulty as the homework was. Some of the exams were very difficult given that we didn't have much material to utilize while studying.

The homework & quizzes are hard, they make up most of your grade, and Dr. Bloss's policy of -10% per hour late probably cost me at least a letter grade. But his lectures are peak and he understands better than any other stat or math professor I've had how to use & teach R coding and how to make stats practical for life science students.

I thought he was a great professor. I felt he really explained things well in lecture and the exams were pretty easy if you understood the lectures and the homework. He is a bit quirky and will get annoyed easily but other than that I thought he teaches much better than the average professor and actually wants to see all the students do well.
First exam was super hard. Seems like a nice guy though. Final isn't weighted more than midterms.

He was very inconsistent in his method of lecturing. At first, he started with slides and then at the end of the semester, he started just writing on random textbook pages that we did not have access to. His lectures were very unengaging and difficult to follow along with. We are not given any material to prepare for the exams.

There is very little material to study with and the lectures are really confusing, he switches between different media throughout the semester (like an ipad, slide shows, black boards, etc) and it is hard to follow. Not much help on Canvas either.
Bloss was great! the class is very test heavy but he is very accesable outside of class and understanding. Exams are very fair and he gives a full sheet of paper that can by typed for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Billy Jackson was a decent professor. He is getting a lot of hate on here from people who, in my opinion, didn't study and/or are just not that good at math. All of the exams were fair. If you did the review guide at all and kept up with the homework, the course shouldn't have been hard. Sorry if this was blunt, but it is the truth. Sorry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best thing that I can say about this professor is that the exams are quite like the exam review, but other than that, his teaching style and the way he taught this already difficult course is terrible. There is no curve in this class, the homework is tough with no answer key to review. The exams are difficult and made harder than needed.

If you have the chance to not take this professor, DONT. I had an ok TA and did well on homework and overall quizzes. I never met Billy Jackson and think the class has incredibly complicated and in depth content for first semester Algebra class. Much of the content I had friends in Calc 2/ tested out of math, be unable to assist with content. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jackson is fine.  Stuff on exams is basically stuff we do in lectures.  Go to class and you're fine as long as you remember the stuff from Calc 2 and calc 3 .  Class can be a bit dry at times but between the homework which 45% of the grad which he helps with when you ask him and the easy exams, the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have basically had to teach myself this entire course. The lectures make no sense, the homework has no answer keys so the grading is unfair and no feedback is given. Dont take this class, if you have to, find a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jackson embodies the Socratic method in his teaching. His exam reviews are helpful and indicative of the exam. His writing is illegible sometimes, but makes up for it with how much he talks in lecture. He has a passion for teaching and it shows in how he answers questions during lecture and office hours. I recommend Billy Jackson 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have done quite well in his 321 class.  He gives you lots of chances to practice in class.  Overall the reviews have prepared me for the exams pretty well --if you can do the problems in the reviews you can do his exams.  Takes things a bit slow at times but it helps to learn it.
graded unfairly, sets students up for failure.

This is the worst class I have taken at UWM. 
*unorganized
*unfair grading
*no feedback is given on homework's
*no answer keys
*no resources
*difficult to read handwriting
*unhelpful office hours
*unhelpful TA
*unresponsive on piazza and in emails
*unprofessional
Overall, I am very displeased with this professor and this class.

Billy is the overall Professor for my class, but the class is actually taught by a TA. I had two different TA's throughout the semester and both were not great. All of the resources and notes you get for the class are not helpful. The notes we do in class are almost all writing instead of practice problems. There are quizzes two days of the week.

Compared to what I've heard about the other instructors that teach Math 112, I don't think Billy Jackson was HORRIBLE. He obviously knows what he's talking about. There are quizzes twice a week which forces you to attend class. The third exam is a (very easy) group exam which boosted my grade. Overall, not an amazing instructor, but not the worst.
he does not explain his teaching. he does not care for students. be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
GRADING FOR TA MAYA BANKS!!!

She is the nicest person ever, connects to the students, and understands what the students are going through. She gets blindsided by Billy Jackson but does her best. She makes sure her students know what is going on. Such a fun TA
He does not care for the students or the TAs. The work compared to the exams is not connected. This was the worst class I have ever taken. I would not recommend.
He is bad

Combination of lectures and us getting to practice and discuss things on our own. I have been to class every day and there is always at least one if not two opportunities for us to practice on our own and I like this because it helps me do the homework.  Two quizzes each work which helps with exams and very fast so be careful not to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Billy Jackson claimed the first day of class he was going to do interactive learning. I was excited because I am not the best at math and need help a lot. Well, this happened rarely. The lectures are too fast paced and his handwriting is absolutely ineligible. The textbook does not help with understanding concepts. Worst math class I've ever taken.

Dr. Jackson does not care about his students whatsoever. If you are sick or have to miss class for any reason, it's basically good luck and you get a zero. He is only interested in doing what's easiest for himself and CLEARLY does not care about the success or wellbeing of any of his students. Overall, avoid this class at all costs.
Awful

Doesn't believe in standard lectures. Work in groups for most of the class, what you learn is often reliant on what your group collectively knows. At least two homework assignments on the online textbook a week. You have a quiz every class (group and individual). He's somewhat helpful, but he understands the content too well to use layman's terms.

Overall, Professor Jackson knows the concepts of the content well, and he teaches them adequately. However, the exams are a bit more difficult than I anticipated initially, but he provided study guides that covered most topics. Talk to your TAs, they helped a lot in the class!

This class was really hard for me. The way the lectures were set up was very odd and I wasnt able to learn very well with his teaching style. The homework was online and sometimes super long and had things on it that I didnt see during the class lesson and had to teach myself. The exams were more straight forward than the homework though.

I took Jackson for Math 240. Grade is approx 40% participation/easy weekly quizzes and 60% tough, proof based exams. Lectures emphasize practicing concepts which is nice. He makes reviews for each exam and very active on piazza. This is a tough class, especially with the math department, but Jackson makes if doable. Just study A LOT for the exams.

Jackson was my professor, but didn't actually teach. My TA Krenz - incapable of teaching. Billy was good and helpful for office hours. I had covid and he was not helpful, I missed a quiz and got a zero and was told there was nothing they could do about it. They also said they couldn't accommodate me at all while in quarantine. I don't recommend.

He worked as the director chair of the course but the actual class was run by incapable TAs. I recommend reading the textbook chapters before going to the lecture. Billy is actually helpful during office hours and cares more about understanding the concept. Although the real issue is the disorganization of the course

As others have said, his reviews are just like the exams IF you know the stuff in the reviews.  He does change the problems on the exam but the problems are the same ideas as in the reviews, so just giving back his solutions is not an option.  I found when I missed class I missed like weeks worth of material.  Get ready to do PROOFs in 240.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did not take Math 114 with him, but Math 240. His lectures can be hard to follow and the exams are a lot more difficult than the homework, some of the problems that are on the exams aren't even on the review. Whenever someone asks a question, his answers can be ambiguous and are not that good at clarifying concepts or any misunderstandings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best largest lecture courses I have had. Makes the class interesting and doesn't just talk the full 75 minutes but gives chances to practice (usually-- though there have been times class would drag on).  Grade is exams, quizzes, final, and homeworks (which come from textbook for 240 that sucks in a lot of ways).Definitely worth taking
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall I think he is a decent prof. I personally thought the class was really easy, he goes over problems on the board. The study guides are legit the exact same as the midterms/ final exam. you get weekly homework and sometimes there are legit like 70 problems for you to do, but it is easy to get 100 on them but takes awhile sometimes.

Dr. Jackson was great!  We spent a lot of class time reviewing how to actually work the problems and prepare for the homework.  I wish I could have him for 221 -- it would make things so much easier.  I passed his class easily but now 221 is tough because my professor can't explain things at all in ways that normal human beings can understand.

He clearly has no desire to teach. All he kept doing the entire semester was talk about his paper he is writing and talk to the guys in the class. We had to do it his way and it wasnt explained well. He gives handouts and doesnt teach. The tests are so much harder than the homework. The only way I passed was with tutoring and he offered no help.

Jackson is ok. You have to know your algebra because he focuses just on the trig. If you have been used to using calculators to do things like graphing, it can be a bit challenging to adjust to having to do it by hand without them. That said, he does help you learn how to do the problems without them but it takes a while to remember the algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I have always enjoyed math and been ok at it but this class made me hate everything. He focuses on the why of math instead of how to actually do the problem so it's hard to apply to tests, especially since there is nothing to practice. His practice tests are the same as the exam which helps, although the answer key tends to have many mistakes.

Hes fine. Its a math class so exams and homework will of course make up the grade. If you go to class and actually do the work the homework and exams are not an issue. I have always been scared of math but he makes math less scary. If you go through the reviews and go to his office you can get by pretty easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Billy Jackson moves through material very fast and isnt a very understanding professor. Your grades are based solely off homework and exams, there are no quizzes to practice the concepts before they are weighted more heavily. No matter how many reviews or office hours you go to, Dr. Jackson will not be understanding of your struggles in his class.

If you put in the work, youll do fine as long as you know your algebra already. He doesnt review a whole lot of algebra since its trig. So if you dont know your algebra, be ready to put in the time to review it for yourself. Unfortunately there were too many people in the groups who didnt know their algebra and it hurt the group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: barely a professor - lectures are youtube videos done by a different prof., & there is no encouragement to ask questions or to retain the information. instruction is not given to ta's as to what to include for lectures which results in a widely unprepared student body for tests and quizzes. also required in-person test during omicron spike.

probably the most insensitive person at this school. he does not care about the well-being of the students. he wasnt my direct professor but he was the department chair of the class i took. he required 600+ individuals to take an exam in person during the omicron spike.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: dont take this prof. worst prof ive ever had. dude cant teach. expects you to just know things. exams are worth 75% of grade. exams dont correlate to hw. randomly takes assignments down. very disorganized. never available for help. doesnt answer emails. has 1 star rating at every other institution.

I LOVED having Dr. Jackson this semester! Like the majority of people taking this class, I was putting off taking Calc 221 until next semester, but Dr. Jackson has definitely made me feel a lot more prepared for it. It's a math class, it's obviously going to be homework / exam heavy, but I think the other reviews are dead wrong. Billy is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: this class was actually horrible. the lectures are online, so it is hard to get clarity on the lecture content. there is not a variety of practice problems given. the tests and quizzes are almost nothing like the lecture content. very easy to get lost, but if you can teach yourself or took algebra in high school you might be okay.

this class sucks. you have to watch the lecture and take notes on your own and the actual classes are a waste of time. the tests are really hard and don't compare to the in class discussion at all. not accommodating either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You take notes by yourself before discussion, in discussion you're given easy worksheets to complete with a group. However, homework is a lot more challenging. Reviews and tests are way harder and do not compare to discussion worksheets. Dr. J is not accommodating of alternate exams. To top everything off all 3 of my exams were mis-graded.

Exams were pretty much like reviews which are mostly like the homework (except the ones you have to explain). Two homeworks were longer, but he did tell about those ahead of time. If you're not about being in a math class at 4pm in the afternoon, then you shouldnt take him because missing a class feels like youve missed TWO WEEKS. Overall decent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: First day of class we were told we'd do interactive learning. At first I was open to the idea, but now I wish he would just lecture us. Barely any outside materials you can use to make up for the waste of time class is. You can't even read what he's writing. The homework was RIDICULOUSLY long. No, I don't want to solve a triangle 63 times.

I learned a lot but I personally didnt like the group work. I got stuck with a group who all had calculus in high school but they couldnt do the stuff we were supposed to be doing like the graphs. I learned way more just doing the problems on my own than I ever did from the group. Asking the TAs questions during class helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Jackson claimed on the first day that this class was not going to be lecture heavy. He proved this to be a complete lie. His lectures are hard to follow as you cannot read what he is writing. He also assigns 70 problem hws where if you get the answer wrong by a tiny decimal, you have to redo the problem a million times (doesnt help me learn)

Dr. J is an easy A. Sometimes he lectures, sometimes worksheets. It helps me because I dont like listening to lecture in a math class for 75 minutes. My high school geometry teacher sucked, so this class has helped a lot because he always explains things really well. BUT it can be annoying at times trying to help other people in your group.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Jackson has made this course a lot more difficult than it needs to be. Class lectures are really confusing because he is very adamant about interactive learning yet continues to write sloppy work on the screens for us to copy down. It is hard to understand when he tries to explain the concepts while he is teaching. Thumbs down.

I'm torn. Professor Jackson means well, and he has complimented my achievements throughout the semester, but this course is unnecessarily difficult. I have a hard time with professors who require you to teach yourself the concepts. Let me put it simple, I shouldn't be paying top dollar at a renown university to end up teaching myself. Sorry Billy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Jackson is ok. The class had a very high average on the first exam, and then people started skipping when they found out that his reviews are just like his exams. Like every math class, if you skip you won't pass. Unfortunately, too many people found this out the hard way on the 2nd exam and bombed it. For me, I passed it with a solid C.

billy is a great example of a prof who knows a lot but just cant teach. his lectures are so confusing that everyone stopped showing up and just watched the online videos. the hw does not correlate to the exams and he makes you explain the math and not just know how to do it. he is very disorganized and goes back and forth between material.

Dr. Jackson is definitely not the best professor I've ever had... I took Trig with him and he makes a 113 class way too complicated. Makes you proof/explain everything and does not let you use a calculator. Gives us "interactive" sheets to do throughout class but we don't finish them. Everyone bombed the first exam because the hw dont reflect exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I like the guy, but lectures are quite weird. He sort of gives us a worksheet and tells us to do it. He sometimes lectures for almost the entire period and doesnt give us time for the worksheet that we are supposed to do there. No calculators. A lot of the hw is not what you need to know for exam. You also need to EXPLAIN the math & not just do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Blackwell started this fermentation class pretty recently. I think we are the second batch of students. The class was a lot fun, and he is a very dedicated instructor. Passionate about what he is teaching and cares about his student. You can learn a lot from him if you put in the work.
Awesome instructor for 255. Takes into consideration many do not have coding background coming into this class. Office hours were very helpful.
Super chill and knowledgeable on coding in general. Going into the class I knew absolutely nothing about coding but he does an excellent job orienting you too it. Very funny delivery of jokes as well

I took Blackwell's material class last year of undergrad and I am now in graduate school. His material class taught me a lot and the knowledges I learned served me well in the graduate level material class I took this semester. Classes were always well organized, and he had a good overall lecture plan as well. Homework and exams were also fair

Blackwell is a chill instructor. There were quizzes on every Monday, but they are nothing to stress over if you watch the video. Office hours were helpful, as he always gets to the point instead of rambling about irrelevant stuff. He has a great understanding of the level of knowledge appropriate for an undergraduate class, which is appreciated.
Solid instructor for 440. Would recommend to any CBE student looking for an some easy materials elective credit.

Prof Blackwell is a remarkably good teacher, I'd highly recommend him for 255 and will try to take him if possible for future CBE classes. Coding projects are actually quite fun and help you learn immensely. Quizzes are harder than he thinks, sometimes they are really easy and other times it's a massive time crunch.

I'm glad I took the others' advice and waited until Blackwell was teaching to take 255. This is my first programming class, so naturally I'm a bit intimidated. BCB does a really good job not assuming not every student has programming background. It's a tough class but he does a good job making it manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework are time consuming but doable. Quizzes were intimidating at first but became easier as the semester progressed. Solid instructor for 255 overall.

324 is a notoriously card class here in the CBE apartment. Your TA will matter a lot more than the instructor. However, it is clear that BCB did all he could to make this class go as smoothly as possible. Very accessible outside of normal lab hours and fun to work with.

I really enjoyed materials with BCB. Lectures were fun and informative. Homework related closely to concepts discussed in lectures, and exams were nothing to stress over compare to other CBE classes. Overall a good instructor doing a comparable job to Dr. Van Lehn, who is another popular choice for this class.

Very humorous and knowledgeable instructor. Lectures were always efficient and well organized. The projects were tough, but he was always willing to provide specific feedbacks. Homework and exams were fair.

Dr. Blackwell is hands-down the best instructors I've had as a ChemE at UW. CBE 324 is notoriously difficult, but his teaching style makes it not only manageable, but genuinely enjoyable. He explains concepts clearly, builds intuition before diving into derivations, and brings a ton of structure and energy to every lecture.

Materials class with Dr. Blackwell was the most fun class I took in all of my CBE curriculum. You can definitely tell he is passionate about materials and it shows in his lectures. One of the best thing about him is that he makes it very clear what he wants, which makes studying much more easy.

Fermentation with Dr. Blackwell was the highlight of my undergraduate engineering career. He single-handedly started this class and did all the paperwork so we can brew beer in lab. He even took us on a field trip to an actual beer factory! Amazing professor! Truly a must have if you get the chance.

324 overall is a time consuming class and the course layout is set by the department, so I'm not gonna comment on those issues. Additionally, the class is way more TA dependent than professor dependent. Blackwell did not have a particularly large role in the class, but he was fair, helpful, and to the point whenever I did interact with him.

I have had this professor for both 255 and 324 now. As a 324 professor, I wouldn't have wanted anyone else. He was fair, kind, and incredibly helpful. As a 255 professor, he can be a bit harsh, especially do those who lack coding skills. However, he is always willing to help and is very enthusiastic about what he teaches in both classes.

Professor Blackwell is one of the most approachable instructors in the department. In other words, he does not play god with his students. He has been a fantastic resource for 324 lab reports this semester. I would not have survived the course without him.
Blackwell is one of the best instructors at the chemE department in UW-Madison. If you get a chance to take any classes with him, do it. You will not regret it.

Professor Blackwell is professional, enthusiastic, and seemed genuinely interested in the subject matter he teaches. Unlike some aloof tenure-tracked professor who would rather be on at a academic conference than in the classroom, he focuses his entire entire energy on disseminating his endless wisdom on transport phenomena and life in general.
Overall, great choice for 324. Speaks very fast, but is always willing to answer questions/give feedback on lab reports. BCB is a great resource if you use him.

Professor Blackwell is one of the best professor you can possibly get for CBE255. He is funny, responsive, caring, and offers good advice both on course content knowledge and academic life in general. Go to his office hours and you will be just fine for CBE255.

Professor Blackwell has very good pre-recorded lectures so you can learn the material asynchronously. He is also very accessible out side of the classroom. The key to success in this class is his office hours, where he will go through a problem with you in extreme detail and help you debug your code. He also replies to email very frequent.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Best professor for CBE 324. Very caring and helpful. You can easily get an A if you spent even minimal amount of effort.

Fair, logical, and kind professor. Speaks a bit fast. This class is pretty self taught. Lectures are mostly example problems. HW can be hard, bring it up in OH or discussion. The 2 projects were a pain, (believe them when they say to start early). Weekly quiz with ten minute timer is stressful. Final exam was very fair.

Dr. Blackwell is incredibly knowledgeable and fun to work with and have as a professor. However, he has a tendency to expect students to do calculus when they haven't learned algebra. Many quizzes and assignments require students to go above and beyond what they are capable of, and the structure of his course makes many dread it.
I found BB to come off as caring to the general class but once you want to speak with him about an idea or a grade he can be dismissive and rather rude. Definitely a class I would like to get back.
BJB is one of the best profs at UW - so genuinely cares about students' learning.

The professor is a very nice and understanding guy. He's fun to talk to and listen to. Sometimes his lectures could be a tad dry, but He's also a fairly easy grader and gives useful and actionable feedback. The class ends in a large research paper (10-12 pages), so make sure not to do all that in one night to ease stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very good professor, it's a decently sized lecture with over 100 students, and he makes a point to get to know you personally by introducing himself multiple times throughout the semester before class officially begins. Incredibly nice man who's very approachable, would definitely take him again.
Professor Bloch is amazing! His classes are so organized and easy to follow. He has a very methodically way of helping his students grow. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Made lectures enjoyable, not too hard a grader, and had clear terms of what needs to be followed. Would take again.

I thought Professor Bloch was super passionate about this topic and the lectures were really enjoyable, although attendance was mandatory. Sometimes I felt like the grading was a little harsh, he doesn't seem to give out 100s at all.

Professor Bloch is genuinely caring and an incredible history professor! He organizes the contest of his History 201: Weimar Republic class by themes and topic rather than chronologically, which helps create organic connections. The course walks you through your final term paper. Also super funny. Would highly recommend!

History 120 with Prof. Bloch was a lovely time! The class will lean a little bit more into German history than other countries as that is his area of expertise, but other than that you can expect a variety of topics and countries covered, as well as important lessons on colonialism in Africa and Asia. It's a great class for freshmen.

Amazing professor, who cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches! The course is interesting and allows you to learn many interesting topics. In discussion sections you just need to complete the discussion post before class and participate. Mid term is allows you to bring a page of notes and well as the final, you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bloch is such an engaging prof and clearly cares about his students. He is very clearly passionate about what he teaches, but doesn't expect students to memorize all content. He's more focused on analyzing sources and contextualizing information. Pay attention, participate, do your readings and you'll be fine!

I truly loved taking this class. Bloch is a wonderful professor and honestly one of the most intelligent people I've ever met in my life. This class is super easy but that's only if you actually pay attention for...most of the lectures. There are two papers, a midterm and a final. None were super difficult and I really liked the TAs as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly passionate about his class, and very caring

Bloch's class has definitely been one of my best gen eds. The bulk of your grade are two essays plus a midterm and final. The essays aren't bad (neither longer than 5-6 pages) and you get a one-sided sheet of notes for both exams (both are written exams). If you just take a day to lock in for the exams you'll be good even if you don't take notes.
Prof Bloch was clearly passionate about what he was teaching. He genuinely cared about everyone in the class, and he kept his class as engaging as possible.

Gets to know students' names even though there's 120+ people in the class. Attendance is mandatory, but he's an excellent lecturer. Lots of reading but I really only read the one's I found interesting and I still did fine.

I really enjoyed his class, I never skipped a class because of how much I enjoyed him and the content. He is very engaging and even takes the time to know each and every one of his 120+ students. I would take another class of his. There are two essays, so get ready to read a primary source (book) for these essays.
Bloch is a very passionate prof, he is interested in what he's sharing with you! This course is a good beginning for anyone interested in history.

Prof Bloch is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches.  He cares about his students and makes an effort to learn everyones name.  Lectures can be heavy at times but Prof Bloch does a great job at answering questions and explaining things clearly.

Prof. Bloch cares a lot about the class, as he gives interesting lectures that he definitely enjoys talking about. Show up to class because attendance and participation isn't "mandatory" but a significant part of the grade. I'd recommend HIST 120 and any course taught by Prof. Bloch to anyone.
i thought he was great! lectures were engaging and the assignments kept me on track. offered a letter of recommendation as well
I took this class because I enjoyed the material. He made me no longer enjoy history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bloch is a great lecturer who clearly knows a lot about the subject he teaches. His class was extremely lecture heavy but he makes them entertaining. If you like history definitely take a class with him. There were only a handful of assignments that were graded very fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bloch is a great professor who is very knowledgeable on the subject. He elaborates a lot on the slides. The readings can be quite long for section but there's not too many of them. This class is one of my favorites and I would 100% take another one of Prof Bloch's classes.

Professor Bloch is an amazing lecturer. This class was organized perfectly for students with a great balance of independence and professor feedback. The lectures very content heavy but given in a very simple fashion. Bloch is a very educated guy with great insight on history!

His lecture is structured not like traditional history chronologically, rather, he breaks down materials according to different aspect of Weimar society. Such design definitely help me better understand the social norms and movements at that period, instead of mixing irreverent events just because they happened in the same year. Knowledgeable.
He cares about the material. Thats where the postive review ends.
Professor was unclear about specific gradings. Had the entire semester to do two essays, yet would not give feedback prior. Would not recommend.

I adored Bloch and His120. His lectures were extremely fulfilling as he is passionate, well-spoken and knowledgeable. He was clear and eloquent in every point he made. His energy is endearing and warm. He's funny and gives great feedback. Take His 120 whether you like history or not. I wish he would teach every course at this school.

I really enjoyed class with him; he learns everyone's name and is super accessible outside of class. Lectures are always engaging, with interesting content. Around 30% of your grade is simply attending lectures and participating in discussion sections. If you are looking for a history course which is not too much work overall, I highly recommend.

Really great professor. Incredibly passionate about the subject and takes the time to learn everyone's name in lecture. Brings a kind of goofy/nerdy and always upbeat personality to lectures which helps break up any boring bits or just general early morning grogginess. I'd take any class offered that he's teaching.

I really like him as a professor. Provides very interesting lectures, and you should go to class bc TopHat is used for participation. He makes an effort to learn everyone's name and there is participation and discussion during lectures. Midterm and final expectations are very reasonable. He is also very easy to talk to. Highly recommend!

I felt that Professor Bloch is a nice guy who puts a lot of effort into his class and really does care about each individual student, however, he grades extremely tough.  Granted, he gives great feedback on each paper, but even when the vast majority of feedback was positive I found I was receiving lower grades than expected based on said feedback.

He's incredible knowledgeable about the European political climate from world War II and after. Its a mix of intellectual and political history,.  You can tell he has a real passion for the focus of his field and its endearing to witness. Approachable and eloquent.
Great teacher! Super nice and approachable, and his lectures were very engaging. Took time to get to know everyone's name in our lecture.
I absolutely loved this class! Professor Bloch was a super engaging professor and I looked forward to going to his class. Could not recommend more.

Professor Bloch is a really great guy and I really enjoyed his class. While the lectures could be dense at times he did his best to make them as engaging and interesting as possible. Prof Bloch clearly cares for his students and made a big effort in trying to learn the names of everyone in my lecture.
By far the best Prof I've had here. He's super passionate about the content and is extremely helpful when it comes to papers. A class you genuinely want to go to. Could not recommend more.

I absolutely adore this professor! He's extremely passionate about what he teaches and makes an effort to get to know every student. His lectures are a little long and but he tries to make it as interesting and engaging as possible. He has a great personality overall and I would definitely take another class of his just for his teaching.
Great professor. One of the best I have ever had. Very passionate on what he teaches and just a great teacher.

I have taken two classes with Prof Bloch and both have been amazing! He really cares about his students and he is so helpful when it comes to writing research papers. He knows a lot about the field and he is so passionate when lecturing. He is definitely one of my favorite professors at UW and I highly recommend him to everyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bloch is a GEM. He is insanely passionate about what he teaches and my classmates and I absolutely adore him. In my History 120 lecture of around 80 students, he made an effort to learn everyones name�� Lectures can feel pretty long, but he makes them super interesting and interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bloch is very flexible and he really wants you to succeed. Lectures aren't very dense and easily digestible. Class mainly revolves around discussing that lecture's assigned reading. A decent amount of reading but that's to be expected for a class that revolves around historical research. Professor Bloch is a great I highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I've read that Prof. Black has lacked in communication through email. Although he's not the most tech savvy, I had no issue communicating with him. When in class, you could tell that he truly valued your opinion and had an open mind to any new ideas. He is very passionate about what he teaches and he encourages students to dive deeper into material

He was an amazing professor! It isn't difficult to get a good grade in the class, and he is so passionate about the subject. Attendance is mandatory, but I really didn't mind coming to class because we talked about interesting topics that were pretty engaging. I have no idea why he has 3 stars?? Definitely take this class, we watched 3 movies too!

when I first read the bad comments about Prof. Black, I thought it was just racism, but it's not. 

His course is disorganized, Canvas, assignments, and lectures. He always cancels/reschedules office hours and barely replies to emails. 

Prof. Black is passionate about what he teaches but is he passionate about teaching is a good question to ask.

This professor might be the most Unaccommodating and unfunny professor you can have. He does NOT care if you missed his class for any reason, I was really sick for a whole week and had trouble even with just getting up. His response for my request to redo an assignment was "It was in the syllabus". If you enjoy reading 60 pages everyday, take it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He claimed my paper was AI. It wasn't. I had proof that it wasn't and he still made me rewrite it. Doesn't get back to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Black is one of my favorite teachers at UW Madison. Yes there were pop quizzes that could be tricky but if you read which (besides 4 short essays) is the only homework. He always greeted us and loved participation and wanted everyone to succeed. If you read, participate and show up you will get a good grade. Great Professor!

afr 338 and professor is a nice guy. class is difficult because there are pop quizzes he thinks are easy but are hard, will be 30 plus pages of dense reading and the quizzes will be on insignificant material that no one will remember like the tiniest details. so hard if you do the readings twice still they are so hard and 30 percent of grade!!

This professor is the worst. The grading is completely inconsistent. One day, he'll dock points for minor things that weren't even mentioned, and the next day he ignores major issues. It's like he's making up the rules as he goes along. You never know what to expect, and he doesn't provide clear guidelines or feedback. It's frustrating and unfair.

WTF is MLA format, I've never seen a professor obsess so much over formatting. This guy will legit give you a failing grade if you don't meet his absurd formatting criteria, which he doesn't even teach! He just sends you to some random website and tells you to figure it out on your own. This professor is a complete joke. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Black is very approachable and helpful when you ask for feedback. Other students had a hard time with the grading on essays, but as long as you truly follow the prompt, there should be no reason for low scores. He made this class engaging, even though I was not interested in science fiction, and it made going to class much more fun.

I STRONGLY ADVISE AGAINST TAKING ANY COURSE TAUGHT BY PROFESSOR BLACK
Professor Black is the most INCOMPETENT professor I've encountered. So much irrelevant reading. The instructions for assignments are so poorly communicated that I often found myself struggling to understand what was expected (and he will relentlessly points off for formatting)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Black is an utter failure as a professor. His assignments are a masterclass in confusion, with instructions so poorly written that I often wondered if he was deliberately trying to sabotage his students. If you have any respect for your education or your mental health, steer clear of Professor Black and any course he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
WHERE TO START...
He's the type of prof to take a blowoff class seriously. He has this pedantic policy where you cant use electronics unless you sit in the front row. As someone who takes notes using my ipad this was completely unreasonable. Avoid any course associated with Professor Black if you value your sanity and GPA.

Prof. Black did a really great job with this class. He shows a true passion for the subject he teaches, and teaches in a way that every student can understand. Class was made of 3 essays and a final project that could either be creative or just a bigger essay. He's a great guy, and by the end of the semester you won't regret taking his class.

Was a great professor who was always passionate about his teacher. He is very lenient with deadlines and will allow for an extension if asked. He made the topics very interesting. I would recommend him as a professor to everyone!

Worst Professor I've had at UW-Madison. Not a lot of assignments but a lot of unnecessary readings that don't correlate with the lecture. I found myself when assignments were assigned lost because of poor instructions by Prof. Black. If you need a class for ethnic studies course DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE or ANY COURSE ASSOCIATED WITH PROF. BLACK.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory (3 excused absences), but he never really learns names, so participation is very optional. The class can be unorganized at times, so don't expect the syllabus to be followed, especially later in the semester. Pretty easy grader as long as you follow the instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Black is a super chill guy, and pretty understanding if you miss an assignment too. There was a student before me after class who literally just forgot to do an assignment and Professor Black just game him a free extension. Lectures weren't always the most interesting, but Black himself is funny and caring. Class is an easy A :)
He is a pretty cool person. Do the readings and participate and you'll have a good time.

Very good profesor. I had no art background but he made the class interesting and understandable. Also handled the COVID situation very well and was very kind to his students. Would definitely recommend AAS 242 if youre looking for an interesting ethnic studies course!!

He's a pretty chill guy but he is stern on attendance; I saw him kick someone out for being like 10-20 minutes late before. This class was a pretty easy A though as long as you show up, participate, and read the books you should be fine. If you're worried about anything, hes pretty accessible during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Anthony was such a great professor to have. I really do not like to read but he made lecture really enjoyable and himself very relatable to all of us. He always emphasized that he was on our side and would push due dates if we needed it. As long as you stay on top of reading, it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I adored this class and Professor Black. He's so funny and interesting, and really engages and relates to students. He values everyone's opinions and wants to get to know his students. He's not a super difficult grader, and he's pretty flexible. All he wants is participation.

The midterm has slide identification that requires a lot of memorization. He strongly encourages participation, as the class is discussion-based. The reading responses take longer than anticipated, but the papers are fairly short and easy to write. You don't really have to do the readings you don't write on, and lecture slides are not online.

Took this class for my Ethnic Studies requirement and had a bad experience with AP Art History so I was dreading it coming in, but the class itself is both interesting and manageable. Only one exam (midterm), three short papers summarizing reading, and two longer analysis pieces (2-3 pages and 4-6 pages). Only complaint is lecture slides not online
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Black's lectures were always interesting, but participation was necessary or else he would get very mad. He is a little disorganized in terms of deadlines. A couple of papers and participating in discussion are pretty much your only grades. You do need to read the material; it is actually pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is often condescending during lecture and corrects students' answers by explaining what was just said (by the student...). Despite this, the class was super easy and the readings had a lot of insightful information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Black's class has been one of my favorite at UW. His social and societal awareness prompts interesting discussions that engage students of all demographics; something not many professors I've had are able to do. This was one of the most engaging classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy, awesome class! I knew nothing about art or ethnic studies but this class was very informative and interesting. Expect to participate, he will cold call if no one answers his questions, and the course is very discussion based. One easy exam and two papers that were graded reasonably. Felt like more of art history than ethnic studies.

Assigned a lot of readings for no real purpose, often didn't guide our lectures. Prof seemed very unorganized with lectures and didn't give time to write down slides. Very educated and passionate about what he taught, but expected everyone to be at his knowledge for a 200-level class w/ mostly freshmen. Maybe this just wasn't his class.

Anthony was a really chill professor for the class. The assignments weren't really hard and you didn't really have to do the readings, but lectures were mandatory cause he took attendance. Easy ethnic studies credit, informative as well.

Took an afro american lit class with him 2 years ago. Honestly the only class I remember taking at UW. In addition to that, the only art history class I have ever taken to actually have an impact on me. Hard class but completely worth it.

Nice guy and fun to listen to. He is very hard to get ahold of however. I emailed him before a class I knew I was going to miss for an interview, only to come to the next class period expecting to have a midterm except he had changed the date of the midterm during the class I missed. When I asked him about it after class he kinda blew it off.

Overall, great professor. Refers to assigned readings in lectures, but is adept to open dialogue. First exam heavily based off memorization, so study well. Walked away with vast awareness to Black art well beyond Basquiat
Cool guy, but very hard to get a hold of and get help from. Lectures are long and discussion based. Notes are not posted on Learn@UW.

He's a very cool guy, his lectures are pretty entertaining. Keeping up with readings is a must. Tells you exactly what you need to know for exams, just have to put in the work to memorize it. He does different takes on assignments than most professors, which is nice. Even with no art background, I learned a lot. Decent class.
Interesting, intelligent, knowledgable, and approachable.  Great class!
Really easy and interesting class.  It is a must to keep up with the readings.

Nice guy, but horribly unclear in his expectations. I was a 4.0 student before this class. I was literally shocked when I received my midterm and paper grade. But even after that, I had no idea how to improve to meet his guidelines. Wouldn't recommend this class.

Anothy is a really relaxed professor and a really nice guy. The texts we read for AfroLit227 were interesting and thought provoking. HOWEVER, he is a little too laid back, he didn't tell us what was on our midterm until two days beforehand and he was late to our final exam b/c he was printing it off. Nice guy, unorganized teacher.
Class is insanely easy, only issue is that the grades are curved rather than actually being cutoffs. So even if you have a 99% going into the final, you could still end up with a C or worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: They should reduce the percentage weight of the assignments. The way this course is structured is unreasonable. Never seen such a disgusting course.
The class was well structured, and the lectures were informative. The professor seemed knowledgeable and was extremely accessible outside the course.

Her lectures and the class as a whole were fairly well-organized. The curve does not work, though, since 70% of the class is homework and nearly everyone has a grade in the upper 90s going into the final. They try to reassure you by saying "a 90 will likely not get a C"... not really what you want to hear.
She does not want to overwhelm students, and I appreciate the course design. Tests are not difficult. I recommend taking CS540 with her.

Her lectures aren't the greatest when she brushes over the hard content, but she has definitely improved over the semester. They provided great study materials for the midterm, and it felt easy had you prepared well. The projects can sometimes be challenging, but for a cs major, it's actually a really light class.

I want the instructor for 540 understand that it is an intro course with the prerequisite only algebra and 300. It should not contain these many high level contents for students with the prerequisite. Maybe it is not hard to cs major students, while not only the cs major students will take this course. It is hard for those who are not cs major

While I agree with others that it does sort of seem like AI is beyond Blerina's area of comfort in terms of knowledge, the lectures are still way easier to follow than other CS classes at UW-Madison. She made studying for exams easy, and the midterm didn't feel too challenging overall when compared to comments I've seen for previous years of 540.

Insanely lecture-heavy, but constantly has a horrible lecture structure spending way too much time on everything easy and brushing past anything difficult. Half the time it seems like someone else made the slides for her and she's trying to bs her way through without knowing what she's talking about.
Doesn't explain anything in lecture
Best professor I encountered so far and I will always be grateful to her.

Professor Gkotse is a good lecturer. She explained concepts clearly, but her lectures were boring. Many of the difficult concepts should've been taught with more time, and some of the easier material should've been glossed over quicker. The class did not provide study materials, and the projects had errors that were fixed last minute. Overall okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Blerina was a great professor. Clearly explained concepts, went slow enough for everyone to understand and fast enough to not be boring and redundant. She was also available to answer questions after class and answered them clearly. Overall a great professor.

Blerina was an amazing cs300 teacher, she explained everything very well so as long as you tune in to lectures you dont really even need to study for the tests. If she is teaching future CS classes, sign me up!

Blerina has very good lectures. She goes slow, so it is easy to let your mind wander, however, it's very important to pay attention in her class. She explains things easily, so if you pay attention in lectures, you won't have to learn from the textbook. When I took her, we used a terrible textbook called codio that was probably written by AI.

I will genuinely enroll in any CS class if I see that she's teaching it in future semesters! Amazing teacher! She presents concepts really well and makes all of them SO EASY to understand. She is also very understanding and will stay and help people in her OH until there's no more questions. Wish every CS professor was like that!!

Prof. Gkotse was a really kind lecturer. Her lectures are a slower pace, but you can watch the recordings of the lecture at 2x speed if her lecture speed bothers you. She explains concepts in depth which helps on the two in-person, paper and pencil exams. I didn't love the organization of CS300 (some projects were BRUTAL), but Prof. Gkotse rocked!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her office hours are great, but the lectures are pretty boring and hard to pay attention to. However, the Codio assignments are really helpful for learning the topics. It's also noteworthy that I am not a CS major (this class is how I eliminated it), so if you are, you may have an easier time following everything.

Professor Gkotse is a very nice and caring professor. She responds quickly through email and always makes sure you get the help needed and she always replies in a compassionate manner. While the content in lectures was explained well, you need to make sure that you understand the material learned through the online textbook thoroughly.

Blerina lectures at a slow pace, which I do not mind. It is easier to understand the harder concepts since she talks slower and does a very good job at explaining them. Lectures do feel tedious however, but are not required. There are weekly online quizzes and 2/4 unit tests are take home. Overall, Blerina is very kind and easy to understand.
The lectures felt very slow but she explained the topics clearly. The weekly programming assignments were designed well and were pretty engaging, and quizzes/exams were generally easy.

Prof. Gkotse is an excellent instructor who explains complex material clearly. Her well-structured lectures focus on key concepts and use real-world examples to make ideas relatable. She is always available to answer questions, creating a supportive learning environment. Overall, she is a dedicated and effective teacher, and I highly recommend her.

Verda is a very sweet professor and she has helpful insight into the industry. The class material can sometimes be boring, but not difficult. 4 quizzes, and then a group simulation. I would recommend taking this class with her for sure!
Verda was an amazing professor. Her lectures were engaging and she really cares about her students, making sure they learn and understand concepts. Would recommend taking any class with her again.
She's great! It's clear she really really cares about her students and has a heart of gold. You will do well if you show up and do all of your quizzes.

Verda is an awesome teacher, her grading criteria is clear, and as long as you try, it should be an easy A/AB. DO GOOD ON THE QUIZZES!! have to go to class to get 20/20. Very little homework, and a larger group simulation at the end is super fun and the most fun I've had in a class project. Would highly recommend!!

Verda is an awesome teacher, and she cares a LOT about her students. Her grading criteria is clear, and as long as you try, it should be an easy A/AB. Most lectures aren't mandatory, but it helps in order to do well in the quizzes. Very little homework, and a larger group simulation at the end. Would highly recommend!!
Verda was amazing. Had her last semester, and she somehow teaches a course that is easy, but not boring. Wish she still taught another class that I needed to take this semester.

Professor Blythe was phenomenal. She really cared that her students fundamentally understood the course's most important topics. There are no exams, just weekly quizzes and a group simulation in the second half of the course. If you put in a sincere effort, you are almost guaranteed an A. This is a wonderful introduction to supply chain management!

The best professor I have had at UW. I wish she taught more/ other classes, I would take every single one of her classes. Super kind and caring, always willing to help and meet outside of class. Clear expectations for grading. No exams, just weekly quizzes but if you go to class you will be fine! Awesome lectures!!!

She adds layers to her expectations so if you can please her throughout the course it will be an easy A for you. She does try to be caring and understand students' needs and adjust to that, overall it was good class but just keep in mind that the difficult part is that she's emotional and takes things personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Verda was such a great teacher for Intro to SCM! She is super clear in her expectations and grades assignments timely. No final exam, just a large group project and presentation that you have the entire second half of the semester to work on. She gives clear feedback and is always willing to help. Can't recommend her enough!

Verda is really passionate about what she teaches and it shows. This class was all online due to COVID & she made it really clear what was expected/due each week. Some of the readings got long, but overall the workload was really manageable. No tests, just some case studies & a group project. Most of the work for it is done near the end of the sem.
Verda is very knowledgeable about current issues in supply chain and has clear requirements for her class.
Great professor, strongly recommend taking any class with her!

Verda was a great professor, even for the GB110, which is a required course! The class itself is so easy as long as you show up, participate, and do the assigned work. If you have Verda, take advantage of all of her industry knowledge! She is so passionate and kind to everyone!

Verda is the sweetest, most caring professor you will ever have. Participation in class is a must, but she makes you want to participate. The exam and quizzes are fine. She grades cases easily (everyone gets a 100 on the first one; the others are graded more seriously). Group project is time consuming (read the manual well!). Overall solid class.
