By far one of my favorite professors of all time. Verda is super nice and really knows what she's talking about in supply chain. The class didn't require a lot of out of class work, the simulation was fun and the only exam in the class was not hard at all. I wish she taught more classes!
Lots of reading that is partly necessary. At least skim the material before class. Verda cares and it shows. One large group project that consumes the tail end of the semester. One exam.

Verda was my favorite instructor this semester. She really cares about each student and wants everyone to do well. The simulation is a lot of work, but very rewarding at the end of the semester. I would have happily added OTM to my major had I met Verda earlier.

I loved this course. I wish I would have discovered Supply Chain sooner! Verda is super nice. She completely understands when life happens and is willing to work with you. Had I taken this course a year ago- I would've added the supply chain specialization. Take this class!
Verda is a great teacher. Takes a real interest in her students and loves teaching. It's relatively easy to succeed in her class.
Really like the lectures. You really have to participate and she always starts with a nice discussion about a recent news fact. Exam was pretty hard but ok. Loved the class!
She is the best professor in the School of Business. Her class was so interesting that I chose my career path in Supply Chain.
Genuinely cares

Nicest prof you will ever have. Genuinely cares about her students and treats you like her own kids. Not a push over but relatively easy grader. Brings in TONS of cool speakers to the class. Class can get boring at times and a little awkward if no one participates but overall an easy class. Two midterms and a final. Two large papers.
She is a very nice person and the most accessible professor you'll ever have. She really cares about her students. Class includes a 15 page research paper which is the bulk of the work.

Easy grader when it comes to papers.  Nearly impossible to get anything less than an AB.  She didn't give any exams other than the final.  A bunch of reading.  We had dinner at her house once, a  field trip, and a movie night instead of going to class, which made things interesting.  She does expect a fair amount of participation, but this is easy.
rlly good prof!

Lectures drone on a bit, but they're interesting enough. Assignments were easy and he gave nice feedback on all of them. It's shakespeare so a lot of the reading is tedious, but you can get youtube explanatories of chapters and it works the same. Super easy A and I think Dr. Bowling is a great guy.
Very nice guy. Easy A if you get all the attendance. The lecture was a bit boring though, but he was trying to make it fun.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are a little monotone and hard to stay interested in for the length of the class. Held class a little late quite often. Grading was labor-based which I see the appeal of, but it can make assignments you're proud of less rewarding since something subpar would have gotten you the same grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowling is an incredible professor and puts a lot of thought into his lectures. I loved the transdisciplinary aspects; he includes linguistic, filmic and folkloric perspectives to help engage with the texts he teaches.

This is my 2nd class with Dr.bowling. I truly believe he cares about his students and likes what he does but god this class is so boring. And honestly I feel like he has a very convoluted and biased view of history. This leaks over into the content and requirements for assignments in the course. His grading system is also incredibly strict.

Prof. Bowling teaches the Introduction to Marxism FIG. The class is graded extremely leniently, but the value that you get from taking this FIG depends on the effort that you put in. The FIG is extremely rewarding and you will learn a lot of things that will change your perspective on many issues often missed in university settings in the US.

I literally never went to class and still did well. You dont need to really read any of the books assigned, and I didn't watch half the movies. A few big assignments make up most of the grade but expectations were super clear and grading was fair as long as you met the rubric. Definitely recommend this class for easy Lit credit.

I have Prof. Bowling for ENGL 241 and omfg I am bored to death every day. The content is a little dull, but his VOICE. It's incredibly monotone and he talks slower than the sloth from Zootopia. He definitely knows his stuff, but often goes into history lessons rather than analyze the text at hand, making papers harder. My TA saved me fr.

Heavy lecture class where participation is not mandatory. Lots of reading material but if you do not get to all of it it is not the end of the world. A lot of freedom is given to students in terms of when the papers are due and what they are about. Highly recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class, books and movies were surprisingly interesting. You can definitely get by without doing too much, but the material relates back to lectures, discussions, and essays. All lectures were posted, Prof talks a little slow, so x2 speed will be your bff. Overall, Prof Bowling made a somewhat slow class very entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The topic for my class was very boring, but the class itself is not challenging. Weekly discussion posts and 2-3 short papers. I did not attend a single lecture but discussions were engaging. I was able to do fine without reading or watching much of the material.

Bowling's Intro to Marx class is a great introduction to theory and covers so many important political philosophers! We were graded on two papers and a group presentation. Bowling is also a very understanding and flexible professor -- he will adjust the schedule to meet the class's needs.
You can tell he enjoys teaching this class, and lectures enhance understanding of the material. Was a fun class to take.

He is a really kind, knowledgeable guy. I took this class as it was offered once a week from 4-6:30 and I could never focus. He is lecture heavy and there wasn't a whole lot of discussion which I didn't enjoy. We were graded on three source studies (structure, character, language), a proposal, and a final essay, and we can revise the first two.

If you're looking for an easy English class, take this one. Three papers and weekly informal analysis writings, discussion once a week, and no mandatory lecture attendance. Dr. Bowling is a great lecturer and was interesting to listen to. I enjoyed reading/watching the material for the class, but you don't have to as long as you get the gist.

The class was based on a few formal and informal assignments that were all connected. You did not need to read all the books but you did need to know the general information. Take this class if you need some credit. Discussion is mandatory but it was not met very often, only when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bowling is what an introductory English professor should be like. There are only 3 papers in 176, and you will probably write it about The Office (show) or Office Space (movie), so they aren't tedious and actually kind of fun to write, especially if you enjoy film. Easy class, would recommend for anyone looking to fulfill English credit.

Bowling is a nice professor and clearly is passionate about the content he is teaching. The class was graded on 3 papers and weekly discussions, none of which were graded too harshly. The lectures themselves are quite boring in my opinion, but going to them is purely optional as none of the homework relates to the lectures at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bowling is sweet, cares a lot about the English language and film/books. The films/shows are super entertaining and all you have to do in the class is make disc posts and 3 larger papers. Homework is literally watching movies or shows and some reading once in a while. Lectures are pretty boring, he talks the whole time but sections can be fun.

I see a lot of reviews rating the content of the class poorly, but it seems he's changed the direction of his course from previous terms. The content is about how most workplaces and jobs aren't actually necessary and can be filled with greed, sexism, and unfairness. Readings were always short and interesting. Passionate and captivating lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not attend many lectures, and the course was still an easy A. Listen to the feedback on your first essay, then the remaining two will be easy. Class is 60% essays, 20% participation, and 20% pass/fail written responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ENG176 is easy and not a lot of assignments, but a lot of shows/movies and books/articles to read. There are 3 large papers the whole semester and a discussion post roughly once a week, so really not much work. NO PROJECTS OR EXAMS, JUST THE PAPERS. The stuff you learn is boring but the books and movies are interesting. Bowling is very sweet too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. He's a little shy and quiet, but he definitely knows what he's talking about. You really have to pay attention in class to understand the dense material but he does a good job. He genuinely cares about his students and constantly asks for feedback to make class more interesting/engaging. Decently light work load also.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Bowling did a pretty good job teaching this course. The films and literature selected were interesting for the most part. The weekly assignments weren't always the most helpful but do force you to engage in the material. The expectations are set and explained within the first week. The TA I had gave good feedback and communicated well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Bowling did a great job teaching this class. His lectures can be a bit dense, but fun if you make an effort to participate. Halfway through the semester he asked us for feedback and then implemented it right away; really seems to care about his students. Graded on two essays and weekly participation in an online discussion board.

I took Topics in Film & Lit hoping for an easy lit credit, and this class was a breeze. 3 SHORT papers and weekly discussion posts and you're golden. Dr. Bowling walks you through EXACTLY what he's looking for in strong papers, and is overall a great teacher. Very caring, and very easy-going. I took another class with him the next semester.

It's easy to be lulled to sleep by his monotone voice, but he seems to care about his students. I wouldn't search him out just to take a class taught by him, but I would be optimistic knowing he was my professor. Lot of sex books though...

If you are reading this, don't do what I did and ignore a lot of the reviews. I can only speak for ENGL 176, but this class is weird. Bad weird. I took a film class in HS expecting it to be similar. You barely watch any movies, and the ones you do watch are so so strange. Worse, the books you read are extremely convoluted and incomprehensible.

Dr. Bowling is a quiet guy, but very sweet and intelligent. His lectures are not posted online, so take good notes. ENG176 content mostly science fiction. not my cup of tea; wasn't too interesting. reviews.comment:
Won't answer questions.

reviews.comment: The videos and lectures seem like from 20 years ago. If u take this class, u are expected to learn everything by yourself.

I can see what people dislike about this professor, but I had no problems taking stat303 online. It is the pace of a 3 cred class that only lasts a third of the semester (hence why its 1 cred), which I wasn't aware of until taking it so I was a little overwhelmed with my workload. But overall its easy and teachable to yourself w/o lectures

Stat 303 itself was not too bad; it was Bo Yang that made it miserable. He doesn't explain things well, and the lectures were not very good. For being a 1 credit class, definitely takes a lot of time/effort. I recommend a different professor, if possible. This course is definitely doable with him, as long as you can self-teach/spend lots of time.

Would not wish him on my worst enemy. His lectures are awful, he does not know how to teach, and he's full of himself. For his lectures he just copies some other guys code that you have access to on video anyways and claims it is his. Everything the other bad ratings say are 200% true
I'm kinda suprised that he's got a 1.7 right now. Just aviod him if you can
He is okay

I don't understand the hate honestly. Tough to understand at times, but covered the material straight from the textbook so you could reference it later. Homework took a long time some weeks, but was manageable. Exams weren't easy, but he didn't ask anything that wasn't on the homework or review. The final being 30% was scary, but turned out okay.

I dont know how this school keeps finding terrible professors like Bo.

Just try to avoid him, he cant teach.
AVOID AVOID AVOID AVOID!

Professor Yang is a terrible professor! He presents the material as if it's extremely simple, meanwhile many students are lost. He is very disorganized at times, and he gets irritated when students ask questions. Most of the time he is flat-out rude and has yelled at students during class. Hands down the worst professor I've had at UW by a MILE!

RUN! Bo needs to learn how to treat students with respect and stop blaming students for his own faults. Lectures are useless and he won't release grades until months after the end of the class. Don't waste your time to take his class. If you have to take this class, at least choose the online sections so you don't need to interact with him.

The class is generally very hard, but Bo does a pretty good job of explaining the topics. He doesn't provide great materials outside of class, so attending class, for me, was a MUST. The lecture notes were not very clear, but he explains better in class. Front heavy class, easy end of the class.
Straightforward

Not an easy class but you are able to understand the topics and help is accessible in this class. Pretty straightforward homework and exams. Extra credit opportunities available that would have raised my grade even more. Definitely recommend.
Great Prof, easy course, and not too much homework. Just keep studying 4 hours before the exam, and you will get an A.

Never ever choose this teacher, He is so mean because he judges other student ability with discrimination. A person was confused by a question, so they just post on piazza, Bo just said improve your reading ability. He even does not post due date. You must click into this courses instead of calendar.

Run. When asking for help on anything related to the class, instead of helping he'll say google it because "how am I supposed to know the answer" His lectures are not helpful at all, for any assignments, I had to YouTube everything, the only reason I passed the class. He likes to talk about how he learned all this information (R Studio) by himself

reviews.comment: BOzo is a perfect description for Bo. Guy is hard to understand, rude, and spends class just rewriting his slides. If you think he's going to teach you the material or even be nice to you, then you're in the wrong place. If you can, avoid him at all costs.

Bo Yang is the least respectful professor I have ever seen. Could not organize a class at all, lectures were pointless and just followed a sheet. He told a student asking a clarifying question  
"If you think the wording is confusing, you'd better improve your reading comprehension in some ways" Save yourself from a rude & disrespectful professor
Excellent!
run. Would Never take this professor's class.
310 is super easy, and I recommend taking this class.

Every worst aspect as a teacher you can imagine you can find on him. He may be terrible at teaching, but he's talented at ruining your day and your whole semester. There is 3 homework due in 8 days and most of the questions he hasn't taught. He is much behind his original schedule, and suddenly speed up to catch up schedule at the end of semester.

Exams are nothing the same as homework or practice exams. Lectures are not super helpful, though lectures notes are sometimes helpful.

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst professor in all of Wisconsin - avoid him like the plague. Disorganized, short-tempered, aggressive, and un-responsive. Really hope the guy is doing alright if I'm being completely honest. Kind of worrying how it seems like he just doesn't care about anything at all besides becoming frustrated with his students.
You are better off learning from Google than him. Probably one of the most passive-aggressive professors I have had here.

Every single aspect of this course has been hand-crafted by Bo to be as infuriating as humanly possible. He even disabled the feature on canvas where it tells you your total score. As far as content difficulty on a scale of 1-10, the homework is a 2, the lectures a 4, the exams an 8, and the discussions a full 10. Nothing about it makes any sense.

I can forgive professors for being bad at teaching if they at least try to be helpful otherwise. Bo is the worst of both worlds in this respect. It's best to pretend he doesn't exist: lectures are a waste of time and asking for help won't help. The extent of your interaction with him should be the poorly worded emails he sends before each exam.

His lectures are basically talking about his own R programming experience, which is useless. He learned R by himself which shows he is unprofessional. The homework, quizzes are the copy of another prestigious professor. Learned nothing from his class although the exam is not really hard.

I took his online class to learn about the data programming language, R. He has never taken a class on R, and did not design this class, yet he is still teaching it. He is very dismissive and unprofessional in email. Do not take this class if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is really bad at teaching. What he teaches in the class is almost the same as the handouts given. The lecture is totally useless. You need to teach yourself for the course and be prepared for the hard and endless exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are really bad, the class is structured pretty alright in general. If you don't mind basically teaching yourself everything you should be fine. I had a really good TA that graded everything fairly and answered questions. Forget about asking Bo Yang a question, he'll just tell you to pay more attention to the lecture.
You need to understand that by taking his class you can only count on yourself to learn everything.

If you can avoid this professor, please do. I have had him twice and he mentioned that he has never taken a stats class or a class in R, which is what he teaches. Why should we learn from him then? He is terrible at answering questions and is kind of just a miserable person to be around. He is the worst professor I have had so far.

The construction of the class is to the students advantage, with quizzes allowing infinite attempts and the homework being fairly straightforward. Professor Yang is not incredibly accessible or immediately helpful, but his general is sensible. If you try in this class, you will do well, but youve got to try. He also extended a hard homework.

Bo is so rude, my gosh. Interacting with him was such a pain to the point where I didn't want to email him or talk to him during class because he would just flip out at me for no reason. I got an A in this class because I had covered the content at a high-pace job I did over the summer, but he does absolutely nothing to help with gaining R skills

The lectures are only giving you the basics. To complete HW and quizzes you need to do 10 more steps, so expect to spend a lot of time outside class understanding and trying to write your own code. Bo's lectures are useful to understand the material but when it comes to helping, he isn't willing to help that much.

Yang is kind of impatient to students and his lecture is boring. He simply runs his code and expects us to understand the output by ourselves. You would have to work a lot after class to keep up if you have never learnt RStudio before. But the final is not so hard as long as you do all the homework and quizzes.

reviews.comment: STAT327 part 1 is not bad since it is pretty easy, you'll be fine if you take this. Part2 and Part3 is a nightmare. reviews.comment: He is actually pretty rude and impatient with students. For a lot of non-statistics students, 327 is kind of an intro level classes and are supposed to be well-structured. But he ruined my experience in this field and don't actually helpful at all. Worst professor and worst class in Madison. I think the school should stop hiring him to teach.
How is he a professor? Honestly he should not be allowed to teach any where let alone the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
He is the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't even use his own presentations.
Grade based on about 5 homework assignments and 3 exams.  The material was not difficult, but was taught so poorly.  Bo is very hard to understand.  Went through the material EXTREMELY slowly.
He is very hard to understand and follow in lecture. 10/10 wouldn't recommend.

If you have a choice between Professor Yang and another professor take the other professor. Theres little to no point in going to lecture he is hard to understand and won't move to new ideas. reviews.comment: As a professor Yang really is not that great of a professor as he moves very slowly through the material and lectures drag on. The homework for this class is insanely long.  With all of this being said, his tests are very fair and he tests you on the basics for the most part making the class with Yang manageable.

Has spent the entire semester teaching us what a random variable is. Says the same things everyday and nobody learns anything from him. The only reason I would recommend this professor is if you wish to lower your IQ.

Yikes.. Bo means well and you can tell he is passionate and energetic when it comes to the material, but that's about it. Lectures are boring, confusing, and most times you leave forgetting you were even there in the first place. Homework is long and annoying and tests are hard. Try to avoid!!

Terrible Lecturer, you won't learn a thing. His powerpoint are a mess and half the time you don't know what he's talking about. Hope for a good TA or you're gonna be in a world of hurt. Exams are tough and long. Would not recommend.

reviews.comment: Very dull lectures, struggles to explain concepts clearly. Lots of homework, but the exams aren't too difficult if you study and do the homework. Not an enjoyable experience
There is literally a 0% chance that you will enjoy having this professor.

Another worst instructor in this campus! Expect a lot of homework. His lecture is super boring. Can't explain the concept clearly due to his poor English. He likes saying 'Look at this figure and you can get this , and THEN you can get this."  I don't know how I can get it only by looking at this or that. And the exam is much harder than previous.

reviews.comment: If you want a class where you can decide to go or not by feeling this is it. Most of the time your body is the only thing there in lec. Just read the slides on your own time. Homework is super easy if you go to discussion and read the slides. The answer is just there. Prof is helpful and willing to stay after lec to answer questions, or ask TA.

Lecture is rough. Hard to pay attention. One discussion a week is plenty to clearly and thoroughly cover a weeks worth of lecture material. Discussion worksheets are exactly like the homework and tests.  Follow along and take notes in discussion and you will be fine. Tests are straight forward.

She is supposedly an easy grader, but only if you're the same ethnicity as her. I have had her ask me some questionable things, she is very passionate but you don't know your grade till the end of the semester and if you're not an amazing writer you won't get an A.

I Took ILS 367 with Professor Botero. She is the best professor I've had; super caring, passionate, and enjoys teaching her students. She is a very good literary analyst and explains difficult concepts between texts with ease. Be ready to read books, attend every discussion section, and participate in discussions by asking and answering questions.

I took ILS 367 (Migration in the Americas) in F24 with her. She is super passionate about what she teaches and the course material is always unexpectedly insightful. Her lectures are delivered with thematic clarity and always end on a conclusive note. She makes you think about the hidden details in passages that may otherwise not have been noticed.
She is very sweet and you can tell she cares a lot. Very easy class with generally clear expectations. Participation is important.

One of the best prof I have had here. She is super energetic and passionate about her lectures, and you can really tell that she is aiming for the best for her students. The course material is interesting, and the lectures are structured so that we get to share our experiences and thoughts throughout the semester.

Botero is a great professor. She makes lectures very interesting and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. There is quite a bit of reading, so be prepared for that. Otherwise, the courseload is quite manageable. There is a presentation, essay, and final exam but she gives very flexible deadlines and provides clear instructions.

~ Disregard last review

(Missed 2 classes due to illness, told the TA, and still did not get full points for my attendance)

reviews.comment: Professor Botero is one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I have ever had here at the university; she really tries to get to know all of her students. Make sure you are familiar with all the readings, otherwise your participation grade & exams may suffer. If you do the work and provide your own honest opinions, it's an easy A!
An awesome professor and a really nice human being. Take class with her if you can, she is really nice and sweet. She knows her content.

I had Beatriz for both 226 and 224, and she is THE best TA ever. She's adorable and fun, and it's clear that she loves teaching. If you're having trouble, she's more than willing to help, and she always tries her hardest to keep class interesting. I would definitely recommend taking her!

Beatriz is adorable! She is super funny and sweet. Not too much homework, 4 exams and 4 papers (which you can correct and hand back in). She can't explain grammar concepts very well in english, but if you have a background in Spanish you'll be fine. Take Beatriz!
Awesome teacher! I looked forward to Spanish everyday with her. Easy grader and she will do whatever it takes to help you. She is very genuine and is one of the best teachers I've had so far!
Beatriz is so adorable. Her class is relatively easy, only studying is vocab etc. Spanish wasn't bad considering it was 4 days a week.

She was a very good teacher. Spoke very clear and comprehensible Spanish.  I thought I would have a lot harder of a transition into a college language but she made it fun and easy.  Was very patient and helpful to students.  She was very fun. I wish I could've had her again.
good teacher. easiest 4 credit class i have taken so far. definately worth the time.
No Comments

Manages to break down advanced concepts very well. Motivates almost everything with examples. The homework directly prepares you for the exams which are very straight forward. Class is lecture-heavy but the lectures are very engaging.

Professor Wang is a IMO Gold Medalist. I expected him to teach us several competition style techniques, but the truth is that you can tell that he is way too busy for his research. Nonetheless, he is great at decomposing bigger problems into smaller ones, which makes understanding pretty easy

Lecture notes in general were unorganized and very messy. I think he is a nice prof who tries his best, but you will end up learning more on youtube for the class. Had 3 exams worth 86% of grade total. Rest was discussion quizzes and homework that were all fairly easy and had 2/3 drops. Look for someone different.

Wang's lectures for 222 are awful. His notes are unorganized and messy. His explanations are confusing and unhelpful. He can't help it, but his accent and stuttering makes a bad explanation worse. He doesn't explain what we're learning & writes on the notes app, which results in missed notes as soon as he scrolls down. Switch lectures if you can.

Botong is really fun. I'd definitely recommend going to lectures. He's a good lecturer. He has a bit of an accent, but I almost never had trouble understanding him. He can be fun sometimes too. Like he used being a sniper as an analogy when talking about polar coordinates, which I still remember. Overall I found 234 enjoyable and not too hard.

Course and lectures are extremely disorganized. Professor himself is always extremely unclear and confused as to what he is teaching. He always makes mistakes in his lecture notes and has to correct himself halfway through the problem. Tests get way harder as the year goes on with all of them making 84% of your grade.
An above average teacher in a below average math department. He definitely cares about his students, and explains concepts in a way that isn't too difficult to understand.

Professor Wang is a great person and it's clear that he is passionate about the subject, but his lectures are hard to follow as he jumps from one step to another without much explanation. I did decent on the weekly quizzes and homework, but the exams are 85% of the grade so it's hard to bounce back after the first exam if you do poorly.
Lots of passion for math, explains things very well.

Professor Botong is a great math professor. His problems given in lecture are incredibly helpful when preparing for exams since he quite literally will go over exam questions. He will go out of his way to prove certain theorems and not just tell you they are true because they are true. He is incredibly efficient with his time so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, Botong was a great professor. His lectures may sway from the main topic at times, but he mostly stays on track. His use of analogies and enthusiasm make the lectures far easier to get through.

I REALLY enjoyed Botong Wang's class and loved his teaching style. Just go for lecture and use office hours - ask your TA's during discussions as many questions as possible. It's honestly what you put into the class - people usually find Calc 2 really hard, but its all about practice and preperation!

I got a 3 on AP Calc BC in high school so I had to take Calc 2, but this class seemed significantly harder and covered more topics than AP. Botong himself is good and answers questions well. I absolutely tanked the first midterm and spent the rest of the semester trying to at least get a C because over 80% of the grade is from 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Botong himself is a great guy who genuinely cares about his student. However, his lectures aren't well structured and often leave you confused. I stopped going and learned the material online instead and did fine after that. Majority of grade(84%) comes from 3 exams without much opportunity for fixing your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Seemed like he cared and was passionate about the material, but wasnt great. Hard to understand at times, jumped all over the place including going backwards during problems making it difficult to follow. Made mistakes fairly frequently as well. Also told us something wasnt gonna be on the midterm and then it was 20/100 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He didn't announce that the class wasn't curved until after the second exam. I got a low score on the first exam and started meeting with a tutor weekly and got an A on the second exam but I still had to drop the class because I wasn't going to get the grade I needed. It's possible to pass, but get a tutor, you will learn way more than in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in lectures and ask your TA questions (during discussion sections), youll be good. Prof. Wang is enthusiastic about math and makes lectures not too boring. He is a good, nice choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can't expect to skip lectures for this class. I had technically already taken this class at a different school so I thought it would be an easy A; however, you are discounted points for your strategy in answering the question and your strategy needs to be in-line with what was discussed in lecture (even if your answer is correct).

Math 222 lectures are very straightforward; the entire time is spent thoroughly walking through very helpful examples of different Calc 2 concepts. Exams are tough but definitely manageable if you follow along in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wang genuinely wanted to help us understand calc, but his lectures were scattered and all over the place. His lectures were v fast paced, and you HAVE to pay attention, attend, and complete ALL the hw. The only thing I liked abt this course was that the exams were v similar to the hw, so everything was fair game. Good person, j not the best teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is a really good lecturer and definitely the best Calc 1 teacher! He gives options for extra credit and dropped the lowest test and homework scores for us. He often gives details in lectures that are confusing but the exams do not focus on these. Exams are straight forward and consistent with the homework. Also very nice and helpful!

Botong Wang is a really sweet professor who clearly has a lot of passion and cares for his students. Lectures can get a little dense but don't get bogged down in details or proofs. Exams are a good reflection of the course material and he often uses problems from the homework. Go to class and do the homework and you'll get a good grade!
Literally just reads theorems from the textbook. Is incredibly confusing and teaches unconventionally. Over a hundred students left this course because of how confused they were.

You can tell hes smart and knows his stuff but his lectures are extremely unclear and hes left a class of over 200 students frustrated and confused. He has 6 tests he gives out and everytime a student asks a question his answer is I dont know. Dont  take him for calc 1 or youll regret it immediately like I did. Do not recommend to anyone

Topology is very difficult to understand on your own but Botong is the man and did a very good job explaining things--lectures were recorded, and he shared his lecture notes--which was super helpful so that I could just concentrate on understanding the content which is very nuanced. Exams were very fair. Homework was tricky but very manageable.

Not sure why my experience with Botong is so markedly different than the other reviews. I thought he'd be great, but it pains me to say that he's not. You can tell that he cares, but the lectures are so unclear that attendance is at 30%. Endless "Proof is left to the reader," "I'll let you think about it," and "This should be really clear."

Sometimes he gets a little confused halfway through a proof and will start over, or will change notation halfway through a definition. Other than this he is an excellent instructor and gives great examples and makes theoretical map very tangible for students just being introduced to topology.

The class overall was tough but not too bad. Go to lecture and do homework and you should be fine. Botong is very smart and often gets ahead of himself and off topics but usually brings it back in and is a good teacher in general.

Took Prof Wang for Math 222 in Spring 2016. Having recently completed the UW Calc sequence, he was without a doubt the best of the three profs I had. If youre taking 222 and Botong is an option, take it with him. You wont be disappointed.

Prof Wang is an expert in topology, and his 551 course is pretty reasonable. He gave only one midterm and a final, but the problems were a decent mix of old homework problems and new challenge problems. He can be pretty helpful in office hours, and it seems like he is primarily interested in the success of his students.
Botong Wang is a very charming professor, and he made the Math 222 straight forward and clear. If you are wondering to take his course, you can definitely take it. It will be fun and easy.

Professor Wang is a very caring and patient professor. He listened carefully and answered each question step by step in the lecture. He did really well on explaining the problems to students. I like his math class.

Botong's exams are very straightforward and mostly comes straight from previous homeworks. Although the lecture is very fast paced, he's very willing to take questions and encourages students to attend office hours if anything is unclear. Makes you work for the grade, but Calc 2 isn't an easy class and it's possible to do well as long as you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall he explains things pretty well and sometimes jumps to answers but is extremely willing to answer questions. The material itself is what is really hard but if you're putting in a lot of time to do the homework and understanding how to get the answers (not just doing it to get it done) and reading the textbook you'll probably be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: . I watched him throw a beaker at a student during lab and the University ignored my concerns and hushed the whole situation. I recommend you stay as far away as you can from him.

Dr. Block manages the 103 labs extremely poorly and is not accommodating. It takes 6+ hours to complete 1 lab and worse if you are blamed when technology and equipment that's broken when you had no control to begin with. Labs are unclear, unforgiving and nitpicked on the poor wording to be used against you. Be very careful with him...

If I had just one—it would be to take this class again.

If you are lucky enough to have Dr. Block, consider yourself blessed by the chemistry gods. He is a genuinely great person. You can tell he is smart—not just STEM-smart, but broadly so. I strongly encourage you to visit him during office hours; he has wonderful stories to tell.

Dr. Block is an amazing professor. He really cares that his students succeed and has very engaging lectures. He is very thoughtful and hilarious which makes his lectures fun to attend. He goes over different examples from what is given in the pre-class readings which really helps solidify what you read.

Chem 109 has a very difficult nature. The tests are incredibly difficult, much more than the practice tests given.  Dr. Block is extremely knowledgeable in his field . The thing is Dr. Block says there will be an "adjustment" to grades at the end, but will not post it anywhere. You cannot see how much (if any) your grade was "adjusted".

I genuinely cannot say enough good things about Professor Block. He presented the material in such a way that it was so easy to grasp, and made you excited about chemistry. He cares about the success and wellbeing of all of his students, and is just a fun guy to be around.
This guy is the greatest lecturer I've ever had. Made the course a breeze, highly recommend.

Dr. Block is an incredibly eloquent speaker, explains complex concepts easily, and will make his lectures feel more intimate by sharing funny anecdotes. He is always available on Piazza to answer questions and makes it clear he cares about your success in the class.

Professor Block was an amazing chemistry professor. He made every lecture fun and engaging - sharing lots of random lore. He is always very responsive to questions on Piazza and is genuinely passionate about chemistry. Would definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Block was such an amazing lecturer! He always tried to explain concepts that the textbook didn't really explain well. For a hard class like 109, he made it easier. He always responded to my Piazza questions within an hour, even on weekends (insane tbh), and guided me through when my TA wouldn't.

Chem 109 is hard, will have you thinking A LOT, but its not impossible. The tests are rough, but block is such a great professor who really tries to give in-depth concept explanations, especially because most of the tests require applied knowledge. He also cares a lot about his students, I definitely recommend going to his office hours if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Block is a cool guy. Chem 109 was hard but I think professor Block did a good job.

He's a great professor that explains things thoroughly and clearly, there's a lot of content but it's not super hard just very time consuming. I can tell he's very passionate about chemistry and always makes class funny and engaging.
He's a great professor and his class is fairly interesting. I will say though chem 109 is hard but Dr. Block can help make the concepts easier. Highly recommend his lecture.

Dr Block is great! He makes lectures funny and engaging. 109 has a reputation for being tough, and will definitely take up a lot of your time, but Dr Block is a good enough lecturer that if you put in the time and effort to do well it is entirely possible to earn an A.

Dr. Block is a great lecturer. He explains difficult concepts very clearly. He is beyond knowledgable, which allows his lectures to be thorough and digestible. He also gives lots of feedback in class that is helpful for exams. If you pay attention to the lectures, this course is not very difficult. He is also very funny and kind, which is a plus.

Awsome guy, all around.

Dr. Block is an amazing professor. It's clear that he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. This is a very fast paced course but I personally believe that Professor Block does a very good job making good use of lectures. He is very thorough and does a good job of making difficult to understand material understandable.

Professor Block is one of the best Chemistry Professors at UW-Madison. His lecture notes are handwritten and easy to follow. He sprinkles in some jokes here and there in lecture and overall a very enjoyable experience for my first general chemistry college class.

Dr. Block is a very engaging lecturer and proved to be very helpful in understanding a tough concept like general chem. I recommend taking 109 with Dr Block

Dr. Block is not only an amazing professor, well spoken, and entertaining in lecture, he is also a great and compassionate man. He genuinely cares about his students and is accessible outside of class.

I loved taking Dr. Block's class! He's a great professor who obviously knows a lot about chemistry and is also very enthusiastic about teaching it. He's funny, his lectures are easy to follow, and he's helpful if you have questions.

Chem 109 is really hard but Stephen is a good professor that cares about his students. His office hours are really helpful and his lectures are really clear.

His lectures and slides were easy to follow! Chem109 was hard but he tried his best for us to make the material digestible.

Professor Block was truly a great professor. During the lectures he kept the class engaged by jokes, interesting stories about the applications of what we were learning, and more. His lectures were engaging because he drew many diagrams to help with understanding concepts. He did a good job explaining what he was looking for in terms of grading.

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've ever had - he writes out his thinking, includes fun (relevant) stories, and answers questions succinctly, non-judgmentally, and clearly. Dr. Block is a friendly teacher. His lectures are amazing. Great ppt style that's easy to follow, and some jokes/experiences/historical stories during lectures. CHEM 109 is not an easy class, but if you get 80% on each test and do all other work, you can still get A. He answers most student questions and got me interested in chemistry major again.

Professor Block is a fantastic lecturer and he was very thorough especially for a class with a ton of material like Chem 109. reviews.comment: His lectures are annotated, so it is easy to follow along. However, to succeed in this class, you will probably need to attend office hours. He is very accessible outside of class, but you are also able to go to the other 109 professors for help. Labs are pretty difficult.

I LOVED having Dr. Block as my general chemistry professor. Lectures are productive and well organized (he takes time to answer student questions and finishes daily material) He will use a student answer to a pre-class question and go over how he would grade the response on exams, so you have a clear idea of what the graders are looking for!

Dr. Block is a great lecturer, but terrible with assigning labs. Dr. Block is super nice and a very approachable person. His sense of humor made lectures enjoyable, and he genuinely wants and believes that his students will succeed.

Dr. Block was a fantastic professor. While the large class sizes can make you feel small, there are numerous resources available for feedback and Dr. Block is very accessible outside of class. Dr. Block was a great professor! He is soft spoken so it makes him seem less intimidating and more approachable, but is also extremely intelligent. He and the TAs were helpful

reviews.comment: If you are great at and interested in chemistry, you will do amazing in this class. If not, avoid it. Run away. Professor Block has the hardest exams out of all chem 104 professors. Do not take this class if you want to be happy.

Amazing lectures! Made content interesting and easy to understand. Tests were all free response and short on time, but were manageable. Dr. Block is a legend, great guy and fantastic professor. Extremely smart but good at explaining.

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, the best of my college experience so far. Nothing was too tough but you definitely had to work for it. Yeah I legit want to be this guy's friend.

This class is the hardest class I have ever took. Do NOT take this class if you can avoid it. Dr Block is a great guy, funny too, but this class is very hard. I regret not taking Chem103/104. Best Professor ever!!! I really like Dr. Block's lecture because he makes complicated concepts easier to understand and uses interesting metaphors. I like his little humor, really makes my day. Extremely difficult exams which somehow someone aces each time. Tests are weighed roughly the same as the labs. Relatively easy to exceed for an advanced class. Great Professor, No complaints.

Dr. Block is an amazing teacher and human being that truly cares about his students. Yes, his exams are difficult and his class is a lot of work, but both reward students who have put in the time to really understand the chemistry at a deep level. Would definitely take again.

Professor Block was amazing he does a really great job of fully explaining concepts and he tries to make sure all questions are answered completely and clearly. Dr. Block was a great professor for a challenging class. He is incredibly smart, but always worked his hardest to explain the material in a clear way. Dr. Block definitely knows what he's talking about; but, he tends to be very wordy and over explains things, making them more difficult to understand than they should be. Personally I believe Stephen Block is one of the best lecturers at UW. Dr. Block is awesome. Be prepared for very difficult exams. Dr. Block has very high expectations of his students, but he is honestly one of the smartest people I have ever met. Dr. Block is an excellent professor. Communication with students was great and created an environment where expectations for class were very clear. It was obvious that he cared about the success and well-being of all students. Dr. Block was accessible outside of class by email or in office hours. By far the best professor I have ever had! Even when the content was difficult I enjoyed the class because of him. I would highly recommend this professor!!!

reviews.comment: Prof Block is a great guy. Really cares about how his students do & his lectures were great. Explains topics well and made a really tough class tolerable.

Block is really awesome in lecture. His slides are very concise and he covers lots of content in each lecture, while not making it seem overwhelming. reviews.comment: The exams are unbelievably difficult. It doesn't matter how much you study, even if you get one question wrong on the exam, you could lose up to 28%. (The mastery problems are worth 14 points out of the 50 total, so if you get that one wrong, you're screwed).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Block is a very charismatic lecturer. He makes lectures enjoyable with intermittent jokes. He really cares about his students. Attending office hours is extremely helpful because he will answer your questions well, and he will try to make sure you understand it. The exams were very challenging, though.

Block was very organized and clear in what he wanted you to know. Not only that, but lectures weren't boring. He likes to throw in jokes and lots of demo videos. Labs aren't that bad, as long as you take time beforehand. I enjoyed the class overall, very good curve.

Great lecturer and always tries to throw a little humor in (always laugh if it was remotely a joke). Tests are pretty tough but other aspects of the class bring the grade up. I fully expected to earn an AB with my final exam score but received an A so he does curve/ round up at the end.

Block is a great lecturer. He is very engaging and cracks a lot of really nerdy jokes. The tests are hard but the curve is reasonable. You need to read the textbook about everyday to understand what is going on in lectures.

reviews.comment: I made the mistake of taking Chem 109 with Dr. Block after having little to no HS chemistry. 3 exams and 1 final, class averages of 59%, 66%, 68% and 69% for the final. Labs and weekly homework are easy A's and help to offset the really difficult exams. Also, the class isn't run on a curve, so you know where you stand.

reviews.comment: One of my all time favorite professors. I only interacted with him a couple times but he still remembered who I was. Gives very clear lectures that are helpful for the homework and exams. Super kind and well respected. 100% would take his class again.

Dr. Block is one of the kindest, smartest people I have met. He truly loves what he does and cares about his students. He makes his expectations very clear, posts all of his lectures, is great at explaining concepts, and is very funny. This class is hard and a lot of work, but Dr. Block reminded me why I love chemistry even through the pain.

Professor Block is awesome! Chem 109 can be a tough class but he was sure to make us laugh and keep us somewhat entertained during the lectures. The tests can be difficult though because some of the problems are about topics we didn't directly learn about.

Dr. Block is a great professor. He's a bit nerdy, but he is enthusiastic about what he teaches and explains concepts in lecture very well. Be warned that if you do take Chem 109, prepare to work very hard. However, Dr. Block made that class far more enjoyable, and I would definitely take him again.

Here's the bottom line: this class is hard and you'll have to work for it. My recommendation is if you just have to take one semester of chem, get an easier professor. If you're moving on to Ochem and need to understand the concepts, Block is a good choice. He knows his stuff but his class will bury you with homework, confusion, and tears.

Attend lecture bc he will screw you with top hat

Good lecturer. Exams make up most of your grade and are often so difficult that the average is between 55-65%. Not a bad teacher by any means but his class is so much more difficult than any of the other teachers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Block for 103 and 104 and I absolutely loved him.. he is a very nice and extremely intelligent guy, he cares about his students and tries to push you to your limit.. Exams are not easy, but I learned how to study effectively and started doing really well on them. If you apply yourself, Block will help you reach your potential.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Go to office hours they are THE most helpful thing in this course. My second midterm grade increased by 20% when I started going.

Stephen cares about his students and makes sure everyone is actually learning the material. His tests are much harder than the other gen chem professors but you get way more out of the course with him. You have to pay attention during lecture but he does his best to keep you focused and engaged.
Funny

Dr. Block was a great professor. The class wasn't easy, but I felt like if you wanted to succeed he wanted that too. He is very funny in lecture and office hours which makes the class more fun. His tests were not easy, but if you put work in, you will get good results. Wish I could take his class again. Overall, great human.

Dr. Block is a very good professor who adds humor into his lectures. I wish I could take him again. I had a strong Chemistry background and put a lot of work in but I did well in the class. I fully participated and went to many office hours but I liked the class. Be prepared to do a lot of work for your grade but you will enjoy the class if you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chem 103 is a hard course and Professor Block makes it a bit harder. The exams are no joke, they are hard so do as many practice problems in the back of the book, discussion packets and past top hat questions. Also, the homework will take longer than the recommended time so don't get discouraged.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Was not prepared for any of his exams even slightly. My TA even said he wouldn't be able to answer some of the questions on Professor Block's exams. They do not reflect the course very well. Doesn't explain lecture slides in very much detail. Homework required many hours even though it says only 45 minutes a weekend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I took Dr Block for Chem 103, and while he is clearly knowledgeable on the subject, I feel like a lot of the time he was trying to assert the fact that he was so smart. He would explain concepts in the most unnecessarily difficult manner, when the book would make it much simpler. Tests are hard but not horrible, but you really have to work hard.

Hardest class I have ever taken in my life. Feel like you are understanding the material and getting problems correct on worksheets, do all the problems on the practice exams, go to review sessions, yet still fail the exams. I do not know what more could be done to try and prepare for exams as they typically have problems we have never seen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He generally has very good lectures, but sometimes when things get tough or when people aren't grasping the material, he does a poor job at explaining it differently. Some exams are very hard and you'll walk out feeling like you should drop. Everyone feels like that so it is really hard to gauge how you are doing throughout the semester.

Block is hilarious and the reason I wake up on mornings with chem lecture. Literally my favorite person in the world. He counts down the seconds until lecture and begins as soon as the second hand strikes the minute. He's fearless af and so cool. I aspire to be as cool as Dr. Stephen Block!!
Lots of homework and he's kinda pretentious, but is an ok guy. Would take again.
Despite hours of studying, Professor Block failed to prepare me for his exams. The exams didn't reflect the difficulty of the course.
Avoid the summer class. It isn't curved and test averages were around 40-60. The final is brutal. Block is a great professor but sometimes can be condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: great professor! Would totally take him again if he taught any of the orgo courses
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Block lays out the course material very clearly with examples for nearly all concepts. He uses clicker questions in class, so attendance is part of the grade. He does not waste any lecture time as it is all just straight chemistry and can be a little dull. Overall an effective, organized, and clear teacher with fair exams.

Best professor I have had thus far.  I fully intend on taking another class of his if he teaches anything else in my major.  Seriously, plan the rest of your schedule around  having him as a prof.  I cannot oversell how good he is.

Dr. Block is an engaging and hilarious lecturer. He loves to teach in demos and is always making funny side comments about everything he does. Lots of easy busy work. Midterm 2 is ridiculous. Class average was a 40 but it didn't matter because everything was curved. Show up to class, do the assignments and try and it's a pretty easy class.

I love Dr. Block. His lectures were always organized and clear and he explains concepts in a way that allows you to understand. His tests are tough and covers all materials including lab and homework concepts, but curves help a lot. He is quite funny and personable. Definitely knows what he's talking about. Study a lot and go to lecture for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Block so much that I made sure I had him again for 104. His exams are rough, even if you study a lot. The curve does help you out a lot though! I highly suggest that you get Block for chem. He has a great sense of humor in lecture, is quirky and really loves teaching to his students.
He is an outstanding teacher and easily conveys the material. The class isn't easy but if you try a decent amount you will be fine.
test are fair assessments of the material but challenging. lectures are pretty good, pre class, post class hw, and discussion help clarify topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I personally think Prof. Block is one of the best chem professors. This class was a LOT of work, but as long as you put enough time into the course, you should be able to get an A. Highly recommend! Taking him again for Chem 104.

Overall, Block was a great professor who cared for his students. The exams were difficult, but he offered a generous curve. If you put in the time and effort to actually understand the material, you'll do well.

I had Dr. Block for Chem 103. His lectures are very interesting and he adds funny jokes here and there so you don't fall asleep. Although his tests are very challenging, if you know the material well enough you will be fine. He is generous with curving and overall knows what he is doing. He is an awesome professor and I would highly recommend him!

Lectures were insightful and relayed the course material effectively, while limiting time spent on trivial tasks. In lecture questions helped gauge the classes capability in certain subjects, ensuring that he wasn't wasting time teaching material that the class already knew.

He's a great guy, he's super funny and therefore easy to listen to. He cares about his students, but makes a hard exam. I spent many hours on this class every week, but still found the exams very difficult. There's a lot of work that goes into this class, but most of it is pretty helpful. Those exams though...

Dr. Block is a good lecturer. BUT his exams can be ridiculously hard, if you go to class, discussions, pre-class work, and do your homework, getting  good grades on exams should not be as hard as it is. People with other professors had averages around 70-80s, Block's exam 2 the average was a 40. My TA said it was the lowest average he's ever seen.

Awesome professor. His exams are pretty hard, about you will really learn a lot in his class. The class typically has curve, and you will see that it is hard to get a good letter grade because your classmates are improving so fast. Can be a tough class, but you will absolutely learn more than your peers in other sections.
really good guy who wants his students to do well. his class is tough but it makes sure you know what you're doing. would definitely recommend, made sure I got him again for chem 104 next semester

Block is a good lecturer. He clearly knows his stuff on chemistry and is great at conveying those concepts. Pay attention in class and you'll catch his hilarious jokes. His tests, however, are stupidly hard, and honestly sometimes seem unfair. As was mentioned below, exam 2's average was a 44%. You will really have to work hard to get an A in 103.
He's awesome. Always helpful and really funny. His tests are more difficult and will test your understanding of the course. And with a good TA you'll do great.
He's a funny guy and explains things relatively well. He expects you really know the material though

Dr. Block is funny and personable, however when it comes to the nitty gritty, his exams are near impossible. I put in about 25 hours a week for the course and got 100's on the quizzes, labs, and homework - however the exams were brutal. It helps if  you have a strong general chemistry background coming in, but if not I wish you lots of luck.

Dr. Block is pretty funny and a great lecturer. Beware however that he will make exams stupidly difficult for hardly any reason and then give everyone an A or B anyway with the curve. Beware Chem 103 exam 2! Hardest test I've ever taken in my life - class average was a 40.

He is very good in lecture as he explains very clearly and easy. However, makes very hard exams that have nothing to do with what he taught or what we learned. If the class average on an exam is high, he will try hard to make it low.

I liked his personality but when I had an issue with my TA, Professor Block was not very helpful. My friend and I had the same TA and we worked on labs together. We had the exact same answers (literally word for word sometimes) and she would not have the questions marked wrong and my answers were marked wrong. Not happy about that.
Dr. Block is the best prof I've had a Madison.  He is a great guy willing to help if you go to his OH's.  Tests are tough but reasonable and he gives a good curve.  Overall great professor.

I really really liked Dr. Block for Chem 103 but I wasn't as fond of him during Chem 104. He's a good prof, but he doesn't give any practice problems or tests to help prepare for the midterms and finals. That was fine at first, but it got old pretty quickly. He's subtly funny throughout class.

Dr. Block's a great person. That being said, his tests are rough. The content is everything he's covered but he is just super picky and detail oriented. Also he grades pretty harshly on his tests. There have been times I got the answer right and received half credit. He's a great professor but you will have to work for that grade.

Dr. Block was a great person but his tests are never straight forward.  His tests are extremely difficult even though I would study for more than 15 hours for each test. I am not the best at chemistry and expected to receive at least a B in the class but even with all the work put in, Dr. Block failed to prepare me for his tests.

I sometimes wake up in cold sweats at night thinking about how Dr. Block won't be my chem professor anymore. Bottom line he was an amazing professor and if you have the chance to take him a highly recommend it.

Dr. Block is literally the best professor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students, even though he has about 600 of them. Put in the work and you will succeed. He makes hilarious, nerdy jokes that really make the class enjoyable.

His test are very hard and he gives no practice exams. You have to pretty much find your own study materials, and that can be challenging when you don't know what he could test you on. His lectures are very long and very confusing. I would recommend taking another professor for 104.

Block cares about his students. He tries to make lectures fun. The tests are hard, but graded fairly. The curve is also good. Homework and reading is average, but if you need to take Chem 104, take it with Block. He makes it as painless as possible.
One of the professors I've had so far. He has great notes during lecture which are super helpful and his tests are pretty straightforward. He's a great and funny lecturer.
I loved Dr. Block! Great lecturer and very helpful (he even cracks funny, cheesy jokes). Exams were difficult but I still enjoyed the class. Overall, I highly recommend Dr. Block.

This class is pretty tough if chemistry is a weak point for you. Block is awesome though and super cute. He has this quirky humor. The tests are hard because they focus on such small details. Studying is a must. The homework each week is easy but long. Uses an iclicker for attendance but you want to go to lecture anyways because they are important!

For a chemistry professor, this is the guy you want! His lectures are pretty entertaining and he writes things on the board so you don't have to scramble to copy slides. He's also young so he's got good energy in lecture. Chemistry is hard, but he makes sure he's clear and

I would absolutely take Chemistry 103 with Block. He is super clear about what is expected in the tests and if you actually take the time to study, you can get an A. He's easily the best general chemistry professor here.

Very clear lectures, always tells you what you will need to know for tests.  Tests are moderately difficult--averages are usually around 60-70% with a generous curve.  The class would be a bit fast paced without a strong chemistry background.  Only downside is the huge amount of work--online homework, quizzes, book problems, and lab prep weekly.

Dr. Block is an amazing professor. Obviously, chemistry is not very easy, but if you are willing to put in the time it is quite possible to get an A. If you are able to get into Dr. Block's lecture, do it, you wont regret it!

*Hello and welcome back to Chemistry 103 lecture section 6, I hope you're all in the right place* Dr. Block should be your first choice for general chemistry. He has built up a reputation as the best, and he lives up to it. Great lectures, they are mandatory to do well in the class. Tests can be challenging, but the curve is forgiving. Take him.

I LOVE STEPHEN BLOCK. Best professor I have ever had at Madison. He is very good at explaining the material and makes going to chem lecture something to look forward to! The tests tend to be really challenging but the curve is usually very generous!
Funny guy and class is easier if you read the book. Getting his help is key, too; he can explain things really well
BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Super nice and patient. Well organized lectures, he does memorize his students. It is lucky to have him as instructor.

Dr. Block is easily one of the best Chemistry professors I have ever had, and I don't even go here. I took this course this summer (summer 2015) and it was HARD. expect to work. Aleks homework will take over your life and lab twice a week was obnoxious. Tests are hard, so if you want to take this course over the summer... stop drinking and study.

Dr. Block is an excellent lecturer. He is very approachable and eager to clarify material for students. The exams could be somewhat challenging, but those who complete and understand the labs and assignments should have no trouble earning high marks. Easily one of the most amusing and engaging professors I've had this year.

Doctor Block is the best professor I have had yet. During lecture he writes notes on the board, provides examples, and overall does a very good job making sure the information is understood by students. His tests require a deep understanding, not just memorization. Overall, great professor with a good sense of humor.

He is such a great professor, and that is saying a lot because I absolutely hate chemistry. His tests are tough, lots of "Select all that apply", but his lectures are so helpful. I would definitely recommend him. Also, he has an obsession with fire ants, which is neat.

If you get the chance, take Prof. Block. He is seriously the best lecturer ever and is very clear in making the material easier to learn. He can tell when students are starting to get bored so he stops to tell a joke or story which makes the power lectures bearable. Definitely study for the exams, he tests knowledge and not memorization.
Doc Block is one of the great legends of the modern age. Take General Chemistry with him, do not think about it, just do it. He is the best, a true wunderkind of a professor.

Take Block for gen chem.  His lectures are very organized and he sets you up for success.  Funny, friendly, cares about his students.  Exams can be tricky and time intensive, but if you study you'll do fine.  Didn't use the textbook at all.  Excellent curve.  Clicker required.

Prof. Block has extremely organized and clear lectures, although I recommend reading the textbook prior to increase your understanding. He is super reasonable and fair with grading homework as well as tests. Super helpful in office hours. IF you can take Block, take him. Probably one of the best Chemistry Professors you could get.

Dr. Block is a god among men-He's truly amazing and a blast to learn from.  It is true that his tests can be tricky, but since the final exam average was a bit lower, if you did reasonably well, you wound up with an "A" in the class.  My advice is to do the homework, and look over your notes.

Such an amazing professor! I thought I was going to fail this course as AP Chem broke my 4.0 in high school, but I understood more in college chem than in high school because of Block. Made expectations clear & was able to toss a joke in once in a while to break the tension of an hour and 15 min long lecture. Great professor, recommend him to all.
The class was hard even after taking chem in high school for 2 years. His lectures are interesting and he is quite helpful. The tests are hard.

GREAT PROFESSOR! If I could take him for every chemistry course I would. He is hilarious and whenever you are about to fall asleep in lecture, he will get everyone laughing with his quirkiness. Tests are not always the easiest. Multiple choice is weighed heavily, and they can be a little tricky. But a great person!

Awesome teacher; lectures were worth going to because he made them interesting, funny, and worthwhile. He explained material very clearly and was willing to answer any questions and often extended office hours to help students. Tests could be difficult but not if you went to lecturesdiscussionspaid attention.

Great teacher!  Makes this hard class way more bearable!  Dr. Block is always available to help you and even stops in during lab to see how everyone is doing.  Although attendance isn't mandatory, if you miss a class you'll be sad you missed his witty puns, hilarious jokes, and interesting demos!  Tests are fair.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Extremely clear in explaining the concepts. Gives notes by hand on chalkboard and doesn't read off of slides, which I like. Class can be a bit hard but it's worth it if you're taking it with Block. He actually made chemistry fun to learn. Go to lectures, otherwise you won't pass. I definitely recommend him.

Best class ever, best professor ever, best experience ever. Block is a great person who clearly explains what will be on the exams and is very fair with the curve! Great class would do anything to have him again.

Block is an excellent professor and is super helpful. He's very young but that doesn't stop him from being a great teacher. Lecture isn't mandatory but there are clicker questions you're held accountable for. As long as you study you'll be fine.

Dr. Block is overall a very good lecturer.  He speaks and writes very clearly and is quite organized.  He likes to make students prove they learned the material rather than memorized so exams can be tricky (especially the final).  He responds to emails quickly and is always willing to meet with students!

Love Prof. Block!  Hated chemistry but he did everything right and helped me to understand.  His lectures were bearable compared to discussion and lab but I would recommend anyone to take a class with Block.  He has a great sense of humor and was super down-to-earth.

Best and favorite instructor I've had in my 3 years at UW. He's helpful, funny, witty, cute, and makes chemistry and learning enjoyable. Wish I could have him again. Never wanted to skip class. Thought I would hate chemistry but I loved it. Fair material, exams  aren't bad if KNOW (not memorize) the material. Do lots and lots of practice problems.

Dr. Block is an excellent teacher. Super clear. He was the cause of epiphanies concerning content that I've been learning for two years. If you can't learn chemistry from this man then you probably never will.

Dr. Block is a wonderful instructor. He truly loves teaching, and will do anything for his students. He is at my lab almost every week (5:40-8:40pm) and will even help us out on our lab report sheets. One of my favorite professors, for sure. His lectures are clear, organized, and have a little bit of nerdy humor, too.

Dr. Block is probably the best professor I've had at Madison! His lectures are clear, well-organized, and easy to follow. He's very helpful and really seems to care about his students. Exams are really hard, but the curve always helps. Absolutely HILARIOUS in class and it doesn't hurt that he's hot. Definitely try to get him if you can!

Overall and probably the best gen chem professor at madison, but the MC sections of his test will destroy your grade regardless of n how much you study or how good you are at normal multiple choice. I wish he would redesign his tests and give you some idea of what will be on them (he goes out of his way to not tell students what they need to know).
Wonderful! Very helpful and easy to understand. With a little work, the course was easy.

Dr. Block is fantastic! His lectures are engaging, well organized, and fun. His class is challenging and fast paced, but he is always available for help. Attend his office hours! He is young and energetic and very funny in a dry geeky sort of way. Also -HOT!

Professor Block is young, but knowledgeable in the subject.  Go to his office hours once and just talk to him if you have a question.  His tests are fair, but make sure you do the homework.  Some stuff will catch you off guard because the reviews usually don't encompass all that is on the test.  Definitely worth taking for intro chem.

If you're deciding on who to take chemistry with, Dr. Block would be a solid choice. Not easy by any means, but better than a lot of them. His three exams during the semester are very fair, if you study you should be fine. However his FINAL EXAM was a ripoff! I found that it lowered some peoples final grade a little more than what it should have.
The fact that this man is teaching chemistry rather than modeling underwear is strong evidence against the benevolence of God.

Best Prof. I've ever had. writes big, demos are cool, is a funny guy. fair grading. fair tests. energized. plays w/ liquid nitrogen sometimes and is awesome. TRY TO GET HIM HE IS THE BEST EVER. I could talk all day on how he's fantastic. he once said "Geek is the new sheek" enough said
Block is my favorite professor this semester. He's completely hilarious, clear, and organized. Do not even consider taking general chem with a different professor.
Professor Block was definitely my favorite professor! He teaches very well and is very clear. His exams are fair and he grades well. Loved him and he is really funny. Take his class if you can!

Dr. Block is the man. Clear, funny, and highly motivated to instruct. Dr. Block keeps the student interested in chemistry. Take him at all costs! TA are friendly and always willing to work with their students when Dr. Block is around. Highly recommend Professor Block, absolutely no complaints to be made!
The best professor of my first semester. Went out of my way to get him again for 104.
He makes the class really interesting with his dry humor
Great guy, explains stuff really well
Great guy, makes an effort to talk to his students, and provides extra assistance at the end of lecture.
Wonderful guy. Young, caring, and hilarious.
Dr. Block is awesome!  Lectures were very clear, and exams were fair.  He had a really generous curve at the end of the semester.  Take chemistry with Block if you can!

In all honesty, I've always hated chemistry (and I still do), but Dr. Block made it at least bareable. His lectures were very engaging, and I rarely wanted to skip. His exams were long and probably the most difficult I've ever taken, but his curves were fair. Funny, approachable, and helpful professor.

I’ll admit that I hate chemistry, but Block did a good job keeping me interested in it. I felt like I actually understood what was going on, which was nice. Lectures were amusing, and I never found myself wanting to skip them, and I really liked the jokes on the PowerPoints. I would totally take another class with him if I needed more chemistry.

Great Professor! Really cares about his students. Material in lecture is rushed through and its easy to get lost so ask for help when needed.
