Lectures are entertaining and he does cool demos as well as tells random stories that sometimes relate to material. Overall an awesome professor for general chemistry.

I absolutely adore Dr. Block! He's an amazing professor, and will tell entertaining stories about the most random things. I never dreaded going to lecture. He's extremely personable, and cares about you as a student. My favorite professor at UW so far!

Professor Block is the absolute best. He honestly cares about his students and wants them to do well. He is looking to do anything he can to help. His test are fair, but usually pretty hard. The curve is good though. He teaches very well and is extremely interesting. Hilarious too! He's very young and just the best.
Dr Block made lectures interesting and very well organized. He did great demos and always cracked a few jokes each class.
Lectures were interesting, helpful and well-organized and tests weren't too hard. Really good guy.
Dr. Block is the best chemistry professor I've ever had! He is so organized and is able to clarify every difficult details using simple explanations and demonstrations! Definitely recommend!
Dr. Block was great! He tried to make a couple jokes per lecture and had many demonstrations. I recommend him
Extremely Helpful professor. Makes lectures very enjoyable. Super funny. All material is covered in lecture, so going is important

AWESOME PROFESSOR!! Doctor Block is awesome at teaching the material and very clear. He is always willing to help and re-explain things when needed! Very helpful in office hours!! One of the best professors I've ever had! I wish he taught other classes I was taking. He is hilarious, courteous and approachable! Best professor, hands down! Recommend!
just take the Iclicker to the lec and study for the exams and you will be fine, the professor is great and I ended up with an A for chem 103 this semester, just take him and you will not regret.
Professor Block is awesome.  Thought I was going to hate chemistry going into the class, but ended up enjoying some lectures.  The exams are hard, but the curve is appropriate.

He is harder than most but he teaches very well. If you need higher level chem take him because the foundation he will give you is awesome. Taking him in 104 , I had to drop a class to take him. Enough said

He's a pretty good professor. At least in the sense that I learned something, studied for the midterms and final, got an A, and sometimes somewhat enjoyed the class. His curves is VERY generous. He makes jokes, they're not funny, but hey at least he tries. I would definitely take this class with him again given the option. PS don't buy the textbook
Amazing teacher, tries to make lectures interesting with jokes. Exams are not too hard and there is a generous curve. Homework actually helps with learning the material.
Great professor! He does a great job getting the material across, managing to be funny while doing so. Can't imagine a better professor.

Great professor! His lectures are clear and organized, and the tests are based mainly off lectures so reading the book is only supplemental. Tests are a bit tricky, but if you put in the work they're very doable. Funny, engaging guy- I would easily take a class with him again.
Lectures were engaging and very helpful. Tests were mainly lecture based so outside reading wasn't necessary. Great prof was surprised to learn it was his 1st semester teaching.
Very funny and engaging during lectures. Impressed after learning it was his first year teaching.
Dr. Block was an amazing professor! He was very helpful and his explanations were clear. He was really engaging and I loved going to his class.

Chemistry is challenging, requiring a large amount of time and effort. Block is super helpful, I went to his office hours and he stayed an extra half hour to finish explaining. I highly recommend him, and I specifically chose my 104 class because he's teaching it.

I'm not a huge fan of Chemistry but Professor Block makes the lectures interesting with his humor. He explains things very clearly and is very willing to explain things during office hours(very approachable). Tests are pretty straight forward and he teaches close to the book. I would take him again in a heartbeat!

This professor was great. Although the class is somewhat hard and boring in general, Prof. Block made lectures somewhat enjoyable. He was easy to understand and even quite sarcastic which was funny. I would highly recommend him.

Professor Block was excellent at teaching the material. This was one of few lectures that I could actually stay awake in. I read the textbook, but I knew of others that didn't and were fine. His exams are very straight forward and he doesn't try to trick us that often. Great class if you can take it with him! He'd be my first choice!
He makes lecture interesting and actually enjoyable to sit through a chemistry class.

He was great. Really funny, took time to explain concepts and i would have gone to all his classes even if i didn't need clicker points. Take him if you can. Exams are a bit tricky but you will learn a lot and the class is curved so at least 60% get a B

First year teaching, did a really good job. Makes you go to lecture with clickr questions. Fairly funny although not quite as funny as he thinks he is. Makes exams tricky. Try to know your stuff inside and out.

She is an extremely tough grader, especially for an elementary-level class. The readings were strange and lacked cohesiveness, and some were weirdly explicit. Overall, just an unresponsive and unreasonable professor
will never respond to your emails and it seems like she just closes her eyes and gives you a random grade, most unfair professor ever NEVER TAKE THE CLASS
Her grading was a NIGHTMARE. This is the first B- I've ever gotten at this university as a sophomore. I never thought I could get a B- in an elementary class. Don't take her class!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: might not be that bad if you weren't in her section but there are very few things to be graded on and everything was graded harshly
dont ever take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN! DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Harsh grader, seems like grades are just made up and assigned at random.

Grades on very few things and grades don't follow any guidelines or rubric, makes content very difficult and complicated for no reason. Very unaccommodating and unresponsive. Clearly favors certain students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take her class only if you want to suffer through an elementary literature class.

There are papers and closed-book exams with harsh graders. Don't take her class if you want an easy A. I don't know how other students were graded or how you would be graded if you took her class in the future, but I can say that I was graded extremely harshly, and I can't guarantee you wouldn't have a similar experience.

I had to pay $65 for “course materials,” but it wasn't even a proper textbook, just a low-quality packet that we were required to buy. The course structure itself is poorly organized, and the exams are weighted so heavily that even small mistakes can cause a major drop in your grade. The grading is extremely strict, even there's no extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very few things to be graded on so one small mistake could hurt you a lot. Lectures were repetitive and boring, but the material was a lot of common sense and easy to understand. Minimal effort needed to pass

The readings for this course are jumbled and unconnected. There are both papers and exams, and the exams require route memorization of the readings. Content on the slides does not match what Dr. Bow talks about, which makes it very frustrating to try and take notes during lectures.

Professor Bow is a masterful and brilliant lecturer, and presents course concepts in a way that encourages students to think for themselves, rather than her just giving you an explicit opinion. There is a lot of reading material, but the content itself is thought-provoking and engaging, regardless if you are interested in ethnic studies.

By far the HARDEST grader I have ever had for an elementary level literature class. I showed up to every lecture and discussion and got an 89% on participation even though the class average was a 95%.... not sure how that works. Test are easy and straight forward same with essays. But damn she is a hard grader. Idk id look for an easier lit class.

Professor Bow is amazing, she gave great lectures and left room for student thought to grow in the classroom. Although it is tough because of the need to memorize essays read in class, it is worth it for the cultural knowledge learned in class. The materials used in class were mostly graphic novels and essays but all great readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class because one of my majors is Chinese. I brought up China a few times in discussion (because I lived there less than a month before classes started for the summer) and was told in class right by other people that I made people uncomfortable. She grades very strictly and chooses favourites so be wary. (1st time i got a B in uni)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, clearly outlines expectations. Exams are fair relying on free response skills and brute memorization of material specifically on recalling context, author name, title, and giving small analysis of text excerpts. Papers are fairly easy if you consult/check in heavily with TA's in office hours. Lecture/Discussion graded on attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Harsh grading and impossible standards to receive all points on assignments. Seemed nice but did not learn from this class. If you're looking for an easier class to fulfill Literature credit I would not do this class.

Since this was an online course, participation and attendance were recorded based a daily reflection post & a follow-up response post. You must complete the readings to do well in the course. Professor Bow consistently gave very helpful and timely feedback. The entire course was engaging and thought-provoking. I would highly recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Always keeps the class well engaged in the discussion. Overall a class that is not too difficult if you keep up with the reading, and participate in discussion.

Professor Bow clearly knows her subject material and she choose her text well. The class was engaging and fun. She does take attendence which is part of your grade along with 2 papers, a group project, and a final. Read the text and you should be fine.

People are too hard on this guy. Very sweet aura, definitely cares about his students. Was he the best professor ever? No, but, he worked through many examples at a slow pace, and did his best to make sure we all were following. If you spend time studying outside of class, you'll survive.

The only decent lecturer of 103. Moves very slowly and thoroughly explains concepts at level that is understand by introductory students. That said, nothing can really prepare you for the types of questions on these exams. Still plan on doing a LOT of work on your own time.

I think Boldyrev is a fine professor who happens to teach a difficult class. While there was not a lot of lecture time for this class, I think the material covered in lectures were useful. It can be hard to know what content will be on the test but the practice test he sends out is very helpful for this.

201 is a 5 credit class, but they only lecture 2 times a week for 50 mins. The professors don't even make the slides and there is too much material in too little time. Exams make up most of your grade, and are all multiple choice with no partial credit. Even TAs said they believed this was a lazy way to test 201 students. This class is bad.

Real unbiased review. I've had it like hell this semester. Stas did not highlight what was important or the equations necessary for problem solving. Multiple choice exams are hard, making up a heavy portion of the grade. He's genuinely a good person; I believe the class is just difficult. PS: His accent is a little hard to understand his lectures.

This class was a nightmare. I am a good student, but the homework assignments and exams were unnecessarily difficult. Lectures were fast paced and difficult to follow as a result of the professor's heavy accent. This is the only class that has left me crying in the hallway at 2am despite my best efforts to perform.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he truly is a great professor that explains things clearly and cares about his students. Tests seemed easier than the practice exams.

Lectures were taken word for word from the textbook. 15-question multiple choice exams being the majority of the grade made the class extremely stressful. He is a nice person but far from the best physics professor out there (although I don't know if 202 could ever be good necessarily).

Difficult to understand, due to his thick accent and the fact that he spoke quietly. Did a lot of writing on the board, which was difficult to read from most places in the large lecture hall. Tests were difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Multiple choice in physics makes me want to throw up. Final exam for fall 2017 semester was extremely difficult, and not at all similar to the easy practice exams given. 1/2 the problems required concept weaving at an instructor level. Makes you wonder whether they deliberately try to make the most difficult exam possible just as a pissing contest

Gary is better but he's still good. He teaches the first midterm material and then a little bit before the final exam. Lectures are boring but content is interesting and applicable. Homework is doable and exams are okay.  Study old exams.

It's a pretty tough class, so you definitely have to pay attention and do the work to succeed. Willing to stay after class and answer questions which is very helpful. Your success in this class is going to depend a lot on how good your TA is.

He's a very straightforward teacher. It's not an easy class, but if you keep up, you should be fine. He gives out a practice test before each exam that is almost the same as the actual exam. (I took this class in the summer, so it was probably easier than during the regular semester.)
He talks really fast, but his lectures are really informative!

He is unclear and just reads off of the power point. He reviews the material from the previous lecture, but using the exact same power point slides and wording, so it's not in more depth or explained better, just more repetitive. Lecture is basically useless in this course.

Puts little to no effort into teaching the class. It's like there's an invisible man standing up there prodding him with a stick forcing him to lecture. He just stands there and reads off the slides. Homework and tests cover material we were never taught in lecture. Read the textbook during lecture and attend discussions to pass.

This guy was no help when it came to learning physics. The only thing that sort of helped was his lecture slides because it gave you the general equations. I stopped going to lecture 2 weeks in and ended up with a B.

This class is not easy. Requires quite a bit of work, and Stan doesn't make it any easier. Lectures weren't very helpful, but at least he has a fun, Despicable Me-esque Russian accent. Hope you get a TA that can explain things a little better.

Class sucks. His teaching style is pretty unclear and he tends to ramble on again and again about the same things while giving you no insight into what the tests will be on. Tests are 20 multiple choice questions, no partial credit. NONE. This is not how a physics class should be run, but it's not his fault. Likely is the standard for this class.

Lecture was useless.  Read directly off powerpoint slides and never actually worked a problem or even discussed how to apply the material to problems.  Exams not at all based on lecture material, making them tremendously difficult to prepare for.  Massively disappointing for someone very interested in physics.

I visited him in his office to talk about confusions I had regarding my scantrons, and he was very approachable and happy to help. Also would have helped me with learning the material, but it was so far over my head I didn't know where to start. Probably gets a lower rating than he deserves simply because he teaches a difficult class jointly with a less approachable prof.

Poor Stanislav--he really wants to help his students, but his lectures can be nearly incomprehensible. The material isn't bad, but it can be difficult to wrap your head around what he's trying to say. I hear he can be helpful outside of class. I do credit him with being in tune with his lecture and knowing when students don't get it.
tests so hard bro. not even like the midterms. that curve be super high. he a nice jolly chill guy tho always smiling. js the tests bro sheesh.

The course was ran very poorly. Lectures were a mix of typed out slides and coding, then homework was all coding, but then the exams were hand written questions. Made no sense. Why teach us how to code if we're going to be tested on solving problems by hand? Don't expect Piazza answers within a few days either. Nowhere to be seen before the final.

GREAT explainer! You can tell he is passionate about the topics and is a master at breaking them down. Also super nice, patient, and helpful at office hours. I learned so much from going to his office hours just once. He also made the 340 slides that other profs use so he really understands them and the examples used in lecture.

I actually think that Prof. Powers is very knowledgeable about stats and programming, and he's actually a good teacher if you listen to lecture and ask questions. The tests in both STAT 240 and 340 are very hard (and sometimes unrelated) compared to hw, and I do think it's odd to not release the curve until end of class.

Worst class I have taken in college. It is a complete mess. We do all of our assignments in R and then take the hardest exam known to man on paper -- we got 50 minutes to do it which was no where near the amount of time we should have been given to complete that monstrosity. Given the amount paid in tuition here, this course needs a re-evaluation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He makes the exams virtually impossible to complete and largely unrelated to the course material or homework. He openly acknowledges that past exams were poorly worded and confusing, yet continues to write them the same way. He also refuses to release a grading curve until the end of the semester (even with the exam average as a 50%).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Actually the worst test I have ever taken in my life. He is a pretty good professor, but the stat 340 curriculum needs a change. The homework has no correspondence with the tests and even knowing probability theory the test was straight-up unfair. The midterm average was a 50%. I would say the course teaches R very good, but the exams are unfair.

He just hit us with the worst test I've ever received on campus. This guys tests are near impossible. Nobody leaves the room until 2 minutes left on the test because everyone is fighting for their lives. Many just straight up leave their short answers blank because of the amount of time pressure this man put on us.

While he does care about is students and is very accommodating, he struggles to lecture in a way that gets the point across easily and quickly. I found the lectures to be tiresome and we didn't gain much from attending. This course was definitely made harder than it needed to be by the bad lectures, hard tests and test-heavy grading.

Dr. Powers is a standout in the stats department, especially compared to the other STAT 340 & 240 professors. He genuinely cares about teaching and goes out of his way to ensure students understand the material. Stat 340 is a challenging course that requires significant effort and study time, and I found the exams to be unnecessarily difficult.

I loved Dr. Powers's lectures and appreciation for the subject. He was very personable from the first day and I felt comfortable asking questions and supported in his responses. He is one of the more fun professors I have had, and highly recommend him for any Statistics course.

Dr Powers is a welcome exception to the rest of the stats department at UW Madison. Compared the other stats professor I've had, he cares way more about educating his students. He answers all questions very thoroughly and was able to answer inquiries well beyond the scope of the course curriculum. His exams are also written very fairly IMO.

Professor Powers is a great mathematician, explains well, gives examples... If you like mathematics/statistics you would like the way he teaches.

In my opinion Stat340 is slightly easier than Stat240.

Super nice professor, but does tend to go off on unrelated tangents quite often. The class is not designed well. Tests are largely unrelated to lecture topics and the final doesn't even have a coding portion, which is at least half of the class, and most of the homework.

Dr. Powers is an excellent teacher. He is very passionate about statistics and he does go on tangents but he makes stats easier to understand and fun with his light-hearted jokes. He is extremely accommodating and helpful to his students and genuinely wants you to succeed sadly STAT 340 is very poorly designed to make the student struggle :(

Powers is an approachable, funny person and a decent lecturer. He tends to go off on tangents that waste time but his explanations are solid overall. His canvas page has additional resources and is organized better than Bi's, so I recommend taking him for 340 if they are the professors teaching it.

While he clearly cares about his students, I don't feel like this tests (midterm and final, cumulatively worth 60% of the grade) reflected the course material we learned. Additionally, doing the homework and discussion assignments only gave a very, very loose understanding of the course material. Not sure if this is a problem with Powers or Stat340
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: good guy. will def help u out if you need it

This professor did a terrible job at explaining things and assumes you have knowledge of stats already. He is very smart and knows what he's doing but does not explain anything in the lectures even when they are 2 hours long. I took this class over the summer so it was very fast paced, but I hated the layout of the class.

He is clearly a very skilled statistician, however his lack of teaching and content creation abilities are apparent. He struggles to stick to a line of reasoning and often loses track of his own sentences as he speaks. His tests are simple but a quick 10 minute video can often explain what Powers tries to cover in 2 hours.

Brian Powers may be the worst math professor I have ever had at UW, and I have seen a vast variety. It is apparent that Brian has absolutely no idea how to effectively communicate and teach his class through lectures, and assumes you already know quite a bit of statistics. This class has guaranteed that I'll never take another stats course.

Professor Powers is most definitely a very gifted statistician, however he struggles in communicating the material in an effective manor. His lectures are defined by chaotic slides and tangential topics of discussion, often leaving the actual lecture material diverging massively from the material intended to be covered by the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was not very well taught, everything was easy to follow. The notes were posted, and they were easy to follow and refer back to when doing the homework. Maybe the best professor I have had.
he's great

Powers is a great lecturer, always willing to and great at answering student's questions, seems to genuinely care that we understood the material, would even use lecture time to answer questions about that week's homework, was very transparent about the exams, overall a fantastic professor. Also clearly enjoys the subject, which really helps.

I really liked how the class was taught. The homework, quizzes, and exams all closely followed lecture material so they were not difficult. Exams were open-note and online which was very helpful. Also, all of the notes were posted as well as the lecture recordings.

Dr. Powers is the best! He genuinely cares about his students and wants us to succeed. His lectures are good and he takes time to explain things when questions are asked. He is accessible outside class, active on piazza, and very understanding. A big part of your grade is from homework, but if you do it the tests are fair and not overly difficult.

I have loved taking statistics with Professor Powers so far. He has made statistics so much easier for me to understand. He teaches the material so well and is a very genuine and caring professor. If you're planning on taking statistics, I highly recommend choosing him as your professor. He is one of the best professors I've had at UW-Madison.

I was looking forward to taking this class, but I was unfortunately very disappointed. This class is hybrid, and the in class portion is often Excel based assignments. She gets annoyed when students ask questions. Exams are online and honor locked, and way harder than they need to be. She does not prepare students well for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's one of those young profs who makes everything harder than it needs to be just to be respected, but it doesn't work. The exams are harder than they should be. She is rude and disrespectful to students time. Weekly content doesn't get posted until like Wednesday night. I wish she cared less about difficulty because it could be a great class.

The slides are pre-recorded lectures that she reads through way too fast, so you have to pause constantly, which takes twice as long as the “estimated time.” She posts necessary materials late, won't give extensions, and complains about being overwhelmed—as if we don't have five other classes, work, and extracurriculars.

It is a hybrid class so basically you're teaching yourself. The textbook is more helpful than the slides are. She's not very accommodating with questions and doesn't explain things the best. Problem sets focus heavily on Excel with minimal guidance. The class is interesting but content is presented in a way that makes it harder than it needs to be.

Posts lecture slides on canvas but attendance is required to sit there and watch her walk through an excel activity that nobody can see. "doesn't have time to answer questions" even though she posts the answers. She is mean and seems like she thinks less of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. Doesn't write her own exams and questions come from a bank so there is no grading standard (one student could get an easy exam while another gets a hard one). The class is not hard, but since the tests do not cover stuff in class it makes it hard to get a 94 for the A.

She is extremely smart and a good professor in terms of learning. I enjoy her lectures. However, the exam felt like a joke. The grade average for this class can't exceed a 3.2 so she makes purposefully makes the exams totally random and barely related. We spend so much time going over main concepts and they weren't even on it.

The class isn't difficult, but the exams are filled with the most random/unrelated questions that make it feel like a trivia rather than something you actually studied. Quite literally any phrase in the textbook is fair game. Her practice exam doesn't prepare you for the actual exam at all. Better to ask Chat to test you than use her resources.
Does not look out for the interests of her students.

I could care less about grades not being rounded; this is university, not high school. But I've never had a professor this boring/bad. She refused to fix TopHat issues, just read slides, ignored exam questions, and exams included material not in the slides/book. She did very little and showed little concern, by far the worst prof in the B school
Exams were hard but you were allowed notes.

Won't change your grade under any circumstances, even if you're an inch away from moving up to another letter grade. Tests were pretty difficult and had many concepts included that weren't taught in lecture (super niche portions of the textbook). Discussions didn't support learning.

Unnecessarily hard and unsupportive. Lectures were unstructured and her talking made key concepts unclear. She showed no empathy when I shared mental health struggles after a loss, allows no grade changes, and the curve does nothing for you. Having gone through a multitude of semesters here at Madison I can for sure say she's the most heartless.

There are a ton of assignments that make up your final grade and they can be super tedious. Exams are easy because you can have a full sheet of paper for a cheat sheet. There is a TON of reading but overall probably the best marketing 300 teacher. Also there is 2% extra credit offered throughout the semester for filling out surveys.

Kristin is a good lecturer and you can tell she cares about her students and wants them to do well. The exams were honestly tough and sometimes big concepts weren't covered in the exams as much as I felt they should have been. The discussions were super helpful for studying and while the lectures weren't mandatory, it helped going a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: easy material, but read the textbook and know the slides as niche content is tested on. the tests are tricky, so study lots and do well on all other class work. she's a great prof and super passionate.
One of my favorites so far! She is so insightful and genuinely cares about how you are doing in the class. If you read the book, take notes, and make a good notes sheet you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a stick up her behind

Activities for points in discussion and one big ind. assign. If you read the chapters and understand them you will be good. The exams are online, in class, and you get one sheet of notes. Kristen loves mkt but lectures very fast and I go for attendance but focus on the book. She will use other terminology than what is in the book which is annoying.

She was kind, answers emails pretty quick, and is very helpful in her office hours. One thing is that she kind of raced through lecture, so taking notes was very hard for me. Another thing is that the exams were multiple choice, but one question at a time and you can't go back once you answer one. Maybe that has changed by now, but that wasn't fun.
Kristin made class very engaging and she was very caring! I really enjoyed her lectures. You definitely have to study to do well on the exams, but it's manageable.

Kristin is a very understanding and caring professor. She moved fast through the slides but it was very engaging. The class contained about 30 pages of reading or week. The midterms were fair. There was a 3% extra credit and a pretty easy project worth 25% of the grade.

Kristin was a good professor but it was clearly her first year. Her instructions on things were very confusing. Her lecture slides were also confusing, she uploading one before class and then a different one after. She was very sweet and caring about her studentsTests weren't hard, given 1 sheet of notes, all mc, and one big (pretty easy) project.

I enjoyed Marketing 300 with Kristin, it was an interesting topic that she was able to make creative during her lectures. I do agree that the PMP project could be reworked as it is very specific and not that useful. The group assignments and things done in discussion classes could also be reworked for the better. The exams are manageable if you try

Professor Branch was a very good professor for Marketing 300. She knows what she is talking about, and the examples in class were very interesting to me. However, the guidelines and grading were pretty confusing. And the lecture slides were difficult to understand if you miss a lecture. The exams were written OK, still misleading and confusing.

Marketing 300 is one of the worse classes in the introductory business classes, but Kristin was a great professor. She brought an unparalleled enthusiasm and knowledge to lecture and always made it super fun! The exams are alright and take a lot of studying and the PMP is a useless project but Kristin was a great person and great lecturer.

He was a good lecturer, but not very interesting to me. Concepts weren't hard to understand but lectures were painfully slow that I was uninterested in the subjects. Talked about the history of genetics, which was nice.

I just did not enjoy Bret very much. I found him condescending and slightly rude when answering questions. His content was also just not engaging to me. He was just fine as a professor but his content and attitude was just not my favorite.
Bret is an awesome professor! 100% recommend just chatting with him after class/at office hours, he's very helpful and fun and also just a great professor.

Dr. payseur did a great job with the first half of Genetics467. He was clear about what you need to know and was very good at explaining concepts. He provided practice that helped to prepare for exams (that were on canvas, being able to take them anytime that day was very nice). If you take notes and do the practice problems you will do great!
Professor that understands how the whole field works and what actually matters. Acknowledges the history and makes the content interesting. Very approachable as well!
A solid lecturer! His exams were much simpler than those in the second half of the class, and he explains things clearly.

Professor Payseur was a great professor. He really cared about students understanding genetics. Clear expectations about what you need to know, helpful homework, and willing to meet outside of class if you had any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good lecturer but tends to lean towards academic language in his explanations which can make it difficult to get to the base of what he's saying, at least when discussing probability. Seems to really care for the students, low-stress exams, and is always happy to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had professor Payseur for the first half of genetics 467 and I enjoyed his lectures! (put them on x2 speed because he talked so slow lol). He was organized and the tests were pretty fair. The class itself was a little more difficult than I thought it would be, and since it is not curved I had to work pretty hard to get my desired grade.
Taught in a way to peak our curiosity and encouraged discussion. Tests were low stress.
Super nice guy and definitely cares about genetics, but his questions are very specific on the exams. Make sure you know the trees and the forest!
Only assignments in the class were the quizzes- easy enough, helpful for studying, and the exams- tough. Lectures were pretty interesting. I didn't read the textbook and did fine.

I  really liked Postle but his class was very hard. The readings take a long time, at least an hour each and there are multiple a week. Without the readings you really can't get a good score on the exams. His lectures are informative but he moves quickly and his slides are mainly diagrams that he explains, but easy to miss details

Dr. Postle is great, especially if you like the course content! He is very passionate about student success, and is quite an engaging lecturer. HIs course flow made it easy to know what you were expected to know for exams, and exams were always do-able. My only regret was not enrolling in the honors section of his class.

Postle is so fun and has a great sense of humor. You can tell he wants you to understand the content. Exams were difficult, but very heavily related to lecture so if you are willing to put in the work and attend class, you will do well. Grade is mostly made up of 3 exams, but some quizzes as a buffer. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty chill professor overall. The exams were literally just questions from the online HW quizzes either verbatim or just slightly changed. Lectures were interesting, entertaining, and he cared about the class and his students. Only thing was he could not figure out how to record the lectures. Reading the textbook is really helpful as well.
Postle is great! Exam content is super lecture heavy, but readings did help to follow during class as the lectures can be a little disorganized!
Brad is awesome! He cares SO much about your learning. 1-2 review sessions for each exam, and always willing to answer questions.

Brad was very funny, knowledgeable about the topics, and showed interesting real-world examples! His lectures were often disorganized and hard to follow but if you study the quizzes and rewatch lectures the exams are reasonable. There are textbook readings that could be helpful but they weren't necessary to understand the content.

He genuinely cares so much about the class that it's wholesome, but its kinda hard to follow his train of thought during lecture. He makes slides very minimal and confusing, but has clear expectations. Quizzes are really the main way to study for the 3 exams throughout the semester, and additionally, reading the textbook helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's okay, obviously knows what he is talking about which is always a good thing and was able to make real life connections to what we were learning. Study the quizzes for the exams, as the exams are worth 75% of your grade. He can sometimes come off as arrogant or pretentious, but I suppose you'll have that in a professor who studies what he does.

Genuinely a sweet guy who cares about you and wants you to succeed! The lectures could be a little hard to follow, but do your best and STUDY THE QUIZZES and you will do fine. The first section of the class terrified me, but once I got used to it I didn't have any issues. Also I loved that he gave his smiley faces noses :-)
Mid honestly. Super dense lectures and exams were hard for me. Always thought I ate it up and would end up getting Bs or Cs. Not my most favorite but could be worse

Great professor, has a great character, super engaging, if you put in the time to study you will get good grades simple. 
The best psych class I have taken here for sure.
Very straightforward class. As long as you attend all the lectures, you will do very well. The textbook is nice for supplementary information, but all the information needed is in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is harder to get less than a B in his class than it is to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knowledgable, sarcastic, and clear but sometimes it can be hard for him to identify when students are struggling. Class is pretty hard but you get what you put into it. My tip would be to have AI generate practice exams for you based on the quiz questions. Once you learn the rhythm of the course you'll be fine, also no attendance required was nice

Very knowledgeable, enjoys teaching about the psychology. Often shares stories from his life and how they relate to the subjects we are covering. Only 3 MC unit tests that make up 75% of you grade (other 25% is free homework points). Very much about breadth of knowledge, not depth of knowledge. Very good overall.

Dr. Postle is amazing. If you are a psych major and are interested in cognition, take this class. Lectures can be confusing, so I find it easier to watch them on Kaltura, as he has no attendance policy. Exams are based on the lectures and quizzes, and they are very easy if you understand the quizzes, which he provides detailed explanations for.

If you studying using the quizzes he gives after each lecture and understand what is on them you'll do fine. 3 exams worth 75 percent of the grade, 25 is the weekly quizzes being done on time, no final. Overall if you are a good multiple choice test taker and are able to understand the quizzes you'll do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This diva was genuinely the worst experience of my life. Lectures felt as if he was reading out of a diary, but not a damn cohesive thought was in the room. 3 exams - 34 questions each, genuinely set up for failure. Words cannot describe the distain I have for this professor. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!!!!!

Brad is a great professor and is super knowledgeable in his field. I took this class as a 1st sem freshman after taking AP psych sophomore year and found it to be fine. Tests are all MCQ and only challenging because of the amount of material covered and not the best structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brad is an great lecturer his class is interesting and you can tell he really knows what is talking about. I mean he literally did papers on some of the case studies we use in the class. The only thing you should know is that he has three mc quizzes which are worth 75% of your grade in total (the rest being free quiz/assignments) they are hard.

He is super smart, but not the best at teaching all of his knowledge to students. His teaching style isn't great for the average student and his tests are very hard. Very important to read the textbook and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst class I think I've ever taken lol. I think he is a great guy and I like that he is able to have a sense of humor and the man is INSANELY smart, but just because you're smart doesn't mean you can teach. Not good lectures/hardly any slides for notes, ENTIRELY exam based grade, besides some quiz grades, impossible to study for.

Never posted materials outside of class, and in lecture, the slides barely had words to write down important concepts. This is problematic when we are learning about complex parts of the brain and a bunch of scientific jargon. When concepts came up on the test, it would be more helpful to have some reference materials (he has weekly quizzes).

Be ready to read a lot! This course is very lecture and textbook-heavy. That said, Professor Postle is easy to talk to and really helpful during office hours—definitely go if you're feeling lost (which I often was, haha). Would I retake this specific class? Probably not. But I would take another class with him, just not 505.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Postle is one of my favorite professors I've had at UW-Madison. I took PSYCH414&505, and while the material is challenging, he cares and provides many opportunities for students to gain a real understanding of the content. His exams are VERY difficult, but if you go to lecture, read the textbook, and study the assigned questions you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: super interesting content and the lectures were entertaining and captivating. Prof Postle is hilarious and engaging, but the class is graded on 3 exams and a series of completion based quizzes. Tough class, but highly recommend

This class was difficult for me to follow along with. I attended almost every single lecture but they never seemed to help when it came to exam content. The class is solely test graded and I never knew exactly what to expect on the exams. Not being curved, the class was very difficult. Professor Postle was very nice but needed clearer lectures.

Super interesting class but there is definitely a lot of content to memorize and be able to understand complicated concepts. He has a very interesting teaching style that not for everyone. He will randomly reference students or make dad-jokes which was endearing but sometimes awkward. Textbook and readings not necessary but help a lot.

He records and shares all lectures and shares slides only when something has a lot of information that would take too long to write in real time. It's easy to tell that he cares about the information he's lecturing on, but he can get frustrated when students don't pick up the less difficult content as quickly. Grades were limited to quizzes & exams

You definitely have to put in effort when it comes to doing the quizzes and readings. The lectures are interesting, and postle (although intimidating) has a dad-like sense of humor.  The class is relatively difficult, but if you are willing to put in the work, you can do well. Also tests are about 35-45 questions all MC!
Lectures are interesting and he's funny but the tests can be hard if you don't understand what he's asking for. Kind of difficult for a psych class but overall I enjoyed it.

Definitely a tough course as UW psychology courses go in terms of the complexity of content, and he'd often move through content on the lectures very quickly which was tough. To succeed in the course, All of the content on the exams is in lectures and quizzes(homework), but because of the complexity and density, readings are extremely helpful.

Postle is overall a very good professor. His material is interesting and he does not require you to purchase a textbook, which is a perk. His lectures were interesting and straightforward. Minimal studying is needed, as long as you do the pre-lecture readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's probably one of the worst professors I've taken at UW. His lectures are disorganized and he continuously takes moments throughout the lecture to stare at his computer. He's pretty nice and will work with you if you're struggling in the class but his "help" is not helpful because his exams are very difficult and wordy. Do NOT take this class.

He is a fine person, but I just don't find his lectures all that intriguing. Also, the wording of the tests doesn't test your knowledge of the actual material so much as it tests your ability to understand what he's saying. Uses very academic jargon which can be difficult to digest, and often there isn't anything explaining the term online.
The most unorganized and unprepared professor I've had. Just rambles/goes on tangents during lecture and comes off as rude in an attempt to be funny.
awful
Not much to say, awesome professor.

Prof. Postle is a nice guy in general but I am so glad I am done with his class. He goes through his material extremely quickly. As everyone else has mentioned, the exams are difficult, and it doesn't help that the three exams make up 75% of your grade. I would study my notes for hours and still get failing grades. Good luck. Go to lecture and work

Professor Postle really does care about his students but the content of the class and the way he taught is SO confusing. It wasn't even that the content was hard it was the way he formatted lectures- it almost seemed like he wanted to make it confusing. DO NOT TAKE !

I usually really enjoy anything psych related, but this was a class I dreaded going to every day. I really felt as though I understood the material, but I still didn't do well on exams even after studying a TON. Brad didn't know how to help students with studying tips and understanding material. Going to office hours seemed like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams are really hard to study for. The questions are more based on your ability to understand what he is asking rather than understanding content. The textbook is helpful but you basically need to know every single thing said in lecture AND in the textbook notes. The quizzes are helpful and it is kind of him to provide those as a grade boost.

Quite honestly the most frustrating class I have ever taken. His lectures make virtually no sense and his tests are based pretty much completely on them. He's very understanding and seems like a great guy, but the class itself was not worth it Would never take again.

Professor Postle's PSYCH 414 is full of deep and engaging materials that will help you truly appreciate the beauty of this field. The class can be difficult at times but is definitely worth the effort. He is willing to help students outside the class but may seem a bit arrogant and oddly humorous. Tests are fair (based closely on lecture).

Professor Postle is by far the worst professor I've had at this university. There's virtually no practice you get with the material; he always explains content in a roundabout way, and the material is very esoteric. There's only 3 exams, no curve, with weirdly worded questions & he grades very unfairly. Avoid this class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and sometimes dry, but if you take good notes and pay attention, you likely will do fine with minimal study time. Graded on three non-cumulative MC exams and weekly short quiz completion. Readings are minimally relevant. He hosts review sessions and posts his lectures online. His personality takes a little getting used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Brad's class was, without contest, the worst educational experience of my life. He is disorganized, rude and his tests are graded in a completely arbitrary way. Most importantly, Brad is boarderline abusive to his students. I've heard of multiple people who had serious anxiety problems after dealing with him. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

The hardest class ever. He gives you insufficient slides (that weren't accessible) for extremely hard concepts and barely anytime to take notes. When he goes on tangents, he rarely explicitly states the topic/concept so you never know what he's talking about. Textbook was practically irrelevant (he wrote it). Very pompous. Tests were unfair. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Postle has the most incoherent lecture style I have experienced at this university. Refuses to post lecture slides but lectures quickly and jumps from topic to topic. Many resorted to taking pictures of his slides. The readings rarely align with the lectures. So never miss lecture or space out for two seconds :D Exams are written pretentiously
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't posted online so attendance was mandatory. Brad would go on tangents about topics, so the clear definition of a concept was never given and you weren't sure of what you needed to know on the exam. Exams were worded weirdly which made you question every possible answer. Textbook reading was difficult to understand when from his tb.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He makes you read from the textbook that he wrote, which is too advanced for this class so it makes it hard to comprehend what you're reading. during lecture, nothing is ever clearly defined, and he can be confusing. the wording of the tests can also be confusing and difficult even if youre well prepared.

The class overall was pretty interesting, but way more difficult than it needed to be. He never gave a clear definition for anything, he always used a really roundabout way of describing things. The first exam was terrible, he gives a study guide but you have to think about the answers much deeper than what he asks to get any use. Reading helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Brad is one of the funniest professors I have had & uses good examples to illustrate lectures. You will have to take very good notes & go to office hours to understand the concepts central to the exams, which are often not mentioned in the textbook. Grading is strict & exams are difficult, but cog. psych is so interesting it is worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Brad does a great job of explaining concepts with definitions, experiments, and real examples, and he connects course concepts together. Lectures are enjoyable and thought-provoking. Attendance is mandatory because notes or videos are not posted online, but definitely worth going to. Online quizzes are very helpful and only graded by doing them.

Brad is a great teacher and funny. His lectures can be hard to follow because he dosnt post slides and just talks all lecture without slides. I've never done bad in a class but I did really bad in his class. His exams are super wordy and tough, I talked to other people in the class who thought the same. No matter how hard you study you won't good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tests are an unreasonable estimation of lecture and textbook understanding, and questions are phrased ineffectively. There is a lot of textbook reading (hundreds of pages) and lecture material is just as important. Brad's constant attempts at distasteful humor distracts from the interesting material, and his personal anecdotes get pretty weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brad is hilarious and is a very intelligent guy. The class itself is a little dry but he tries to make it more engaging. He requires reading and quizzes that help your grade. The only downside is the exams and if you miss lecture. They are pretty tricky and everything he says in lecture could be on the exams, so take good notes and do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The honors seminar for Cognitive Psych is comprised of reading something each week, writing a question about it, and then listening to him talk in a small lecture room for 75 minutes once a week. Easy 1-credit A but difficult to stay awake through on a Thursday afternoon.

If you have a neuro background, the class isn't too bad, but no matter how much you study (whether you're a Neuro major or a Psych major or anything), it's easy to get tripped up on his confusing exam questions. The fact that he won't usually put his slides online means you have to pay VERY close attention during class.

The professor and TA mean well, but I recommend not taking it if you do not have to. The three tests are incredibly hard and found no matter what I did I always had the same results. This class is interesting, but the motivation drained out of me as the semester went on. Definitely a class you do not feel accomplished towards the end.

I was disappointed in this class, because I was looking forward to it being a really interesting. Instead I was really turned off by his personality, and that made it hard for me to muster the motivation to concentrate. That, and the fact that the lectures were hard to follow in the first place.

This is one of those professors who makes test questions impossible to understand unless you're a genius. You really have to know everything to do well on tests and it's not one of the classes  where you can memorize everything. It's a super boring class if you ask me and I would not recommend it to anyone. And I'm a psych major.
All i can say is that he loves to use long words, even when it isint necessary. Not very clear on anything

LOVED this class! He is very interesting to listen to in lecture and very helpful outside of class. If you read and take decent notes, you will get a good grade. He holds a review session DURING class before each exam that basically outlines what you need to know.

He is a great professor. I highly recommend him. If you prepare well for the exams and attend lecture, you will do fine on the exams. He really cares about his students unlike a lot of professors and is willing to go the extra mile for you to be successful in his  class. Don't freak out at first about the idea of online labs, they are very easy and
Really hard class.  Brad is dry but does crack the occasional pretty funny joke, but usually tries too hard to make jokes.
hardest class ever. he is so full of himself and the tests are worded terribly. very frusterating, i wouldnt take this class
exams unfair.  lecture sometimes unclear
SO hard, terrible exams
Brad rocks my box
Good lecturer, although his tests are very difficult to understand.
would never take a class with him again if i didn't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: T Bone is one of the funniest and realistic professors I've had here. A lot of people are intimidated of him and that is literally what he is trying to do. He's trying to show you a certain type of person you may encounter in a professional setting and not let the pressure get under your skin. It's a safer environment to do now vs. in the office.

This is supposed to be an intro to consulting class and he teaches like you've been in the industry for years. He'll cold call on you, expect you to do a case in front of the class, and follow along his tangents about the news and various industries. I didn't like this guy and I won't be taking a class from him again.

Like other reviews say, he has no structure. He shows up to class with intimidation and rabbit holes on the agenda. His class feels very cutthroat, yet you're basically graded on participation scores only. It doesn't feel like he respects his students, and if his goal is to turn people away from the field than he's doing a GREAT job.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Tom for a different class and wrote a scathing review. I do not feel the same after this class. This is where he shines. Take him for this class -- he is a BEAST for consulting and is excellent. Funny guy, clearly knows his stuff and will get you there too. This class was great, if the pacing was not a bit weird (not his fault though)

Tom has literally no class plan/structure. He spent whole class periods just going down rabbit holes of news and then telling us we really should know this stuff for our future. It was kind of funny like I have no clue what he thinks we learned? As someone going into consulting with lots of case experience, his "cases" will not help you.

I would only take class with him again because he likes me. That being said, I don't think he understands how to teach. I think that he treats class like we are his employees without an HR department. I had to go to the Dean due to the way he scheduled exams and our finals. If you're not good at sticking up for yourself I wouldn't take.

If you want to get into consulting I would take this class seriously. He teaches the basics of the consulting process and does a lot of real-world examples in class. He will cold call but is only trying to get you comfortable with the uncomfortable. You'll have to do a case in front of the class. Tom knows his stuff and is a great resource and guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is super funny and passionate about what he does.

I loved Bunn! He has a great dry sense of humor, is super knowledgeable in the field, and cares about his students. You have to go to lecture, but they were very interesting (as an anthro major, I can see how others would think they're boring). He's a tough grader but always gives good feedback. I would recommend this class to any anthro major!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone who isn't an Anthropology major. Bunn's lecture slides are awful, you have to take notes on literally everything. However, he does provide a study guide/slide that literally tells you what you need to know for the exam. If you miss lecture you will NEED to go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 102 is taught by 5 professors throughout the semester and professor Bunn is the worst one. He is so boring. His exam is the hardest one and requires that you remember minuscule details. There are also essay questions on exams worth 50%. You must cite assigned readings without even knowing what the essay question will be beforehand.

Do not take this professor's courses, unless you're an anthropology major and you have to. His lectures have barely any words and mostly pictures, so you HAVE to attend class and listen to every word he says. Exams are overemphasized, you can barely read his hand-written feedback, and he is a relentless grader. His classes set students up to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he does! You can tell he loves the topic and is able to go into depth on every aspect. I will say due to the course I took, he had to compress millions of years of information into a months worth of classes, which did make lectures a bit rushed and quite a bit of reading outside of class.

Do not take this course. Your entire grade is based off of 3 papers, 4 exams, and participation in discussion. Exams have an essay part where you are expected to cite anthropological papers, from memory, each paper being around 20 pages in length. For an introductory 100 level course for non-majors, it was made way harder than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty dry and confusing, but he 100% knows what he is talking about. His section of the class is filled with a ton of information.
Pretty dry lecturer but seems like a nice guy

Lectures were pretty boring. He knew what he was talking about, just class was so dull and monotonous. It was a little difficult to study for the exam, but making a timeline helped visually to study for it.
Super boring, exams are only memorization and very little helpful instruction.

Prof. Bunn is one of 5 teachers who work together to run this class, and his section was kinda boring. The content itself is clear but the online lectures weren't all that good. Still manageable, but if you want to take this course, definitely take it because the other professors are more interesting with their lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bunn covers interesting material in his lectures and has good insight from his experiences, but I was glad that I could speed the videos up as he talked too slow for my liking. Be prepared to also do a lot of reading for this section of the course, with a lot of unusual names, dates, and places to make note of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bunn is very nice, but his lectures are incredibly dull and confusing. He lectures so dryly and in such a monotone voice that it is easy to zone out. He also has a habit of contradicting himself, such as saying something was true but 10 minutes later saying it was false. He does not really make the class interesting, and it is an easy A.

You can tell Bunn is interested and cares about his students. He sometimes says one thing about a topic then tells you 10 minutes later that it's is false. He assigned a few readings but they were just his research publications and not worth reading for exams. I would only have him for a professor for upper-level classes. Exams were irrelevant

Professor Bunn is obviously very knowledgeable in the field of archaeology. However, his lectures are extremely dry and I found it hard to stay attentive for the entire period. 321 is graded solely on 3 exams, and you need to attend lecture and do the readings if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a decent professor, just kind of monotone and boring. Definitely mediocre, but taking notes in his lectures should lead to good results.

Anthro 102 was the worst class I have ever taken. The class is extremely boring, and the exams are pretty hard because you are tested on the most minute details possible. Avoid this class if possible; look for other ways to meet social science/humanities requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I LOVED Bunn. He is an amazing anthropologist and a well-known and respected one too. Yes, his lectures can seem dry or boring, but if you are an anthro major or if you enjoy the material, then you will probably find it easy to pay attention. He has a dry sense of humor and it's hilarious to hear him lowkey roast other anthropologists in his field.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's fine but just so unorganized, and boring. The archaeology section just doesn't even feel like anthro and he makes it so boring to listen to. It's a ton of reading and the exam is definitely not easy and asks a lot of specific questions that you would only understand if you read the (very long, detailed) textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was 1/5 professors in Anthro 102. One of my favorites as an Anthro major, but seems difficult for those who don't have an Anthro/hominin/human evolution background. Not impossible, and VERY willing to explain during office hours. You will learn some cool things in 102, and I'm taking another class with him next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunn has a pretty boring period to lecture about in Anthro 102. He is the first of 5 professors in the course and covers a huge span of history, mainly stemming back to the arisal of early hominins in Africa. He speaks slowly during the lectures and the test is very easy (mostly objective with few short answer and an essay). Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super boring lectures about archaeology and the tests were very hard, covered a lot of material he didn't talk about in lecture.

Bunn is a decent lecturer and can get pretty dull sometimes. Do the readings even though they're long. His test questions are rather all over the place so you just have to study everything instead of being able to focus your studying.

The class mainly focuses on early hominins and evolution, not culture.  You're graded solely on three essay/short answer tests (not cumulative) and there's an optional paper for extra credit.  He lets you know what will be on the tests for the most part, but DO THE READING.  It's a tough class, but Bunn's a funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible, always seems like information is irrelevant. Gives a lot of information and you dont know what will be on the test. Dont take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bunn is a solid dude. He's been in the field for ages and really knows what he's talking about. Grades are based solely on blue-book exams, which was kind of a pain, but it wasn't bad. Lectures/topic is super interesting. There's no textbook, but there's readings online that aren't that necessary if you go to class every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bunn is a man that knows a lot on what he is talking about. Most of the things he lectures on were things he worked on during his career. Many readings are assigned but no necessary at all to succeed in the class. Material can be interesting

One of the worst classes I've taken. Bunn is one of the most boring lecturers I've listened to, and not to mention he contradicts nearly every fact he gives, or doesn't follow up with additional evidence which completely changes the conclusions. I DO NOT recommend this class, and this is coming from someone interested in the topic as a whole.

Anthro 102 is taught by 4 different professors (Bunn, Kenoyer,Kim, Clayton) who each teach about a specific location around the world. It is a very interesting class, but the lectures can sometimes be hard to follow if you are not an anthropology major. They call the readings "mandatory" but you will never be tested on them. Would take again.
Lectures are somewhat dry, but if you are interested in the material it can be kind of cool. Slides are easy to follow. Reading isn't mandatory.

Bunn is the best professor in the anthro dept. His material is difficult yet clearly presented. His grading system is fair. A's are not easy to achieve, which makes getting one all the more wonderful. Bunn manages to make complex ideas about human evolution and paleontology easy accesible to undergraduates. He also is easy on the eyes.

Bunn is extremely knowledgeable but also an extremely dry lecturer.  Do the readings, take good notes, study and you will do fine in the class.  Sure, the lectures are boring but he has a dry sense of humor and is super super knowledgeable. I had to take 321 and the effort I put into this class is exactly the grade I got.

Do not take this class. If you are an anthropology major take 112 and 322. Bunn class is terrible and he is also. His grading scale is outrageous. Do not set yourself up. It will be a headache everytime. You've bee WARNED

Because of this professor I am no longer majoring in Anthropology. He is well versed in his field and very knowledgable but seems arrogant and full of himself. Lectures are very information dense and can be hard to follow. An intelligent professor but not a class (or professor) I would recommend.

Avoid having this teacher at all costs.  He is a terrible lecturer, teacher, and test maker.  Put another way, good luck not always falling asleep during his lectures and even if you don't he doesn't tell you what to study to do well on his tests.  Even though he says don't read the book do so in order to do well.

If you are interested in the field, Bunn is the man. He is the epitome of what an archaeologist is. he is knowledgeable and loves this field. He will make jokes and poke fun at the material but most people are too oblivious to pay attention.

I didn't find Prof. Bunn hard to listen to during lecture. He is well-versed in his stuff. However, he talks a lot about his own research and doesn't pay much attention on the book. He even mentioned that it would be more beneficial to study the lectures rather than the textbook. My advice: Read the textbook!

I heard a lot of bad things about Bunn before I took the class, which scared me a lot. He was a pretty good lecturer though. He's quiet, so sit close and do the readings (even though there are a lot) and GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. His exam is mult choice and not bad. The others are essay and difficult, so be sure to ace Bunn's.

I think he knows what he's talking about, but lectures are torturous. He's way too quiet and makes everything really boring. It seemed like in terms of test material the things you learn in discussions are more important than the lecture itself.

Driest lecturer ever. Gives you study questions for the exam, but more material is always on there. IF YOU ARE NOT GOOD AT WRITING BLUE BOOK ESSAYS, DO NOT TAKE THIS TEST. That + hours of cramming was the only reason I got an A. I would never, ever recommend this class over 322 with Clayton. Take that for your archaeology requirement instead.

This professor is terrible.  He is a terrible speaker, so his lectures are extremely dull.  The only things that is worse than his lectures are his tests.  He won't tell you what to study, but I recommend looking at all of your notes and reading the book, although  he says not to read the book.

I was not a fan at all. I could barely hear him when he talked. It didn't seem like he knew much of what he was trying to say because his sentences were slow and choppy. Couldn't distinguish between what I should know for the test and what not. Total bore.

Henry Bunn is a fantastic professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable and is one of the best resources you could have to learn about anthropology. His classes are interesting and he is very clear and fair in what he expects of his students. One of the best professors at the UW and a huge influence in the world of anthropology.

Bunn is great in the sense that he has had a great amount of actual fieldwork, so he really knows what he is talking about. As a professor he was unorganized though. His presentations focused on his findings, yet very little of it was on the test. However, he is very willing to answer questions and is very friendly.
Interesting professor, extremely knowledgeable about his material. Test was relatively easy, definitely needed to go over all of the different topics in depth before the exam. Great sense of humor.
He's so disorganized and he jumps from topic to topic.  He also goes through his slides so quickly and is impossible to hear.  I am not a fan.

Lecture was okay, somewhat disorganized though (from the standpoint on trying to figure out what to study for the test). Test is a lot of memorization of dates and events (since it's archeaology). Sometimes puts a little humor in.
Bunn is no fun. :(
Henry is a great professor! He can tell if you're actually interested in anthro or if you're full of BS. He would do anything for a student he thought was serious.

Good professor, really knowledgeable about the subject. Names of sites, dates, and artifacts can get pretty confusing but the short answer part of the exam won't make or break you. Put a lot of effort into the essays, use lots of readings, and take into consideration Bunn's opinions based on his own articles!

Prof. Bunn is a very clear and knowledgable professor.  He tells you everything you need to know in lecture, including the questions on the exams.  He really wants you to feel as passionate about the topics as he does.  He also has a sense of humor.  All you need to do is show up to lecture and not be afraid to ask questions.

archaology is a subject that i am interested in, so the level of detail he was able to present was fascinating. learning from a person who still does research in the field and is moving the subject forward is great. too bad early human evolution isn't the most pressing subject to science

Bunn may not be the most engaging professor, but if you are a student who is actually interested in paleoanthro and arch then you should be able to see his knowledge and experience come through in his teaching.  Very nice guy as well, he's my advisor, only wish he assigned readings that were worth the time.

Unable to distinguish between core concepts and trivial details. Puts minimal effort into preparing for class. Assigns random, outdated technical articles that he aut****d decades ago, for the sole purpose of gloating over a few cherry picked examples of him winning some obscure argument against another equally self indulgent researcher.

He talks very softly, but he isn't boring if you pay attention. Reading the book is practically useless - don't waste your money. Write down everything he says and MAKE A TIMELINE. The timeline is what got me an A in this class. I got very sick of talking about strangely-shaped rocks and there's lots of studying, but he's not that bad.

Although I had this guy ages ago (pardon the pun) I just had to come and see the comments in the "new age" and lo and behold, NOTHING has changed!  So, he's still boring and still giving the same old detailed crappy tests he did way back when.  And despite his resume, he hasn't moved on to bigger and better things in his profession.  UW should boot

despite his "boring-ness", he was a great professor. he covers everything thoroughly and definitely knows what he's talking about. i barely studied for his exam and still got an A on it! i did, however, go to every lecture/discussion.. it's worth it though.. archaeology was very interesting and he was a really nice guy :)

BORING. Impossible to listen to, but you must to get a good grade. When you take notes, dont just write what is on powerpoint (USELESS) you must write practically everything he says. His tests are very detail oriented. Almost nothing comes from book. Hope to get a TA who gives hints on what to study

Bunn is horrible. SOOOO boring and doesn't even talk about the stuff that's going to be on the test, but it's not in the book either. You have no idea what is going to be on the test, and no idea what to study.  Avoid Bunn at all costs!

This class is taught in 3 sections with 3 different professors.  Henry Bunn was the 2nd professor and was extremely boring.  It was sooo hard to pay attention to him.  If you can avoid taking him as a professor, you should because he has a very monotonous voice and like I said before...I had a very hard time paying attention!!
Not helpful during office hours.

Bunn is great and has a bizarre sense of humor that you've got to love. The class is interesting but you must go or else suffer on the exams. Exams you need to know every bone, tool, cut mark, etc to get even an A/B. Beware this means lots of studying or one superb memory.

Tests are a game of guessing not only what he wants as an answer but what he meant to write as a question.  He gave us a studyguide for the essays w/ a 2 part question, but only wrote half the question on the actual test. He graded the class down for not answering the half he didn't bother to ask, saying we should have known he meant to include it.

makes interesting subject dull, tiresome. lectures are poorly prepared, to the extent they are prepared at all. has difficulty distinguishing between important and irrelevant points. copious required readings are a tribute to his own ego and little more. well educated on the topic, but does not impart this knowledge in a meaningful way.
