Professor Butcher's section was very easy! The exam is straight-forward and he does not try to trick students with his questions. He has clear expectations; he tells students exactly what they need/don't need to know.

He is the 1st professor in the 501 sequence, I thought he did a good job.  He wasn't boring to listen to, but generally professors pointing at a ppt all lecture is a sign of a lot of personal work to learn the material.  I thought I was well prepared for the exam, but wasn't.  Make sure to get a full understanding of the material which can be hard.

He is awesome! Best professor of the Biochemistry 501 sequence. He is very clear and he makes learning the material interesting. It is a great way to start out the course. His portion is about learning the foundation to what Biochemistry is all about.

Well organized lectures. Each concept is built on the previous one, so clear progression of knowledge. Explained expectations for the test, and the practice exams were very helpful in preparation. Basically, the course was so well taught that even though I'm an awful organic chemist I was easily able to follow along.
Clear lectures and doable exam questions, which are based on ppts and lectures. Read and memorize 2-3 days and do the practice exam. Then, u are good to go.
Very clear, great teacher, challenging iClicker questions, and a fair exam. I feel like I learned the most from this professor.
Straight forward. Clear. Fair exam. Don't bother with textbook. Slides are online with podcasts.

He taught the first section. Very easy to follow. Crystal clear. Appreciates anyone who comes to ask him questions. He seemed friendly for the most part. The exam was pretty straight forward. I didn't bother with the textbook.

BIOCHEM 501: Professor Butcher is a pretty good professor. His lectures are easy to follow, and once in a while he'll throw in a nice anecdote to help you remember a concept. Overall, I'd say the exam was pretty fair. Mostly based off lecture slides, so make sure you go over those in great detail.

Super sweet and kind professor! 525 is very challenging, but she makes the slides clear and logical. Even if it may be hard to get an A due to the (potential) department restriction, you can gain a lot!

Hardest class I took this semester. Do not let the RMP ratings below fool you, if you are not an elite math major, you will not have a good time. Not a lot of proofs, but the proofs are insanely in-depth and you need to know every little detail. HWs take a LONG time to do, and the first exam is brutal. You also need a 95 or higher for an A.

Prof Carla is one of my favorite professors in Mathematics(and Computer Sciences). Her ability to explain the difficult concepts in clear manner is inspiring. And she genuinely cares about the students. The course is theoretical but I enjoyed it a lot because of her clear teaching skills. And yes is super sweet too:))
The best math professor I have had. The class was pretty easy.
Awesome professor, she knows content too well and explains it in easiest way possible, and very sweet and accessible to all the students

Prof. Carla is an wonderful professor and have a very strong grasp in the field of linear optimization.The class, was super interesting because of her amazing content delivery and profound insights in the field of optimization. She appreciates student participation and always invites questions during and after class and during office hours.

Great professor. Courses were kind of boring because of its content but Carla tried her best to explain those concepts. She knows optimization a lot although with some accent. Anyway if you want to take this course she might be the best choice.
An extremely difficult course. 70% of your grade depends on your exam. The professor is nice tho

Overall a solid lecturer and exams are more than fair. Get a good homework partner for the assignments, study the proofs continuously throughout the semester and you will not have to spend much time at all studying for exams.

You need a deep understanding of the proofs and homework to do well since you aren't allowed a note sheet or textbook access during exams, which make up 60% of your grade. With that being said Professor Michini seems to care about student success and encourages students to ask questions or attend office hours if they ever don't understand something
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good prof. Knows whats she's doing. Lectures are hard to watch.

Really nice to students. Clearly interested in the topic as it's heavily related to her research. Knows the content inside and out. Homeworks were extremely hard at times though, but there were only eight of them.
Easily the most approachable Professor. Don't hesitate, take anything he teaches
The best prof you can have. His lecture style is like an inner monologue stand up comedy show,  but the way he walks through arguments is so clear and it makes the material so easy

He is the exception to the rule the lecture is boring. He's funny and all but there's something magnetic about him. Do yourself a favor and take his class and go to every class and just watch and listen. His lecture style is almost like an internal monologue and it's amazing how clearly and funnily he communicates difficult ideas. Don't miss out.
take his class u won't regret it! His class is very low stress and he does a really good job at making the material interesting!
Casey is an amazing guy who is very down to earth. His teaching style is refreshing, and I recommend taking any of his classes.
great guy fr

My goat. The only problem I have is that I wanted to take more philosophy classes after his but dint like the ones. he does such a good job at making really weird and difficult arguments easy to understand. Mad friends in his class and wed talk about class at lunch everyday after class

He breaks down complicated arguments and texts in a way that anybody can understand. The course is structured in a way where he helps you learn all of the foundations so you can think about the topics Hes really relatable and you definitely want to talk to him in office hours also. Love the cat content

Casey's lectures are entertaining and valuable. He is very lenient with absences if you let him know in advance and his lectures cover exactly what he asks on exams. One of the best professors I've had

The best. super chill about everything. generally a very interesting class. attendance isnt mandatory but helps answer questions in exams. there were two midterms and a final. all of them were take home and final paper was super short which helped me focus on other subs.

Casey is the embodiment of how every great professor should be. He cares a lot about both the students and what he teaches, he's charismatic, and his class is extremely engaging and fun. You'll never want to skip a lecture because the class is just that interesting, and Casey is an amazing lecturer. Highly recommend any class with him!

Lectures were very engaging and fun. Not a lot of reading or assignments outside of class. There were weekly discussion posts and discussion section was mandatory, but that was about it. Would highly recommend.

Casey is the best professor I have had, and he will most likely stay the best. He is super engaging, funny, and a great lecturer.  If you want to take a fun class with a professor that makes things easy for you take his class. All the exams were take home open notes, and were helpful to connect all the ideas from lecture.
The best class i could've taken he is so nice and this class was so chill. The professor is also so funny and makes class entertaining.

Casey is, in all likelyhood, the greatest professor you will have in college. Super fun and chill guy, often stays after class to answer any questions students may have. Exams are all take home and participation is not mandatory, but lectures are super engaging and funny so it's worth going.

Super chill. Greater Lecturer, although lectures weren't mandatory they were engaging and helped with the exams. All exams were take home, open note. Great explanations and discussions of philosophical topics.
Very chill. Very cute. Very nice.

Absolute chiller of a professor. Light workload and straightforward readings. All exams were take-home and open-note. I don't think attendance was mandatory, but the lectures helped with some of the topics.

Casey was a great professor who was super chill and wanted to make sure students didn't feel stressed about material or workload. Discussions were super chill, and attendance was encouraged, but I don't think it was mandatory. The finals are take home and you get a week to complete them. Fun class, and interesting material. Would recommend.

Byers is a funny teacher and is clear during lectures. He managed to entertain me for the majority of the semester. Take good notes and pay attention in class and you will do well on the exams. I recommend this class if you are interested in evolution at all.
Funny guy. And really, his tests aren't hard if you're willing to take good notes and study. The discussion section projects are pretty annoying though.

My first and greatest professor. He has a great sense of humor and makes the information very interesting. Even after lots of studying, his tests are difficult. If you know the concepts and are confused by the wording or just are unsure, ask him because he is extremely helpful and very patient.
Favorite Prof
Interesting man; but retired last year.

He's a funny professor but the tests ARE tricky! Literally, every question on the exams includes "all of the above" and "none of the above." If you are looking for a seriously easy geology class, I suggest GEO 101.

One of the BEST PROFS IVE EVER HAD. the class is very interesting, very easy, and he's hilarious. plus, what could be cooler to learn about than dinosaurs, evolution, and the origins of life on earth?
really great prof, funny and interesting (most of the time). another ridiculously easy course

Charlie can be hilarious, he can also put you to sleep and I enjoyed this class even though the tests were tricky. The geology department will be surely lacking without him!! If you didn't take him, you've missed out.
He is a pretty goofy and entertaining guy. Tests could be tricky, but mostly a straightforward class.
Best Teacher in my 5 years! Funny, intelligent- amazing class!
He is fun, and entertaining. Lectures weren't too bad. Tests were a little tricky, but manageable.

Prof. Byers is so far my favorite prof I've had in three years at UW. He loves what he teaches and makes boring topics seem interesting. He is very smart. His tests are more difficult than they should be, and sometimes studying doesn't even help. It's certainly not an easy A but DEFINETELY worth taking!
Evolution and extinction was probably my favorite class last semester. Byers keeps everything interesting and makes everything seem so simple.
Prof is funny, but class can be boring and test are quite tricky because of the odd wording.

He was an awesome professor! he made class interesting, and he was hilarious! The class was pretty easy, and so were the tests if you came to class and took notes. The TAs were AWESOME, if you can, get MaryRuth, she was so nice and helpful! The final was a little more detailed than i though, but overall, and VERY FUN class! recomend this class/prof
he's a sweet prof./very knowledgable.  the subject matter got very dry after our first exam...  but whatev, he's a good prof.

He's hilarious and lecture is very entertaining. Tests, however, are pretty tricky. You may think you know the material, but he likes to throw in "all of the above" and "none of the above" in EVERY multiple choice question. Sometimes throws in bogus questions, but that's just my opinion.
A great teacher.  Keeps class entertained.  Very easy if you take good notes.  Interesting subject matter.  Great science class to take if you are not a science major.

Awesome professor and really interesting class. Easy to take difficulty for granted because you basically don't do any work until the exam, which can be pretty difficult. Make sure to take good notes and don't zone out because test questions are one's you probably didn't cover that well. Hilarious guy though.
really funny and entertaining professor. you can tell he really loves his topic. tests are tricky but if you study your lecture notes you shoud do ok.

Funny guy, keeps things light and easy. Wording on tests, along with "all of the above" and "none of the above" being a choice for every question, makes class fairly difficult, but the material itself is rather simplistic and interesting.
He rocks.  One day he turned around and was wearing a Yoda mask.  By far the best class at the University.  Tests are tricky, but don't read the book.  Great class.
Funny professor, keeps it interesting, not extremely difficult, but tests are pretty tricky
Good class....the professor is so funny and the tests are tricky but arent hard if you study.
His tests are not fun, no tests are, but his have such hard wording and precisive answers that it's a real pain
No Comments
This guy is hilarious, and 110 is a great class. I highly recommend him.
I agree. Great professor, interesting material, non-drowsy lectures, a good one to take if you're a non-science major who needs those general education requirements.
Interesting class.  THE BEST PROFESSOR.  Kinda hard though.
He is knowledgeable, receptive to feedback and differing opinions, engaging, genuine, funny, kind, and interesting. He is one of those rare teachers who really cares about his students well-being.

Professor Cederstrom's awesome. His lectures were super interesting and filled with memes. The class enabled me to relate folklore to my daily life + have a better understanding of the communities I am a part of. There were a few papers and a final project due, but it's definitely manageable + enjoyable. Would 100% take it with him again :D

Marcus tries to make his lectures interesting with humor but they didn't help me much. The lectures aren't mandatory but there are pop questions that are either graded or for extra credit. The discussions are mandatory. This class has lots of papers but are very easy to get full credit. Definitely recommend if you want an easy comm b class.

Prof. Cederstrom really cares about your mental health and allows for paper extensions. The content is super easy and you only really need to attend lecture a majority of the time, the main content is the first few weeks then everything is building upon it. 5 main papers/projects that aren't too hard, but don't wait to finish them. Easy graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill two gen ed requirements. There are about 5 papers that you write throughout the semester, but he was the only professor I have had that has even mentioned the importance of mental health, so if you ever needed an extension for whatever reason, he allowed it. Passionate about what he is teaching.
Very easy class but the professor just seems bored. I would not recommend taking it unless you are just looking for an easy A.

Marcus is a really great professor. He is very interested in Folklore, and even though I am not, I found his attitude towards the subject made the class more enjoyable. He is a generally easy grader, he wants you to focus on the content and knowledge you gain from the readings and activities. For sure take one of his classes for humanities credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Don't even try to take notes because the content she uses on exams and quizzes is nothing that we learned. There were multiple occasions where I was asked a question on an exam and I had never heard or seen the content before, and I read the book along with attending every lecture. She uses irrelevant examples and they do not make sense at all.

Belkis is not the primary teacher for this class, and it really shows. She uses outdated examples in her lectures and isn't the clearest on some ideas, but the topics covered in this class aren't difficult so it is not that bad. The annoying part was the group project and paper due just before the final exam. Show up to class and this won't be bad.

She cares about her students but her experience teaching seems a little questionable. She has a PhD in Econ and clearly knows a lot about the subject. The class wasn't  difficult as long as you do all the assignments and attend lecture. The end of the semester was annoying because of the group paper, presentation, and then the final on top of that.
Cecile is a great professor. Explains the lecture very well. Very helpful all the time.
Worked with her for Directed Study. Really interested in making sure I genuinely learned material and concepts.
Overall pretty awful. Very boring lectures with examples that only fall into her field (biology). Lengthy homework, exams not too tough.

Ane is very helpful and obviously passionate about this material. While the material of this course isn't too difficult, the course itself was harder than I expected. Homework was pretty difficult and relied a lot on the statistics program R, of which I had no prior experience. It also seemed to be graded inconsistently or arbitrarily.

Best professor ever! Cecile uses extremely interesting examples, and offers real insight. She is very helpful during office hours, and gives fair exams. She also extremely attractive. So extremely attractive. And she has a French accent, which multiplies the attractiveness by at least ten. It makes a good class that much more interesting.

Pointless. Haven't been to lecture or discussion in over 4 months. Stats lab is essential for homework, which is worth a big part of your grade. Tests are open book, making it easy to teach yourself most concepts. Try to get the other 371 teacher, I've heard they're better.

Cecile is a sweetheart. Do extra practice problems because the homework isn't enough. The group project makes this class feel like 4 credits, not 3. She can be vague, so be assertive and keep asking questions. Grading was picky, they were skimpy on partial credit. And problems were worth a lot of points each. She uses the R project extensively.

the most adorable flake you'll ever come across!!  she simplifies anthing that can be simplified and information for tests is given straightforward in lecture and in homework.  the class is, miraculously, easy yet semi-interesting.
Such a boring class...but totally easy. Tests were open book and notes. Weekly homework helped with the exams. Willing to help if you needed it.

At first I wasn't sure about Alicia, but she is AMAZING! She went above & beyond to help/check on me when I had a family emergency and genuinely cares about students' success. Make an effort to contribute to class discussions one or twice each class period and you will get an A. Also, some of the readings are actually phenomenal!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I normally hate literature, so I was really worried to take a literature class in Spanish, but Alicia made it a decently enjoyable class for me. She does a great job of connecting with students and helping them. She also makes content very interesting and understandable. Attend class, do the readings, and participate, and you should do well.
Lecture 2 times per week, and homework is assigned a week in advance. She is very reasonable and will take more time if something is unclear. She wants to make sure all of her students succeed.
Shes really nice, but I'm a native speaker and the tests were so hard for me.
Such a sweetheart and really cares about every student. Explains everything very clearly and is an easy grader. Easily my favorite Spanish professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Alicia is so sweet and caring, I would take a class with her again in a heartbeat. You have to participate in class in order to be successful but she is a very easy grader.

Rather than provide a course packet, she forced us to print out every reading and homework assignment and bring it to class. This amounted to hundreds of pages by the end of the semester. The homework she assigned was super tedious and 90% of the time she didn't even collect it, meaning I could've written it in english and she wouldn't have known.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful professor, but sometimes she goes overboard on reading assignments. Having to read 170 pages of a Spanish book for two class periods and write is simply ridiculous. I would take her again, but for some of her bigger books she has you read you really need to plan ahead, and hope you don't have any other exams that week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: simply the best

Alicia is the absolute best! I took 3 of her classes and loved them all. Show up to class, do the readings/homework, and participate. Assignments are designed to facilitate our understanding of the material and she makes sure EVERYONE in  class understands. Alicia is the most caring, hilarious, and thorough professor I've ever had!! Take her class!
Honestly Alicia is my favorite professor so far at UW-Madison (in the Spanish department). TAKE HER if at all possible.

She's a wonderful professor who has made me enjoy learning about literature (in a foreign language, no less). She's Spanish, so for people who prefer native speakers as teachers, that's a plus. Honestly, a wonderful class. Everyone seems to really enjoy it and her teaching.

I love Alicia. She's a fantastic professor and cares deeply about her students. I wouldn't want to skip class because I didn't want to disappoint her. Take her class if you need a spanish lit credit!!

I am a senior, and she's my FAVORITE professor EVER. All topics covered in class are extremely interesting, and she makes sure everyone understands 100%. Cares so much about EACH student! Her motto is "no stress," and she's very kind and good-natured. tests are simple if you go to class daily. Make sure you participate every day... TAKE THIS CLASS!

I would recommend taking any and every class you possibly can with Alicia! She's a fantastic professor and got me to love Spanish literature. Considering I wasn't a fan of it before her class, this is huge! TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!! :)

Alicia is SUCH a great prof! Her classes are always engaging, and the content flows really well from one topic to the next. This class was especially straightforward, as there is not much literature. In lieu of a textbook, she assigns short articles, YouTube videos, and other material, which is then combined together and discussed openly in class.

First of all, Alicia is the cutest human. That said, she is also a great professor. I find literature classes challenging to begin with, so taking them in my second language is normally a nightmare. However, Alicia is a wonderful professor. She really makes a great effort to make sure that her students understand the material. Tests are fair too.

She's the most enthusiastic teacher iv'e had a UW.  She expects you to read and participate but the tests are easy, presentations are chill, and she creates a really comfortable setting for spanish speakers at different levels to talk.  Possibly my favorite teacher at UW

Amazing professor! While Alicia expects that you do the readings, she also understands if not all is understood. She highly values discussion/conversation and engages everyone. Her exams are easy, although the work/author IDs can be tricky. Oral presentations are laid back and receive ample feedback. She cares greatly and is all around awesome!
Take every class you can with Alicia! She is delightful.

I love Alicia! She really cares about her students & wants them to succeed. I had a rough semester & some personal problems. Alicia reached out to me & was an incredible influence. The class is a little heavy on readings (about an hour or two of prep per class). Exams are easy/fair. I actually enjoy coming to class! You will learn a lot!

I absolutely loved this class with Alicia and can't wait to take more of her classes. She really wants every student to do well and she's always willing to help or further explain anything. She chooses interesting material and is very enthusiastic about it. Great sense of humor, personality and teaching style.
BEST. TEACHER. EVER. I love her. Take all of her classes. She is the nicest, most wonderful person in the whole world, and super helpful. :)

Alicia is an amazing spanish professor. I went into her class hating spanish, but she is so helpful and wants her students to do so well that it made me change my opinion! She will do anything to help you get a good grade. Take any class you can with her! She's so nice.
Lowkey he is chill and gives good examples, but it was kind of hard to understand him sometimes because the examples were not really related to things we did in discussion.

Shiva's lectures were extremely hard to follow and understand, and he spent a lot of time doing proofs rather than clear examples. The class felt like I had to teach it to myself with him as my professor.

Shiva was less than subpar; you can't understand him and what he is trying to lecture to you, and if you can't understand him and what he is teaching, you are screwed. My TA also couldn't speak English very well, and I struggled. One thing that saved me was this website called Asher Roberts; I recommend it if you are struggling in lecture.
has good knowledge on the material and his lectures are very content heavy. Lectures are really straightforward and easy to follow.

He is a good lecturer if you have a good understanding of Calculus. Other than that, he had a little trouble explaining when people had some minor questions. I never went, but he does mention that he is available for his office hours a lot, so he seemed pretty accessible.

Definitely attend lectures unless calculus comes easy. He is not the best at explaining topics in lecture soI relied heavily on videos. For tests, if you use the resources he gives you'll be fine, they are mostly predictable. There are weekly quizzes, weekly homework's and modules, and each exam is 30% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I mistakenly submitted an incomplete review earlier so this is the final: I thought that Dr Shiva was a decent professor and I'd come out of every lecture understanding a good amount of what was taught that day. He does use the textbook(which I didn't use) and is a heavy grader on tests. The tests also make up A LOT of your grade so be prepared.

In my experience Dr. Shiva was a decent professor. I went every lecture and I came out of every lecture understanding a decent amount of the material. He does have an accent so be aware although it was easy to understand for me. I will say his grading is pretty heavy and the tests make up A LOT of the grade and he do
Class content wasn't horrible but explanations from professor were excessively complicated.
tests are worth a lot of the class, professor made things seem way more complicated than they actually were.
Final and Midterm2 were nothing like prior exams, but technically easier. Just super unexpected. READ THE TEXTBOOK!!

Professor Chidambairam was pretty decent. Most of the time, I could go to a lecture and come out understanding a good amount of the material. I did bomb midterm 2, hence my grade, but that was on me. Do not listen to others saying he has a thick accent; you can understand him perfectly fine.

The material itself wasn't awful, but the teacher often created his own way of doing things without explaining his reasoning, making the content seem more difficult than it actually is. Also, often explained simple steps while not explaining new content. Overall, don't go to him for questions, and self study helped more than he ever did.

Impossible to understand because of his thick accent. TA's were just as hard to understand. Your entire grade is 90% exams. Exams weren't the hardest but the class in general is quite difficult. TA grade exams so hard and take off points for the smallest things. Lectures are very dry and confusing.

To be fair, this class is generally difficult, but professor Chidambaram doesn't make it much easier. His lectures are difficult to understand and he goes quite fast. Most of the time discussion wasn't very helpful either. The test rubric was also harsh sometimes and unnecessarily deducted points.

Lectures were practically useless, the pandemic lecture recordings on Canvas were much clearer and easier to understand. Lecture is rushed through, showing formulas for a few seconds and then straight into solving, with a lot of missing steps and a lack of explanations. Questions were rarely answered directly. 87% of grade are exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class wasn't terrible, but it definitely took me time to understand the material at the beginning. (I haven't read the textbook once this semester) Do the practice tests and you should be fine. Once you get to vectors it's not bad at all.

This class was the bane of my existence freshman year. During the lectures I could not understand anything he was saying and would move on way too quickly. Even during the discussion sessions where I am supposed to ask questions, I was not able to because I could not understand my TA either. Never take this class unless you have to.

Lectures were basically useless and just went through examples, skipping steps along the way that made it hard to follow along. He bases his class off of our ability to read the textbook, which we have other things to be doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is probably the best professor I have ever had, very funny, amazing lectures, and fire outfits. The class was like an advanced sex-ed course which covered menstruation, hormone cycles, birth controls, gender, different sexualities, and much more. I took this class for fun and Dr Chadwick's personality made it very enjoyable!
She basically just read from the PowerPoint.

Dr. Chadwick is an incredibly passionate and knowledgeable professor. Her lecture slides are always well-designed, well written, and often includes relevant media, like TikToks/videos to prompt discussion. She's got great humor and wit, so class discussions are a blast & you learn a lot. Much reading, but each is broken down accessibly in class.

I LOVED Professor Chadwick. She was so engaging, relatable, funny, intelligent, and charismatic. Her lectures were super interesting, and even though the textbook got a little boring, she would find an interesting study/video to tie it back. This was her first class as professor and she knocked it out of the park!

Very organized, very knowledgeable, lectures are well structured and interactive, offers EC, fun discussion sections and the course content is sooo interesting. You learn something that improves your relationships and sex life every day. Some people saying tests are too hard/specific but if you're a real STEM major you'll sleep through this class
Super interesting lecturer. Exams are heavily based on readings. Cumulative exam in which 20+ chapters are tested. Nice amount of extra credit. Doesn't provide many helpful study tools.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sara is a great professor, and very engaging. The class material was fascinating; however, the final grade depends on 4 exams (the last is cumulative!!) an article response paper, and an essay on a book. So if you bomb an exam, it will tank your grade. The discussions are mandatory points, you only get one sick day, not worthwhile in my eyes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a new teacher and has some quirks that I think will work themselves out after the class has ran a few times. Slides are interesting and lectures are fun & she creates an open atmosphere for questions. Many of the exam questions come from the textbook. If I had to take her again I would but the discussions were the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chadwick doesn't want her students to succeed, she wants to make the course as difficult as possible. She made this class unnecessarily challenging through insanely specific exams. Any little detail from the textbook is fair game yet she barely covers relevant information during lecture. Averages on every exam

Great professor. Clear, engaging, and funny. The class is super material heavy and requires a lot of textbook reading that isn't reviewed in lecture which can be challenging. She is a great lecturer and wants her students to succeed, but the class itself isn't just an easy A. You get what you put into it.

I dropped her class the very first day because the syllabus was riddled with red flags. If you take one of her classes, get ready to never miss a day, because they won't record the lecture, let you zoom in, go over what you missed in office hours, etc. Beware, yall.

one of if not the best professor I have had at Uw-madison. So kind, charismatic, hardworking, knowledgeable and thoughtful! prof chadwick is very involved in her field and brings tons of field knowledge to lectures. Lecture is discussion based with some mini lectures by her and lots of small groups and full group convos. weekly quizzes+1 paper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was such a great professor. Very informative and really taught me a lot about sexuality in science. This class is very discussion heavy, so make sure to read the articles before going to class. At least the articles are actually interesting though!

literally the most amazing prof ever. HATE science, loved this class. prof. chadwick is so kind and a very fair grader, plus her lecture are extremely interesting and she always listens to what we have to say! she even deleted an entire assignment when she noticed that we were kind of stressed out toward the mid-semester point. take her class!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Sara is amazing!!!! Lectures were super personal and focused heavily on discussion, and she brought a ton of insight. Made me actually enjoy science which I did not think was possible.
Would not take this professor again, he was not able to explain concepts to students clearly.
Would not take again.  Agree with others, stay away from his class at all cost.

This was the worst class, wish I had never taken it.  Disorganized, lectures were rambling, difficult to understand.  And the  color theme with coordinating nails!  Save yourself from sitting through this.

Class was okay, but Professor Rycroft stumbles a lot in class and does not present the material in a clear way.  Wish I had taken from another professor instead.  Lots and lots of homework and tests are hard

Highly recommend mainly bc we rarely used Rudin. Lectures closely followed Kenneth Ross' book, which is very accessible. Caring prof and responded well to Piazza questions. Homework was very hard, with 2 weeks for ~12 problems. Exams had very strict time limits, but class was curved heavily (A:76, D:40). Practice exams closely matched exams. 8/10

Incredibly dense class, but he makes it work. His lectures are good, he uses a lot of graphs to help you understand different theorems and such. His homework problems are long and difficult, but they're (usually) fair, and they do a great job at solidifying your understanding of different topics and theorems. One of my favorite lecturers at UW.

Horrible professor.  Disorganized, difficult to understand, lectures were like watching someone stumble around in the dark and not know how to lead anybody anywhere.  It's hard to hate listening to a lecture in British accent, but somehow Rycroft managed it.   Please don't subject yourself to taking a class with Rycroft.

Very average professor, lectures are basically just repeating his slides. He's so good at what he does, it feels like a show off to listen to him. He can't make low-level students learn things, only high level students learn more.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Had me confused the entire semester.
Great teacher. Has a very good understanding of the concepts. Also, a great person.

Best professor I've had - insanely smart, helpful, and entertaining. The lectures go into a perfect amount of detail - only going into proofs when necessary, and giving great intuition on concepts. Homeworks were very fun and a good challenge, and exams were fair. He had plenty of ways to get help from him outside of class & he was very helpful.

Rycroft is very enthusiastic about math. While he tends to teach out of the textbook, he does it well and gives motivation for everything. Exams can be challenging but he gives out a lot of partial credit. The final project was fun, and he even gives less homework to let students focus on it. Homework can get very tedious.

Chris Rycroft gives concise lectures that are easy to follow, but the problem sets and exams are difficult. Rycroft is a godsend on Piazza and in office hours. Rycroft makes the analysis fun. More professors should be like Rycroft. Moral of the story: Rycroft.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rycroft is the GOAT. He may not be a pure mathematician but he knows his stuff. A lot of our homework used results proved in class so the proofs on the homework weren't hard. My only complaint is that the final was worth 45% of our grade meaning you could do good all semester but get sick the last day and get a B in the class because of that.

He isn't a super great professor, but the class also isn't super hard. I would really recommend taking it with someone else to understand what is going on. He rambles a lot and it would be a much easier class if he walked through problems. Also he mentioned he's requiring attendance next semester, so just a heads up.

He's friendly but he's a terrible teacher. He rambles a lot in lecture about random, unrelated topics and the textbook he uses is not all that good either. The one plus is that he's a very lenient grader. But if you want to actually learn and understand experimental design, you should take it with someone else.

I enjoyed taking the course. Professor Chien gave interesting examples of chip production and shared stories about statisticians. We learned methods like two-way ANOVA, Latin square, and factorial design. I suggest attending office hours, as he excels at inspiring thoughts, which gives you opportunities to explore and deepen your understanding.

Peter is nice and he's pretty good at explaining the course topics. He gives a lot of review material for the exams, so you can do well if you try. But, the exams did take most of the class the entire period, so be aware that you'll need to work fast. He's inconsistent at answering Piazza posts, but is very willing to help if you speak to him.

The course contents have already made no sense, and I am not sure what is the meaning of learning those things. His lecture cannot clarify things for me. Prof. Chien is not positive about communicating with our TA, so the discussion is not helpful. His tests are not capable to test one's true ability.

Peter not only excels at explaining statistical formulas, but also goes beyond that to impart a deeper understanding of statistical knowledge. This makes him stand out as one of the best statistics professors I have ever encountered. Additionally, he is incredibly patient and willing to answer all of your questions.
Prof. Chien's class was easy to follow and fun. He covered a variety of topics and gave a lot of practice problems before exams. Peter is an excellent teacher.

Peter is an amazing professor and lecturer. He makes his online class very enjoyable. He explains the materials in a clear, simple way that is easy to follow. He has inspired me to pursue the path of Statistics. He always makes himself available to answer my questions.

There were lots of positive feedbacks about Peter, but this semester he really did poor in teaching. Maybe it is due to the online instruction, he just talked through the problems in class and did not write anything down, which is very hard to understand. Also the grading is super unclear. Did not provide any grade cutoff for exams. AVOID!

Peter is a really nice person, but a really horrible professor. He is about as unorganized and ineffective as a professor can get. He wastes class time and leaves you more confused than when he started. His lectures and examples lack clear direction. He made a class that should have been straightforward unreasonably difficult.

DO NOT be fooled by the positive comments! Here are just a few of the many examples of why Peter is subpar, academically and as an instructor. 1) Failed to answer questions in class 2) Replied to questions in piazza only by saying "TA will address this". It is true that Peter is a nice person, but you would want to avoid him.

Do not take his classes. He's extremely unclear in his instruction, unavailable outside of class, wastes so much class time every single lecture, and when you ask a question he'll literally pick other students to give an answer rather than answering himself. Each exam question is also worth a ton of points with very little option for partial credit

his class may sound boring at first, but it gets better. the exams are almost the same as the practice exams, which is very helpful. for the exams you need to pay close attention for what he says in class, and get ready to read the textbook for supporting materials. homework requires writing R codes, lectures and exams will not.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Chien is really a good person and he inspired you to learn deeper in Statistics. His teaching is really fascinating and useful. I think everyone can learn some from his class. The exam is not too difficult if you follow his instruction and do all required material. He is really good at teaching.

Peter is one of the best stat professors I've ever meet. If you attend the lecture and take the class seriously, you would get an A easily. Peter would give you lots of advice about the final project. Of course, the best way is to talk to him personally about the project, which will make you in the right direction and an A.

His lectures were fine but I really learned the material by reading the book and going to section and listening to the TA. He skimmed project proposals and approved them without actually reading them. Mine had errors that I didn't realise until too late, a friend of mine was told to redo his project with a diff idea even though it was approved...
It wasn't difficult to follow her instructions and take A. Her class was very interesting.

Charo is very accommodating and willing to give students opportunities. She often even sacrifices her own after-class time to offer remedial chances to those students who did not attend the lecture. The questions she sets are all intended to help students understand the class content, rather than to cause students to receive poor grades.

Charo was the best professor I had. She was kind and made the lecture engaging. Class expectations are made clear from the first day. It is not a lot of work or a lot of reading. Do remember this is a com b class with com b requirements! Discussion attendance is essential for the A, not the lecture. She also gives opportunities for bonus points!
Nice class and fun stories

Took her class on The Tale of Genji. Engaging lecturer and is very clear about grading criteria. This is by no means an easy class, but if you do the reading and attend lectures, the work will not be too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a picky professor on absolutely random things, like citing a book with the date, and will give you a zero. The TA I had for her class, Max Kanne, was also absolutely terrible in the same way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are no formal tests or quizzes in this class, but there is a decent amount of reading. Most of the grade for this class comes from class recaps, write ups, and talks. Overall this class was very interesting and it is clear that professor Etcheverry cares and knows a lot about Japanese culture.

Charo is just an overall great person who clearly cares about her students. I had her as my discussion leader for The Art/Science of Human Flourishing, which was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. All of the information was applicable and the assignments were very manageable. They emphasize the experience of the class rather than grades!

Charo is a wonderful professor overall. She's incredibly enthusiastic, well-spoken, and caring. And while she is a generous grader, her class is by no means a cakewalk. She isn't afraid to assign a lot of reading, and expects a lot out of students. Put in the work, come to class, show you care, and you'll do great.

Professor D'Etcheverry is amazing! She knows what she is teaching and handles uncomfortable topics in some books with dignity, understanding and respect. Her lectures are extremely engaging and informative and will grab your attention if you are in class. She is one of the best professors on campus and I highly recommend taking a course with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The grading is contract-based, but the professor does give you some chance to earn extra credit. The coursework feels somewhat intensive with 2 papers, 2 talks, weekly posts, storytelling, and lecture participation. Professor Charo responds quickly via email. She also modified her schedule multiple times to set aside some time for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Charo was nice and actively tried to help students succeed in the course. The main problem though was that instead of actually teaching about Asian culture, she instead taught about how to write essays and do homework. This felt like a basic English course, where bibliographies and formatting was more important than the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She taught every day how to do homework in lecture instead of the Asian culture I was expecting. The various tasks she assigns are very demanding. This elementary course cost me a semester of study time, and it took me more time to study this class than I took my major class! Now that the semester is over, I don't know what I've learned!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Charo was a great professor for this class. The class has no exams, only weekly posts, and a few papers. There is a very clear grading criteria, and if you don't get it right the first time she tells you what area could use improvement and gives you another chance to fix it for full credit. There are some hefty weekly readings, but also some movies
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The biweekly Global Badgers seminar for the International Learning Community is small, low pressure, and fun. Charo is understanding and caring and leads interesting discussions and field trips.

Contract grading is great as you know what you need to do for an A on day one. The presentation responses are tedious but manageable and the group project isn't too much work. The lectures are pretty abstract and she can get sidetracked but she is really enthusiastic and passionate about the course material. Super nice and accessible to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Etcheverry was super nice and helpful. It was contract graded, which means if you do a certain amount of work it will qualify you for that grade. I thought this layout was stressful, in addition to the very unorganized canvas site. The class material was interesting, but I'd recommend waiting until in-person classes return.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was really cool and satisfied a Communication B credit. Our class was on a grading contract, so basically if you do all the work to a decent standard, youll get an A. The canvas page was kind of hard to operate, so just ask questions if youre confused. Overall really liked this class and the professor!

Charo is a great choice for if you just need Comm B. She cares about the material, and uses contract grading so you get an A if you just do the homework. The only tedious thing in her class is that there are a lot of focus points on citing work, so the class feels more focused on that instead of the actual readings and ideas from asian studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic about the course material. She is also extremely helpful inside and outside of the class and works with students to help them improve their writing and grades. Highly reccomend

The most committed instructor I had the pleasure of taking a course with. She will give you all the information you ever need if a topic interests you and will make sure that you succeed in class. She grades decently enough, kinda nit-picky but she won't harass you for it. The readings are long, yes, but read them and you will be rewarded greatly.

One of my favorite professors on campus; she faces her students with immense energy & enthusiasm. Although she is a tough grader, she offers a lot of feedback and WANTS to see you succeed. We've discussed much outside of class and even then she serves as a mentor and a friend, she really does want the best for her students.

She pretends that she is the most helpful and warm-hearted teacher in the world. She looks so nice but never explained the key points. She told you what to do and you did exactly what she asked. But every time she returned your essay with an undesirable grade. And she always points our new weakness in your essay that she has not said before.

She is just an amazing professor. I received a rather bad grade on the first essay assignment, she gave me a talk from which I was really inspired. It was a painful semester in her classical literature, but I did learn how to read. She is absolutely awesome
She is nice, but you have to read a lot. i would recommend this class if you like reading 20 pages of two articles and three chapters of the text book every week.

The best literature class I have ever had! The class is funny and the proefessor really makes me think. She teaches me how to read books and what literature is by reading " The Tale of Genji." She makes you know how history and politics background relate to a book in her class. And she is a pretty pretty nice and warm-hearted people. Take her !

Amazing professor. Grading was based on discussion attendance (lecture is optional), 3 essays, and a final exam. Used 7 books so it was a lot of reading but she has a great sense of humor to make boring books enjoyable. Final was super easy. So, I got an AB with a moderate amount of work.

Mrs. D'Etcheverry has always been my favorite teacher in the UW. Her lectures are amazing - interesting, sometimes comical and always passionate. You can tell she loves the material - it makes a difference. She's willing to listen and help. Fair grading (leaning towards the nice). Best in EAS Department in my opinion. Love her!
One of the best professors! Generous about grading, passionate about teaching and helpful in the office hour. I would definitlely take another class with her.

Very good professor. I love her class for her teaching style, with my only reason for frustration being that I'm not keeping up with readings. Have the stories read and be in class. Excessive note-taking not necessary, as she tests on general ideas and concepts. In addition, she sometimes shows movie clips at the start of class, which is fun!
Fantastic professor.  Care passionately for her subject matter and for her students. One of the best professors at UW.  The course itself somewhat muddy, not sure how much I actually learned.

She is knowledge and always willing to help, gives detailed suggestions on paper revision. She replies email very fast. She speaks very fast~I'm sure that's because she is so smart~Reading assignment is really a lot(especially for those non-English native speakers...), it's a little like literature class though it's not.

I loved Charo,but didn't care much for the class. Her lectures are captivation and she is a great speaker,however I feel I learned very little about Japanese Civilization and a great deal about Japanese Literature. Her focus is clearly literature,and I think labeling this course "Japanese Civilization"as extremely misrepresentative of what's taught

Loved her, loved her, loved her. Such a sweet lady. Very funny, very lively. She spoke so well you'd swear she'd rehearsed the lecture word-for-word (of course not the case). Very knowledgeable. Made a potentially dry subject interesting.

She took what might have been a very dry ethnographic course and made it interesting by relating stories about her adventures in Japan and by challenging her students to critically consider the material. The course reading complemented the curriculum very well, and was a joy to read. I wish more classes gave credit for reading Murakami.
She's fun..she can make a boring class interesting..work is ok i guess..not too hard
Good Class, a little too much reading but tests are very straaight forward.  Must go to class but basically if you do you will get better than a BC.  Easy 3 credit class if you put in any work.
Discussions were very engaging.  Classes seemed mainly like a discussion despite being a lecture.  EAsian253 was a low-workload class.
She's SUPER fun :D
A relatively easy course.  Lots of reading, but quizzes and tests were very easy provided the reading had been done.  Had a grand total of 3 pages worth of papers to write all semester.

I wohld rather taking notes instead of going to his lecture. Poorly organized board writing, never stops, difficult homework problems without any hints or instructions. 
Never take with him.
Subbed one time for my modern alg class, genuinely the worst lecture I've ever sat through. Goes fast, doesn't take a breaks, board is very disorganized. Don't take

Chenxi should not teach undergrads, but don't be too scared of his low rating. He goes way too deep into the theory, given what is on the homework on exams, but he cares a lot about his students and asks for a lot of feedback. His lectures are confusing, but he can come up with examples on the spot if you ask him, which helps clarify things.

I don't know what the other reviews are talking about, I've never had a professor ask for as much feedback as Chenxi. He also had a very lenient grading system and he is very sharp and can easily answer any question or come up with an example if you have a question. He is great at communicating and grades everything himself very quickly.

I took this class Fall semester of the 2022-23 school year.

The lectures were hard to follow and lacked a clear idea of the goal from the beginning. If you end up having Chenxi Wu I would highly recommend that you look in the Course Schedule and watch a Youtube video about the topic beforehand to better understand what he is trying to teach.
The class is pretty confusing already but he made it even more confusing

Very kind professor, but the lectures were useless. Stopped going after 2 weeks and did well on all exams except for the final. The lecture notes are easier to understand if you dont go to lecture and read them yourself. Use them as a guide.

Throughout the whole semester, I never learned any of the material that we were doing through him. Almost everything in the class I taught myself through videos online. Chenxi just goes too much into proofs, simplifying a lot of things and making it overall confusing. After every lecture, it just felt like I was more stressed than anything.

Avoid at all costs, impossible to understand and he teaches everything in the most complicated ways possible.  If I hadn't already taken this course in high school I would be completely lost.  Don't even bother going to his lectures you will leave more confused than when you got there.  By the end of the semester the lectures were 20% full

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. I have already taken this course in HS (Calc BC), but thought I would retake to get a solid foundation for my math major. If I hadn't already taken this course, I would be completely lost!! Makes lectures so confusing by not explaining topics well, and is terrible at answering questions. Take with Brian Lawrence if able to!!

Worst teacher experience made an effort to go to lecture but had to stop due to his poor teaching style. I recently went and the lecture room was just a fraction of what it was at the start of the semester. If you take him get ready to teach yourself everything because you will not learn anything from him. Waste of tuition money, seriously.

He tries and obviously cares about how well his students do. Unfortunately, he is godawful at teaching. He writes in super weird notation so even if you've done the material before you wouldn't understand it. I stopped going to his lectures because I got literally nothing out of them. Luckily the textbook was good at explaining things.

I was struggling so much in this class because it is very difficult to understand and after the final exam I had a C. I asked the professor what I could do to get some extra points. He sent me his address and said if I make him happy, he'll make me happy. How disgusting!

The professor is very caring and wants to help students succeed, but his way of teaching is not the best way to learn. He teaches through the general formula instead of examples and uses weird notation. Despite having already learned calc 2 in HS, I still was lost in lecture.

Grading policies/tests are consistent with all teachers that teach 222.
If you want to fail Math 222, go ahead and take this class with this professor.
He is extremely smart, but cannot describe basic calculus concepts if it killed him.

Don't take him if you don't have to, my professor got switched and even though I tried to make the best of it he is incredibly confusing 99% of the time and I left every lecture more confused than I thought possible. His work is incredibly hard to follow as well.

Professor Wu is obviously an incredibly smart guy who is very passionate about math. With that being said, I went to one lecture and switched professors mid lecture because we were doing IBP (one of the easiest topics in calc 2) and he was all over the place. I left confused even though I took it in high school. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can be a little confusing at times but I thought he was very helpful. Homework was relevant and useful. He probably gets a bad rep because he has an accent but his homeworks and exams were straight forward. Show up and study his lectures and the class should be easy

Looks like he tries, but the reality is that he's super confusing and does not have a sense for how difficult the material or the homework/exam is. Sometimes his answers to student questions may come off as rude or pedantic. Overall, one of the worst math professors I've ever had. Stay away if you can!

The good: he usually answers all questions, and usually fast. He asks for feedback. The bad: He is extremely inexperienced + has a gift to teach as confusing as possible. The ugly: he makes typos / numerical errors all the time. Sometimes serious/conceptual mistakes too. He refuses to clarify things if he thinks it is already clear enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I tried to understand his lecture, but I can't. My homework grade was about 96 (40%). My two exam grades were not high, 71 average. I got BC 0.3% lower than B. I spent a lot of time on homework and textbook. However, one-third of students got 80+. He did not use Honorlock. Maybe everyone is math expert.

Man if i'd known what I was signing up for in the second half, id have dropped instantly. 95% of the effort I put in was wasted. His lectures were confusing and textbook was the only resort. 95% of the hw didn't matter at al in final
Difficult to understand what is going on, but he puts in a lot of effort to answering student questions and is always looking for feedback.

Please avoid him if you can. Literally impossible to understand his lecture. Makes every content super confusing. Hard exam with nothing related to hw or notes. The worst professor I've ever had. You gotta teach yourself.

She's very sweet :) Her lectures were very fascinating and I learned A LOT. This class went so well I decided to minor in Asian American Studies. Her no-tech policy can make some people groan, but it's there for a reason + to help you pay attention and succeed. Readings are dense, but skimming will be okay since most of it's covered in lecture.

Professor Cheng is super awesome! Her lectures are super helpful and as long as you take notes and understand, you'll do well. Readings can be heavy, but most of it is unpacked during lecture or discussion. Overall a super good class and I would def recommend!

I enjoyed listening to her lectures, she made them very interesting! The class was overall pretty easy as long as you do the homework readings. Extra credit opportunities were provided, and attendance was randomly taken in certain lectures as a part of your grade.
Amazing professor - few tests and no other homework. Very interesting material

Lots of readings and if you want to do well you have to read it all. You are given all the possible exam questions before each of the 2 non-cumalative exam which is nice and there are 2 simple essays along with multiple extra credit opportunites. You will be called out for using any tech in class. Lectures can be boring/take longer then needed.

The readings are long and boring, but Cheng and her TAs made the class really interesting. I just wish we did more analytical study regarding the immigration stories, but, this is a 100 lvl course, so it makes sense for the very surface level and boring analysis
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A genuinely amazing professor. She is warm, sagacious, humble, and willing to cooperate with students to help them succeed. The course reader packet is thick, and the reading hours are kind of long. However, the readings are interesting, and you can learn a lot if you read faithfully. Take her class for your ethnic studies requirement or for fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cheng is so nice and her class is very clear. As long as you do the readings, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is a great professor who cares about her students and knows most of them on a personal level. Her cell phone policy is very scary at times and she is not afraid to call you out in front of the entire class. Electronic policy sucks, but it helps since its very lecture dependent. Cheng is very emphatic and truly loves her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: no tech lot of reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took this class for ethnic studies, I shouldn't have. She doesnt post anything online, her lectures are long and for the most part useless, she doesnt let you take notes on your computer (technology ban in her class), her grading system is arbitrary and horrendous, the readings are looooong, and attendance is mandatory and unmakeupable. Just bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Way too much of homework and reading for anyone who's just trying to pass the breadth requirements. Also no electronics during lectures and no extensions of any kind, so you just have to intensively copy notes and memorize. It's a heavy class with a heavy textbook you have to buy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She truly wants all of her students to succeed and has set the standard for professors for me. I got a bit lazy and stopped showing up to class and it was reflected in my grade, which was fair. So make sure to show up to class!

Interesting course, terrible professor. Vague to no grading criteria given for assignments, expect to be in the dark on what she wants for most of the course. She asks random rhetorical questions at points during discussion for no real reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is a great lecturer and knows how to present, although she at times becomes a little too intense. She has a very strict no phones in class policy and will periodically shout at students in the back of the lecture hall for being off devices. She seems nice and understanding however also scares me at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher. The course content itself is super interesting and the teacher makes the class awesome. She has first-hand experience with the material taught and is beyond capable of expressing her ideas. The class was really well structured and made it easy for you to succeed as a student aslong you put the work in.

I really enjoyed Professor Cheng as an instructor. She does have a strict no electronics rule and attendance is heavily graded. If you do the readings and prepare for exams, you will get an A. She also gives lots of extra credit! Would definitely take AA 160 if you need an ethnic studies course

Professor Cheng is great! I loved History 200. She's incredibly knowledgable, pushes her students, and asks critical questions. Also gives great advice and insight on things outside the class! I highly recommend participating for easy points, and it's not hard to do. She 100% wants her students to succeed. Prob. 3-4 hours of reading/class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng was a good professor and did things in our best interest, like giving us the exam questions in advance. Her class is very organized but no phones or electronics are allowed in class and there are long, sometimes boring readings assigned in the course reader. But the last two books we read were actually very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, and take this class is just waste your time. The TA is not helpful at all.
I took HIS160 in Fall of 2020 (completely online). Lectures and discussion were both synchronous. Not hard to get an A if you did the assignments, which were based more on participation than quality.

Professor Cheng was always so nice during lectures. She adapted well to the online format and truly wanted everyone in the class to get a good grade. If you put in the time and do the work, the class is easy. She even gives extra credit opportunities for you to earn points you missed. Really nice and easy to be in class.

Loved her teaching style and probably the best professor I've had so far. As long as you show up for the lectures and listen you can definitely make an easy A. The class is slightly reading heavy, but as long as you keep up it shouldn't be too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is a gem who really cares about her students. Knowing how difficult online classes can be, she got rid of all exams and quizzes this semester and changed her lecture to be only once a week. Grades were based entirely on weekly homework assignments. As long as you do the readings and participate, you'll get an A. Loved the class!

Professor Cheng is a fine professor, but one that loves assigning readings. These readings are important and need to be well understood to pass, as well as her lectures. However for a 100 level class the amount of effort you will put into receiving a good grade is not worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cheng is a really good professor and she cares about how you do. It's not hard to get an A as long as you read and do the study guides. She will give you review sheets with every possible question for the exam. Then, the questions that are actually on the exam are randomly chosen. Go to review sessions. I did not like the no electronics policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Asian American 160 is a great choice to take for an Ethnic Studies Requirement because it also covers humanities. Professor Cheng's class was pretty simple: if you read, try on your papers, and go to lectures and exam review sessions, you will get an A. Cheng also offers optional extra credit which makes getting a good grade much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good lectures, but they are early. Make sure that you go to the review sessions that she holds before the tests, because she will give you the answers for each ID term and short answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Made a 75 minute 8 AM lecture super interesting. Only class I never missed or slept through.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng makes a class usually boring class interesting. She gives many extra credit opportunities in a class where there is no weight, and gives out review guides and review sessions where she gives you the answers to the exams. Skim readings and go to review sessions and you'll get an A. Take this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extra credit adds 2.5% of your grade, Cheng's lecture may be long and not mandatory but she is extremely intelligent and makes you think thoughtfully, discussion is great and a good use of time, and tests are extremely easy if you go to the review sessions. Put in about 5 hours of work a week, and you'll get an A.

Professor Cheng was amazing and super sweet. She truly cares about her students. There's a lot to read in this class, but the professor and the TAs go through the readings with the students for better understanding of the text. They also help you with the exams, basically giving you the answers. Highly recommend taking this class.

Ms. Cindy Cheng was a great professor. She gave interesting lectures on a history subject that not many know about, and her comments and insights on how this history was very interesting. She also is very caring and loves her students, although beware if you pull out an electronic device during lecture or arrive late on paper turn-in day.

I really like this class! Professor Cheng is super sweet and makes the course really interesting. It's a fair amount of reading, but not horrible. The tests and papers are exclusively on the reading, so lecture isn't super necessary. She and the TAs will basically give you the answers for the exams and papers. Discussion is mandatory but very easy.

When she says no electronics, she's NOT bluffing. Tips: Do the readings or you'll struggle with the exams, go to EVERY review session because she gives you the answers to the exams, and attend lecture because she gives out pop quizzes for extra credit. Oh, and study a head of time. The material isn't hard, but there's a lot of material covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is really a passionate professor, wants her students to success the course. She is clear about not permitting cell phones or laptops, which is somewhat convenient and inefficient, but on the other side, this encourages students to attend class. The course itself is interesting, fun and inspiring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a good professor but has a few flaws. A big thing was she would stop lectures to call students out for being on their phones. She is somewhat stubborn but not to a fault. Her class is very easy to pass if you do all the readings. She doesn't grade anything so it's up to TA's. However, she is passionate and wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is kinda ditzy and can be awkward at times, but she is a good professor. She is passionate and truly knows her stuff when it comes to Asian American studies. There are two papers that weren't that bad and 2 exams that were non cumulative. She also offers extra credit. The TA's grade everything tho so you should go talk to them.
Awful teacher, horribly run class. TAs are even worse. Take a different course to fulfill your ethnic studies requirement.

Phenomenal professor! She's VERY CLEAR at the beginning of the semester about her teaching style, is very caring, and gives you everything to succeed. She lectures at at a good pace for note-taking. Anyone complaining about her is an irresponsible student with poor listening skills. NO LATE WORK!!! She says that many times; there's no excuse.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cindy's the bomb. She's very smart, qualified, and passionate.  She's interesting to listen to and a great professor. She wants you to learn and succeed, and is very willing to meet you at office hours.   One of the best professors and best classes I've been in.  Easy 4 credit class, but be ready to do the work. not hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She has enthusiasm  on what she is teaching but I can say she's terrible at actual teaching. She's so stubborn so that she would deduct 1/3 of your paper grade cuz u turned in  late like 2 minutes. The most terrible thing is she's suck at making ppt for lecture. You will find urself wasted 1hours just writing on notes. At last she's soooo verbose.

Professor Cheng is fantastic. Her lectures are thought-provoking and even though I only took the class to fulfill a gen ed requirement, it was still interesting! Reading the articles and going to the review sessions before the exams is extremely helpful; she gives the answers and definitions at the sessions. Definitely complete the review sheets.

Extremely interesting. Loved her teaching and her passion for Asian American studies. One  of the best professors I have had on campus. Has a clear grading criteria and is a generous grader. Lectures are interesting. Tries to help with grades as much as possible. Absolutely recommend her!

This class made me realize that the true tragedy of Asian American immigration lives on today. The decedents of Asian-Americans are oppressed to this day by having to take this horrible class.  Lectures are borderline useless if you do the reading, just go to discussion. Take another ethnic studies class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very interesting lecturer but exams are based solely on readings. Very easy class as exam questions are given beforehand and answers are given during office hours and lecture. Put in the effort and you will get an A.

Professor Cheng is the best professor I have ever had, she is so clear in her lectures and she gives a study guide for each exam with everything on it. There is a lot of readings, but if you keep up with the readings and show up to lecture, it will be an easy A. Prof. Cheng is ALWAYS there for help, and loves to get to know her students.

Not a super hard class.  2 papers, 2 exams.  She gives you the exam study guide about 2 weeks prior to the exam and chooses 4 ID's and 4 short essays to put on the exam.  Therefore you know what's coming ahead of time sort of.  She gives 4-5 pop quizzes, 5 points each that count as extra credit toward your final grade.  A lot of weekly readings!

Cheng is a tedious lecturer, often times saying the same thing over and over again without actually teaching much. She also assigns a staggering amount of readings that are equally tedious and uninteresting.

Great professor. Lectures aren't online and  2 papers and 2 essays are the only things that count toward your grade. However, she helps you a lot and makes sure that you get a good grade in the class.

Professor Cheng is engaging and cares about her students success. She is passionate about her subject matter and clear cut about her grading. I learned so much about Asian American history that I had never known and probably wouldn't have. Moreover, she is respectable and tries to get to know students that seek help. I would definitely recommend!

Not the worst when it comes to course material, but lectures are tedious. She belabors points and beats you over the head with "clever" cliches and neologisms. The class itself wasn't too difficult, but there's a lot of reading. I wouldn't recommend it for an ethnic studies requirement.
Great Professor. Take note though, no lectures will be put online ever. If you miss lecture you have to get notes from someone else.

The amount of reading for this class is ridiculous. Take SOC 220. For a 100 level class, the Cheng assigns many readings and long books, all of which seem to be due around papers, forcing you to trade off doing readings for papers. Additionally, papers must be turned in on paper and cannot be late at all, which she makes an odd obsession over.

Dr. Cheng is an absolute gem. She's very passionate about what she teaches. You have to write some papers and take a midterm and final. These are all super easy if you go to her office hours because she gives you the answers and outlines. 10/10 would recommend Dr. Cheng.
Lectures are frequently long and repetitive. This is mirrored in the readings almost perfectly as they will frequently make you stop and think "why am I reading the same thing again and again?"
You don't want this. "If you do the work, you'll get an A." False.
