Professor Cheng is great. Her lectures are clear and relatively interesting. My TA was awesome and made discussion fun and interesting. That being said, if you are looking for an easy ethnic-studies class, this is not it. Two 5-7 papers along with a writing midterm and test. Plus, there are 40-50 pages of reading a week that WILL be on the test.

This is the only class that I could stay awake in. And it's pretty interesting in my opinion. The only thing is that she does is push her opinions pretty strongly. Also she doesn't put lectures online and the readings are really long and repetitive.

if you were international students, it is very difficult because midterm and final review requires for good listening skills and there is not grading standard for evaluating midterm and final exam. For example, most of TAs have a little different grading standard. And, Cheng professors always laugh at something, student cannot understand it.

Professor Cheng is amazing because she knows how to teach, is passionate about the class, and knows her stuff. Readings are long, but are very interesting and beneficial. Exams are easy because ques are given to you beforehand. Every day I leave class learning a lot! Great professor, very interesting class, and an easy A.

If you put in an honest effort, you should get an A in this class. She gives you all the essay questions before an exam, so it is very easy to prepare. Readings are long and boring, but it is easy to go back and pick out the points you will need for tests. Recommend for ethnic studies.
Pretty boring class but extremely easy. Cindy provides all the questions that will be on the exams. Papers are graded generously.

Class is a joke. Incredibly easy; if you get below an AB, you clearly did not try in the class. Getting extra credit is crucial to getting an A, so make sure you try your best to do that. Just do a thorough job on the study guides that she gives you and try on the papers and you'll ace the class.

The readings are super dry and long as mentioned. However, I found the class to be quite interesting. Don't hesitate to speak with TAs and/or Prof. Cheng for essay help. They are very willing and very helpful. Exams are great because she gives you exactly what you need to study.

Professor Cheng is helpful and nice. She always likes to give you wonderful suggestions to help you develop your paper, as well as answering questions. She will give you the about 20 questions and choose 7 of them in each exam. As long as you attend class, take notes and read books, you will earn a A. Dennis is my TA. I recommend him to you.Nice!

She is very friendly and nice. The only bad thing about the class is the loooong, boring weekly readings and having power lectures because after the first 50 minutes of only listening to her talking and taking notes you start zoning out.

I really enjoyed Cindy. Young and lively. Left the class very interested in topic. She made the class interesting. Readings are very bland and long. Discussions are pointless but manditory. Tests are blue book essays but she gives you all the possible questions a head of time. Lecture attendence is manditory for a good grade.

Although she gives you a study guide with the questions, she is just way to annoying and boring to give a good score.  She laughs about everything which and just looks foolish.  The readings are the worst, most boring pieces of literature I've  ever seen! Plus, you need to read all of them for the test! Only take her if you like LONG boring text!

Good professor. Reading is long and boring and you'll be tested on it. Tests weren't bad because she'd give you the possible questions beforehand and pick some and put them on the test. The hard part was reading the really boring and dry course reader.

Professor Cheng was the best professor that I have ever had. I came into the class with very low interest and left with a very high interest. This is definitely the best ethnic studies option out there. The exams are very straightforward as long as you put the time in to plan your answers before the exam. Take this class. You will not regret it.

Good for ethnic studies. The Course reader is thick and literally dense. The pop quizzes are good and there's plenty of extra credit. She's easy to talk to but very repetitive of herself. If you do everything right you can get %50 on the final and still get an A. She cares about the subject and the students. She's also a very fine looking woman.

Professor Cheng was a delightful professor who truly cares about the hard times of Asian Americans throughout history in America.  If you're looking for an easy ethnic studies course with lecture attendance optional, this is it.  I had no interest in anything to do with asians and managed to pull of an A with MINIMAL effort.  Go Cindy Cheng!

She is VERY enthusiastic, clear, and helpful. However, in my class, she covered what is at most 10 minutes worth of material in 75 minute lectures, which made for easy but very repetitive sessions. She is friendly with students; as long as the painfully repeated instructions are followed, it is easy to get an A. As indicated, she is indeed a babe.

Professor Cheng is great! She really likes what she teaches and is always loose and has fun with the material. She is also more than happy to help you with your paper. She holds a review before the test and tells you exactly how to answer as many questions as you can get through as possible. Also do your readings and this is an easy A.

She gives awesome lectures, makes you really interested in the subject matter by teaching it in easy-to-digest bits. Shows lots of videos. Exams aren't that hard as long as you attend class, def. can get an A. Very approachable during office hours. One of my favorite professors so far!
So nice, and really helpful. Just go to lecture and read and you will get an A!

Definitely not an easy class, she is a very tough but fair grader and explained why I got points off. Previously I have struggled a lot with public speaking and giving presentations, but because of this class and her teaching I was able to overcome that. I thought it was going to be a useless class but it ended up being one of the most useful.

Professor Poe is an engaging and effective lecturer, and I genuinely learned a lot from her course. However, her grading is quite harsh, which sometimes made the effort I put into the class feel pointless. I would certainly take another course with her if grading were not such a significant factor.

Cindy is a great lecturer who understands the importance of what she teaches. She clearly puts a lot of effort into putting lesson plans together and teaches effectively. People get upset that a writing class isn't significantly easier than an engineering class. Take this class seriously, put in some effort, pay attention, and you'll be fine.

The only reason why Cindy has bad ratings is because she has actual standards. If you put in above minimal effort into her class you will do fine. She is a great lecturer and gives valuable feedback on assignments.
Try to get a diff professor, otherwise expect a bad grade.

She has a low grade average for 397 and grades everything more severely than other professors teaching the course. Most feedback is arbitrary and is written around how she doesn't understand technical topics that are the basis of introductory courses here.
Grades based on how she feels about you as a student. Offers feedback but does not reward the use of it.
Did not expect a 397 professor to be this rigorous!
honeslty the worst professor i have had

He is passionate about culture and Spanish speaking opportunities in the city. He is very educated about literature and linguistics. He is caring and reliable for helping each passionate and motivated student´s success. I enjoyed talking and learning interactively, but some Americans prefer rigid outlines instead.

Arsenio is pretty personable. He rather talk about culture and happening topics that the actual class work. He does favor students, accepts late homework, and takes attendance but do not take advantage of his leniency because he will notice. Try to be on his good side and you will probably get a good grade.

Arsenio was my TA for Spanish 223...I strongly disliked him. In discussion we hardly EVER discussed lecture material, just talked about "culture."  He called on the same 3-4 people in my discussion, giving no one else a chance to earn participation.  Definitely favors people.  Extremely picky with essays, but doesn't give advice on how to improve.

First off, Arsenio is a spanish speaking native from Cuba- so if your going to complain about having a spanish speaker to listen to- dont take him. However, if you want your Spanish abilities to improve- I advise you to take Arsenio. I had him as a TA for 223, and I really enjoyed his class. He may speak quickly, but it helped me pronounce better!

Avoid Arsenio!  I love Spanish, but this class was a HUGE waste of my time!  Arsenio is really nice, but I would rather go to the pub with him than have him as a teacher.  DUE DATES CHANGE ALL THE TIME.  LOTS of busy work, but at least it was easy.  You'll need to learn everything on your own time outside of class to succeed.

Arsenio is a terrible teacher. Avoid him at all costs. I liked spanish and was good at it. I am now not taking anymore spanish. He is unorganized and unclear. He's a nice guy but is just a terrible teacher. He is very willing to meet for help, but a lot of the times he doesnt help at all. He doesn't understand not everyone is a native speaker.
HE IS REALLY HELPFUL TO ME...BUT NOT TO EVERYONE

If you're hoping to improve your Spanish, you're in for a big disappointment. While Arsenio is relatively likable, he is unclear about both class expectations and due dates. Arsenio made me seriously reconsider Spanish as a major; thankfully, not all classes are as bad as his.

Easily the worst teacher I've ever had.Hardly teaches anything in class,and expects you to learn everything from the book.On exams,we even had vocab that wasn't in the book.He tried to explain things in English, which didn't help since he can't speak English very well and has a strong accent.Very unclear grading policy, esp. on written assignments.
He's a fun teacher and he genuinely wants his students to do well.  He gets really excited about teaching and his class isn't hard as long as you do the homework.

You don't do much in class, he doesn't teach and than expects you to learn it all on your own.  Always changes due dates and doesn't give much warning for exam dates.  Corrects a lot on papers, but only explains  his marks if you go office hours where I have had to wait at least an hour almost everytime.  Plus accent is hard to understand.

This is definitely a class where you don't do much.  There is no learning involved, and minimal review.  The due dates are always changed, and most of the time people don't know what is going on.  On the plus side, if you go to office hours he will help you a ton, and you will probably get a fair grade.  Be prepared to talk in class!

If you're looking for a class where you sit around and do nothing, this is it.  As a Spanish major, I was very upset that I was doing and learning nothing, while the class next door was learning a whole bunch.  He's not very helpful with his corrections and the due dates for things are never what he says they are.  Have fun with this one.
He is a very kind professor, always reachable after class, willing to take any questions from students.

368 with Mike is conceptually very easy, however you will waste your time and lose a LOT of points because of weird issues with your daq. You will also waste a lot of time debugging these stupid issues, so do not take it in a heavy semester. Lectures are useless, he is a poor lecturer and wastes a lot of time debugging (ironic). HW is redundant.
He doesn't test what he taught during class.
Great guy. One can show up to his office any time and ask any questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Some of the least engaging lectures I have ever attended. The professor will pause for 45 seconds at a time after asking pointless questions instead of getting to actual useful parts of the content. Attending a class with this professor was always the worst part of my day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grading policy is frustrating. The difference between a 60% and 100% can be as simple as one block in your Labview code. Teaching this content via 100 person lecture is not the way to go; I think most of the content is interesting and applicable, but his instruction made this class a chore.
rude guy

I've had Mike for 3 classes at this point, and I'm not sure why he has this low of a rating. Overall, he's a very approachable guy who knows his stuff. I think a lot of the bad reviews might just be because of the classes themselves being difficult.

If your major is ME, this class is the rated as the worst by most students on the flow chart. Beyond awful, it is something worth learning but taught in such a generic and cookie cutter way. This class should be smaller and more time in lab. The hw is the worst and so vague. It is boring and slow. It makes you questions so much...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful.  His lectures are exceedingly dull.  He teaches from long, boring packets that look like printouts from Wikipedia.  The worst part is, I made it through his entire course and honestly felt like I learned nothing.  His final exam is extremely difficult and looks nothing like anything seen throughout the course.

Lectures are extremely long and boring with the way he writes down every single thing that he says. This also makes it hard to study for a test due to the massive amount of notes you end up with. I missed the next letter grade by 1/10 of 1% and was dismissed when I asked about getting copies of my graded work back. Horrible Class, I'd stay away.

The entire class had basically no calculations and then the final exam-BOOM here's a random calculation worth a bunch of points. I was on track for a solid A from the first part of the class and all the labs, but then the plastics exam, which I studied a lot for, ruined that and I got an AB. And of course you HAVE to take him again in 314!

Absolutely terrible.  He literally would write down every word he said during lecture, which made lectures extremely slow and boring.    Not clear on many subjects.  I would try to avoid him, but I really don't think you can.  You will probably wind up taking at least one class with him.

I unfortunately had to take this guy back-to-back semesters just to graduate. This guy is dirty. I didn't think he was good at teaching from his very first lecture, and it had not improved one bit. There's never any enthusiasm in this guy. If you find the subject boring, he finds it boring too, and he teaches it that way. I want my money back!

He confused precision and confidence interval when introducing the topics. I asked him how to do a problem and using the method he told me I lost a point on a quiz. Quizzes and homework are nothing alike and do not help with the labs. As others have already said, avoid him.

Absolutely no grading consistency between assignments. Quizzes are on subjects that were glossed over in lecture. All open booknotesinternet available for quizzes but guess what, none of the material on the quizzes is found anywhere. Has to update lecture notesexamples because he makes mistakes on them. Avoid if you can, bring lube if you can't.

I've had him for several classes and absolutely hate him. Terribly unclear, barely even qualified to read off material which is all he does anyway. You're probably better off reading Wikipedia. I would say avoid, but it seems he's the ONLY "professor" for some of these ME courses. Best part is I'm paying for this garbage.
Very difficult grader with no clear policies or really any sort of order in the entire class. DO  NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM

Jorge was awesome!! He was so fun and laid-back; he made a lot of jokes and kept class exciting!  It's important to participate because he doesn't just give everyone 100% but for the bigger, harder assignments he gives students more leeway.  Seriously he was great!

I loved Cienfuegos!  He has a really cool name and even cooler personality.  He is really easygoing, would make jokes, always ask if anyone wanted clarification, and did his best w/ the rigged Supersite online system.  I would 100% take him again for any class, he was so insightful and helped me understand Spanish on a different level.

I had Jorge for Spanish 311 and he was great. The content of the class is boring because it focuses on grammar but Jorge went over the key points from each chapter during lecture. I rarely read the textbook, but you need it for homework and it's helpful for harder units. Grading was based on 3 essays and he looked for improvement in your writing.

Jorge is a funny guy and very laid-back. Lectures felt long and boring but that might've just been because I took this class at 8am. There were 3 papers for the semester and 1 assignment each week. The class is graded on whether or not you made progress over the semester, so you don't actually get any grades until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Shout out to Jorge! He is one of the best teacher Ive ever had. The course itself is not hard and Jorge made the class so dope. Spanish is not my major requirement courses but if my credits allow I would definitely talk his class in the future!!!

I love him so much. The course material is pretty easy in itself but he creates a friendly and jovial atmosphere in class which makes talking in Spanish or saying the wrong things less intimidating. He is very hip and sassy but also kind and informative when you need help. He plays music videos at the end of class which is great to pack bags to!
Great TA, and extremely helpful! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Attending class is extremely helpful! Pretty easy class, if you attend lectures.
Very fun and interesting. Caring and willing to help. Guides class through book reading very nicely. Attendance and participation are mandatory, NEVER SKIP CLASS!
Explains everything really well and super hilarious

I think she's fine compared to what everyone else below me is trying to say. I do agree with the exams being kind of long and more brain-intensive than any of the homeworks, but I feel like that's sort of cancelled out by the fact that they were open note.

She's caring, willing to help, and is generally positive. Still, the lectures cover a lot of material, the weekly HW takes a significant amount of time, and the tests are a time crunch. You have to be ready to dedicate extra time outside of lectures if you want to do well. I spent ~4 hrs/week reviewing material and ~4hrs/week on the HW and quiz.

She is kind but the workload is heavy. There is a lot of homework, and exams are much harder than the assignments. Lectures move fast and the explainations are unclear, so it takes a lof of extra time to learn on your own especially without prior knowledge to stats. The exams are also very time-pressured.

Chelsey is a decent lecturer and very kind, but I would avoid taking her class if you have no prior stats experience. She fails to explain root topics and flies pretty quickly through examples. However, she is very helpful and quick to respond through Piazza. Exams are much harder than the weekly homework, though not impossible.

She's a sweet and seems to genuinely love her job, but she screws you over in the exams. The content is fairly easy in lecture, but its presented in such a difficult way on the exams, which are also just way too long for the given time. I've never had a class where every single person stays until time is up except for this one. Wouldn't recommend.

Chelsey Green was a caring professor and wants her students to succeed, however, this was not actually what occurs. We had discussed topics at length but many of the concepts do not seem to be explained in a way that made sense to the class. I don't know of a single student in the class that was able to do the homework on their own.

She is a very sweet professor, and she cares about the success of her students. She provides a lot of resources if you don't understand the material, and she grants extensions for all homework as long as you ask. I don't know why the other reviews are bad, she is very sweet and good and teaching the material.

She was a decent teacher, the class was reasonably hard for me mostly because I expected it to be easy and didn't lock in until the end. The second midterm was super hard but the other tests were ok. Chelsey is a good enough professor but you will need to spend some time on the homeworks to make sure you fully understand them for the test.

I don't know why people are rating her so low. She is literally the best professor I've ever had. Her lectures are straightforward and interesting. The tests are easy and open note. Discussions aren't even required. She is amazing.

I thought Chelsey's class was difficult, but if you put in the time for exams and worked with other people they weren't too bad.  The homework was annoyingly long and definitely took a lot of time, but she is very generous with extensions if you have other things going on.  Her lectures were all posted online so its nice to just watch them at 2x.

Yall need to chill about my glorious queen Chelsey Green. She is super nice and she always starts lecture by giving us a nice debrief of her weekend and what her family is up to. If you go over the notes and ask questions before each homework/quiz and really try to understand everything, you will do well. Everything you need is in the notes/HW/quiz

bad at teaching. not enough time on midterm exams. I ended with a high A but only because I took AP Stats so the entire class was review. I cant even imagine trying to finish her exams in the time given if this was my first time taking the class. So annoying when professors do that like just make the exam time longer jfc???

so bad lol. no textbook at all so notes and lectures are the only info you have. exams are impossible and NO ONE finishes in time. repeats the same basic info 100x but fails to even mention twice content that will cover half of the exams. seems very nice but not a good professor.

The final exam was the only exam that felt fair purely because there was enough time to go back and correct mistakes. She writes all of her questions in the most confusing way possible i swear it has to be on purpose. I have to like mentally brace myself every time I move on to the next question.
class is a mess take the 240 340 combo by any means instead...

I love taking my final exam and there being a question with a big fat typo that makes all of the answer choices incorrect. I love when she uses word salad in the problem statements with like 4 double negatives and a run on sentence instead of just saying "Which gives the most evidence to reject the null". I CANT DO THIS ANYMORE

i hate myself for not checking this site before I took this class. Horrible at teaching, no study guides, piazza questions take 3-5 days to answer and some just don't ever get answered. ruining my grade in all my other classes by the amount of work I have to put in to not just completely fail this class

I saw a couple of people ask on piazza if she could post blank copies of the first 2 exams so we could study from it. she ignored both people and answered everyone else. She simply just doesnt want to go through the trouble of posting empty copies so she ignored it. so lazy. this single moment just sums up all of my frustrations with her.

I think these reviews are being a little dramatic ngl- sure the class is pretty hard, but Chelsey's genuinely the sweetest person ever, and I think she's pretty fair in terms of the homeworks and the tests. She'll answer your questions after class or during office hours thoughtfully, which can be super helpful.

Her exams are filled with trick questions and things meant to catch you off guard, or introduce unnecessary complexity. If we had a 2 hour exam slot it would be totally fair but you have to race through the exam as fast as possible to finish within 75 mins and this causes those things to be overlooked.
If you are considering taking this class and you love yourself in any capacity, then don't. Just don't
look at these "good reviews" they have to be fake no one speaks like that. would recommend a browse through the reviews before attempting this class.

shes like the epitome of putting so little effort into everything she does and then making the consequences of that everyone elses problem. like she will vastly inconvenience 300 people just to avoid 5 minutes of work for herself. its unbelievable.

Weekly homework assignments unnecessarily long and complicated. Lectures were oftentimes unclear. Exams are somewhere in between "pretty hard" and "very hard" -- but you do get unlimited paper notes. She seemed like a pretty nice person though

All of these troll reviews are basically right. I have been putting in a crazy amount of work just to be met with impossible questions with too little time. Also I didn't learn anything from her at all.

This is the worst. it's worser than the worst actually. She has made me emotionally numb, I should be crying every single day but I cant even do that because there nothing left of me. its like my wings have been stripped. she turned me from a soaring hawk, tuah falling rock. I have to talk tuah therapist every day because i have no mental health.
She is just a really bad teacher and the class is organized so weirdly?

You guys are kind of dramatic. This class is not easy but she totally gives you the tools, coming from someone who failed midterm two. 
Tests are completely open note (not sure if it was like that in the past), but they are HARD. Thats why you gotta go into them with good assignment grades and youre fine. Shes also really nice and will sit down w u

The weekly homework, canvas quiz, auto grade quiz and, exams too hard considering her inability to teach these concepts. EVERY part of her class is just THE WORST. it's like getting kicked in the balls every single day over and over. its like not even that hard but she just makes it all as miserable as possible.

she seems like a nice person so i feel bad sounding almost mean, but...my friends have convinced me to finally just say it: no one should be allowed to get away with making other people feel the way that chelsey makes them feel. im quite introverted and quiet but her total lazy mess of a class has turned me into an angry person every single day

I cant believe I had to pay to subject myself to her torture of a class. I did only fans for the whole summer to afford this and now I will be dropping the class today to retake it. Now I have to do more only fans to pay for the class again all because of her. This class is easily the second hardest thing ive ever done.

I took this professor because I enjoy failing my classes. I love destroying my mental health. Green single handedly got my parents divorced and made me drop out of college. I love taking my exams and finding out she put only wrong answers on them. If you enjoy being humiliated then take this class like I did.

I no longer look both ways when I cross the street because of what she has put me through. Nothing compares. everything about this class is a hot garbage mess. its like she ate all of the course content and violently barfed it out into homework and weekly quizzes and lectures.

Professor Green doesn't teach well enough to have the tests she gives that difficult. If you want to do well in this class it is entirely up to you to learn everything on your own for very difficult midterms and finals.

As a person who has never taken AP Stats in high school, this class is rough. Homework due every week, and there is a weekly quiz that easily takes over an hour. Her notes can be confusing. For a class that isn't supposed to be too hard, it really can pile up on you especially with other courses. Midterms were hard, midterm 2 average of 69%!

This course was a refresh of concepts from AP stats in high school plus some more methods. Coding website R is used and is annoying. Exams are open notes and never anything surprising. Chelsey is the most accommodating and caring professor I've had. Very helpful during Office hours and goes out of her way to help students succeed.
midterms are very rough, would recommend taking any other class to fulfill a rec. Nice person but not a great teacher
She's good but this class is very heavy. Took this class last semester and believe me it was TOUGHER than my chem courses.
Very heavy, didn't like it at all. Extremely tough midterms. AVOID IT AT ALL COSTS.
She is a tough grader, I gave my midterm yesterday and it was awful. I feel the class is very complex, try to take online course from somewhere else if possible. Otherwise, good luck 👍

Chelsey is a great lecturer. I thought stats was one of those useless classes but, man was I wrong. It is applied everywhere. I personally found it most useful for research. She records the lectures which is nice, HW's are long but, extremely helpful for understanding content. I wouldn't recommend a book. Just do purple text examples she provides.

I appreciate that Dr. Green seemed to actually like the class she taught, and was very animated/personable in lecture, her teaching style was really awful and made it very hard to learn. Dr. Green gives very little material to learn from and her lectures are just her going through some notes. She seems nice but I didn't learn a thing from her.

Professor Green is the BEST professor I ever had in 3 years at UW Madison. A professor that truly cares and respects students. Professor Green responded to my email even after 10 PM! If you explain what happened to you that caused you any trouble with the class. Professor Green will show extremely understanding and compassion!

Really nice teacher and will try her best to help you. Very understanding. Concepts are all simple algebra with some R code which was tedious. Lots of workload but if you do the homework and quizzes, the class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is a disaster. Lectures? Gibberish. Exams? Impossible. Homeworks? Long and don't relate to tests. Quizzes? Does not show correct answers. Practice problems/study guide for tests? Nonexistent. Avoid!
Green likes pain.
I have never written a review on here before but I feel like I need to warn people to not take this class with Green. Unsure how she has any positive reviews on here?

Nothing to read, nothing to understand. no textbook, no powerpoint, even the note will not be provided. All the material should be organized by yourself, you need to handle everything if you take this course with Green. Terrible teaching!! Really difficult Tests. Awful.

Got a good grade but put in A LOT of work. Can't tell you what I learned from Chelsey though. Her lectures are very unorganized and makes easy topics complex. If I did not take a stats course before this, I would have easily failed.
goodluck
I would not recommend taking this class. It was very difficult. Professor is not good at teaching. Very tiresome class.
Professor Green is nice but as a teacher she is pretty bad. Her lectures are very ineffective at teaching any material which is why nobody shows up to them. Exams are very difficult.
Chelsey Green is one of the best professors I've had. The material was complex, but she was wonderful to have as a lecturer.
Very hard midterm. There was not relationship between test and quizz/hw. The language description was difficult to understand

The lecture notes were sometimes difficult to use when she keeps hitting enter on a word document (which I can't do on a pdf), but she was generally a fine professor. She explained the topics well enough for people to do fine on homeworks and exams, and I also really enjoyed getting updates about her family at the start of each lecture.

Makes you suffer in useless LATEX with 15-20 page notes, test heavy and they super challenging. She was a definitely a nuisance and the class was crazy for first timers. she talks ab her kids and family but that takes 15 minutes in every start of lecture. every day and also that holy moly or other onomatopoeias that she make = extremely annoying

Lectures are boring but her notes are insanely helpful if you take key formulas and ideas because everything is on there. Homeworks take too long for a 3 credit class but they were very similar to examples from the notes packet. Tests can be hard as you need to know all the assumptions you must take for each exmples. Little bit of a learning curve.

Overall, Chelsey was a solid professor. Very organized notes, and the homework problems generally followed in-class examples pretty closely. That being said, the homework sets took probably 5-6 hours at a time (VERY time consuming) but Chelsey was very accessible to answer questions during office hours and on Piazza. Good professor.

The contents of this class are generally boring, and that doesn't help her case, however she does all notes in LaTeX, which has a steep learning curve. While she seems to have a great family, and I would probably love to be her child, the amount of time she spends talking about her family is a bit excessive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend Chelsey! Her lectures were engaging and she is extremely friendly and really wants to help you learn the content.
Very kind and understanding. Enthusiastic about the content. Willing to help.

Listen Chelsey was so kind & accomodating & all her lecture material was super available but I honestly can't say what I learned from her. I know it's hard to teach coding but this class felt like being told what to do & being expected to know everything. She's still really nice though so take her if youre ready to teach yourself everything ig

She provides helpful and clear lecture notes, full of definitions and examples. Recordings are always there to help you, and she is very caring about her students and very willing to give extensions. Exams are fair and grading is clear. Just put in efforts into this class and you will succeed.

Chelsey was a very accommodating professor throughout the semester. My biggest caveat with her was the amount of work that needed to be put in for a three-credit class. Overall, I really enjoyed her teaching and was able to move at my own pace with the recordings that she created for every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chelsey is easily the nicest most caring professor I have had. She will give extensions if needed, is always on piazza answering questions, and overall you can tell she cares for her students wellbeing. But her lectures are boring and kinda confusing to follow and the exams are challenging given the vast amount of topics and conceptual questions.

Probably the nicest and most accommodating instructor I've had. I found lectures a little hard to follow, especially as she types in LaTeX a lot of the time. The homework is difficult, but after doing it you know the concept pretty well. I find stats boring, but I think she taught the content well.

Prof. Green is nice and responsive to emails/Piazza and allows extensions. However, tests are challenging to a degree where the exam being open note doesn't even help you. Large packets are unorganized as she will commonly change them up during lectures, by hitting enter 50 times and then type a latex equation. Notes given don't relate to the exam.

Prof. Green is nice and responsive to emails/Piazza and allows extensions. Tests are challenging, but open note, and the class is manageable. Large note packets provided. Lecture videos are recorded, making it easy to keep up at your own pace. Disorganization is minor.  Know where to look on the notes so you can answer test q's w/o wasting time.

Class format changed, exams are open note, but questions are ridiculously hard. She breezes by lectures and types her notes in Latex (trying to fill out a 24pg note packet in 1hr). Essentially created a two-day exam, where the 1st day is in-person, 2nd day online. Basically, picture your passive-aggressive high school math teacher as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lecture recordings are available and tests are open note
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the note sheets are around 23 pages long each unit, which feels really messy, feels like lots of clutter, unorganized and hard to follow. she is nice though and responds to piazza posts pretty often.

She is not a great lecturer, and it makes no sense that she uses ~26 page word documents as lecture notes that you are supposed to fill in when she is speaking. She should take a statistics class here for herself and see how ineffective her lecture style is. Easier class, would not recommend taking a course with her, however.

They're a very nice and understanding person, but their lectures aren't useful at all for the class. The homework is nothing like the exams now that they have in-person portions. You can print out notes and bring them but none of the examples will be applicable to the problems on paper exams. They don't work out any problems on paper at all.

Professor Green is definitely my favorite professor that I've had. She's so kind and understanding and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. Lectures were recorded, which was extremely helpful, and I thought the exams were fair.

Chelsey is amazing, very kind, and understanding. You can always ask for an extension on homework. Discussion wasn't very helpful other than the few quiz questions that were given. Each week there is one homework assignment with a homework check, to check your answers and one quiz per week that had three tries.

Chelsey is an amazing, kind person. But this class was awful. Lectures aren't organized well/ are all practice problems that don't help you learn the material. The homework was a lot. I spent hours on it- but if you go to office hours, she will walk you through it. If you aren't great at math/have no stats background- this class is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Green truly cares about her students and makes accessing her outside of class easy. She offers a ton of office hours and will guide you step by step on all problems. Though RStudio is used, it is not difficult at all. She does all the coding for us and provides detailed notes. Exams are open note and very fair.

Chelsey Green was a good professor, very flexible deadlines, it was just the content that was difficult. Coming in with no coding knowledge, it was a bit hard to keep up at times. However, she is very understanding and easy to meet outside of class with.

I feel like this class assumes students to have a small foundation of basic stats knowledge which can make it difficult. It is so important to note that this is NOT a math stats class. Overall, she was an amazing prof. and was so understanding and EXTREMELY flexible on deadlines and truly emphasizes that as a student you cant give 100% every time.

Absolutely my favorite professor so far. Super accommodating with homework assignments, will help you through weekly quizzes, and its easy to get an A in this class by just paying attention in lecture. All lectures are also posted online which is super helpful. 11/10 professor, take this class with her or don't take it at all

Prof. Green was really nice and helpful but her tests were outside applications that we never really learned to do in class. Learning R Studio takes a bit of time but she is willing to help. Use her office hours and she will walk you through HW. She's not the best lecturer so I'd advise watching outside videos on stats basics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: there is a lot of homework each week but is probably necessary for a subject like statistics. You can tell she cares about her students and is very lenient with due dates. I found it easy to follow along in lecture but her notes/lecture style makes it difficult to take good notes to look back at

Professor Green is a quirky and caring professor. Statistics is hard to understand, and she tried to make it more simple. I met with her outside of class to talk about my grades and she was nice and supportive.

Chelsey is one of the best profs I have had so far. If you like to handwrite notes, she does move fast through the notes, but she truly cares about her students and is very lenient with extensions. I was nervous coming in based on the reputation of 371, but the homework is straightforward and Chelsey made the class a lot easier than anticipated.

This class was extremely difficult, especially if you have no prior stats knowledge. It is very easy to fall behind. Professor Green's lecture style is disjointed. Although she explains topics in detail she does not do so in a manner that links them together in a way that makes sense for intro level stats students. I would not recommend.

Can be challenging if you have no background in stats or the R program. I went in for office hours just about every week to get through the homework. Exams weren't too bad if you know basic concepts. Green is a funny and quirky lecturer. She is super sweet and always willing to help you outside of class. Also so understanding about extensions.

Love Chelsey Green as a person but not as a lecturer- lectures are unorganized and hard to follow. She is super accessible outside of class and gives help and sometimes answers to anyone who is struggling. Exams are tough, minimal curve. Prior experience with statistics and R help a lot- get ready to be very confused if you are going in without any
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Green is really good a throwing you a bunch of materials and examples, but you have to review the notes and rearrange them to make more sense chronologically. The lectures go pretty fast, but she is one of the friendliest professors so go in to talk to her to review. Super fair and reasonable about assignments.

She just goes over practice problems in lecture without really explaining anything and uses complex formulas without explaining the significance of any of them. Unless you can type complex formulas and large amount of text, watch the recorded videos.
The lectures were difficult to pay attention to and didn't always prepare you well for practicing the material. If you fall behind it will be very difficult to catch up and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stopped watching lectures after the first few weeks and taught myself the whole course from a suggested online textbook. Lectures were just watching her work through practice problems. She did go more in depth and give better explanations in office hours.

A very very nice professor! It is hard to connect with professors during the pandemic but Chelsey makes herself extremely available on Piazza and through email. You can tell she cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. The exams are also very reasonable and there is no reason anyone should struggle in this class.

Stat 371 is a hard class but I'm happy to have had Professor Green. She was very helpful in office hours and on piazza with questions on homework and quizzes. She is also very receptive to student feedback and though the homework may seem long, it is very helpful in preparing you for exams. Exams can be difficult but were fairly straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Recorded lectures always went over the 2 and a half hour limit. Didn't really teach the material, just had you follow along to her doing the problems. Homework and exams were always a few questions with a ridiculous amount of parts to them. Homework and exam problems were always 10 times harder than the examples given in lecture and quizzes.

Professor Green is honestly so so so nice. Her lectures are really clear and she's always so helpful whether it be in Piazza or in her office hours. Stats 371 is a hard class, but she makes it a lot more bearable. I genuinely feel lucky to have her for stats during this entirely remote class.

Green explained concepts in lectures with clear examples that made the work interesting. She also used the online format well, encouraging the use of the program R to solve/check problems. Beware, Green doesn't explain vocab in lecture, so that needs to be studied on the provided notesheet beforehand. Also, test problems can have confusing wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The learning experience is horrible for the summer time. Heavy workload but make sense for summer courses. She just go over examples without clarify any terminologies and concepts, taking it for granted that we know everything before watching the lecture videos. There are just so many examples with little explanation.

I love this professor! She is incredibly caring and willing to go over all material outside of class. What matters is that YOU take the initiative. Sometimes the homework feels tedious but it really hits home important concepts. Dont be discouraged by other comments- she has been one of my favorite professors at UW Madison!!

Professor Green's class was pretty difficult, but you could tell she cared a lot and wanted students to succeed. The examples in lectures were helpful for the homework and she would hold review sessions before exams. Her curve of the class also made it easier to get a good grade, even if it felt like you were struggling throughout the semester

Overall great professor. She posts lecture slides with blanks, but recorded every lecture and posted on canvas (watch at x1.5 speed if you miss lecturetime saver!) Textbook isn't necessary. Quizzes are on canvas with multiple attempts. Homework and quizzes reflect exam content. She was also willing to meet outside of office hours to go over HW

Concepts and formulas would be listed in PPT or outlines given, but they're vague. She'd try to explain every idea and how to use formulas but rarely clarify relationships between them, which could be confusing, given so many similar concepts in stats. The way lectures normally goes is that she reviews and introduces new things and endless examples

Chelsey has a great personality but I still struggled in this class, even after having taken AP Stats. Homework is graded extremely strictly, exams are too long, and Im not a fan of the fill-in-the-blank slides. Grading criteria was vague, as we were told there would be a curve but were never told the cutoffs.

Having AP stat in high school definitely made this class easier for me but the homework assignments can take an eternity simply because you need to do half the problems in R (A statistical programming language). Her quirky personality helped ease the pain of power lectures but her notes were all over the place at times. Hw helps with exams a lot.

Chelsey is a hard teacher and the homework is relatively long (you cannot find it on Chegg). She is always available to help you through the homework even outside of office hours. Power lectures always make me zone out and if you zone out in this class you have blanks in the notes. ALWAYS PRINT OUT LECTURE NOTES.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Chelsey is sincere with teaching, but she does not know that her lecture style is not the most effective at making sure her students understand the material. Additionally, Chelsey is not very transparent about how the class grade will be computed.

Fill in the blank Lectures, If you don't go to lecture you have useless notes. Does not give enough exam re view material (i.e., Practice exams, practice problems, etc.). Doesn't post HW solutions, so you don't have those to study either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The textbook is genuinely not good. complete lecture notes are not posted, you have to go to lecture and fill in the blanks. Not a fan of this class.
Lectures slides are useless and not enough example driven class. Unnecessarily hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are all fill in the blanks which require students to attend every lecture since Professor Greens does not post her lecture notes after classes. This made me spent extra time reviewing lecture notes since I could not get a complete note each time I go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Uses PowerPoint and has students fill in blanks. Seems easy but it makes it really hard to go back and try to understand what happened without flipping through all the slides multiple times. Not very good at giving general tips on how to apply what's learned to new problems. Does lots of examples, but most are very similar to each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I too this class in summer. Everything is fast-paced but you still got a good chance to follow up on every step. Chelsey explains every thing super clear, which helps me to build connections and really understand the intuition of those stat methods. She is caring and very patient. Office-hour also helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chelsey is a great professor. She's lovable, funny, relatable, and not condescending like many professors. She tells it like it is and is very clear about her expectations. The homework is graded fairly hard so use the TA help desk and work with others. It is very beneficial practice for the tests. No surprises on tests, but study everything well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Cindy was hands down the best professor I've ever had. She is extremely understanding and personable and genuinely wants to get to know you. If you have the chance to take a class with her, do it.
Not a teacher. Just a grader really. Learned very little from this class. She is not very approachable, understanding or really anything you would want from a professor. Take another class.

Cindy put a lot of effort into this class to make sure students are engaged and learning. The class doesn't take a lot of work to get an A. Cindy lets you resubmit projects that you didn't get a good grade on in order to improve your chances at success.

This class was not very useful and was overall a waste of time. The assignments and quizzes were unrelated to what we did in class. Quizzes are all on quizlet. The textbook is "required" for the class but you can get by easily without it; Cindy posts videos with key points from the reading so just save some time and money & don't bother buying it.

This class is really boring. The homework is pretty much the same every week. Cindy doesn't actually teach the class, but I've met her and she is very nice and cares about the students. Kines 119 is just a really dumb class and there isn't much any professor could do better

This class wasn't what I expected. Honestly the first half of the semester was quite boring, the speakers are mostly Researchers trying to explain to the general public what they do. It's basically all presentations and the homework seems to get graded kind of randomly. Tests are online and completely unrelated to presentations in class.
Best professor on campus. Hands down.

Cindy is more excited for this class than any of the students. You go to class once per week to listen to a guest speaker and write a reflection based on their speech. Cindy expects that you do hours of prep work before coming to class, but you can easily pass the class without much work. Don't bother with the textbook, it's not needed to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The c lass is pretty much pointless, but it's a prereq for a lot of kinesiology programs so many will have to take it. If it's not a requirement, do not take this class. Lecture meets once a week, Cindy has speakers from the Kinesiology program come in and speak about your career. Attendance isn't required, grade mostly comes from papers and exams.

Cindy rarely taught the class as a traditional professor. Instead, the class consists of guest speakers coming in once a week to discuss their career in Kinesiology. Easy to get an A, especially if you do the extra credit that is easy to forget about. Don't buy the textbook. Tests are online during weekends with a couple tricky questions.

Class is only once per week and is mostly speakers that come in and talk about their jobs This can be very interesting if you are interested in the field but also very boring Class is pretty much optional go when you are interested in the job Dont buy the textbook bc you can look up answers online Assignments are easy tests online Cindy is nice
Not helpful and condescending. Does not care for students' well-being.

She didn't teach the class, she just had speakers come in and talk about their fields. It was easy and kind of interesting, but it was hard to tell what we would be tested on for the two exams in the class

Cindy is really nice and really enthusiastic about the class! You do some activities that seem very trivial but if you actually reflect on them they are helpful. Definitely take notes on all the lecturers, she pulls questions from their talks for her final which is online and easy AS LONG AS YOU PAY ATTENTION.

There isn't a lot of instruction in this course. It is basically a bunch of speakers whose jobs are related to Kinesiology. Your grade is made up of a group powerpoint, two papers (one that takes little effort), and the final. Also she offered about 10% extra credit for listening to your classmates presentations. DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK.

Class itself is really easy. All you do is watch guest speakers and play little games like you are in elementary school again. She's not very helpful at all and your whole grade is a semester long presentation and a final with a couple papers and smaller assignments.

Not a hard class at all. One semester long project that is very easy. No tests except for the final, which is online and super easy. Some of the speakers that come in are interesting, but there are others who are very boring and make the class dull. She enjoys teaching, but her class was honestly a joke.

CIndy is nice and funny. However, she doesn't do most of the teaching.  She has a bunch of guest speakers come in and talk about what they do for a career.  Then you take a final at the end that's worth 30% of your grade that is completely irrelevant to anything she's put any emphasis on.

The class itself with the guest speakers is helpful, but Cindy does little to help, makes you do little clapping activities in class like we're back in kindergarten, and makes a final exam that is hardly relevant at all to any of the class and will only hurt your grade. The weighting of all the assignments is totally out of whack as well.

Expect no help from her in this class, even if you ask multiple times. Also, if you tell her the videos on learn@uw don't work you will be told you are wrong and she wont fix them. The class is easy until you get to the final exam. The final exam is on nothing you learned, impossible to do good on and will tank your grade.

Most unhelpful teacher I've ever had. Class is easy as anything, but a discussion comment that takes 1 minute to write is graded at the same weight as a research paper that takes 5 hours to complete.If Learn@UW glitches and you miss a discussion the highest you can get is a B. Unless this class is required don't take it.

Not extremely difficult to get an AB, but since there is only 1 Exam (worth 30% of your grade) on random facts that are not even studied in class, it is hard to get an A.  You can only lose 7 points in the whole class to maintain an A, as a 93 is an A. Lastly, Cindy will refuse all help you ask of her on essays "because she does not have the time."
Cindy is the greatest! She's funny, exciting, and very kind. The class is extremely easy. Two online quizzes, two papers, and some homework.

Claus is so amazing! The way he teaches is very straightforward and he is always so open to questions! For this being a 4 credit course the workload is surprisingly light and studying for quizzes and tests doesn't take long. I can not recommend Claus Andersen enough!

Phenomenal lecturer and cares a lot about students. If you want a guy who can make fairy tales insightful and genuinely meaningful to our lives Prof. Andersen is the teacher for you. While you could miss a lecture or two without harm you never will want to

Professor Andersen was incredibly kind and fun. His lectures were very chill, and you didn't really need to pay attention to do well. The readings were not very long compared to other literature classes. Overall, he is a great professor and his class is easy and fun and if you need a literature class this is definitely a good option.

This class was very interesting, however his TA for the class was absolutely horrible. He would constantly not grade things, provide horrible feedback. He would also give out very scathing reviews of your work a couple hours before its due so you can change it. Worst TA I have ever had, he should not be allowed to teach ever again.

Professor Andersen is the perfect teacher for this class, he comes from Denmark giving him an interesting connection to the stories we read. His lectures don't fully pertain to quizzes, but he makes them interesting and brings up good points. Pretty easy class.

He does a lot of lecturing, and for the most part it is not mandatory that you show up to class. He does give random in-class quizzes. There is a lot of reading, but its mostly fairytales, but they can be really long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gave lectures that had nothing to do with readings or really anything. If you memorize what he says you will get a good grade but you cannot interpret on your own, which is strange for a literature class.

Professor Andersen gives interesting lectures that give good insights into all the fairytales. For a literature class, there is generally not too much reading, with the exception of some nights when it takes an hour just to read everything. He's from Denmark which makes the class even more interesting, and incorporates humor into lectures too!

Professor Andersen is absolutely incredible! He embodies everything I believe a professor should be: humble, respectful, intelligent, dedicated. His lectures are fantastic and philosophical without being overly complicated. He is clearly passionate about both the subject and his students. Take a class with him!

If you are thinking about taking a class with Professor Anderson, TAKE IT!!! This guy is the best. I have never had a professor that is more caring than him. He constantly reiterates that he is there for his students and wants to help them succeed. This class is about fairytales which is awesome already, and he makes it even more enjoyable.
This class was great. Would recommend.

As a stem major I was just looking for an easy A lit credit, I do not like English type classes at all but I loved this one. Andersen is honestly so amazing and just a great guy and professor. I will look into taking another class with him. I cannot say enough great things about him. If you are considering taking a class with him, do it.

Professor Andersen is great! I had him this spring and was always super helpful and passionate about the topics. I was even very generous dropping low scores and giving us a few days off to ease up on the load with this tough semester. If you take 275 with him, flipped fridays are the only thing you really need to spend time on.

Andersen is an amazing professor. I am a stem major but his class was probably the best literature/english class I have ever taken. He truly cares about the well being of his students and is open to having "coffee hour" every so often so he can connect with his students. Wish I could take this class again. The material is really interesting.
Super philosophical lectures. Not a difficult class at all, the lectures felt more like a break from a busy day than a task. The readings are mostly fairytales, very fun, relaxing class.

this class is great, and highly recommend taking it with this professor. He is very passionate about these topics, and I think the exams are fair. As long as you go to lecture, read the textbook and study you will be good. Overall, would take another class with him.
He's a nice guy but the readings take a long time to do every week. He does give extra credit surveys which take like 3 minutes to do and they're easy points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sorry, I just had to post, the last comment is talking about how the exams are so different from the course material which is craaazy! We just took our first exam last week, so I don't even know what they are talking about. Maybe the practice exam that had a super high class average score??? Exams seem totally fair and I'm loving this class!!!
Not a great professor, lectures are the same as textbook but exams are nothing like either.

Read the post about Clint not being a math person and teaching statistics. I guess I feel differently about that. I'm not a math person either, and I really liked his Clint's honesty about that and that he didn't take for granted that we knew everything. So I feel like it was super helpful how he talked about stats. I'm glad I was in his section!
Sometimes very confused, the materials that given for review has little relationship with exams.

Good class Dr Jensen seems really interested in the content which makes it engaging most of the time. If you study and do the extra credit it's pretty easy to do well. He is easy to approach and takes time to answer questions. Can't really ask for much more from an intro course professor.
Doesn't teach at all, does a "flipped method". Just take this class online instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Clint is a very enthusiastic teacher and I loved going to his lectures; however, he rarely checks for attendance in class and puts all slides online. In 202, he gives a generous amount of extra credit (5% if you do everything), so there is a lot of flexibility. Exams are not the best quality, but also not super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor openly told the class he's "not a math guy" on the first day of Statistics. Curriculum was copied and pasted from online summer term. Flipped classroom with little to no content-related insight from him. Answer keys frequently wrong. If you don't understand a concept you're not going to get any help from Clint. Would have taken online.
Very friendly! I would go up to the front of the class after a number of lectures and have very nice and productive conversations with Professor Jenson.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class was pretty good for an intro and Professor Jensen is pretty approachable. I thought some of the material could have been presented in a more engaging manner. If you study the tests are easy enough and the final is basically a combo of the semesters tests so if you do good on those you're  golden.

I thought this was a pretty straight forward class. I think he's a decent lecturer and a pretty nice guy. If you read the material, go to class and do the extra credit you can do well. He provides the lecture materials which a plus. He could do a little more test prep.

Professor Jensen was a decent lecturer and his exams were super fair. Listened to recorded lectures at 2x speed couple days before exam and got A every single time. References in-class videos and content, not too many surprising questions. As long as you keep up with the lecture content you can get an A.

Honestly I really liked him as a professor. If you go to the lectures I think it kinda helps but if you skip your fine. The extra credit is easy to get and boosted my grade 7% so thats nice. He talks about Dr.G so much you would think he's the professor. Overall exams are easy and if you watch the videos or read the textbook your fine.

Offered extra credit, definitely max out on that. Lectures are useless because he provides no additional information beyond the textbook. I wouldn't recommend taking 202 with him, but if you have to don't go to lecture, just study the textbook and you'll be fine.

He seems like a nice guy but not a good for lectures. Exams are more tedious than they should be for a intro course. No direction on what to study. There is extra credit so do that but wouldn't rec if you have to take this course. You cant look at what you got wrong on exams. Takes course way to serious for an intro course

I thought Professor Jensen was an absoltely amazing professor, he provided insightful materials and always strived for his students to learn more. His lectures were interesting and engaging, exams were challenging but pushed me and fellow classmates to work harder. I would reccomend taking his course, he is an incredible professor.

Despite the other not so great reviews, I really enjoyed Prof. Jensen's teaching style. He cares a great deal about his students and is happy and excited to meet students in office hours. I reading the book is INCREDIBLY important! Attendance at lecture was taken, but if you were to miss, looking over the lecture slides is a definite must.
Clint is awesome

Clint was a great professor. He was really down to earth, enthusiastic about the material, and (most importantly to me) understanding of extenuating circumstances. If you show up to his class and take notes, you'll be more than fine. Just show up, stay focused for the hour, and start studying at least a few days before the exam.

Clint's class is one of the best I have taken in the psychology department. The class felt more like a discussion where everyone could meaningfully contribute. The research paper was somewhat challenging but he provided consistent support, chances for success, and great detailed feedback. He was a very personable and nice instructor.

I've had Clint as a professor for Child Development or Psych 460. The material was presented in a clear way, and exam expectations were very clear. All material from the exams were clearly emphasized on the slides which made studying simple. There were some projects due over the course of the semester, but they were simple.

I had Clint for my psych capstone and it was by far my favorite course I have taken in the Psychology Department. It was clear he cared about our understanding of the subjects and wanted to know us all individually. As long as you put in effort to your assignments, it is easy to get an A. If you I highly recommend taking a course with Clint!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great instructor! The class was a little difficult if you hadn't done the readings so definitely do those. The main thing is it was a little unorganized but it was overall a great course. The main grade was the final paper and that was not meant to be a difficult assignment if you had a solid plan. Definitely go to office hours for that paper.

Professor Jensen was incredibly kind and accessible outside of class. He offered multiple extra credits and was great at answering questions. The exams were challenging but bearable. Some questions were more difficult than others, but that's what goes into an exam anyway. I recommend doing the readings, as they helped immensely with the exams.

I don't understand why everyone here is hating. I thought he was a great professor, and as long as you showed up to lecture and did the readings, you were fine. I did minimal studying for this class, and just did all the assignments while reading the rubrics carefully and was fine. Grading sometimes took a while, but that's because there was one TA

He is kind and wants students to succeed. But he was not prepared for tests. Exam 2 was horribly written and everyone did bad. He does not help prepare for exams or give any guidance on topics. He was horrible at answering questions and everyone got frustrated. I once asked him a question and he responded so badly I was dumbfounded

I will say, it does seem like he really cares for his students and he is a very genuine person. However, exam expectations were extremely unclear and he gave you basically no direction on what to study. The exam questions were horribly written and confusing. The class average on the exams was way lower then it should have for this content.

I loved this class, one of the easiest psych courses. Clint was super engaging and seemed to really care about the content. TONS of extra credit options. I never opened the textbook and still did very well on exams. Just go to lecture and you'll be good.

I feel like he cared about his students but with his lack of experience he was unable to give people proper education. Even after studying for countless hours for an exam, I ended up receiving a D, due to the fact that his exam questions made no sense. When asked about the exam, he said that they were meant to trick you. Give me a break.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why a university that actually cares about its reputation would even hire this guy. He's so lazy that he didn't create any of his own assignments, and then also did not want to put grades into canvas, so nobody knew their grades until the semester was over. He is also so horrible at writing exam questions. Worst teacher I've had here.

WORST "professor" I have ever had. He is very unorganized and does not give clear expectations for assignments and will take points off for no reason. He is incredibly passive aggressive and rude with students. He grades you on your attendance and does not even have that listed in the syllabus. DO NOT take any class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unorganized and unclear expectations 24/7. "Participation" worth 20% of our grade was mandatory attendance with one "freebie" regardless of whether an absence was excused (this was decided when final grades were due) and not stated in the syllabus. Take 601 with a professor who knows what they're doing and supports students' success.

It is very difficult to pass some of the assignments. She is a very tough grader. She also gets annoyed when students ask questions during lecture. Unnecessarily hard grader and unpleasant attitude. I don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: At first, she seemed likable and knowledgeable and I expected to enjoy her class. However, she often comes across as sassy and snotty. If you don't clearly express her exact opinion in assignments from lectures/discussions, your grade may suffer. Her assignment feedback feels sarcastic and snooty rather than constructive, which can be frustrating.

Taylor is very knowledgeable and passionate about her subjects, and I found her seminar engaging and informative. Her scholarship is commendable and leaves no room for doubt. However, there were instances where her behavior came across as petty, condescending, and cynical, which I found unacceptable for a professor.

Professor Taylor is an engaging and knowledgeable lecturer. While she is firm in her class expectations, the content of the class was interesting and thorough. The grading system is fair, you just need to pay attention and submit your work on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She can be a bit abrasive at times, but she's a great lecturer. They were all organized nicely and easy to follow. The grading criteria is a bit complicated, but you essentially get to pick your grade based on the amount of work you choose do. Attendance policy is more than fair, and she allows a few make-ups at the end of the semester as well.

She is an amazing professor who has engaging lectures. However, people do find her a bit rude with her expectations, however, if you listen to what she says and follow her grading scale you will do fine. Additionally, she was funny and chose interesting readings to read inside and outside of class. Overall would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gets a tough rep because she's harsh. Her expectations are clear and her lectures are entertaining (she's funny). If you show up and you're a good student, you will be just fine. She isn't flexible about deadlines and won't give extensions (even if you've got an emergency). As long as you come to class prepared and do your work, you'll be ok.

She is very knowledgeable but is completely rude. She is someone who looks down on her students and will tell you off. I know of multiple of my peers who emailed her and did not get a response back. If you plan on missing class think again. Do not take a class with her if you don't have to.

She's a very intelligent person in her field. She's also very nice and funny. However, she is a very tough grader and will take points off if you don't regurgitate her exact opinion/what she talked about in class. Do not even try submitting things late or you'll flunk. Attendance was mandatory and you must be involved in the discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was demeaning to students and what grade you would get was based on a complicated flow chart. She was clearly knowledgeable but it hard to get through lectures purely based on how she talked to students.

Mandatory Attendance in lecture (1 in class activity per class). A few quizzes that are based on lectures and weekly readings (easy). A few papers that get progressively more difficult but are not bad. Some lectures are very boring and some are extremely interesting it depends on interests. Lectures are nothing special just typical college course.

she's clearly an intelligent professor, but is condescending and spiteful towards students. emailed her multiple times when I was violently ill for a week and never got a single response back. She expects you to already know so much information or just look it up yourself. I didn't enjoy this class and felt I had no guidance on the final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would avoid this professor at all costs. I graduated, but still view this my only negative experience at UW. Class is easy but dry. However, the issue resides in the fact that she is spiteful and takes it out on students. Don't miss a class even for medical. She patrolled us when while writing her evaluations saying she needed to collect herself

Had very well thought out and engaging lectures, unfortunately was incredibly rude and inconsiderate which should be step one for any pedagog. This class left a very sour taste in my mouth due to the gaping disconnect between Professor Taylor and her students' needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor's class is extremely easy but you have to show up to lectures. She is passionate about the subject and chooses to tell you about what's going on instead of throwing it on slides. She kind of has an attitude sometimes but means well and is a decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a bit of a chip on her shoulder. She also swears in class not infrequently - which I usually don't have a problem with if it's meant as a joke but she sounds unprofessional. Her lectures are excruciating, and she's sometimes unclear what of the material is important to know. If you are in love with the subject, take the class, otherwise not
Professor Taylor is awesome. One of my favorite professors I've had at UW. Had her for her 201 and 303 and loved both classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taking the class for Comm-B, thinking Athenian Democracy sounds cool, but she expects you to know a lot or look it up yourself. She pulls in ancient sources, but isn't good at explaining who they are, what they are talking about, or even which century it is! My TA is awesome at actually helping. Prof is smart but condescending. She's not teaching.

I have had Professor Taylor for two different classes and specifically chose her class the second time because I liked her teaching style so much.  Every lecture she hands out a sheet that outlines that lecture.  She is clear and concise and you actually learn in her class. Fair grader. Funny. Awesome British accent :)

Prof. Taylor is a super engaging, interesting, and fair professor. She lectures in a pretty old-school way, but she's a fantastic lecturer and really makes Greek history digestible. Keep in mind that she takes zero crap, and attending lecture is an absolute must. Class lacks tests and she's a super reasonable grader.

Great lecturer. The major reason people don't like her is that she lectures the old school way without slides or much writing on the board. Unfortunately, that's just a matter of the students not being used to it. I'd definitely take a class with her again if I hadn't fulfilled all my liberal arts electives.

Claire Taylor is definitely the best lecturer I have had at UW in my four years. She is very clear in her lectures, and you can tell how passionate she is about Greek history, more specifically Athenian history. One paper at the end of the course with the option of 10 points extra credit and two online exams. I recommend this course to everyone!

This was one of my favorite classes! The communication B aspect was not hard if you attended class and read the seminar readings. Even though the material could have been really boring, she made it very interesting! I also learned a lot! Take it with her if you get the chance.
