Furthermore, the instructions for his assignments were often lacking direction and the only clarity on instructions was found through office hours, which I found somewhat irritating.

Oh, where do I begin? 

One of the best professors I have ever had at UW.

Professor Fischer is hands down one of the best I've ever had at UW Madison. The way he taught complicated court cases made them really accessible, and the assignments were actually kind of fun to do. Legal writing was daunting at first, but he gave us a lot of advice on how to do it well. He's also hilarious, would recommend if you're prelaw

Craig was excellent when I had him for 470. The concepts were extremely boring on paper but he made them interesting. There was a lot of reading expected before each class (to preview the material), but I never did it and Craig made the concepts easy to understand. Only thing in the grade book are 3 papers so be ready for that. Funny and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome class, talked about hot political issues without sounding political at all. Very objective and approached issues from a literary/argument analysis perspective. Reasonable grader. Lectures writing on the blackboard so he goes slow enough to take notes, but it doesn't drag.

He is very nice and understanding. The lectures are fun and engaging, but get ready to write! He has a strict no electronics policy. There are 3 exams, no mid-term or final. The exams are quite difficult with the class average being a C on the first exam and an average of a B on the last two. The only homework is to read articles posted on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not a philosophy or business student, but I enjoyed his lectures. He showed personality, not monotone or wishing you'd taken another class. His notes on the board are very clear and are basically what you most need to pass the class.

A great teacher who is very helpful and supportive. I am not a Philosophy major but he makes the class very interesting and engaging and I would definitely recommend taking this class if you want to talk about relevant issues!

Caring and relatable prof with kind grading rubrics for exams. Honestly lectures are unnecessary if you are capable of self-study due to the nature of the course content. If you are able to tackle and make a solid effort on 60+% of the problems from the textbook I'd say you are 90% likely to get an A.

This class felt like she was throwing equations at us and we had no clue where they were coming from. The amount of work was also ridiculous since she changed the format going online - she even said that the graders were constantly overwhelmed. If you put in the work (and check solutions!), though, you will get a good understanding of the material.

She's not bad! Gives great real life illustrations. Always hands out plenty of practice materials before the exam. Doesn't do the best at explaining complex topics, but does REALLY well with simple Mechanics explaining
Wendy was a solid prof, she cares that people learn.

Prof. Crone is an intelligent professor and very helpful in office hours and with questions. Her lectures are extremely boring though and hurt my interest in the subject because she takes way too long on algebra and simple math. There's also a ridiculous amount of homework that doesn't really help with learning or the test. Discussions are key.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Crone is an incredibly intelligent professor, but wow her lectures were incredibly boring. The content learned in this course seemed interesting, but most of the time was spent brushing over the derivations and instead doing long calculations. Homework took a long time and was tough to reap valuable information from.

Professor Crone did an alright job teaching this course, but where she excels is going into office hours and asking questions. The course isn't too difficult but if the conceptual topics aren't nailed down you will struggle. Don't be afraid to ask her that nagging question because it will 100% be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her exams were easy but the class was not curved. You can understand her from the lectures, and if you don't you can easily use MecMovies to help you understand. She does some pop quizzes for attendance and you don't have to know the material to answer. She likes to have visual aids (materials) to help understand the topic discussed.

Don't skip classes/discussions especially around test times. Because of how assignments are weighted pop quizzes and attendance checks end up being worth a significant amount. Homeworks are overly difficult, but tests are fair and lectures/slides cover all of the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Wendy Crone is by far the best engineering professor at UW and all her students love her. Her lectures are very clear and she is extremely knowledgeable. I highly recommend going to office hours as she is super helpful. The homework is tough and time consuming, however, it prepares you for the tests. I highly recommend taking any of her courses!

Very good teacher overall. She turns off all of the assistive features for the homework, so you have to struggle until you get the right answer. The first two exams were easy, but the final was significantly harder and almost no one finished it. Generous grader, show work to get partial credit. Take advantage of photo credits (extra credit).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Crone was great. Lectures slides are given before class so they can be used to help with note taking. Tests were pretty easy, and the three projects throughout the semester were fun. Homework takes a hundred years to complete, but it is valuable for studying and graded fairly. Take this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lecture hard to understand. Just go through the problems very fast and not clear

Not a good lecturer at all, just monotonously burns through problems and bores you to death. She also found it necessary to completely change the requirements for one type of assignment after we had already completed two of them. Honestly one of my least favorite professors thus far.
She is not a great teacher.
good professor but tough work load. go to class.

Extremely helpful teacher. If you don't understand something, she'll keeping helping you until you do. Examples done in class were exactly what to expect on homework and in exams. If you need to take 303, take it from her!
Great teacher! Is really good at explaining concepts. Makes you work for your grade. Assigns a lot of random assignments and randomly takes attendance but it worth it.

A lot of work for a 3-credit course. Gives trivial assignments randomly to encourage attendance. Grading is fairly generous on exams. Weekly homework often contains material not covered until after the assignment is due. Expect to spend a lot of time in TA's office hours to understand the material and get a good grade. Lecture quality is average.

best professor i ever had. she makes you work like hell for your grade but she makes it rewarding in the end because you learn SO much from her. lectures are done so well and notes are crystal clear. very helpful, nice and friendly in office hours and its obvious she wants to help you. seemed like a lot of work for a 3-credit class.

I actually really loved Professor Crabb. His sense of humor was right up my alley as he'd go on tangents telling stories about his family or his old jobs. He was always VERY responsive and VERY helpful whenever I emailed him, even after the new professor started teaching, and he's great at explaining things. Would 100% take a class with him again!
Richard is a very wholesome and nice guy. He really cares about his students. He does a great job at explaining the material

Great teacher, the material is hard if you have never taken a stats class before but it is manageable if you commit time to it. The exams are difficult but there are no surprises. Overall a great teacher that really cares about his students.
Entertaining lectures, super helpful during office hours.

Richard Crabbs is an amazing and understanding instructor, truly cares for your academics. I had multiple technical errors with turning in my final papers and he was very understanding of my situation. Although lecture can be a bit hard to read for his handwriting, but he truly knows what he's talking about!

Professor had all the materials needed online, so missing lectures were no big deal. Very understanding and a large portion of the grade was a case study that was very easy to do given out discussion sections walked us through everything step-by-step. 
Professor was engaging during lectures, funny and easy to understand.

Good lectures (other than the handwriting). Good professor. Accessible outside of class. Kind of wish that there was not just 2 exams. Additionally, I was VERY sick during finals and reached out to see if anything could be done. I had to go in, and could not focus because of my illness. Only reason he does not get a 5. That dropped my grade to a B.

Professor Crabb is awesome! I had no prior stats experience and his teaching and resources facilitated success. I really ended up enjoying the class as well as using Excel. Definitely recommend taking him for Gen Bus 306

You can immediately tell he is perfect for teaching a tough statistics class like this. He ensures this class will turn out well for everyone, even if you haven't taken statistics before. The lectures are clear; he sometimes makes funny jokes and is very flexible. His take-away messages from this class are things I won't forget during my time here.

Richard is definitely one of the best professors I have had so far at UW-Madison. He is an amazing lecturer and very engaging. Very helpful during office hours as well. Exams are a little hard, but the review material covers almost everything. Definitely would take again!

One of the best business courses I have taken at UW - Madison. Richard is an amazing lecturer and very engaging. Exams are a little tough, but as long as you study and go to lecture, you should be fine.
Definitely take a class with Crabb if you can.

Richard was extremely funny and a great lecturer. Some people think that he might be too fast during lecture but as long as you stay locked in this class is a breeze! Richard always brings in loads of interesting industry experience that make his lectures inspiring and interesting. His comedic delivery is always on point too.

Fave professor in the b-school. Class structure is super clear and flexible and gives you all the tools you need to succeed in the class. He is interesting and hilarious, as well as a great lecturer. Posts his notes and detailed info for every lesson on canvas. It's not necessarily an easy class, but Crabb makes it manageable and even enjoyable.

Richard is phenomenal! I thoroughly enjoyed GB306, and I believe Richard was a key factor in that. Richard made lectures enjoyable by integrating stories from his personal and professional life with the material. There was plenty of material on canvas to prepare for exams, and requirements for success in this course were clear from the start. 10/10

Best professor I've had at Madison by far. His lectures are interesting and engaging and made me want to come to class. Exams aren't easy, but if you go to class and do the homework, you'll be fine. There's a generous curve and two case studies. If you're confused on anything, go to office hours and he'll walk through the problem step by step.

Professor Crabb is an amazing professor that is not easy to forget! He makes class fun and interesting! I was warned how difficult this course would be but taking it with him made it a lot easier! Great guy and class all around!

Super hard class if you don't know Stats -- like you will be behind if you don't work hard. However, Mr. Crabbs might be the most accommodating prof in the entire school and a super nice guy. He used to bring in soda to office hours and would help me with all of my many questions. It will be hard, but you will learn along the way.
Good

He is the best professor I've ever had at UW-Madison. He responds to emails very quickly and always accommodates students' needs.  He is kind and always there to help his students to succeed in this class although the course materials are pretty challenging. Take his class for sure!!!!

GenBus306 is a hard class, but Richard Crabb made it enjoyable for me. He has a ton of industry experience in analytics & is open to sharing stories while also teaching the course content well. I email him a lot w/ questions lol, & he always explains things rly well & makes me enjoy learning. Honestly one of the best profs in the entire B-school.

Richard is very funny, and he might be the smartest professor at Madison. He wants everyone to succeed in his class, and even though the material can be challenging, he provides tons of practice. I strongly recommend taking Richard if you have the option.

He is the best professor I've ever had at UW Madison. He truly wants his students to succeed in this course by providing plenty of resources such as practice exams, ungraded homework, and unlimited time quizzes. He is always there to answer students' questions and accommodate students' needs. 100% take his class!!

The excel cases are pretty easy except the write up takes a lot of time. Office hours really helps for the cases. Quizzes were open note, difficult sometimes. Probability was confusing and overly difficult for no reason.
super understanding, & overall nice human being with great teaching skills

the actual material for the class is difficult, but he acknowledges that and provides plenty of resources to help you; practice exams, ungraded hw, videos, problems with solutions worked out. great guy who truly cares about his students

Richard teaches a fully online class, so the interaction with him is slim if you do not go to office hours. The material in the middle of the class is quite difficult, but the beginning and end are easy. Watch the online lectures and do the homework problems and you should not have a problem getting a good grade. 2 exams, 2 case reports & quizzes.

The material is quite difficult but can be learned with time and effort. Mr. Crabb and Dr. Bavafa are both engaging and make the course enjoyable. The questions on the exams are not meant to trick you. The course is very exam/project heavy. Weekly quizzes help you stay on track with the content.
Mandatory class the quizzes and tests were difficult, but I was able to muddle through and get a decent grade. Class was completely online.

Projects are very useless and there is no way to know if you are doing it correctly. Professor isn't really helpful in  answering questions and doesn't seem that friendly. Smart guy that knows his stuff but could structure the class differently.

Professor Crabb is a genuinely nice person. He cares a lot about his students and is very patient and accommodating to extenuating circumstances. The class is by nature very difficult but he does a great job walking you through the content and makes sure it is not too overwhelming. Practice exams are very helpful!
Super smart, super funny, and a great guy overall. I had never taken a stats class, but he did a great job of explaining the concepts nonetheless.

Crabb was funny, nice, and understanding. Expectations for class were explicit, with weekly lectures, homework, and a quiz. Lectures relevant and broken down into short vids. Exams/quizzes were challenging, but not impossible. Casework was a diffucult but TAs/Crabb always available for help. Needed to work for good grade, but great prof for GenBus.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I didnt do great in this class, however this was mostly due to my own personal reasons. When I talked to Professor Crabb about class content or any personal issues I had, he was very helpful, understanding, and overall genuinely enjoyable to talk to. Definitely go to office hours if struggling, or meet with him. Awesome guy
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The supplemental readings nicely bolstered the lecture videos. Hes very responsive to emails; if you ever have a question, just reach out to him and hell give you an answer. Even in a semester that was online, it felt like he was accessible at all times.

The course is very organized and the lectures are clear and pretty interesting because he always uses his own industry experience in examples. The supplemental modules are also nice if you learn better by reading than lectures (There's no TB for the class). Just get ready for a steep learning curve if you're not good with excel

The lectures were broken up into 10> minute segments and there were a lot of practice problems, quiz attempts, and past exams provided that were similar to questions on the exam. The two cases weren't hard, just time consuming, but the TAs were super helpful and all the TAs and Prof Crabb had many office hours and were very responsive.

All exam content is learned through lecture videos and notes. Gives plenty of examples and practice problems if you don't understand. Is pretty easy if you've taken stats before. Case studies require a lot of time but you have plenty of resources to figure out how to complete them(except the grading on the write-up by the TA's is a bit subjective).
Great guy. Friendly. Understanding. Excellent teacher. Precious and to the point. Clear examples.

2nd professor in the class. Covers probably the hardest modules in class if you've never taken statistics before. Class is pretty easy if you've taken AP Stats in highschool though as it's the exact same content. Exams ask tougher questions though. I felt like his online instruction was mediocre, and he asked way too convoluted questions at times.
GB 306 is overall a do able and enjoyable class as long as you take sometime and prepare for quizzes and midterms. Overall I enjoyed this class!

Good teacher, explains well but like others said - very fast. Either record the lectures or go to both lectures he teaches because you can't keep up with him and your notes. Do not rely on the HW problems he provides as a gauge of your understanding. The exams are much more difficult, so do the practice exams or I guarante you will do bad on exam.
This class was difficult but Professor Crabb made it interesting. You definitely have to work to do well in this class but if you want to learn something, Crabb is the right guy for you!

Professor Crabb is a good guy but his teaching style isn't for everyone. He goes pretty quickly through material and says things like, "pretty simple, right?" that make it hard to ask questions in lecture. Tests are definitely hard and require you to go to class in order to understand the content and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Richard Crabb is a pretty good lecturer who spices up things during a lecture. He's funny (talks about his life a lot), and is the only professor who still uses Kahoot! college (Kudos to him). Really flexible if you have to extend deadlines. Exams are semi-hard because they are time-crunched. This class is super easy if you took AP Stats.
Decent professor, but the tests were difficult (especially the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall Professor Richard held inspirational lectures and the practice problems are really helpful. Do the practice problems early will help you survive the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Richard is a great professor. Class is difficult but he provides plenty of help for you to succeed. Great guy who makes real life connections.

Richard is hilarious, I love his class and he is super funny! The lecture is useful and not driving me sleepy. The homework is fine but the exam is definitely hard. My TA--Kenny is so great. Just take this class even if you are not going into this field!!!!!!!!

Richard is funny, but goes very fast in lecture. This class was really hard for me, not gonna lie, but never fear - the class is curved generously. Got a BC on the first case, failed both exams, and got an A on the last case, and still somehow ended with a C. Study hard, but know if you're really struggling you should still be okay in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Richard is a great professor, the material is difficult but he tries to make real life connections and answer questions to the best of his ability.

I'm really conflicted about this one. Richard Crabb is hilarious. He has great stories and plenty of applicable experience. Lecture is definitely interesting. This being said, if you don't have a stats background class can be really tough. Studying for the midterm can seem impossible because the material is extremely unpredictable.

Crabb is SO funny. I absolutely loved his antidotes and stories. Seriously, he made me want to study about a subject I did not know much about and made 50 minutes FLY by. He truly cares about his students and is brilliant. I hope I get to take a class with him, and am so bummed he only taught 1/3 of the class. Crabb, you rock!

Richard is a great guy. He gives fun lectures and shows you real-world applications of Analytics. The Module 2 Exam is hard, don't get me wrong. But, if you do all of his problem sets, go to lecture/discussion, you will succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This course is taught by 3 different professors. Richard is the 2nd and although he is a great guy, his teaching is fairly accelerated. It's as simple as, if you don't show up, you won't pass and if you DO show up, you'll still be confused. It's a REALLY tough module so start reviewing from Day 1. Rumor is most students fail the module 2 exam - GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm currently in the second module and I love Prof. Crabb. He does a fantastic job of working through examples, even though they are pretty complicated. He responds to emails within hours which is always a bonus. As well, he's just a really nice guy who always tries to tell jokes and liven the class up by being a genuinely cheerful guy!

Crabb is a great guy, he is funny, social, really likes to teach, and is interesting to listen to. The one exam is tough and determines a large part of your grade in the class but the cases aren't bad. However, I wish he would make the exam more predictable and easier to study for.

Prof. Crabb is an incredible/passionate lecturer who brings in a lot of real world application. He takes a break during lectures to tell a story (usually quite funny) to keep students engaged. The course itself is kinda difficult, the exam (only 1) is long and hard, but if you put the work in on the cases you will do very well. Overall grade curved

Crabb makes a sometimes boring topic very interesting and relevant. He has real world experience so can easily connect to the material he is teaching and explains how it is used in real life. The cases are manageable.  Exam is sort of difficult but the class is curved. I recommend this professor as he is very passionate about the subject.
This class can be difficult because you really need to be self-motivated. Cases aren't too bad but the midterm is pretty difficult. No final exam though.
Great lecturer. No graded homework or quizzes. No textbook used for the class. The exam is extremely hard. No final. He was funny.

To preface my comments, I had a good amount of education in statistics before taking this course.  That said, Richard is one of the best teaches at the UW.  He made a subject that is traditionally boring interesting and made the class move super quickly.  Definitely would take another course with him.

Very good lecturer, connects concepts in class to work experience and the 'real world' . Very helpful after class or in office hours and an all around great guy. Go to class because the problem solutions aren't on the lecture slides.

he's a really funny and engaging lecturer, but it is very lecture heavy. there's a ton of readings to do every night, but honestly not mandatory since there's no quizzes so they're mostly extra information to know. there's no tests (actually one canvas test, but it's more like if you pay attention then you'll get it) and two essays.

Michael is such a funny professor—one of the most interesting lecturers I've had. Attendance policy only for discussion. He also posts the lecture slides on Canvas. For lecture, he usually just goes over the slides in class, but also adds extra information. Readings are necessary for exams, but can just pull quotes for exams, which are take home.

Lectures are just him reacting to his slides, but still interesting. He's a funny guy. The lectures occasionally drag, especially in the beginning and during the interminable unit on the Philippines, but otherwise engaging. Very low workload. Grades based mostly on discussion participation and no-rubric essays. You learn a lot!
Professor Cullinane is kind and energetic. Office hours are accessible and helpful. A great class for anyone interested in SE Asia!

Very passionate about Southeast Asia. Essay exams based on the readings, but it's not necessary to actually read them; can just pull quotes when writing the essays. Comprehensive lecture slides that lay out the whole picture. Fun guy!

He's probably my favorite professor I've had thus far. You must attend the lecture and take notes because he goes through a lot of information, but it's interesting. He's eccentric: makes a lot of jokes, talks about movies, and gets off topic. In the honors section, he leads the discussion, but he just answers your questions. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Mike is great and passionate. Layout of class is tough, SO many readings and harsh essays. Essays had absolutely no clear criteria or rubric and I would get downgraded for the smallest things, and I had to pry for an explanation. Don't take for an "easy" ethnic studies credit, much better options available. Only plus is zero tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting course content, especially in the readings/memoirs. Rubric requirements not clear for honors section. Grading system not clear. When I asked what an A was for the class he did not have a numerical answer. It seems that grades are decided based on first impressions rather than actual work. Maybe those who had TA had different experiences

His lectures are very long, but is VERY knowledgeable about SE Asia. This class was interesting and you do not necessarily have to read everything he gives you to do well. If you are remotely interested in the subject, take it. Just show up to lecture and go to discussion and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cullinane was funny sometimes, but I've never met anyone who went through content as simultaneously quickly and slowly as he does. The readings were repetitive and boring. He does offer extra credit for people who know more than what's expected, though. Still, I get why people like him and his classes - he's a good guy with good one-liners.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are impossibly dense and long, assigns an unmanageable amount of readings and films, two intense papers due within a week of each other at the end of the semester. Does not grade with a rubric (just how he feels).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Cullinane knows what he's talking about, but his lectures are super long. I have to watch them on 2x speed in order to make it through them without falling asleep. I learned a lot in his class and would recommend it if you're interested, but if you just need a requirement and don't really care about SE Asia, definitely skip it.

Interesting class about Southeast Asia. I waited to long to actually read the books for the fiction project so that stressed me out a little. He's a very good lecturer and encourages students to come and talk to him outside of class. I didn't bother reading most of the articles assigned, as long as you attend class and take notes you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not an intriguing class if you have no interest in Southeast Asia. I definitely learned a lot, despite being bored (through very long lectures). Very knowledgeable professor. You only have to write two papers -- a take-home midterm essay and a writing project. The final is an in-class essay and worth 40% of your grade, use your note sheet well!

Even though I hated the class I took, I absolutely loved Professor Cullinane. I am not a huge history buff but he made it as enjoyable as it could have been with his witty comments and quirky tangents. He also always does review sessions which are an incredible help and it is clear that he wants his students to do well.

Professor Cullinane is an awesome professor. His lectures can get long and he uses no visual aids for lecture, but if you go and take notes it is an easy A. I didn't go to class hardly at all and got the notes from a friend (although I would not advise doing this). Would recommend. DISCUSSION IS MANDATORY.

Cullinane is a very interesting character. He is very knowledgeable about the countries of Southeast Asia. He is a head person at the Center for Southeast Asian Studies in Madison. I learned a lot in this course but the expected time outside of class was pretty ridiculous. Over the course I read a book, 47 articles, and watched 9 docs (all required

He makes the material a lot more interesting that it usually would be, and it's especially helpful that he was so loud as well as added funny commentary to get through the hour and a half long lecture.

This man is amazing! He really knows his stuff, and he's passionate about it, which makes the whole thing less boring than it should be. You may get sleepy, because he talks for an hour and a half, but he'll give you a detailed outline of what we're seeing, including key terms. Expect weekly readings, although his exams are not that tough.

He's like, 80 and hilarious. He'll just stand and talk at you for an hour and half, no power point, so make sure to pay attention in lecture. He has a bad habit of using too many pronouns, so if you zone out for a min you'll come back to a lecture full of "and then they" ,"they did" , etc and you'll never know who "they" are. Overall like the class

Great historian, really makes the history come alive and has fun doing it. He has a movie reference for everything and is very easy to talk to and ask for help or clarification. Doesn't bombard you with work and tries his best to make it easy on you. Take it for honors credit, he teaches the honors discussion and it's easier than the standard.

His roller coaster voice will ceaselessly shift from whisper to shout during his lectures. His endless movie references will make you question whether you have taken a cinematography lecture. His shady FBI history will make you skeptical of his past. All that means is AWESOME prof. Take him. Hail to the chief! Salutes to General Patrick Swayze!

Awesome professor! He is really excited and passionate about teaching the subject. Lectures were very stimulating and I didn't mind that it was a power lecture. The class overall is easy and your grade is based on the TA.

Really awesome lecturer - he will keep you awake even during an early morning power lecture! Class is very interesting but fast paced. If you go to lecture and pick up on the main themes, you'll do fine. Tests are extremely simple and straightforward. Review sessions clear up any confusion. An A is definitely possible with a little effort.

Good guy, interested in the subject and extremely knowledgable.  Helpful outside of class.  Lecture was unorganized, no visual aids or books other than his outlines. Power lecture was painful to sit through, 75 minutes of his random ranting.  Class wasn't difficult, but wouldn't recommend it.  Grade entirely dependent on TA.
Really cool dude. Class is designed to be about what you absorbed, not what you memorize. Overall very interesting and his lectures are informative and hilarious.

A very dynamic lecturer, and a nice guy as well. His lectures are vital for success in his class. He allows students a lot of flexibility in this class, letting them focus on areas that interest them. I'd definitely take him again.
Great prof, really knows what he's talking about. A lot of reading though, and you have to attend lecture. Speaks fast, lectures can be a bit boring but you'll be able to get through it.

Lots of reading.  Speaks very fast during lecture and there is no powerpoint or notes.  But he is hilarious and a great guy.  Very passionate about what he's teaching.  Don't expect an easy A, but it's not too hard.

Really LOVES what he teaches! Speaks incredibly fast so be prepared to take good, quick notes. Lecture is not mandatory, but if you don't go you will fail (no online notes or anything). He goes through material quickly; there is a TON of reading. Midterm was a breeze, but be sure to have a good notecard for the final.

He's a great guy, to be sure, but this class is so unstructured that it's frustrating! Discussions have no relations to lecture, it's frustrating that there doesn't seem to be a rubric for exams that he grades in ways that he likes instead of what you argue. Talk to him in his office hours though and he'll help you out a lot.
Great Prof, very interested in the topic and shows enthusiasm when teaching. Grade based on disc grade, book assignment(2 books), midterm, and final. Learned a lot and enjoyed the class. Take him!

Really good class, learn a lot about Vietnam, The Philippines, Thailand, and Indonesia.  Cheat sheet on final exam so make sure to actually go to lecture and take decent notes.  Overall great professor

This professor was the man! I'm not a history major but I really enjoyed the class. It might seem difficult in the beginning but it gets a lot easier after the midterm. Take good notes because they'll help you out big time...especially for the open note final

AWESOME professor. Loves this subject and makes lectures interesting. He is always available if you need help and will work around your schedule. I had him for discussion in honors section and he'll help you with any questions you have. Also, the tests are only on what he says is on the test. No tricks or games. Great class, great professor!
Professor Cullinane is my hero.  You can't ask for a better prof.  Seriously.

Great class. Lectures are informative and as interesting as a power lecture can be.  The class is easy, with an emphasis on writing with a paper as a midterm, a paper on two books, and a blue book final.  Readings not bad.
Fun, lively guy... makes it easy to do a 9:30 class. Tells the history of a spoonful of sugar and the King and I. open note final
Great professor and a very engaging lecturer.  I'd definitely recommend taking this class-just pray Ruth de Llobet isn't your TA!!

Fantastic professor.  Very funny and excited about the subject, and thrilled to teach you about anything related to SE Asia.  I did very few of the readings, went to every class, and got an A.  Honors section is interesting and fun too.
Easy course.  You don't even have to do the reading as long as you pay attention in lecture and know what each reading is about.  Lectures are pretty good as well.
No Comments
This guy is great, he reminds me of Harry Carey.  He's got a good sense of humor and makes tuesday morning class lots of fun.
Fun, exciting lecture.  Never a dull moment.
Very exciting and dynamic.  Always willing to help students.  Tells you exactly what will be on the final exam ;).

Professor Bronkhorst explains topics concepually, and not just mathematically. He pauses frequently during lectures to ask if students have any questions, so I don't know why people are saying he "refuses to answer questions". He did sometimes cold call on students, especially towards the end of the semester.
Poorly structured course and unnecessarily cruel at times

I would avoid him as a professor if at all possible. He seems to go above and beyond in being harsh to students. Don't ask a question if you don't want a mocking remark or question in return. He is a tough grader and does not allow much for leniency. He definitely creates a toxic learning environment.
Whenever I was waiting for the bus I thought about jumping infront of the cars because I hated this class so much. he also is mean.
bad. just awful.

bad lecturer, rushes through example problems and just assumes we all understood. Doesn't care about his student's success, won't give points back for regrade without the guarantee he won't take any away. Answers questions vaguely or with another question.
Lecture is waste of time, he reads off his slides with no explanation. Just read through the slides or watch online lecture in half the time.

Awful professor. Very difficult to communicate with and was not understanding of students situations. Was completely unhelpful in class. Answered every single question with another question. Did not care about his students learning or success.

He does not like collaboration between students (going against everything about engineering) and refuses to answer questions, so having him as a professor and being taught by a wall is the same thing. He doesn't care for his students well-being and says he is pushing them to be good engineers, but in reality, he pushes them to fail.

Nice course with lots of material. Book is a must. Prof. Bronkhorst taught it well considering the difficulty of the course and he inspires a lot. It's difficult to get much help though, and he expects to resolve ur doubts on your own. Exams are tough (in spite of him saying it's trivial) but he grades genuinely.

Professor Curtis is AMAZING! She is so passionate about what she teaches, and every lecture genuinely makes you think. The exams are difficult, but if you pay attention in class, go to discussions, and study the study guide, you will be fine.  I genuinely learned so much that I didn't care if I didn't get an A because the class was still worth it.

I LOVED Prof Curtis. She is an amazing human, and so passionate about her work that she can make super boring policy stuff super interesting, and makes it matter to you. She is incredible, not enough of that can be said. The two exams are hard, but this class is worth it. The world would be a better place if more people took this class.

Starts every lecture asking "How are you?" Very passionate about her work. The class topic is dry, but lectures are straightforward and make sense. Lots of group work (not graded). Funny and cares a lot about her students. She loves teaching which makes it easier to learn the content. Very responsive to questions and incredibly kind. I loved her.

Class was dry and dragged on, and our only grades were 3 exams. I mostly just didn't like her, though. She was condescending, shouted at us, and stalked around the lecture hall, touching students without consent (grab shoulder, etc.). Also did not honor my McBurney accommodations and accused me of abusing them after missing one lecture with a note.

I loved Prof Curtis!! I did not do well in this class but I would still 100% take it again. She's so passionate about what she's teaching and I learned so much throughout the semester. Your grade is based on 3 exams which make it difficult, but the class is definitely worth taking!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis is AMAZING! She is interesting, articulate, and clearly very knowledgeable about the subject. However, if you do not actually major in Social Work (or something within the social sciences), I would not recommend taking this class. The exams are challenging and also very weighted, it was pretty difficult to get by personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis is an amazing lecturer and probably the best teacher someone interested in social work or policy could have. The class is graded on 2 exams, an essay, and attendance so it's fairly hard to get an A (9% will get an A according to Madgrades). I would still recommend the course though as it's informative and really engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curtis was a good prof however she kind of just rambled on many topics in lectures. Exams were hard and overall I struggled. It's not a class that I hate but she goes through everything super fast during lectures.

Curtis is so passionate and educated. She makes lectures interesting and is a talented speaker. I took this course as an elective and it widened my world perspective and political knowledge. I would recommend that anyone wanting to gain knowledge on the welfare system to take this class.

Marah Curtis is an AMZING professor. But I performed horribly in her class and I don't understand why. She is a very fast paced professor, passionate, fun and has great energy however her exams are very difficult. Maybe its just me but I spent hours and days studying for her exams and performed so bad in them, prepare for lots of reading and notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Graded on 3 things so don't make my mistake and not take something seriously, it's very manageable. Prof Curtis is INCREDIBLE, the most passionate teacher I've had, knows so much about her subject + has real world experience. Lectures were engaging, thought provoking + informative. She's an amazing, intelligent, exuberant professor.

Prof. Curtis is so freaking engaging you will never be bored in her class. She presents the material in such an interesting way and makes it all simple to understand! I feel like this class should be mandatory because it was all really important to know! Take her class! She assigns lots of readings but they're basically optional--not tested on

Professor Curtis is one of the most engaging professors I have had. If it weren't for her intriguing lectures I would have never discovered my passion for policy. She is extremely understanding and truly wants each of her students to exceed. I have yet to meet a professor as passionate about their work and teaching as Curtis. Definitely recommend.

I've never had a more passionate professor at this school! Curtis really cares about the subject matter and the students! She assigns a million readings but honestly, I only did the first 2 readings and I did fine so they really aren't important for the exams. The TAs are great as well and discussions are helpful and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Curtis' grasp of the material and ability to deliver engaging lectures cannot be understated: she is stellar at both. I didn't find the class to be terribly difficult, though her tests are fair & she does a great job of helping you prepare for them. I've never had a professor who matches her enthusiasm & energy; she loves what she does & it shows!!

Marah Curtis is a good professor, but sometimes does not elaborate very clearly on course material. She is very willing to answer questions and make things clear if you ask. The course is very test heavy, as three tests are the only grades that go in.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Curtis was amazing! She had very engaging lectures that made me want to learn more about the material! Readings were long and boring, but supplemental and not tested on. Tests weren't super difficult if you paid attention in class most of the time.

I honestly cannot say enough about Professor Curtis! She is SO knowledgeable and easy to listen to. She is energetic when presenting material and makes you think about the policies/theories from multiple perspectives. Lots of readings, but they just supplemental and aren't tested on. First midterm is straightforward with a decent average. Love her!

I took her class on a whim, but ended up adding social work as a major largely because of this class. She presents the information in a way that keeps you engaged and makes you want to participate/ask questions. She keeps most of her opinions to herself, which I mostly like in a course, but will tell you more in her office hours. Highly Recommend!

Prof Curtis is good at her job. She makes the course about learning, and less about grades. She is clearly very passionate about social policy, which made me more interested. She runs around class a lot, but it's comical so it was fine. Her slides are a tad jumbled, but you're able to figure it out. There was 2 tests & 1 essay. Good class to take!

Professor Curtis is obviously passionate and educated on the material. She has lots of energy, she spends most of class walking or jogging around the class. The only flaw is that she is not great with technology, but she makes up for her in her friendly attitude and patience. Also, class is easy if you have previous government knowledge.

If I wasn't sure I wanted to be a Social Work major before, now there's no doubt. I loved this class and always left feeling (depressed because of our welfare state) but inspired to be a part of real change. She's hilarious, fashionable and incredibly engaging.
Can be rude to students, refuses to provide assistance when asked, makes students feel unworthy.

Prof. Curtis is an absolutely phenomenal instructor. Whether you have a previous interest in social policy or not, you will leave knowing so much more about it and being inspired to learn MORE because of her passion. Extremely intelligent and intriguing professor. Exams are very fair.

AMAZING PROFESSOR. AMAZING. I'd be lucky to grow up to be half of the women that she is.  She is inspiring.  In terms of the class, initially it is kind of intimidating, but she does a great job of making it clear what you need to know.  Everything that she writes in red on her lecture slides (which she posts online) will be on the test.

Professor Curtis is PASSIONATE about social policy. She encouraged student participation, tied in current events to policy issues and attempted to show a few perspectives on a wide range of issues without sharing too much of her own. Highly recommend this course and this professor.

I had no interest in social policy as a social welfare prior to her course but now I am planning on working in social welfare and poverty policy.  The most intelligent and impressive professor I've had, hands down.

Great class! You can tell that she is incredibly knowledgeable and excited about social policy. She teaches policy from a politically neutral stance, which is nice. Lectures are dense and you will learn a lot, but she gives very clear study guides so exams are pretty straightforward/easy. Three exams, one is take home.

Katy is AMAZING! So friendly and engaging. She is also very helpful outside of class. This is a challenging course, but if you take initiative to get help where you need it, she will be there for you to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Katy is a FANTASTIC professor. You have to attend lecture to keep up with important notes, but exams are open book/group work and are pretty easy if you just pay attention. The class is a lot of work and fast-paced, but you learn so much about media law, and Katy is always available for help. She is empathetic and a great lecturer!

I LOVED this class. Ngl after the first week I thought about dropping it because I was so lost but I quickly got the hang of it and turned out to be my favorite class. There are 4 exams for 70% of your grade, a group project, and discussion. This was such an interesting class and Katy and Indi did a great job teaching it. I definitely recommend!

Like some reviews have said, took this class for Katy herself. Awesome professor and lecturer and super knowledgable when it came to media law. I'll admit the topic wasn't for me and I struggled a little bit, but that comes down to if you are interested in the topic. Katy made it as enjoyable as possible, she's one of the best profs in the j-school

While 202 is lots of work, Katy really overexaggerates the level of difficulty. Your grade is entirely dependent on your TA, although most of the TAs are really wonderful. Katy herself is a great professor, but her lectures are kind of irrelevant to the actual course work and if there weren't weekly quizzes, I wouldn't have even bothered going.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: 202 is fine and very much dependent on your TA. Katy is high energy but if her lectures didn't have quizzes I wouldn't have gone to them. Very heavy on the strat comm aspect and a lot less so on the reporting aspect made this class less enjoyable for me. I felt that grading was at times random (but again TA dependent).

She's ok. The comments abt kissing her butt or not existing are so true. Just sitting in her lecture stresses me out. Overall this is not a hard class but boy does she do a good job of making it seem terrifying.

Let's be real I signed up for this class because of her name. Culver is an absolute all-star. I loved going to her lectures because she is so nice, energetic, and knowledgeable. Tests are open note, translates well online, discussions are simple. Could not recommend J563 with Culver more!!

I really like Katy! It's clear that she really cares about her students and that she puts a lot of time and care into preparing for class. J563 itself isn't overly difficult, but you definitely need to put an effort in to receive a good grade. I'd definitely recommend taking this class with her! Super interesting.

It's true that Katy hypes J202 up maybe too much, but if you do engage with the class and put effort in, I think you learn a lot and the class is a positive experience. I think Katy puts an effort into her students and shows that she cares for them. Although I can't speak from experience, I think she is super receptive during office hours

J202 is hard in general, and Katy is very nice, but you really have to figure a lot of this class out on your own. Attendance in lecture is strict, especially because of quizzes--read the news THOROUGHLY every week, because the news quizzes can get unfairly difficult. Her lectures can be engaging and fun but only if you're passionate about SJMC.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Katy is hilarious and makes lectures fly by. She's passionate about media law, and it shows in this class. Super interesting material. Took this class with no background in law/law language and I did fine. Exams are online and you have a couple of days to work on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great  person and clearly knows what she's doing. Kind of disorganized and you never really know what is going on at times and don't know your grade until the end of semester. She is very laid back and personable and her lectures are interesting. Time flies in this class and she sometimes brings snacks which is always a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Katy Culver is fun and keeps class energetic. In all honesty, your TA is what it really going to make it or break it in this class because Katy doesn't do most of the grading. It's obvious Katy has done this class many many times and has things organized as best as she can, but there's too much going on in J202 for it to ever feel organized.
Katy was very helpful when coming into office hours, but lecture is pretty pointless. Her deadlines and expectations are not very well laid out.

First of all, J202 sucks. Second, she is a very nice, impassioned professor.  There is too much information from every authority in this class, so they need better management and corporation. Her requirements are not systematic, unified and clear enough.

Katy Culver is one of the best professors on this campus. She engages the class and has fun with her job, which makes it easier for us to be receptive students. She's all about social media and loves hearing from students outside of class. Awesome class experience. Learn her sense of humor and you'll be set.

Katy Culver is one of the worst professors I have had at UW- Madison thus far in my academic career. She has you do stupid tutorials to learn dreamweaver yet they don't teach you anything except for changing the color to pink. She picks favorites and crosses the teacher/student line by contacting them via text, twitter etc.

Decent teacher in that she is clear and makes herself available for students, but she's also delusional about her own greatness.  Loves to say her own name and thinks she's too cool to reply to your emails with more than about three words.  She's alright but definitely not a standout teacher.

Here's the thing: Katy's actually really nice and really willing to help. It's J202 that sucks, which try as she might, cannot and will not change. Readings aren't necessary. Everything counts for a fraction of your grade, and your experience will totally depend on your TA. Just try to enjoy taking a class that's basically taught by your mom.

Katy pours her life into J202, making it a course that shows you the ropes of media regardless of if you are taking the reporting or strat com track. You will write A LOT and have multiple assignments simultaneously. Go into office hours and speak with her- she wants you to succeed and will go the extra mile to help you become a better communicator
Culver is pretty high-energy and enthusiastic about the things she's teaching.

I can't believe the ease rating for this is in the 2's!  Katy was a great professor! J202 was not a hard class.  It's a demanding class.  There's quite a big difference.  I'd say most journalism majors on campus would agree that generally our coursework is pretty easy.  The hard part is juggling the amount of work with your internships, jobs etc...
Katy is a great professor. She has high expectations and will work you hard, but she also works incredibly hard and has high expectations for herself.

Katy is an excellent teacher who makes herself as available as possible to her students. That being said, J202 takes a tremendous amount of work and effort.  The JSchool advisers aren't lying when they tell you this.  Expect to pull many all-nighters if you're unable to budget your time. Listen to her podcasts as well--they really help!

Katy is a GREAT professor.  She really inspires interest in the coursework.  She shares a great amount of knowledge and expertise in the subject. She's also available for help and questions pretty much all the time. Plus, she's hilarious.  Overall, a great professor.

Katy knows her stuff and is very approachable. The class is a major time-commitment, but it is great for preparing students. Overall, she is very nice and a wealth of information. I was blown away reading some of the "full-of-herself" comments - didn't get that vibe at all. Highly recommended!

Most of what Katy has to say is totally up-to-date and relevant. In a class of over 100 people, if you want her to remember you, you have to make yourself known to her, but you certainly don't have to suck up. However, you must do your work. She has stern rules about labs, homework and quizzes, but she will bend them in truly extreme circumstances.

If you're a big suck up, you'll like her and she'll like you. She thinks she "saved" the journalism department and thinks she's the greatest professor ever. If you hate people who are full of themselves, you'll probably hate her. She talks fast, doesn't teach much of anything at all and is just plain obnoxious. She's right, you're wrong.

Katy Culver is an amazing human being with an amazing heart.  If anyone takes one minute to conference with her about her past jobs you will learn she is a skilled communicator and the perfect professor to guide incoming j-students along the right path...

I liked Katy a lot, but I can def. see how her personality turned a lot of people off. She can be a little full of herself, but I've never actually had a negative experience with her. I actually decided to take her magazine class with her next semester, so I'll have a better impression of her soon.

BOO to all of you who see her as "inspirational" because she is very transparent. She'll love you if you brown nose her (which it sounds like you do from your comments) and she'll forget who you are if you don't. If you want to be like her, I am nervous for you.
just not that good
Yes, she is a bit out there, but Katy knows her stuff... just because some of you did poorly in her class doesn't mean you have to knock on her

While the class was very helpful, Katy Culver was one of the worst professors ever.  As the core class of the J-school is 202, Katy is high on her horse thinking she is the best thing since sliced bread.  If you kiss her butt she will love you, otherwise you don't exist to her.
No Comments

Katy is an awesome professor.  She has tons of energy and keeps class interesting.  Although the structure of J202 is weird (ex: grading system), it's still a great class.  Definately preps you to be a journalist.  I loved the class and the professor.

This is a teacher who thrives on her own "wit" , is self-cogratulatory, and could care less about struggling students. Some people go into teaching for status-this is one of them. Run as fast as you can

Dr. Rick Curry is a fantastic professor! His online class is very organized and easy to follow. Each week you are assigned to watch a lecture video that he puts together, write a reflection on the lecture, and complete a Connect assignment. No tests, easy assessment grades, and extra credit. Highly recommend his class!
Best Professor I have EVER had. Take any class he offers and you'll find out why. He could make "Introduction to Watching Paint Dry" your favorite class of the week.

I took Rick for Gen Bus 300 and LOVED it. Even when Rick is lecturing to the whole class he makes it feel like he is speaking to you as an individual which makes you feel really valued in his classes. He helped good and bad public speakers improve throughout the semester with precise feedback and encouragement. Highly recommend.

Rick is probably the best professor I have had here at UW. He is extremely intelligent and tells it how it is, yet he makes it clear he truly cares about his students. He challenges you in the best ways and does a good job of creating a positive and fun atmosphere. Very unconventional. Very real. Shares life lessons. Absolutely amazing.
Rick is one of the best professors I have had at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. If other teachers were as realistic and passionate as he was, I would never miss a class.

Rick was a great professor that made boring subject matter enjoyable. Great sense of humor and general attitude towards the course material. He is also very passionate about communication and really tries to help students see its purpose in Business.

Rick is definitely one of the best professors I've had here. The class itself isn't too interesting as it's a required class about professionalism, but Rick does a phenomenal job teaching it. He has a lot of experiencing with professionalism in the business world and cuts through all the crap and tells you how it is.  Super helpful and funny.

Prof Cveykus is my all time favorite professor at UW. He knows his stuff beyond belief and makes it actually fun to follow and learn. While it is true he sometimes talks a bit fast, he will answer any questions both inside and outside of class. I would take him in any Poli Sci class. His class was the one I looked forward to every week
The man lectures at a million miles a minute

Prof. Cveykus is my favorite prof at UW-Madison to date. Hilarious, knows his stuff, and very accessible outside of class. Grade is based on just 3 exams, but they are take home, and the criteria is pretty clear. He also offers an extra credit assignment that can add up to 3% to your final grade. Highly recommend to anyone with a passion for law.
Cindy was so caring and amazing, she is such a great advocate for her students and is always willing to work with you so you are successful. You would be lucky to get her as your instructor!

Cindy is a great teacher; she is very caring about her students and will challenge you to improve. I felt lucky to have her as my clinical instructor because she created a supportive yet motivating environment that pushed me to grow both personally and professionally. Her guidance, patience, and dedication truly made a lasting impact on me.

I had Cindy for clinical this semester and she was amazing! She was incredibly caring for her students and always made sure we had what we need to be successful. She is very flexible and understanding of things happening in life and willing to work with you to get caught up. You would be so lucky to have Cindy!

His lectures feel longer than they need to be, and yet attending them is still critical. Despite considerable use of R in this course, we're only taught the bare minimum required for assignments. Exam grading criteria is considerably tougher and more mysterious than homework grading. Show up to everything and do your best with what you're given.

Prof. Culberston was actually one of my favorite professors this semester. Culbertson. Prof. Culbertson had an excellent course layout, exams were identical to the homework and things we did in class. He is very responsive on Piazza, and attendance is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely attend lectures, or you probably won't pass. The material is tough, but he does a good job explaining the material in class. Homework assignments pretty much follow the examples from lecture, and doing well on those will help keep your grades up. The class is certainly work, but it's not impossible.

By far the most confusing stats class I have taken. The material itself is not hard but the professor made the class impossible. He literally had the most confusing ways of explaining incredibly simple topics. His teaching style was very convoluted and all lectures were read off a script.

I found his slides really helpful and easy to grasp. I thought the homework grading was a little strange and inconsistent, but if you want to discuss your homework with him, he is ready and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Initially I thought he was okay but his grading makes absolutely no sense. I went to all office hours to get the homework done (where the TAs basically walk through the hw) and still got Cs on a lot of assignments. He's inconsistent about grading and doesn't explain concepts to the standard that he expects you to understand them.

He definitely didn't start out good, but toward the end he was great! I think it was his first semester teaching. He uses TopHat in lecture in a way that makes learning the material so much easier. The homeworks are EXACTLY like the tests, which are also open note. The lectures are pretty straightforward which is nice for the exams.

In the beginning of the semester, I really did not like the teacher. I thought the class was super hard and I didnt understand a thing he was talking about. Thats until I actually started looking into what he was talking about. The language he uses may be sophisticated, but the material is actually easy. And the test is open to all recourses!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Culbertson's lecture slides are very vague and his explanations in class make concepts seem more complicated then they really are. Key to this class is staying organized. Tests are open note and discussion + lecture quizzes are easy to do well on if you keep up but homework was hard to do alone, find a study group for this class for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Did not have a great experience in Stat 371 with Culbertson. I found his lecture slides very unhelpful, resources to prepare for the exam confusing and not related to how the exam actually was, and just overall not the best teacher. My one positive I have for him is that he was very accessible during office hours. Avoid taking his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Culbertson is a friendly guy, helpful in a 1 on 1 setting, but not a good lecturer. He uses a power point that gives you little to work with. However, the way he teaches the classes forces you to engage and actively think about topics. If you get him, utilize office hours and meet with him outside of class for help and you'll be good.

Professor Culbertson is rarely prepared for lecture and most materials are prepared within 24 hours so students have little time to complete them. He is not a good lecturer and often struggles to explain concepts to students. Grading is not timely, and exams are much different than other homework and material in class. Find another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Culbertson read off of his computer for the entirety of his lectures making it very hard for students to follow along. Get ready to hate TopHat. Dr. Culbertson gives TopHat quizzes every lecture. These questions are extremely difficult. He will explain the question concepts after he gives the question. Homework takes 5-10 hours each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Culbertson's lectures can often be a little tricky and leave you more confused than when you came. The homework assignments connect to class work loosely and are somewhat difficult to comprehend, since they're never discussed in discussion. However, Professor Culbertson is respectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Culbertson is a genuine person, and I believe he cares about his students. However, his lectures are very difficult to understand. He speaks hypothetically and does not offer many real life examples. His responses in piazza are often vague. Stats is a difficult course to teach but there is room for improvement. Test are open resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think people are pretty harsh on him and he's not a bad professor at all. Some of his wording is super confusing and convoluted, but you can start to understand his language as the course progresses. He includes everything you need in the lecture slides; he's pretty well organized. Overall he's kind of funny but definitely not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Culbertson is an extremely genuine guy and its clear that he cares about the success of his students. I truly dont understand the bad reviews he gets. Exams are online and open note. You have every resource available to you to succeed. Lectures can be tricky, but its because he wants you to think and not be spoon fed like high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are often confusing and are made to confuse students by going over why each question could possibly be right. Top hat are graded and often not explained, thus, you have to go back into your own time and re-do quizzes to get back points that you missed that were way out of your control to earn. DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PROFESSOR!

Lectures consist of reading off an script and attempting to confuse students with answers. Participation is at an all time low and no one wants to answer any of his questions because no one knows what he's talking about. Homework is often long and not explained in class. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got a 5 on the AP Stats test in HS & I think this prof made Stats way harder than it should be. Culby CAN'T teach. He reads off a script during lectures (using unnecessarily big words to make him seem smarter)&grades understanding of new material DURING lecture. Don't try to ask him a question, bc he will not know the answer. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frustrating and difficult course. Does not explain concepts well nor does he give us the right answers for tophat, which is also graded on accuracy based off concepts we have not learned. Lectures are not recorded so if you miss class, good luck. Slides make 0 sense and is extremely unhelpful. Everyone is confused in this class. Don't take stat371.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am appalled at such a terrible professor that is even allowed to "teach" his students. This is not teaching. I have put in timeless hours for this class and am still almost failing. Someone needs to report his "teaching" as this is disturbing to see as a part of the statistics community here. Students deserve better,give us an A,and stop teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have never, ever taken a class with a more dysfunctional professor and curriculum. I thought I was taking statistics, and I did not know that there wouldn't even be math or anything logical. Never have I ever had a professor teach me histograms for an hour and be confused on it, HOW DO YOU MAKE HISTOGRAMS CONFUSING? You attend lecture or fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He could talk for hours but never really say anything at all. avoid at all costs

The way he lectures makes no sense and is really difficult to follow and understand. All the practice problems you do in class and for homework are COMPLETELY different than what you will see on the exams. The exams are from left field and make no sense. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF
Grades understanding in lectures but doesnt even teach the content beforehand, presents a slideshow instead of teaching the content, unclear about a lot of the content even after explaining it
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader,wouldnt recommend.Worst grader i had in college.
She is a nice prof and patient to students but her grading is wayyyyyyy tooooooo tough than we should get and I don't understand why we did such a good job but only got like B or BC
Somewhat difficult grades and the presentations are annoying but very nice person and always willing to help.
Efforts never paid off.  Grading is not quite fair and you never know what she is expecting. Assignment schedule is clear though.
Pretty easy class, didn't have many assignments but when you do they're large. Seems easy to pull a B but difficult to get an A
She is pretty good. Class is way harder than what a 2 credit Comm A class should be. I honestly would have rather taken Comm A 100. I recommend the prof but not the class

Cindy is really great. Class is easy if you just listen to her in class and do what she tells you to in class. Overall very passionate. Class can get boring and there are some pointless assignments, but it is impossible to get lower than a B with with cindy and an A is easily attainable.

As someone who doesn't have natural speaking talents, this class was difficult to do well in. She increases the grading standards with each speech, so effort and improvements throughout the semester don't really improve your grade. However, people who are naturally good public speakers could get high grades with very little effort.
The class sucked and was incredibly boring but she made it just about as easy as she could. I don't think it was even possible to get lower than a B on a presentation.

If you have a chance of taking EPD 397 with Poe, YOU TAKE IT!! She's super easy, super chill and very lenient. She can spot out slackers easily and will make it difficult for you if you don't do the work. Just show her that you're making an effort and doing what she wants you to do, you'll get an A/AB. She's the easiest EPD397 professor, SO TAKE IT

She handed out a 24 page single spaced syllabus at the beginning of the semester. WHAT? It has everything, homework, guidelines, and all. If you ask her about the assignments she'll just refer to it. She's able to teach engineers but I didn't find her helpful when it came to asking about written work. She plans great presentation assignments though

She understands that we are engineers, not english majors and grades very fair. This class is a lot of work for only 3 credits but it does help with writing/presenting skills. Talk with her after class/in office hours, she will help you a lot with your projects. I recommend taking this class with her.

She grades pretty easily so if you did well in english in high school, you should get at least a B. Since it's an english class for engineers, she kind of assumes everyone is stupid.  Some assignments in class are pointless though.
Semi tough, good professor, always willing to help out of class if you are struggling.

By habit, I never missed a single college lecture or discussion.  Prof. Pondrom, made it easy to want to go to the lectures.  I gained lifelong analytic and critical thinking skills which I've applied to as wide ranging areas as business management, computer programming and even parenting.  Prof. Pondrom sought and rewarded devotion to the material
She has only ever treated me with contempt.

Sadly, I liked poetry until I took this class. Pondrom is old and extremely wise, but a very poor communicator. Syllabus was constantly revised, midterm exams were NEVER returned, papers were returned WEEKS later. Clear expectations were not laid out. If you don't mind disorganization, this could be a fascinating class. 2 exams, 2 papers.

I'm a slacker by nature - i'm an abstract thinker who would rather be out in the sun than in a classroom. With that said, Prof. Pondrom has been one of the few (if not the only) prof at Madison who has inspired me to not only attend every one of her lectures, but also challenge the work given to us. She really is a great teacher, hard, but great.
She is an incredible teacher. Does a great job of bringing abstract concepts into an understandable realm. She is adept at facilitating discussion. Really knows her stuff yet isn't too intimidating.

She has so much knowledge on the subjects that she teaches, but explains it on too high of a level. I read all of the texts and was unsure of how I could contribute to the discussion. I often felt out of place and that everyone else had this hidden knowledge about what we were discussing

An absolutely wonderful professor. Very willing to help students with their problems and, let's face it, anyone who makes the avant-garde approachable has to be good. Her lectures are always interesting and insightful. Great at facilitating class discussion. If you want to learn a lot in a short period of time, I highly recommend her class!

Fantastic clarifier of poetry, great at reading it, and it's always great fun to hear early 20th century poetry in a Texan accent. Delightful, and a great teacher. Whether you're bored in her class or not depends almost entirely on if you like the poet she's currently on.

she is wonderful. very involved with t.s. eliot scholarship and knows her stuff.  in her class you definitely will not spend time looking at the clock.  she is excellent at both instructing and guiding class discussion.  does a fantastic job of helping students illuminate the literature for themselves.
I found Prof. Miller clear, helpful and rigorous.

Her powerlectures were the most boring class I have taken in 5 years at UW by FAR.  Every day is like pulling teeth.  We talk about such basic stuff over and over and over and over.  Unless this is a requirement, do not take it.  I took it so I could learn about the bible and all we learned was remedial english skills with TONS of busy work.

It was an ok class but it got really boring at times. lectures and readings are an example of the boringness! not an overly bad class and i felt she was nice and could be helpful at times.  it wasn't something i particularly enjoyed but it might be for you.

I've never had a professor before that so clearly disliked teaching her subject.  She was extremely unflexible about providing a make-up date for the final exam for a student who needed an emergency medical procedure done the day of the exam.  She was so unkind about it she made the student cry.
Awesome professor, really knows her stuff. Also, she is super friendly and easy to talk to. Take time and talk to her after class if you have time. I would highly recommend her and this class.
Cynthia is super awesome and her classes are very easy. You lead two discussions and write one 8-10 page paper graded on completion. Probably my favorite UW professor of all time

CNS SCI 357- retail theory- is a really easy class to earn an A in if you do the textbook reading. You only meet once a week and she writes notes on the board each class that she copies exactly into her exams. She wants her students to do well and she cares about what she teaches!
Very easy A but you won't learn much. Nice professor, but doesn't understand the material

One of the worst lecturers at the university. She's kind but doesn't seem to grasp the content well and is disorganized. Exam work must be done 'her way.' The class is required for BME majors, so you can't avoid her. The TAs seem aware of the situation and do their best to teach what they can in their sections. Most likely should not be employed.
