Professor Suarez explains the course concepts very well (including complex concepts such as fluid dynamics and mass transport) very well and solves problems during lecture in a clear, stepwise manner to further elucidate these topics. Prof. Suarez is also very accessible outside of class and gives good advice about how to prepare for exams.
Dr Suarez is a great person and teacher. She is ready to help and has a great positive attitude. She gives great feedback and supports your projects.
This was a "flipped classroom" that was entirely group projects with random groups. I would faster drop FHCE than take this course again. Not a good use of my busy semester

No need for explanation, she actually made class feel rewarding. As someone with senioritis, Im not the biggest fan of homework, until her class. her assignments are simple, and the grup work is heavty but very effective in keeping brain retention and actually learning

Dr. Warmath was one of my favorite profs at UGA and one of the nicest down to earth people. She was easy to reach out to and helped anytime you would need it. The class was not too hard, but required attendance to participate in group projects almost every class. I would take her class again.

Took FHCE 4100/6100 at UGA for my minor course and it was 100% group project all semester with an individual project at the end. She was an awesome professor that mainly graded us clearly alongside her asst. professor Chen. Would take this class again!

To be clear, I am a UGA student since she is at UGA now. She is always busy, so she has no time for us. She is interested in everything, every topic, every person, every work that makes her busier. I don't think she is interested in teaching, so I learned nothing, but an easy A class. I wish she knew how to pick and choose, focus, and organize.

Dee is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at UW. The class is basically one big group project though, and sometimes the grading can be a bit ambiguous. The exam wasn't too bad, but the topics on it could have been explained a bit better. Just do the pre-recorded lecture notes every night before class and you'll be fine.
She is so amazing at what she does. She's very knowledgeable at everything she teaches. You can learn so much from her; I regret not taking more of her classes.

So at first I was going to drop CS301 It is literally so hard if youve never taken a Stats class or dont have excel experience. She moves really fast through examples and youre at risk of falling super behind during lecture. However, if you have a solid group you can get an A and Dee is super super caring and is always willing to help. I got an A!

This special topics class was a semester long group project. It is not that it was hard, it is just that when Dee attempts to explain things, she talks in theory and goes off on these rants that never seem to add up. It seemed that every time we went to Dee for questions we left with more, she always made us more confused. No class structure.

Dee is extremely helpful and well respected by her students. Advanced Consumer Analytics was a special topics course using excel and working in small groups. Material was tough and a bit confusing at times but she is always willing to help (even if that means calling her at  home - very willing) Her feedback and help on the projects was the best.

Very knowledgeable and experienced in retailing. However, she is a tough grader. You work in class covering different channels in the retail industry and giving a group presentation after each channel. Bad group=Bad grades.

This class is not easy. Sometimes the homework takes several hours to complete. However, I really enjoyed Professor Dennis's classes. I was very interested in what he taught. He gave many extra credit opportunities, so it wasn't difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really cares about his subject, sometimes meanders in lecture but generally covers all the material you need to know. A couple essays, two exams, one final paper, and no final exam. Great guy honestly
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were very interesting. There's no exams in this class, just a final paper.

Having taken history courses previously, I was not expecting this course to be this hard. He's very knowledgeable but not great at explaining how to do these convoluted research assignments. HW was laborious & sometimes I was straight-up unable to figure it out. Only got an A cause my paper was good. He's probably better on non-201 courses though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cool dude, knowledgeable and visibly cares about teaching. Read the syllabus, it tells you in-lecture quizzes and due dates. Had to write a couple essays but they weren't too difficult honestly. Exams were ok; some topics weren't covered much in class but he tells you what he's testing ahead of time. Lots of reading, but not always necessary.
Dennis may be a kind person. His lecture is not pretty relevant to the quiz and exam. Dennis never let you know his exceptation on homeworks, but grade strict.
Lots of reading. Lectures are dense but interesting. Brings in props and keeps it interesting. Quizzes on reading. Papers are hard because of the history aspect.

He is a great, well-informed professor, genuinely nice, and caring.  He gives up to 5 points of extra credit if you attend outside talks. The tests are easy if you study for them. The reading is quite heavy tho but I was able to do fine with little reading. There are lots of quizzes in discussions and the ta is nice and smart! Shout out to Tobin!

Dennis is a good guy, know lots of stuff even outside his own expertise. A new course so bumps were expected, but he handled them well. There will be quiz on the reading, so make sure u do it. Possible exam questions were given beforehand, if reviewed it won't be hard. Gives extra credit for going to talks about EA history, so why not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Dennis is great. The class is technically mandatory to attend and to read a decent amount but he really never took attendance and only gave a few reading quizzes, with most being towards the beginning of the semester. His lectures are interesting and he really enjoys Chinese history which helps make the class more enjoyable. Take it!

The course was majority guest lectures, so the curriculum did not go together and each lecture was irrelevant to the previous one. Lots of readings that you are quizzed on. Some of them are easy and others ask such specific questions that all you could do was guess. Only take if you are thoroughly interested in East Asia or have previous knowledge.

Easy class and he offers a lot of extra credit. Not sure if attendance is mandatory it says it is in the syllabus but doesn't seem to take it. Keeping up with readings is necessary but otherwise most of the assignments are easy and graded easy.

History 201 was very interesting. The class as a whole was not that difficult. If you come to lectures, do the assignments and listen you will be fine. He doesn't provide clear directions for assignments which I found annoying but a lot of people liked because it left it up to your interpretation. Great guy  overall!

Great professor fun class, we got to go visit a Buddhist temple, which could seem dumb but it was fun and a life changing experience. I now know a ton about Buddhism just from meeting that monk and my life is changed forever. Some really interesting reading material, first exam was hard second one wasn't because you're used to it.

Great professor with lots of knowledge on chinese history.  His lectures are pretty interesting. The readings are the hardest part of the class because they are very long and sometimes not very interesting.  I would recommend this class only to those interested in history.

Class is interesting but his lectures are not organized at all and he tends to tell stories about his experiences that don't pertain to the what is on the exam. Discussion wasn't much better. It helps if you know all the important (talked about within a paragraph or multiple pages) people/events and dates.
He's a really nice guy but gives you almost no explanation about assignments or his expectations for an assignment.
Very knowledgeable and willing to talk with you about topics.  Seems like a nice guy but exams are based off reading not lecture, so make sure you read all 4 textbooks that are assigned.
Great, knowledgeable professor who never comes off arrogant. One of the nicest professors I know. Only downside is sometimes his requirements are not always clear. Highly recommend!

Professor Delgadillo kept me engaged in lectures every day! I loved our discussions, and most of the books we read are ones I would have finished even if it wasn't for class. There were questions we had to answer and have ready to discuss at the beginning of class. Our bigger assignments were a panel presentation and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Delgadillo was one of the best professors I've had to date, she was kind, caring and really tried to get her students out of their comfort zones which I appreciated. I am taking a class with her next semester and am beyond excited to be taught by her again!!

Lots of Extra credit.
Class is cross listed as 6 different things and only one topic is taught.
requires AI and never shuts up.

I ended up dropping the class because she was a hard ass about attendance. i lived 25 minutes away (mind you in -20 degrees) and she expected you to be in class on time (like not even a minute late) or your grade would drop a whole letter grade. it was too risky. also a lot of unnecessary work and i didn't learn much in the time i was in class.

Deb is respected, kind, and very helpful. You really do learn a ton about PR in this course, but it is A LOT of work. Genuinely feels like an unpaid internship since you are creating a plan for a real client and have to rely on group members to pull their weight. Stress of the workload really adds up if you're taking other high-level classes.

Deb is my favorite J-School lecturer. She was super caring for me as a student and wanted the best learning experience for all of her students. I learned a lot and she is very passionate about her teaching. Deb is amazing and knows a lot about her topic. Would def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We had real client this semester, and except the first few classes she introduced the brief of the client, she didn't teach anything except give the class time as work time. She 100% supported and gave feedback to media relations team but almost ignored the other two groups which are creative and social media team. I learned 0 PR knowledge!

Deb thinks that her class should be her students #1 priority during a global pandemic, and dismisses any class concerns by saying were all busy, ignoring the lives and experiences of students. She also has 0 regard for the ethical implications of Public Relations she condoned marketing a psychoactive substance to addicts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Deb is tough, almost like a real-world boss because that's what she expects from her students, but will give good feedback if you really present yourself as willing to learn from her. A portion of your overall grade is professionalism in class. She's an easy grader and genuinely wants the best for her students, but definitely has favorites.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Interest in advertising doesn't matter- being a teachers pet does. J449 was one of the least positive college experiences I've had. The guidance on putting together strategies and research would have made sense if the client didn't suck (a real agency wouldn't take that work). Group work is very dog eat dog. Deb was not very accommodating at all.

She is very passionate about what she teaches and if you show interest and enthusiasm, she will like you. She is willing to communicate and negotiate if you come to her reasonably and respectfully. Never had a prof more willing to mold assignments and deadlines to the stress levels of her students. Class gives you real-world work experience

Great class,  great real-world experience. You're assigned to an "agency" team with a few other students who you'll be working with the entire semester, and you work for a real client. If you work well in a group, you'll do fine in this class. Deb can be a little unclear sometimes, but nothing an email or question after class can't fix.

By far the greatest class I've taken at UW.  Deb managed to recruit a real client for us to work for all semester, making it feel like our work really mattered.  Deb goes above and beyond to help students develop both in the classroom and professionally.
Deb is a good teacher and a relatively easy grader.  She is always willing to help when you don't understand something. I had her for 2 classes and I would definitely recommend her.

Probably the worst 'professor' I have had in college. There are no redeeming qualities to her teaching style -- she manages to be both condescending and totally incoherent at the same time. The book is hardly used, except for trick questions on her exams. Also, no matter what size the class is, there is only a 25% chance she'll know your name.

The worst instructor I have ever had!  She thinks that the only thing you have to do is her class and assigns ridiculous amounts of homework.  She plays favorites so much it is disgusting, and can't take any student feedback that doesn't worship her.  Avoid her classes at all costs, trust me.
Great Professor, difficult content but makes it very easy to understand and doing the problem sets and practice exams sets you up very well for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kimberly is amazing, the exams are really hard but the content is just meant to be hard. It is also a tough transition from bowman's 343 because the classes annd exams  are structured very differently. However, if you go to lecture and do the review material the class is really not bad.

Kimberly was the best professor I have had yet at UW. She doesn't go too fast, her lectures are organized, and she is always open to answer any questions I had. The content was heavy, but she taught it very well.
Best prof ever

shes a good professor who cares a lot about her students. the exams however can be extremely difficult and its unclear what you need to know, as lecture alone is not enough to understand exam content. i'd def recommend doing problem sets ahead of time. exams are curved significantly so i'd say an a isnt impossible. also love her humor

Deglopper balances her in-depth explanations of chemistry with useful techniques and examples of reactions. Her lectures are concise and structured. Exams however, were extremely difficult, with averages in the 50s and 60s due to an extremely specific rubric. However, the class is graded on a curve, so an A is very much attainable if you work hard.

I would die for Kimberly. Had her for both 343 and 345 and her courses are hard but she really puts effort in to teach help you understand. She is always on her piazza grind, answers emails quickly, always helpful in office hours. You can tell she really enjoys what she's teaching and I love her awkward jokes. Ochem was hard but she made it better.

Focuses on why things happen, not just memorization, which is great. That said, if you're going to try to memorize things anyway instead of understanding, you probably will not have a good time. Her exams are very fair, and you will learn a TON from her if you're willing to put in the work!

Prof. DeGlopper is a fun educator who clearly explains the material. This is a tough course, but she makes it bearable. She is very available outside of class and offers incredibly helpful grade reports after each quiz/test to measure where you are at in the course. Very few graded works, so be prepared to study lots, which she is super helpful in
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knows the material, helpful, does her best to make sure everyone has the tools necessary to do the work. If people are complaining it's probably because the material is difficult (welcome to Ochem).

Her lectures are clear and move at a good pace. She explains material very well. She is very kind and accessible outside of class. The course expectations were reasonable. If you put in the time to learn and understand the content and get help, you can get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Deglopper is incredibly caring and knowledgeable. After taking ochem 1 with a prof who didn't truly aid me in my understanding of the material, she has entirely reversed how I think and feel about organic chemistry. Content is always difficult, but exams are fair, and she is reachable outside of class. Would definitely recommend!
Chem 345 is very difficult but she is a very good professor and really puts in the time. She also has funny, awkward jokes.

Very good lectures, focused on understanding the material over pure memorization. You need to actually learn the content, not just memorize mechanisms. The grading is interesting, due to the very large standard deviations on the exams there is quite a push to the mean. You have to be really good to get an A and preform quite poorly to get a C or D.

Professor Deglopper is a remarkably good o-chem teacher, her lectures and lecture style is very informative and not memorization based. She also cares a lot about the students, which in my opinion is rare for professors here, I highly advise you to take this class, it's actually quite enjoyable.

You can tell she enjoys the subject and that helps get students more engaged. Because your grade is on so few things, quizzes and exams only, it is up to the student to utilize the very many different resources provided to keep up. That works well for me, but I can see it being an issue for people who can't manage time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's nice and fair. There are a lot of tools to help with practice. There's no surprises on the tests that haven't been talked about. Just pay attention, ask questions, and do the practice. She knows the subject and is happy to help. I only wish the time for tests was longer because I couldn't finish it.

She's a girl boss, but she is a hard professor. Be aware to spend a lot of outside time reteaching yourself concepts from Ochem 1. Do ALL the practice quizzes and exams multiple times; it's the best way to grasp the concept and learn it. Piazza is a huge tool, so USE IT. She's really good about answering questions on there. Also, use office hours!

I hope you love teaching yourself organic chemistry. Material covered in lecture is like 2% of what they expect you to know and Discussions will take an hour to get through a single problem and leave you hanging. I guess they expect you to get actually taught in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures don't really cover what she tests on, and it's not in the book or OChem 1. The lectures are really just her walking through practice problems that don't entirely cover what she expects you to know.  Just be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr. DeGlopper is an amazing professor for Chem 343! The class is difficult, but she explains things really well and at a good pace (she doesn't talk too fast, and she writes out everything on the slides so it's easy to follow along if you're taking notes). Going to lecture or watching the recording is super helpful because she's a great teacher!

She is probably the best professor I've ever had. Genuinely such a nice person who always tried her best to help you understand the material. If you have the opportunity to take her section definitely do it because she's the best!

Dr Deglopper is such a nice professor. I would choose to have her again so fast. Ochem is hard obviously but she breaks it down very well and I grades fairly. I would say reading the textbook is not necessary, but going to lecture and maybe even rewarching it is. Also always go to discussion. There are always test like questions gone over.

Very good at lecturing and takes her time to go through each reaction and draw out the process. The material itself can be tough but really not that bad if you know how to study - I found it much easier than both semesters of gen chem. She's also very clear about what you need to know for exams and what is just extra information.

She is equipped to teach 343, but not 345. Highlights irrelevant things outside the scope of 345, very hard exams (avg~40%) & lectures move very fast. Tried to blame students for the low avgs- The students taking OChem2 are not slackers, they want to go to med school, etc. - No accountability for poor teaching. Do all of the problem sets you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Professor Deglopper. Her lectures went at a good pace and were easy to understand. She throws in a lot of funny little personal stories that help students connect with her even in a large lecture based class. I wish I could take more chemistry classes with Professor Deglopper

All the Chem 345 reviews are tweaking cause that is nothing close to what me and my peers experienced in 343. Very clear lectures and extremely helpful in office hours, and only having exams being graded was great because you could booze on the weekends and not worry about 1000 pre lab/lec assignments.

Graded by only a few quizzes and exams. She is quite kind and caring professor who is willing to help, but her grading is incredibly strict, and her exams are unnecessarily difficult. I believe that if the average is as low as it was, then you are no longer appropriately testing students' knowledge. Study lots, she will throw curveballs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did well in this course but most everyone did not do great. (45% exam avgs) The exams are insanely difficult but problem sets and intensive reviewing can help. Kimberly is sweet and cares but struggles to hammer down course material if u get what I mean

She struggles to teach the scope of 345. In lecture, you're fighting to keep up with copying down what she's writing on slides. Gives unnecessary info about reactions or just doesn't complete them. Takes no accountability for low test scores, blames students for not studying properly (averages for exams were ~40%). Wouldn't recommend for 345
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I learned so much from Kimberly. She and Esselman worked so well together and answered all of my questions. If you have the chance to take her as a professor, please do.  Ochem is hard but I went to her office hours and learned so much.
The way the chem department works is weird, so I wasn't able to have her as my actual professor, but I love her

Dr. Deglopper was very clear in her lectures. They were certainly a little monotone and boring at times, but she did a good time of emphasizing the important concepts. Exams were very difficult, they all had averages in the 50s but the class is curved. She is very good at answering questions and very responsive on piazza and in emails.

Dr. Deglopper is a very succinct lecturer who understands what is important for students to know and the most effective ways to teach concepts, making the complexities of organic chemistry manageable. In office hours, she interprets student questions and explains them fully when necessary, ensures sure that key exam concepts are emphasized.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: she is very clear and organized in lecture!!!!!!!!

Kimberly was awesome (better than Bowman in my opinion). She cares about students and is very organized and provides lecture slides to follow during class. She answers questions well and responds to emails quickly. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kimberly was a very good lecturer, writes out live notes on lecture slides, makes it clear what we need to know. Also answers questions well.

Professor DeGlopper gives good lectures and is helpful in office hours. O Chem is not an easy class, but she makes expectations clear and tells you what you need to do to succeed(do the problem sets!). The practice tests and quizzes are very similar to the actual tests and quizzes. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kimberly is an amazing professor. She writes out her notes live during lectures so they are very easy to follow, she clearly cares about her students and is very willing to take and answer questions during lecture. She has high expectations but they are made very clear. There are also practice exams that are very reflective of the actual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went to maybe a quarter of the lectures and still got an A. She posts everything online and the homework really helps to understand the class. She explains things very clearly and she does a lot of practice problems which really helps.
Makes calc seem easy. Very clearly knows what she is doing and has taught the class for a long time. Follow her lectures and you'll do great

Professor Benguria had some of the most organized lectures I've ever been in. I liked how she led us through examples and let us work through exercises by ourselves. It helped me really grasp the content. You can tell she's passionate about the subject, and I would 100% recommend her class to others. This course was very interesting to me as well.

Soledad was a great professor who goes through a lot of important stuff and although she writes fast she explains things well and gets the important stuff across and simplifying harder content on the first go through.

She is so adorable and makes class nice + easy to listen to. Def go to every lecture, it's super important. TAs grade like everything, and only 3 exams that make up majority of your grade. Calc1 can be tough, especially if you didn't take in hs (me), but fs manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course is tough, but the instructor did an excellent job of teaching. Her teaching structure was very organized, with lots of examples, which made it very easy to follow along and understand.

Tough material but good lectures. Lectures can be fast-paced, but lots of good examples that help you understand the material. Exams are similar to old exams. I would definitely take the class with professor Soledad again.
Lectures are clear and helpful. Exams are just like past exams. Overall, she is a pretty good professor.
Calc 3 is a difficult class. Soledad's lectures aren't amazing but not terrible either.

I hate math, but Soledad was such an awesome professor that she made it manageable. She really cares about student success I feel like and even though the grading criteria for Calc 3 was harsh, she did a good job to help students. Lectures can sometimes be a little hard to follow because of her accent, but also it's Calc 3 so it's going to be hard

Soledad is a solid lecturer, but the class moves fast. Take diligent notes - even a minute of distraction can mean missing key content. Luckily, Soledad posts her lecture videos online, which are great for review. And tools like Unstuck AI can help with study prep.

An amazing professor who is very nice and patient with questions. The course is almost too easy and has minimal rigor (application-oriented), but I suppose it is just how this course is designed and not about the instructor. Definitely do take another proof-based class if you want some real math.

Honestly she is an incredibly professor. She tries to make the most complicated topics easier by using and perfectly drawing out diagrams. The reason I believe that she deserves a 4/5 is that the final unit is rather abstract and I believe could be taught in a more concrete way. I guess his is more of a math department issue though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really appreciated the way she taught calc 3. She was easy to understand and very responsive to questions. The first two midterms had high high 80s averages with a low 70s final average that balanced the 88 and 89 midterm 1 and 2 averages out. Overall awesome teacher and would absolutely do more math with her.
Good lecturer, using examples and pictures to explain materials. Class is super dependent on exam scores. I think they weigh 87% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: goated professor, very nice and had very clear lectures that were super easy to follow along with.

I took calc 1, 2, and 3 with Soledad and she is easily the best professor I've ever had. SHe explains things clearly and effectively, answers questions well, and is clear about exam topics and reviews! I cannot recommend her enough!

Dr. Benguria's lectures were very helpful when explaining complicated topics. She uses a lot of pictures/diagrams and example problems. The only downside is that the calc department at UW weighs exams so heavily that they're really the only thing that matters. Calc 2 is not an easy class but she made it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Benguria does a nice job of breaking down Calc 2 topics. New subjects didn't feel very rushed for the most part, but the last unit is a lot quicker than the rest of the course. Her lecture style is pretty clear with lots of worked out example problems and general explanations for a new topic. Exams and quizzes were fair for the content.
Lectures clearly and cares about students, consistently answering questions and checking for understanding with ample practice problems and examples in lecture.

Like almost all math classes, exams are like 87% of the class, Soledad is a good lecturer though, sometimes it's hard to understand her if your in the back of the class but her written solutions and explanations are excellent. Exams are luck based, some are easy and others are cringe.

Really didn't like how fast she went in lecture. I would have to write everything down without comprehending it at all because she would move on to the next topic. However, everything she covers in lecture will show up on exams with a slight twist that requires creative thinking to solve. Content is hard but exams are fair (for the most part).

Very engaging lecturer. Lectures mostly consist of a few examples of each topic before moving on, and she is sure to stress the most important details of each topic. Exams made up a large portion of the final grade, but none of them were designed to be overly tricky. Lots of materials are provided to study with as well before each exam

Professor Benguria's lectures are straightforward and she keeps good pace throughout the semester. She teaches most of the concepts through practice problems, so it is helpful to look at the textbook ahead of leacture to get a general idea of what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Soledad's 222 was decent. Nothing to sway it either way -- lectures were good, exams were tough and required prep. Nothing felt unfair, which is really all you can ask for. Definitely one of the best out of the department.

Soledad is a tough professor, but probably the best in the Math department for the Calc sequence. The lectures will cover the exam material (this isn't always a given) so you stand lots to gain by going to lectures. Additionally, she is responsive and will curve the class if she feels it's needed, sometimes generously! Overall, a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty average professor. Teaches almost entirely by examples so if that works for you, you will enjoy her. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams, so make sure you do as much practice as you can, and take advantage of the published past exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the math department
Good lectures, but this class moves very quick. Be sure to pay attention and take notes. If you look down at your phone for like 1 minute, you'll look up and find you missed a lot of content.

Professor was super nice and made lectures enjoyable. The class was extremely difficult, but she used lots of examples and definitions to try to help with understanding. Your grade consisted of many homework assignments, 3 exams and weekly quizzes in discussion. She also posts her notes and lecture videos online to rewatch.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The final is extremely difficult.

Soledad is a solid lecturer, and she's kind to students with questions. She projects her Ipad screen, which is easier to follow than a chalkboard. My one gripe is she often changes the slide almost immediately, which can make it hard to write everything down. But, her notes were always useful to reference & she has videos to watch if you're absent.

Soledad is a terrible lecturer. She goes on about rambling and completing various useless derivations, using complicated notations that have no bearing for the rest of the course and often spends the entire class on them. Her lectures tend to be very scattered and useless taking time to explain a formula using her delta notation. Try to avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Benguria is very organized in lecture, and her notes are easy to follow. She evens posts them after lecture, as well as her videos from virtual learning during the pandemic. These are all super helpful because she does tend to go really fast in lecture. So although she explains concepts well, sometimes it went a little too quick.
Very good lecturer
Wonderful Lectures. Wouldn't mind taking all math classes with Soledad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had in the math department. She has very clear grading criteria and shows her patience with students. 100/100
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was only an OK lecturer, which is why I don't give her a 5. But she wasn't a bad lecturer either, and she was understanding and communicative insofar as you can be in an huge entry-level math class. Did the best she could with a full lecture. Overall a positive experience with her.
Hard class, but good professor. The teaching of this class was as good as it could be. She gave examples after explaining what something is, which was very helpful.
The instructor was always prepared for class and very organized. She gave examples, pictures and definitions, along with letting us do exercises in class and working with classmates.

She does not care about students even after going in for office hours with her and my TA. The tests were not similar to the practice ones she handed out but were similar to ones she would try once in class and never discuss again. On top of that the lecture felt so long.

Soledad was one of the better math professors at Madison. But that is a low bar. I went to every lecture-- it was a complete waste of time. She went over useless proofs rather than problems. I struggled in this class, so I joined small group tutoring, which saved my grade. If you are taking this class, get Oumar as your peer tutor. Trust me.

Good lecturer and a nice person. Sometimes focuses too much on useless proofs but good overall. Worst part about this class is that 3 exams make up 84% of your grade. So make sure you do lots of practice problems and go to lecture and discussions. Also many concepts build on each other so make sure you stay caught up.

Great math prof (compared to the awful math profs at this school she is a saint.) Goes over examples that look exactly like test questions, if they don't she moves grade boundaries accordingly. Easy to follow lectures, homework didn't really help but her class felt fair and it was one of the more positive math experiences I've had at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has a bit of an accent but she explains everything very well and makes sure everyone is getting the help they need. She goes into a lot of detail to explain everything and was one of my best professors. She projects her iPad on a projector instead of using the chalkboards and it makes it a lot easier to see what is going on.

Professor Benguria is an okay lecturer. She's sometimes difficult to understand, especially with a mask and mic. When explaining difficult concepts, it sometimes appeared that she didn't fully understand the reasoning behind what she was saying, which is frustrating.

I was kind of worried going into this class since math is not a strength of mine. However, professor Benguria made the class flow well and some of the difficult concepts became easy to follow. She is also very kind and open for questions so that made the class environment feel welcoming as well. 100% recommend for anyone who is going to take 221
Tests were very difficult with little thorough instruction to go along with it

I truly enjoyed my time with Professor Benguria. She takes the time to thoroughly explain concepts, and although calc is already a tough subject, I feel as if I understand the concepts extremely well, and I entirely credit that to her teaching. I would recommend her to anyone, and if I needed to, I would take a class with her again.

Great professor, one of the best in the math department at UW. All lectures are low on math jargon as she really tries to emphasize how to solve the problems. If she teaches MATH222 I will definitely take it with her.

Took her during the online fall semester. Lectures were uploaded to canvas and were easily accessible ahead of time, some funny moments during the videos as well. HW is typical for a math class, tests were monitored with Honorlock and were reasonably hard, but not too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Though this class was pretty difficult the prof was very kind and caring. Her lectures were very clear and helpful. This class was tough but the prof definitely helped me get through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Benguria is very organized when it comes to lectures. Her lectures are also easy to follow and were uploaded very early in the semester. I never interacted with her personally but she seems like a nice person. So, I would still recommend her if you're taking in-person classes.

Shes good, although I wouldn't say amazing or anything. Her lecture videos during online semesters were easy to follow, sometimes dragging a little bit, but I would imagine in-person lectures to be better. Lots of online homework was assigned, but it does help you learn the material. Would recommend her, but not super strongly.

Having weekly midterms was one of the worst ideas for this class (online). They will constantly stress you out. Not only that, but the material on the midterms was always harder than the examples presented in class. The homework was very similar to the exam, but that means its way harder than the class examples too so you have to learn from the hw
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: explain the whole thing clearly and help a lot. She also made some slight changes for students under this special circumstance.
Way better than my other online classes. The lecture videos were straightforward and easy to follow. Lots of examples.

I took her class online during the pandemic, so I'm not sure what her class is like in person. However, she seems super sweet and her lecture videos were fairly straightforward. She tends to give easy examples in her lectures that don't at all compare to exam-level questions, so you definitely need a good TA to fully learn the material.

Imo she doesn't go over enough examples. Im always learning new things while doing the homeworks, which I don't particularly like. She cares a lot about proofs, like she'll literally do a 30 minute video of her moving numbers around to prove a theorem and I just dont care lmao. Also when I go to office hours she can't always answer my questions.

Content is taught well if you write down lecture examples and copy homework down. Weekly exams and homework due twice a week. Exams consist of problems seen on homework and written/printed notes are allowed. As long as you stay on top of the homework the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: During COVID she thought it would be a bright idea to give us WEEKLY CUMMULATIVE EXAMS. The homeworks/discussions dont cover everything youll see on exams and she doesn't give any review material. Thus you have to spend hours shuffling through "extra" resources potentially doing problems that wont even prepare you for the exam. This is evil.

UW isn't known for having the best math program so shes pretty standard. If you took calc in high school and you got a B or A or a 4 on the AP exam you should be fine. Lots of examples are given so just pay attention and stay on top of your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I only had Professor Benguria for half a semester, she left before the second midterm when she had her baby. But I enjoyed her teaching style, her lectures were organized and to the point, with lots of examples. I wish she'd stayed the whole semester. Exams were pretty similar to previous exams.
Math 221 is a challenging course, but Soledad presented the main ideas clearly and took time to answer questions.

She's great. She goes over lots of examples. She also gives time to work on problems during lecture. Solutions to old exams are posted on the Canvas site. The exams are easy if you work through the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Soledad goes over many practice problems and thoroughly explains theorems. Homework is extensive but standard across all 221 classes. Exams followed same structure as past and were pretty straight foreword. Note: she doesn't upload her slides or her lectures but you can learn the material by yourself by following course plan.

I took two semesters of Calc with her. She explains things several times and always stops to ask for questions. Makes you do problems in class. Do the assigned homework and pay attention in class and you will do OK on the exams. They are hard but similar to the posted practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The math department at UW is honestly bad, and she is no exception. I ended up teaching myself the whole class, and it was a bad experience. Would highly recommend taking math at another university.

Not good, if you just need to finish up calc classes take them at a different school. If you are generally trying to learn math just watch youtube, thats what will end up teaching you if you take her class anyway.

Hard class, but great prof. Makes you work hard, be prepared for lots of homework and hard exams. The lectures are awesome, though. She's very clear, gives you a chance to ask questions, and doesn't go off on tangents. She focuses on the important stuff to prepare you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I was optimistic, her reviews were positive! sadly, I feel as if she was the worst professor Ive had in the math department. She seemed super complacent and had no control over her class. I learned absolutely nothing from her regurgitating the textbook and I felt that she was underprepared. I wouldnt take her for any class.

Soledad is a great teacher. Her lectures are clear and she always stops to ask for questions and takes the time to answer them well. Way better than my Calc 1 prof. She follows the textbook pretty closely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Shes honestly not that good, she gives way too many proofs and doesn't really explain why or how to solve anything. I hated going to her class because I could barely understand her. I personally would avoid her, I thought she was bad.
The class was hard, but I'm glad I took it with Solidad. Her lectures are really clear if you pay attention and go to class. The class gets loud sometimes, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the best profs I've had. I had her for 222 and 234. Her lectures are clear and she really seems to care. Super helpful during office hours. The exams were hard, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: everything about her is bad. I sat in the first row and attended every lecture and got absolutely nothing out of it. she showed unnecessary proofs and had no control over lecture. she was way too quiet and used the slides instead of the chalkboard which made her go super fast. I taught myself the course, only reason I got an A. dont take her....

I thought she would be a good teacher, because all of her reviews were pretty good. I was highly disappointed by her teaching style and lack of communication with students. I dreaded going to her class and it was the worst one I have taken here. DO NOT TAKE HER

I have taken a different math teacher since algebra and not only was this the worst math class I have taken. The tests are hard and are 80% of the grade. There is also no direction on what to study for each test which can add more stress. Complacency is the problem here.

reviews.comment: contrary to other opinions, I believe that she is one of the worst professors at UW. she talks way too fast, and I honestly loved math before taking her course. worst ever, and her exams were awful.

Great prof. Has like 6 names. I had a savage TA so I had to study really hard to manage about a 70% average on quizzes but it payed off on tests. reviews.comment: She talks too fast and her final exam was crazy hard. I didn't like her as a teacher and I wouldn't pick her again. She goes through her lectures so fast and is really hard to understand, and it didn't help that my TA was little to no help at all. The worst course that I took at UW.

Math 222 is hard. I heard she was one of the best profs to teach math 222, but math at UW comes down to the work you put in outside of class. Her lectures outline the book material and she gives you examples. She was inaccessible to students, only holding office hours on Friday for two 50 min periods during the busiest class times: 9-9:50, 11-11:50

Professor Benguria is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I took both Math221 and 222 with her and her lectures are very clear, organized, and made the material fairly easy to understand. Calc 2 is inevitably hard, but with all of the homework, quizzes, and one group project (easy) it doesn't feel too bad. She is so sweet and caring, too.

Great professor for MATH234. Not difficult but still worth going to lecture. Not hard to follow course as long as you go to discussion. They say they will not curve course, but always ends up with strong curve at end.

I had Soledad for math 222 & 234. Both semesters were great! Her class average on exams is super high compared to other sections of both classes. Her notes are clear and her explanations make sense. If you have the option to be in her lecture, DO IT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Soledad has great lectures, she gives way more examples than most math professors and uses her tablet to project her notes to the class. She allows 20 attempts per problem for the online homework and provides resources for the exams.
Really great professor. Always takes time to stop lecture and ask if anyone has questions. Gives lots of examples during lecture.
Shes an amazing proffessor. She is not only caring, but clear concise and breaks down very tough and difficult topics into easy to understand steps.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Tests are tough and you don't have a great idea of what to expect. Quizzes every week written by TAs. Soledad is nice but tends to spend time on unnecessary proofs and quickly go over the important information actually needed. In class problems make lectures mandatory. Online homework is easy to get 100% on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Soledad is a very reliable professor. When she lectures, she's calm and organized. Her explanations aren't incredibly engaging, but she always answers questions in class which is really useful. There is a lot of homework to do, but 20 tries per problem ensures that at the very least you can google it for credit. Great calc class overall.

Soledad was a pretty solid professor. Sometimes her explanations were a bit confusing, but she gives you the chance to ask questions during lecture which is helpful. Homework is kinda long but you have unlimited tries and you have a week, so you'll be fine.
Super sweet lady. She explains everything clearly and always answers questions. My favorite professor at UW so far. Would definitely recommend for 222.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Soledad, she is a sweet woman who is always willing to clarify things when topics may get vague. The class itself isn't laid out the best, but I think that has more to do with the math department than it did with Professor Soledad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was a fantastic professor! Not only does she teach at a good pace, she breaks down difficult concepts into steps and makes them understandable. She doesn't dwell on proofs but instead gives examples on how to apply what we just learned. She is a sweet and understanding person who only want to see her students do well! Highly recommend her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Having taken calc in high school, math 221 wasn't too bad with soledad; however, those who didn't struggled a little. Soledad wasn't a bad lecturer, but she did overexplain concepts in a way that made them more difficult. I didn't put a whole lot of effort, but this semester's exams were A LOT harder than the previous' semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Math 221 is a generally hard class, but Soledad taught the lectures well. She focused too much on easy examples and proofs when there were a lot more complicated problems on her midterms. Two easy group projects and weekly discussion quizzes. It is also homework-heavy with online weekly modules and homework.

She definitely cares about her students, but has a tendency to over-explain simple material and under-explain new concepts. She didn't explain when to use different equations very well. Also, there were 2 group projects that were kind of a waste of time.
She was nice and always answered questions, answers questions and has 2 midterms that are worth 25% each, then a final worth 25%. Homework is easy and online

She's a good professor overall. Her lectures are handwritten (doc cam), and she goes over example problems in class. She takes TopHat attendance, so in order to get full credit you have to attend lectures. She also has time to work on problems during lecture when she walks around to answer questions. Super nice, has an accent but easy to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not very clear in lecture. Does not go over useful rules always, so you have to really pay attention to what shes doing to the numbers in the examples.
Difficult to understand, and lectures are quite dull. Tends to baby us, so I'm not sure how this is going to prepare me for future math classes.

I love Maria, she is an amazing professor. Super adorable and sweet- always makes sure to give people time to ask questions after going over difficult topics and help them understand in lecture. Best professor Ive had!

Soledad was a great professor. She made concepts clear and easy to understand. The class in general is a little harder, but as long as you put effort in and do your work it is fairly easy to get an A. She was always available for students and was one of the sweetest professors I have ever had.

Soledad is a great calc teacher, which is a real find and she is also so sweet! She always asks for feedback during lectures in terms of questions and on in-class practice problems.  The exams challenge you a little bit but strongly reflect the course material so if you study and keep up with the hw and worksheets, you'll do fine!

Soledad is a great professor. Her lectures are very clear and she is unbelievably nice. She provides practice tests which are very similar to the actual tests. If you have the opportunity, take Soledad.

She's an amazing professor.,Really care about her studednts. The test is not hard at all. Though there are modules and weekly quiz, you can try for UNLIMITED time and UNLIMITED number, and only the HIGHEST counted. She also dropped 2 of the lowest. I mean how can you be nicer than that?

She's pretty kind and makes the material clear. In lecture she likes to do a lot of proofs which can get kind of boring and don't really help on tests. I didn't go to lecture very often and still did well in the class. Pay attention to discussion materials/quizzes & practice tests. The final was a lot like the practice final in fact slightly easier

A pretty good instructor for elementary math classes like 221. She speaks slowly enough and hopes to make sure that everyone understand after introducing topics. Patient and accessible after class. She doesn't use textbook at all. The only thing making me feel not good is she sometimes makes mistakes. But generally I would recommend her.

She is very clear during lecture and is willing to help students with specific questions. If you pay attention and put in a decent amount of work on assignments your grade will reflect that. Absolutely do the extra credit even if it takes hours. Don't skip lecture or you'll take way to long on homework questions and have a hard time with exams.
She's great. Lectures are clear and she works through a lot of examples. She assigns too much HW, though.

She's great. Her tests are fair. Before taking this class, I did take Calc BC. I didn't do great on the AP test, but I feel like BC helped me a lot with this class. However, if you study and know how to do the homework you'll do great even without previous calc. She's the best 221 professor to get. She's also super helpful and gives extra credit.

Soledad is a good professor and most of what she lectures about is clear before she moves on to another topic. However the homework often has incredibly hard problems, much more complex than anything covered in homework. She is a good teacher, but expect impossible problems to appear out of nowhere on the homework, group project, and exams.

Soledad was a good professor, but her lectures are very dull and the information presented is pretty basic, especially if you have a calc background. The tests can be difficult, but as long as you put in the time to actually practice the problems, you can do well. Also, she offers an additional  5% extra credit, and it's a pain, but it's worth it!!

So much busy work that's genuinely hard and just worsens your grade. I looked on ratemyprofessor before taking her, and thought she would be amazing. NOPE definitely not worth it. Try to take a different teacher if you're not a "math person". if you get math, she might be good for you though!
Soledad is super nice and she did a good job explaining concepts. The prelecture quizzes and the online homework could be a pain but I was glad I took the class with her.

As a professor, she's wonderful, but she assigns so much busy work! 60 homework problems a week, even during the midterms.  Many times the homework doesn't even match the work done in class. Also, there are group projects, pre-lecture quizzes, and in-class quizzes.  Don't take her unless you want to put in an unnecessary large amount of work

Prof Soledad is so sweet. She always gives many examples to ensure that you understand the concepts. The weekly homework was super long and not too related to the material on the exam but overall the class was a good experience.
Prof Benguria appears to care about her students, but outsources too much of the work.  Homework assignments are poorly prepared.  Exams do not reflect the material covered in the course.

Highly recommend Soledad for 221. Very helpful during office hours and provides a good amount of examples during lectures. Textbook is an absolute joke - totally worthless. Attending discussion was valuable. Course is not bad if you've taken AB or BC in high school.

Soledad is a great professor. She is one of the nicest professors you will probably meet. Sometimes hard to understand due to her accent but she always double checks her mic before class. Attendance is important, but it's easy to get notes from other people and understand them (I was in BC Calc, so just be sure you understand the concepts).

You dont have a textbook but you are given a unbound packet thing which absolutely sucks. Only helps for prelecture quizzes because the answers R word for word in the text. The tests dont cover what you learn in lecture nd are much harder than lecture. Soledad is pretty nice though nd always has a smile on her face. The extra credit is not worth it
She is very nice and patient. She almost can explain everything that may be cod using.

awesome professor, used A LOT of examples, which really helped me understand the concepts. the exams were difficult of course, but the examples we did in class were basically on the exam with a new numbers switched around. as long as you go to class and do the homework, it's not hard to pass

Soledad is very sweet and genuinely wants her students to succeed without expecting math to be their entire life! She worked mostly in concrete, number examples and made the usually "impossible" topics of Math 222 understandable. I would definitely recommend her to anyone!
My favorite professor at UW so far! Math 222 is known to be a very tough class but she made it much more manageable. Super approachable and fun, explained clearly with examples before proofs!

I was nervous coming into Math 222 because of its notorious dificulty, but Soledad ended up being the best teacher I had all semester!  Her lectures were very clear and she went over tons of example problems that were extremely helpful for homeworktests.  Her exams are fair and we were even allowed to use a double-sided notecard!  Good curve too!

Had her for 222. Great lecturer. Doesn't waste too much time with proofs or lengthy definitions that just get confusing anyway. Does tons of example problems which are really helpful. Is quite clear in her work. Her english is great. Exams are not too difficult if you study. Notecard for 222 exams (not sure about other classes). Curve is helpful.

Her lectures are well organized and seems to care about doing well in teaching students. She is helpful in office hours. This was her first year, so she has some things to work out, like confidence, but I expect her to get to be very good (she was pretty good when I took her).
Soledad is an amazing professor who is clear and wants her students to succeed. I highly recommend taking her.
Explains Calc 2 topics very clearly and thoroughly, If you go to lecture and pay attention you're almost guaranteed to understand everything.

I would highly recommend taking her for Math 222. She shows lots of examples and she will stop in the middle of lecture and ask if we have any questions and clarify any. Super sweet lady. Although her tests aren't terribly hard, the course itself is tricky and she makes it more understandable. Gives a generous curve!

She lacks confidence and often seems confused while teaching. Her accent and notations are sometimes difficult to pick up on and the biggest issue was her not explaining the steps she took. She runs through difficult examples too quickly when you haven't learned the material before. Discussion was the only reason I understood the class. Nice curve!

Lectures are long but Professor Dharwadker is very knowledgeable and you learn a lot. His feedback on papers is very insightful. His prompts are great and the papers are enjoyable to write. His course is relatively easy and I would recommend.

Professor Dharwadker is amazing. He's so caring, compassionate, and kind. He gives great feedback. Genuinely wants his students to succeed. Very knowledgeable. Great guy, great class. Put in effort (do your best) and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was Eng 443 (the modern short story). Prof is so sweet, caring, passionate, knowledgeable, wants to help students. Lectures are woven with cool facts/tidbits about random topics. Easy grader, isn't trying to make your life difficult, just go to lecture and give him the time of day and you'll be fine. Highly recommend any class with him.
Super passionate about the short stories we read. Very knowledgable about current events and the authors. Long lectures and lots of listening but enjoyable class.
Nice but rambles and takes close reading to an extreme. Spends minutes on 3 lines and spends 45 min+ of each class catching up from the last class. Unclear paper instruction. Narrowminded
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great guy and cares about his students. HOWEVER, I did not learn a single thing about English and lectures were extremely boring and unrelated to the readings. Was unable to contact him outside of class despite many emails, and he does not have open office hours. Easy A, but don't expect to learn anything.

Vinay is a great guy and the class is pretty easy and interesting. Not too much reading at all and the stories are memorable. Class is graded on three easy quizzes and a midterm and final paper. Other than that, just sit back, relax, and enjoy Vinay speak about India and Indian authors.

Prof Dharwadker is absolutely amazing! He is the nicest, most caring man and is so knowledgeable about all things India and literature. He also is an overall genius and will randomly have facts about the world woven into his lectures. He is light on homework, and the short stories he assigns are very interesting and relevant to today.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR, he is so awesome! His lectures were really engaging and he was so passionate about the topic and what he was teaching. The class had 3 quizzes and 2 papers so the work load was perfect. Cannot say anything bad about his class or him as a professor.
The best! Cares about the subject, and it made me care too.

I took "The Modern Short Story" to fulfill my literature requirement, and Dharwadker is a fabulous professor. He brings lots of current events and life lessons into all of his lectures on the stories. It's a great class, and he grades things pretty easily.
Amazing professor. His lectures are very engaging.

Fantastic prof, very intelligent and teaches very well, had great English too. Goes of on pretty extreme tangents sometimes (gave the same lecture twice once) but you'll always learn something if you're engaged.

Vinay was a very resourceful & knowledgeable professor that did a great job at giving us an interdisciplinary approach to literature and made class topics relevant. The class grade is based on 2 essays and a few easy geography quizzes (with extra credit!).  Essay feedback also good. Overall  fun & laidback class. If you need a Lit credit, TAKE HIM!

Took Mod Indian Lit in Translation and this class is pretty interesting and laid back. The work demand for the class is pretty simple and are based off the readings or whatever is covered is class. Don't have to do all the readings, but you'd be lost if you didn't and they do help for the papers. Professor is very knowledgeable and good grader.

Prof. Dharwadker teaches his class in a way that makes reading literature interesting and not tedious. He opens a world to South Asian literature and his selections reflect a wide variety of styles and concepts. One of the nicest people and one of the best classes (and easiest) I've taken. Talk to him and participat and you will do more than well.

This is the easiest class i have ever taken at UW. He babied us like none other. For the first month we just talked about the basics of indian culture and took map quizzes. He was late all the time, and showed us pictures that his daughter took of india. I would have liked to read A LOT MORE than we did but man this class is easy. super nice guy

Vinay is great..he knows a lot about history and current news and ties it in with what we are talking about for the day.  The class is verrry easy. There are a few quizzes at the beginning of the semester on geography and then a few papers due. But you have to do hardly any work for this class, I would definitely recommend it!

He is unorganized and usually shows up late to class. We were like 2 months behind the syllabus and really didn't cover that much material. He kept saying we were going to start to use powerpoints and just have more structure in the class but we never did. With that said, he is very smart and has a ton of cool information. He is really nice and eas

Clear and detailed lectures and he does indeed have a great wealth of knowledge that makes almost every lecture interesting. But he had a hard time getting class participation. Occasionally, it was very hard to appreciate the analysis of the texts when it got overly thorough. But the assignments are clear and the subject interesting. Recommend.

probably one of the easiest graders at this school.  the class is very slow paced, and you dont really have to read anything because he summarizes everything for you in class.  he's full of very interesting facts...take him!!

Modern Indian literature.  I HATE literature classes but Vinay had awesome enthusiasm and made dull material seem interesting.  He is like a Jeopardy contestent with all the strange facts he knows.  He was very helpful during the class and always friendly.
Not as deep as he thinks he is...
Assumed people read the book, just filled in notes all lecture with little to no explanation

Debra is OK. I found CS252 to be a very interesting course, but mostly because of Patt and Patel's Intro to Computing Systems (very good textbook by the way). I learned almost everything from the textbook. She gatekept all of her lecture materials up until the final few weeks, which is weird. She does have a +2% extra credit quiz though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: The fact that she records every lecture and chooses not to post them is weird, its a CS class even if the lecture was in the afternoon half the class would just watch the recording. Content is fine, but many people choose to read Skrentny's notes from last semester. I wish you could regenerate hw's after finishing to practice for exams.

Technically attendance is not required but she doesn't post lectures nor filled notes DESPITE the fact that there are only two lectures and one of them is at 8am. HWs are more like a test/quiz bc you only get one attempt on a canvas quiz. She writes very small on the projector but gets mad if you take photos bc she thinks youre recording her (???)
Tough class good professor, caring and willing to meet with you to help. Only downside is she kind of expects you to have an "ah-ha" moment way to early sometimes in her explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CS252 with Prof. Deppeler was not that bad. Course material is a little dry but just go to lecture and pay attention and you should be fine.

Lectures are just fill in the blank and they are NOT recorded and NOT posted online. Starts off really simple but then the content gets a little easy to get lost in. Project keys are not posted so you can't use those to study and later on, homeworks don't help either unless you got them correct. No cummulative final tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest class in the CS department. Her lectures are subpar at best, but the textbook they picked out for this class, the one by Patt and Patel, is probably the best textbook they could've picked. I stopped attending the lectures after a while, because the textbooks just taught so much better, and had questions that better prepared me for the exams

Condescending teacher with a very antiquated way of lecturing, just filling in an outline. Often skips questions if she believes we should "already know" certain material, and has no lecture slides to review after class. No review material is posted, but homeworks have most of the test material. Class is not hard if you go to every lecture though.

Lectures were very good and explained topics clearly. I don't understand why there are so many negative reviews. Projects are very manageable if you pay attention in class. Also very accessible outside of class, was a really nice person and happy to help.

Generally just unhelpful...no posted cutoffs, ignored piazza questions, would not post lectures even though they were recorded, snaps at students during lectures and sits in a chair all lecture and hand writes notes...hard class, but deb did not make it easier by any means....

The class is taught horribly. The only study material is lectures and home works, but she deletes the lectures and doesn't reopen home works for practice. She also keeps the final grade cutoffs a secret and said she would remove 5 points on the final project if you requested a regrade that didn't result in 10 points back.

Condescending, often leaves students' questions hastily or not even answered. Lectures are old-fashioned fill-in-the blank, and videos are removed after a week. Lies about exam contents, which are already tricky and hyperspecific. Gives neither practice nor cutoffs prior to exams and gatekeeps exams from being viewed, likely because they're reused.
Difficult class, long and boring lectures, and tricky exams. Deb is a old fashioned lecturer and felt like it was an outdated format.

Worst professor I have ever taken. She takes off lectures, doesn't tell the questions you might have gotten wrong, no clear grading criteria, very condescending. Exams were full of crap, lied about the material thats going to be on the exams, it felt like she wanted people to struggle. There is literally nothign you can do to practice for the final

Condescending, says "we don't have time for this" to certain questions. Gives very little advance detail about exams. Regrade policy was verbatim "If I agree, I will recompute your final percentage. If I disagree, I will take 5 points off for the extra work to come to same grade as is already recorded." Avoid her if you can, good luck if you can't.

The content is pretty difficult, and her old-school style of teaching does not help this. Lecture videos are deleted so for the final exam there was no chance to go back and watch anything you forgot. Piazza posts were ignored a lot. Felt like taking a class from the 90s.

The class really soured for me at the end when the Piazza was completely ignored for the days leading up to the finals and when no resources were given for studying the final other than a few hints on what may be on it (spoiler alert, its cumulative). The immediate morning of the exam the Piazza was closed, so no last minute questions I guess?

The class itself isn't bad, the issue is dealing with Deb, which ruins it. Half the time she is MIA and ignores students' questions online. She often seems passive-aggressive toward students, and her lectures are surface level, while the exams and homework often require much more.

Meh class with meh notes. Always felt like I was lacking concepts or information on the exams or on the homeworks. The homeworks took a lot of time and I never ever felt fully prepared or that I had all concepts ready. The TAs were super nice (except for one, always felt like they never wanted to be there and was super unhelpful).

If I had to describe my experience with Deb in one sentence it would be: She told me 'C'mon you should know that!' when I asked a question about something I clearly didn't know. Lectures are the same horrible format as Jim Skretneys, but at least she puts the lectures up for a week so you can download them and refer back later
big time yapper, takes down lec vids after a week, and gives a bullet point key word outline for review material. prime uw madison cs prof tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures with handwritten notes, no slides or animations, feels like in the 90s. Recordings are removed from canvas after a week. She does not share completed notes with students. The canvas page is way too complicated to navigate. The exams are ok, just with some trivial stuff.

Gets upset at any students seen taking pictures of her notes in class, records the lectures just to take them down within a week, and doesn't upload her own notes. Half the class is self taught through textbooks and Linux commands on a terminal. No practice exams, past exams or study guides, just a list of topics that might be covered in the exam.
don't waste your time. switch majors to avoid this person.

Learn Comp Sci in the year 2024 by watching her write in different colored markers and write thousands of line of code based on the marker notes in class. prepare for exams with no recordings, no study guides, nothing. Doesn't post grade cutoffs, just guess what your grade is. Don't ask for regrade, will dock your score 5 points merely for asking.

Worst. She thinks her exam is easy because she knows what's on the exam. She likes to test just 1 line of notes (out of thousands line of notes) as a 3 pt question on Final Exam (1 pt overall grade) because she has no idea what the core of the course is and she herself cannot solve some of the problems that's the core of the course.

Deb really cares about our learning, and that is why her class was tough. She encourages students to learn by seeking answers themselves by writing code, searching man pages and reading the textbook. 354 is difficult but if you take it with Deb you will learn a lot. Lectures are great. Start p3 early and study for the exams and you will be fine.

Lectures are good and explain everything you need to know with notes and examples. Deb really cares about her students learning, and I can see why people don't like it. She's paranoid about cheating, she doesn't allow people to take pictures in lecture, she takes down recordings after 2 weeks, and doesn't allow any colabing. Tests are very hard.

Her lectures are great on the 2nd watch/if you already know the topic. That's where the "positives" end, she was test-heavy and she gave no study guides or ability to view your previous exams. Only recorded lectures for the week and virtually no help/very unclear on how to do the projects and homework. You'll have to teach this course yourself.
I guess there is nothing I have to say

Deb's lectures are great and have all the information you need for exams. Reading the required textbook is also super helpful. Only issue I had with her was that she wouldn't answer a lot of questions- she would either say that we have to figure it out ourselves or say that we will learn it in the future. Kinda mean but good lecturer.

I found it quite hard to get help from her or the TAs. She has a tendency to ramble and not explain concepts very clearly. She forgets that there are other students waiting and takes a long time to get to you. She has also yelled at students for taking pictures of her notes during lecture even though she goes too fast sometimes.
One of the horrible instructors in UW Madison.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My issues were with trying to use accomodations with the professor. When I initially went in to discuss the accomodations (which I had been approved for by McBurney) I was essentially blown off and told to simply "apply myself" (along with a long lecture about her daughter). I did fine but I really felt singled out for a disability I can't control.

Canvas page was very organized and her information to access what topics we are studying were very accessible. Past this, her lectures were a mixed bag on whether it made sense or not. Additionally, no lecture notes were posted after class, except the blank outline. Homework and projects took up a large chunk of time, even if they weren't difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Deb is an enigma. Some days she explains topics super well & assignments are crystal clear, others you struggle to figure out what's important & what on earth to actually do. Class is a lot better with a support system, whether that's classmates, Discords, or TA office hours. Tips for success: go to every lecture, and take the class with a friend.

In lectures she has an issue of people taking pictures of the notes, where no professor does. Sometimes some people ask questions and she straight up ignore the question entirely. Looking at the other professor for cs354, go with him if you want to be taught by a real educator. Go with her is you want someone who treats teaching as a chore.
