Really great professor. Nothing bad to say about him. He is super intelligent and just a great teacher. Really great with Kines content and my favorite Kines teacher so far.
Dr. Diffee is incredible. You can tell that he really does care about educating his students in a way that makes them want to learn. Would recommend taking a class with him if you have the chance.

Dr. Diffee is an amazing lecturer. The information he presents is intricate, but he makes it easy to understand. He is understanding to students situations, and he has a friendly and helpful personality.

Dr. Diffee is my favorite professor as of right now! He cares about all the students and makes his lectures interactive (sometimes). He's also a fun person to get to know. The only downside is that you won't know your grades of your assignments until the end of the semester. Otherwise, you'll enjoy Dr. Diffee!
Really great guy. His lectures are very advanced and a bit confusing but he makes sure to answer questions

Super easy class and chill guy. He gets super distracted though and can't get his words out. It's honestly kind of annoying. If you can overlook that though he is a great guy that really wants his students to succeed. Class consists of projects over the course of the semester and one final at the end. Overall really easy class.
Great FIG professor! His class consisted of lectures, demonstrations, student presentations. He really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.

Diffee is great for the FIGS course. He is very caring and willing to help outside of class.  Projects are manageable and he is clear about what is on the final. You learn a lot of physiology. Not an easy A, but not a hard A.

His lectures sometime get disorganized as he writes stuff everywhere on the chalkboard. It is nice how he gives out outlines for each lecture so you have something to help you keep on track. Exams are pretty difficult as it is all short answer application questions. He is way more clear than the other professor for this class! Labs are pointless.

Took this class as part of my FIG, and it was awesome! Diffee does a great job of giving us an overview of exercise physiology, even though we don't know too much about it yet. As a freshmen, we got a lot of experience doing actual kinesiology experiments. AWESOME class taught by a GREAT professor

He seems passionate about what he teaches and does his best to get the class excited about the topics too. Did a lot of research but was not an overwhelming amount. If you are interested in exercise, his class is perfect! I learned a lot without doing too much outside of class, and I enjoyed it a lot.

Diffee is super nice .. However, he never really makes eye contact with his students, he's always looking around the room and it's actually really distracting.  However, he knows his stuff really well and doesn't give any assignments that are hard.  He's really big on citing sources so be sure you actually know how to do it properly.
Super nice guy. You can't bs him if you don't actually know what you are talking about. He cares a lot about the process not the end result. very approachable

I took this class as a part of my FIG and it was so easy! Diffee is an awesome guy and although the class is more about the process and not the content, I did learn a lot from him! This class will NOT take up a lot of your time, but it will be interesting if you love kinesiology and bio! No exams or textbook, just a couple projects & one final!

After having an extremely hard time with Physiology I was terrified of this class. BUT Diffee is AMAZING. He is by far my favorite professor at this school. If you work hard and study hard you can totally get the A. Take advantage of office hours to clarify the concepts, though. You might think you know them when you really don't.

Took his physiology of human performance class which was a first year interest group class (FIG).  Easier than 1st grade art class (although all figs are).  Dr. Diffee is KIND, APPROACHABLE, KNOWLEDGABLE, INTERESTING, FAIR, AND CHILL AS HELL!

This class is harder than it seems. Exams are not very straight forward and considering there is not enough time given for the exams, it's hard to get an A;the grading is strict. I used the textbook a lot. Loved the labs though.

Great professor. Makes class fun, and doesn't make it harder than it needs to be. You don't actually NEED the book - he provides lecture outlines and you're responsible for those, although you need to take good notes. Got an A, but earned it. You'll need to study in this class.

I haven't met a single person who hasn't absolutely adored Prof Rodriguez-Gomez. So so loving, so caring, and so interesting to learn from! Not to mention her course content was compelling, informative, and extremely relevant. Love her!!
LOVED HER AND HER CLASS! The best professor ever! Super engaging and cares so much. Would 100% take a class with her again.

Cares about students so much, and wants everyone to do well. Lectures can be a little boring but since how nice she is it makes up for it. Lots of readings but I didn't read any and did fine. Also willing to give extensions and is very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THE KINDEST PROFESSOR EVER. She really cares about all of her students and wants them to succeed!

She's the sweetest. She'd make a point to go up to everyone and ask how we were. It's obvious how much she cares about our well-being. She's willing to allow extensions, take suggestions, etc. In most classes, she lectured, then we'd do group activities. Readings were long but I didn't read them and I was fine. Class based on a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rodriguez-Gomez really cares about her students and wants them to engage in the material in a way that they are most passionate about. Online format made it hard to participate but I hope she can improve this. 2-3 readings for each class with 15 reading summaries due throughout the semester, 2 papers, and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. Class is engaging and she is super open & responsive to student needs(ie people had difficulty finding peer reviewed sources, so she decreased req'd # & helped w/ resources to find them). Really cares about students as humans and is super knowledgeable. Wants you to learn and be able to share ideas and think critically

Unfortunately, I am a bit lower than the A cutoff becasue of academic burnout. However, I am surely that Dieter is the one of best professors I met at UW-Madison, from both academi and moral aspects. You can surely perform better than me if you do not choose too many other courses and spend time in this subject!

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had here. I broke my ankle in February, and he was the only professor to reach out to check in on me. He's knowledgeable and very approachable. The class is tough but the cutoff to get an A was about 80% - my advice would be to spend quality time with the hw to give your grade a buffer for the tests

I take his CS 577 Honors version. Although this is an extremely hard course, prof Dieter is very good and caring. He always encourages us and provides useful feedback. His rubrics are clear and detailed. Just try your best in the exams, then your partial credits will not be terrible, although the process is painful (for me, not a theory guy).

Deiter is an incredibly conscientious, caring professor. VERY hard material, but he graded very generously. I struggled early in the semester with a bad test grade, and I have never felt more empathy and genuine concern from a professor. He is very willing to accomodate/help all his students, even bending the rules sometimes.
Professor was nice even though the class is very tough, go to TA office hours is usually more helpful than his lectures unfortunately
Took the honors section of CS577 previously, which was much easier than this one. Dieter is always accessible after class, but it is easy to get lost during his lectures

Takes the Honors section with Dieter last Fall. Super solid choice. Super hard course but very generous grading. Dieter is always accessible (even not in office hours) and being super nice outside class and willing to give help. The way Dieter is presenting the material is touch but very inspirational.
Best CS professor, he explain everything clear. DEFINITELY take his section instead of whoever else is teaching. Really kind and generous professor. HIGHLY recommend his section.

Took the honors section with Dieter in Fall'21. Very solid choice. Cares a lot about you, and tries to accommodate. Tho I will say this was particularly because the class size was small (< 40), don't know how he fares in big classroom settings. Overall, if the class size is small, he will be a great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Occasionally, Dieter's lectures can be too math-heavy and proof-based, and often times I was lost by the end, but Dieter does an excellent job answering any questions after class. Overall he cares what his students think, but it is just a hard and difficult class. Find a good hw partner and put in the time every weekend on it and you should do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a very knowledgeable professor and knows what he's doing. That being said, his handwriting tends on illegible. Hardest course I've ever taken, but I never for once thought it was because of bad teaching. Only other complaint was not knowing the curve until end of semester. Very stressful not knowing if I should drop the course due to my grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Love him.

Dieter is a nice guy. But his teaching style is not good. I had to learn the material from YT MIT lectures even after watching his lecture videos. Graded by exams(90%) which was a lot of pressure. I did not get a clear understanding of the material from his lectures. For such a crucial cs class it was taught very poorly- hindered my cs knowledge

Based on the fact that algrithm is hard, Dieter did a good job on teaching this. Though some notations on the writing are elusive, this course is well-organized and you can learn tons from it if you really put your time in and figure out what those concepts mean and how to make proofs. Abstraction is what algorithm is.
He is clearly a smart professor, but the hinders him from being able to explain topics to students that have no idea what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes a good professor. He teaches well and takes the feedback from students very seriously. His handwriting improved so much over the semester. His lecture note is useful but can be a bit too rigorous. Reading the textbook first may be better. Expect to spend lots of time for the homework and reading if you want to do well.

Dieter teaches the material in a very convoluted math-y way that won't make sense to those just learning the material for the first time. The TAs and peer mentors are much more helpful in aiding your understanding than he is. The homeworks take a while to complete but are not unreasonably difficult if you pay attention in lecture and discussion.

Always talking to himself and illegible handwriting make the class even harder to understand. I mean, when teaching algorithm, a professor is supposed to "teach and explain" in a way that students can understand, but what he does is just "saying" in a way that he can understand. Boring professor who lives in his own world.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor has a terrible handwirting, and he most often doesn't use lecture slides. He uses a projector and project his handwriting duing the lecture. To make things worse, sometimes he only read out after he finished writing the sentence. It's hard (but do-able) for me to catch up with his lecture in my notes. The lectures are recorded though.

Nice guy, but terrible professor. The book is so old and thin, you will feel like you have no resources to go to to learn about the subject, including the Internet. Numerous times he has assigned homework problems that literally he and the TA cannot solve. It's like the unsolvable math problems from the movie Good Will Hunting.
Prof is very intelligent and fair. Take the course, you will really learn

One graded HW problem plus some ungraded ones and an autograded EC programming problem per week. Very difficult, but usually possible if you give it some serious attention. Exams are difficult, but he gives plenty of time and grades generously. Good, clear lectures and notes. He's a genius and passionate. Difficult, but good if you want to learn.
Amazing Professor

Pros: He is very knowledgeable and you will learn A LOT from him. He quickly and clearly responds to emails, online/Piazza questions, etc. The curve was generous; 78% was an A.  Cons: Words cannot describe how hard the weekly homework is. I put at least 10 hours per week into the homework. This was the hardest class I've ever taken hands down.
Course will teach you how to think

This class is about as difficult as it gets, and Dieter expects a lot from you. The weekly homework is challenging, as are the exams. However, Dieter is an incredibly thorough lecturer. He misses no details. If you want to really gain some ground in theoretical computer science, take 577 with him.
Hard to do without post-grad math knowledge, unnecessarily complicates concepts and tests on related but not actually taught topics.

Dieter's teaching philosophy relies on challenging you (almost to the point of disillusionment; homeworks were harder than a comparable class at MIT) like you've probably never been challenged before. That being said, you won't learn more in an algorithms course.  He's incredibly helpful in office hours. Review sessions are also super helpful
Monotonous speaker; but great course. Assignments make you learn and some effort is required to keep up. Definitely worth it.
I worked hard and get A for other CS courses but get a C at CS577. Only 50% of students can get a score of A-B, others will get a BC-D. So be careful before you take Dieter's CS577, yikes!
Pretty monotonous speaker. Homeworks are difficult and involve a lot of problem solving. That said you'll definitely learn -a lot- from this course, provided that you put in the work.
I hate it!
My best class ever. Dieter rocks!
Most homework solutions can be found online, ACM,  OJ or other universities' hwk. So don't  worry about the homework.
Best professor other than Joseph.
So hard, Dieter is good at make things you like to you hate. Make your dream become nightmare.

This is the hardest CS class I have ever taken on campus. I did very well for all of the intro CS class and expect i could nail this one. However, it is not easy. Expect to work a lot of time on the exam and homework. TA is very helpful. Also, Dieter is a really smart professor, once you take his class, you will learn much more than otherwise.

Very Hard intro teacher, but was a very smart guy. Just not the best teacher. I felt as though I didn't really learn anything, I got an A/B  because I didn't bomb the tests as bad as everyone else. Curve was awesome and homework was hard and took a lot of time. Avoid teacher for math/cs240 but I'd image he's good for the higher level classes.
worst professor ive had at UW. managed to make a 200 level class ridiculously impossible. avoid at all times

Clearly a smart man, but should not be teaching this class.  Avoid!

Dieter is one of the smartest professors I have ever met. He has a hard time coming down to the level of an undergrad taking a 200 level course. The explanations and proofs are all pretty difficult to understand. You don't need to go to the lecture to do well in the class.

Dieter is obviously very smart--one of the smartest people I have ever met. However, I would not advise him for CS240 or any other "intro" level class. Just look at his class history--it is all 700/800+ grad classes. He knows his stuff, but makes the material way too complicated and the homework and tests ridiculously hard for a 200 level.

Much harder course than I was expecting. Dieter is obviously incredibly bright, but doesn't seem to be able to explain the material all that well. Lectures are very boring, but missing puts you way too far behind. Office hours help a lot for the homework. The course was redone this semester, and it is definitely a lot more difficult than before.

Prof van Melkebeek is obviously a super smart guy, but he is NOT a good teacher. The hw requires you to know things not brought up in lecture. Second midterm class avg grade was a 52%. He also seems annoyed when people ask questions in class, I get the impression he hates having to be there.
TOOOOOOOOO HAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAARD

If you take his course you need to attend his officer hours every week or else you will get a horrible grade on homework. One of the hardest entry level course I have ever take. Two exams and one homework right after spring break!!

terrible professor. he cant explain things clearly and he tests laws and theories that are never covered in lecture or the reading materials. he makes this class impossible. Go take CS240 with him if you really hate yourself.

This class is very tough - other professors have told me he teaches it like a graduate class, but that means you learn a lot as well. If you're serious about algorithms, take Melkebeek, but expect to work for it.

I liked Professor Dienstag as a person, but his lectures could be kind of out there-- having a good TA was really important to make sure I understood the readings. I really didn't like his PS160 at first. Thought it was boring and was intimidated by the (almost) weekly essays on highly intellectual thinkers and concepts. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Dienstag is such a good lecturer.  His lectures are loaded with great insight about the readings.  Going to lecture is the best way to develop a full understanding of what you are reading.  Be prepared to write a lot.

reviews.comment: Prof Dienstag is the most knowledge person I've ever met. He gives amazing lectures. 50% of your overall grade is a final exam and essay, which was a little difficult for me. He was really nice and is actually really funny. His lectures are super dense, so you have to pay attention. Also, there is a lot of reading. It is a really complex class. 

It was challenging he was really good at teaching it, but you're not going to do well if you don't do the work. 

THIS IS NOT AN EASY A! TAKE IT IF YOU'RE ACTUALLY INTERESTED.

reviews.comment: You either love her or hate her. Her lectures are heavily based on stories from her life/career, which I enjoyed but I understand that it could not be for everyone. Psych601 - Dr. Gooding is a very smart and eccentric professor. I don't think the current rating reflects her teaching ability accurately. Her teaching style involves a lot of story telling and constant review of material as a way to build off of what you have learned and just learned. Do the readings and participate in class and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought that Professor Gooding was an amazing professor (although goes off topic occasionally)! Would recommend!

reviews.comment: Dr. Gooding is the best professor I have ever had. She extremely smart and teaches the course in a great way. I find that people just complain about her because they are soft. exams are pretty hard but you will do fine.

Unfortunately I did not have a good experience in this course with Dr.Gooding.  She is an extremely tough grader and does not give any feedback after exams. She is also very inaccessible with her office hours being only 1 hour a week on Sunday night.
Very very difficult exams, HOSTILE AND CONDESCENDING. Very rude and condescending as well as narcissistic. Exams are very hard and no extra credit.
Professor Gooding says she loves teaching, and she was interested in the course material, but I thought she could improve by staying more on the topic during her lectures

Very poor professor. Not accommodating at all and would not own up to her own mistakes. Often blamed her TA for things that were done incorrectly.

reviews.comment: I read all the other ratings and thought, how bad can it be? I was wrong. Listen to the ratings and don't take this class if she is teaching it.

reviews.comment: I've had this professor for one month and I am going to rip my hair out because she is slow, boring, and conceited. I am sitting in class and we haven't done anything for a half hour because her computer died. She reads the lecture slides instead of teaching and tells irrelevant stories about herself. She shows no care for her students. AVIOD HER!!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSORs CLASS!!!!!!!! DO IT ONLINE OR WHATEVER, DONT TAKE THE LECTURE! You will regret!!!! She never tell you important things, but all her non-relevant experiences. Very disrespectful and self defensive! Never know how to use technology and never prepared it before class. Very confusing examples and never logical. Just dont
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The topic is so interesting but she spends too much time talking about herself, is extremely pretentious and gets very defensive if someone disagrees with her. There were unfair exam ?s that were not talked about in class OR in the assigned reading but she said we SHOULD'VE KNOWN what pages to read even tho the syllabus was wrong. AVOID HER CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: My first review got taken down for my use of profanity so I'll keep it simple this time. Just stay away my friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at UW. Dr Gooding is conceited, incredibly condescending to students and fails to convey material in any sort of engaging way. She will literally read definitions verbatim off of a sheet paper to you, and rather than explain concepts, gives irrelevant and elementary anecdotes that will not help you learn. Stay away my friends

Doesn't stay on topic during lecture and talks about herself most of the time. Not organized and your 3 exams are youre only grade. The tests are extremely difficult and she isn't open to hearing different perspectives on her answers. very defensive when someone proves her wrong. very lazy also.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good person, kind of pretentious. Often late to class. She made the cutoff for an A in our course 95%. 95%! Kind of ridiculous. It took her 3 weeks (20 days) to grade one of our exams (which are scantron). She clearly demonstrates that she doesn't care about her students performance in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nice person, mediocre lecturer, inconsistent tests, goes on tangents/off topic every lecture. Not great at taking criticism, incredibly defensive, will not listen to the class whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Although very knowledgeable about the topic, Professor Gooding spent too much time talking about her own personal achievements. Tests were fair. Comes to class late.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: (Abnrml Psych) Class material is undeniably interesting, but the class is made difficult for really no reason. Gooding writes the exams herself and you don't get them back. She's very humorous and straight up but I felt the class lacked organization and structure. You're only graded on two exams and a final, which doesn't fit the teaching style.
Exams are hard. Doesn't really teach but talks about herself a lot. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors in the psych dept! She's incredible at what she does, yet still down-to-earth, relateable, and kind. Exams are tough but fair.

Her grading is unpredictable as is the lecturing.  She spends very little time in class discussing the topics that you will be graded on. She is extremely unclear and unorganized in the presentation of material. I would not advise anyone ever to take a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hands down the WORST professor at UW! She goes off tangent literally all the time. Out of 75 minutes of lecture time, you can expect her to teach for just 20+ minutes. Talks about herself A LOT. LIKE SERIOUSLY A LOT. Assigns 7-10 readings at a time to make up for the fact that she doesn't teach anything in class. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I didn't think she was as bad as some of the other reviewers were saying. She did go on tangents, but she still taught the material well and tried to be as accessible for her students as possible.  She did go on conferences occasionally, so we had to watch video lectures instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gooding's lectures were all over the place, her stories often took too long and then when real information was presented she skimmed over it. I underestimated the first test because it was all on psychological perspectives and didn't study as much as I should have, BEWARE OF THE FIRST TEST. After that I studied hard and did well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Your grade in the class depends on your 3 exams and nothing else. There is no homework, and no final. I thought that the material was very interesting, but I was not a fan of Professor Gooding. She wasted a ridiculous amount of class time, and was frequently disrespectful to her students. On the other hand, her lecture outlines were very helpful.

I loved the material we learned in this class, but Prof. Gooding was probably one of the most arrogant and off-topic lecturer I've ever had. She spent almost half of the class period talking about completely irrelevant things. Her lectures are very content heavy, and I am glad she made lecture outlines. Exams were somewhat difficult.

It's very obvious Diane is very knowledgeable of this information and has done lots of research (did she attend Harvard, I forgot?). Sometimes I question why I came to class explaining she would show up upwards of 20 minutes late and then spend at least 25 minutes talking about her cats or her hair. Condescending as well. Won't be seeing her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Spends 95% of lecture discussing her personal life, which did not relate to the material at all. Will mention something very briefly and expect you to know it in depth for the exam. Very, very full of herself. Mentioned she went to Harvard roughly 5 million times. Very,very,very rude and insensitive. Honestly not sure how she has a job.

Gooding goes on the longest tangents in lectures. She probably only talks about relevant content for maybe 40 minutes of the total 75. I love the content we are learning about but it is lectured in a terrible way. She is super funny sometimes and very condescending at other times. Take this class with a dif professor if you want to learn something
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are disorganized and she goes off on barely related tangents that distract from material, and her lecture outlines that are supposed to help are sometimes just as disorganized. Also, extremely arrogant and rude. She is clearly very intelligent and knows what she's talking about, but does a poor job of relaying info to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Gooding made a solid impression on me; I had her my first semester of college for abnormal and she made me love psych even more. She loves her cats and goes on tangents sometimes, but I still learned a ton. I've remembered more from 509 than I have from most other classes. She's tough, but is caring and generally pretty lovely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Gooding is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had the pleasure to meet. Take her abnormal class over the summer! The exams are online and you can use your notes and text. While it is true that she goes off on tangents that have nothing to do with lecture, I still learned a lot!

One of my favorite professors here at UW and made this class amazing. The content is interesting and she shares personal stories to supplement it. The tests are fair based on the content she presents. The book is also neccessary to do well on tests.

Professor Gooding was one of my favorite professors at UW. Her lectures are quite funny and entertaining, and she is extremely intelligent. Her exams require work, but an A is achievable.  Extremely interesting material! I would definitely take the course again just to have Prof. Gooding. Go to lecture and pay attention!

I probably would've learned more from a Wiki article about each disorder, and it would've saved me time and frustration. I'm sure she's an intelligent lady, but she doesn't present herself as such. Tangents are pointless and important material is vomited out with little organization from her notes. Thinks VERY highly of herself. Tests are weird.

This class is not as hard as people have been saying. If you attend lecture and do the reading, you will do fine. I agree she can be a little condescending, but people do ask dumb questions sometimes and she doesn't like it when people try to suck up. She tells interesting stories and I don't think anecdotes are off topic, they are helpful.

Professor Diane would often talk about personal anecdotes in class, which made the class easier but also far less interesting. If psychology is interesting to you, I would recommend taking this class with a different professor.

Honestly one of my least favorite professors on campus. She goes off on long tangents during class that do not relate to the material at all and breezes by important slides. Extremely unclear lecturer, very condescending. Her tests, while not extremely hard, are neither a great nor fair representation of the material she presents in lecture.

Only three exams make up your entire grade. She can be very condescending when students ask questions and you can tell she likes herself a lot!!! DO NOT SKIP LECTURE (unless you can get the notes from a friend). If you can find another professor teaching this course, wait for that professor.
Talks a lot about her cats, and often goes on tangents about a subject. Overall, though, I really enjoyed the subject material and would recommend her as a professor.

Professor Gooding provides very thought-provoking lectures, yet can be very judgmental and tends to digress often. Overall, the lecture material was fascinating, yet Prof. Gooding was not very effective at covering all of it and tends to rush through important parts, while spending loads of time on personal anecdotes. Very funny though!

Abnormal Psych with Dr. Gooding wasis my favorite class I'm taken at UW.  I recommend downloading the lecture outlines and adding to them while in lecture (bring your laptop!).  Expectations are pretty clear, and if you've taken another psych class at UW the tests are no surprise.  I would HIGHLY recommend her.

Professor Gooding is one of my favorite professors here.  She is very helpful, and offered additional options to review material outside of class and office hours in a casual setting at U South.  Her lecture are really interesting, which makes it easy to bear the power lecture.  Grade is 3 tests, which are pretty fair.  Would definitely recommend!

Dr. Gooding is very knowledgeable on the material. She uses every minute of lecture and speaks fast, so if you take notes by hand you'll have a pretty sore wrist. But her exams are very straightforward and repeat concepts, so if you understand the material you'll get it. She talks a lot about her life, but all examples are relevant to the topic.

One of the worst professor I have ever had on the campus. The topic is definitely interesting, but Gooding is so self-absorbed and condescending. She talked about herself extensively and about her own research. she can spend 23 of the class on a topic that is not even that relevant. Don't advise take classes with her.

Dr. Gooding loves to brag about herself and the researchwork she has done & the important people she knows in the psychology world. That said, she is incredibly knowledgable in the subject. Definitely have to put in a lot of effort but overall its a good class.

Diane is such a great professor and is really into her research.  Her lectures are long but interesting, although she goes fast.  Her tests can be challenging no matter how hard you study. She provides lecture outlines which really help, but lectures are mandatory because she adds onto the outlines and simply reading the book won't get you an A.

Professor Gooding goes off nearly every day about her cats or some clients or friends that she had at some point that she attempts to relate back to the class, painfully so. She showed up late more times than I could count with numerous excuses. Expect her to breeze by important slides and go off for hours about redundant information

Professor Gooding is really passionate about her work and works really hard to keep her lectures interesting and understandable for students. If you show up to lecture, be respectful, and ask for help when you need this class is really easy and fun!

I actually like her and her lectures a lot. She's interesting and it's true that she gets off topic from time to time. The thing is she tries to make up some examples but kind of goes way to far. Hard to ace. I feel that's because my classmates are too damn good because the exams are fair (I aced my previous psych class with even worse performance

Most unclear professor ever. Super interesting material, but lectures are completely disorganized. She will literally repeat the same slide in two different lectures by accident. Goes off on random tangents. Study guides are lazy and I never have any idea what to study for the exam. Material isn't hard, but she makes it hard.

I absolutely love abnormal psych, but Professor Gooding is one of the worst professors I've had. She goes off on random tangents that have nothing to do with the subject being discussed and she spends half of class time talking and bragging about herself and her cats. She is also very condescending and rude towards people. Would not recommend.

Professor Gooding is a wonderful teacher! I took both 512 and 509, and really enjoyed both of them. While her tests are slightly challenging, if you read the textbook and articles and go to lecture, you will do well. Prof. Gooding is my favorite professor at UW, and is so knowledgeable about the material and is really helpful if you go to OH!

Egocentric and rude; typically goes on tangents about her pets and her "amazing" accolades. By far the single worst professor I have had at this university. The material for this class itself is interesting. It is unfortunate that the department put such a useless teacher to lead this class.
hands down the least understanding professor I've had to date, does NOT care about the individual. Not willing to help in anyway shape or form. her way or the highway.
Was really good overall, and very nice. Only bad thing is that she got off topic a lot. It was a fair class though. If you worked hard your grade would reflect that.

Absolutely atrocious. Borderline hostile towards questions asked in class. Very rude during office hours. Questions on the tests are very ambiguously worded. Often more than one answer is correct and you basically have to read her mind to know the right one. Something like 10% of people got an A, which is ridiculous for this class.

Her course is very interesting if you like psychology, but you definitely need to read the textbook. Lectures can be pretty fast-paced, but she's very engaging and excited to teach the material. Can be rude to students who ask questions in class however.
One of the best professors I have had, she makes class funny unlike some other professors whose lectures are dry she uses personal anecdotes to explain concepts.
Very poor class. She goes off on tangents all the time. She is not prepared for class and uses notes straight from the book. Easy if you study notes and book

Very interesting Psychology professor. She is passionate about her work and that becomes obvious with her personal stories in class. SHE LOVES CATS, and often uses them as examples.. Her tests aren't ridiculously hard, but they require you to know your material and do the studying necessary. She gives you many resources, USE THEM!

exellent professor for psych 509! granted I took it over summer with a smaller class so got more 1 on 1 contact with her, but I think she would do just as good a job in  a more formal session of 200+ students. clear concise notes, and interesting anecdotes to make the class fun!

Make an effort in the class and she will notice and you will be rewarded by the grade your receive. Intelligent and interesting person..loves cats. alot. DO NOT go over the time allotted on the take home exams..she and your overall grade will take notice.

She spends half of lectures talking about how great she is.  You can't challenge her on anything.  Her tests are not fair for the level of the class and seem to have subjective answers.  Disappointing because I was very interested in this subject but she was awful.

One of the worst professors I have ever had at Madison. She is completely unaware of how her students experience the readings and exams. One lecture she spent 30min of a lecture telling us her entire itinerary of her trip to Italy. Her exams are ridiculous and if everyone gets a question wrong, she doesn't believe that she should throw it out.

My worst experience in college was being taught by Professor Gooding... she is a terrible teacher with lectures that are all over the place and tests that are absolutely impossible. Highly recommend not taking this class.

I remember really enjoying her lectures and personal anecdotes,  as well as the material covered.  That said, the amount of reading was out of control (and was often from poorly copied/unreadable scientific journals), and the tests.  Oh, the tests.  They were supremely unfair and she was not honest about how difficult they would be.

I am very interested in abnormal psychology but this class is hard! It is completely biologically based in nature. It's way more focused on science and etiology of diseases then expected. Dr. Gooding goes on long personal stories, can be hard to follow and is often egotistical. Don't recommended this course unless you're very interested in it.

Can be rude and often completely shuts down students who ask questions that she considers irrelevant. The tests are challenging, but not impossible (I got As). Doesn't do a good overview of the disorders like Henriques in 511, instead she focuses more on genetics and biological treatments (we have never discussed psychotherapy in any detail).

Completely obsessed with herself and her work. Goes off topic and is extremely rude. I often feel as though I am disrespected and being talked down to. I avoid asking her questions because all she does is give me an answer I don't understand and make me feel stupid. Do not take this class.

Way too many readings and it's difficult to figure out what she wants you to know.  She uses analogies from her own life that are excessively long and take up a ton of class time.  Not good at answering questions if they're even remotely off topic.  Can be rude.  Very different class to 511(much more recommended).
do not take the class!!! effort does not matter, nor does interest or invested time/learning/studying/etc. absolutely egotistical and ridiculously impossible teacher

absolutely terrible teacher- very unfair grading system, does not care about her students or their learning but is simply interested in herself and her own personal interests. i was so excited to take this class and it was a complete disappointment.

I was so excited to take this course, and what a major disappointment it was. Gooding was rude, goes off topic constantly, and made what should be interesting material very very dry. She also has a major ego problem and likes to talk herself up. Overall not an impossible course. LOTS of boring reading and a large amount of material to learn though.

Although she can get off topic and has strong opinions, she gets across a lot of interesting information, and definitely tells you everything that you need to know for exams.  I've never gotten more than 3 questions wrong out of at least 50.  She assigns a lot of reading, but you learn whats important. Overall: she is wonderful 1on1, and good prof

Would not recommend Prof. Gooding. I was very interested coming into the courses (I took both her 411 and 512) but was very disappointed. She is very unclear and there is an unreasonable amount of reading that you are expected to know a lot from. She expects too much from her students. Pretty rude also. I would not take a course with her again.

Completely full of herself (and her cats).  Strays constantly off-topic during lecture, often wasting the better part of it.  Readings are redundant and uninteresting.  Consistently disrespectful of students and other professors.  If you want to have a good semester, stay away.

I had good hopes because I loved Abnormal, but I hated this class. She shows up late, strays from topic, calls people out in the middle of class. Her exams are VERY hard, especially since she usually does not finish her lecture after straying from the topic to talk about other things. Do not recommend.
I really liked this class until the day I went into her office hours. VERY unapproachable. The final is ****ulative and weighted at more than twice a normal exam--watch out.
Great professor who loves what she teaches!  Somewhat hard exams, but not if you go to class.
lectures on herself more than the course material
No Comments

This woman is really intense.  Her exams are pretty challenging, but if you keep up with the LOADS of reading, you will do fine.  It's geared towards a lot of neurological material, esp. schizophrenia.  But she is full of energy and will never fail to entertain.  Overall, very thorough and she knows what she is talking about.

Good professor - lectures are interesting and entertaining.  Exams so far have been fairly easy.  She assigns tons of reading, but goes over the important parts in class.  Yes, she talks about her cats, etc, a lot, but it gives you a chance to stop taking notes and her stories are usually fairly relevant. I would definitely recommend this professor

Challenging, to be sure, but exams are fair.  The curve is set so that the highest score anyone gets = 100.  There are questions on the reading (and there is a lot of it), but those are always straightforward.  Her lectures are well-organized, interesting, and her jokes and stories are genuinely amusing.  My favorite psych professor by far.

She does talk about cats and Denzel Washington A LOT. However, I learned an incredible amount from her class, and I think it really helped prepare me for grad school (esp. all of the journal article reading).
No Comments

Very clear at teaching the material, very helpful slides.  The only downside was a somewhat hostile response to some questions, I detected a touch of anger that people weren't getting the material at times.  The exams were fair, but I'm biased because I'm getting an A.
Talks way too much about herself and her cats. It gets to be a little boring listening to her stories.
Media and Mental Illness. Such a fun class! We watched "Law and Order" or a movie at least once a week.  Great discussions.

Very easy class but this professor must be working hard to make this information boring.  Her packet of readings is totally useless (the books are good though). Getting an A so this is not a retaliation.  Poor in general.
Intersting topic and not difficult. But she was annoying and self-absorbed. Totally unresponsive to questions, and downright rude at times.

She is not a good teacher.  She gives an unbelievable load of reading, especially journal articles, and then expects you to pick out tiny, insignificant details that show up on the test.  Her classes are wretched and she's bad at helping students.

Not only was she the worst professor I had at Madison, her class was a joke.  We watched about 5 episodes of Law and Order.  Watch out, because she penalizes students who disagree with her opinions of mental illness in her classes by giving them bad grade
Talks about her cats all the time. Should not be allowed to teach students.

Don't take this course with her unless you have to. Super insensitive and the class environment was extremely uncomfortable with her rude comments. You'll end up with an A, but it was obvious that no one in the class wanted to be there, even the ones that truly cared and wanted to learn more about disability rights.

Dian is a sweetheart with a lot of real experience to share with her students. She asks her students to be at every class and it was not hard to be there very week. She has really fun speakers come to class every week. I barely had to read all semester. Easy A if you attend lecture and do all assignments.

Her strong suit is not lecturing, but she gets you to participate and engage in class. Read the textbook, and youll ace the final. A big common sense course. Easy homework load. Super understanding when it comes to the service learning project, and is very willing to work with you and help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Djurdja is the most understanding professor I've had at The University of Michigan. She genuinely cares about her students. She is very funny and very passionate about what she teaches. She really knows her stuff. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Djurdja--you should. She is amazing.

She is a great teacher. She thinks outside of the box and she will make you think. I am impressed by her knowledge. She is VERY good at referencing popular culture and making connections for us. Her selection of texts is awesome as she uses youtube, films, music to show culture. Her research projects are super fun! Awesome teacher!

She is a great teacher. Her passion for literature and culture is inspiring. She knows a lot and is very good at sharing that. I loved being challenged in her classes. I strongly recommend you take a literature class with her. She thinks outside of the books.

awful awful awful spanish TA. made mistakes in spanish... no interest in students and totally indifferent towards material. misgraded assignments consistently. she looked bored in class. she didn't write the tests so it was up to us to prepare for them on our own and teach ourselves from the book. she made me dread coming to class.
Her passion for teaching is clear - and she leaves me wanting more.  I look forward to her class everyday - and the opportunity to gaze into her big brown eyes.
No Comments
She rocks.

Goes above and beyond and willing to do anything to help you. He's too nice that sometimes it's cringeworthy because he's so scared of offending anyone. Tests very similar to practice tests(40% of grade). Hw is fine but can take long. High bar for A because everyone scores well and tests are open note. Final project course grading subjective asf.
Lectures were great and homework is manageable. 3 tests - 40%, homework - 20%, and the rest is participation/weekly assignments. Highly recommend.

Dmitry is such a genuine and caring guy, actually one of my favorite profs I've ever had. The material is tough but he does a great job of giving examples and the homework really nails in the concepts. He gives you a practice exam before the exam and runs through the entire thing with a video, which is just like the actual exam. Love this prof!!

Yes, this class is hard, but you can learn tons of useful practical things from it. Be prepared for the heavy homework, and if you don't keep up with the materials, you can get totally lost, so come prepared.

I second that the other reviews are too harsh, definitely nowhere near the worst b school prof. He couldn't explain tough concepts well, expected too much prior knowledge, if you can get past confusing parts you can get a lot out of the class. What wasn't understandable was the insane workload but he eventually lessened it. Absolutely hilarious tho

Some of the comments here are too rough. Dmitry is one of the most caring professors I ever had at UW-Madison. He gives his students everything. Yes, the material is hard and it takes time to digest stuff, but it will all come together if you put in the work. Also, this was Dmitry's first teaching experience at UW.
Avoid

The midterm was hard but the average was much higher than anticipated. The concepts toward the end of the semester were helpful because they were on Excel (this is during the Coronavirus semester). He goes too fast and isn't good at explaining, you kind of figure it out the reasoning at the end. His slides have lots of info he never goes over.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Orlov is the worst teacher I have had in my four years at UW. Not only are there typos in all of his slides, but he also makes students scared to ask questions and show up to class. He races through his lectures, which makes the material impossible to understand. The problem sets are also impossible.

Dmitry is a really nice guy outside of class who obviously cares about the subject. However, he doesn't seem to understand how difficult this material is for students and rushes through material. The examples he gives in class don't help at all with the homework and he doesn't take enough time to clarify what variables mean/where #'s come from.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class has been awful. Professor Orlov has created an environment where his students scared to ask questions out of fear of being ridiculed or made look stupid. The examples in his slides are filled with many unexplained variables with no numbers involved. He goes way too quickly through units to be able to understand these difficult topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
The class isn't difficult and the professor is nice. 

That said, much of the course centers on theoretical and social discussions, that at times feel very obvious and one sided. I personally would have liked to see more analytical support/data to make the ideas feel more balanced and practical, for example in a business report.

This was the worst teacher I've had at UW–Madison. Her tone was condescending, instructions were unclear, and she acted annoyed when students asked questions. Our section got far less time for major assignments than others. She created a frustrating, disrespectful, and unhelpful class environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was incredibly condescending and rude, did not offer helpful feedback and graded far harder than the other professors.  If you search madgrades you can see she has half the amount of A's given out and 4 times as many B's as the average class. This class truly was not helpful and a waste of everyones time.

GENBUS320: This is the worst prof I've had at UW-Madison. I'm a senior and have never felt so disrespected in a class. She is extremely condescending and will shut down students' opinions after asking for them. Her assignments are all extremely unclear and have not taught me anything. She grades harshly and is ignorant of many topics she teaches.
She was condescending to her students and treated us like we were young kids. Then would grade very hash on every assignment even small assignments such as email cases.

Dominique is a tough grader and gives a heavy workload. She is passionate about what she teaches, and if you ask for her help, she is very willing to work with you. She wants everyone to improve and succeed. Business writing is important for our future careers, and while there are many dumb assignments, you will become a better business writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is the most condescending professor I've ever had. She pretends to care about what her students have to say but she does not in the slightest. She doesn't answer any questions and provides no feedback.
Whatever you do, pick another professor if you’re going to take GB360. If you pick her, be ready for heaps of busy work, zero feedback, and pointless assignments.

Dominque is a passionate teacher. She might come off a bit condescending; it's because she wants to challenge you. Her goal is to make your writing direct and concise, because in business there's no time for fluff. The more communication you have with Dominique, the more she will understand your writing style and help you develop it. Go to her O.H.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Although a difficult course, and peer-feedback heavy, Dominique made the class enjoyable and ensured you would get to know your peers well. Lots of reading and work before each class, each class is working in groups/teams/pairs, lots of room for questions/feedback, she wants participation, and the final portfolio is SO MUCH WORK for SO MANY points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dominique is a difficult professor. She seems to thrive by giving her students busy work. Each week has multiple assignments, all ending up with one huge paper that is complete bull. Would never take her again. Avoid at all costs.

Worst class I've taken at UW. Each assignment is overly complicated and unclear, they take forever, and you gain absolutely nothing from them. Some of the directions are longer than the assignments themselves and asking Dominique questions only makes the assignments more confusing. It's embarrassing that this class is offered at WSB.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Two years ago my roommates were complaining about this class (then called Gen Bus 300) calling it the most ridiculous class they have ever taken. It consisted of tedious assignments every week and unclear directions for a God awful final portfolio. Unfortunately, after two years nothing has changed with this curriculum. Seriously WSB, do something.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am a third year business student and I can confidently say that this is the worst class I have EVER taken. Each week I spend hours upon hours trying to do the assignment EXACTLY how prof. Hacker wants it done just to get so many points docked from the assignment bc one or two words were off. She provides little to no feedback. I learned nothing.

Words cannot actually describe how awful this class was. I cried, I ranted with fellow classmates, I debated posting passive aggressive piazza comments. I respect a hard class if it is graded fairly and I learn something, but Prof Hacker is unclear in expectations and docks points for opinion based things. Learned nothing and hated every second
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It is a huge time sucker, so take the class during a semester you have time for it. A lot of the assignments are absolutely pointless. All I gained from this class is resentment for Prof Hacker and the course in general. It is required for business majors, otherwise I would say NEVER take it. Least favorite class in my entire college career.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dominique is the worst. The class is so unclear, with new assignments popping up every week. The work is busy work, but it takes so long to complete and she doesn't consider how long her assignments take. She also is a super hard grader and doesn't provide good feedback or even teach us- the class is based off of readings, she does not lecture.

I don't think I have ever and will ever take a class with this much work. The schools requirement 9-12 hours a week for a 3 credit class is easily hit every single week. If you want to have a social life don't take this class. She grades harder than any professor I have ever had and doesn't take into account how much time we put in on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was a very difficult course. At easy it seems first with short busy work assignments, but the last month of the class is absolute overkill with he final report. Directions on the report are unclear, and when you ask questions you only become more confused. The class needs a complete redesign so students can actually learn something!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I attended every lecture. He is very knowledgeable and knows how to teach. He is humorous and friendly. He is open to questions and will answer your questions patiently, and won't let you feel bad. Provides you with a categorical point of view, introduces you the modern algebra. I'm afraid I've left too much unsaid, but I am out of space.

A phenomenal professor! Very clear and provides plenty of motivation! Couldn't wait for the lectures every week because I was learning so much in each of them! 

Also, he engages you as a student by asking questions and inviting participation. I think it's the ideal way to teach a course, though it takes a very capable professor to teach this way.

Dima is one of the nicest profs in the math dept. Hes passionate about algebra, and hes fun and engaging, both in office hours and lecture. His exams can be tough, but he gives big hints and useful practice problems. Overall would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Very friendly and helpful.  I struggled with the class but that was of my own fault, as Dima gives you everything you need to succeed in the class.  Tough exams, but the practice tests are EXTREMELY similar to them, so you know exactly what to expect.  Does lots of examples and will keep explaining things in different ways if you don't understand.
Awesome prof. One of my favorite professors. Go to office hours. He is very patient when it comes to answering questions. Recommend to anyone who needs to take 222.

This man is absolutely brilliant.  Any struggles I had in this class had little to nothing to do with him.  His tests were not the easiest, but his practice exams were very similar and doing them helps a lot.  Do what I didn't and go to office hours and work with friends.  I absolutely despised this class but I loved Dima as the professor.

Dima might be one of the coolest professors on this campus. He knows all of the stuff very well and explains it great. In my class we had one kid all year questioning him everyday about his work and asking him to prove things. Dima's so chill he put up with it every time 10/10 wish Dima was my dad.

First time teaching 222 but did very well. DID give an extensive amount of examples. Made a couple of concepts harder than they could've been but a good TA  and friends never hurt. Exams just like final. Minimal HW (due weekly). Had his funny moments.  Very personable. Go to office hours. Textbook only used for HW problems.  Wants you to succeed!

Dima teaches theories and tests your understanding of concepts, rather than straight plug & chug. He also provides few examples and often goes on tangents during lectures. This made the course extremely difficult, personally. I wrote down a conversion wrong and didnt realize it until a few days before the final because he never showed examples.
Dmytro  is an amazing instructor because his explanations are in depth and are very clear. However, he doesn't give examples in the class and his explanations are very theoretical.

Dima is a good professor. He definitely knows what he is talking about and can explain it well in lecture. He is a bit more conceptual in lecture and will not do example after example, which for some people is definitely a plus. I could understand him at all times. He also seemed receptive and open to all questions in lecture. I didn't attend OH.

I felt as if i learned the material well from lectures (with little help from discussion), however, even though I felt like i knew everything pretty well, the tests were extremely difficult. We were given questions we've never seen before. He was a good professor but tests were difficult. Slight accent but still easy to understand.

Dima's a nice guy who knows his stuff, but he throws material on tests that you've never seen before. Homework was graded harshly and the exams were so much harder than the practice tests he would provide you. Heavy curve at the end though.

He is a good lecturer who does a good job at making some pretty difficult material approachable to undergrads. He did have one unit of material which was not found in the book, making it difficult to find a good reference outside of class for those concepts.
He is clear through his practice tests on what he expects you to know. The curve was also very generous in my class.

I absolutely loved Professor Arinkin! The lectures could be a bit boring and long (I mean, it is math.) but he was a great lecturer! He's really funny and his accent is a bonus for me haha I've only been to office hours once, but he was willing to help, and even agreed to meet me early I wish he taught more classes that I need to take for my major!
Dima was a great professor for this class, definitely one of the better professors. He's a really nice guy and grades fairly.

Excellent lecturer!  He would constantly ask the class if what he said made sense and if there were any questions.  Lectures were very informative and quite funny at times.  Doing the weekly homework is very easy and helpful.  The exams are pretty easy except for the last question is normally a little challenging.

He is really engaging; kept me focused for a power lecture. His accent is cool too. It reminds me of a Russian Mario.  Calc. 3 is a tough class but Professor Arinkin really helps you visualize everything.  Rather than just copy from the textbook he does examples that help master concepts.  Really smart and quirky dude.

Overall, a very good professor.  I thought he presented the material clearly and he was engaging, given it was a 75 min. lecture.  I really enjoyed how he began each lecture with a 5-10 min. recap of the important topics from the previous lecture.  Exams were somewhat difficult but were similar to the provided practice exams.

He is a good lecturer that explains things clearly and knows what he is talking about, and can make the class laugh now and then. The tests are moderately hard, but are very close to the practice exams. Small mistakes can cost you big though. If you have a good TA , it will help make things more clear. He also has an accent, but it's understandable
Great professor with engaging lectures. Explains everything clearly and teaches so you will be prepared for exams.

Class is challenging, but fair. Homework from the text book is often times unhelpful, but the practice tests he gives are good. He teaches toward the test, and teaches at a very reasonable pace. Also, a funny guy that makes things more understandable in laymen terms.

Awesome professor. Extremely helpful and clear both in lecture and office hours. Exams are very close to samples. Homework problems were somewhat difficult but class was enjoyable with him. Found free legal pdf of our textbook.
I loved taking his class he made math power lectures enjoyable with his enthusiasm and clarity

Excellent professor and very entertaining! I come from a foreign background so maybe I could understand him more than other but he certainly went over the material well and covered the topics that would be on exams. His exams on the difficult side, especially when compared to homework. Dont be suprised by a proof on the last page! Great professor!
He just makes this ultimate calculus class nice and easy. The homework has everything to do with the exams. He also makes the lecture funny and informative. Great prof.
I really liked this professor! He's really funny, but definitely look at the examples in the book too. If you do the homework and pay attention in lecture, you should get a good grade.
Lectures were well organized, but material was difficult and they were not overly helpful. Very nice guy, and he tries to keep the class engaged during difficult sections.
Lectures aren't very helpful. He goes over mostly the same thing, but at least he gives you practice exams similar to the real exams and the class isn't too much work.

Susan Dominguez is objectively the worst professor I have had in my time at UW. Her assignments are worth very few points, and small mistakes are penalized. In my experience, she has a profound lack of respect for students and was extremely condescending when asked questions. It is quite a bummer because the course material is interesting.

A terribly run class with confusing instructions that won't she wouldn't even explain on. The content of this class was unbelievably great, but the way that we were dissecting the readings was unbearable. She asked for things to see in papers, but then took away points for adding that exact thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She can be a little unconventional at times and not play by the books (which is funny because the class I took with her is about literature.) Nevertheless, at least for her Gen Ed class, just be respectful and put in effort, and take pride in your work, and you should be able to succeed!

Not sure how people have such negative reviews, I had a completely different experience. She is one of the kindest teachers I have had and has gone out of her way to help me. The lectures are boring but if you just show up you get all the points. Same with the exams, she tells you what to do, and if you just follow directions you will do well.

The worst professor I have ever gotten. I went to ask why her TA had marked me down on my paper and she made up random criteria that was not in the assignment to justify it and when I probed further, was extremely rude and demeaning. Assignments are very unclear and she makes no effort to explain them.

she's an engaging professor, but she's particularly harsh on students and uses the 'old age' card to get away with it. Even walking up to her and asking her a doubt/correction error or literally anything was a scary experience because her responses were kinda passive aggressive and standoffish. Overall an interesting professor,though.

Her TA gave me a terrible grade on a final paper that I worked extremely hard on. When I confronted Susan to ask about it, she told me she hadn't seen my paper. After reading it she said she would have given it an even lower grade. Then proceeded to belittle and bully me over a string of about eight emails. Reported her to department.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Instructions for essays and discussion posts are vague, but you'll get docked if you miss one thing. Attendance is mandatory but lectures are terrible and add nothing to the course. She clearly wasn't familiar with material, but didn't make any attempts to change that.

While this class was incredibly easy, Professor Dominguez displayed incredibly unprofessional behavior throughout the semester. She is rude to students, her assignments are unclear, and her lectures are irrelevant. Luckily most assignments/papers are based on readings which is why many students get by. Her lectures online would have you screwed.

On first day, when the only POC walked in, she yelled at him for being 15 seconds late and no one else who was late. She won't assign 1000+ word papers until a few days before they're due, and they're only 4 points with small grammar mistakes being -0.25 EACH. Talks a lot about when we "get to the real world." Made me come to class w/ a concussion.

Took the class just to satisfy breadth, and it was perfect. She understood that many ppl were doing this, and assigned the workload accordingly. Only a few papers, could get away without reading, and although some the the grading was questionable, most people got an A in her class. Excellent class to take for reqs, and interesting topics covered.

Somewhat difficult class. Assignments (even whole essays) are all worth about 3-4 points and little mistakes like incorrect word order of a citation will cost you about .5 points. Go to office hours. If you're thinking about taking a class from this professor, do not let the other ratings completely steer you away, but be prepared to put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a nice teacher and is accommodating if you need extensions or extra resources, but her directions for assignments are very unclear and if assignments are not done to her standard, she doesn't explain why or how to improve. Also, she grades assignments out of 4 points so if you make one mistake you're down to 3.75/4 right away.

Took class online spring 2021. Dominguez was awful. Spouted COVID-19 conspiracy theories in the third week of class, rambled on and on about nothing comprehensible, made us buy a textbook and then didn't use material from it, played favorites, was just generally terrible. Avoid her at all costs unless you can get on her good side right away.

If I am honest I feel like the class was very unorganized, this was because about a week or two in the restarted the entire class as she forgot to inform us a lot. The end of the year pulled in very quickly and she forgot about the end of the year paper but still required it from us though she was very lenient on it as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The worst professor I had in my four years at UW. Very condescending and inconsiderate, and to be quite frank, flat out rude to students.
On the first day of class, she gave a land acknowledgment and then said that we should "get over it." This is completely unacceptable for an instructor in this department.

This professor was beyond disorganized. She would ramble on end for the entire lecture time about unrelated topics like 9/11 and the Vietnam war (she never made an attempt to relate this to any native nations). She also was extremely hostile to students who would ask questions or attempt to provide accurate data on reservation life or covid stats.

She mentioned her unvaccinated daughter multiple times. She excused not being vaccinated. Many bias reports filed against her. The textbook also becomes your professor! Felt like I was in an 80's college movie, she would write a single word on the board and talk for an hour and those were our "notes."
Easily the worst teacher Ive ever had at UW. Her lectures were miserable and the material was beyond boring.

There were never clear instructions or grading criteria. For example, the instructions for our midterm were in multiple different places, hidden in canvas. There were never rubrics at all. This professor also is unhelpful when confronted with questions, and gets very hostile. Not sure why UW hired her...

Prof Anhai is the Uncle Iroh equivalent of UW madison - if that interests you, take the class with him. 

PS. gives a lot of tips for tech interviews
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the only professor that I clapped for 10 minutes after the last lecture. Marvolous lectures which are easy to understand. Funny style of teaching that helps you concentrate on the class. Important life-time ideas that you should keep in mind even outside Database world. You are my light in my academic life, Anhai!
GOATED!!!!!!!!

He's the funniest professor in the CS department—I didn't go to any lectures, but when I was cramming for exams, I actually wished I had. I would voluntarily listent to his stories and unsolicited life advice.

He does water down the course heavily tho. So if you're here for vibes, he's your guy. If you're here to learn, maybe look elsewhere.
Funniest Professor I've ever had. He is somehow always able to crack jokes in the middle of the lecture despite seemingly boring (database) topics. 10/10 take his class if you can

TAKE THE CLASS WITH ANHAI.
Professor 2% created genuinely engaging lectures filled with iconic quotes, jokes, as well as the class you actually signed up for. It's only graded by two exams and five group assignments. The assignments are all manageable and the exams connect to the lectures well. Is this a good or bad thing? "It depends."
Overall great guy

Prof. AnHai is an expert in data science with strong industry experience. Lectures are informative and funny, and he includes a lot of advice about how things work in industry. The class was graded from 2 exams (short answer, just attend class and it's easy) and a group project. However, he provides minimal grading feedback. I think most got an A.

Hilarious professor that is passionate about the field of database systems. Elucidates complex topics with plenty of in-lecture examples and extra notes to read. Cares deeply about the success of his students and gave a variety of life and career advice in many lectures, take this class with him if you can!
Very funny and engaging, makes the content easy to learn

Anhai is a nice guy but if I had to describe him in one word, it would be LAZY. He barely takes lectures and the exams are uninspiring, to say the least (basically if you can cram definitions, you do well). Take him if you need a chill course and don't plan to learn a lot from it.

An Hai was the best CS professor I've ever had. He's also a brilliant data scientist and he explained complex concepts in a clear way. His lectures were hilarious and full of career, dating, and life advice. He even sent a long email after final grades were posted to give extra advice to the class. He truly cares about his students.
Cool prof

He's a great guy who is willing and able to help his students. He seems to care about that his students understand the content but isn't super pushy about needing to learn unnecessary specifics. He also is really funny and makes lectures as bearable as lecture can be. I would definitely take a course with AnHai again if I had the choice.
Professor Doan is brilliant and down to earth. Database management systems expressed in terms of boats, sailors and beer.

The class is pretty easy as CS classes go. The textbook sucks so its important to go to lectures. There's too much covered to really have time to practice and get comfortable with things and as such, the assignments are superficial.

This class is online, which was great for making it approachable and easy to manage. I recommend taking notes on this class and it's really not that hard with effort put in. Doug does a great job covering everything needed for quizzes in the lectures and projects were fun. Discussions, however, need improvement.

Doug teaches out in California, which makes this course somewhat difficult if you dislike online classes. I enjoyed the course's simple structure, so it made it pretty easy to get things in on time. I will say, the grading criteria was pretty confusing and depends on your TA. That being said, once you get the hang of it its pretty easy.

This professor teaches all his classes remotely, even classes that are listed as in-person. All lectures are prerecorded and often from other random sources, usually of poor quality and outdated. Very little direction, poor communication and very inconsistent and harsh grading with little to no feedback. Would not recommend any class taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Aside from everything that everyone else has said, the class also just sucks. You will learn a minimal amount of important information in this class. Things that are taught/tested are either rudimentary or  beyond obscure. Project rubrics are also unclear because he does not know how to hierarchically structure instructions.

All the lectures are recorded and can be extremely lenghty as well as incredibly low quality, and a lot of them are from random other professors. Discussion and paper reports have unecessarily long prompts, and grading rubrics are very inconsistent. Quizzes have questions about a lot of random facts that you probably don't have in your notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is super easy, but man I wish I knew Doug lives in California so the entire class is basically online where you meet with your TA once a week. The lectures are incredibly dry, boring, and long so I never watched any of them (but still got a good grade). Would be way better if he was an in person professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Full of busy work. Supposed to be an in-person lecture, but the prof is remote and doesn't even live in Wisconsin. Take this class online. If you take the "in-person" version, you'll just be taking an online class but still have to go to a classroom. Dates from his material are wrong because he reuses it every semester and can't be bothered.

Biggest warning: professor teaches from California the entire semester and so we only ever met in person for discussion with the TA. I wish I knew this before I signed up because I really dislike online learning and always seem to do somehow worse, the class is fun tho. If you don't have a problem with online school then you'll be fine.

LA250 was not a terrible class, but this guy is an extremely dry lecturer. All of his lectures are uncut and sometimes he lets out an ear piercing cough or clears his throat into the mic.
